intro.heading: Three sciences, one calendar, and the decisions that close quietly
paragraphs: Science is the part of an IGCSE timetable where the calendar does most of the damage. A triple-award candidate carries three separate subjects, each with its own theory papers and its own practical or alternative-to-practical component, and each competing with seven other subjects for the same evenings. A family in City Walk who starts looking for help in the spring of Year 11 is arriving after several decisions have already closed: the award route, the tier, the practical component and the entry itself.

So this page is organised by date rather than by syllabus. It sets out what each term of a two-year science course has to finish, when the award and tier decisions actually close and what can still be influenced afterwards, how the practical component is decided and by whom, what the final twelve weeks can realistically change across three sciences, and how a mock fortnight containing six science papers should be used. The content is here, inside the timeline, because a topic list without a deadline attached is what most tutoring pages in this market already provide.

Two dates anchor everything. A UAE candidate sits the June series or the November series: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. And one warning that costs families real planning time: the Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only. A science revision plan built around a February or March exam window is built on the wrong country's calendar.

City Walk's own contribution is logistical. The district sits between Al Wasl and Jumeirah with no school inside it, so every candidate here travels out, most often to the Al Safa, Al Wasl and Jumeirah cluster, sometimes further to Al Quoz or Al Barsha. The return journey is short by Dubai standards, which means a City Walk family can often start a session at 4pm where much of the emirate cannot start before 5pm. In a final twelve-week run across three sciences, that half-hour head start is worth real sessions.

On delivery, plainly. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE and we operate no centre here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Practical skills are assessed by the school or by a written paper set by the board, and a tutor does not substitute for the laboratory; what a tutor can do is teach the writing that the practical and alternative-to-practical components actually reward, which is work that happens perfectly well over video.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-city-walk.programmesIntro: A science course has four decision points and families usually engage with the last one. These are the stages in play for a City Walk family, described by what closes at each.

programmes.name: Year 9, when the award route is chosen
programmes.description: The year the school decides, often in consultation with families and often not, whether a student takes three separate sciences, a double award or a combined course. That decision shapes two years of content volume and influences which sixth-form science routes stay open. Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint results are the most useful external evidence a family has in that conversation, and they arrive before it rather than after.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the award route is usually settled alongside the wider option choices in Year 9, and the practical consequence for a City Walk family is that the window to influence it is a term long. Once the school has built the timetable around a cohort's choices, individual changes become difficult rather than impossible.

programmes.name: Year 10, when the tier closes
programmes.description: Content is met for the first time across all three sciences, and the Core or Extended tier entry decision is formed on the basis of internal assessment. This is the cheapest and most effective year to buy science support, because gaps have not yet compounded and because the tier can still be changed. It is also the year almost nobody buys it.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the tier entry decision is usually made during Year 10 or very early Year 11, within the board's deadlines. A City Walk family that raises a tier concern in the autumn of Year 10 is having a productive conversation; one that raises it in the spring of Year 11 is having a different and much shorter one.

programmes.name: Year 11, when only marks are left
programmes.description: Content teaching completes, the mock window delivers data, and the work becomes converting knowledge into marks across six or more papers. The useful interventions here are command-term discipline, the six-mark extended-response structure, practical write-up technique and timing. Genuine content repair is possible in the autumn term and expensive by the spring.
programmes.countryNote: A City Walk Year 11 arriving home around 4pm has roughly three usable evening hours contested by eight subjects. Three sciences cannot all be tutored in that week. Choosing one, from marked papers rather than from anxiety, is the decision the calendar forces and the one most families resist.

programmes.name: The resit window
programmes.description: A science grade can be improved by entering the next available series, and for a UAE candidate that means November after a June result or June after a November one. Whether a previously achieved practical or coursework mark can be carried forward depends on the specification and on the centre's arrangements, so confirm that with the school's examinations officer before planning anything.
programmes.countryNote: Looking at a published pattern: Pearson's November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November entry therefore produces a grade in the following January, which is in time for many sixth-form confirmations and not all of them.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-city-walk.subjectsIntro: The science subjects and components a City Walk family will be choosing between, with the calendar point at which each one matters most. Confirm every code and weighting against the current syllabus document the school holds.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Edexcel 4BI1)
subjects.description: The largest content volume of the three sciences, which makes it the worst candidate for a late content rescue and a good candidate for early weekly support. Extended-tier marks are won on command terms: explain, suggest and compare each want a different answer shape, and correct biology written in the wrong shape scores nothing.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Edexcel 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and organic chemistry concentrate the lost Extended marks. Organic is cumulative, so it is cheap to secure in Year 10 and expensive to repair in the spring of Year 11. Calculation marks, by contrast, respond to a few weeks of repetition at almost any point in the calendar.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Edexcel 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism are where Extended separates from Core and where most City Walk students lose their grade. These need sustained weeks rather than a late block. Equation selection and unit discipline, however, are technique and move quickly whenever they are addressed.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: One course covering all three sciences and awarded as two grades. Reduced content against the three separate sciences, with a correspondingly reduced claim on the week. The route decision between this and triple science is made in Year 9 and shapes which sixth-form science options remain comfortable.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: All three sciences in one course awarded as a single grade. Suited to a student whose strengths lie elsewhere and who needs a science pass rather than a science route. Worth confirming the sixth-form implications in writing before accepting it, because some courses expect more.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (Pearson 4SD0)
subjects.description: Pearson's equivalent of the co-ordinated route, awarded as two grades. The practical difference from Cambridge is in paper structure and phrasing rather than in content coverage, which matters for which past papers are worth working in the final term.

subjects.name: Theory papers
subjects.description: Carry the majority of the marks and are where the calendar pressure concentrates, because six theory papers in one series means six sets of past-paper practice. Multiple-choice and structured-response papers reward different preparation, and students who practise only the structured papers lose marks to careless multiple choice.

subjects.name: Practical test and alternative to practical
subjects.description: Some specifications set a practical examination, others an alternative-to-practical written paper. Which applies is a centre and specification matter, decided by the school rather than the family. Either way the marks come from precise description of method, variables, control and sources of error, which is a writing skill.

subjects.name: Six-mark extended response
subjects.description: The highest-value recoverable item in science. Students who understand the content still score four out of six because the answer lacks structure or omits a required linkage. Teaching the structure is three sessions per subject and shows in the next marked paper, which makes it the right work for a short block.

subjects.name: Mathematical skills in science
subjects.description: Rearranging equations, standard form, significant figures, gradients from graphs and percentage calculations. Weak mathematics shows up as weak physics and weak chemistry, and the repair belongs in the maths plan rather than the science plan. Diagnosing it early saves a term of misdirected science teaching.

subjects.name: Command terms
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare, evaluate. Each requires a specific shape of answer and each is worth marks. A student writing a description where an explanation was asked for loses every mark for otherwise correct science, which makes this the cheapest repair available in the subject at any point in the year.

subjects.name: Formula and equation recall
subjects.description: Which equations are printed on the paper and which must be recalled differs by specification and tier, and students routinely memorise the provided list while neglecting the required one. Confirm against the specification document the school holds, since boards revise it and a wrong list costs marks.

sections.heading: The two-year science course, term by term
paragraphs: Laid out as a sequence, a science course has a predictable shape and a predictable set of closing doors. Year 9 settles the award route. Year 10 teaches the content and forms the tier decision. The autumn of Year 11 completes the content and delivers the mock data. The spring of Year 11 converts knowledge into marks across six or more papers. After results, the resit question.

The mistake families make is not failing to work hard. It is engaging with the sequence at the final stage, where the available interventions are narrowest and the cost per unit of effect is highest. A City Walk parent who reads this in Year 10 has access to decisions that a parent reading it in March of Year 11 does not, and the difference is not marginal: it includes the award route, the tier, and whether three sciences was the right load in the first place.

The practical use of the table below is as a checklist of questions to ask the school at each stage, in writing. Most of these questions have short factual answers that schools provide readily when asked clearly, and most families never ask them. Which award route is my child on. Which tier are they entered for in each science. Which practical component does the centre use. Which specification codes. When is the mock window. These are the inputs to any sensible plan and they are all free.

One honest caveat about the final stage. In the spring of Year 11, with three sciences and six papers, the realistic question is not how to raise all three grades but which one grade matters most and whether the marks are recoverable. That is a narrower and more useful question, and a provider who answers it with a three-science package has not answered it.

sections.heading: The award route decision, and the door it closes
paragraphs: Triple science, double award and combined science are three different loads and three different outcomes, and the choice between them is usually made in Year 9. Triple science means biology, chemistry and physics as separate subjects with separate grades and the fullest content coverage. A double award such as Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0 covers all three with reduced content and produces two grades. Combined science produces one.

The consequence that matters is what each keeps open at sixteen. A sixth-form science course, particularly an A Level or an IB Higher Level science, generally expects strong attainment in the relevant separate science or in a double award, and a combined award can constrain the choice. Expectations vary by school, so this is a question to ask the receiving sixth form in writing rather than to assume from a general rule.

The consequence that matters for the calendar is load. Triple science is three subjects' worth of content and six or more papers inside a nine or ten subject timetable. For a student who is comfortable across the sciences that is manageable. For a student who is already struggling in two of the three, it is a decision that guarantees a difficult Year 11, and the honest conversation in Year 9 is sometimes about taking the double award and doing it well rather than the triple and doing it partially.

If the decision has already been made and the year is underway, the useful move is not to reopen it but to plan around it. A triple-science student in Year 11 with three weak sciences needs session distribution by marks lost rather than by fairness, and needs to accept that one of the three will receive almost no support. That is an uncomfortable plan and it beats spreading a week's capacity so thinly that nothing moves.

sections.heading: The practical component: decided by the school, written by the student
paragraphs: Families consistently underestimate this component and consistently misunderstand who controls it. Depending on the specification and the centre's arrangements, a science candidate may sit a practical examination or a written alternative-to-practical paper. Which one applies is determined by the specification and by the centre, not by the family, and it is worth establishing early because the preparation differs.

What does not differ is where the marks come from. Both routes reward precise description of method, clear identification of independent, dependent and control variables, awareness of repeats and anomalies, and specific rather than generic sources of error. A student who writes that a source of error is human error has written nothing; a student who writes that the thermometer was read at an angle, introducing a parallax error, has written something marked. That difference is teachable in three or four sessions and it transfers across all three sciences.

This is also where the honest limit of online science tuition sits, and it is worth stating directly rather than glossing. We do not run a laboratory and we do not substitute for the practical work your child's school provides. The laboratory skill is built at school. What a tutor can do, and do well over video, is teach the writing that both components actually mark, using the student's own practical write-ups from school as the material.

The calendar point is that practical preparation is frequently left until the last fortnight, when it is competing with six theory papers. It does not need to be. The writing discipline is independent of the content and can be built in Year 10 or in the autumn of Year 11, when the week has room. A family that moves practical preparation earlier buys itself a quieter final month at no extra cost, which is the cheapest scheduling improvement available in science.

sections.heading: The mock fortnight: six science papers as free diagnostic data
paragraphs: A triple-science candidate in Dubai sits a substantial number of papers in a mock window, often including two per science. Most families receive three grades out of this and discard the rest. The marked papers are the most valuable free data the whole year produces, and they are the only honest basis for deciding how a final twelve weeks should be distributed.

Ask for the marked papers rather than the grades, then sort each one's lost marks into four piles. Questions not attempted. Questions attempted and wrong on content. Questions where the science was right and the command term was answered in the wrong shape. And the six-mark extended responses, scored separately. Those four categories need completely different work, and the proportions differ noticeably between the three sciences for most students.

The pattern that recurs in this corridor is instructive. A student will often show a content gap in physics, a command-term problem in biology and a calculation problem in chemistry, all producing the same grade. A three-science package treats them identically and wastes most of its hours. A plan built from the marked papers puts eight sessions into the physics content, three into biology answer shapes and one diagnostic session into chemistry calculation technique, and produces movement in all three.

One further check costs two minutes. Look at whether the lost marks concentrate in the second half of each paper. If they do, the problem is pacing rather than knowledge, and the intervention is question-order strategy rather than any topic at all. Across three sciences and six papers that single observation redirects a surprising number of final-term plans, and it requires no tutor to make.

sections.heading: What twelve weeks can change across three sciences
paragraphs: With twelve weeks and three sciences, a City Walk family has perhaps twelve to sixteen sessions of realistic capacity inside a Year 11 week. Distributing those evenly is the instinct and the mistake. Distributing them by recoverable marks is what works, and it produces an uneven plan that looks unfair and performs well.

What moves inside twelve weeks is technique. Command-term discipline across all three sciences, which is the same skill taught three times. The six-mark extended-response structure, where students who know the content routinely score four. Practical write-up language. Equation selection and unit discipline in physics. Mole and titration calculation repetition in chemistry. Each of those is two to four sessions and each is worth marks on every paper.

What does not move inside twelve weeks is a missing year. If a student cannot do electricity in physics at all, or has never understood organic chemistry, twelve weeks across three subjects will not repair it while also preparing six papers. The honest plan then is to secure the topics that are secure, maximise the technique marks, and be realistic about the grade. That is a worse answer than families want and a better plan than the alternative.

The distribution that usually works looks like this: identify the science with the most recoverable marks from the mock papers, give it the majority of the sessions, give the second science a short technique block, and give the third a single diagnostic session with a homework plan rather than ongoing support. Then put the whole papers on weekend mornings, because a full science paper cannot be worked to time on a weeknight after a City Walk commute and eight other subjects' homework.

sections.heading: Counting a series backwards, with the zone problem
paragraphs: A UAE science candidate sits the June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The February/March series is offered to India only, and any plan quoting a February or March exam window to a Dubai family is working from the wrong country's calendar.

Cambridge adds an administrative item that genuinely matters. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. With six science papers in one series, a wrong-zone timetable is not a minor inconvenience. Build the revision calendar from the timetable your own examinations officer confirms.

Dates in the past are safe to state because they are checkable, and they illustrate the shape of a series better than a projection can. Pearson's November 2026 final International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can be revised.

For a City Walk family planning a final run, the practical consequence of six papers in one window is sequencing. The sciences will not be examined on consecutive days in most zones, and knowing the actual order lets a student front-load revision for the earliest paper rather than revising all three in parallel to the end. That is a free improvement and it depends entirely on having the correct timetable in hand early.

sections.heading: Ramadan, breaks and the weeks a science plan loses
paragraphs: A twelve-week plan drawn on paper is usually a nine-week plan in reality, and in science that gap is more damaging than in most subjects because the content volume is higher. Ramadan shortens school days and reorganises evenings around iftar. Winter and spring breaks remove whole weeks. School events, trips and internal assessment weeks take more. Count them before drawing the plan rather than discovering them inside it.

Ramadan needs a decision made in advance. For a Year 11 whose series falls after the month, three or four weeks of lost continuity at that point in the calendar is the single largest avoidable loss available. Early-afternoon sessions and post-iftar sessions both work; what fails is improvisation. Agree the alternative pattern before the month begins and the continuity survives.

Breaks are the opposite case and are routinely misused. A break is the only period a science candidate has whole uninterrupted days, which makes it the correct window for full papers under timed conditions and the wrong window for new content. For a triple-science candidate, two or three marked papers across a one-week break produce the diagnostic data that shapes the rest of the term, at less cost than six rushed weeknight sessions.

Travel is the last item and it is underestimated in this corridor. A student spending four weeks abroad in the summer before Year 11 returns having lost calculation fluency and equation recall rather than conceptual understanding, so the first September sessions should be retrieval work rather than new topics. Online delivery means sessions can continue through travel where a family wants them to, which is a genuine scheduling advantage rather than a selling point.

sections.heading: What three sciences cost, against what one costs
paragraphs: The cost question in science is not the hourly rate but the number of subjects being funded, because three sciences at one session a week each is three times the commitment of one. Setting that out plainly usually changes the decision, and in the right direction.

Here are the published Dubai bands to apply that to, each attributed to the provider or publication that stated it and read in October 2026. Take the in-home figures first, since City Walk families mostly buy visits: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and independent home tutors reach AED 200 to 500 once travel is priced in, charged per visit, so a physics tutor and a chemistry tutor arriving on separate evenings pay that premium twice. Online removes the travel and reshapes the choice. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase quotes AED 270, Bestimate puts IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialist work at AED 200 to 450 or more, and BartyED sits at AED 650 at the premium end. Monthly packages compress the same money differently again, at AED 799 for eight online sessions or AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

Apply those to three sciences over a twelve-week run. At the qualified-tutor online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, one science at one session a week for twelve weeks is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600. Three sciences on the same pattern is AED 5,400 to 10,800. The uncomfortable finding is that the three-science version frequently delivers less than the one-science version, because thirty-six sessions in a Year 11 week is not a load a student can attend, and sessions not attended are sessions paid for.

IB Gram does not publish a UAE rate card on these pages and does not present any of these figures as ours. The free trial lesson exists so a family can see the teaching before discussing money, and the consultation exists so the number of subjects is chosen from marked papers rather than from worry. For wider budget context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

sections.heading: Honesty, regulation and getting started with a date in view
paragraphs: A science tutor teaches content, explains assessment criteria, models technique on a different example and gives feedback on the student's own work. A tutor does not write a practical report, complete coursework or edit a piece to completion. That boundary protects your child, because a malpractice finding falls on the student. We will not do it and will not accept such work if a family offers it. We also do not distribute board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; your child's school has legitimate access to all of them.

Regulation is the other thing to settle before a date goes in the calendar, and in science it is three checks rather than one, because three subjects often means three different people coming into a City Walk apartment. Each of them needs the same document: the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. The eligible categories are broad enough that almost any genuine science tutor falls inside one, covering teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, which is the whole cost of compliance. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here, and none should appear in a tutor's pitch either.

On equivalency, since science subjects are part of the count: the sourced British-track rule is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or above or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. At least one ranking site in this market publishes six, which is wrong. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency for anybody, and tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, admission or progression.

To start with a date in view, bring four things: the specification code and tier for each science, the award route, the marked mock papers rather than the grades, and the series your child is entered for. With those, a diagnosis is possible in the trial lesson and the twelve weeks can be distributed the same day. Coverage across the three sciences at both boards and both tiers is reliable, so a match is usually available within a few working days; what fills first is the hour, and City Walk's short run makes 4pm and 4.30pm the easiest slots in this corridor to hold for a full term.

process.title: Establish the award route and the codes
process.description: Email the school for the award route, the exact specification code for each science and the tier of entry. These determine which past papers are worth working and whether the grade ceiling matches what your child needs at sixteen. One reply usually settles all three.

process.title: Ask which practical component the centre uses
process.description: Depending on the specification and the centre's arrangements, a candidate may sit a practical examination or a written alternative-to-practical paper. Which applies is not a family choice and it changes the preparation, so it is worth establishing early rather than in the final fortnight.

process.title: Collect the marked mock papers
process.description: Six science papers from a mock window are the best free diagnostic data of the year, and most families keep only the three grades. Sort the losses into unattempted, content, command term and six-mark response, because those four need completely different work and differ between the three sciences.

process.title: Count the usable weeks, then distribute
process.description: Subtract the breaks, the Ramadan weeks, school events and travel from the weeks remaining before the series. What is left is the real calendar. Then distribute the available sessions by recoverable marks rather than evenly across three sciences, which produces an uneven plan that works.

process.title: A free trial lesson that ends in a plan
process.description: A taught session that produces a written note of marks being lost by type in each science, and a proposed distribution of the remaining weeks. No card is required, and the note is useful whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: Review at six weeks on marked work
process.description: Compare marked papers against the baseline, then continue, redistribute between the sciences, or finish. Redistribution is the common outcome: the science that looked weakest from a grade is frequently not the one with the most recoverable marks once the papers have been read.

whyPoints.title: Planned from the series, not from a topic list
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from the June or November series your child is entered for and counts backwards through breaks, Ramadan and the mock window to the weeks that genuinely remain. A science plan that assumes twelve clear weeks when nine exist fails on the calendar rather than on the teaching.

whyPoints.title: Sessions distributed by recoverable marks
whyPoints.description: Three sciences do not get equal shares. The science with the most recoverable marks gets the majority of a limited capacity, the second gets a technique block, and the third gets a diagnostic session and a homework plan. Even distribution is the instinct and the reason most three-science plans stall.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Cambridge Physics 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 cover much the same physics with different papers and phrasing. In a final run where a student will complete a limited number of papers, working the wrong board's papers wastes the scarcest resource in the plan.

whyPoints.title: Practical writing taught as a distinct skill
whyPoints.description: Method, variables, control, repeats, anomalies and specific error sources, written the way the scheme marks them. It transfers across all three sciences, it is three or four sessions, and it is usually left until it is competing with six theory papers.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the laboratory
whyPoints.description: We run no laboratory and do not substitute for school practical work. The laboratory skill is built at school; what a tutor builds is the writing both components mark, worked from your child's own school write-ups. Saying that plainly is more useful than implying otherwise.

whyPoints.title: Sources and limits both stated
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure carries the provider that published it and the month it was read; every regulatory fact carries its authority. No in-home visits in the UAE, no office or centre here, no regulator approval claimed, and no statistic without a number, a date and a method.

faqs.question: Our mock is in twelve weeks and all three sciences are weak. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With the marked papers, not with a three-science package. Within twelve weeks a Year 11 in this corridor has realistic capacity for twelve to sixteen sessions, and distributing those evenly across three sciences is the most common reason a plan stalls. Sort the lost marks in each science into unattempted, content, command-term shape and six-mark response. Then give the science with the most recoverable marks seven or eight sessions, the second a short technique block, and the third one diagnostic session with a written homework plan.

faqs.question: When is the award route between triple and double science actually decided?
faqs.answer: Usually in Year 9, alongside the wider option choices, and often with less family consultation than parents expect. Triple science means three separate subjects, three grades and six or more papers. A double award such as Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0 covers all three with reduced content and produces two grades. The window to influence the decision is roughly a term, because the school builds a timetable around a cohort's choices and individual changes become difficult afterwards.

faqs.question: Will a double science award limit my child's sixth-form options in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It can, and the answer varies by receiving school, so ask in writing rather than relying on a general rule. A sixth-form science course, particularly an A Level or an IB Higher Level science, generally expects strong attainment in the relevant separate science or in a double award, and a single combined award can constrain the choice. The practical move is to name the two or three sixth forms you might apply to and ask each what they accept for the science courses your child is interested in.

faqs.question: Can my child still change science tier in Year 11?
faqs.answer: It depends on where in the year you are and whether final entries have been submitted. The tier decision is formed in Year 10 or very early Year 11 on the basis of internal assessment, within the board's deadlines. Raised in the autumn of Year 11, a change is sometimes possible. Raised in the spring, usually not. If the ceiling is fixed and it sits below a sixth-form requirement, the honest plan is to maximise the grade available within the tier and have the sixth-form conversation early rather than late.

faqs.question: Which practical component will my child sit in each science?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's examinations officer, because it depends on the specification and on the centre's arrangements rather than on anything the family chooses. Some specifications set a practical examination and others a written alternative-to-practical paper. Either way the marks come from precise description of method, independent, dependent and control variables, repeats, anomalies and specific sources of error. Establishing which component applies early matters because the preparation differs and because practical work is usually left too late.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on practical questions despite doing the experiments?
faqs.answer: Because the marks are for the writing rather than for the doing. A source of error described as human error scores nothing; the same error described as reading the thermometer at an angle, introducing a parallax error, scores. Variables must be named rather than implied, control variables stated explicitly, and repeats and anomalies addressed. That discipline is three or four sessions per science, transfers across biology, chemistry and physics, and can be built in Year 10 when the week has room for it.

faqs.question: What should we do with six marked science papers from the mock window?
faqs.answer: Sort each paper's lost marks into four piles: not attempted, attempted and wrong on content, right science in the wrong command-term shape, and the six-mark extended responses scored separately. The proportions usually differ noticeably between the three sciences for the same student, which is exactly why a single three-science package wastes most of its hours. Also check whether losses concentrate in the second half of each paper, because that means pacing rather than knowledge and needs question-order work instead of content.

faqs.question: Why does my child score four out of six on extended-response science questions?
faqs.answer: Almost always structure rather than knowledge. A six-mark question expects a developed chain of reasoning with specified linkages, and a student who writes three correct but unconnected statements scores for three. Teaching the structure, which means a stated starting point, explicit links between steps and a conclusion that answers the question asked, takes about three sessions per science and shows in the next marked paper. It is the highest-value recoverable item in IGCSE science and it is rarely taught explicitly.

faqs.question: Which science topics are not worth starting twelve weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: Electricity and electromagnetism in physics, and organic chemistry, if they have genuinely never been understood. Both are cumulative, both need sustained weeks, and attempting either from scratch across a twelve-week run that also has to prepare six papers takes capacity from work that would actually move marks. The honest plan in that situation is to secure what is secure, take the technique marks across all three sciences, and be realistic about the grade rather than pretending.

faqs.question: When do science candidates in Dubai sit their papers?
faqs.answer: In the June series or the November series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The Cambridge February/March series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a February or March window is on the wrong country's calendar. Read exact dates from the board's live timetable rather than from any tutoring website.

faqs.question: Why does our school keep asking about an examination zone?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. With six science papers in one series this is not a minor matter. Get the correct zone timetable from your own examinations officer, and use it to learn the paper order so revision can be front-loaded.

faqs.question: Does a practical or coursework mark carry forward to a science resit?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specification and on the centre's arrangements, so ask the school's examinations officer before planning a resit. This is exactly the kind of detail no tutoring page should state as fact, because it varies and because a family would act on it. What can be said generally is that the resit decision should be made from component marks rather than the overall grade: a theory paper that fell a few marks short is a narrow piece of work, and an evenly spread shortfall usually reproduces itself without a change of approach.

faqs.question: How much does it cost to fund all three sciences in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Roughly three times one science, which is the point of asking. At the qualified-tutor online band, Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places specialist work at AED 200 to 450 or more. One science at one session a week for twelve weeks is about AED 1,800 to 3,600 at AED 150 to 300 an hour; three sciences on the same pattern is AED 5,400 to 10,800. The three-science version frequently delivers less, because thirty-six sessions is not a load a Year 11 attends.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor help with science when the laboratory is at school?
faqs.answer: For the part that carries the marks, yes. We run no laboratory and do not substitute for the practical work the school provides; the laboratory skill is built there. What a tutor teaches over video is the writing both practical routes actually mark, using your child's own school write-ups as the material: method, variables, control, repeats, anomalies and specific error sources. That is the component families most often neglect and the one that moves fastest, and it needs no equipment on either side of the screen.

faqs.question: How do we keep three sciences moving through the Ramadan weeks?
faqs.answer: Agree the pattern before the month starts rather than deciding week by week. School days shorten and evenings reorganise around iftar, so the usual slot stops working for most City Walk families. Early-afternoon and post-iftar sessions both work. For a Year 11 whose series falls after Ramadan, three or four weeks of lost continuity at that point is the largest avoidable loss in the calendar, and with three sciences the recovery afterwards is longer than with one subject.

faqs.question: Can a science tutor come to our home in City Walk for the final weeks?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the United Arab Emirates and has no office, branch, centre or laboratory here; home visiting is a service we run only in India. All UAE tuition is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In a final run this is practically useful: a session can be moved by a day around a mock or a school commitment in a message, which with six science papers to prepare is the difference between twelve sessions received and eight.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-city-walk.closingHeading: Count the weeks, read the papers, then choose one science
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-city-walk.closingBody: Four free pieces of information make a science plan work. The award route and the specification code and tier for each science, confirmed in writing by the school. Which practical component the centre uses. The marked mock papers rather than the three grades. And the number of weeks genuinely remaining once the breaks, the Ramadan weeks and the school events are subtracted. With those, the distribution across three sciences is decided by evidence rather than by worry, and it is almost always more concentrated than a parent expects. Bring them to a short consultation on Gulf Standard Time. The trial lesson is free, no card is required, and it ends with a written note of marks being lost in each science and a proposed plan for the weeks that are left.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-culture-vil.tutorsIntro: These are the tutors covering IGCSE sciences for families in Culture Village: matched to the award, the board and the tier, working from that board's own past papers and marking to its published scheme.

intro.heading: Which award is your child actually taking?
paragraphs: IGCSE science is not one qualification and a surprising number of Culture Village families do not know which one their child is entered for. Cambridge offers Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as three separate awards, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award covering all three, and Combined Science 0653 as a single award covering all three in less depth. Pearson offers Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 separately, and a double award covering the three together.

That is not a technicality. It determines the content volume, the number of grades on the certificate, the depth per topic and what a post-16 course will assume. A student taking Combined Science has one science grade and has met each subject at reduced depth. A student taking three separate sciences has three grades and has met each in full. Those two students need completely different tutoring even though they would both answer the question what science are you doing with the same word.

The board matters too, and it matters in a specific way that families rarely hear. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination, which means apparatus description, variable control and data handling are written skills on a written paper. Cambridge's arrangements have varied by syllabus version, so the current syllabus document on the board's own site is the only safe reference and we check it per cohort.

The tier decision sits on top of all that. Cambridge sciences divide into Core and Extended, with Core carrying a grade ceiling and Extended the full range. The content difference is substantive rather than cosmetic: Extended adds quantitative treatment in chemistry, more demanding calculation in physics, and additional detail in biology. For a student heading towards an A Level science or an IB Higher Level science, the ceiling matters more than the safety does.

One correction worth making before any planning. Cambridge's February and March series is offered in India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones with a separate timetable each, stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone version was used.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Culture Village or anywhere else in the UAE. Tuition for UAE families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and home visiting is a service we operate only in India. The obvious objection for a science subject is practical work, and it deserves a direct answer rather than a deflection: that answer is in a section of its own below.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-culture-vil.programmesIntro: Culture Village families need IGCSE science support across three different award structures, and the work differs sharply between them. These are the routes we cover.

programmes.name: Cambridge separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 taken as three awards, each entered at Core or Extended, each assessed by its own written papers. The heaviest content load of the three structures and the one that leaves every post-16 route open, including A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Three separate sciences is also three sets of past papers, three mark schemes and potentially three different tiers. For a Culture Village family that becomes a scheduling question as much as a teaching one, and our usual recommendation is to diagnose all three with one marked paper each before buying support in any of them, because the losses are frequently concentrated in one subject rather than spread.

programmes.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences
programmes.description: A double award covering biology, chemistry and physics with content depth between Combined Science and the separate sciences. Two grades on the certificate. A common choice for students who want breadth without the full three-subject load, and a sound route into most post-16 options with some checking required.
programmes.countryNote: The practical consequence of a double award is that revision must rotate across three sciences rather than block on one, because every paper draws on all three. Students who revise in blocks reach the exam strong on whichever science they studied last. A rotation schedule is one of the few genuinely structural things a tutor can fix in a double award, and it costs one planning session.

programmes.name: Cambridge Combined Science
programmes.description: A single award covering all three sciences at reduced depth, producing one grade. The lightest content load and the structure that most constrains post-16 choices, since an A Level or IB Higher Level science usually assumes more depth than Combined Science provides.
programmes.countryNote: Combined Science is frequently the right choice and is frequently chosen without the post-16 conversation having happened. A Culture Village family whose child may want an IB Higher Level science or an A Level science should ask the school directly what gap would need closing from Combined Science, because the answer is usually specific and it is better known at fourteen than at sixteen.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 taken separately, with a double award also available. Practical skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical examination, which makes apparatus, variables and data handling a written-paper skill.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official document is what any plan should use.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-culture-vil.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE science topics Culture Village families ask about, each named with where the marks actually go rather than a description of the content.

subjects.name: Moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The topic that decides a chemistry grade and the one Combined Science students meet in least depth. Lost marks cluster in limiting reagent questions where the correct reagent is identified and the wrong mole ratio applied.

subjects.name: Electrochemistry and electrolysis
subjects.description: Electrode products, half-equations and the rules for aqueous electrolysis. Students who can construct a half-equation from scratch rather than recall one score consistently higher, and balancing under time pressure is where the marks go.

subjects.name: Organic chemistry and homologous series
subjects.description: Alkanes, alkenes, alcohols and carboxylic acids with their reactions, plus polymerisation. Reagents and conditions are examined specifically, so a reaction named without its conditions earns partial credit at best.

subjects.name: Electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits, and power. The standing failure is applying a series rule to a parallel branch, which produces a confident wrong answer that no later step exposes.

subjects.name: Forces, motion and energy
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, graphs of motion, Newton's laws, moments, work, power and efficiency. Unit conversion inside multi-stage calculations is the reliable loss, closely followed by graph gradients quoted without units.

subjects.name: Waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, total internal reflection, the electromagnetic spectrum and sound. Ray diagrams carry marks for labelled normals and correctly directed arrows, and an unlabelled diagram is treated as decoration.

subjects.name: Human physiology and transport
subjects.description: Circulation, breathing, digestion, excretion and homeostasis. Marks go to named structures and named processes, so a description of what happens without the correct terms scores well below what the student understands.

subjects.name: Genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid inheritance, Punnett squares, sex determination and variation. A drawn Punnett square earns marks that the same reasoning in prose does not, and probability answers need the ratio stated explicitly.

subjects.name: Plant biology and photosynthesis
subjects.description: Photosynthesis, transpiration, transport in plants and plant nutrition. Limiting factor questions are the discriminator and reward a student who names the factor and explains the mechanism rather than describing the graph.

subjects.name: Practical skills on paper
subjects.description: Apparatus choice, independent and dependent variables, controlled variables, repeat readings, anomalies and the evaluation of a method. Assessed inside the written papers for Pearson candidates, and a written skill in every case.

subjects.name: Graph and data handling
subjects.description: Plotting, lines of best fit, gradient calculation, and reading values with units. Scale choice costs marks on plotting questions, and a gradient quoted without its unit loses the mark on correct working.

subjects.name: Command words across the sciences
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate are not interchangeable. Explain wants a causal account and a description of the observation earns the knowledge mark and stops, which is the largest shared loss across all three subjects.

sections.heading: Combined, Co-ordinated and separate sciences compared
paragraphs: This is the comparison that should happen before any science tutoring is bought, and it frequently happens after a disappointing result instead. The three structures differ in content depth, in the number of grades produced, and in what a post-16 course will assume. Those three differences compound, and the third one has the longest shadow because it appears two years later in a different qualification.

Separate sciences carry the heaviest load and leave every route open. Three awards, three sets of papers, each subject met in full depth. Co-ordinated Sciences sits in the middle: a double award with content depth between the other two, producing two grades, and adequate for most post-16 options with some checking. Combined Science is the lightest, producing one grade, with each subject met at reduced depth.

The revision implication differs too and is routinely missed. In a Combined or Co-ordinated award every paper draws on all three sciences, so revision has to rotate rather than block. A student who revises biology for three weeks, then chemistry, then physics arrives at the exam strong in physics and rusty in biology. A rotation schedule costs one planning session and is one of the few genuinely structural things a tutor can fix in these awards.

The post-16 conversation is the one worth having early. If an IB Higher Level science or an A Level science is a realistic destination, ask the school what gap would need closing from the award your child is taking. The answer is usually specific, and it is considerably easier to act on at fourteen when the award can still be changed than at sixteen when it cannot.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson for the sciences
paragraphs: The boards differ in ways that change the preparation, and the one families should know about is how practical skills reach the mark scheme. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers, which means apparatus choice, variable control, repeat readings and method evaluation appear as written questions on a written paper. A Pearson candidate therefore needs those drilled as writing tasks rather than as laboratory habits.

Cambridge's arrangements have varied across syllabus versions, which is why this page does not state them. The current syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org is the only safe reference, and we check it per cohort rather than relying on a remembered arrangement. A tutor who asserts a practical arrangement without checking the current syllabus is making a claim the board may have changed, and on a page like this that would be worse than saying nothing.

The second difference is scheduling and it catches Culture Village families out because the district's children attend several schools. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each, stating plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone version was used. Pearson publishes one international timetable per series, provisional first and then final.

The third is the past-paper question, which is the practical consequence of everything above. Cambridge and Pearson papers for the same science are not interchangeable: they differ in question structure, in how practical skills are examined and in the balance of recall against application. A tutor preparing a Pearson candidate with Cambridge papers is doing honest work on the wrong material, and the result shows at mock time with no runway left.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, across all three sciences
paragraphs: Cambridge sciences divide into Core and Extended, and the difference is substantive. Core covers a narrower syllabus and is capped below the top grades, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded them however well they perform. Extended carries the full range and adds real content in each subject rather than simply harder questions on the same material.

In chemistry, Extended adds the quantitative treatment that everything else rests on: moles arithmetic used across topics rather than touched once. In physics, it adds more demanding calculation and a fuller treatment of electricity and of forces. In biology, it adds detail in genetics, in transport systems and in the quantitative handling of data. A student who found Core comfortable has not necessarily demonstrated readiness for any of those.

The tier decision is normally made by the school on Year 10 evidence, and a parent who does not ask will often learn it afterwards. The window in which support changes the decision is narrow: between the provisional indication and the final entry. Inside it, focused work on the specific Extended topics the department doubts can move the call. Outside it, the ceiling is fixed and support becomes about maximising performance within it.

For a Culture Village family with post-16 ambitions in a science, the ceiling is the consideration that matters. A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences assume the Extended content, particularly the quantitative chemistry. Accepting a Core entry at fifteen to secure a safer grade at sixteen can mean paying for bridging support at post-16 rates eighteen months later, which are higher in every band of this market.

sections.heading: Which science is hardest? The honest answer
paragraphs: Families ask this constantly and the general answer is unhelpful, because the three subjects fail different students. The useful version is to ask what each one punishes, and then compare that against what the student has already demonstrated. That turns an unanswerable question into a straightforward one.

Biology punishes imprecision. The content is wide and the marking is specific: named structures, named processes, correctly directed arrows on a diagram. A student who understands a system thoroughly and describes it loosely will score below their understanding, which surprises families who assume biology is the undemanding choice because it involves less arithmetic. The fix is terminology discipline rather than more revision.

Chemistry punishes weak quantitative fluency. Moles arithmetic is used as a tool across the whole subject, so a student who treats it as a topic to be recalled struggles everywhere rather than in one place. Physics punishes weak representation: an incomplete free-body diagram, an unlabelled ray diagram, a gradient quoted without units. Both of those are habits rather than gaps, which makes them cheaper to fix than a content weakness.

The comparison that actually helps a Culture Village family is between those three failure modes and the student's existing evidence. A student who writes precisely and dislikes arithmetic may find biology the strongest of the three. One who calculates confidently and writes loosely may find chemistry or physics easier than biology, which is the opposite of the usual expectation. Three marked papers, one in each science, answers this in a week.

sections.heading: How practical skills are assessed if lessons happen online
paragraphs: This is the reasonable objection to online science tuition and it deserves a straight answer. A tutor over video has no apparatus and cannot run an experiment with your child. No honest provider should imply otherwise, and we do not. What matters is where the practical marks actually sit, and for a Pearson International GCSE candidate the answer is unambiguous: inside the written papers.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills through written questions. Those questions ask a student to choose apparatus, identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, describe a method another person could follow, explain why repeat readings matter, identify an anomaly and evaluate a method's weaknesses. Every one of those is a writing task applied to science, and writing tasks are exactly what one-to-one tuition over video is good at.

The specific skills respond quickly to drilling because they follow patterns. Variable identification becomes automatic after about twenty questions. Method descriptions improve dramatically once a student learns to write them as instructions rather than as narration. Method evaluation improves once a student has a checklist: measurement precision, control of variables, repeats, equipment limitations, and the effect of each on the result. That block of work serves all three sciences simultaneously.

Where a family wants genuine hands-on support, the honest recommendation is the school. The teacher has the laboratory, the technician support and the duty of supervision. A tutor offering to replicate that would be duplicating something better provided elsewhere. What we add is the written half, which is where the marks are allocated and where most candidates lose them.

sections.heading: Command words: the loss shared by all three sciences
paragraphs: If a Culture Village family buys one block that helps every science at once, this is it. Command words are published by the boards, they are tiered, and in the sciences they produce a single dominant failure: a question says explain and the student describes. The description is accurate, the understanding is present, and the marks are not awarded because the scheme wanted a causal account.

The distinction is easy to teach and hard to remember under pressure, which is why it needs drilling rather than explaining. Describe wants what happens. Explain wants why, in terms of a mechanism. Suggest wants a plausible answer applying known science to an unfamiliar context, and is marked generously if the reasoning holds. Compare wants both sides addressed explicitly, not one described and the other implied. Evaluate wants a judgement supported by points on both sides.

The cheapest single improvement is a highlighting habit. Before answering, underline the command word and the number of marks. Six marks and explain means a causal chain with roughly six linked statements. Two marks and state means two facts and nothing else, written quickly so the minutes go elsewhere. Students who adopt that habit stop writing four-mark answers to two-mark questions, which is where their time was going.

The transfer is what makes this good value. The same command words appear across all three sciences, in mathematics, in economics and in geography, with the same meanings. One session with the published list and a set of past questions improves several subjects simultaneously. For a triple-science candidate in Culture Village it is the single best return per hour available, and it is almost never what a family asks for.

What does not differ is local availability of science specialists matched to a specific board and tier. A tutor advertising in one of these three districts is drawn from the same pool as one advertising in another, and none of the three has a concentration of people who have taught Pearson 4CH1 Higher to a June series. Rotate the three subjects across short weekday sessions, placing chemistry and physics in the earliest slot available and biology later, and put full timed papers on a weekend morning where they can be sat under proper conditions. In that session, ask the tutor how practical skills are assessed on your child's board. A specialist knows whether the answer is inside the written papers or through a separate arrangement, and a generalist will give you a general answer about laboratories.

If no specialist is free in your window we say so, give a realistic wait, and offer the nearest honest alternative rather than placing a general science tutor against a specific board and tier. Scarcity concentrates in Pearson sciences at Higher tier and in mock season and the final eight to twelve weeks, when every Dubai cohort reaches the same point at once. Booking before that cluster costs the same and secures a better match.

Two limits stated plainly, and the first of them is arithmetic a science family should run before buying anything. Nothing here implies tutoring is required for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression; on the British track the sourced rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science award my child is taking?
faqs.answer: Ask the exam office or look at the statement of entry. It will name the board and the codes, and the codes tell you the structure: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 are three separate sciences, 0654 is Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award, and 0653 is Combined Science as a single award. Pearson uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 separately plus a double award specification. The structure determines content depth, the number of grades and what a post-16 course will assume.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Combined Science and three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Content depth, grades produced and post-16 consequences. Combined Science covers all three sciences at reduced depth and produces one grade. Co-ordinated Sciences sits in the middle as a double award producing two grades. Three separate sciences cover each subject in full depth and produce three grades, leaving every post-16 route open including A Level and IB Higher Level sciences. A student on Combined Science heading for a post-16 science usually has a specific gap to close, and the school can name it.

A student who spends three weeks on biology, then three on chemistry, then three on physics arrives at the exam strong in physics and rusty in biology. A rotation schedule costs one planning session and is one of the few improvements a tutor can make to these awards without touching content at all.

faqs.question: How do Cambridge and Pearson differ for the IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: In how practical skills reach the mark scheme and in scheduling. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers, so apparatus choice, variable control and method evaluation are written questions. Cambridge's arrangements have varied across syllabus versions, so the current syllabus document is the only safe reference. Cambridge also allocates centres to one of six administrative zones with a timetable each, while Pearson publishes one international timetable per series.

faqs.question: Can online tuition cover practical skills in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: The assessed part of them, yes, and the limit is worth naming. A tutor over video has no apparatus and cannot run an experiment with your child. But for a Pearson candidate the practical marks sit inside the written papers: choosing apparatus, identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, describing a method another person could follow, explaining repeats, identifying anomalies and evaluating weaknesses. Those are writing tasks applied to science, and they respond quickly to drilling because they follow patterns.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences is genuinely hardest?
faqs.answer: They fail different students, so the useful question is what each punishes. Biology punishes imprecise terminology: the marking wants named structures and processes, so a student who understands deeply and writes loosely scores below their understanding. Chemistry punishes weak quantitative fluency, because moles arithmetic is used as a tool everywhere. Physics punishes weak representation: incomplete diagrams, missing labels, gradients without units. Three marked papers, one per science, answers it for your child in a week.

faqs.question: What does Extended tier add in the sciences that Core does not have?
faqs.answer: Real content rather than harder questions on the same material. In chemistry, Extended adds the quantitative treatment with moles arithmetic used across topics. In physics it adds more demanding calculation and a fuller treatment of electricity and forces. In biology it adds detail in genetics, transport systems and quantitative data handling. Core is capped below the top grades, so a Core candidate cannot be awarded them however well they perform, which matters if a post-16 science is the destination.

faqs.question: Can tutoring still change which science tier my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Within one narrow window: between the department's provisional indication and the final entry. Inside it, focused work on the specific Extended topics the department doubts can move the decision, because they are watching particular evidence rather than general effort. Outside it the ceiling is fixed and support becomes about maximising performance within a limit somebody else set. So ask the department what evidence would change their mind rather than whether they will reconsider.

faqs.question: Should a triple-science candidate buy support in all three subjects?
faqs.answer: Almost never at the start. Losses in a triple-science candidate are usually concentrated in a single subject rather than spread evenly, and three parallel arrangements cost three times as much to discover that. One marked timed paper in each of the three sciences costs three sessions and identifies where the marks are actually going. Often the answer is one subject plus a shared-skills block on practical questions, graphs and command words, which serves all three at once.

faqs.question: Which single block of work helps all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Practical-skills questions, graph and data handling, and command words. All three appear in every science paper and follow patterns that respond quickly to drilling: variable identification becomes automatic after about twenty questions, method descriptions improve once a student writes them as instructions rather than narration, and method evaluation improves with a checklist. Command words transfer further still, into mathematics, economics and geography, with the same meanings everywhere.

faqs.question: Why do science answers lose marks when the student clearly understands?
faqs.answer: Usually because the command word asked for an explanation and received a description. Describe wants what happens; explain wants why, in terms of a mechanism. The description is accurate, the understanding is present, and the marks are not awarded. The cheapest fix is a habit: underline the command word and the mark count before writing. Six marks and explain means a causal chain of roughly six linked statements; two marks and state means two facts, written quickly so the minutes go elsewhere.

intro.heading: Four comparisons, and the one that saves the most money
paragraphs: Science enquiries from DAMAC Hills nearly always arrive as a single request — science is going badly, three subjects are involved, help is needed — and nearly always need to be broken into four comparisons before anything is bought. Which route the school entered. Which board. Whether one tutor or three. And which of the three sciences is genuinely the problem rather than merely the loudest.

The fourth is the one that saves most. Where marks are falling in biology, chemistry and physics at once, the cause is frequently a single quantitative gap appearing three times: rearrangement, unit handling, significant figures, or data questions answered without specific figures. One block addresses that in one weekly session rather than three, which costs a third as much and moves marks on three papers.

The first comparison decides how much there is to cover. Three separate sciences gives three IGCSEs with the fullest content and the heaviest Year 11 workload in any subject combination. Cambridge Coordinated Science 0654 is a double award with less per discipline. Combined Science 0653 is a single award with the least. The school makes that entry, usually in Year 9 or early Year 10, and it has consequences at sixteen that are rarely explained at the time.

The second decides what the papers look like. Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 and Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 cover similar science and ask for it differently, including how practical skills are examined. A tutor matched to the subject rather than the code teaches correct material against unfamiliar question shapes, and in a mock report that reads as the student's carelessness.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In this community that matters practically: secondary students travel out to school and arrive home after five, so a session that starts on the minute and adds no journey is the version that survives a term.

The comparison families run instinctively — this community against the next, this provider against that one — turns out to matter least. Science tutor pools are not deeper in Arabian Ranches than in DAMAC Hills once lessons are online, and the only local variable is what time a tired Year 11 student can usefully sit down.

What follows is the four comparisons with the evidence attached, plus a comparison of the formats a family can actually buy and what each of them can reach. If money is limited, read the section on one tutor against three before anything else, because the twenty-minute test it describes can be run at a kitchen table and routinely turns a three-block plan into a one-block plan without changing the result.
