programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry and Physics entered as three separate IGCSEs, each with its own papers and grade. Cambridge tiers each into Core and Extended, with the Core route capping the grade available. Pearson runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 as the equivalent separate entries.
programmes.countryNote: Triple science is the standard route for students in this belt heading towards A Level or IB Higher Level sciences, and it produces the heaviest Year 11 workload of any combination. Requests from DAMAC Hills and the Ranches concentrate here and usually name one science rather than all three.

programmes.name: Coordinated Science, double award (Cambridge 0654)
programmes.description: A double award with more content than Combined and less than three separate sciences. Papers mix disciplines, so a question on energy may be followed by one on cells, and revision has to be organised around paper structure rather than around subject.
programmes.countryNote: A reasonable middle route for a student who needs science but not three full syllabuses, and frequently the better recommendation for a student struggling across all three. Progression to a post-16 science from this route should be confirmed with the receiving school in Year 10.

programmes.name: Combined Science, single award (Cambridge 0653)
programmes.description: A single award covering all three sciences with the least content per discipline. The lightest science workload available and the most constrained for progression, since entry to an A Level or Higher Level science from a single combined award is not automatic.
programmes.countryNote: Appropriate where a student is not continuing science at sixteen and the hours are needed by other subjects. The conversation to have in Year 10 is with the school a student intends to join at sixteen, because requirements are set by the receiving school rather than by the board.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-damac-hills.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the codes and the specific cause of lost marks in that subject, because the three sciences fail for three different reasons and that is the comparison that decides the first block.

subjects.name: Biology — Cambridge 0610, Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: Cells, transport, enzymes, nutrition, respiration, coordination, reproduction, inheritance and ecology. The heaviest content load of the three. Marks go to near-synonyms the scheme rejects and to data questions answered without quoting figures and units from the graph or table.

subjects.name: Chemistry — Cambridge 0620, Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Particles, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, electrolysis, the periodic table, organic chemistry and analysis. Three calculation families carry most of the numerical marks and the scheme pays for the layout of the working as much as for the answer.

subjects.name: Physics — Cambridge 0625, Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Motion, forces, energy, thermal physics, waves, electricity, magnetism and nuclear physics. Explanation questions want a chain of consequence in words, and beneath that sits rearrangement, where a large share of apparent physics difficulty actually originates.

subjects.name: Combined Science — Cambridge 0653
subjects.description: A single award across all three sciences with reduced content per discipline. The papers mix disciplines, which changes revision organisation entirely and catches out students who prepare one science to completion before starting the next.

subjects.name: Coordinated Science — Cambridge 0654
subjects.description: A double award sitting between Combined and three separate sciences. Long papers mixing disciplines, where revision organised by paper rather than by subject is not a preference but a requirement for finishing in time.

subjects.name: Practical assessment and the alternative route
subjects.description: Cambridge sciences carry a practical component with an alternative-to-practical option, and Pearson handles the same skills within its own structure. The examined skills are written: variable control, apparatus and precision choice, tabulation, anomalies and criticising a method.

subjects.name: Data and graph questions
subjects.description: Common to all three sciences and routinely under-prepared. Marks require figures quoted with units, trends described against specific values, and anomalies identified rather than ignored. A generic description of a rising line earns a fraction of a specific one.

subjects.name: Quantitative skills across the sciences
subjects.description: Rearrangement, ratio, percentages, standard form and significant figures, appearing identically in all three sciences and in mathematics. A student stalling at the same step in four subjects has one problem rather than four, which is the single most valuable diagnosis available.

subjects.name: Extended-response questions
subjects.description: Longer answers requiring a claim, the supporting science and a conclusion that answers the question asked. Students write everything they know about the topic instead, which rewards relevance rather than volume and leaves marks unclaimed.

subjects.name: Command terms in science papers
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest, compare, calculate and state are defined and enforced. 'Describe' answered with an explanation wastes time; 'explain' answered with a description earns nothing. Learning the handful that recur takes two weeks and pays in all three sciences.

sections.heading: What this search returns, and what is on offer
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in DAMAC Hills means one-to-one teaching in one or more of biology, chemistry and physics, arranged outside school for a student in the community. IB Gram provides that live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a DAMAC Hills address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, which is stated here rather than discovered later.

The first thing any provider should do with a science enquiry is refuse to treat science as one subject. The request has to be resolved into which science, which syllabus code and which tier before a sensible plan exists. The three subjects fail for different reasons, respond to different first interventions, and are marked by schemes with different habits, so a single tutor across all three will be strong in one and adequate in two.

The second thing is to look for the shared cause, because that is where the money is saved. Where a student is losing marks in all three sciences, the explanation is more often one quantitative skill gap appearing three times than three separate subject weaknesses. Rearrangement, unit handling, significant figures, or data questions answered without specific figures. Fixing that once pays in three subjects and costs a third of three blocks.

So what is on offer is a diagnosis first and a block second. A marked paper from each science, read together, usually shows the pattern inside one session. Where it is shared, the first purchase is a shared-skills block. Where it is genuinely subject-specific, the block is matched to the code and the tier, and where no specialist is free for that code the honest answer is a stated wait rather than a substitution.

sections.heading: Triple, double or single award: the workload comparison
paragraphs: The route comparison is usually framed as a question of ability and is better framed as a question of workload against return. Three separate sciences is the fullest content and the heaviest Year 11 timetable of any subject combination available. A double award is substantially lighter per discipline. A single combined award is lighter again and the most constrained at sixteen.

The return depends entirely on the post-16 intention. A student taking two sciences at A Level or IB Higher Level needs three at IGCSE where possible, because dropping one narrows options at exactly the wrong moment. A student taking no science at sixteen gains little from three full syllabuses and loses real hours that other subjects need. A student who does not yet know should keep options open and manage the load deliberately.

That middle case is where the honest recommendation most often differs from the commercial one. A student struggling across all three sciences but needing science at sixteen is frequently better served by a shared-skills block and a double award than by three thin separate entries. That advice costs a provider two subject blocks, which is a reasonable explanation for how rarely it is offered.

Timing is the constraint on all of it. Routes and tiers are fixed at the entry deadline, which sits months before the papers, so the conversation belongs in the first half of Year 10. The table compares the three routes on workload, progression and what to ask the school about each.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson for the sciences
paragraphs: Two schools a few minutes apart in this belt can enter the same science with different boards, and the differences affect preparation rather than difficulty. Content overlap is substantial. Question styles, tiering vocabulary and the handling of practical assessment are not, and a student drilled on one board's practical question style and entered for the other knows the science and misreads the task.

The first fact to establish is the code. Cambridge biology is 0610, chemistry 0620, physics 0625, with Combined 0653 and Coordinated 0654 for the non-separate routes. Pearson International GCSE uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The codes appear on the school's subject information sheet and at the top of every past paper, and they settle which board's papers and mark schemes should be used in practice.

The second is how practical skills are assessed, because that varies and it is examined every series. Cambridge sciences carry a practical component with an alternative-to-practical option whose question style is distinctive: which variable to control and why, which apparatus and to what precision, how to tabulate results with units in the headings, which point is anomalous, what is wrong with a described method. Pearson assesses the same skills within its own structure.

The third is what is provided on the paper, which changes what must be memorised and is stated in the current specification rather than in anybody's memory of how the paper used to look. The table compares the boards on the dimensions that affect preparation, with a note on what to check for the student's own cohort.

sections.heading: One tutor or three: the comparison most families get wrong
paragraphs: Faced with three sciences going badly, the instinct is to buy three tutors. It is almost always the wrong first move, for two reasons. The first is diagnostic: three subject blocks assume three subject problems, and the single most common finding is one quantitative gap appearing three times. The second is managerial: nobody reviews three blocks honestly, so three unreviewed blocks run to the end and the term disappears.

The diagnostic test is cheap and takes twenty minutes with no specialist knowledge. Ask the student to make a named quantity the subject of three formulae, convert units in two directions, and write two values in standard form. Watch for hesitation rather than wrong answers, because a student who arrives at the right result slowly in a quiet room will not arrive at it in a timed paper with six questions waiting.

Where that test shows a shared gap, the right first purchase is one weekly session on the shared skills: data and graph questions, command terms, units, rearrangement and significant figures. It is slower to show visible movement than topic teaching, which is why providers rarely propose it, and it is the only version that lifts three papers at once.

Where the test is clean and the losses really are confined to one science, buy that one and add a second only once the first has demonstrably moved. The arrangement used here is a specialist per syllabus on separate evenings, which also spreads the homework rather than landing two sets on a single night after a long commute.

sections.heading: Biology, chemistry or physics: which is hardest for your child
paragraphs: Parents often ask which science is hardest, and the honest answer is that it depends on what the student is good at rather than on the subjects themselves. Each rewards a different aptitude, and a student can be badly matched to one while comfortable in another with no difference in ability at all.

Biology rewards precise terminology and careful reading of data, and it carries the largest volume of content to retain. Chemistry rewards calculation discipline in a narrow set of forms plus a body of organic reactions that has to be known. Physics rewards algebraic fluency and the ability to explain a mechanism in words, and is comparatively light on memorisation.

So a student who recalls well and manipulates poorly will find biology least punishing and physics most, while one who manipulates comfortably and dislikes memorising will find the reverse. That is a statement about assessment shape rather than about intelligence, and it is useful because it predicts which science will respond fastest to a short block and which needs a longer one.

The table compares the three on what they reward, what they punish, and how quickly a block moves the mark. It is the comparison worth making before choosing which single science to support when the budget covers one, and it also informs the route decision in Year 10 for a student who may be able to drop one.

One practical use of the table deserves spelling out. Where a budget covers a single science block, the better choice is usually the subject whose first intervention is fastest rather than the subject with the lowest grade. A biology vocabulary block showing results in two or three weeks frees attention and confidence for the others, whereas starting with the slowest rebuild often means the term ends with one subject half-improved and two untouched.

sections.heading: Why the community comparison closes quickly
paragraphs: Families in DAMAC Hills comparing themselves with Arabian Ranches or Mudon for science support are comparing something that barely varies. Once lessons are delivered online, every community in this belt draws on the same pool of science tutors, and biology in particular has a deep pool everywhere. There is no neighbourhood advantage to find and no agency holds one either.

What does vary is the clock, and here it varies in one direction. Secondary students in DAMAC Hills generally travel out to Al Barsha, Jumeirah or the Ranches and arrive home after five, which rules out the late-afternoon slots available to families living next to their school. The adjustments are shorter sessions, two rather than one, and a weekend morning where a weekday evening keeps collapsing.

The second variable is which school the student attends, because that determines the route, the board, the tier and the mock window rather than the supply of tutors. Two students living on the same street in DAMAC Hills can sit different boards and different routes if they attend different schools, and their plans should differ even though their postcode does not.

There is one real exception. For a family that wants a tutor in the room, geography does matter, because the pool shrinks to people willing to drive to Dubailand at the hour the session would run. That is why published in-home rates in this part of Dubai sit above online ones, and it is the single scenario in which this address is a disadvantage relative to a community nearer the centre of the city.

sections.heading: Group class or one-to-one: what each reaches
paragraphs: Tuition centres in Dubai commonly offer group science classes and they are a legitimate product for a particular job. They cover content at a fixed pace with a fixed curriculum, which suits a student who has missed teaching or who needs the material presented a second time. They cost less per hour than one-to-one and the comparison deserves to be made fairly.

What a group class cannot do is match to a board, a tier or a student's specific error pattern, because the class is set before the student arrives. It cannot spend a session on one marked script. It cannot drill one student's recurring convention failure while others wait. For a student losing marks to a nameable mechanical habit, that is precisely the work required.

The honest division is therefore by diagnosis. Where the problem is missing content, a group class at a lower rate is a reasonable purchase. Where the problem is that the content is known and the marks are being lost to terminology, layout, units or command terms, one-to-one matched to the code is the only format that reaches it, whatever the relative cost per hour.

The table compares the formats on reach and on published rate together, because comparing them separately is how a family ends up paying a low rate for a job the format cannot do. All rates quoted name the provider that published them and the month they were read.

The option worth asking about first is the one that costs nothing. Many schools in this belt run after-hours science support or clinics, staffed by the department that set the mock and entered the student. Where it exists it is matched to the board and the tier by definition, and the only question is whether it has time for one student's error pattern. Asking before buying anything is a reasonable first step and a surprising number of families never do.

sections.heading: Entries, the two series and practical assessment
paragraphs: Two administrative facts bound every science plan in this belt, and both sit with the school. The first is the entry: which board, which route, which codes, which tier. The second is the entry deadline, which closes months before the papers and after which the route and tier are fixed for that series.

The second is the calendar, and the science-specific risk inside it is the sheer number of papers. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October for the years below. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a candidate sitting in the UAE plans around June and keeps November as the resit route, with no third date to move a weak subject to. A triple-award student then faces six science papers inside those few weeks, and their exact spacing is not a national fact: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. With six papers to arrange revision around, the wrong version is not a small error.

Pearson's calendar runs on its own labels, with Edexcel International GCSE sitting in May/June and November. Pearson issues provisional timetables ahead of each series and then a final one, and across three sciences that distinction is not pedantry, because the order in which the biology, chemistry and physics papers fall is what a twelve-week revision split is built on, and the provisional version moves. Plan from the live official timetable only. The published record gives the rest of the year its shape: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read as a planning tool, those tell you that a November entry decided in September leaves roughly eight teaching weeks, and that its grade does not land until the following term.

Practical assessment is the science-specific point. The laboratory is the school's work and no tutor replaces it in any format. What is examined is the written craft around practical work — variable control, apparatus and precision, tabulation with units in the headings, anomalies, criticising a described method — and all of that is drilled on screen using real past-paper data. Saying which half belongs to whom prevents a family paying for something no tutor can supply.

sections.heading: The regulator, the permit and the claims avoided
paragraphs: Everything that decides a science entry, from the board to the award route to whether practical work is assessed by paper or by coursework, is the school's to decide, and in DAMAC Hills the school answers to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Across the rest of the country the same function sits elsewhere: ADEK for Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority for Sharjah, a Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Two of those authorities reach further into a science department than KHDA does, because in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so a change of award route is an approval question there and a school decision here.

KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a triple-science student in Year 11 the effect is material: the examined subjects are not the whole timetable, so a revision plan drawn from the entry sheet assumes hours that are already committed elsewhere.

Underneath the school sits a second, smaller licence, and it belongs to the individual rather than the institution. A private science tutor in the UAE needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Hiring separately for biology, chemistry and physics means asking three people the same question, which is tedious and still cheaper than the alternative, since tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws and no fine schedule is published, so nobody can tell you what the exposure actually is. The categories eligible to hold one cover essentially every credible science tutor in this belt, including teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, which is why a missing permit says something about the tutor rather than about the rules.

IB Gram holds no Cambridge, Pearson, International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Specifications, past papers, mark schemes and examiner reports are linked at source rather than reproduced. No grade is promised, no rating is published, and no statistic appears without a sample size, a date and a method.

process.description: The target is measured in writing. If the categories in the log have not changed, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes at no cost. In a Year 11 science timetable, catching that at week four rather than week eight recovers a month.

whyPoints.description: Two shorter sessions rather than one long one, from 5.30pm or on a weekend morning, with the two sciences deliberately spaced across the week. Online delivery is what makes that pattern choosable rather than dictated by a tutor's driving route.

faqs.question: Should we buy one science tutor or three?
faqs.answer: One, in most cases, and often not for the subject that looks worst. Where marks are falling in biology, chemistry and physics at once, the cause is frequently a single quantitative gap appearing three times — rearrangement, unit handling, significant figures, or data questions answered without specific figures. A shared-skills block addresses that in one weekly session rather than three. Buying three tutors before diagnosing is how a term and a budget disappear at the same time.

faqs.question: Does a double award close off science at sixteen?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, but it depends on the receiving school rather than on the board. Coordinated Science 0654 as a double award is usually acceptable for post-16 science and a single Combined Science 0653 award is the most constrained, since entry to an A Level or Higher Level science from it is not automatic. The conversation to have in Year 10 is with the school your child intends to join at sixteen, because requirements are set there.

faqs.question: Is one science genuinely harder than the others?
faqs.answer: Not in the abstract; it depends on the student's aptitude. Biology rewards precise terminology and careful data reading with the largest content load. Chemistry rewards calculation discipline plus a body of organic reactions. Physics rewards algebraic fluency and causal explanation and is lightest on memorisation. A student who recalls well and manipulates poorly finds biology least punishing and physics most, which is about assessment shape rather than ability.

faqs.question: Can a science tutor come to DAMAC Hills?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors do, at published market rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel is counted. IB Gram does not: all UAE lessons are delivered live online, one to one, over video in Gulf Standard Time, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. In this community the online format also protects the evening, since the student has already made two journeys and a 5.30pm session starts at 5.30pm rather than whenever traffic allows.

faqs.question: How do I check whether the real problem is maths rather than science?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes, no specialist knowledge required. Ask the student to make a named quantity the subject of three formulae, convert units in two directions, and write two values in standard form. Watch for hesitation rather than for wrong answers, because a student who gets there slowly in a quiet room will not get there in a timed paper. Consistent hesitation means the first block should be quantitative, taught through science problems rather than abstract algebra.

faqs.question: Does a tuition centre group class work for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: For content that was missed and needs a second pass, at a lower rate per hour, it can be a reasonable purchase. For a student whose content is known and whose marks are being lost to terminology, calculation layout or command terms, it cannot help, because the class is set before the student arrives and cannot spend a session on one marked script. The format should be chosen by diagnosis rather than by price.

faqs.question: How are practical skills examined if we are tutored online?
faqs.answer: The examined skills are written: which variable to control and why, which apparatus and to what precision, how to tabulate results with units in the column headings, which point is anomalous, and what is wrong with a described method. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical route, and all those techniques are drilled on screen with real past-paper data. Handling apparatus in a school laboratory remains the school's part of the work and no tutor replaces it.

faqs.question: Is DAMAC Hills at a disadvantage for science tutors?
faqs.answer: Only if you want someone in the room, in which case the pool shrinks to people willing to drive to Dubailand at the hour a session would run, which is why published in-home rates here sit above online ones. For online tuition there is no disadvantage: every community in this belt draws on the same pool, and biology in particular is deep everywhere. What differs locally is the arrival time home and therefore the session pattern.

faqs.question: Which board's past papers should we use?
faqs.answer: Only the board the student is actually entered for, identified by the code at the top of a past paper or on the school's subject information sheet. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625; Pearson uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The archives are large enough that there is no reason to borrow, and practising the other board's practical question style in particular teaches a technique that will not be examined.

faqs.question: What is the single fastest mark recovery across the three sciences?
faqs.answer: Command terms, because they appear in all three subjects and are defined and enforced in marking. 'Describe' answered with an explanation wastes time needed elsewhere; 'explain' answered with a description earns nothing; 'suggest' invites a reasoned possibility rather than a recalled fact. Learning the handful that recur in a student's own papers takes about two weeks and pays in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously, which few single interventions do.

faqs.question: Should a struggling triple-science student drop to a double award?
faqs.answer: If science is needed at sixteen but three separate grades are not, frequently yes, and the recommendation is unpopular with providers because it removes two subject blocks from the invoice. Three thin entries prepared badly serve a student less well than two solid ones. The constraint is timing: routes and tiers are fixed at the entry deadline months before the papers, so the conversation belongs in the first half of Year 10.

faqs.question: What does supporting two sciences cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour at the university-student end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, to AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour sessions are AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more by tier. Multiply before committing.

faqs.question: Can two sciences be tutored on the same evening?
faqs.answer: They can and it is usually a mistake, especially for a student arriving home after five. Two sets of homework landing on one night tends to mean one of them is done badly, and the second session of an evening gets the tired half of a student's attention. The arrangement used here is a specialist per syllabus on separate evenings, which spreads both the teaching and the work the student has to do between sessions.

faqs.question: When do entries and tiers get fixed for the sciences?
faqs.answer: At the school's entry deadline, which sits months before the papers and after which the board, the route and the tier are fixed for that series. Where a Cambridge science is tiered, a Core entry caps the grade available however the revision goes. Ask the school when entries close, during Year 10 rather than Year 11, because a tier conversation held before that date is a decision and one held afterwards is a complaint.

intro.heading: Does anybody near DAMAC Hills 2 know your child's science entry?
paragraphs: The honest answer is that general science tutors are reasonably available out here and entry-specific ones are not, and that distinction is the whole point. Parents searching for an IGCSE science tutor in DAMAC Hills 2 are usually not worried about finding somebody who can explain photosynthesis. They are worried about hiring somebody who will teach broadly correct science while missing that the school entered coordinated sciences rather than three separate subjects, and that the paper looks nothing like what is being practised.

Because science is three or four different purchases depending on the entry. A triple-award student sits Biology, Chemistry and Physics as separate qualifications and receives three grades — Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. A coordinated-sciences student covers all three disciplines in a single qualification and receives one or two grades, with reduced content in each. A double-award student sits a combined qualification worth two grades. The topics overlap. The depth, the paper structure and the grade outcome do not.

Add the board question on top. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers for the same subject, tier differently, and assess practical work by different routes. Dubai schools are not obliged to use one board across the curriculum and plenty do not, so a household can have maths on Pearson and sciences on Cambridge without anybody mentioning it. One email to the school office returns all of it: the entry route, the board, and the syllabus code per subject.

The geography is the other half of the problem. DAMAC Hills 2 sits out along the Al Qudra corridor, in a belt of newer villa communities where the residential build-out ran well ahead of the professional tutoring supply. Dubai's tutors cluster near the older school districts. A tutor prepared to drive out here on a weekday evening is a smaller group than a tutor prepared to work in Al Barsha, and once you require the correct entry, board and subject, that group can empty.

IB Gram's response is not to find somebody closer. Lessons for DAMAC Hills 2 families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and we make no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. The pool is therefore defined by which specification a tutor teaches, which is the variable the grade depends on, rather than by who is willing to drive down Al Qudra Road at six.

KHDA reported 387,441 pupils across Dubai's 227 private schools in 2024-25, with UK-curriculum schools at 37% of enrolment, the largest single bloc. That is an enormous IGCSE science cohort, which explains why the market is full of general science tutors advertising to it, and why so few of them will tell you which entry and code they teach. Ask. A specialist answers in one sentence.

subjects.name: Biology, separate science

subjects.name: Chemistry, separate science
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry are the wall. Students who can balance an equation still lose marks converting between mass, moles and volume against a clock. Qualitative analysis and the required ion tests are heavily examined and quick to secure once named.

subjects.description: All three disciplines in one qualification with reduced content in each, awarding two grades. A tutor who teaches separate-science depth to a coordinated student wastes time on content that will not be examined, which is a specific and common mismatch.

sections.heading: Triple, double or coordinated? The entry decides what you are buying
paragraphs: This is the first question and most parents cannot answer it, partly because schools describe it loosely and partly because the timetable looks similar whichever route is taken. A student may have three science teachers and three sets of lessons and still be entered for a single coordinated qualification.

The three routes diverge in content depth and in grade outcome. Separate sciences, the triple-award route, means Biology, Chemistry and Physics as independent qualifications with three grades — Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 — each covering its full syllabus. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines in one double-award qualification with reduced content in each, awarding two grades. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 is a single-award version at further reduced depth, giving one grade.

The mismatch this creates is concrete and expensive. A tutor who assumes triple award and teaches separate-science depth to a coordinated student spends sessions on content that will not be examined. A tutor who assumes coordinated and teaches reduced depth to a triple-award student leaves the top of each syllabus uncovered. Both scenarios look fine week to week and neither is visible until a paper arrives.

The entry also has a consequence beyond Year 11 that families frequently discover too late. A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences generally expect separate-science grades at a good standard, and the coordinated route can narrow which post-16 options are straightforwardly available. If a chemistry-requiring or physics-requiring degree is anywhere in view, the entry decision in Year 9 or Year 10 matters more than any single grade.

sections.heading: Three syllabus codes, three different papers
paragraphs: Once the entry is established, the board and code question follows, and it is the one that most often goes unasked. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers for the same subject. Content overlaps heavily. Paper structure, formula provision, practical assessment route and the command-term vocabulary each board favours do not.

What this means practically is that past papers are not interchangeable. A term of Cambridge 0625 physics practice for a student entered on Pearson 4PH1 teaches real and correct physics while training the wrong instincts about what a question is asking for and how much to write. It is invisible until the real paper arrives, which is why it is one of the more expensive mistakes in this market and one of the easiest to prevent.

Dubai schools also mix boards across departments. A household can have maths on Pearson and sciences on Cambridge, or biology on one board and physics on another where departments made independent decisions. The school office will confirm all of it in one email, per subject. Bring those codes to any tutoring conversation and refuse to hire anyone who cannot say immediately which specification they teach.

One further difference worth knowing: Pearson offers modular assessment in some subjects, which changes when a result can be banked and therefore changes the whole planning picture compared with a single terminal series. If your child is on a modular route, that is a fact worth building a plan around rather than discovering mid-year.

sections.heading: The Alternative to Practical paper, and why it is undervalued
paragraphs: For many Cambridge science entries the assessed practical route is a written Alternative to Practical paper rather than laboratory assessment, and it is reliably where students lose the most marks relative to effort spent. Three things conspire: it is taught last, it is a different skill from content revision, and parents have usually never heard of it.

What it actually tests is experimental understanding on paper. Reading a measuring instrument to a sensible precision. Spotting that a described method cannot answer the question it was set. Identifying which variable needed controlling and was not. Constructing a results table with correct headings and units. Plotting points, drawing a line of best fit, reading a value from the graph and saying what it means. Judging whether a conclusion is supported by the data presented.

Every one of those is a paper-and-screen skill, which has two useful consequences. First, it responds very well to one-to-one online work, because the whole task is a document being marked and discussed. Second, it transfers across all three sciences simultaneously — the same reasoning earns marks in biology, chemistry and physics — which makes it the single most efficient thing a triple-award family can buy.

Where a school runs assessed laboratory work instead, bench technique happens at school and no tutor substitutes for it. What one-to-one work adds there is the surrounding reasoning: predicting the expected result, handling an anomaly, simple uncertainty treatment, and writing up to the expected standard. Ask the school which route each science is entered for, because the answer changes what is worth preparing.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one week: how to divide the tutoring
paragraphs: This is the practical problem a triple-award family in DAMAC Hills 2 actually faces, and the market's answer — three tutors, three sessions — is almost always the wrong one. Three weekly sessions plus a long school run plus the homework three sciences generate leaves a student with no independent study time, and independent practice is where science grades are made.

The better approach has two parts. First, buy the shared skills once. Scientific calculation and rearrangement, command-term discipline, data handling and the Alternative to Practical reasoning are examined identically across biology, chemistry and physics. A six-to-ten session block on those improves three grades, and it is the cheapest intervention available to a three-science household.

Second, after the diagnostic, pick one subject for weekly work — the one with the most movement available per hour, which is often not the subject the student complains about most. Students usually name the subject they dislike; the diagnostic frequently finds that the recoverable marks sit elsewhere, in the subject where the content is nearly there and the technique is not.

What we will not do is sell three weekly sessions to a family who would be better served by one plus a shared-skills block. That is a smaller sale and it is the honest recommendation in most three-science cases. sections.heading: The June series, the November route, and the series UAE candidates do not sit
paragraphs: One correction first, because it circulates among UAE parents constantly and acting on it costs a term. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. If anybody has told you a March resit is available for your child, they are describing another country's provision.

Cambridge runs International GCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school which zone it sits in rather than downloading a timetable from a search result.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For how a November route times out in practice: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results reach students in January — the November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so work from the live official PDF rather than any date restated on a tutoring site.

For a three-science family the November route is genuinely useful rather than a consolation. A student who did well in two sciences and poorly in one can re-enter that single subject, work a narrow fixed-scope block over the summer and first term, and have a January result in time to update post-16 applications. That is a better plan than trying to lift three grades at once in the spring of Year 11.

sections.heading: Is the science tutor you hire permitted to teach in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is a permitted activity, and most parents have never been told. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, is issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service is Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services with a stated two-working-day completion time.

Because it costs nothing and takes two working days, there is no legitimate reason for a tutor not to hold one. Eligibility is wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, and Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify amounts, so disregard any figure circulating informally.

The permit's code of conduct bars a tutor from serving students affiliated with their own school, and press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules describes the same prohibition for Abu Dhabi school staff. A provider offering you your child's own science teacher privately is telling you something about itself.

An individual needs the MoHRE permit; an organisation running tutoring from premises in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership, claims none, and has no UAE office or centre.

sections.heading: What we will not tell you about science grades
paragraphs: No guarantee of a grade, a tier change or an improvement in any of the three sciences. The variables are not under a tutor's control, and in a market where several ranking pages do offer guarantees, declining is information rather than modesty.

No statistics without a sample size, a date and a method, which in practice means no statistics at all. No average science grades achieved by students we have taught, no percentage improved, no satisfaction figure, no self-generated star rating. Competitors publish such numbers routinely, sometimes in two conflicting versions on the same page, and almost never state how any of them was produced.

No awarding-body material hosted. Past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson; we cite and link them rather than supplying them as downloads. No description of tutors as examiners either, because current examiner status is not something we can evidence, and examiner status gives nobody access to marking or boundaries whatever is implied.

And no home visits anywhere in the UAE at any price, because there is no UAE visiting service to buy. What we will do instead is diagnose which of the three sciences has the most movement available, recommend the shared-skills block where it is the better value, and tell you when three grades cannot all be lifted in the time remaining. That verdict is sometimes unwelcome and it is always more useful than a plan built to be agreeable.

One more omission. We publish no specific exam dates beyond naming the series, because awarding bodies revise timetables and a date restated on a tutoring page is the version a family should trust least. Cambridge and Pearson both publish live official timetables, your school knows its Cambridge administrative zone, and those are the sources worth acting on.

faqs.question: How do I find out which science entry my child is on?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office directly, because the timetable does not tell you: a student can have three science teachers and still be entered for a single coordinated qualification. You want the entry route — separate sciences, Coordinated Sciences 0654 or Combined Science 0653 — plus the board and the syllabus code for each subject. It matters because the content depth and grade count differ, and because a tutor teaching separate-science depth to a coordinated student spends sessions on material that will not be examined.

faqs.question: What is the difference between triple award and coordinated sciences?
faqs.answer: Triple award means biology, chemistry and physics as three independent qualifications covering their full syllabuses, awarding three grades — Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines in one double-award qualification with reduced content in each, awarding two grades. Combined Science 0653 is a single-award version at further reduced depth. The topics overlap but the depth, paper structure and grade outcome do not, and the entry also affects which post-16 science routes are straightforwardly available.

faqs.question: Does coordinated science limit A Level or IB options later?
faqs.answer: It can, and this is the consequence families most often learn late. A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences generally expect separate-science grades at a good standard, so the coordinated route can narrow which post-16 options are straightforwardly open. Check the published entry requirements of the schools and programmes your child may move into, rather than relying on general advice. If a chemistry-requiring or physics-requiring degree is anywhere in view, the entry decision in Year 9 or Year 10 matters more than any single grade does.

faqs.question: Which science syllabus codes should I ask the school for?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge separate sciences: 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics. For Cambridge combined routes: 0654 Coordinated Sciences double award or 0653 Combined Science single award. For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE: 4BI1 Biology, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4PH1 Physics. Ask per subject rather than assuming one answer covers everything, because Dubai departments make independent board decisions and a household can genuinely have biology on one board and physics on another. Bring the codes to any tutoring conversation.

faqs.question: What is the Alternative to Practical paper and why does it matter?
faqs.answer: For many Cambridge science entries it is the assessed practical route: a written paper testing experimental understanding rather than bench work. It asks a student to read instruments to sensible precision, spot that a method cannot answer its question, identify an uncontrolled variable, build a results table with correct headings and units, plot and interpret a graph, and judge whether a conclusion is supported. It is taught last in most schools, it is where students lose most marks relative to effort, and the same reasoning earns marks in all three sciences.

faqs.question: Should we hire three tutors for triple-award science?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Three weekly sessions plus the homework three sciences generate plus a long DAMAC Hills 2 school run leaves no independent study time, and independent practice is where science grades are made. The better sequence is a shared-skills block first — scientific calculation and rearrangement, command terms, data handling, practical reasoning, all examined identically across the three — then one science weekly, chosen by diagnostic. At published mid-band rates, three separate weekly tutors runs to AED 1,800-3,600 a month.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences should we tutor first?
faqs.answer: The one with the most movement available per hour, which is frequently not the one the student complains about. Students name the subject they dislike; a diagnostic often finds the recoverable marks sit elsewhere, in the science where the content is nearly there and only the technique is missing. That is why we test all three at the correct entry level before recommending anything, and why a plan built from a school report rather than from marked questions tends to start in the wrong place.

faqs.question: Is scientific calculation really the problem across all three sciences?
faqs.answer: Very often, and it is the most efficient thing to fix because one block improves three grades. Rearranging a formula with the unknown in the denominator, carrying units through a multi-step calculation, standard form at speed, and percentage work appear in chemistry stoichiometry, physics formulae and biology data questions alike. Students name a topic; the diagnostic finds this underneath it. Along with command-term discipline and practical-paper reasoning, it is the shared layer that a three-science household should buy once rather than three times.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if our lessons are online?
faqs.answer: It depends on the entry, so ask the school. Where the assessed route is a written Alternative to Practical paper, the whole task is a document to be marked and discussed, which is exactly what one-to-one screen work does well — and it is where the most marks are available. Where a school runs assessed laboratory work, bench technique happens at school and no tutor substitutes for it, in person or online. What one-to-one work adds there is prediction, anomaly handling, simple uncertainty treatment and writing up to the expected standard.

faqs.question: Is there a science tutor near DAMAC Hills 2 who knows our entry?
faqs.answer: General science tutors are reasonably available out here; entry-specific ones at Year 11 level are not. Dubai's tutor supply clusters around the older school corridors rather than the newer Dubailand communities, so the group willing to drive down Al Qudra Road on a school night is small, and smaller again once you require the correct entry route, the correct board and the correct subject. Online matching removes the proximity filter, which was never the variable the grade depended on.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor visit our home in DAMAC Hills 2?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram delivers IGCSE science tuition to DAMAC Hills 2 one-to-one over live video and makes no home visits anywhere in the UAE — in-home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Other Dubai providers do visit, at published rates of AED 180-500 an hour including travel, and from this corridor a real share of that is driving. For three sciences the in-home model is rarely attempted anyway, because the weekly cost and the travel time compound across subjects.

faqs.question: What should a three-science family in DAMAC Hills 2 expect to spend?
faqs.answer: At published Dubai rates read in October 2026, one weekly hour runs AED 240-600 a month at the budget band, AED 600-1,200 mid-tier and AED 1,000-2,000 or more at the specialist exam-year band. Multiply by three for three separate weekly tutors: AED 720-1,800, AED 1,800-3,600 and AED 3,000-6,000 or more respectively. Those are the providers' published figures, not ours. The reason we recommend a shared-skills block plus one weekly subject is that it is cheaper and, in most cases, more effective.

faqs.question: Can my child resit one science in the February or March series?
faqs.answer: Not in the UAE. Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, and UAE candidates sit the June and November series. The belief circulates widely here and planning around it costs a term, so confirm with your school. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. For a three-science family the November route is genuinely useful: re-enter the single weak subject, work a narrow fixed-scope block over the summer and first term, and have a January result in time for post-16 applications.

faqs.question: Does our science tutor need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Any individual charging for private tuition in the UAE needs a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE listing a two-working-day completion time through its smart app, website or e-services. Eligibility covers school and sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. Since it costs nothing and takes two days, there is no legitimate reason to lack one. Ask to see it and verify with MoHRE.

faqs.question: My child is weak in all three sciences with mocks done. What now?
faqs.answer: Triage, honestly. Three grades cannot all be lifted substantially in a final term, and a provider implying otherwise is selling. After a diagnostic we would normally propose the shared-skills layer — calculation, command terms, practical-paper reasoning — because it touches all three at once, plus focused weekly work on whichever single science shows the most movement per hour. For another subject, a November entry with a narrow block over the summer is frequently the better outcome than a diluted spring.

intro.heading: The comparison that decides what a tutor should teach
paragraphs: Parents in Deira ask for an IGCSE science tutor and are usually surprised to be asked which science and which award. It is not pedantry. A student entered for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences sits a different syllabus from one entered for Physics, Chemistry and Biology separately, with narrower content and a different set of papers, and a tutor revising separate-science material with a Co-ordinated candidate will spend weeks on topics that will never appear. That error is common, expensive and entirely preventable by one question to the school.

There are three entry patterns in Dubai schools. The separate sciences, where a student takes Physics, Chemistry and Biology as three qualifications with three sets of papers — Cambridge codes 0625, 0620 and 0610, or Pearson 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The double award, where all three sciences are covered in one qualification worth two grades, which is Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences or Pearson's double award equivalent. And the single combined award, Cambridge 0653, covering all three in one qualification worth one grade. Larger schools, including several in the Al Qusais cluster near Deira, run two of these patterns side by side in the same year group.

The second comparison is practical assessment, which differs by board as well as by award. Cambridge sciences carry a separate practical component, sat either as a practical test or as an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which of the two a school enters for is a school decision a parent can simply ask about. Pearson assesses practical skills within the written papers rather than through a separate component. Revision material for one is not revision material for the other, and the alternative-to-practical paper in particular has a question style that repeats across series and is therefore unusually learnable.

The third comparison is consequence. Three separate sciences keeps the widest set of post-16 options open, including A Level or Diploma sciences in all three subjects. A double award keeps most of them open. A single combined award narrows them, and a family should know that before Year 10 rather than after results. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track the requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, so how the sciences count towards that five is worth establishing with the school.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For science there is an honest limit worth stating at the outset: we teach theory, calculations, written explanation and data analysis, and we cannot handle apparatus for your child. Laboratory work belongs to the school. What tutoring adds is making a student's practical experience earn marks on paper.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-deira.subjectsIntro: Below are the content areas across the three sciences, with a note on what each demands in writing. Which of them are on your child's paper depends entirely on the award code, which is why that comes first.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits and electrical power. The topic with the widest gap between confidence and marks, because students can recite relationships and then cannot reason about what happens to the rest of a circuit when one component changes.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and energy
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, graphs of motion, Newton's laws, moments, work, power and energy transfers. Graph interpretation carries real marks: students read values correctly and fail to say what a gradient or an area under a line represents.

subjects.name: Physics: waves, thermal and magnetism
subjects.levels: All awards; more in the separate entry
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum, specific heat capacity and electromagnetic induction. Explanation questions here reward a sequence of cause and effect, and students who write a definition instead of a mechanism lose the marks.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and quantitative work
subjects.description: Relative masses, the mole, reacting masses, concentration and titration calculations. Marks go missing on units and rounding rather than on chemistry, and on answers given without working that would otherwise have earned method credit.

subjects.name: Chemistry: bonding, structure and the periodic table
subjects.description: Ionic, covalent and metallic bonding, giant structures and periodic trends. The written failure is naming a general force rather than the specific interaction, and giving a trend without the reason the mark scheme wants alongside it.

subjects.name: Chemistry: acids, redox, electrolysis and organic
subjects.levels: All awards; organic deeper in the separate entry
subjects.description: Acid reactions, oxidation and reduction, electrolysis products and the basics of organic families. Electrolysis questions require products at both electrodes with a reason, and half-equations where the tier demands them.

subjects.name: Biology: cells, transport and enzymes
subjects.description: Cell structure, diffusion, osmosis, active transport and enzyme action. Osmosis questions are a reliable mark loss because students describe water moving to where there is more of something rather than using water potential language correctly.

subjects.name: Biology: human physiology and plant processes
subjects.description: Digestion, circulation, breathing, excretion, photosynthesis and transpiration. Content-heavy and highly improvable in a short block, because the marks sit in using the exact term the scheme requires rather than in conceptual understanding.

subjects.name: Biology: inheritance, variation and ecology
subjects.description: Genetic crosses, variation, natural selection, food webs and nutrient cycles. Genetic cross questions reward a correctly laid out diagram with gametes shown, and students who work it mentally lose the method marks.

subjects.name: Practical and data-handling skills
subjects.levels: All awards, assessed differently by board
subjects.description: Variables, apparatus selection, tabulation, graph plotting, anomalies and sources of error. In Cambridge this is a separate component sat as a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper; in Pearson it is assessed inside the written papers. Either way the question types repeat across series and are learnable.

sections.heading: Separate sciences, double award or single award
paragraphs: This is the comparison that determines what a tutor should be teaching, and the one families most often cannot answer. Three entry patterns exist in Dubai schools and they are genuinely different qualifications rather than three difficulty settings of one.

The separate sciences give three grades from three syllabuses with the fullest content in each discipline, and occupy three timetable blocks. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences, code 0654, gives two grades from one syllabus covering all three sciences with narrower content in each, in two timetable blocks. Cambridge Combined Science, 0653, gives one grade from the narrowest content of all. Pearson's double award equivalent works like 0654 in structure while differing in paper style. All of the Cambridge options are tiered into Core and Extended.

The point that costs families money is that narrower content means different papers, not easier versions of the same papers. A 0654 candidate revising from separate-science resources will study topics that cannot appear on their paper while possibly missing the specific emphasis their own syllabus places on others. The standard of written explanation expected does not drop with the content, so a student on a double award still has to name the specific interaction, give the trend with its reason, and explain a mechanism rather than define a term.

What a parent should do takes two minutes. Ask the school for the award code and the tier for science, in writing. Then give that code to any tutor before the first session and ask them whether they have taught it. A tutor who says they teach all the sciences at all levels has not answered the question.

sections.heading: Comparing the practical assessment routes
paragraphs: Practical assessment is where the two boards diverge most sharply, and where a Deira family in an apartment with no laboratory has the most to gain from understanding the difference. It is also the most learnable part of the whole science entry.

Cambridge sciences carry a separate practical component, and a school enters candidates either for a practical test, sat in the laboratory under examination conditions, or for an alternative-to-practical written paper that tests the same skills on paper. Which one your child sits is a school decision, and it is the single most useful thing to ask about, because the preparation differs completely. The alternative-to-practical paper asks about apparatus choice, variables, tabulation, plotting, anomalies and improvements, and those question types repeat across series with remarkable consistency, which makes them drillable in a way content questions are not.

Pearson does not use a separate practical component in its International GCSE sciences; practical skills are assessed within the written papers through questions about method, data and evaluation. The skills tested are similar, the context in which they appear is not, and revision material designed for a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper is not the right preparation for a Pearson paper, nor the reverse.

Two consequences follow. First, a practical-skills block is one of the best-value purchases in IGCSE science for either board, because the material is narrow and repetitive and most students have never practised it deliberately. Second, this is work that can be done entirely online: variables, tabulation, graph plotting and error analysis need paper and data rather than apparatus. What no tutoring can supply is the laboratory experience itself, which belongs to the school.

sections.heading: Comparing the three sciences on where each is hard
paragraphs: Families often ask which science their child should be tutored in and expect the answer to be the one with the lowest grade. A better question is which one is hard in a way that tutoring can fix quickly, because the three sciences fail differently and respond to different work.

Physics is hard because it requires reasoning rather than recall. A student can know every relationship in electricity and still be unable to say what happens to the current elsewhere in a circuit when one resistance changes. The marks sit in explanation sequences and in interpreting graphs — what a gradient represents, what an area under a line means. That is teachable, and it transfers across topics, which makes physics a good target for a single term of weekly work.

Chemistry is hard because of precision. The content volume is manageable and the mark schemes are unforgiving: a named interaction rather than a general force, a trend with its reason, a correct sign, products at both electrodes with a justification, units and sensible rounding on every calculation. A chemistry grade often moves faster than a parent expects once presentation is fixed, because the underlying understanding was already there.

Biology is hard because of volume and terminology. There is more to know than in the other two and the marks turn on using the exact term the scheme requires — water potential rather than more water, active transport rather than movement. It is the most improvable of the three in a short block before an examination, which is why a late intervention in biology is more defensible than a late intervention in physics. The table sets the three side by side.

sections.heading: What each route lets your child do at 16
paragraphs: The consequence comparison is the one families make last and should make first, because the science entry is decided in Year 9 or early Year 10 and is difficult to change afterwards. A Deira student's post-16 options sit either at an A Level school in Al Qusais or Bur Dubai or at an IB Diploma school across the Creek in Al Garhoud or Dubai Festival City, and both have expectations about the science entry behind an application.

Three separate sciences keeps everything open: A Level or Diploma sciences in any of the three, including the Higher Level Chemistry that medicine, dentistry and pharmacy applications generally expect. A double award keeps most routes open, and schools will often accept it for one or two post-16 sciences, though a student arrives with less content behind them and the first term is harder. A single combined award narrows the field considerably and can close post-16 science entirely at some schools.

Nobody should read that as an instruction to take three separate sciences. Three sciences occupy three timetable blocks in a Dubai week that also carries mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies lessons, and a student struggling across three is worse placed than one doing well on a double award. The right comparison is between a student's realistic capacity and their realistic plans, made honestly with the school in Year 9.

One further point on equivalency. For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. How a double or combined award counts towards the five is a question for the school and, ultimately, for the Ministry; verify it on moe.gov.ae rather than relying on any tutoring website, including this one.

sections.heading: Comparing the cost of supporting one science against three
paragraphs: This is where the comparison becomes a budget. A student taking three separate sciences has three times the content and three sets of papers, and a family's instinct is to support all three. The arithmetic and the week both say otherwise.

Published Dubai rates, read in October 2026 and attributed: budget online generalists advertise from AED 33 to 52 an hour at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik; qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150; specialists are quoted AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's Dubai rate table in the same range; in-home one-to-one runs AED 180 to 350 per Bestimate and up to AED 500 for independent home tutors. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year work.

Run those against a twelve-week term. One science supported weekly at the qualified band is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600. Three sciences supported weekly at the same band is roughly AED 5,400 to 10,800, and requires three evenings a week that a Dubai Year 11 student does not have alongside eight or nine other subjects. The alternative shape — one science weekly, a practical-skills block covering all three, and fortnightly weekend timed papers — costs closer to the single-science figure and addresses all three entries, because practical skills and written-explanation discipline transfer across the sciences in a way content does not.

That is the genuinely useful finding on this page for a family with three science entries. Buy the transferable things once rather than the content three times. These are market figures rather than IB Gram's prices; we quote after a free trial lesson against a written plan with a term total.

sections.heading: Comparing what a good science session contains
paragraphs: Two science tutors charging the same rate can deliver very different hours, and the difference is visible to a parent who knows what to look for. This comparison is worth running during a free trial.

A weaker session looks like a lesson: the tutor explains a topic, the student listens, worked examples appear on screen, and everybody leaves feeling the hour was productive. Nothing in that sequence tests whether the student can produce a creditable written answer, which is the only thing the examination measures. The student will report that the tutor explained it well, and the next marked paper will look the same as the last one.

A stronger session is mostly the student working. They attempt a question in writing, the tutor watches the answer appear and stops them at the point where the mark would be lost, and then the answer is marked aloud against the scheme with the specific credited phrase named. Over an hour that might cover three or four questions rather than a topic, and it produces one nameable behaviour to change. Ask your child afterwards what the session asked them to do differently; if there is no answer, it was a lesson rather than a correction.

Two further things to compare. Whether the tutor uses past papers from the correct award code and board, which you can check by asking to see the paper used. And whether written work is marked against the official scheme or simply checked for right answers, which is the difference between discovering that a method mark was missing and discovering that the final number was wrong.

sections.heading: Why the award code decides the revision material
paragraphs: This section exists because the mistake it describes is the most common and most wasteful one in IGCSE science tutoring, and it is made with good intentions by competent tutors who were never told the award code.

Revision resources are written for specific syllabuses. A guide aimed at Cambridge 0620 Chemistry covers organic chemistry, moles and electrolysis at a depth that a 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences candidate will not meet. A 0653 Combined Science candidate's content is narrower again. Work through the wrong guide and a student spends weeks on material that cannot be examined while the specific emphases of their own syllabus go unpractised — and then performs worse than their effort deserved, which damages confidence as well as the grade.

The same applies across boards. Pearson papers distribute marks across fewer, longer questions than Cambridge papers, and Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate component. A student drilling a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper in preparation for a Pearson entry is practising a paper that does not exist on their timetable.

The fix is one email to the school asking for the award code, the tier and the practical route for science, and then handing that information to any tutor before the first session. Ask the tutor to name the papers your child will sit on that code. If they can, the hour will be spent on the right material; if they cannot, no amount of teaching skill will put that right.

sections.heading: What a Deira address changes for science specifically
paragraphs: Most of what this page compares is independent of where a family lives, but two things are specific to this district and worth naming.

The first is that there is no laboratory at home, anywhere, and in dense apartment housing there is not even a kitchen table free for a demonstration. That sounds like a disadvantage and is mostly a clarification: the laboratory part of IGCSE science is the school's job under any arrangement, in a villa or a flat, and no in-home tutor arriving in Deira is bringing apparatus either. What a family can do at home is the data-handling, tabulation, plotting and error-analysis work that the practical component actually examines on paper, and that needs nothing but a desk and a printed data set.

The second is the quiet hour. Students travel out of Deira to school in Al Qusais, Bur Dubai or across the water, arriving home late and variably, and in a full flat the hour when a room is free moves from day to day. A session set to a fixed arrival estimate fails; one set from the real arrival, or moved to a Friday or Saturday morning, holds. This is also why a weekend timed-paper session works well here: a complete science paper takes well over an hour with marking, which is unrealistic on a school evening and straightforward on a quiet morning.

Ask the school about supervised study rooms as well. Most Dubai secondaries run them after hours free of charge and they are badly under-used, and for a student whose obstacle is space rather than teaching they are worth more than an additional paid session. The Metro running through Deira makes them reachable independently, which is a genuine advantage this district has over the villa suburbs.

sections.heading: Why the delivery answer is the same across all three entries
paragraphs: Having compared the entry patterns, the practical routes, the three sciences and the costs, it is worth noting what none of those comparisons changed.

Whatever the award code, the requirement is a tutor who has taught that code and can mark a written answer against the scheme. That is a supply problem rather than a geography problem: specialist supply in Dubai is thin and distributed by where tutors live, and a radius around Deira is a poor filter for a syllabus code. Matching from the whole available pool is what makes it possible to say yes to a 0654 Extended request one week and a 4PH1 request the next.

Whatever the award code, the session has to happen at an hour the student is genuinely available in a quiet room, which in this district varies day to day. And whatever the award code, the working surface needs to show the question, the student's written answer and the correction together, with the previous week's work retrievable — which a shared whiteboard does and a single sheet of paper does not.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The honest limit is apparatus, which belongs to the school under any arrangement. Everything else in IGCSE science — theory, calculations, written explanation, data analysis and the whole of the practical-skills component as it is examined on paper — is work that an online one-to-one hour does at least as well as any other format, and from a far larger pool of people who have actually taught the code on your child's entry form.
