faqs.question: Is Co-ordinated Sciences easier than taking three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: It is narrower, which is not the same as easier. Cambridge 0654 covers all three sciences in one syllabus producing two grades, with less content in each discipline than 0625, 0620 and 0610 carry, but the standard of written explanation expected does not drop. A 0654 candidate still has to name the specific interaction, give a trend with its reason and explain a mechanism rather than define a term. It occupies two timetable blocks instead of three, which is usually the real reason a school recommends it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between 0654 and 0653?
faqs.answer: Both cover all three sciences in a single syllabus, but 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences produces two grades and 0653 Combined Science produces one, with 0653 carrying the narrowest content of any IGCSE science route. The practical consequence is post-16: three separate sciences keeps every A Level and Diploma science open, a double award keeps most open with a harder first term, and a single combined award often restricts or closes post-16 science entirely. Establish which your child is on in Year 9 or early Year 10.

faqs.question: How do I find out my child's science award code?
faqs.answer: One email to the school asking for three things: the award code for science, the tier, and the practical route. The answer will be separate sciences with codes such as 0625, 0620 and 0610, or Pearson's 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1, or a combined route such as 0654 or 0653, with Core or Extended attached. Hand that answer to any tutor before the first session and ask them to name the papers your child will sit. It is two minutes of work that prevents weeks of wasted revision.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how is it prepared for?
faqs.answer: It is a written component Cambridge schools may enter candidates for instead of the laboratory practical test, testing the same skills on paper: apparatus choice, variables, tabulation, plotting, anomalies and suggested improvements. Because the question types repeat across series with unusual consistency, it is one of the most drillable components in the whole entry, and most students have never practised it deliberately. Three or four sessions on it is among the best-value purchases available in IGCSE science, and it needs no apparatus.

faqs.question: Does Pearson have a separate practical exam for sciences?
faqs.answer: No. Pearson International GCSE sciences assess practical skills within the written papers through questions on method, data and evaluation rather than through a separate component. The skills tested are similar to Cambridge's but the context in which they appear is not, and Pearson papers tend towards fewer, longer questions. A student preparing for a Pearson entry using Cambridge alternative-to-practical material is practising a paper that does not exist on their timetable.

faqs.question: If we can only tutor one science, which should it be?
faqs.answer: Whichever the marked papers show is weakest at the upper tier, with a tilt towards physics if the choice is close. Physics is hard because it requires reasoning rather than recall, and the explanation and graph-interpretation skills that fix it transfer into chemistry and biology answers. Biology is the most improvable in a short block close to the examinations, because its marks turn on exact terminology. Chemistry often moves quickest once calculation presentation and named interactions are fixed.

faqs.question: Should we support all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Almost never, on both arithmetic and timetable grounds. Three weekly sessions at the published qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour comes to roughly AED 5,400 to 10,800 across a twelve-week term, and requires three evenings a Dubai Year 11 week does not have alongside eight or nine other subjects. The better shape is one science weekly, a practical-skills block covering all three, and fortnightly weekend timed papers — because practical skills and explanation discipline transfer where content does not.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in biology despite revising hard?
faqs.answer: Usually terminology rather than understanding. Biology mark schemes credit the exact term — water potential rather than more water, active transport rather than movement, specific named structures rather than descriptions — and a fluent paragraph that avoids the required word scores poorly. The fix is a condensed definition set plus command-term discipline, drilled on past-paper questions and marked against the official scheme. It is one of the fastest grade movements available in the subject and it is not achieved by re-reading the textbook.

faqs.question: What makes physics harder than the other two sciences?
faqs.answer: It asks for reasoning rather than recall. A student can know every relationship in electricity and still be unable to say what happens to the current elsewhere in a circuit when one resistance changes, because that requires following a consequence rather than retrieving a fact. The other recurring loss is graph interpretation: reading a value correctly and then failing to say what the gradient or the area under the line represents. Both are teachable and both transfer, which makes physics worth a term of weekly work rather than a late block.

faqs.question: Can science tutoring work at all without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: For everything the written papers examine, yes. Theory, calculations, written explanation, data handling, tabulation, graph plotting and error analysis all need paper and data rather than apparatus, and that includes the whole of the practical-skills component as it is tested on an alternative-to-practical paper or inside Pearson papers. Laboratory work itself belongs to the school under any arrangement — a visiting tutor in Deira is not bringing equipment either. What tutoring adds is making the data a student generated earn marks.

faqs.question: How can I tell a good science session from a bad one?
faqs.answer: By how much of it the student spends writing. A weaker session is a lesson: the tutor explains, the student listens, everybody feels productive, and the next marked paper looks like the last one. A stronger session has the student attempting questions in writing while the tutor stops them at the point the mark would be lost, then marks the answer aloud against the scheme naming the credited phrase. Ask your child what they were asked to do differently; if there is no answer, it was a lesson.

faqs.question: Does a double award count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: That is a question for the school and ultimately the Ministry rather than for a tutoring provider. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. How a two-grade double award is treated within those five should be verified on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before you plan around it.

faqs.question: When is the right time to change a science entry?
faqs.answer: Year 9 or very early Year 10, because the entry pattern determines two years of teaching and the school builds timetable sets around it. By Year 11 the decision is effectively fixed, and a student unhappy with their entry is better served by working on performance within it than by pursuing a change that will not be granted. If your child has any chance of post-16 science, raise the question before sets are allocated rather than after the first disappointing report.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our flat in Deira?
faqs.answer: Not from us. All UAE lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video with a shared whiteboard, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that is part of our India service. For science the honest position is that no in-home tutor brings apparatus either, so the laboratory part belongs to the school under any arrangement, while everything the written papers test works at least as well online. In-home tutoring exists in the Dubai market at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel.

faqs.question: What does science tutoring cost for a Deira family?
faqs.answer: Published October 2026 figures: qualified subject tutors online AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; specialists AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270; budget online generalists AED 33 to 65, suitable for supervision rather than mark-scheme work. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 plus for examination-year specialists. Those are market rates; we quote after a free trial.

faqs.question: Where can my child sit a full science paper if the flat is busy?
faqs.answer: A weekend morning at home is the commonest answer, since a complete paper plus marking takes well over an hour and is unrealistic on a school evening after a long commute. Beyond that, ask the school about supervised study rooms after hours, which most Dubai secondaries run free of charge and which are badly under-used. The Metro running through Deira makes them reachable independently, which is a genuine advantage this district has over the villa suburbs for an older student.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-difc.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE science to a named specification rather than to a general science brief. Each one works from the current syllabus document and the past papers for that code, and each has taught the Extended tier through a full June or November series.

intro.heading: Is there anyone near DIFC who actually knows these syllabuses?
paragraphs: That is the real search behind the phrase IGCSE science tutor in DIFC, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales page. DIFC is an office district with residential towers inside it: Gate Village, Index Tower, Central Park, Limestone House and the Burj Daman cluster. Children living there attend British-curriculum schools spread from Al Quoz to Al Jaddaf to Al Safa. The science teaching those children receive is specification-specific, and the gap between a tutor who knows the specification and one who merely knows chemistry is the gap between a grade 6 and a grade 8.

Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel are not interchangeable. Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry carries the code 0620 and offers a Core and an Extended tier with different papers. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry carries the code 4CH1 and is untiered, with one set of papers for every candidate. The content overlaps substantially; the question style, the command verbs, the mark allocation and the practical requirement do not. A tutor who drills Cambridge Paper 6 technique into a 4CH1 candidate is teaching a paper that child will never sit.

So the honest answer to whether anyone near DIFC knows the syllabus is this: proximity is the wrong filter. Within a fifteen-minute drive of Gate Avenue there are tutors who will take a science booking, and most of them will teach science competently. Far fewer will open the session by asking which code appears on the top right of your child's exam paper. IB Gram filters on the code, not the postcode, and because lessons run over live video the pool is the whole roster rather than whoever can reach Trade Centre by five o'clock.

This page therefore does the work in the order a DIFC parent needs it. It sets out which codes exist and which papers each one requires. It shows what each component is worth and where Extended-tier candidates lose marks year after year. It publishes what the Dubai market charges for science tuition, with the source of every figure, so you can check the number against the page that published it. It explains the two exam series a UAE candidate actually sits, counted backwards from the exam to the point where entries close.

It also states plainly what IB Gram does not do. There is no IB Gram office in Dubai and no tutor will be sent to a DIFC address: home visits are a service offered only in India. Everything for a UAE family is delivered as one-to-one live video tuition, screen-shared, recorded where the family asks for it, and timed around a school day that for most DIFC children ends between 14:45 and 15:30. The case for that model is made in a comparison table further down rather than asserted here.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-difc.programmesIntro: Four routes cover almost every DIFC science booking. The first two are the Cambridge and Edexcel separate sciences, the third is the double-award compromise most option blocks offer, and the fourth is what IGCSE science has to prepare a student for once Year 11 ends.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE separate sciences (0610, 0620, 0625)
programmes.description: Three standalone qualifications, each tiered into Core and Extended. An Extended candidate sits the extended multiple-choice paper, the extended theory paper and either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. The grade ceiling differs by tier, which makes the tier decision the single most consequential choice in a Year 10 science timetable and the one parents are least often shown in writing.
programmes.countryNote: Most Dubai British-curriculum schools near DIFC enter candidates for the Extended tier by default and move individual students down only after the Year 10 internal examinations. If your child's school is reviewing tier placement in the spring term, that review is the moment tutoring changes the outcome, because the evidence the school looks at is internal paper performance rather than classwork.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences (4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1)
programmes.description: Untiered qualifications with a single paper set for all candidates and no alternative-to-practical component in the Cambridge sense. Practical skills are assessed inside the written papers, which changes the preparation entirely: there is no separate paper to drill, but experimental-method questions are embedded across both papers and carry a disproportionate share of the marks students drop.
programmes.countryNote: Edexcel publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November resit series long before it starts, so a Dubai family planning a resit can see the window before entries open. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Always read the live timetable on the Pearson support pages rather than a date restated on a tutoring site, including this one.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Science (0654, 0653)
programmes.description: Co-ordinated Science as a double award yields two IGCSE grades from roughly two thirds of the separate-science content; Combined Science yields one. Both keep a child's option block free for a language or a humanity. Neither closes the door on A Level science, but a student moving from 0654 into A Level Chemistry has genuine content gaps to close over the summer.
programmes.countryNote: Option blocks at Dubai schools fill in the spring of Year 9, and the double-award route is often presented as the safe choice for a student who finds science hard. For a DIFC family planning on an engineering or medical pathway, the more useful question is which separate science could be dropped instead, since that keeps the remaining two at full depth.

programmes.name: What IGCSE science has to prepare for: A Level and IB DP
programmes.description: Dubai schools split after Year 11 into A Level and the IB Diploma, and both assume specific IGCSE science foundations. A Level Chemistry assumes confident mole calculations and organic mechanisms. IB Diploma sciences assume data-handling and uncertainty work that Cambridge Paper 6 touches only lightly. The summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is where that gap is cheapest to close.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector added six schools during 2025-26 and is adding seven more for 2026-27, four UK-curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. For a DIFC family, that means the sixth-form choice is widening while your child is still in Year 10, so the IGCSE tier decision should not be made as though the post-16 route were already fixed.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Heaviest mark losses sit in transport in plants, genetics notation and the respiration-photosynthesis comparison questions. Extended candidates also face the osmosis practical write-up, where method criticism rather than recall earns the marks.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis products and organic reaction conditions are where Extended grades are decided. Students who can balance equations often still lose marks by omitting state symbols or by naming a product without naming the electrode it forms at.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and the thermal-energy calculations account for most dropped marks. The recurring error is unit conversion inside multi-step questions rather than conceptual confusion, which is why timed paper work beats re-teaching for most candidates.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Science 0654
subjects.description: Two grades from a syllabus that samples all three sciences. The risk is uneven depth: a student strong in biology can carry a weak physics third a long way before the final papers expose it. Diagnostic paper work by discipline is the fix.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade across all three sciences, usually chosen to protect an option block. Tutoring here is mostly triage: identify which of the three disciplines is costing the most marks and spend the hours there rather than spreading them evenly.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Paper 1 and Paper 2 with practical skills embedded rather than separated. Candidates lose marks on experimental design and on the extended-response questions, which expect a structured argument rather than a list of recalled facts.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Calculation-dense, with titration and yield questions appearing in both papers. Students arriving from a Cambridge school mid-course frequently need the untiered paper structure explained before anything chemical is taught.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Formula selection under time pressure is the recurring weakness. The specification expects recall of relationships that Cambridge supplies, so the revision pattern for a 4PH1 candidate differs from a 0625 candidate in a way that matters.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: Two grades drawn from biology, chemistry and physics papers. Timetable clashes and the sheer paper count in a single series make session planning as important as content work for these candidates.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical skills
subjects.description: Table design, anomaly identification, graph-line judgement and error sources. These are teachable in a screen-shared session with real data sets, and they are worth a fifth of the Cambridge grade, which makes them the best-value hours on the whole page.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-difc.modesIntro: Three session patterns cover nearly every IGCSE science booking from this corridor. The pattern matters as much as the hours, because a Year 11 candidate sitting three sciences cannot absorb three separate weekly sessions on top of a full school day.

This is the pattern most Year 10 families start with, and it is usually enough to move a specific topic weakness before it compounds into the next unit.

sections.heading: What a DIFC parent is really asking when they search for a science tutor
paragraphs: The search is for a person who can read your child's exam paper and recognise it. An IGCSE science tutor in DIFC is not a generic science teacher who happens to live nearby; it is someone who knows whether the paper in front of them is Cambridge 0620 Extended or Edexcel 4CH1, and who teaches accordingly from the first lesson rather than the fourth.

That distinction is not pedantry. A Cambridge Extended candidate sits the extended multiple-choice paper, the extended theory paper and either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. An Edexcel candidate sits two untiered written papers with experimental method embedded inside them. The two preparations diverge on question style, on command verbs, on how working must be presented, and on whether there is a separate practical paper to practise at all.

Most DIFC parents discover this somewhere in the second half of Year 10, usually when a tutor sets a past paper that turns out to be from the wrong board. The lesson is cheap if it happens in week two and expensive if it happens in March of Year 11. So the first thing to establish is the code, and the second is whether the tutor you are considering asked for it unprompted.

IB Gram treats that as the opening move. The free trial lesson starts with the specification, the tier and the papers your child is entered for, and the teaching plan is written against those. Nothing on this page claims a tutor is nearer to Gate Village than anyone else; the claim is that the match is made on the specification, and that live online delivery is what makes a specification-level match possible at all.

sections.heading: The syllabus code is the whole question
paragraphs: Dubai schools choose their own boards, and campuses within a ten-minute drive of each other make different choices. That means two DIFC children in the same tower, in the same year group, studying what their parents both call IGCSE Chemistry, can be sitting different papers with different structures and different grade scales. The table below sets out which codes exist and what each one demands.

Read the rightmost column carefully, because it is where the preparation actually differs. Cambridge separates practical assessment into its own paper, which can be practised to a mark scheme. Edexcel distributes experimental questions across its written papers, which means practical skill is tested without a dedicated paper to rehearse. A tutor who does not know which model applies will either over-prepare a paper your child never sits or under-prepare questions that appear throughout.

The grade scales differ too. Cambridge IGCSE sciences report on A* to G alongside the 9 to 1 scale depending on the syllabus variant and series, while Edexcel International GCSE reports on 9 to 1. Where your child's school reports internally in one scale and enters them for the other, the mock grade you are shown may not mean what you assume. Ask the head of science which scale the final certificate will use.

Codes also change. Cambridge and Pearson revise specifications, and a syllabus taught from 2025 may differ from the one a tutor last taught in 2021. Every teaching plan here is written against the current syllabus document on the board's own site, and the correct response to any doubt is to read that document rather than to trust a summary, including this one.

sections.heading: Component by component: what each science paper is worth
paragraphs: Parents are rarely shown the weightings, and they change how hours should be spent. A Cambridge Extended science candidate takes three components, and one of them is the practical route worth a fifth of the grade. Yet practical technique is the component schools have least timetable room to rehearse, because it needs apparatus, a lab slot and a technician.

The consequence is predictable. A student who is solid on theory and untrained on Paper 6 arrives at a ceiling they cannot see, because their classwork never tested table design or anomaly identification. Four sessions on that one component often move more marks than ten sessions of topic revision, and they are the easiest sessions to run over live video because the work is data on a shared screen rather than apparatus in a room.

Durations and exact weightings vary by syllabus and by series, so the table gives the structure and sends you to the syllabus document for the current figures. What does not vary is the shape: a multiple-choice component, a theory component carrying the largest share, and a practical route carrying the rest. Build the term plan around that shape rather than around chapter order in the textbook.

One more structural point. Cambridge Core and Extended candidates sit different papers for the same subject, and the Core route carries a grade ceiling. If your child's school is still deciding tier in the spring of Year 10, the internal paper performance is the evidence that decision rests on, which makes the months before it the most valuable tutoring window in the whole two years.

sections.heading: Where Extended-tier science marks actually go missing
paragraphs: Mark loss at Extended tier is rarely about not knowing the science. It is about a small set of repeated habits that a marker is obliged to penalise. The most common is an unfinished calculation: the student has the right method, arrives at the right number, and omits the unit or the state symbol that the mark scheme requires before awarding the final mark.

The second is command-verb blindness. State, describe and explain carry different mark counts and demand different answers, and a student who explains when asked to state wastes minutes they need later in the paper. The third is graph work: axes chosen badly, a line drawn through every point rather than through the trend, and anomalies circled without being named as anomalies.

In chemistry specifically, electrolysis questions cost marks because products are named without the electrode, and mole questions cost marks because the student converts at the wrong step. In physics, almost all of the dropped marks in multi-step questions come from unit conversion rather than from the physics. In biology, genetics notation and the transport-in-plants sequence account for a disproportionate share.

None of this is diagnosable from a report card. It is diagnosable from three marked past papers, which is why the first fortnight of any booking here is spent on timed paper work rather than on teaching. The output is a short list of the specific habits costing your child marks, in the order of how many marks each one costs.
bullets: Final answer given without a unit, or without a state symbol in an equation
Command verb ignored: explaining when asked to state, or stating when asked to explain
Line of best fit drawn point to point, with anomalies included rather than named
Unit conversion performed at the wrong stage of a multi-step calculation
Significant figures inconsistent between the table and the final answer
Improvement questions answered with 'be more careful' rather than a method change

sections.heading: What science tuition costs in Dubai, and how to check the figure yourself
paragraphs: Every number in the table below was published by the provider named beside it, which means you can open their page and read it for yourself. That is the point of printing the source column: a rate with no attribution is a sales claim, and a rate you can verify is information. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no Dubai family transacts in.

The cheapest end of the market is university-student and platform tutoring, which starts around AED 33 to AED 65 an hour. The middle is a qualified subject tutor working online, roughly AED 150 to AED 300. Specialist IGCSE and IB tutors run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, and a named or examiner-tier tutor can reach AED 650. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to AED 500 because travel time is priced inside the hour.

Monthly packages are where comparison gets difficult, because a package fixes a session count rather than a number of hours. Figures seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits. Divide by the actual minutes before comparing anything, and ask whether marking between sessions is included or billed.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page. The honest reason is that a science booking from DIFC can be a single Paper 6 block or a two-year two-subject plan, and a single number would mislead either way. What is quoted is quoted after the trial lesson, in AED, for the specification your child is actually entered for. The trial lesson itself carries no charge and no card requirement.

sections.heading: The two series a UAE science candidate sits, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. The February series that appears in some tutoring material is offered to India only, and a Dubai family who plans around it will miss an entry deadline. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the school sits in before printing any timetable at home.

The dated anchors below come from Pearson's own timetable pages. The November 2026 Edexcel International GCSE final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which is the pattern a November resit candidate should plan around.

Work the table from the bottom upwards. The exam is fixed, so everything else is a countdown: the last point at which a resit decision is useful, the last point at which an entry can be made, and the point at which paper practice has to replace topic teaching. For IB Diploma dates, confirm against ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator, because no IB session date in this project has been verified from the IB itself.

sections.heading: Why these searches say home tutor, and what is actually delivered
paragraphs: A large share of DIFC science searches use the phrase home tutor, and that phrase is worth answering honestly rather than redirecting. In the Dubai market, an in-home science tutor is quoted at roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with travel time priced inside the rate. The practical reality in this corridor is that an evening visit from Al Quoz or Jumeirah to a Gate Village tower absorbs a meaningful part of the hour you pay for.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE booking is delivered as one-to-one live video tuition. That is a limit, and stating it plainly is more useful than discovering it at the booking stage. What it buys is the thing a DIFC family cannot get from a travel radius: a tutor matched to the exact syllabus code rather than to a postcode.

The trade is specific. A Cambridge 0654 double-award candidate with a weak physics third needs someone who has taught that exact combination through a full series. The number of people who have done that and who can reach DIFC by 17:00 on a Tuesday is small. The number who can open a screen share at 17:00 on a Tuesday is much larger, and the second group is where the specialist actually is.

There is a second, quieter advantage for an apartment family. A video lesson needs a quiet corner and a stable connection rather than a spare room and a visitor, and it ends when it ends rather than when a tutor's next booking across town dictates. For a household with two working parents on office hours, that is often the deciding factor rather than the price.

sections.heading: KHDA, the mandatory subjects and what they do to a Year 11 timetable
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Naming the right body matters, because the rules differ by emirate.

Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

That has a direct timetable effect on a science candidate. Mandatory-subject instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises a minimum of 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson. Those periods sit inside the same week as three sciences, which is why Year 11 science revision so often has to happen outside school hours rather than inside a free period.

One caution worth stating directly. IB Gram is not KHDA approved, accredited or licensed, and no page on this site should be read as claiming otherwise. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai, which is a different legal animal from an individual online tutor. Any provider describing its tutors as regulator-approved should be asked to show the permit number.

sections.heading: Academic honesty in science: what a tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: Science at IGCSE carries less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but the boundary still matters, and it matters more where a student also does a school science project or a Year 11 investigation. A tutor may teach method, explain a technique, model an analysis on different data, mark a draft against published criteria and explain why a mark was lost. A tutor may not produce the work.

The distinction is not a style preference. Work submitted for assessment must be the student's own, and a tutor who writes a lab report or an investigation hands the student a malpractice risk that sits with the student, not the tutor. There are operators in this market selling completed Internal Assessments at a set price. That is an academic-integrity breach, and no part of what IB Gram offers includes it.

In practice the line is easy to hold once it is named. A session on a science investigation looks like this: the student explains their method, the tutor asks the questions a marker would ask, the student identifies what is missing, and the student makes the changes. The tutor's notes record what was discussed rather than what was written, so a school asking how the work was supported gets a clear answer.

Nor will any tutor here supply board material as a download. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB, and the correct handling is to reference them and link to the official page. A provider offering a bundled pack of mark schemes is reproducing copyright material and should be treated with suspicion.

sections.heading: Starting from DIFC, and what is not being claimed
paragraphs: The first step is the syllabus code. Send the subject, the code from the top of your child's paper or report, the tier if it is a Cambridge science, the school and the series they are entered for. That is enough to say honestly whether a specialist in that specification is free in the slot you need, and if the answer is no, the answer will be no rather than a substitution.

The trial lesson follows, at no charge and with no card requirement. It is a working session rather than a sales call: a diagnostic on a past-paper question set, a short conversation with you afterwards about what the paper actually showed, and a written plan naming the components and topics the first six sessions will cover. If the fit is wrong, nothing further is booked.

After that, sessions run weekly on Gulf Standard Time with the same tutor, work set between lessons from the correct board's papers, and a topic log you can read. Marking is to the published mark scheme with the mark allocation shown, because a parent who can see where two marks went is in a far better position than one holding a percentage.

What is not being claimed: no grade outcome, no regulator approval, no UAE office, no partnership with any school named on this page, and no statistic about past students that could not be produced with its sample size and method. Tutoring is also not a requirement for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any page suggesting otherwise is selling urgency rather than teaching.

faqs.question: Should my child sit IGCSE science at Core or Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Only Cambridge syllabuses are tiered; Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, so the question does not arise there. For Cambridge, Extended covers more content and carries a higher grade ceiling, while Core caps the attainable grade. Schools usually enter candidates for Extended by default and reconsider individual students after the Year 10 internal examinations, based on paper performance rather than classwork. If a tier review is coming, the months before it are the most valuable tutoring window in the whole course, because the evidence the decision rests on is exactly what timed paper practice improves.

faqs.question: Do your tutors cover both Cambridge and Edexcel IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Yes, but as separate specifications rather than one subject. Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 are tiered and assess practical skill through Paper 5 or Paper 6. Edexcel 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 are untiered and embed experimental questions inside the written papers. The teaching plan, the past papers set and the mark scheme used all follow the code your child is entered for. The first thing asked at booking is which code appears on their paper, because preparing a candidate for the wrong board's paper structure wastes the hours you are paying for.

faqs.question: How is the science practical assessed if lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: The practical component is set and marked by the school as exam centre and by the board, not by a tutor, so online delivery does not affect how it is assessed. Cambridge candidates sit either Paper 5, a supervised practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Paper 6 is entirely paper-based: table design, data handling, graph work, anomaly identification and error analysis. All of that is teachable over a shared screen with real data sets. For Paper 5, a tutor rehearses recording, significant figures and layout, which is where most of the marks are lost rather than in apparatus use.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science subjects do Dubai students struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Across bookings from this corridor, chemistry calculations and physics electricity come up most often, followed by biology genetics notation. In chemistry the recurring losses are mole conversions performed at the wrong step and electrolysis products named without the electrode. In physics it is unit conversion inside multi-step questions rather than conceptual confusion. In biology it is the transport-in-plants sequence and genetic crosses written without the notation the mark scheme expects. None of these is diagnosable from a report card, which is why the first fortnight of any booking is spent on marked past papers.

faqs.question: My child struggles with electricity in physics. Can that be fixed before the exams?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because electricity is one of the most tractable topics in the syllabus. The marks are lost in a small number of repeatable places: series and parallel resistance treated interchangeably, current and potential difference confused in a circuit diagram, and power calculations where the unit conversion happens before rather than after the substitution. Those are habits rather than gaps, and habits respond quickly to timed question sets with immediate marking. A four to six session block on circuits, with past-paper questions from the correct syllabus code, is the usual shape.

faqs.question: What are the hardest topics in IGCSE Chemistry Extended?
faqs.answer: Moles and stoichiometry, electrolysis and organic reaction conditions account for most of the mark loss at Extended tier. Moles cause trouble because the conversion step moves depending on what the question gives you. Electrolysis costs marks when a product is named without the electrode it forms at. Organic questions cost marks when conditions are omitted from an equation. There is also a presentation issue running through all three: missing state symbols and dropped units cost final marks even where the chemistry is right, which is why marking to the published scheme matters more than re-teaching.

faqs.question: Is it better to take three separate sciences or Co-ordinated Science?
faqs.answer: It depends on the post-16 plan rather than on current attainment. Co-ordinated Science as a double award gives two grades from roughly two thirds of the separate-science content and leaves an option slot free. Separate sciences give three grades at full depth. Neither closes off A Level or IB Diploma science, but a student moving from 0654 into A Level Chemistry has real content gaps to close over the summer. If an engineering or medical pathway is in view, a more useful question is which single separate science could be dropped, keeping the other two at full depth.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE science tutor in DIFC cost per hour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from roughly AED 33 to AED 65 an hour for platform and university-student tutors, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IGCSE or IB specialist, and AED 500 to AED 650 at named or examiner tier. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 because travel is priced inside the hour. Those are market figures from the providers that published them, not IB Gram prices. A quote here follows the free trial lesson, once the actual scope is known.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE science exams held for a Dubai candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February series sometimes mentioned in tutoring material is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the school sits in, and read the live timetable on the board's own site.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does one science subject need?
faqs.answer: One weekly session of sixty to ninety minutes, with marked work between lessons, is the usual starting point for a Year 10 candidate with a specific topic weakness. Year 11 candidates in the term before a series often move to two. The limiting factor is rarely contact time; it is independent practice time, which is why a second weekly session sometimes produces less than the same hour spent on marked past papers. The pattern is reviewed after each school assessment and changed when the marks lost say it should change.

faqs.question: Can a science tutor come to our apartment in DIFC?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. Every UAE booking runs as one-to-one live video tuition on Gulf Standard Time. That limit is stated before booking rather than after. What it buys is a match on the syllabus code rather than on a travel radius: the number of tutors who have taught Cambridge 0654 through a full series and can also reach a Gate Village tower by five o'clock is small, while the number who can open a screen share at that hour is much larger.

faqs.question: Does a private science tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Individuals providing private tuition in the UAE need a MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: For UAE equivalency, how many IGCSE subjects and which grades does a DIFC family need?
faqs.answer: On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires a pass in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among the five required subjects. One competitor page states six subjects, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own site, because IB Gram does not perform equivalency and the process is not something any tutor guarantees.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a science school project or lab report?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the method, explain a technique, model an analysis on different data, ask the questions a marker would ask and mark a draft against the published criteria. A tutor cannot write it. Work submitted for assessment has to be the student's own, and a tutor who produces it hands the student a malpractice risk that sits with the student. In a session, the student explains their method, the tutor questions it, the student identifies what is missing and the student makes the change. Session notes record what was discussed rather than what was written.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor covers my child's exact syllabus code?
faqs.answer: You are told that, with a realistic wait, rather than matched to someone who will learn the paper alongside your child. Separate sciences at Cambridge and Edexcel are well covered. The harder requests are double-award candidates needing one weak discipline addressed, and combinations where a specific tier and a specific evening slot have to coincide. Where the wait is a few weeks, the usual interim is a different session pattern, such as a practical-skills block that is board-neutral in parts, rather than a weaker match now that has to be unwound later.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-difc.closingHeading: Start with the code on the paper
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-difc.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the first question. Find your child's syllabus code, the tier if it is a Cambridge science, and the series they are entered for, and ask any tutor you are considering to tell you what the paper structure is before they quote you a rate. A tutor who answers that without looking it up is the tutor you want. To book a free trial lesson with IB Gram, send the code, the school and the slot you need, and you will get a straight answer on availability for that specification, delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-discovery-g.tutorsIntro: These are the science tutors a Discovery Gardens family is matched with for Years 9 to 11. The first thing any of them should ask is how many weeks are left and which components have already closed.

intro.heading: Three sciences and a calendar nobody mapped
paragraphs: Science is the subject area where timing does the most damage, because a student sitting three separate sciences carries three sets of content, three practical demands and three papers that often fall within the same fortnight. Families usually make contact at one of two moments: the week after mock results, or six weeks before the series. One of those is a good moment and the other is late, and the difference is worth understanding before any money is spent.

The structural reason is that parts of a science grade close early. Depending on the board and the entry, practical or coursework components complete before the written papers. Entries themselves close months ahead and fix the board, the award and the tier. By the time a parent is worried enough to search, several of the variables that shape the grade have already been settled and cannot be reopened.

Discovery Gardens adds its own rhythm. It is a high-density apartment community of 291 buildings in themed districts beside Ibn Battuta, with its own Route 2020 metro station. Students travel out of the community for school, so they are home from about 15:50 on the nearest Dubai Investments Park routes and from about 16:30 from the Al Barsha corridor, with Year 11 revision clinics pushing it later again.

Then there is the UAE calendar itself, which almost no tutoring page accounts for. The academic year is interrupted by a winter break and a spring break. Ramadan shifts roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, and in recent years has fallen in the spring term, overlapping mock results and the start of serious revision, with schools operating reduced hours. All of that changes when revision actually happens.

IB Gram matches on the board and the award, and delivers every UAE lesson one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India. In a compressed run-in that matters practically, because a missed session can move to the next evening rather than the next week, and a week is a large fraction of eight.

What follows is the science year counted backwards: what closes when, how the papers stack for a three-science candidate, how Ramadan and the breaks change the plan, what the mock window is actually for, and what eight weeks can realistically achieve across three subjects. UAE candidates sit the June and November series; Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so any plan quoting a February exam window to a Dubai family is working from another country's calendar.

One more thing is worth stating at the outset. Nothing on this page argues for more hours. It argues for hours placed where the calendar still allows them to reach marks, which usually means fewer sessions bought earlier rather than more sessions bought in a panic. The families in this community who get the strongest science results are almost always the ones who asked for the practical component dates in the autumn.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-discovery-g.programmesIntro: Each stage has a different calendar and a different thing still open to influence. These are the four phases either side of the Year 11 papers.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: No external assessment and therefore no calendar pressure, which is why this stage gets skipped. The habits formed here are examined from Year 10 onward in every science entry: reading an instrument to the right precision, tabulating with units in the heading, plotting a sensible scale with a line of best fit, naming a control variable with a reason.
programmes.countryNote: Discovery Gardens students in these years are home earlier and have fewer commitments, so a 16:30 session places easily. A term in Year 9 on practical and processing technique pays back across three subjects for two years, which is a return no Year 11 intervention can match, and almost nobody in this community buys it.

programmes.name: IGCSE sciences, Years 10 to 11
programmes.description: Three separate sciences, a double award covering all three disciplines, or a single combined award. Entries carry either a laboratory examination or a written alternative-to-practical paper. Most lost marks are procedural: units misplaced, graphs badly scaled, methods without controls named, anomalies identified but not explained.
programmes.countryNote: This is where almost all Discovery Gardens enquiries sit, and where the calendar bites hardest. The workable pattern is one discipline at a time in a 17:00 or 17:30 slot, chosen from the paper-level breakdown, with the choice reviewed each term rather than rotated weekly across three.

programmes.name: The mock window
programmes.description: Full papers under exam conditions, usually in the winter term, producing a paper-level breakdown most families never request. The mock's value is diagnostic: it shows which discipline and which skill is losing marks and whether the cause is content, practical technique, command terms or timing. The grade itself is the least useful output.
programmes.countryNote: Mock results are the most common trigger for an enquiry in this community, and the week after them is a good moment to act provided the breakdown comes too. Without it a tutor is working from a grade and a feeling, which produces a generic plan across three sciences and a term of effort with little to show.

programmes.name: The November series
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. A resit is worth entering when the paper-level breakdown shows a near miss on one component in a subject needed for an offer, and usually is not when marks sat evenly below target across every paper.
programmes.countryNote: The decision window after August results is days rather than weeks, so the breakdown should be reviewed in the first week with the exams officer involved. The November route is also the easiest time of year to secure a specialist, because Dubai demand collapses once results are out and summer availability is at its widest.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-discovery-g.subjectsIntro: Each science has its own position in the calendar and its own time-critical elements. These notes name the codes and what has to happen when.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, genetics, ecology and human physiology. Late-year work should target language precision, since naming a mechanism and a direction is required and vague answers score nothing, plus the required practical techniques and genetic cross notation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Atomic structure, bonding, moles, organic chemistry and chemical tests. Mole arithmetic underpins everything quantitative, so it is the first thing to drill in a short window; the chemical tests must be answered as an observation plus a conclusion, which is quick to fix.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Forces and motion, electricity, waves, thermal physics and radioactivity. The fastest late improvements are gradients read from a line of best fit, unit prefix discipline, and writing a method with control variables named rather than implied.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences, double award
subjects.description: All three disciplines in reduced content, with each appearing inside every paper. In a short window that structure is decisive: hours should concentrate on the weak discipline rather than spreading across three, because the weakness is in every paper rather than one grade.

subjects.name: Combined Science, single award
subjects.description: A single award covering all three disciplines with further reduced content. Worth checking against post-16 plans early, since some schools will not accept it as preparation for Advanced Level study in a science, and that is an entry-stage question rather than a revision one.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical skills
subjects.description: Either a laboratory examination or a written paper testing the same skills. Whichever applies, it closes before or alongside the written papers and the skills are narrow, trainable and examined. This is the work to finish before study leave rather than during it.

subjects.name: Data handling and graph work
subjects.description: Units in the column heading, scales that fill the grid, lines of best fit read for gradient, anomalies explained rather than circled. Shared across all three disciplines, which makes it the only genuine three-for-one purchase in a short window.

subjects.name: Command terms in science answers
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest and compare each require a different answer shape, and a knowledgeable answer to the wrong command earns little. Written answers marked against the command used, then rewritten once, is the version that works and is slower than content review.

subjects.name: Mathematics within the sciences
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, percentages, ratios, standard form and unit conversion. Where a student understands the science and stalls on the arithmetic, the correct late purchase is mathematics support rather than more science teaching, and one marked paper distinguishes them.

subjects.name: Arabic and the mandatory UAE subjects
subjects.description: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools under KHDA requirements, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. They occupy timetable space alongside three sciences, which is part of why the Year 11 week is as tight as it is.

subjects.name: Post-16 science preparation
subjects.description: For students continuing to Advanced Level or IB Diploma sciences, the summer gap is uncertainty treatment, extended explanation and investigation design. Four to six sessions in the quietest months of the tutoring year, which is also when specialists are most available.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics for science students
subjects.description: Taken alongside the main entry, it removes much of the quantitative shock from post-16 sciences as well as mathematics. Worth considering at entry stage rather than discovered afterwards, and the hardest subject in this corridor to staff locally.

sections.heading: The science year counted backwards
paragraphs: Counting backwards is more useful than counting forwards because it shows what has already closed. The entry closes months before the papers and fixes the board, the award and the tier, which between them determine how much content there is and what grade is available. Practical or coursework components close before or alongside the written papers depending on the entry. Mocks sit in the winter. Then study leave, the series, results in August, and a narrow window for a November entry.

For a three-science candidate every one of those milestones is multiplied, which is why the calendar needs writing down rather than carrying in anyone's head. Three practical components. Three sets of mock papers. Six or more written papers in the series itself, sometimes two in a day. Families who map this in September spend fewer hours in total and place them better than families who meet it as it arrives.

The document that makes this concrete is the school's own zone timetable. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. The exams officer holds the version that applies to your child.

Pearson's published dates give a sense of the calendar's reach, and they are backward-looking citations so they keep their dates. The November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Forward planning should use the live official timetable, since provisional versions are revised.

sections.heading: How the papers stack for a three-science candidate
paragraphs: The exam fortnight looks very different for a student sitting three separate sciences than for one sitting a single award, and the difference should shape the preceding months. Six or more science papers, sometimes with two on one day and sometimes with a four-day gap, produce a pattern of pressure points and recovery windows that is knowable in advance from the zone timetable and almost never used.

Those gaps are where the last genuinely useful revision happens. A two-day gap before a chemistry paper is worth planning for specifically: it is the window for a final pass on the chemical tests and mole arithmetic, not for starting a topic. Knowing in March which gaps exist changes how February is used, because it tells you what can be left until the gap and what cannot.

Two papers on one day is the other pattern worth preparing for, and it is a stamina question as much as a knowledge one. Students who have never written two full papers in a day discover during the series what that feels like. One rehearsal in study leave, under realistic conditions, is worth several hours of topic revision because it is the only way to find out whether the afternoon paper suffers.

For double and single award candidates the shape is different but the logic is the same: fewer papers, each containing all three disciplines, so there is no recovery from a weak discipline between papers. Every paper carries it. That makes the pre-series priority different, concentrating entirely on the weak discipline rather than on timetable management.

sections.heading: The practical component closes before the papers do
paragraphs: This is the piece of the science calendar families most often miss. Depending on the board and the entry, a science candidate sits either a laboratory examination or a written alternative-to-practical paper, and in either case that component is completed before or alongside the written papers rather than after them. Once it is done, that share of the grade is fixed, and no amount of revision in the final weeks reaches it.

What makes this frustrating is that the skills involved are the most trainable in the whole science syllabus. Reading an instrument to the precision it supports, tabulating with the unit in the heading, scaling a graph so the data fills the grid, drawing a line of best fit, naming a control variable and saying how it was controlled, explaining an anomaly rather than circling it, and writing a conclusion that answers the hypothesis.

None of that requires a laboratory to practise and all of it is written work. For a student taking a coordinated or combined award, the same skills are examined across all three disciplines in the same paper, so the return is multiplied. This is why practical technique is the one thing a calendar-led plan should finish early rather than leaving for the revision term.

The practical instruction for a Discovery Gardens family is therefore simple: ask the school when each science practical or alternative-to-practical component falls, and schedule technique work to finish a clear fortnight before the earliest of them. Doing that in the autumn costs a handful of sessions. Discovering the deadline in the spring means the cheapest marks in the syllabus have already gone.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the breaks, and when revision actually happens
paragraphs: A revision plan written for a UAE family has to account for the local calendar, and most tutoring advice does not. The academic year runs from late summer to early summer, interrupted by a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break in the second term. Both breaks are either opportunities or losses, depending on whether anyone planned for them before they arrived.

Ramadan has a larger effect. It moves roughly eleven days earlier each year in the Gregorian calendar, so its position relative to the school year shifts, and in recent years it has fallen in the spring term, overlapping mock results and the start of serious examination revision. UAE schools operate reduced hours during it, which changes both the teaching time available and the shape of a student's day.

The adjustments are straightforward once anticipated. Reduced school hours free earlier afternoon slots, which is genuinely useful for a Year 11 student who is otherwise not available before 17:00. Energy patterns change, so a fasting student may work better at 19:00 than at 17:00, or the reverse, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Shorter, more frequent sessions generally beat long blocks in this period.

What goes wrong is only ever the unplanned version. A family books a fixed weekly slot in January, Ramadan arrives, the slot stops working, two sessions are missed and the arrangement quietly lapses in the term that mattered most. Agreeing in advance that the slot will move for that period costs one conversation. Across three sciences in a compressed term, two lost sessions is a meaningful share of the support paid for.

sections.heading: What the mock window is actually for
paragraphs: Mock results are the most common reason a Discovery Gardens family contacts a tutor, and the document they arrive with is usually the wrong one. A grade tells you how far from target a student is. It does not tell you why, and with three sciences it does not even tell you which discipline is responsible. The paper-level breakdown does both, and schools hold it and frequently do not send it out.

The reason it matters is that identical grades mean opposite things. A 5 produced by one weak paper with the others solid needs targeted component work in one discipline. A 5 spread evenly across every paper needs broad consolidation. A 5 caused by three unfinished papers is a timing problem and nothing else. Those are three different plans, and a tutor working from the grade alone will default to content revision for all three.

In a coordinated or combined award the question is sharper still, because all three disciplines sit inside every paper. A disappointing award grade can come from weak physics content appearing throughout, from poor practical skills applied across all three, or from command-term errors in extended answers. Guessing between those three wastes a term, and the breakdown distinguishes them in minutes.

The best use of the week after mocks is therefore three to five diagnostic sessions working through the breakdown, categorising errors by cause, and producing a written plan with a stated number of sessions. Families in this community who do that in the winter term rarely make a second, more expensive enquiry in the spring, which is the pattern this page exists to interrupt.

sections.heading: Eight weeks, three sciences: what is realistically possible
paragraphs: Eight weeks is the window most families actually have when they make contact, so it deserves a concrete plan. The principle is narrow focus. With three sciences and eight weeks, attempting coverage produces a thin pass over everything and no measurable change. What produces change is the two or three highest-frequency causes of lost marks, plus the shared practical and data skills that benefit all three disciplines at once.

The first week is diagnosis. Two marked papers from the weakest discipline, errors categorised by cause, a written plan. The second and third weeks go to the practical and data skills, deliberately early, because they are shared across all three sciences and because the practical component may close before the written papers. That is the only genuine three-for-one work available in a short window.

Weeks four to six are timed papers in the weakest discipline, marked strictly, with errors grouped by cause rather than topic. Week seven turns to the components students avoid: the data sections, the extended-response questions, the practical write-up style. Avoidance is the most reliable predictor of where marks are being lost, and these are usually the quickest gains because they have been neglected.

The final week is exam-room behaviour and nothing new: reading a question before answering, allocating time per mark, checking the command term, and for three-science candidates rehearsing two papers in one day if the timetable requires it. Families who try to learn content in the last week lose the consolidation the previous seven earned, which is the commonest way a good run-in is wasted.

sections.heading: Results week, and the decisions that cannot wait
paragraphs: The science calendar does not end with the papers. After results there is a short window in which a resit decision has to be made, and families who have not anticipated it make it on disappointment rather than evidence. Cambridge runs IGCSE in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November, so the route exists in both boards.

Published Pearson dates show how tight the window is. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. An entry decision for a November series therefore has to be made within days of August results, with the school's exams officer involved from the beginning rather than consulted afterwards.

The decision should come from the paper-level breakdown. A student who missed a boundary by a few marks on one component, in a science needed for a post-16 offer, is a strong candidate for a resit. A student whose marks sat evenly below target across every paper usually needs a different plan rather than another sitting, and saying so honestly is more useful than selling a second block by default.

There is also a quieter advantage to the November route worth knowing. Dubai's tutoring demand collapses after August results, so specialist availability through the summer and autumn is at its widest of the year. A family entering a November series has a genuine choice of tutor rather than whoever is free, which is the opposite of the position in study leave before the June series.

sections.heading: What a calendar-led science tutor does differently, and our limits
paragraphs: A tutor working from the calendar asks different opening questions. Not what grade is your child getting, but which board and award, how many weeks remain, when the practical components fall, when the mocks are, and whether the paper-level breakdown exists. The plan follows from those answers and changes shape as components close. That is a different service from a weekly hour of general science support.

It also means reducing or declining work. Where a family arrives with three weeks and three sciences, the useful answer is one discipline and one skill rather than three weeks spread across everything. Where the practical component has closed and the losses were practical, we say that the cheapest marks have gone and plan around the rest. Some enquiries end with advice rather than a booking.

Our delivery limits are the same throughout this site. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time between 15:30 and 21:30. No tutor attends a UAE address; home visiting is a service we offer only in India, and there is no IB Gram office in the UAE. In a compressed run-in the format has a practical advantage, since a missed session moves to the next evening rather than the next week.

On assessed work and claims the boundaries are fixed. A tutor teaches technique, questions a method, explains what each assessment strand rewards and gives written feedback on the student's own draft; a tutor does not write, rewrite, process results or supply content. We do not reproduce board syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes. We hold no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not guarantee grades.

process.title: Send the entry list and the weeks remaining
process.description: The board, the codes and the award, plus how many weeks until the papers. For a science candidate the second question is as important as the first, because it determines whether practical technique is still worth buying or whether that component has already closed.
