process.description: The zone timetable, the practical or coursework component dates, and the paper-level breakdown of the last mock. All three are free and rarely volunteered. Between them they show what is still open, when the pressure points fall, and which discipline is losing the marks.

process.title: We match to the board and award and name the tutor
process.description: You are told who will teach, which board they work to, and whether your child's entry carries a laboratory paper or the written alternative. If we cannot match the exact entry we say so rather than offering a near equivalent.

process.title: Free trial that starts with diagnosis
process.description: Two marked papers, errors categorised by cause, and a written plan with a stated number of sessions. No payment is taken and there is no obligation. If the diagnosis says the available window cannot deliver what you want, we will say so rather than booking a block.

process.title: Do the shared skills first
process.description: Practical and data technique benefits all three sciences at once and may close before the written papers, so it goes early in any plan rather than being saved for the revision term. In a short window it is the only genuine three-for-one purchase available.

process.title: Plan around Ramadan and the breaks
process.description: Agree at the outset that the slot will move during Ramadan and across the winter and spring breaks. Reduced school hours free earlier slots and energy patterns shift, and an unplanned clash is how two sessions get lost in the term that mattered most.

whyPoints.title: Plans built backwards from the series
whyPoints.description: Entries, practical components and mocks all close before the papers, so what is reachable depends on the date you start. We ask for the dates first and tell you honestly what the remaining window can achieve across three sciences.

whyPoints.title: The practical component treated as a deadline
whyPoints.description: Practical and alternative-to-practical skills are the cheapest marks in science and they close early. We schedule technique work to finish before the component rather than leaving it for the revision term when it is no longer reachable.

whyPoints.title: The zone timetable used, not a generic one
whyPoints.description: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and warns that the wrong timetable can cost a candidate an exam. We plan the final term from your school's own version, including the gaps and the two-paper days.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis from the breakdown, not the grade
whyPoints.description: In a three-science or combined award entry, identical grades mean three different problems. The paper-level breakdown distinguishes content, practical technique, command terms and timing in minutes, and it is free.

whyPoints.title: The UAE calendar accounted for
whyPoints.description: Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each year and UAE schools run reduced hours during it, which changes available time and energy patterns. We agree how the slot moves rather than losing sessions in the spring term.

whyPoints.title: Willing to say the window is too short
whyPoints.description: With three weeks and three sciences, the honest answer is one discipline and one skill. Where the cheapest marks have already closed, we say so. That costs enquiries and is the reason to believe the rest of the page.

faqs.question: When do the science practical components actually close?
faqs.answer: Before or alongside the written papers, depending on the board and the entry, and that is the piece of the calendar families most often miss. Once the laboratory examination or the alternative-to-practical paper is sat, that share of the grade is fixed and no later revision reaches it. Ask the school for the component dates and schedule technique work to finish a clear fortnight before the earliest of them. In the autumn that costs a handful of sessions; in the spring it is already gone.

faqs.question: Why is the practical paper the cheapest grade in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Because the skills are narrow, written and examined, and need no laboratory to practise. Reading an instrument to the precision it supports, tabulating with units in the heading, scaling a graph so the data fills the grid, drawing a line of best fit, naming a control variable with the method for controlling it, explaining an anomaly, and writing a conclusion that answers the hypothesis. In a coordinated or combined award the same skills earn marks across all three disciplines in one paper.

faqs.question: What should I ask the school for before booking science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Three documents, all free and rarely volunteered. The zone timetable, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version. The practical or coursework component dates, so technique work can be finished before they close. And the paper-level breakdown of the last mock, which identifies which discipline and which skill is losing the marks. Those three decide what tutoring is worth buying.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a Year 11 science revision plan?
faqs.answer: It shifts roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, so its position in the school year moves, and in recent years it has fallen in the spring term overlapping mock results and the start of serious revision. UAE schools run reduced hours during it, which frees earlier afternoon slots and changes energy patterns through the day. The practical step is agreeing in advance that the session slot will move for that period, rather than losing two sessions and letting the arrangement lapse.

faqs.question: Can three sciences be covered in eight weeks?
faqs.answer: Not as syllabuses, and a provider claiming otherwise is selling. What eight weeks can do is the two or three highest-frequency causes of lost marks in the weakest discipline, plus the shared practical and data skills that benefit all three at once. Week one is diagnosis, weeks two and three the shared skills, weeks four to six timed papers in the weak discipline, week seven the avoided components, and week eight exam-room behaviour with no new content at all.

faqs.question: How should the exam timetable shape the final term?
faqs.answer: It shows where the pressure points and recovery windows fall, and both are plannable months ahead. Two papers in one day is a stamina test as much as a knowledge one, and one full rehearsal during study leave is worth more than several hours of topic revision. A two-day gap before a paper is the window for a final pass on named weak areas rather than for starting a topic. Get the version for your centre's zone from the school.

faqs.question: My child has a 5 in Coordinated Sciences. What do I ask next?
faqs.answer: For the paper-level breakdown, and specifically which discipline and which skill is responsible. In a combined award all three disciplines sit inside every paper, so a disappointing grade can come from weak physics content appearing throughout, from poor practical skills applied across all three, or from command-term errors in extended answers. Those need entirely different interventions and guessing between them wastes a term. The breakdown distinguishes them in minutes and schools hold it.

faqs.question: When do UAE candidates sit IGCSE science papers?
faqs.answer: In the June series and the November series. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a February window uses another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; its November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that using the wrong zone timetable can cost a candidate an exam.

faqs.question: How quickly does a Discovery Gardens family have to decide about a November science resit?
faqs.answer: Within days of August results rather than weeks. Published Pearson dates show the shape: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Review the paper-level breakdown in the first week with the exams officer involved. A near miss on one component in a science needed for an offer is a strong resit candidate; marks sitting evenly below target across every paper usually are not.

faqs.question: What is the best use of the winter and spring breaks?
faqs.answer: A short, planned block rather than either nothing or a full timetable. The breaks interrupt the Year 11 run-in twice and are the only periods with whole days available. Three or four well-targeted sessions across a break, on whole timed papers with marked feedback, achieves more than a daily schedule that collapses after three days. Agree the block before the break starts, because specialists fill those weeks quickly and the spring break often sits close to study leave.

faqs.question: What time can science sessions run for students in this community?
faqs.answer: Usually 17:00 or 17:30. Discovery Gardens is compact, so pickup is quicker than the villa communities nearby and students on the nearest Dubai Investments Park routes can be home by about 15:50, while those travelling the Al Barsha corridor arrive from about 16:30 and later with a revision clinic. Sessions run to 21:30 Gulf Standard Time, and during Ramadan reduced school hours open up earlier afternoon slots that are otherwise unavailable in Year 11.

faqs.question: Is it ever too late to start science tutoring?
faqs.answer: For some parts of the grade, yes, and we say so. Once the practical or alternative-to-practical component has been sat, those marks are fixed, which removes the cheapest available work. With three weeks remaining and three sciences, spreading hours across everything changes nothing measurable; the honest plan is one discipline and one skill. We would rather give that answer and lose the booking than take payment for a plan with no realistic path to a different result.

faqs.question: Why do families contact a tutor at the wrong moment?
faqs.answer: Because the trigger is a result, and results arrive after the relevant doors have closed. Mock results come after the practical technique window has narrowed, and a disappointing predicted grade often arrives after the entry and the award were fixed. The two good moments are the autumn of Year 10, when tier, award and technique are all still open, and the week after mocks, provided the paper-level breakdown comes with the grade.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic alongside three sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, under KHDA requirements, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Those occupy timetable space alongside three sciences, which is a large part of why the Year 11 week in this community is as tight as it is and why one tutored session has to be chosen carefully.

faqs.question: Should the whole eight weeks go on the weakest science?
faqs.answer: Mostly, with one deliberate exception. The shared practical and data skills benefit all three disciplines at once, so two or three weeks on those early is better value than the same hours inside one subject, and they may also close before the written papers. After that, concentrate on the weakest discipline rather than rotating, because rotation gives none of the three enough continuity to change anything measurable in the time available.

faqs.question: What does a calendar-led tutor ask that others do not?
faqs.answer: Which board and award, how many weeks remain, when the practical components fall, when the mocks are, and whether the paper-level breakdown exists. Those five answers determine what is reachable, and a provider who does not ask them will sell the same plan whatever month you call. It also means the plan changes as components close, rather than being a fixed weekly hour of general science support running to the same shape in October and April.

intro.heading: The question behind the search: does anyone here know this exact syllabus?
paragraphs: A Downtown Dubai parent typing "IGCSE science tutor near me" is almost never asking about distance. The real question is sharper and more anxious than that: my child is sitting a specific paper set by a specific board at a specific tier, the mark scheme rewards a particular kind of answer, and the last tutor we tried taught a different syllabus and did not notice. Is there anybody who knows this one?

That anxiety is well founded, because Dubai's science landscape is genuinely fragmented. The emirate's private schools licence seventeen different curricula, and the UK curriculum accounts for 37% of enrolment according to Dubai Media Office figures published in January 2025. Inside that UK share, schools choose independently between Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel and Oxford AQA. They then choose whether science is three separate IGCSEs, a co-ordinated double award worth two grades, or a single combined science award. They then choose, per candidate, between the Core and Extended tiers. And in Cambridge sciences the school decides whether candidates sit the laboratory practical test or the written alternative to practical. That is four independent decisions before a single topic is taught.

A tutor who gets any of those four wrong teaches confidently and uselessly. Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry cover overlapping content with different paper structures, different mark allocations and different command-term conventions. A student on Cambridge Core cannot be awarded above a grade C and should not be spending revision time on Extended-only material. A student sitting the alternative to practical paper needs a very different kind of preparation from one taking a practical test in a lab.

So the honest answer to "is there anyone near me" is that proximity is the wrong screen and specificity is the right one. The screen that matters is whether the tutor can name the paper structure for your child's code without looking it up. Because IB Gram teaches live online, the pool is every tutor who knows that code and is free at your hour, rather than the much smaller set who know it and also happen to live within a short drive of the Boulevard. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we offer only in India, and we say so rather than letting a parent discover it at booking.

This page is built to answer the question honestly. It shows you how to find out which syllabus your child is on, what each board's papers look like, how the tier and practical decisions change the preparation, what coverage we genuinely have and what we do when we have none, and what the Dubai market charges. Where a figure appears, the source is named.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-downtown-du.programmesIntro: IGCSE science in Dubai is a two-year course sat at 16, and it sits inside different structures depending on the school. These are the routes Downtown families are actually on, and what each one means for the kind of tutor they need.

programmes.name: Separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry and Physics taken as three independent IGCSEs, giving three grades. Cambridge codes are 0610, 0620 and 0625; Pearson Edexcel equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. This is the route most academically selective Dubai schools take for students heading towards A Level or IB Diploma sciences, and it carries the heaviest content load of the three options.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai this route is the standard expectation at British-curriculum schools with strong science departments, and it is the one that produces the most tutoring requests in Year 11. Three separate sciences means three sets of practical skills and three revision timetables, which is why students on this route most often need help with workload sequencing rather than content.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated or double award science
programmes.description: One course covering biology, chemistry and physics, leading to two IGCSE grades. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences is 0654; Pearson's Science Double Award is 4SD0. Content is reduced relative to three separate sciences but all three disciplines are still examined, which is why students often find it harder than expected: the breadth remains while the teaching time per discipline drops.
programmes.countryNote: A large number of Dubai schools use the double award for students taking nine or ten subjects, because it frees a timetable slot. Finding a tutor who has actually taught 0654 rather than the three separate syllabuses is harder than finding a biology tutor, and that scarcity is exactly where a local search fails a Downtown family.

programmes.name: Combined science, single award
programmes.description: Cambridge Combined Science, 0653, leads to a single IGCSE grade covering all three disciplines. It suits students whose strengths are elsewhere and who need science certificated without three grades' worth of content. The practical and theory structure mirrors the other Cambridge sciences, and the grade still counts towards the subject totals universities and the Ministry look at.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer Dubai schools offer the single award, and parents sometimes discover their child is on it only when option forms come back. If your child is on 0653 and a tutor starts teaching 0620 content, the mismatch will not be obvious for weeks, which is the clearest argument for matching on code rather than subject name.

programmes.name: Where IGCSE science leads next
programmes.description: After IGCSE, Dubai students split between A Level sciences and IB Diploma sciences. The IB route reorganises content into themes and adds a Scientific Investigation worth 20% of the subject grade. A Level goes deeper in a narrower space. Separate-science candidates have the smoothest transition into either; double-award candidates have a real content gap to close in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: This matters while choosing in Year 11, not afterwards. A Dubai student on the double award who wants Chemistry HL should be told in Year 11 that the first DP term will involve catching up, and should plan a short bridging block over the summer rather than discovering the gap in October.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-downtown-du.subjectsIntro: Downtown families book science tuition by discipline and by code. These are the IGCSE science subjects we are asked for most often, with what each one actually examines and where the marks tend to disappear.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Heavy on precise terminology and named processes. Extended adds depth across transport, coordination and inheritance. Marks are most often lost on command terms, where students describe a graph they were asked to explain, and on labelling that uses everyday words instead of syllabus vocabulary.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations, bonding, the periodic table and organic chemistry. Extended adds quantitative work including electrolysis and rates arithmetic. The commonest avoidable loss is in moles questions, where students can do the sum but set it out so untidily that method marks are not awarded.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: Forces, energy, waves, electricity, magnetism and atomic physics. Extended adds algebraic rearrangement and more multi-step calculation. Electricity is the topic Dubai students most often flag, and it is almost always a circuit-reading problem rather than an equation problem.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three disciplines in one course leading to two identical grades. The challenge is breadth against reduced teaching time, so students arrive at revision with thin coverage in whichever discipline their teacher knows least well. Tutors who have taught this specific code are genuinely scarce.

subjects.name: Cambridge Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade across all three disciplines, with a reduced content scope. Suits a student carrying nine or ten subjects who needs science certificated. Revision has to be guided by the syllabus content list rather than by a separate-science textbook, which over-covers and wastes time.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers with no separate practical examination; practical skills are assessed within the papers. The style rewards extended written explanation more than Cambridge does, and students moving between boards mid-course notice that first.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Two written papers covering principles of chemistry, inorganic, physical and organic chemistry. Practical skills are examined inside the papers. Calculation questions carry more marks per question than many students expect, which makes layout discipline worth real points.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers, each two hours, with calculators permitted throughout. Content spans forces and motion, electricity, waves, energy, magnetism, radioactivity and astrophysics. The astrophysics content catches students out because it is taught late and revised less.

subjects.name: Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: A single course leading to two IGCSE grades across the three disciplines. As with Cambridge's double award, the content is reduced but the breadth is not, and the main tutoring need is systematic coverage of whichever discipline the school taught thinnest.

subjects.name: Oxford AQA International GCSE sciences
subjects.description: Used by a smaller number of Dubai schools. Content and assessment differ from both Cambridge and Pearson, so a tutor needs to confirm which board before planning anything. Check the board name on the statement of entry rather than assuming from the textbook on the shelf.

sections.heading: How to find out which syllabus your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: This takes about ten minutes and it is the single most useful thing a parent can do before booking any science tutor. There are three reliable sources and one unreliable one. The reliable sources are the statement of entry the school issues for the exam series, which carries the board name and the syllabus code for every subject; the exams officer, who holds the entry data for every candidate; and the science department's curriculum overview, which most Dubai schools publish on their website. The unreliable source is the textbook on your child's shelf, which is frequently from a different board than the one they are entered for.

What you are looking for is four facts. First, the board: Cambridge International, Pearson Edexcel or Oxford AQA. Second, the award structure: three separate sciences, a double award worth two grades, or a single combined award. Third, the tier: Core or Extended for Cambridge, Foundation or Higher for Pearson where tiering applies. Fourth, for Cambridge sciences, whether candidates sit the practical test in a laboratory or the written alternative to practical paper.

Those four facts change what good tuition looks like, not just its label. A Core candidate who spends six weeks on Extended-only content has wasted six weeks and cannot be awarded above a grade C whatever they learn. A student sitting the alternative to practical needs drilled practice on reading apparatus diagrams and spotting the flawed method in a written scenario, which is a different exercise from handling real equipment. A double-award candidate following a separate-science revision guide is studying material that will not appear.

Once you have the four facts, the tutoring conversation changes character entirely. Instead of asking whether someone teaches chemistry, you can ask whether they have taught 0620 Extended with the alternative to practical, and the answer tells you something. That is a question a parent can ask with confidence in a five-minute call, and it filters harder than any claim on a website.

sections.heading: Why "near me" is the wrong filter for a syllabus problem
paragraphs: Proximity filtering made sense when the tutor had to be in the room. Applied to a syllabus-matching problem it does active harm, and the arithmetic is easy to see. Suppose a tutor needs to know Cambridge 0654 Extended with the alternative to practical route. That is a narrow specialism. Now require that the same person lives within a twenty-minute drive of Downtown Dubai and has a free hour at 6pm on a Tuesday. You have taken a small set and made it very nearly empty.

Parents feel the consequence as a sequence of near misses. The first tutor is a biology graduate who teaches 0610 well and has never seen 0654. The second taught Pearson in the UK and keeps referring to papers your child will not sit. The third is excellent and is full until February. By the time a family reaches a tutor who actually knows the code, a term has gone, and the conclusion they draw is that tutoring does not work.

Removing the distance constraint fixes this without changing anything else about the lesson. Your child sits in the apartment they came home to, opens a laptop at the hour that suits the bus, and works with someone whose only qualification for the slot is knowing the syllabus and being free. No parking in a tower basement, no security sign-in, no tutor stuck on Sheikh Zayed Road, and no compromise on the match in order to satisfy a radius.

We should be clear about what is lost rather than pretending nothing is. A tutor in the room can see a page, notice a student disengaging and manage a younger child. For a nine-year-old that matters a great deal. For a Year 11 student working past papers on a shared screen it matters much less than knowing the mark scheme. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE in any case, and home tutoring remains a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: Core against Extended, and the decision that caps a grade
paragraphs: Cambridge sciences are tiered, and the tier decision has a consequence that catches Dubai parents late. A Core candidate is assessed on a reduced content set and can be awarded grades C to G. An Extended candidate is assessed on the full content and can be awarded A* to E. The ceiling is structural. No amount of revision moves a Core candidate above a C, because the papers they sit do not contain the questions that award higher grades.

Schools make this decision for sensible reasons, usually based on Year 10 performance and on how many subjects a student is carrying. It is often the right call: a student who would be overwhelmed by Extended across three sciences may do far better with Core grades in hand and a realistic workload. The problem is not the decision; it is that families sometimes learn about it only when a revision guide does not match the class, and by then the entry may already be submitted.

What a tutor can do about it depends entirely on timing. Early in Year 10, a short intensive block aimed at the specific weaknesses behind the Core recommendation can genuinely change the conversation with the school, and some students move tier. Midway through Year 11, the entry is usually set and the honest advice is to stop fighting it and maximise the grade available. A tutor who claims otherwise in February is selling hope.

sections.heading: The practical component: a laboratory test or a written alternative
paragraphs: This is the Cambridge detail most parents in Dubai have never been told, and it changes a fifth of the grade. For Cambridge sciences, the practical component carries 20% of the final mark, and candidates take either a practical test conducted in a school laboratory or a written alternative-to-practical paper. The school decides which, and different schools in the same district make different choices. Pearson handles this differently again, assessing practical skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate component.

The preparation diverges sharply. A practical test rewards handling apparatus accurately under time pressure: reading a thermometer to the right precision, setting up a circuit that works, recording to consistent decimal places while the clock runs. That is laboratory work and it is done at school. A written alternative-to-practical paper rewards something else entirely: reading a described method and identifying the flaw, completing a results table, plotting and interpreting a graph from supplied data, and suggesting a specific improvement in mark-scheme language. That is desk work, and it can be taught very effectively over a shared screen.

The practical irony is that the component parents assume cannot be tutored remotely is, for most Dubai candidates, precisely the one that can. If your child's school enters candidates for the alternative-to-practical paper, almost everything they need is trainable at a desk with past questions. If the school enters for the practical test, the tutoring value lies in the planning and analysis around the bench work rather than in the handling itself, and that should be stated plainly rather than glossed.

So the first question in a trial lesson for a Cambridge science student is not which topic is hard. It is which practical route the school has entered them for. If a tutor does not ask that in the first session, they do not know the syllabus as well as they said.

sections.heading: What we actually cover, and what we do when nobody covers it
paragraphs: No tutoring provider in Dubai publishes its coverage limits, and that silence is why parents end up with the near-miss sequence described above. Here is ours, stated as plainly as we can. Cambridge and Pearson separate sciences are well covered at both tiers, because they are the highest-volume codes in the market and most science tutors have taught them. Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences is covered but thinner, because fewer tutors have taught the double award specifically rather than the three subjects separately. Cambridge 0653 Combined Science is thinner still. Oxford AQA sciences are the narrowest coverage we have, and we will tell you that before you book rather than after.

When a request arrives that we cannot match well, the options are a wait with a named date, a tutor strong in the underlying discipline with the code-specific gap stated openly so you can judge it, or a different hour where a better-matched tutor is free. What we will not do is take the booking and hope the discipline knowledge carries the code difference, because with double awards and tier differences it frequently does not.

There is a second disclosure that belongs here. Some of our science tutors are UAE residents; others teach from India, where our in-home service operates, and work with Dubai students over live video in Gulf Standard Time. We do not route UAE families to a non-UAE phone number while implying a local presence, and we do not claim an office in Dubai, because we do not have one. sections.heading: The June and November series, and what a resit really costs
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit two series a year. Cambridge runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests at other points in the year. The February and March series that circulates in some revision forums is offered to India only and does not apply to a child in Dubai; quoting those dates to a UAE parent is a planning error, not a detail.

Cambridge also divides centres into administrative zones. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. For a Dubai family that means the timetable your child works from must be the one the school issues, not one downloaded from a search result.

Pearson publishes its own pattern openly. Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results reach students in January; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is exactly why any plan should be built from the live official timetable rather than from dates restated on a tutoring page.

The practical point for a Downtown family is the gap between the series. A November resit decision made in late August gives roughly eight weeks of preparation and a January result. A June resit decision gives a longer runway and an August result. Which one suits depends on whether the grade is needed for a sixth-form place in September, and that is a conversation to have with the school's exams officer in the week results arrive, not a month later.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tuition costs in Dubai, per subject and in total
paragraphs: A parent with a child sitting three separate sciences is not buying one tutor. That is the arithmetic most cost conversations in this market skip, and it is the reason tuition budgets break in Year 11 rather than Year 10. The honest way to price it is per subject per week, then multiplied by how many sciences are genuinely in trouble, which is usually one or two rather than three.

Taking the published rates: Unitors lists IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour, which for one weekly session is roughly AED 600 a month per subject. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates weekly one-hour tutoring at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. At the cheaper end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to AED 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, which buys a university student or generalist. At the premium end, TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for named or examiner-linked tutors. In-home rates sit higher with travel included: Bestimate records AED 180 to AED 350, and independent home tutors AED 200 to AED 500.

Run that across two sciences for a Year 11 student and a mid-market online arrangement comes to roughly AED 1,200 to AED 1,600 a month, while the equivalent in-home arrangement sits closer to AED 2,500 to AED 3,500 once travel is inside the rate. Advertised monthly packages in this market illustrate the same gap: around AED 799 for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Every figure here belongs to the provider named beside it and none of them is an IB Gram price; we quote after the free trial, once we know the code, the tier and the frequency.

A useful piece of context: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. School fees are flat; tuition is the line that is not. That is a reason to spend on the one or two sciences that genuinely need it rather than on a defensive package covering all three.

sections.heading: What a parent can verify in ten minutes before booking anyone
paragraphs: Everything on this page reduces to a short list of checkable questions, and they work on any provider, not only on us. Ask which syllabus code the tutor has taught, and listen for whether the answer contains a number. Ask which tier your child is entered for and whether the tutor will teach to it. Ask, for a Cambridge science, whether the school enters candidates for the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and whether the tutor has prepared students for that route. Ask whether the first lesson is free and what happens if the match is wrong.

Two further checks are about the provider rather than the teaching. Ask whether the tutor holds a MoHRE private tuition work permit. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as unverified.

Then ask about regulatory claims, because this is where the Dubai market is weakest. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and inspects schools annually. It does not inspect or rate individual private tutors. A separate KHDA Educational Services Permit applies to training institutes operating with premises and staff. IB Gram holds no such permit and runs no centre, office or branch in the UAE, which is why no address appears on this page. Any provider implying regulatory endorsement of its individual tutors is describing something that does not exist.

Finally, ask what happens with your child's data. We ask for the school, the year group, the subject code and the time your child is home, because those four things determine the match. We do not need grades, a report card or a photograph, and we do not ask for them. Under UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on personal data protection you can ask what is held and ask for it to be deleted, and a provider that cannot answer that question quickly is telling you something.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science syllabus my child is sitting?
faqs.answer: Three reliable sources. The statement of entry the school issues for the exam series carries the board name and the syllabus code for every subject. The exams officer holds the entry data for every candidate and can confirm it in a short email. The science department's curriculum overview, which most Dubai schools publish, usually names the board. The unreliable source is the textbook on the shelf, which is frequently from a different board than the one your child is entered for. You want four facts: board, award structure, tier, and for Cambridge sciences the practical route.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences and taking three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: 0654 is a double award: one course covering biology, chemistry and physics, leading to two identical IGCSE grades. Three separate sciences are three courses leading to three grades, using codes 0610, 0620 and 0625. The content in the double award is reduced, but the breadth is not, so students often find it harder than expected because teaching time per discipline drops while all three disciplines remain examined. Tutors who have taught 0654 specifically, rather than the three subjects separately, are genuinely scarcer, which is worth asking about directly.

faqs.question: Can a Cambridge Core science candidate in Dubai still get an A?
faqs.answer: No, and it is better to know that early. Cambridge Core candidates are assessed on a reduced content set and can be awarded grades C to G. Extended candidates are assessed on the full content and can be awarded A* to E. The ceiling is structural rather than a matter of effort, because the Core papers do not contain the questions that award higher grades. If your child is early in Year 10 a tier change can sometimes be discussed with the school. By the middle of Year 11 the entry is usually set and the sensible aim is every mark available within Core.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam for IGCSE science in Dubai, or a written paper instead?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school, and this is the detail most parents are never told. For Cambridge sciences the practical component carries 20% of the grade, and candidates take either a practical test in a school laboratory or a written alternative-to-practical paper. The school chooses, and schools in the same district choose differently. Pearson assesses practical skills inside its written papers instead, with no separate component. Ask your exams officer which route applies, because the preparation for the two is almost entirely different.

faqs.question: Can the alternative-to-practical paper be prepared for online?
faqs.answer: Yes, and unusually well. The paper supplies a described method or a set of results and asks the candidate to identify a flaw, complete a table, plot and interpret a graph, read apparatus to an appropriate precision, and suggest a specific improvement in mark-scheme language. All of that is desk work built on past questions, which is exactly what a shared screen is good for. The component parents assume cannot be tutored remotely is, for candidates on this route, the one that responds fastest to remote practice.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science topics do Dubai students struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Three come up repeatedly in enquiries from the central corridor. Electricity in physics, which is almost always a circuit-reading problem rather than an equation problem, and responds quickly to drilled diagram practice. Moles and quantitative chemistry, where students can do the arithmetic but set it out so untidily that method marks go unawarded. And command-term discipline across all three sciences, where a student describes a graph they were asked to explain and writes a true answer that scores nothing.

faqs.question: Is Pearson Edexcel IGCSE science easier than Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Neither is easier; they reward different things, and a student who moves between them mid-course feels the difference immediately. Pearson's separate international GCSE sciences are untiered, graded 9 to 1, assessed by two written papers with practical skills examined inside them, and the style leans towards extended written explanation. Cambridge is tiered Core or Extended, has a separate practical component worth 20%, and uses a tighter question style. The right question is not which is easier but which one your child is entered for.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science exams held for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit two series a year. Cambridge runs International GCSE examinations in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. The February and March series sometimes mentioned online is offered to India only and does not apply in the UAE. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, so work from the version your school issues.

faqs.question: Should my child resit IGCSE science in November or wait for June?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the grade is needed for. A November entry decided in late August gives roughly eight weeks of preparation and a result in January; Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A June entry gives a much longer runway and an August result, with June 2026 results reaching students on 20 August 2026. If a sixth-form or A Level place in September depends on the grade, November is usually the only option that arrives in time. Book a meeting with the exams officer in the week the original result lands.

faqs.answer: Price it per subject per week and then multiply. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour, so one weekly session per subject is roughly AED 600 a month each, around AED 1,200 for two. faqs.answer: We tell you. Cambridge and Pearson separate sciences are well covered at both tiers. Cambridge 0654 double award is covered but thinner, 0653 single award thinner still, and Oxford AQA sciences are our narrowest coverage. When we cannot match well the options are a named wait, a different hour where a better-matched tutor is free, or a discipline specialist with the code-specific gap described openly so you can judge it. faqs.question: My child is on the science double award but wants IB Chemistry HL. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a manageable gap if it is identified in Year 11 rather than in October of DP1. A double award covers all three disciplines with reduced content per discipline, so a student moving into a Higher Level single science starts with thinner foundations than a separate-science candidate. The practical answer is a short bridging block over the summer aimed at the specific topics the double award trimmed, particularly quantitative chemistry. Schools will usually tell you which topics those are if asked directly, and that list makes an efficient four-session plan.

faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted rather than unregulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it. Individuals without one face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule.

We do not need grades, report cards or photographs and do not ask for them. If you choose to send a marked past paper it helps the tutor diagnose faster and is used only for that. intro.heading: Three routes wearing one name, and what each one closes
paragraphs: 'IGCSE science' describes at least three different things and the difference matters more than almost anything else a tutor will tell you. Three separate sciences means biology, chemistry and physics taken as individual subjects with individual grades. A double award - Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SC1 - compresses all three into the equivalent of two subjects with two identical grades. A single combined science, such as Cambridge 0653, compresses them into one.

The consequence appears at sixth form rather than at sixteen. A student with three separate science grades can usually take any of the three at A Level or at Diploma Higher Level. A double-award student can often continue one or two sciences, depending on the school's entry rules. A combined-science student frequently cannot continue any science at the higher levels, and nobody mentions this when the option form is signed in Year 9.

In this cluster the routes vary by school. Dubai International Academic City is a university free zone whose own secondary, Dubai English Speaking College, runs the British route through IGCSE to A Level. Across the junction in Silicon Oasis, in Mirdif, Al Warqa and Al Qusais, schools make their own decisions about which routes they offer and which students they place on each. The same child could be entered differently at two schools a few kilometres apart.

The second thing to settle is how practical work is assessed, because it differs by board and by school choice. Cambridge sciences offer either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the school decides. Pearson's 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SC1 have no practical examination and assess experimental skills inside the written papers instead. A student revising apparatus technique for a paper that does not test it directly has misallocated weeks.

The third is that science marks are lost in predictable places that are not content. Command terms, where 'describe' and 'explain' carry different mark allocations and students answer both the same way. Units omitted. Graph work where the axes are read wrongly before any thinking happens. Specific practical vocabulary - separation techniques, gas tests - where a vague answer earns nothing even when the science is understood.

There is also a cost argument specific to this route question. A triple-science family often buys three tutors when one timed paper in each subject would show that a single science is carrying the entire problem. Chemistry is the usual culprit in this cluster, generally because of mole calculations at the higher tiers, but the papers should decide rather than the pattern. One diagnostic session ahead of any booking routinely cuts the monthly commitment by two thirds.

IB Gram delivers this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. Apparatus handling happens in the school laboratory under any arrangement, and the marks in the written practical components sit in skills that are taught better on a shared screen with real data than standing beside a clamp stand.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 science, Years 7 to 9

The gaps that cause trouble later are numerical rather than conceptual: rearranging formulae, handling units and prefixes, reading a scale precisely, and plotting a graph with a sensible scale. programmes.name: Three separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology, chemistry and physics as individual subjects, each with its own papers and grade. The heaviest content load of the three routes and the one that keeps every onward option open. Students on this route who struggle usually struggle in one of the three rather than across all, which makes targeted tutoring unusually efficient.

programmes.name: Double award: Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SC1
programmes.description: All three sciences compressed into the equivalent of two subjects, with two identical grades awarded. Content is reduced but the examination still moves between biology, chemistry and physics inside a single paper, and students lose real time re-orienting between them. dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-acade.subjectsIntro: Science tutoring is subject work even when the qualification is combined. These are the areas families in this cluster raise, with the specific demand each makes.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and exchange
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, circulation and gas exchange. Marks go on explanations that name a structure without saying what its feature achieves - large surface area, thin wall, moist lining - which is the form the mark scheme credits.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid crosses, probability, variation and selection. Genetics questions reward drawing the cross out on paper rather than attempting it mentally, which is a habit rather than knowledge and is worth several marks a paper.

subjects.name: Biology: enzymes, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: Rate graphs, limiting factors and the experimental contexts both appear in. The recurring loss is explaining a plateau on a graph by describing it instead of naming the limiting factor and saying why it caps the rate.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Mass to moles, concentration, reacting masses and percentage yield. The highest-return topic in IGCSE chemistry at the higher tiers, because the calculations appear inside questions across the whole paper rather than in one section.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and redox
subjects.description: Products at each electrode, half-equations and the reasoning behind which ion is discharged. Marks are lost on half-equations and on predictions stated without the reasoning that justifies them, which is where the marks actually sit.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and separation techniques
subjects.description: Homologous series, basic reactions, and the practical vocabulary for filtration, crystallisation, distillation and chromatography. Practical questions reward exact terminology, and vague descriptions score nothing even when the method is understood.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits. The heaviest mark load in IGCSE physics and the largest source of confusion. Students lose marks on circuit reasoning stated as assertion rather than derived from the relationships.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and energy
subjects.description: Speed and acceleration graphs, forces, moments and energy transfer. Graph questions dominate, and the recurring error is calculating a gradient from two data points rather than from widely separated points on the line of best fit.

subjects.name: Physics: waves, magnetism and radioactivity
subjects.description: Wave properties, electromagnetic effects and nuclear decay. Mostly a numerical-discipline problem: unit prefixes, powers of ten and conversions applied inconsistently inside one calculation, which costs marks the student thinks they earned.

subjects.name: Experimental skills and the written practical components
subjects.description: Variables, range and interval, repeats, precision, significant figures, plotting, lines of best fit and evaluations that name a specific limitation. Examined in the Cambridge alternative-to-practical and inside Pearson's written papers, and teachable entirely on a screen.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline across the three sciences
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate specify different answers with different mark allocations. Students answer nearly everything as describe, which is the most comfortable mode and the lowest scoring on the extended questions.

subjects.name: Double-award paper navigation
subjects.description: The specific skill of switching between biology, chemistry and physics inside a single paper without losing time to re-orientation. Practised under timed conditions by paper section rather than by subject, which is the opposite of how most students revise.

sections.heading: Which science route is your child actually on?
paragraphs: This is the question to answer before anything else, and the answer comes from the examinations officer rather than from the class teacher. Ask for the entry list: subject, board, syllabus code, tier and option. Three separate sciences will appear as three entries with three codes. A double award appears as one entry - Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SC1 - and yields two identical grades. A single combined science appears as one entry yielding one grade.

The practical difference during the course is content volume and paper architecture. Separate sciences carry the most content and the cleanest structure, with each paper confined to one subject. The double award reduces content and keeps the breadth, but its papers move between biology, chemistry and physics, which costs students time they do not budget for. Combined science reduces content furthest.

The difference that lasts is what each route permits afterwards. Entry rules for A Level and for IB Diploma sciences are set by the receiving sixth form, not by the board, and they vary across this cluster. Some schools accept a double award for A Level entry in a science; some require the separate subject; some require a specific grade. This is a question to put in writing to two sixth forms during Year 10.

The table below sets out the three routes with what each typically permits. Treat the last column as a prompt to ask rather than as an answer, because the only authoritative version is the receiving school's own published entry requirements for your child's year group.

sections.heading: How each board assesses practical work
paragraphs: This is where revision most often goes astray, because the boards differ and the school adds a further choice on top. Cambridge sciences offer either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the school decides which its candidates sit. Pearson's International GCSE sciences - 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and the Science Double Award 4SC1 - have no practical examination at all and assess experimental skills inside the written papers.

For a Cambridge candidate entered for the practical examination, apparatus familiarity matters directly: reading instruments, following a method under time pressure, recording as you go. For a Cambridge candidate on the alternative-to-practical, the same skills are tested on paper through described experiments and supplied data. For a Pearson candidate, experimental skills appear as method-design and data-analysis questions inside the theory papers.

The skills themselves overlap almost entirely, which is the useful news. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables. Choosing a sensible range and interval. Deciding how many repeats and why. Reading a scale to the appropriate precision. Recording to consistent significant figures. Plotting with a sensible scale. Drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points. Writing an evaluation that names one specific limitation and one realistic improvement.

Every item on that list can be taught on a shared screen with a real dataset, which is why online science tutoring works better than parents expect. What cannot be taught that way is handling the apparatus itself, and that belongs in the school laboratory under any arrangement. Ask the school which component your child is entered for before buying any revision aimed at practical work.

sections.heading: Where science marks actually go, subject by subject
paragraphs: Mark two timed science papers properly and the losses sort into a short list that is mostly not content. Command terms account for the largest share: 'describe' and 'explain' carry different mark allocations and students answer both the same way, which costs marks on every extended question in the paper. Units omitted or wrongly converted account for the next share. Graph questions where the axes were read carelessly before any thinking happened account for a third.

The subject-specific losses are equally predictable. In biology, explanations that name a structure without saying what its feature achieves, and genetics crosses attempted mentally rather than drawn. In chemistry, half-equations, mole calculations at the higher tiers, and vague practical vocabulary where exact terminology was required. In physics, circuit reasoning asserted rather than derived, and gradients calculated from two data points rather than from the line of best fit.

None of this is a failure of understanding, which is why technique work moves a science grade faster than content revision in the final months. A student losing six or eight marks a paper to command terms and units can recover most of them in six to eight sessions, and that is a better return than the same hours spent re-reading notes on topics they already know.

The method for finding your child's own list: have one timed paper in each science marked question by question against the published mark scheme, with the reason for each lost mark written in the student's own words. Three or four reasons will dominate. That becomes the lesson plan, and the error log is checked for recurrence every session. It is also how you find out which of three sciences is actually carrying the problem.

sections.heading: Academic City, Silicon Oasis, Mirdif and International City compared
paragraphs: Families in this cluster shop by comparison, so it is worth doing the comparison honestly. What differs between these four neighbourhoods is the length of the school run, the time a weekday session can realistically begin, and whether a child can continue sciences at the same school into sixth form. What does not differ is the supply of tutors who teach a named international science specification at the higher tiers.

Academic City has one real structural advantage: Dubai English Speaking College runs the British route from IGCSE through to A Level on site, so a student there can continue sciences without changing schools. Silicon Oasis and Mirdif have schools inside the district with short runs, making a 4.45pm session realistic. International City has no international school at all within the district, so children travel out and weekday sessions start around six.

On tutor supply, the comparison collapses in the same way it does for every subject in this cluster. The number of people in eastern Dubai who teach Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SC1 routinely, and who hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, is small everywhere. A Mirdif family has a marginally better chance than one in Al Khawaneej, and neither has a choice worth calling a choice.

The practical conclusion from all four addresses is therefore the same: choose on whether the tutor knows the route and the specification, and let the delivery be online so that choice exists. The timing differences in these neighbourhoods are worth planning around, particularly for a triple-science student needing help in two subjects. The geography differences are not worth paying a travel premium for.

sections.heading: The sixth-form consequence, spelled out
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a science tutor can do for a Year 10 family in this cluster is make them ask one question of two sixth forms, in writing, before Year 11 begins: what IGCSE science route and grade do you require for entry to A Level biology, chemistry and physics, and to the equivalent Diploma courses? The answers vary, they are not always published clearly, and they are the only thing that makes the Year 9 route decision legible in hindsight.

Where the answer rules out a route the child is already on, there is a window. Some schools will consider moving a student from combined science to the double award, or from double to separate sciences, during Year 10, if there is evidence of performance at the higher route. The evidence a school wants is marked papers at that route under timed conditions, which is precisely what a targeted block of tutoring can produce in a term.

By the second term of Year 11 the window has closed in almost every school. Entries are made, content is nearly complete, and the remaining lever is technique within the route already chosen. Technique is worth real marks and it cannot change what the qualification permits afterwards, which is why this conversation belongs in Year 10 rather than in Year 12 when the consequence arrives.

For completeness: Ministry of Education equivalency is a separate and much lower bar. The published British-track requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. A double award counts as two of the five. Equivalency is not the number to plan science routes around.

sections.heading: The June and November series, and the resit question in science
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so any advice to prepare for a February science paper is advice for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

Useful sourced reference points: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, so any date you plan around should come from the live official timetable rather than a summary.

One Cambridge detail that belongs in every science plan: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Science candidates often sit several papers in a short window, which makes the zone check more than a formality.

On resits, science has a wrinkle the other subjects do not. A double-award or combined-science resit means resitting the whole award rather than one science, which is a much larger undertaking than repairing one weak paper. For separate sciences, ask for the component breakdown and resit the single subject that failed. That distinction alone often decides whether a November entry is sensible.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs here, and what each band contains
paragraphs: Every figure below was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram rate. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. That band is usable for Core-tier and combined-science content support and rarely contains anybody fluent in Extended-tier chemistry calculations or the alternative-to-practical technique.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. This is where most useful IGCSE science tutoring in Dubai actually happens. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home one-to-one including travel runs AED 180 to 500, per Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500.

The arithmetic for a triple-science student matters here. Three sciences at one session a week each, at the mid band, is a substantial monthly commitment - published monthly figures include AED 799 for eight online sessions, and Bestimate's mid-range estimate for a weekly hour is AED 600 to 1,200 a month per subject. Which is exactly why the diagnostic matters: most triple-science students need one subject tutored properly, not three.

Context on education costs generally: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For our own rates, the free trial lesson comes first and the figure is quoted against the specification and the work the diagnosis identifies.

sections.heading: Checking the tutor, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you. Ask the individual teaching your child whether they hold a current permit and ask to see it.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated two-working-day completion time.

One arrangement to decline rather than seek: the permit's code of conduct bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and in Abu Dhabi ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. An offer of your child's own science teacher, privately, is a problem for the teacher before it is a benefit to you.

And what we do not claim. No office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE. No KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is the permit issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai. No approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. No published star ratings we cannot evidence with countable reviews, no guaranteed grades, and no supplied board papers or mark schemes - we cite and link the official sources instead.

faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your address, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. faqs.question: Is my child taking three sciences, a double award or combined science?

faqs.question: Does the double award close off A Level sciences?

Some accept a double award for A Level entry in a science, some require the separate subject, and some require a specific grade. Put the question in writing to two sixth forms during Year 10, because that is the window in which a school may still move a student to a different route with marked evidence.

faqs.question: Why does my son run out of time on the Co-ordinated Sciences paper?
faqs.answer: Because the paper moves between biology, chemistry and physics inside a single booklet and he is paying a re-orientation cost at every switch. It is a real and specific effect that content revision does not touch. The fix is to revise by paper section rather than by subject, and to practise the transitions under timed conditions until switching stops costing a minute each time. Most students have never been told the paper is structured that way.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical examination for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board and the school. Cambridge sciences offer either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper, and the school decides which its candidates sit. Pearson's International GCSE sciences - 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and the Science Double Award 4SC1 - have no practical examination and assess experimental skills inside the written papers instead. Ask the school which component your child is entered for before buying revision aimed at practical technique.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences should we actually get a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Have one timed paper in each science marked question by question against the published mark scheme and the answer is usually obvious. Most triple-science students are losing marks in one subject rather than across all three, and most families discover this only after paying for three tutors for a term. Chemistry carries the problem more often than the others in this cluster, usually because of mole calculations at the higher tiers, but the paper should decide rather than the pattern.

faqs.question: Which skills does the written practical component award marks for?
faqs.answer: Not dexterity. It tests whether a student can identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, choose a sensible range and interval, justify a number of repeats, read a scale to the appropriate precision, record to consistent significant figures, plot with a sensible scale, draw a line of best fit rather than joining points, and write an evaluation naming one specific limitation and one realistic improvement. All of that is taught on a screen with a real dataset, which is why it suits online sessions.

faqs.question: My daughter knows the biology but her answers score two out of four. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually the command term and the structure of the explanation. Mark schemes in biology credit the link from a feature to what it achieves: a large surface area for faster diffusion, a thin wall for a shorter path, a moist lining for dissolving gases. A student who names the structure without making that link has described rather than explained. Underlining the command term before writing, and knowing that explain means causes, moves marks across every extended question in the paper.

faqs.question: Is Mirdif or Academic City better placed for IGCSE science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Academic City has one real structural advantage: its secondary runs the British route from IGCSE through to A Level on site, so a student can continue sciences without changing school. Mirdif and Silicon Oasis have shorter school runs, which makes a 4.45pm session realistic. On tutor supply the comparison collapses: the number of people in eastern Dubai teaching Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SC1 routinely is small everywhere, which is the argument for matching online rather than by distance.

faqs.question: Can we move my son from combined science to the double award?
faqs.answer: Possibly, in Year 10, with evidence. Some schools in this cluster will consider a move upwards if a student can show performance at the higher route under timed conditions, and marked papers at that route are the evidence they want. By the second term of Year 11 entries are made and the window has closed in almost every school. If a science at sixth form is a realistic ambition, raise it with the school in Year 10 rather than waiting for the Year 11 mocks.

faqs.question: How much would three science tutors cost in eastern Dubai?
faqs.answer: At the mid band it is a substantial monthly figure, which is precisely why the diagnostic matters. Market rates read in October 2026: qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; published monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions; Bestimate's mid-range estimate for a weekly hour is AED 600 to 1,200 a month. Most triple-science students need one subject tutored properly rather than three tutored thinly.

faqs.question: Should a double-award student resit in November?
faqs.answer: It is a bigger decision than for separate sciences, because resitting a double award usually means resitting the whole award rather than the one science that went wrong. For separate sciences you can ask for the component breakdown and resit the single weak subject. Request the breakdown either way as soon as results arrive. Note also the timing: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, after most sixth-form courses had already started.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science papers sat in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two; the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Science candidates often sit several papers in a short window, which makes one Cambridge detail important: every centre is allocated to one of six timetable zones, and Cambridge says using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's own risk.

faqs.question: Must a tutor teaching IGCSE science in Dubai hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so it cannot be priced into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any amount quoted at you as unverified. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents and university students.

faqs.question: Will the tutor send us the practical papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. That material belongs to Cambridge and Pearson and reproducing or distributing it is a copyright matter. We cite and link the official sources on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, which is also the only place certain to hold the current version rather than a specification two revisions out of date. Schools hold past papers and will usually release them to candidates, and the subject teacher is the fastest route to the right tier, option and variant.

intro.heading: What Creek Harbour families pay for IGCSE science, and what it buys
paragraphs: Start with the cheapest option, because that is where most families begin and where the decision is usually settled. Tutopiya advertises online tutoring from about AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. At that price the tutor is typically a university student or a recent graduate, and for a Year 9 or Year 10 student who needs homework supervised and arithmetic steadied, it is defensible value. It becomes poor value at a specific point: when the problem is not understanding the science but producing it in the form an IGCSE paper rewards, under time, with the command term obeyed.

One tier up, published figures change shape. Unitors lists IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Dubai 2026 rate table puts specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level tutoring at AED 200 to 450 and above. In-home one-to-one visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutoring. Three of the six competitor pages researched in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not a currency a Dubai family transacts in.

What makes this difficult is that none of those tiers advertises itself differently. Every listing says experienced, qualified and results-driven. So the useful question is not what a tutor costs but what the price is actually buying, and for IGCSE science the answer is specific. The cheap tier buys supervision and confidence. The middle tier buys subject competence. The specialist tier buys knowledge of the paper structure, the tiering decision, the command terms and the practical assessment format for the exact syllabus code your child was entered for, which is where IGCSE science marks are genuinely won and lost.

Creek Harbour matters to this arithmetic in one particular way. The district is new and has limited school provision inside its own boundary, so families here commute to schools in Al Jaddaf, Al Garhoud, Nad Al Sheba and Al Quoz, and any tutor driving to a Creek Harbour tower in the late afternoon crosses the Ras Al Khor approaches at their worst. That driving time is inside the in-home hourly rate whether or not it is itemised. The gap between the online specialist band and the in-home band is, to a large extent, the price of someone's commute rather than the price of better teaching.

IB Gram publishes no hourly price list on these pages, because the right arrangement depends on level, subject count and frequency, and a single number would be less honest than none. What we publish is the market with its sources, so you can judge any quote including ours. Lessons for UAE families are delivered live, one-to-one, over video, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India, and that is stated here rather than discovered later. The rest of this page covers where the money goes wrong, how the science routes differ in cost, what the boards actually do differently, and the entry and equivalency costs that sit behind the tutoring bill.
