dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-creek.programmesIntro: IGCSE science is not one product, and the cost of supporting it depends almost entirely on which route your child's school entered them for. These are the routes we cover and what each one demands in hours.

programmes.name: Separate sciences: Biology, Chemistry, Physics
programmes.description: Three distinct qualifications, three sets of papers, three grades. Cambridge codes are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics; Pearson's International GCSE equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. This is the route for a student heading towards A Level or IB sciences, and it is the most expensive to support because tutoring hours multiply by subject rather than being shared across one course.
programmes.countryNote: Most British-curriculum schools around Al Jaddaf, Al Garhoud and Nad Al Sheba enter stronger science students for separate sciences. For a Creek Harbour family that means deciding whether to fund one subject properly or three subjects thinly. Our consistent advice is one properly: a student with a secure method in Chemistry usually transfers that method into Physics on their own, whereas three hours a week spread thin tends to produce three unfinished conversations.

programmes.name: Combined and Coordinated Science
programmes.description: A single award covering biology, chemistry and physics content at reduced depth. Cambridge offers Coordinated Science as a double award, syllabus 0654, and Combined Science as a single award, 0653; Pearson offers an International GCSE Science (Double Award) route. Fewer papers and less content, which makes it cheaper to support, but it closes some A Level and IB Higher Level science routes, so the saving has a consequence worth checking before Year 10.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools use these routes for students carrying a heavy subject load or needing a science award without three separate grades. For equivalency purposes, what counts is the five-subject rule rather than which science route was taken, but for A Level and IB Diploma entry individual schools set their own expectations. Ask the head of science directly rather than inferring it, before any tutoring budget is committed.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9 science foundations
programmes.description: The cheapest place to spend money on science and the place families spend least. Three terms of patient work on units, rearranging formulae, graph drawing and writing a method clearly removes most of what later presents as an IGCSE problem. Lower-tier tutoring at AED 45 to 65 an hour is genuinely appropriate here, which is worth saying on a page about cost.
programmes.countryNote: For Creek Harbour families this is the stage where a budget online tutor delivers real value, because the work is supervision and habit rather than examination technique. We will say so rather than selling a specialist. The money is better kept for Year 11, when paper technique for a specific syllabus code starts to matter and a generalist stops being enough.

programmes.name: The route into A Level or the IB Diploma
programmes.description: IGCSE grades decide which sciences a student may continue and at what level. A strong Extended grade in Chemistry supports Chemistry HL in the Diploma or A Level Chemistry; a Core entry generally does not. This is the real financial argument for spending in Year 10 rather than Year 11, because an entry-tier decision made on weak mock performance is expensive to unwind later.
programmes.countryNote: Creek Harbour students split between A Level routes at British schools in Al Garhoud and Nad Al Sheba and Diploma routes at IB schools in Al Jaddaf and Nad Al Sheba. Both read IGCSE science grades closely. Where a student is borderline, the cheapest intervention is usually targeted work before the tiering decision rather than remedial work after it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-creek.subjectsIntro: These are the science and supporting subjects we cover at IGCSE for this district, with the syllabus codes where they are the thing that determines what a tutor needs to know.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Marks concentrate in moles and concentration, electrolysis and organic reaction types. The commonest avoidable loss is an unbalanced equation carried through a correct calculation. Practical skills are assessed on paper, so a student who has done the experiment still needs to practise describing it.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity is the topic that decides grades, followed by moments and pressure. Unit prefixes cost more marks than any concept. Graph work rewards a practised method: axes, scale, best-fit line, gradient with units, in that order and every time.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Terminology precision decides the grade more than understanding does. The difference between 'state', 'describe' and 'explain' is worth several marks per paper. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance are where Extended students most often lose structured marks.

subjects.name: Coordinated Science (Double Award)
subjects.description: One award covering all three sciences at reduced depth, with its own paper structure rather than a selection from the separate sciences. Tutoring has to follow the Coordinated specification, because a tutor teaching separate-science content will cover material the student is not assessed on.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Single Award)
subjects.description: A single grade across the three sciences with the lightest content load of the science routes. Appropriate for a student with a heavy timetable, and worth checking against intended post-16 routes, because some A Level and IB Higher Level science entry expectations are not met by it.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: The subject that most often masquerades as a science problem. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and graph interpretation all appear inside science papers. A student losing Physics marks on algebra needs maths sessions, and we will say so rather than billing for Physics.

subjects.name: IGCSE Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by stronger mathematicians heading to A Level Maths or Maths AA HL. Useful alongside separate sciences because the algebraic fluency feeds directly into Physics and Chemistry calculation work.

subjects.name: IGCSE English as a Second Language
subjects.description: Relevant to science outcomes more than parents expect, because an Extended science paper demands written explanation. A student whose science marks drop on extended-response questions and not on calculation is often facing a language task rather than a science one.

subjects.name: IGCSE Computer Science
subjects.description: Commonly taken alongside separate sciences by students heading to engineering. Marks are lost on documenting logic rather than on coding, which surprises confident programmers and is fixable with structured practice.

subjects.name: IGCSE Geography and Environmental Management
subjects.description: Often chosen as a fourth science-adjacent subject. Shares the data-handling and graph-interpretation skills that IGCSE science papers test, so support in one tends to improve performance in both.

sections.heading: The four ways Creek Harbour families waste tutoring money
paragraphs: This is the section we would want to read as a parent, so it comes before the sales argument. Across the families we work with in Dubai's central corridor, wasted science tutoring spend falls into four recognisable patterns, and none of them involves a dishonest tutor. They involve a reasonable decision made without a piece of information that was available.

The first is paying a specialist rate for a mathematics problem. A student losing Physics marks on standard form, rearranging formulae and gradient calculation is not short of physics; they are short of algebra, and a Physics specialist at AED 300 an hour will spend the session teaching maths at a Physics price. The second is spreading a budget across three sciences at one session each, which produces three unfinished conversations and no secured method. The third is buying volume early: twelve sessions bought in September against a problem nobody has diagnosed, usually because a package discount was offered.

The fourth is the most expensive and the least visible. It is paying for content teaching in the final term, when the marks available are almost entirely technique. In the last eight weeks before a June or November series, the highest-yield work is timed papers with mark-scheme comparison, command-term discipline, practical-description questions and graph method. A tutor covering new topics in that window is teaching material the student will not be examined on deeply enough to matter, while the recoverable marks sit untouched in a drawer full of unmarked past papers. The table sets out each pattern with the cheaper alternative.

sections.heading: Separate sciences, Coordinated or Combined: the cost follows the route
paragraphs: Before any rate matters, establish which science route your child is on, because it changes both the tutoring bill and what it can achieve. Separate sciences means three qualifications, three sets of papers and three grades: Cambridge 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, or Pearson's 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Coordinated Science, Cambridge 0654, is a double award covering all three at reduced depth with its own paper structure. Combined Science, Cambridge 0653, is a single award with the lightest load.

The cost implication is direct. Three separate sciences multiply tutoring hours by subject, because the content does not overlap enough to share a session. Coordinated and Combined do not, which makes them substantially cheaper to support, and that is a legitimate factor in a family budget. What is not legitimate is treating them as interchangeable, because the route constrains what comes next. Some A Level and IB Higher Level science entry expectations are not met by a single-award Combined Science grade, and a school's head of science will tell you theirs in one email.

There is a specific trap for tutoring here. A tutor who does not know which route a student is on will teach separate-science content to a Coordinated Science candidate, covering material in a depth the papers do not reward while skipping the cross-cutting content the specification actually sets. This is the clearest argument for asking a prospective tutor for the syllabus code rather than the subject name. A specialist asks you for it before the first lesson. A generalist asks which topics the student finds hard, which is a question about symptoms.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and why the tier decides the value of every hour you buy
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE sciences are entered at Core or Extended tier, and the tier sets a ceiling on the grade available. That single fact changes the economics of tutoring more than any hourly rate does. Buying specialist support for a student entered at Core, in the hope of a top grade, is buying something the entry does not permit. Equally, leaving a capable student on Core because a mock went badly in Year 10 is a cheap decision with an expensive consequence, because the ceiling follows them into post-16 choices.

The timing point is what parents most often miss. Tier entry is decided by the school, usually on the strength of mock performance, and there is a window in which it can still be changed. Tutoring money spent before that decision is worth considerably more than the same money spent after it, because it can move the ceiling rather than just the mark underneath it. For a Creek Harbour family weighing whether to start in Year 10 or wait until Year 11, this is the whole argument for Year 10.

Pearson's International GCSE structure works differently, with a modular assessment pattern rather than a Core and Extended tiering, and students may have already sat and banked components. A tutor needs to know which. This is a routine question that distinguishes someone who works with these qualifications from someone who teaches the science generally, and a parent can ask it in one sentence on a first call.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel: what actually differs for the same science
paragraphs: Schools in this corridor use both boards, sometimes within the same building for different subjects, and a parent is rarely told which one matters. It matters quite a lot. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series, which is why any session table, including ours, should be read alongside the live official timetable rather than treated as the authority.

One correction worth making loudly, because it circulates widely in UAE parent groups. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June and November series. If a tutor, an aggregator site or a WhatsApp forward tells you your child can sit a March series in Dubai, that is wrong, and acting on it could cost a year. Beyond dates, the boards differ in paper structure and in how practical skills are assessed on paper, which is the real reason a tutor needs the syllabus code rather than the subject name.

A tutor in the room reads a child's face, removes a phone from the table, and holds the attention of a thirteen-year-old who will not sit still for a screen. For younger students and for some students with particular attention needs, that is worth paying for, and we would not argue otherwise.

For a Year 10 or Year 11 science student, the arithmetic looks different. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against an online specialist band of AED 200 to 450. The overlap is substantial, and the part of the in-home figure that is not teaching is driving. In this district that driving is specific: a tutor reaching a Creek Harbour tower at 5pm has crossed either the Ras Al Khor approaches or Al Khail Road at their slowest, and will do the same in reverse afterwards. Those ninety minutes are inside your hour whether or not anyone itemises them.

To be unambiguous, because this page targets a search families type: IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. sections.heading: Practicals, coursework and the line a science tutor must not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE science assesses practical skills, but in most routes it does so on paper rather than in a laboratory, which confuses families whose children study partly online. A practical question asks a student to describe a method, identify a control variable, explain why a particular apparatus choice limits precision, or interpret results from an experiment they have not personally run. Those are teachable skills and they are examinable without a bench, which is why online science teaching works better at IGCSE than parents expect.

Where there is assessed coursework or a school-marked practical component, the boundary matters. A tutor may teach method, question a plan until the student improves it themselves, explain what the marking criteria reward, and give written feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply data, or provide a template to be completed, which is ghost-writing with extra steps. We also do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables; we reference them and link the official source, because copying them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure.

This boundary is worth paying attention to as a buyer, not just as a matter of principle. Services selling completed coursework appear in these same search results, at published prices. For a family under deadline pressure the offer can look like a solution. It is the most expensive purchase available in this market, because the cost is not the fee. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under the boards' rules and the consequence lands on the student's certificate.

sections.heading: Equivalency and entry costs: the bill behind the tutoring bill
paragraphs: A cost page that stops at the tutor's hourly rate is incomplete, because there are other charges attached to an IGCSE science year and they affect how a family should allocate money. Private candidate entry, where a student sits a subject outside their school's entry, carries a centre fee that varies by centre; resits in a later series carry entry fees again. Those are school and centre questions rather than tutoring questions, but they belong in the same budget conversation, and they are a reason to get the first attempt right rather than to plan around a resit.

Then there is equivalency, which almost no competitor page in this market mentions at all. Certificate equivalency through the UAE Ministry of Education is what allows a secondary qualification to be recognised here for university admission and employment. For the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That five-subject rule is worth holding firmly, because at least one ranking competitor page in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is wrong, and a parent who believes it may fund an unnecessary sixth entry. For the American track, English proficiency requires IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math before applying. We publish no IB points threshold, because we have not read one on moe.gov.ae. Equivalency is a process the authority performs; it is not something IB Gram performs, guarantees or accelerates, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

sections.heading: Spending the first AED 1,000 well
paragraphs: If a Creek Harbour family has a limited budget and one science to fix, here is how we would spend the first thousand dirhams, which is roughly four sessions at the mid tier or two and a half at the specialist tier. Nothing in this sequence requires buying from us, and it is the advice we give on the phone before anyone pays anything.

Spend nothing on the first conversation. Take a free diagnostic lesson, from us or from anyone who offers one, and insist that it works a real question with your child rather than presenting credentials. Send a recently marked science script beforehand; it is the single most valuable document in this process, because a marked paper shows in ten minutes whether the loss is content, command terms, calculation method or timing, and those four problems have four different and differently priced remedies.

Then buy four sessions, not twelve. Four is enough to see a change in a marked piece of work and short enough that a wrong match costs little. Fix the slot after the bus arrives, which in this district means 5pm or later on weekdays and mid-morning at weekends. Judge the result on the next school assessment rather than on how the sessions felt. If it has not moved and the tutor cannot say precisely why, change the tutor rather than extending the package. And if at any point someone offers you a discount for buying a term in advance before the problem has been diagnosed, treat that as information about the seller.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE science tutor cost in Dubai Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates run from about AED 33 to 650 an hour. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget end. Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270, and Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table reaches AED 450 and above for specialist IGCSE and A Level support. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 because travel is inside the rate, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutoring. Those were all read from the providers' own pages in October 2026. IB Gram does not publish an hourly list, because the right arrangement depends on subject count and frequency.

faqs.question: Is the cheapest tutor ever the right choice for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Yes, for a specific stage. For Years 7 to 9, where the work is homework supervision, arithmetic confidence and habit, a budget online tutor at AED 45 to 65 an hour is genuinely appropriate and we will say so. It stops being appropriate in Year 11, when the marks sit in paper technique for a named syllabus code, the tiering decision, command-term discipline and practical-description questions. That is knowledge a tutor acquires by working with the qualification rather than by having passed it, and it is what the specialist band is actually charging for.

faqs.question: Why does my child's syllabus code matter to a tutor?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge 0620 Chemistry, Pearson 4CH1 Chemistry and Cambridge Coordinated Science 0654 are different qualifications with different papers, different tiering and different practical assessment. A tutor teaching separate-science content to a Coordinated Science candidate covers material the papers do not reward and skips cross-cutting content the specification does set. A specialist asks you for the code before the first lesson. A generalist asks which topics your child finds hard, which is a question about symptoms rather than about the examination they will actually sit.

faqs.question: Should we fund all three sciences or just one?
faqs.answer: One, properly, in almost every case we see. Three sciences at one weekly hour each costs three times as much and typically produces three unfinished conversations with no secured method in any of them. The deficit is usually not biology, chemistry or physics content; it is graph method, command terms or algebra, and those transfer. A student who secures the method in Chemistry generally applies it in Physics without paying for Physics. Where all three genuinely need work, we rotate two weekly hours by the school's assessment calendar rather than running three parallel sessions.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Core and Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Core entry caps the grade available; Extended gives access to the full range. The school decides the entry, usually on mock performance, and there is a window in which it can be changed. That makes the timing of tutoring money important: spending before the decision can move the ceiling, while spending afterwards only moves the mark underneath it. It also means past-paper practice has to match the tier actually entered. Buying specialist support for a Core entry in the hope of a top grade is buying something the entry does not permit.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a February or March IGCSE series in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International's February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. This matters because the claim circulates widely in UAE parent groups and acting on it could cost a year. Note also that every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used.

faqs.question: How are science practicals assessed if my child studies partly online?
faqs.answer: In most IGCSE science routes, practical skills are assessed on paper rather than at a bench. A question asks the student to describe a method, identify a control variable, explain why an apparatus choice limits precision, or interpret results from an experiment they did not personally run. Those are teachable without a laboratory, which is why online science teaching works better at IGCSE than parents expect. Where a school-marked practical component exists, a tutor may teach method and give feedback on the student's own work, but may not write or supply any part of it.

faqs.question: When is the best time in the year to spend money on science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10, before the tiering decision, and then the final eight weeks before the series. Year 10 money can move the ceiling, because the school sets Core or Extended entry largely on mock performance and there is a window to change it. The final eight weeks are high-yield for a different reason: the recoverable marks there are almost entirely technique, which is drillable. The worst time to buy content teaching is those same final weeks, when new topics arrive too late to be examined deeply enough to matter.

faqs.question: Do you send science tutors to homes in Creek Harbour?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, including Creek Beach, Harbour Views, Creek Gate and the Address Harbour Point towers. Home visiting is a service we run only in India, and we state it here rather than after a booking. For UAE families every lesson is live, one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. We target the phrase because it is what parents search for, and then answer the question honestly. If a tutor in the room is a firm requirement, we are not the right service.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying the in-home premium for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the numbers say so rather than our preference. Bestimate quotes in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors up to AED 500, against an online specialist band of AED 200 to 450. The overlap is large, and the part of the in-home figure that is not teaching is driving, which in this district means crossing Ras Al Khor or Al Khail at their slowest in both directions. For a younger child who needs a person in the room, the premium can be worth it. For a sixteen-year-old, rarely.

faqs.question: Should I buy a package for the discount?
faqs.answer: Not before a diagnosis. A twelve-session package bought in September commits a term's budget against a problem nobody has yet identified, and the discount is the seller transferring risk to you. Buy four sessions. Four is enough to produce a visible change in a marked piece of work and short enough that a wrong match costs little. If someone offers a discount for a term in advance before any diagnostic lesson has happened, treat the offer as information about how they operate rather than as a saving.

faqs.question: Will paying for a sixth IGCSE subject help with UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: It should not be necessary. The British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. At least one ranking competitor page in this market states that six IGCSE subjects are required, which is wrong, and a family acting on it may fund an entry and a term of tutoring they did not need. Verify the current position with the Ministry before paying for anything extra.

faqs.question: My son understands the science but his marks are low. What is going on?
faqs.answer: Usually one of three things, and they have different prices. Command terms: answering 'explain' at the length of 'state' loses marks that needed no extra knowledge. Algebra: standard form, rearranging formulae and gradient work sit inside science papers, and a student short of those loses science marks for a maths reason. Or timing: a student who can do every question but not in the time available. A marked script tells us which within about ten minutes, which is why we ask for one before quoting any arrangement.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with assessed science coursework?
faqs.answer: Within a boundary we state plainly. A tutor may teach method, question a plan until the student improves it themselves, explain what the marking criteria reward, and give written feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor may not write any part of it, supply data, or hand over a template to be completed. We also do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge, Pearson or IB syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; we link the official source. Services selling completed coursework appear in these search results, and the consequence of using one falls on the student.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need a permit, and does that affect what I pay?
faqs.answer: They need one, and it should not affect your price, because the permit is free. The private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued by MoHRE free of charge for two years. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are all listed as eligible, with a two-working-day completion time. Any tutor citing permit costs as a reason for a higher rate is misinformed. Tutoring without one attracts penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule.

faqs.question: What would you do first with a budget of AED 1,000?
faqs.answer: Spend nothing on the first conversation. Send a recently marked science script and take a free diagnostic lesson that works a real question with your child rather than presenting credentials. Then buy four sessions at the tier the diagnosis actually calls for, which is sometimes maths rather than science. Fix the slot after the bus arrives, so 5pm or later on a weekday in this district. Judge the outcome on the next school assessment. If it has not moved and the tutor cannot say precisely why, change the tutor rather than buying more hours.

intro.heading: What you are actually asking for when you ask for a science tutor
paragraphs: Science at IGCSE is not one subject. Your child is sitting either three separate sciences, each with its own syllabus code and its own papers, or a combined or coordinated award that covers all three more narrowly and reports one or two grades. Those are structurally different qualifications with different content, different paper counts and different grade consequences, and a tutor who assumes the wrong one will teach confidently in the wrong direction for several weeks.

Then there is the board. Cambridge International uses four-digit codes: 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, with 0653 Coordinated Science and 0654 Combined Science. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses forms like 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the separate sciences. Many Dubai schools enter some subjects with one board and some with the other, so the answer about your school is not the answer about your child's science entry. Ask for it subject by subject, in writing.

Within Cambridge there is a third variable: Core or Extended. The Core route does not reach the top grades, and the decision is made by the school during Year 10 on the basis of classwork. A family aiming at A Level or IB Diploma sciences needs to know which route their child is on, because the sixth-form entry requirement may sit above the ceiling of the current entry. That is worth establishing in Year 10 rather than discovering after results.

So the honest answer to the question in the search box. Is there a science tutor near Dubai Festival City? Almost certainly, for one subject at a reasonable tier. Is there someone nearby who knows all three sciences at Extended level and the specific board your school enters? That is a much narrower requirement, and applying it alongside a driving radius and an available after-school hour leaves very few people in the eastern suburbs.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For Al Badia, Festival Boulevard, Nad Al Hamar and the wider eastern suburbs the delivery is live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. The reason that is the better answer here rather than merely the cheaper one is the filter arithmetic above: removing the distance requirement leaves subject, entry shape and hour, which is how a family actually reaches the right tutor.

The rest of this page is practical. How to establish which entry your child sits. Whether one tutor can cover three sciences. How practical skills are assessed from a UAE centre, which almost nobody explains. The questions that test real syllabus knowledge. And where marks go in each of the three subjects, so you can aim the money rather than spread it.

None of that is an argument against local tutors as a class. For a single science at Core level, a capable nearby teacher is a perfectly good answer and often the most convenient one. The point is to know which situation you are in before you choose, because the request that fails quietly is the one where a parent asks for science help, a willing tutor agrees, and nobody establishes the entry shape until a mock paper arrives looking unfamiliar in week nine.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-festi.subjectsIntro: This grid covers the three sciences across both boards, with the syllabus code and what the subject actually asks for. Use it to check your child's entry and to test whether a prospective tutor recognises the code you quote.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, nutrition, coordination, inheritance and ecology. Biology punishes imprecise writing more than any other science: an answer that does not name the structure, the process and the consequence scores nothing even where the student clearly understands it.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: States of matter, atomic structure, bonding, stoichiometry, acids and bases, metals, organic chemistry. Moles calculations and the Cambridge qualitative analysis tables are the two highest-return areas, because both are learnable procedures rather than vague skills.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Forces and motion, energy, waves, electricity, magnetism, nuclear physics. Marks go missing in two predictable places: multi-step calculations where units are dropped, and six-mark answers that describe an effect without naming the mechanism behind it.

subjects.name: Coordinated Science
subjects.description: All three sciences taught and assessed together, awarded as a single grade. Content is narrower than the separate sciences but spans everything, which means a tutor has to be genuinely comfortable in all three rather than strong in one and adequate elsewhere.

subjects.name: Combined Science
subjects.description: A broader, narrower route again across all three subjects. Chosen by schools wanting science breadth without three separate subject blocks in the timetable. Catching up a missed unit here is harder than in a separate science, because the unit may sit in a subject the tutor is weakest in.

subjects.name: Double and triple award patterns
subjects.description: Some boards and schools award science as a double or triple block rather than as separate subjects. Which pattern applies affects how many grades appear on the certificate and how sixth-form entry treats them, so ask the school to state it explicitly.

subjects.name: Practical skills, written assessment
subjects.description: Apparatus selection, identifying sources of error, reading scales, suggesting improvements and interpreting results. Cambridge offers a written alternative-to-practical paper on several syllabuses, which is the route most candidates sitting from a UAE centre meet, and it is entirely teachable without a bench.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside science
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, percentages, ratios, unit conversion and graph work. A student weak here appears weak at physics and chemistry simultaneously, because the same gap recurs in both wearing different labels. Often the cheapest single fix across three subjects.

subjects.name: Extended written answers
subjects.levels: All three sciences, Extended tiers especially
subjects.description: The six-mark questions that ask for a reasoned explanation. The commonest failure is writing three sentences that restate the first, which earns one mark and feels like three. Responds to marked practice with a mark scheme visible, not to further explanation.

subjects.name: Command terms and question reading
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, calculate and compare ask for different amounts. A student who writes an explanation where a state was wanted loses time; one who states where an explanation was wanted loses marks. One session with a past paper improves all three subjects at once.

sections.heading: Establishing which science entry your child actually sits
paragraphs: This is the first job and most families skip it, because a school report prints subject names rather than syllabus codes. Ask the school, in writing, for the board and the code for each science your child is entered for, plus the tier where Cambridge applies. The reply will say something like 0620 Extended and 0625 Extended, or 0653 Coordinated Science Extended, or 4CH1 and 4PH1. Those are three different situations requiring three different tutoring plans.

The distinctions matter in concrete ways. Three separate sciences means three sets of papers and three grades, and a weakness can be isolated and treated. Coordinated Science is awarded as a single grade across all three subjects, so a weak area inside it drags one grade rather than one of three, and the tutor needs breadth. Combined Science is narrower again. Pearson's separate sciences are single-tier with their own paper structures rather than Core and Extended routes.

The tier question is specific to Cambridge and it has a hard consequence. The Core route does not reach the top grades. If your child is aiming at A Level or IB Diploma sciences, check whether the sixth-form entry requirement sits above the ceiling of the current entry, and check it in Year 10 while the entry is still reviewable with the school. Discovering this in the spring of Year 11 means paying the highest rates in the market for a ceiling fixed months earlier.

One final practical point. Schools sometimes enter biology with one board and physics with another, usually for historical or staffing reasons. So ask subject by subject rather than once. Quote the codes when you request a tutor and ask the tutor to repeat them back, because a tutor who does not recognise 0653 or 4PH1 as distinct things is not yet the specialist you were looking for.

sections.heading: One tutor for three sciences, or three tutors?
paragraphs: The arithmetic depends on the entry. For a Coordinated or Combined award there is one grade, one set of papers and one teacher at school, so one tutor with genuine breadth is the natural match and three specialists would be both expensive and confusing. For three separate sciences the opposite usually holds: the weakness is rarely spread evenly, and paying three specialists to cover subjects that are already fine is the commonest overspend in this request.

There is a middle case worth naming. Physics and chemistry share a mathematical spine, so a tutor comfortable with both is a realistic match and a useful one, because the formula rearrangement and unit handling that cost marks in physics cost marks in chemistry too. Biology sits further away, since its demands are precision of language and volume of content rather than calculation. Pairing physics with chemistry and leaving biology separate is a common and sensible split.

The question to ask a prospective tutor is specific rather than general. Not can you cover three sciences, to which almost everybody says yes, but which of the three have you taught to a full IGCSE cohort and which have you only supported. The answers differ more than the initial claim suggests, and a tutor who distinguishes honestly between them is telling you something valuable about how they work.

For a combined award there is one more honest warning. A single weak subject inside a coordinated entry is harder to catch up than the same weakness in a separate science, because it may sit in the area the tutor knows least and because the content is compressed. Families whose child is on 0653 or 0654 should ask specifically whether the tutor has taught that syllabus, not merely the three subjects individually.

sections.heading: How practical science is assessed from a UAE centre
paragraphs: This is the question parents ask most often about online science tuition and the one competing pages answer least. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical written paper on several science syllabuses, and that written route is the one most candidates sitting from a UAE centre meet. It assesses apparatus selection, reading scales, identifying sources of error, interpreting results and suggesting specific improvements, all in writing, all based on described experiments.

That has a direct consequence for tutoring: practical marks are largely won by reasoning that can be taught without a bench. A student who can explain why a measurement was repeated, distinguish systematic from random error, read a scale to the correct precision and suggest an improvement that is specific rather than generic will score well on that paper. None of those skills requires the tutor to be in a laboratory, and all of them respond to marked practice on past papers.

Where a syllabus does require laboratory assessment, the laboratory is the school's and should be. Your child has access to apparatus, a teacher who knows it, and technicians who maintain it. A tutor offering to replicate any of that would be offering something worse than what the student already has. What a tutor adds is the thinking either side: anticipating the error sources before the experiment and interpreting the numbers honestly afterwards.

Confirm which route applies to your child, because it changes what the preparation should look like. Ask the school whether each science entry includes a practical assessment or an alternative-to-practical paper. The answer takes one line and it determines whether past-paper practical reasoning is a central part of the plan or an incidental one. It is also a question that reveals quickly whether a prospective tutor knows the syllabus.

sections.heading: Questions that reveal whether a tutor knows your science syllabus
paragraphs: Credentials in this market are largely unverifiable, so ask about the syllabus instead. Somebody who has taught your child's entry answers these in specifics; somebody working from a general science background answers in adjectives. You do not need science yourself to hear the difference, which is the whole point of using questions with concrete answers.

Start with the entry. Which code is my child on, and what are the papers? What does the Core route cap, and when can it be reviewed? Is there an alternative-to-practical paper on this syllabus? For Cambridge chemistry, what are the qualitative analysis tables and how do you teach them? For physics, how do you teach a six-mark question? For biology, what is the difference between describe and explain in a mark scheme?

Then the operational questions. Do you hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit? Will you teach every session or could it be reassigned? What will you do with a piece of my child's coursework, exactly? And the most informative question available, which almost nobody is asked: what would make you tell me you are not the right tutor for this student? A specific answer indicates experience; an insistence that nothing would indicates a sales script.

Write the answers down. A week later every provider sounds similar in memory, and the distinction between an answer that named a paper structure and one that described enthusiasm is the only comparison worth making. Ask the same questions of us. If we cannot answer them for your child's specific entry, we are not the right match for it and you should know that before you book rather than in week three.

sections.heading: Where marks go in each of the three sciences
paragraphs: Biology first, because it is the most commonly misdiagnosed. Students who understand biology lose marks to imprecise language. An answer that does not name the structure, the process and the consequence scores nothing, and the student leaves the examination believing they answered it. The fix is marked practice in which the tutor reads the answer back and shows exactly which clause earned nothing, repeated until the habit changes.

Chemistry has two high-return areas. Moles and concentration calculations are a finite set of procedures and respond to four focused sessions. The Cambridge qualitative analysis tables, which cover the tests and observations for ions and gases, are pure drillable content that students are rarely made to learn systematically. Both are cheap repairs with a visible effect on a marked paper, and both are better value than general chemistry revision.

Physics loses marks in two places. Multi-step calculations where a unit is dropped or an answer is left in the wrong power of ten, and six-mark written answers that describe an effect without naming the mechanism. The first is fixed by a standard working layout, written out every time; the second by marked practice with a mark scheme open. Neither needs more content teaching, which is what most families buy.

Across all three there is one shared gap worth attacking first: the mathematics. Rearranging formulae, standard form, percentages and unit conversion appear in every physics paper and most chemistry ones. A student weak there looks weak in two subjects simultaneously, which leads families to buy two subject tutors when one four-session maths-for-science block would have lifted both. Diagnose it before deciding how many tutors to hire.
bullets: Biology: imprecise language, not missing knowledge, is the usual cause
Chemistry: moles and qualitative analysis are the two cheapest high-return repairs
Physics: a standard working layout and six-mark technique beat more content

sections.heading: The series, the resits and when science money should be spent
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no student at a Dubai Festival City school will sit it, and any page handing a UAE parent a February entry deadline has imported another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them. So take dates from your school's exams officer or the board's live timetable, never from a tutoring page.

The useful shape for spending is this. Year 10 autumn for establishing the entry and the tier. Year 10 spring for the one subject or the one cross-subject skill that is structurally weak. Year 11 autumn for reading the marked mocks, which are the best free diagnostic data available anywhere in the two years. Year 11 spring for marked timed practice and practical reasoning, which is where science technique genuinely moves.

On resits, Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day. That January timing makes the November series a workable resit route for a sixth-form conversation. Entry fees are set by the examination centre rather than by a tutor, so ask the school and hold a reserve rather than committing the whole budget to lessons.

sections.heading: Verifying the person, and the boundary on coursework
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no schedule of amounts is published anywhere official.

Because the permit is free, a tutor who does not hold one has saved nothing by skipping it, which makes it a reasonable question to ask directly. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different matter: it needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and does not describe itself as KHDA approved.

Two further checks. Be sceptical of self-asserted star ratings: competitors in this market publish review figures that contradict each other on the same page, and at least one shows a rating in its markup that differs from the visible number. And be sceptical of examiner labelling, which is the cheapest unverifiable credential available. We do not describe any tutor as a current Cambridge or Pearson examiner unless the status can be evidenced.

On coursework and assignments the boundary is the same across all three sciences. A tutor may teach the content, explain what a task is assessing, work through a comparable example on a different topic, read what your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write, complete or edit the work to a finished state. Assessed work submitted as a student's own that is not theirs is a malpractice matter, and the consequence lands on the student.
bullets: MoHRE private tuition work permit: free for two years, so ask directly
Centres with premises need a KHDA institute permit, which is a different authorisation

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Festival City, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Send the codes and tiers for each science, the entry shape, and the last two marked papers for the weakest subject. Add the hour your child is genuinely at a desk, allowing for the bus from Al Mizhar or the queue out of Festival City. We then match a tutor to that entry and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard City time, at no cost, with the tutor expected to name the paper structure back to you.

Afterwards you receive a written note setting out where marks are being lost, sorted by cause rather than by topic: command terms, language precision, procedures, units and formula handling, practical reasoning, or a genuine content gap. For many students the recommendation is a cross-subject skills block rather than a subject tutor, because one booking then lifts two or three sciences. If that is the finding, we will say so even though it sells less.

The limits, plainly stated. IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. There is no UAE office, centre or branch, and we claim none. We hold no board or regulator approval. We do not supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as downloads, because reproducing them is not ours to do; we reference them and link to the official source.

And we make no grade predictions. What the first month should produce is a child who can name their syllabus code and their tier, a written note identifying the dominant cause of lost marks, and one visible habit change, usually in how a six-mark answer is structured or in whether the unit appears on every answer. Grade movement takes longer, and a provider that opens with a prediction has told you how it operates.

faqs.question: Does my Dubai Festival City child sit three sciences or one combined award?
faqs.answer: Ask the school in writing, subject by subject, for the board and the code. The reply will name something like Cambridge 0620 and 0625 for separate chemistry and physics, or 0653 Coordinated Science awarded as a single grade, or Pearson 4CH1 and 4PH1. Those are structurally different qualifications: separate sciences give three grades and let a weakness be isolated, while a coordinated award gives one grade and needs a tutor with breadth across all three subjects.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover biology, chemistry and physics for an eastern Dubai student?
faqs.answer: For a Coordinated or Combined award, one tutor with genuine breadth is the natural match and three specialists would be wasteful. For three separate sciences, usually not, because the weakness is rarely spread evenly and paying for subjects that are already fine is the commonest overspend here. Physics and chemistry pair well because they share a mathematical spine; biology sits further away since its demands are language precision and content volume rather than calculation.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if my child studies with an online tutor?
faqs.answer: Cambridge offers a written alternative-to-practical paper on several science syllabuses, and that is the route most candidates sitting from a UAE centre meet. It assesses apparatus selection, reading scales, identifying sources of error, interpreting results and suggesting specific improvements, all in writing. Every one of those skills is taught through marked past papers rather than at a bench. Where school-assessed practical work applies, the school's laboratory does that and a tutor should not try to replace it.

faqs.question: What does the Cambridge Core route cap, and can we change it?
faqs.answer: The Core route does not reach the top grades, because the papers sat do not contain the marks needed to cross those boundaries. The entry is decided by the school, usually during Year 10, and the realistic review window is Year 10 and the very start of Year 11. If your child is aiming at A Level or IB Diploma sciences, check whether the sixth-form requirement sits above the current ceiling, and bring a written diagnostic assessment to that conversation rather than a conviction.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science do Dubai Festival City families ask for most?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, then physics, then biology, with Coordinated Science requests rising because several schools in eastern Dubai use that entry. Chemistry comes first partly because two of its hardest areas, moles calculations and the Cambridge qualitative analysis tables, are learnable procedures, so families see movement quickly. Biology requests come later, often after a mock, because students who understand the content lose marks to imprecise language and that pattern is not obvious from a report.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand biology but still score badly?
faqs.answer: Almost always language precision. Biology mark schemes want the structure, the process and the consequence named, and an answer that conveys general understanding without those three elements scores nothing. The student leaves the examination believing they answered the question. The repair is marked practice in which the tutor reads the answer back and shows exactly which clause earned nothing, repeated until the habit changes. It is technique rather than knowledge, and it moves faster than content work.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to homes in Al Badia or Al Khawaneej for science lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For eastern Dubai the practical point is that a visiting tutor must satisfy subject, entry shape and driving distance at once, and it is the third filter that makes a Coordinated Science or Extended-tier match fail locally. Lessons here are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, with working, scale diagrams and mark schemes shared on screen.

faqs.question: Which board does our school enter for science, Cambridge or Pearson?
faqs.answer: Ask subject by subject rather than once, because many Dubai schools split boards across the sciences for staffing or historical reasons. Cambridge uses four-digit codes such as 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, plus 0653 Coordinated and 0654 Combined. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses forms like 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Quote the codes when requesting a tutor, and ask the tutor to repeat them back with the paper structure attached.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science exams held for a UAE candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series in the UAE. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no Dubai Festival City student will sit it, and any site quoting a February entry deadline to a UAE parent is using another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so take the real dates from the exams officer.

faqs.question: Is it worth fixing maths before paying for two science tutors?
faqs.answer: Very often, yes, and it is the cheapest decision available. Rearranging formulae, standard form, percentages and unit conversion appear in every physics paper and most chemistry ones, so a student weak there appears weak in two subjects at once. A four to six session maths-for-science block frequently lifts both without anybody being paid to teach either subject. Diagnose it from two marked papers before deciding how many subject tutors to hire.

faqs.question: How do I test whether a science tutor actually knows the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Ask which code and tier your child is on and what the papers are. Ask whether that syllabus has an alternative-to-practical paper. Ask what the Core route caps and when it can be reviewed. Ask how they teach a six-mark question, and for Cambridge chemistry what the qualitative analysis tables are. A specialist answers in specifics; somebody with a general science background answers in adjectives. Write the answers down, because every provider sounds similar a week later.

faqs.question: Can a science tutor help with school assignments and coursework?
faqs.answer: With teaching and feedback, yes; with producing the work, never. A tutor may explain what a task is assessing, work through a comparable example on a different topic, read what your child has written and say where it falls short, and teach referencing. A tutor may not write, complete or edit the work to a finished state. Assessed work submitted as a student's own that is not theirs is a malpractice matter, and the consequence lands on your child.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor in Dubai need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no amounts are published. Because the permit costs nothing, ask the question directly and expect a straight answer.

faqs.question: Does a Coordinated Science award count the same for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: It is counted differently from three separate sciences towards a subject total, so check rather than assume. Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Verify on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority; IB Gram does not perform equivalency.

faqs.question: What should the first month of science tuition show for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Three things and no grade. Your child should be able to name their syllabus code and tier for the subject being tutored. You should hold a written note identifying the dominant cause of lost marks, stated as command terms, language precision, procedures, units or practical reasoning. And one habit should visibly change, usually how a six-mark answer is structured or whether a unit appears on every answer. Grade movement takes longer than a month and nobody can promise it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-festi.closingHeading: Get the code first, then the tutor
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-festi.closingBody: Almost every bad science tutoring experience in this corridor starts the same way: a parent asks for an IGCSE science tutor, a willing tutor says yes, and nobody establishes whether the child is sitting three separate sciences at Extended level or a single coordinated award with a different content map. One message to the school fixes that permanently. Send the codes, the tiers and two marked papers, take the free trial lesson at no cost, and read the written note before you commit. If it says fix the maths first, fix the maths first.

intro.heading: Three routes, three different futures, one line on the report
paragraphs: Science at IGCSE is offered three ways and the choice is usually made for a student rather than with them. Three separate sciences produce three grades and the fullest preparation for A Level or Diploma sciences. Coordinated Sciences as a double award produces two grades across all three disciplines in reduced depth. Combined Science as a single award produces one. Those are genuinely different outcomes on a transcript, and the decision is normally taken in Year 9 on the basis of sets rather than through a conversation with the family.

The consequence that matters arrives at 16. A post-16 provider reading an application sees how many science grades there are as well as what they say, and a combined single award is thin preparation for A Level Chemistry or Higher Level Biology whatever the grade attached to it. Families discover this when sixth-form applications are being written, which is after the entry has been filed and the route is fixed. Asking in Year 9 or Year 10 what route the school intends, and what evidence that intention rests on, is the single most valuable question in this part of a school career.

The second comparison families in this district should make is between the boards' practical models, because they differ in a way that affects preparation. Cambridge assesses practical skills through either a practical test paper or the alternative written paper, and the school chooses which. Pearson Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers, with no separate component. Preparing for an alternative-to-practical paper and preparing for practical reasoning distributed through theory papers are different pieces of work, and most families do not know which applies.

Dubai Harbour shapes the delivery question. The district is new, built around a cruise terminal and marina berths, approached through one corridor off King Salman Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud Street shared with Emaar Beachfront and the Palm Jumeirah approach. There is no school and no tuition centre inside it, and children travel to Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah, leaving before 07:00 and returning after 15:30. Two or three science appointments in a week is already a crowded timetable. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service.

What follows compares the three routes on content, grades and post-16 consequences, sets the two boards' practical models side by side, explains how the science basket interacts with Ministry equivalency, says plainly when a group class at a centre is better value than one-to-one, and publishes the market rates with each figure attributed. Confirm the board, code, tier and practical route for each science with your exams officer before acting on any of it.

sections.heading: The three routes, compared on what happens after 16
paragraphs: This is the comparison nobody makes and it is the one with lasting consequences. Three separate sciences produce three grades and the fullest preparation for post-16 science courses, because each discipline is covered in its own depth with its own practical component. Coordinated Sciences as a double award produces two grades across a coordinated selection of content, which is genuine breadth in reduced depth. Combined Science as a single award produces one grade across the narrowest selection.

Post-16 providers treat these differently and they publish how. A sixth form offering A Level Chemistry will state what it requires, and that statement frequently assumes separate chemistry. An IB school offering Chemistry at Higher Level will state its own expectation. A combined single award may satisfy a requirement for a science pass and will rarely satisfy a requirement to continue a specific science at a demanding level. None of that is a judgement about the student; it is a statement about what the qualification covered.

The practical step is to ask the school in Year 9 or early Year 10 what route they intend and what evidence it rests on, and at the same time to ask two or three likely post-16 providers what they require for the science courses the student might want. Those two answers together decide whether the route is right. Doing it at the point of sixth-form applications is too late, because the route and the entry are already fixed and the options have closed without anybody choosing to close them.

sections.heading: How many grades a transcript shows, and why it matters
paragraphs: A grade count is information in its own right. A student presenting three science grades has demonstrated performance in three disciplines separately assessed; a student presenting one has demonstrated performance across a narrower selection in one aggregated result. Readers of an application, whether a sixth form, an IB school or a university admissions office, use the count as well as the letters, and they do it quickly and without asking for an explanation.

This interacts with Ministry of Education equivalency in a way worth understanding. On the British track, equivalency counts five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. A double award produces two of those five and a single award produces one, so a student on the combined route needs their remaining subject basket to carry more of the count. That is an arithmetic check worth doing in Year 10 rather than discovering later.

None of this argues that separate sciences are always right. For a student whose strengths sit firmly outside the sciences, three separate sciences consume two years of effort for three grades they will never use, and a single award frees that effort for subjects their application actually needs. The error is not choosing a lighter route; it is choosing it without knowing what it closes, and without the family having been part of the decision.

sections.heading: The two boards' practical models, side by side
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson handle practical skills differently and the difference changes what preparation looks like. Cambridge offers two options for the separate sciences and the school chooses: a practical test paper sat in a laboratory with apparatus, or the alternative written paper, which presents an experimental scenario and tests the same reasoning on paper. Pearson Edexcel has no separate practical component for its separate sciences; practical skills are assessed inside the written papers.

For a family considering online tutoring this is more consequential than it sounds, and in a reassuring direction. The alternative written paper tests nothing but written reasoning: apparatus choice, sources of error, reading a scale correctly, completing a results table, and drawing a conclusion the data supports. All of that is taught on a shared page, and every past question can be worked and marked against a scheme. Where the practical test applies, the apparatus handling happens at school and the reasoning still has to be taught separately.

The Pearson arrangement spreads the same requirement through the theory papers, which changes the revision shape rather than removing the requirement. A student on 4PH1 cannot drill practical reasoning as a single block aimed at one paper, so it has to be woven into ordinary topic work. Ask the school which arrangement applies to each of your child's sciences, because it can differ between subjects within one school, and plan the practical preparation a term ahead rather than in the final fortnight.

sections.heading: When a group class is the better purchase
paragraphs: Worth saying plainly, because almost nobody selling tutoring says it. In Year 9 and much of Year 10, where the need is content exposure and consolidation rather than diagnosis, a small group at a centre is good value for science. The student hears the material, works problems alongside others, sees demonstrations, and the cost per hour is lower. If that is the need, buying one-to-one is buying precision that nothing in the arrangement is using.

The calculation inverts in Year 11. The marks a particular student is losing are individual: a circuit redrawn incorrectly, a unit conversion, a command term misread, a mole calculation that hesitates, a structured answer written in the wrong order. A class pitched at a group cannot see which of those applies to your child, because seeing it requires reading one student's script closely and watching them write. That is the point at which one-to-one becomes necessary rather than preferable.

There is also a logistics cost specific to this district that families underestimate. A centre class in the Marina or Al Barsha means a second journey after a school run that already takes ninety minutes of the day, along a single approach corridor, at the hour the whole cluster is moving. For three sciences that is three second journeys a week. Our sessions run over live video and we provide no home visits anywhere in the UAE, so the real comparison is between a video slot and that journey.

sections.heading: What the market charges for science support, with sources
paragraphs: Published rates in this market, read in October 2026 and attributed to whoever stated them. At the budget end, Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, typically university-student provision. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270 for specialist cover. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, and BartyED sits at AED 650 at the premium end. Independent home tutors quote AED 200 to 500.

Three sciences multiplies all of that, which is why the format decision carries real money. Three weekly one-to-one sessions with specialists is a substantially larger commitment than one, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a single hour a week run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 mid, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. A family running three subjects at the middle tier should do that arithmetic before committing to a term rather than during it.

This is also the strongest argument for the shared-skills block. Where the mock scripts show the same habit failing in all three sciences, three or four sessions on command terms, unit conversion, graph work and results tables produce gains in three subjects for the cost of one subject's block. That is a better purchase than three parallel subject arrangements, and it is the recommendation we make whenever the scripts support it. All figures here describe the market, not IB Gram's rates, which are set after the free trial.

sections.heading: Reading three mock scripts together
paragraphs: This is the diagnostic step that changes a three-science plan and almost nobody takes it. Read the chemistry, physics and biology scripts side by side rather than one at a time. If the losses in all three trace to command terms, unit conversion, graph construction or answer order, that is one habit failing three times and it needs one block of work. If the losses concentrate in one subject while the other two are clean, that is a genuine content gap and the sessions belong there.

Those two findings produce completely different plans and identical report cards. A family reading one script at a time will conclude that their child has three science problems and buy three subject arrangements, which is three times the cost for the same repair and crowds out the independent work that makes any of it effective. A family reading all three together frequently discovers that four sessions on command terms moves all three grades.

There is a third pattern worth looking for: unattempted marks on the last page. Count them in each subject. A student leaving eight marks blank at the end of three papers has a pacing problem rather than three content problems, and the repair is a timing rule plus two or three full papers under genuine conditions. That number is invisible in a percentage and it takes a minute to find, which makes it the highest-return minute available to a parent in a Year 11 spring.

sections.heading: Protecting the science a student avoids
paragraphs: In a three-science week one subject always gets the leftovers, and it is reliably the one the student finds hardest. The avoidance is not deliberate and it is not visible until results arrive: a conscientious student who works steadily produces two reasonable grades and one poor one, and nobody can explain why because the effort was there. The explanation is allocation, and allocation responds to structure rather than to encouragement.

The structural fix is to give the weakest subject a fixed weekly slot and let the stronger two share a second, with a fortnightly timed paper rotating between all three. The fixed slot is the part that matters: it removes the daily decision about what to work on, which is the decision avoidance exploits. Write the allocation down and put it somewhere visible, because an allocation held in someone's head reverts to inclination within a fortnight.

This is also the reason we usually recommend starting with one subject rather than three. A family who buys three appointments in week one has crowded out the problem sets that make sessions productive, and from this district has added three second journeys or three evening slots to a day that already loses ninety minutes to the school run. Begin with the weakest subject or the shared-skills block, let the pattern become clear over three or four weeks, and add then.

One signal worth watching for. Ask the student which science they would work on if they had a free hour, and then look at which one they actually did work on last week. Where those two answers differ, the allocation problem is already running, and it will not correct itself without a slot that removes the choice.

sections.heading: Booking science support from Dubai Harbour
paragraphs: Send the board, syllabus code, tier and practical route for each science, the marked mock scripts if the school will release them, and the hours that genuinely exist after a bus that leaves before 07:00 and returns after 15:30. The practical route is the item families almost never have and it changes the preparation plan. The hours are the hardest part with three subjects, which is why we would rather see them honestly than be told what would be ideal.

We match one tutor per subject at that tier and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing a written breakdown of lost marks by subject and by habit. Where the scripts show one habit failing across all three sciences we will recommend the shared block first, even though it is a smaller purchase than three subject arrangements, because it is the better one.

The limits. Finding three Extended-tier science specialists with compatible hours takes longer than finding one, and occasionally a particular code and tier has nobody free in a given week. We will say so and offer alternatives rather than putting one generalist across all three, which is the arrangement most likely to produce pleasant sessions and three static grades. We cannot promise a grade, and the problem sets between sessions are the student's own work in each subject.

If a mock window or a practical component is imminent, say so in the first line of the enquiry. A fixed date in three weeks changes which block is worth starting, and occasionally changes our answer about whether it is worth starting at all, which is a conversation better had before a fee than after one.
