process.description: A Cambridge practical test, the Cambridge alternative paper, or Pearson's distributed assessment inside the theory papers. It can differ between sciences in one school, and preparing for the wrong one wastes the block. Nobody will tell you unless you ask.

process.title: Read the three mock scripts together
process.description: Side by side rather than one at a time. One habit failing in all three sciences needs one block of work; losses concentrated in one subject need subject sessions. Those produce identical report cards and completely different plans, and three times the cost if you get it wrong.

process.title: Give the avoided subject the fixed slot
process.description: Students neglect the science they find hardest and the neglect is invisible until results day. A fixed weekly appointment in that subject, with the stronger two alternating, removes the daily decision that avoidance exploits. Write the allocation down and keep it visible.

whyPoints.title: The route compared on consequences
whyPoints.description: Three, two or one science grade, with different post-16 options attached. We set that out and tell you to ask the receiving providers directly, because the decision closes at final entries and families usually discover it at application time.

whyPoints.title: Practical models explained per board
whyPoints.description: A Cambridge practical test, the Cambridge alternative written paper, or Pearson's assessment inside the theory papers. Each needs different preparation, and most families do not know which applies to each of their child's sciences.

whyPoints.title: Honest about group classes
whyPoints.description: For Year 9 and early Year 10 science coverage a centre group class is better value than we are. We say so, because a family who buys precision nothing is using concludes the spending was wasted and does not return when it is needed.

whyPoints.title: Three scripts read together
whyPoints.description: One habit failing three times needs one block rather than three subject arrangements. That diagnosis is only visible when the chemistry, physics and biology scripts are read side by side, and it saves most of the cost of a three-science plan.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure is attributed to the provider or market source that published it, read in October 2026. With three sciences the arithmetic matters, and three of seven researched competitor pages publish no price at all.

whyPoints.title: A structure that protects the avoided subject
whyPoints.description: A fixed weekly slot for the weakest science, the stronger two alternating, and a rotating fortnightly timed paper. That is a structural fix rather than an exhortation to work harder at something the student finds unpleasant.

faqs.question: Which science route is our child in Dubai Harbour actually on?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the board, syllabus code and tier for each science entry, in writing. A report card naming three sciences does not reveal whether those are separate 0620, 0625 and 0610 entries or a coordinated award recorded by subject. The distinction decides how many grades appear on the transcript, what post-16 courses will accept, and which specification to revise from, and it is the question families most often never think to ask.

faqs.question: Does a combined single award close off A Level sciences?
faqs.answer: It often limits them, and the only authoritative answer comes from the post-16 providers themselves. A sixth form offering A Level Chemistry publishes what it requires and that statement frequently assumes separate chemistry; an IB school offering Chemistry at Higher Level publishes its own expectation. Ask two or three likely providers in Year 10 while the route can still be revisited. Asking at application time is too late, because the entry is filed and the route is fixed.

faqs.question: How many science grades will each route produce?
faqs.answer: Three separate sciences produce three grades, a coordinated double award produces two, and a combined single award produces one. The count is information in its own right: a reader of an application sees how many science grades there are as well as what they say. It also affects the Ministry equivalency arithmetic, where five accredited subjects are counted and Arabic and Islamic education are excluded from that five.

faqs.question: Which practical component is our child sitting?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge separate sciences, either a practical test paper sat in a laboratory or the alternative written paper, and the school chooses, sometimes differently for different sciences. For Pearson Edexcel separate sciences there is no separate component and practical skills are assessed inside the written papers. Ask subject by subject, because preparing for an alternative paper as a block and weaving practical reasoning into topic work are different pieces of work entirely.

faqs.question: Can practical skills be taught over video?
faqs.answer: The examinable reasoning can, entirely. Apparatus choice, sources of error, reading a scale, completing a results table and drawing a supported conclusion are all written skills, and the Cambridge alternative paper tests nothing else. A shared page lets a tutor watch a results table being filled and intervene when a convention is broken. What video cannot do is handle apparatus for a student, which matters far less for a Year 11 candidate than families assume.

faqs.question: Is Coordinated Sciences a sensible middle option?
faqs.answer: For many students, yes, and it needs the same check as the others. It produces two grades across a coordinated selection of content, which is genuine breadth in reduced depth, and some post-16 science courses accept it while others do not. It is also not a reduced copy of the separate syllabuses: some separate-science topics are absent and some treatments differ, so revising it from 0620 or 0625 resources wastes effort and leaves gaps.

faqs.question: Is one tutor across chemistry, physics and biology ever workable?
faqs.answer: Eventually, if all three need subject work, because chemistry, physics and biology fail in different ways and a specialist in one will not spot the others' patterns. But the first purchase is often not three tutors at all. If the three mock scripts show the same habit failing everywhere, a single shared-skills block on command terms, unit conversion, graph work and results tables produces gains in all three for the cost of one subject's sessions.

faqs.question: How much should a three-science plan cost?
faqs.answer: Market figures read in October 2026 put qualified subject tutors online at AED 150 to 300 an hour and specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, with monthly estimates of AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 respectively for one hour a week. Three subjects multiplies that, which is why the shared-skills block is often the better first purchase. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours; ours are set after the free trial.

faqs.question: Why does one science always end up neglected?
faqs.answer: Because students avoid the subject they find hardest, and the avoidance is invisible until results day. A conscientious student who works steadily produces two reasonable grades and one poor one, and nobody can explain it because the effort was genuinely there. The fix is structural rather than motivational: give the weakest subject a fixed weekly slot, let the stronger two share a second, and write the allocation down somewhere visible.

faqs.question: What is the quickest useful thing to check on a mock script?
faqs.answer: Count the marks left unattempted on the last page, in each of the three sciences. A student leaving eight marks blank at the end of three papers has a pacing problem rather than three content problems, and the repair is a timing rule plus two or three full papers under genuine conditions. That number is invisible in a percentage and it takes about a minute per script to find, which makes it exceptional value.

faqs.question: Should we revise from Cambridge or Edexcel science resources?
faqs.answer: Only from the board on each entry confirmation, and check subject by subject because some schools in this cluster use different boards for different sciences. Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 cover similar physics in different house styles with different formula provision, and Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Practising the wrong archive trains a student to decode the wrong question format, and the time lost decoding comes out of thinking time.

faqs.question: Our child is on the combined route and now wants to study biology. What can we do?
faqs.answer: Speak to the school before the entry deadline, because the route may still be changeable, and speak to the post-16 providers about what they will accept. If the route is fixed, the realistic plan is to identify the missing content from the two specifications side by side and close it deliberately, which is more achievable over a summer than people expect. Ask the receiving provider what they expect a combined-route student to have covered.

faqs.question: When should practical preparation start?
faqs.answer: A term before the papers, not in the final fortnight. The examinable skills are finite: a limited number of apparatus choices, sources of error, scale-reading traps, table conventions and conclusion structures. Four to six sessions covers them properly for a Cambridge alternative paper, and for Pearson the same reasoning has to be woven into ordinary topic work from the start of Year 11 because there is no single paper to aim a block at.

faqs.question: How many science sessions a week is realistic from this district?
faqs.answer: Two or three in total across all subjects, not four, and that includes mathematics if it is also being supported. Children here lose ninety minutes a day to the school run, and more appointments than that crowd out the problem sets that actually build fluency. One fixed slot for the weakest subject, one alternating slot for the others, and a fortnightly timed paper is the structure that holds through a term.

intro.heading: The syllabus code decides everything else
paragraphs: Most IGCSE science tutoring goes wrong before the first lesson, and it goes wrong in the same way: nobody checks which qualification the student is actually entered for. Around Dubai Hills Estate, in a British-curriculum belt that stretches from Al Barsha South to Motor City, children sit at least four different science routes. Three separate Cambridge sciences. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences as a double award. Cambridge Combined Science as a single award. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE separate sciences, or Pearson's double award. Each has its own paper structure, and several have different grade ceilings depending on the entry tier.

A tutor who teaches 'IGCSE science' without naming the code is teaching an average of all of them. That sounds harmless and is not. A child entered for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences is being examined on content drawn across biology, chemistry and physics in proportions set by that syllabus, and spending lessons on separate-science depth wastes the hour. A child sitting a Pearson Edexcel separate science has no standalone practical exam, so drilling a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper trains a skill the board will never assess in that form.

So this page is written from the subject outwards rather than from the neighbourhood inwards. It starts with the codes and the papers, moves to the tier decision and its grade ceiling, then to the command words that decide where marks land, then to the specific places biology, chemistry and physics each leak marks for students in Dubai. After that it covers the past-paper routine that actually changes grades, what the market charges in AED with the source named, and how practical work is handled when teaching happens over video.

The practical question deserves an early answer because it is the one parents ask first. Your child's practical work and any practical examination happen at school, under the school's supervision and entry. Online tutoring does not replace that and should never claim to. What it does is teach the thinking the practical papers reward: controlling variables, identifying sources of error, reading a results table critically, and writing a conclusion that refers to the data rather than to the expectation. Those are explained and practised on screen as well as they are at a bench, and often better, because the tutor can mark the writing.

One thing stated plainly before the detail. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a science student in Dubai Hills Estate that is the better arrangement anyway, because a specification specialist matters far more than a short drive, and the specification is the whole subject of this page.

sections.heading: Which science qualification is actually on your child's statement of entry
paragraphs: Find the statement of entry before you do anything else. It names the board, the syllabus code and the entry tier, and those three facts determine what useful tutoring looks like. Around Dubai Hills Estate the same question gets four or five different answers depending on the campus, and in some schools different year groups sit different boards because a specification changed mid-cohort. Parents who assume are usually assuming the arrangement they knew in another country.

The distinction that catches most families is between separate sciences and an award route. Three separate Cambridge sciences give three IGCSE grades and the deepest preparation for A Level. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 gives a double award drawn across all three disciplines. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 gives a single award covering the same three in less depth. Pearson Edexcel runs separate sciences as 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, plus its own double and single award routes. These are not interchangeable, and tutoring aimed at the wrong one is simply the wrong lessons.

The second distinction is practical assessment, and it is the one where board choice changes tutoring most. Cambridge sciences carry a practical component that may be a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on how the centre enters candidates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences examine practical skill inside the theory papers. A student sitting Pearson needs to write confidently about method, variables, error and improvement; a student sitting a Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper needs that plus the specific conventions of that paper. Train the wrong one and the hour is wasted.

Codes are given as a starting point for a conversation with the school, not as a substitute for one: boards revise specifications on their own cycles and a code can change between cohorts. Ask the science department which code and which tier, in writing, and keep the reply.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the grade ceiling nobody mentions at the parents' evening
paragraphs: Cambridge science candidates are entered at Core or Extended tier, and the tier determines the grade range available. A Core entry is designed for a narrower range of attainment and does not reach the top grades; an Extended entry does, and is the route that A Level sciences assume. Schools make tier decisions on evidence, usually during Year 10, and the decision is reversible for a window that closes well before the exam series. Families who find out about the ceiling in March have found out too late.

Ask the science department three questions. Which tier is my child entered for. What is the highest grade available on that tier. When is the last date the entry can be changed. The third is the one that matters most, because it is the only one with a deadline attached, and because entry deadlines sit months before the exam. For a candidate in Dubai Hills Estate the choice is the June series or the November series -- Cambridge offers its February and March series to India only -- and the entry window for June closes in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, with forecast grades following a few weeks later. Pearson shows the same shape with dates you can check against a published timetable: its November 2026 International GCSE papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and entries for that window had closed long before the autumn term got going. The exact day is on your school's statement of entry, so ask the exams officer for it rather than working from a date you read online.

Where a tier change is the right decision, tutoring has a specific job: evidence it. A student who needs to move from Core to Extended has to demonstrate Extended-standard work on past paper questions, not enthusiasm. Six weeks of marked Extended questions, with the marks recorded, is a stronger case to a head of science than any conversation. Where a tier change is not realistic, the honest answer is to maximise the grade available rather than chase a ceiling that cannot be reached, and we say so.

Grade ranges are deliberately described rather than numbered, because Cambridge publishes 9-1 and A*-G graded versions of the same science syllabuses under different codes and the labels differ between them. The syllabus document for your child's exact code is the authority on this, and it is free to download from the board.

sections.heading: Command words: where the mark scheme actually puts the marks
paragraphs: Science mark schemes are not generous or stingy; they are literal. A question that says describe is asking for what happens. A question that says explain is asking why, and an answer that describes earns nothing however accurate it is. A question that says suggest is inviting a reasoned answer about an unfamiliar situation and will credit several different sensible responses. Students who learn this stop losing marks they already understood the science for, which is why command-word work is the fastest return available in Year 11.

The habit we teach is mechanical and takes about three weeks to stick. Before writing anything, underline the command word and read the mark allocation. Three marks means three distinct creditable points, not one point expressed at length. If the command word is explain, the answer needs at least one because or therefore in it. If the question gives a context, the answer refers to that context rather than to a textbook example. None of this is clever. All of it is worth marks on every paper, in every science, on both boards.

There is a second layer that separates a grade 6 from a grade 8. Precision of vocabulary. In biology, diffusion and osmosis are not synonyms and a mark scheme will not accept one for the other. In chemistry, an answer about rate that says the reaction speeds up earns less than one that names more frequent successful collisions. In physics, heat and temperature are different quantities. Tutors who correct this consistently, in writing, change a student's written work faster than any amount of content revision.

The table lists the command words that recur most and what each one actually requires. It is worth printing and keeping next to the student while they work, which is a slightly old-fashioned suggestion that works. Confirm the full list for your child's board in the published syllabus document, because each board defines its own set and the definitions are the examiner's, not ours.

sections.heading: Where marks go missing in biology, chemistry and physics
paragraphs: Biology first, because it is the science students underestimate. The content reads as familiar, so revision feels productive while the marks do not move. The losses cluster in extended-response answers: a six-mark question on transport in plants answered with a description of xylem, or a homeostasis question that names the organ but never completes the feedback loop. Biology rewards complete chains of reasoning and the specific named example the mark scheme asks for. Nothing about that is intuitive, and all of it is teachable.

Chemistry marks are decided by quantitative work. Moles, concentration, limiting reagents, percentage yield. Students who can balance an equation still lose marks for missing state symbols, wrong units, and answers rounded to a number of significant figures that the data does not support. The organic sequence is the other recurring complaint, and it is usually a symptom of memorising each reaction separately rather than seeing the pattern. Taught as patterns, the topic shrinks to a fraction of the apparent load.

Physics is where the complaint is loudest and the diagnosis is most often wrong. Students say they cannot do electricity. What is usually true is that they cannot reliably rearrange a formula under time pressure, convert units in their head, or read a gradient from a graph using points far enough apart to be accurate. Those are three separable skills, each fixable in a few sessions, and none of them is about electricity. A tutor who re-teaches circuits to a student with an algebra problem will spend six weeks achieving nothing.

Across all three there is a category that belongs to none of them: exam management. Students who answer every question in order run out of time on the questions worth most. Students who leave a calculation half-finished get no credit for the half they did, when writing the formula alone would have earned a mark. Students who never check whether an answer is physically plausible submit a mass of two thousand kilograms for a test tube. These are habits, they are coached rather than taught, and they are worth more than most topics.

sections.heading: The past-paper routine, counted back from the exam series
paragraphs: Past papers are the most misused resource in IGCSE science. Doing them is not revision; marking them honestly is. A student who works through fifteen papers and marks each one generously has learned to feel prepared. A student who works through five and compares every answer against the mark scheme line by line has learned where the marks are. The second student scores higher, and the difference is not effort.

The routine below is counted backwards from an exam series because that is how the work has to be planned. Note what is not in it: new content in the final six weeks. By then the honest job is technique, recall of the things most likely to appear, and keeping the student calm enough to read questions properly. A tutor proposing to cover the whole syllabus in April is either misreading the calendar or selling hours, and families in Dubai Hills Estate should treat that proposal as information about the tutor.

Two practical details. First, use papers from the correct tier and the correct syllabus code; a Core paper flatters an Extended candidate and an old-specification paper tests content that may have been removed. Second, keep an error log organised by syllabus topic rather than by date, so that by March the student can see that eleven of their last thirty lost marks came from one topic. That single document changes how the final term is spent, and almost nobody keeps one without being asked to.

Entry deadlines deserve a place in the same plan, because they are the dates with consequences. Pearson is the easiest board to anchor a plan to, because its windows are published plainly: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs the same rhythm across its June and November series -- entries close months ahead of the first script, forecast grades a few weeks after that, results in August for the June series and in January for November -- but the precise days sit on your centre's statement of entry rather than anywhere we can usefully restate them. Work from the board's own live timetable PDF, and check which Cambridge administrative zone your campus is in before you trust any published day.

sections.heading: Online science lessons and the practical question, answered plainly
paragraphs: Parents ask about practical work first and they are right to. Here is the honest position. Your child's practical work, and any practical examination their centre enters them for, happens at school under the school's supervision. No tutoring arrangement changes that, and any provider who implies they can deliver a Cambridge practical test should be treated with suspicion. What tutoring does is teach the reasoning the practical papers assess, which is a written skill in both boards' designs.

That skill has four parts and all four are taught well on screen. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar method. Spotting the specific source of error that a method invites, rather than listing generic ones. Reading a results table critically, including the anomalous value nobody mentioned. Writing a conclusion that refers to the data obtained rather than to the result the student expected. Students who can do those four things score on practical-skills questions regardless of how much bench time they have had.

Live video is in some respects better for this than a bench. The tutor can put a results table on screen, ask the student to annotate it, and see the annotation as it happens. Written answers can be marked in the session, against the published scheme, with the student watching each mark being awarded or withheld. Try doing that while two people are setting up apparatus. IB Gram delivers lessons for UAE families one-to-one and live online, timed to Gulf Standard Time; we do not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, as home visits are a service we run only in India.

What a family needs at home is small. A device with a real keyboard, a stable connection, pen and paper, and a room with the door closed. Science involves drawing, so a cheap graphics tablet or a phone used as an overhead camera repays its cost quickly, because the tutor can watch working as it is written rather than seeing only the final answer. No laboratory equipment is required and nobody should be selling you any.

sections.heading: Five subjects, not six: what UAE equivalency actually counts
paragraphs: Families planning an IGCSE subject list in Dubai need the equivalency rules in front of them, because the subject count affects which sciences are worth sitting. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3.

The detail that catches people out is the exclusion. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. One competitor page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five, with those two excluded from the count. A family building a subject list around the wrong number either sits an unnecessary subject or, worse, arrives short.

For the American track the requirements are different in kind: English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no points threshold we can publish, because none has been read on a Ministry of Education source; anybody quoting one to you should be asked where it came from.

Two boundaries to be clear about. Equivalency is a Ministry of Education process and IB Gram neither performs it nor influences it; we describe it and point you to the official channel. And tutoring is not a requirement of equivalency, university admission or school progression. Any provider suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process, which is both inaccurate and a reason to look elsewhere.

faqs.question: Is my child sitting Coordinated Science or three separate IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry answers it in one line. Three separate sciences will show three codes, typically Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson Edexcel 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. A co-ordinated or combined route shows a single code such as Cambridge 0654 or 0653. The distinction changes everything about useful tutoring, because the content map and the depth expected differ. If the document is not to hand, ask the science department to confirm the code and the entry tier in writing, and keep the reply for the sixth-form conversation later.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge 0654 and 0653?
faqs.answer: Both draw content from biology, chemistry and physics, and both are entered at Core or Extended tier. Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences is a double award, so it counts as two IGCSEs and covers more content. Cambridge 0653 Combined Science is a single award covering the same three disciplines in less depth. The practical consequence sits two years later: a single award narrows A Level science options at some campuses. Check the entry requirements of your target sixth form before choosing, because that is the decision the code is really making.

faqs.question: Can a Core-tier science candidate still reach a grade 7?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge Core entries are capped below the top grades by design, which is the single most important thing for a family to know and the thing least often said at a parents' evening. If your child needs a top grade, the entry has to be Extended, and entries can only be changed inside a window that closes months before the exam. Ask the science department which tier your child is on, what the ceiling is, and the last date it can change. Then make the tutoring plan serve that deadline.

faqs.question: How is the alternative-to-practical paper different from a real practical exam?
faqs.answer: A practical test is sat with apparatus under exam conditions. An alternative-to-practical paper asks the same thinking in writing: identify the variables, spot the error a method invites, read a results table, draw a conclusion from the data given. Which one your child sits depends on how the centre enters candidates, so ask. Either way, the reasoning is the teachable part, and it is taught well over video because written answers can be marked against the scheme while the student watches each mark being awarded or withheld.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science loses the most marks for UAE students?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, on quantitative work, and physics for a reason that is usually misread. Chemistry marks go on moles, concentration, state symbols, units and significant figures, and students who can balance equations still drop them routinely. Physics complaints centre on electricity, but the underlying problem is normally formula rearrangement, unit conversion or reading a gradient badly. Biology is the quiet one: the content feels familiar, so revision feels productive while extended-response marks stay flat because explanation chains are left incomplete.

faqs.question: What does the command word explain require that describe does not?
faqs.answer: A reason, stated. Describe asks what happens, in sequence. Explain asks why it happens, and an answer that only describes earns nothing even when every fact in it is correct. The practical test is whether the answer contains a because or a therefore. Students who form the habit of underlining the command word and reading the mark allocation before writing recover marks they had already earned in understanding. It takes about three weeks to stick and keeps paying on every paper, in all three sciences, on both boards.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Year 11 science student do before the exam series?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families think, marked far more carefully than most students manage. Five papers marked line by line against the published scheme teach more than fifteen marked generously. Use papers from the correct tier and the correct syllabus code, because a Core paper flatters an Extended candidate and an old-specification paper tests content that may have been removed. Keep an error log organised by syllabus topic rather than by date; by March it will show that a disproportionate share of lost marks comes from two or three topics.

faqs.question: My son keeps getting the units wrong in physics calculations. Is that fixable?
faqs.answer: Quickly, and it is one of the highest-return fixes available. Unit errors are a procedural habit, not a knowledge gap: the student calculates correctly and then loses the mark at the last step. The fix is to write the unit before the number, convert everything to base units at the start of the question rather than at the end, and state the formula on its own line so a method mark survives an arithmetic slip. Three or four sessions of deliberate practice usually settles it, and the gain shows up across every physics paper.

faqs.question: Do Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences use the same paper structure as Cambridge?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference matters most for practical skills. Pearson Edexcel examines practical skill inside the written papers rather than in a standalone practical test, so a student needs to write confidently about method, variables, error and improvement. Cambridge sciences carry a practical component that may be a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre's entry. Training the wrong format wastes the hour. Confirm the board and the paper numbers from the statement of entry before any tutoring plan is written.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Practical work and any practical examination happen at school, under the school's supervision and entry, and no tutoring arrangement changes that. What tutoring teaches is the reasoning the practical questions assess: identifying variables in an unfamiliar method, naming the specific error a method invites rather than generic ones, reading a results table critically including the anomaly, and writing a conclusion that refers to the data rather than the expected result. All four are written skills, and marking written answers live on screen works better than it does at a bench.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE science tuition cost per hour in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: The published Dubai bands, read from providers' own pages in October 2026, run roughly AED 45 to 150 for budget online tutoring - EdFlik AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 - then AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and above, including TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits sit at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. Those are market rates with sources attached, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Should we tutor all three sciences at once or start with the weakest one?
faqs.answer: Start with the weakest one almost always. Three sciences at once means three hours a week on top of a Year 11 workload and mandatory UAE subject hours, and the plan is usually abandoned by the second month. One science, diagnosed properly and fixed, frees attention for the other two and often improves them indirectly, because the maths and command-word habits transfer. For a co-ordinated or combined award the content is drawn across all three anyway, so one tutor covering the single code is the natural arrangement rather than a compromise.

faqs.question: Do the sciences count towards the five subjects the UAE requires at equivalency?
faqs.answer: Yes. The sourced rule for the British track is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Sciences count towards the total in the normal way. Note that one competitor page currently ranking in this market states six subjects; the sourced figure is five. Verify the current rule on the Ministry of Education's own pages before building a subject list, and remember that the A Level requirement sits alongside it.

faqs.question: When should a Year 10 science student start tutoring rather than wait?
faqs.answer: When the school's reports show a gap widening rather than a single poor test, when the tier entry is in doubt, or when the student has stopped asking questions in class. Year 10 support is cheaper per mark than Year 11 support because it prevents triage rather than performing it, and because tier entries are still changeable. If you are deciding between starting now and starting in September of Year 11, start now with one session a week and review it in six weeks against marked work.

faqs.question: How do we know which science specification the school entered my child for?
faqs.answer: Ask the science department for the board, the syllabus code and the entry tier, in writing, and ask for the statement of entry when it is issued. Also ask which Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six zones and states that using the wrong zone's timetable is the centre's risk, not the board's. Keep all of it in one place: the same three facts will be needed for the sixth-form application and for any equivalency paperwork later.

intro.heading: Three disciplines, three different reasons marks go missing
paragraphs: The three IGCSE sciences fail in three distinct ways, and that single observation is worth more than any general revision advice. Biology marks are lost to imprecise terminology and to long answers that contain fewer distinct points than the mark allocation required. Chemistry marks are lost to method selection in calculations and to notation: a missing state symbol, an unbalanced equation, a charge left off an ion. Physics marks are lost to algebra, standard form and graph reading. A student who is told to revise harder is being given the same instruction for three different problems.

Dubai Internet City is a free zone in Al Sufouh rather than a residential district: the regional offices of large technology companies, bordered by Dubai Knowledge Park and Dubai Media City, with the Red Line of the Metro running past it. Families connected to it live in The Greens, The Views, Barsha Heights, Al Sufouh and the Marina towers, and their children attend schools across Al Sufouh and Al Barsha. Enquiries from this postcode typically come from a parent during the working day about a student who will be home at five, which shapes what a sensible arrangement looks like.

What that arrangement needs is a record. A parent who is in the office when a session runs cannot ask how it went, so written session notes, a fixed weekly slot that does not need reconfirming, and a recording are not conveniences but the substance of the service. We treat them as deliverables rather than as extras, and families in this district consistently tell us they matter more than any other operational detail.

There is one more variable families underestimate, and it is the tier. Cambridge separate sciences are entered at Core or Extended, and the two are not the same syllabus: Extended carries supplementary content the Core specification does not contain, and Core is capped below the top grades. A student revising the wrong set of material is working hard in a direction the paper will not reward, and a capped grade can quietly close a post-16 science route a family assumed was open. Pearson's separate sciences are untiered, which removes the question but introduces another one about whether separates or the double award was taken. Both questions are answered by the entry rather than by memory, and both are settled by one email to the examinations officer asking for the codes and the tier in writing.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches UAE students online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For science specifically the screen is not a compromise. Diagrams are annotated live, a graph can be redrawn three times in two minutes, and a student's own marked script sits on screen beside the mark scheme, which is where almost all useful diagnosis in these subjects actually happens.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science actually covers, discipline by discipline
paragraphs: Parents often ask what is on the syllabus, and the honest answer is that it depends on four things: the board, the code, the tier and whether the student is sitting separates, a double award or a combined award. Those four determine both the content and the paper structure. Cambridge separate sciences are Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625. Pearson's are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Cambridge 0654 is a co-ordinated double award and 0653 a combined single award; Pearson's double award is 4SD0.

Within that, the broad shape of each discipline is stable. Biology runs from cells and biological molecules through transport, respiration, photosynthesis and coordination, into genetics, inheritance, variation and ecology. Chemistry runs from particles, atomic structure and bonding through stoichiometry, energetics and rates into acids and bases, the periodic table, metals and organic chemistry. Physics runs from motion, forces and energy through thermal physics, waves, electricity and magnetism into atomic and nuclear physics. Each ends with material that is frequently taught late and therefore under-rehearsed.

The practical component is examined in writing at most international centres, through an alternative-to-practical paper rather than a laboratory test. That paper is examinable technique: reading an instrument to the correct precision, identifying variables, finding the flaw in a described method, building a results table with units, plotting and interpreting a graph, and suggesting an improvement that addresses the actual weakness. It is among the most trainable components in the whole qualification and among the most neglected.

What the content list does not tell you is where the marks go, which is why the next sections are organised around failure rather than around topics. A tutor who can recite the syllabus is less useful than one who can look at a marked script and say that your child is losing marks to point-counting in biology, equation balancing in chemistry and rearrangement in physics, in that order of size.

sections.heading: Biology: terminology, point-counting and the questions students answer too well
paragraphs: Biology at IGCSE is content-dense and language-sensitive. Marks attach to precise terms, and an approximation of a term scores nothing even when the understanding behind it is sound. A student who writes that something moves from high to low concentration has described diffusion without naming it; depending on the question, that may or may not score. The repair is vocabulary discipline rather than more reading, and it works best as a short routine at the start of each session rather than as a revision list.

The largest single recoverable loss in biology is point-counting. A six-mark question requires six distinct scoring points, and students regularly write three good points at length and assume thoroughness substitutes for coverage. The mechanical fix is to read the mark allocation first, plan that many separate points in the margin, and then write them. Two sessions of this on the student's own answers usually changes the habit, and the gain appears across every long-answer question rather than only in the topic being revised.

The third issue is the questions students answer too well. A two-mark question answered with a paragraph scores two marks and costs the time that the back of the paper needed. Biology papers are long, and students who over-write early run out of time for material they knew. Pacing in this subject is therefore a content question in disguise: the marks lost at the end of the paper are often the easiest on it.

sections.heading: Chemistry: equations that balance, calculations with a chosen method, notation that counts
paragraphs: Chemistry at this level is where notation first starts carrying marks, and students read notation as presentation. An unbalanced equation is wrong. A missing state symbol, where the question or the convention requires one, loses a mark. A charge omitted from an ion changes the species being described. None of this is unfair and all of it is mechanical, which is good news: mechanical habits survive examination pressure better than conceptual understanding does, and they take weeks rather than terms to establish.

The calculation issue is method selection rather than arithmetic. A student who can convert a mass to moles when told to, and does not recognise that a question requires it, has a selection problem. Teaching more worked examples does not help, because every worked example announces its own method. Mixed sets do help: questions in random order where the student has to decide the approach before applying it. A few weeks of that changes performance noticeably, and it is one of the cheapest interventions available in the subject.

The third area is the practical knowledge examined in writing: tests for gases and ions, separation techniques, how a titration is carried out and what makes a result reliable. These are facts and procedures rather than reasoning, and they are often the last thing revised. A student who can describe a test with its observation and conclusion, in that order, scores reliably on questions that others treat as recall lotteries.

Organic chemistry arrives late in most schemes of work and is consequently the least rehearsed part of the course. Homologous series, naming conventions and the basic reaction types are a small amount of content, and a student who covers them properly in the final term often finds the easiest marks on the paper sitting there. It is worth checking whether the class has actually finished it.

sections.heading: Physics: the algebra behind the grade
paragraphs: Physics is the IGCSE science where a strong student most often underperforms, and the cause is usually mathematical rather than scientific. Rearranging a formula when the unknown is in the denominator, handling standard form, converting between unit prefixes, and reading a gradient from a drawn line rather than from two plotted points: those four skills decide a large share of the marks. A student who is capable in biology and struggling in physics almost always has a specific algebra gap, and diagnosing it is worth more than a term of topic revision.

The second physics issue is working. Method marks are available on multi-step questions even when the final answer is wrong, and a student who writes only answers forfeits marks they had already earned. Teaching a student to set out the formula, the substitution and the result as three separate lines takes a fortnight and protects marks for the rest of their school career. It also makes their own errors findable, which is the beginning of self-correction.

The third is graph work, which is manual and therefore trainable. Choosing a scale that uses the grid, plotting accurately, drawing a line rather than joining dots, reading a gradient from the line, and quoting that gradient with units. Each is a mark somewhere in the paper and each improves with supervised practice far faster than with unsupervised practice, because the errors are invisible to the person making them.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: what the tier actually changes
paragraphs: Cambridge separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended, and the two differ in content, in papers sat and in the grades available. Extended reaches the top of the scale; Core is capped. The decision is usually made by the department on set performance, and families frequently learn which tier their child is on when a mock timetable arrives. That timing is the problem, because a capped grade can quietly close a post-16 science route that the family assumed was open.

What changes with tier is not simply difficulty. The Extended content includes material the Core syllabus does not contain, so a Core student revising Extended material is doing unnecessary work, and an Extended student revising Core material is under-prepared for their paper. Confirming the tier is therefore as important as confirming the code, and the same single email to the examinations officer gets both.

Where a student is on Core and aiming at A Level or Diploma sciences afterwards, the conversation with the department belongs early in Year 10 while sets are still fluid. Ask what specifically would need to improve for an Extended entry to be considered, and treat that as the work plan. By the spring of Year 11 the entry is lodged and the question has changed into how to get the best possible outcome from the tier taken, which is a smaller and less hopeful conversation.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson: the same science, different papers
paragraphs: Schools in this corridor use both boards, sometimes across different subjects in the same year group, and the practical consequence for revision is larger than families expect. The science content overlaps heavily. The question wording, the paper structure, the calculator rules and the way practical knowledge is examined do not. A student revising on the wrong board's past papers is doing real work in a dialect that will not be spoken in the examination hall.

Cambridge separate sciences assess practical skills either through a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, with most international centres using the written route. Pearson examines practical knowledge within its written papers. Cambridge's Core and Extended tiering has no Pearson equivalent in the separate sciences. These are not small distinctions when a student is deciding which hundred past-paper questions to attempt in the final six weeks.

There is one piece of Cambridge administration worth knowing as a parent. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A timetable found through an internet search is not a timetable. Ask the school for the zone-correct version and keep it.

On the series: Cambridge IGCSE runs in June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only and has no bearing on a UAE entry, so a Dubai family should ignore any date attached to it. Pearson's published pattern gives a sense of the shape: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: A free-zone household: sessions planned around a working day
paragraphs: The scheduling constraint in this district is the parent's working day rather than the school run alone. A family connected to Internet City typically has one or both parents in the free zone until the evening, and a student who gets home at five is unsupervised for the hour that matters. That shapes what the arrangement must provide: a fixed slot that does not need confirming each week, written notes after every session so the parent knows what happened, a record of work set, and a recording.

Journey times still matter. Students returning from Al Barsha or Jumeirah arrive home across the same hours the free zone empties, and Marina and JBR students arrive latest of all. A session booked before 17:30 for those students will eventually be rescheduled, and a rescheduled session in a content-heavy subject is a lost week rather than a lost hour. Because sessions run online there is no second journey, which is why blocks in this corridor tend to complete rather than fragment.

The student's end needs very little: a hard surface rather than a sofa, squared paper and a ruler for graph work, their own calculator rather than a phone, and headphones so a shared apartment is not part of the lesson. The camera is angled at the page, because in every science the diagnosis comes from watching the working appear. Setting this up once, properly, before the first session prevents most of the friction families anticipate.

Ramadan shifts the pattern for a few weeks and Dubai schools adjust their hours. We agree the revised timetable before the month begins, usually fewer and shorter sessions moved to the late morning or the post-Iftar window, with lighter work between them. Where a parent's own hours change during the month, the written notes carry more weight than usual and we write them with that in mind.

sections.heading: Permits, limits and the things worth verifying yourself
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and the application is made through its smart app, website and e-services system. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no fine schedule is published, any specific amount you read should be treated as unverified.

IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, the International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or the Ministry of Education, and no page here will suggest otherwise. We have no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We do not enter candidates for examinations, we do not perform Ministry equivalency, and we do not provide home visits anywhere in the Emirates. Each of those sentences is here because a competitor in this market implies the opposite of it.

On materials: we reference and link official syllabus, specimen and timetable documents rather than reproducing them, and we do not supply board-owned papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables. Your child's school has legitimate access through its own subscriptions. On figures: every number on this page carries a source, and we publish no success rates, satisfaction scores or star ratings, because we could not produce the data behind any of them.

Worth verifying independently in every case: the syllabus codes and tier on the entry, with your school's examinations officer; the zone-correct examination timetable, from the same person; the school's inspection judgements on the regulator's own site rather than from a summary. Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, described on u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK; Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education.

process.title: Get the code and the tier in one email
process.description: Ask the examinations officer which syllabus numbers appear on your child's science entry and which tier. That single answer settles how much content exists, which past papers are worth sitting and whether practical skills are examined by a test or a written paper. Every plan we build sits on top of it.

process.title: Send one marked paper per discipline
process.description: Three marked scripts take twenty minutes to read and show where the marks are actually going: point-counting in biology, equation balancing and method selection in chemistry, algebra and graph reading in physics. Without them, allocating weeks between three subjects is guesswork presented as a plan.

process.title: Free trial lesson in the weakest discipline
process.description: The first session is free and runs in whichever science the scripts put furthest behind, working through real questions rather than discussing services. A short written note follows naming the two priority topics and the recurring error types, and that note is yours whether or not you continue with us.

process.title: Fix the slot and the reporting
process.description: One weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, set after the return from school. Because the parent here is often still at work, we confirm in advance what arrives after each session: a note on what was covered, what was set, and what is next. That record is the part of the service families in this district value most.

process.title: Re-mark at week four
process.description: A second paper is sat and marked at week four and the error tally compared with week one. If the pattern has not shifted, we change the approach or the tutor rather than defending either. If the diagnosis turns out to be maths rather than science, we say so, because a term of physics teaching will not repair an algebra gap.

whyPoints.title: One discipline fixed properly beats three covered thinly
whyPoints.description: The weakest science is usually weak for a reason it shares with a second, most often algebra. Repairing that lifts two grades at once, which is a cheaper and more honest recommendation than three weekly sessions, and it is what the marked scripts normally support.

whyPoints.title: Tutors matched to a syllabus code, not to a subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson examine the same science through different papers, and Core and Extended are different content. Matching online means selecting a tutor who teaches the exact code rather than whoever is nearby and willing, which for a student six weeks from a paper is the whole difference.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper is treated as technique
whyPoints.description: Precision reading, variable identification, table headings, flaw spotting and specific improvements are built into sessions from the first month. It is the component most often postponed to the final fortnight and one of the most reliably recoverable on the paper.

whyPoints.title: Designed for a parent who cannot be in the room
whyPoints.description: Written notes, recordings, a record of work set and a slot that never needs reconfirming. In a free-zone household the person arranging tutoring is usually at a desk when it happens, and the reporting is the service rather than an extra.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE science tutoring cost for a family near Dubai Internet City?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates put a qualified subject tutor working online at roughly AED 150-300 an hour and an IGCSE specialist at about AED 200-450 or more. Monthly figures from the Bestimate Dubai table run around AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 in the mid band for one weekly subject. In-home visits are quoted at roughly AED 180-500 an hour because the journey is inside the fee. Across three sciences the multiplication is what makes most families fund one discipline properly. Those are market figures with sources, not our price list; we quote after the free trial.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our apartment in The Greens or Barsha Heights?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; sending a tutor to a family address is a service we run only in India. Science sessions here are delivered one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. In a free-zone household that is usually the better fit: the parent organising the tutoring is often still at work when the session runs, so a fixed slot, written notes and a recording are more useful than a doorbell, and no session is lost to the evening traffic out of Al Sufouh.

faqs.question: Which science should we start with if our child is behind in all three?
faqs.answer: Usually physics, and the reason is mathematical rather than scientific. Rearranging formulae, standard form, unit prefixes and reading gradients are maths skills examined in a physics paper, and the same weaknesses quietly damage chemistry calculations. Repairing them therefore improves two subjects. Biology is more often a terminology and point-counting problem, which a disciplined student can work on with less supervision once the method is taught. Send one marked paper per subject and we will tell you which single discipline gives the best return for the weeks you have.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child is on Core or Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer, because the entry is the only reliable source. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered: Extended covers the core plus supplementary content and reaches the top grades, while Core covers less and is capped. The tier matters for revision as much as for outcome, since a Core student working through Extended material is doing unnecessary work and an Extended student revising only Core material is under-prepared. Pearson's separate sciences are untiered, which removes the question. Either way, get the codes and tier in the same email.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether the school uses Cambridge or Pearson for science?
faqs.answer: It matters for revision rather than for difficulty. The content overlaps heavily, but question wording, paper structure, calculator rules and the way practical knowledge is assessed all differ, and Cambridge's Core and Extended tiering has no Pearson equivalent in the separate sciences. A student practising on the wrong board's past papers is doing genuine work in a dialect that will not be spoken in the hall. Confirm the board and code before choosing which papers to attempt, particularly in the final six weeks when there is no time to waste.

faqs.question: Why does a six-mark biology answer score only three?
faqs.answer: Because it contained three distinct scoring points rather than six. Students read a six-mark question as an instruction to write thoroughly, and depth does not substitute for coverage. The mechanical fix is to read the allocation first, plan that number of separate points in the margin, then write them using the precise terminology rather than an approximation. Two sessions working on the student's own answers usually changes the habit, and the gain shows up on every long-answer question in the paper rather than only in the topic that was being revised.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but the grades do not show it. What is happening?
faqs.answer: Four things, usually. Rearranging a formula when the unknown sits in the denominator. Standard form on very large or very small values. Converting between unit prefixes. And reading a gradient from a drawn line rather than from two plotted points. Alongside those, students who write only answers forfeit the method marks available on multi-step questions even when their final figure is wrong. Setting out formula, substitution and result as three separate lines protects those marks, takes a fortnight to establish and makes the student's own errors findable.

faqs.question: How are practical skills examined if we never set foot in a laboratory with you?
faqs.answer: Laboratory work for school purposes happens at school under the school's supervision, and no tutor participates in it. What tutoring affects is the written assessment of practical skills, which most international centres sit as an alternative-to-practical paper. The question types are predictable: reading an instrument to the correct precision, identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, spotting the flaw in a described method, completing a results table with headings and units, plotting and interpreting a graph, and suggesting an improvement that addresses the specific weakness described rather than a generic one.

faqs.question: We arrived in Dubai in the middle of Year 11. Is it too late?
faqs.answer: Not too late, and the approach has to change. We start with an audit rather than teaching: one session going through the specification topic by topic to establish what the previous school covered and to what depth, compared against the new department's teaching order. The output is a prioritised list, not a full re-teach, because there is not time for everything and nobody should sell you the idea that there is. We will say plainly which topics we expect to leave uncovered, which is the honest part of this conversation.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take all three sciences for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is often not the best arrangement. Most strong science tutors teach two of the three disciplines well and are honest about the third. For a student in the final year, two specialists on two evenings with one shared written plan usually beats one generalist across three, because the difference between a capable explanation and an expert one is largest in the topics that are actually causing trouble. If we do not have a good match for a discipline we say so rather than stretching someone into it.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science papers sat by candidates in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge IGCSE runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Dubai centres usually enter the main Year 11 cohort for the summer window and treat November as the resit route. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only, so disregard any date attached to it. Ask the school for the zone-correct Cambridge timetable, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version.

faqs.question: Is a marking clinic enough, or does our child need weekly teaching?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the scripts say. A student who is working hard, understands the material and keeps landing in the same grade band usually needs marking rather than teaching: they sit papers independently, we mark line by line against the published scheme, and a shorter session covers only the error pattern. A student with genuine content gaps needs weekly teaching sequenced against the school's scheme of work. Many families do both, with weekly teaching in the weakest subject and clinics covering the two stronger ones, which keeps the cost proportionate.

faqs.question: What happens in the last two weeks before the science papers?
faqs.answer: Nothing new, by design. At that point the work with a positive return is eliminating errors the tally says are recurring, practising pacing, and settling the order in which the student will attempt each paper. Introducing a new topic in the final fortnight produces anxiety rather than marks, and it displaces revision of material the student half-knows, which is where the recoverable marks actually are. Students resist this rule and it is the one that most reliably protects a grade, so we agree it in advance rather than arguing about it at the time.

faqs.question: What if you cannot match a tutor for a specific science syllabus?
faqs.answer: We say so instead of filling the slot. Mainstream requests such as Extended 0610 or 4PH1 are matched quickly. Narrower ones, including 0653 Combined Science or centres using the practical test rather than the alternative-to-practical route, draw on a smaller group. The honest options are a different time, a short wait for the right tutor, or a marking clinic in the meantime so the weeks still produce something useful. We also tell you where a tutor is based before you book rather than after.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-inter.closingHeading: Three marked papers and two codes is all we need to start

Everything runs one-to-one, online, over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with written notes waiting for whoever is still at the office.

intro.heading: One tutor or three? The answer is in two marked scripts
paragraphs: Dubai Investments Park sits in the southern corridor, split between DIP 1 and DIP 2, mixing industrial and commercial plots with residential enclaves including Green Community and Ritaj, served by Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, Emirates Road and its own Metro station towards Expo City. A British-curriculum school and two IB schools sit inside the district, with most secondary students travelling out to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan or Dubai South.

A family here looking for science support is usually looking at three subjects at once, or at one combined award covering all three, and the practical question is whether that means one tutor or three. Three tutors is three times the cost, three times the scheduling in a week already shortened by a long school run, and three separate relationships to manage. One tutor is cheaper and simpler and is sometimes the wrong answer.

The thing that decides it is whether the deficit is shared or specific, and you can establish that yourself. Take the last marked script from two different sciences and compare the annotations. If the same comment appears in both, such as a description offered where the question said explain, or a method that assumes the reader was present, the deficit is a shared convention and one tutor fixes all three subjects in a single block of four to six sessions. If the comments are unrelated, you have one topic problem in one science, which is a three to five session fix with a specialist.

The second thing to establish is which award your child sits, because separate sciences, Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 and Cambridge Combined Science 0653 are three different qualifications with different papers and different depths. A tutor practising separate-science past papers with a Combined Science candidate is teaching material that will not appear, which wastes the block and dents confidence simultaneously.

The third factor is the week itself. Three sciences need three contacts, and in this corridor children travel to schools inside DIP, to Jebel Ali, Al Furjan, Dubai South or further north, so arrival home ranges from under four o'clock to past six. A household that can hold three weekday science slots is unusual here; most can hold one or two plus a weekend morning, which is a reason to sequence the work rather than run it in parallel.

One premise, stated plainly: IB Gram delivers one-to-one IGCSE science tuition into DIP homes as live online video sessions on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams and working shared and annotated on screen. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home visits are a service we run only in India. For a three-science household that is useful in a specific way: three specialists can take three evenings without three cars crossing two motorways at the same hour.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-inves.subjectsIntro: Science support here is organised by what shows up in marked work, since that is what decides whether you need one tutor or three.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and exchange
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, circulation and gas exchange. The dominant loss is an explanation that describes a structure without linking it to the function the question asked about, which is a shared convention problem rather than a biology one.

subjects.name: Biology: inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Genetic crosses, variation and selection. Students produce a correct Punnett square and omit the ratio or probability the question requested, and use gene and allele interchangeably in written answers.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The arithmetic underneath most chemistry marks. Errors are almost never conceptual: a ratio inverted, a limiting reagent ignored, or units dropped partway through an otherwise sound calculation.

subjects.name: Chemistry: rates, energetics and equilibrium
subjects.description: Collision theory, exothermic and endothermic changes, reversible reactions. The characteristic error is predicting correctly and then explaining the prediction by restating it rather than by reference to the change that caused it.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and analysis
subjects.description: Homologous series, basic reactions and identification tests. An answer naming a correct product without the balanced equation, or a correct test without its observation, scores nothing in most schemes.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The topic DIP students name most often. The difficulty is reasoning rather than recall: saying what happens to current and potential difference when one component changes requires holding the whole circuit in mind.

subjects.name: Physics: waves and energy
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum and energy transfer. Diagrams are marked on specified features, so a qualitatively correct ray diagram without labelled angles or a normal line loses most of its marks.

subjects.name: Practical skills on paper
subjects.description: Describing a method reproducibly, classifying variables, reading apparatus to the right precision and evaluating a specific weakness. Reliably the weakest paper in the set, shared across all three sciences, and therefore the single most efficient block available.

subjects.name: Command terms across the sciences
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate each demand a different response shape, and the conventions are shared across biology, chemistry and physics. Fixing this once pays three times over, which is the whole case for one tutor rather than three.

subjects.name: Data handling and graphs
subjects.description: Tables, plotting, line of best fit, gradients and conclusions supported by the data. Shared across the sciences, taught in a hurry separately in each one, and the second most efficient shared block after command terms.

sections.heading: The twenty-minute test: shared deficit or specific?
paragraphs: This is the most useful unpaid work available to a family in this situation, and it decides whether you are buying one tutor or three. It needs no scientific expertise, only the marked scripts and a willingness to ignore the grades.

Take the last marked script from two different sciences, ideally biology and physics because they feel least alike. Read the marker's annotations rather than the ticks, and look for repetition across the two papers rather than within one. Markers use remarkably consistent shorthand, and the same comment appearing in two unrelated subjects is the clearest possible signal that the problem is a convention rather than a content gap.

The shared comments to look for are these. A description offered where the question said explain. A method that assumes the reader was present at the experiment. Variables mentioned but not classified as independent, dependent or controlled. A graph without labelled axes or units. A conclusion the data does not support. An evaluation consisting of generic remarks about human error. Any of those appearing in two sciences means one tutor and one block fixes three subjects.

If instead the comments are unrelated, such as stoichiometric ratios in chemistry and ray diagrams in physics, the deficit is specific and you need a short block with a specialist in whichever science shows the clearest recoverable loss. Either answer is cheaper than booking three weekly sessions, and both are reachable before anyone quotes you.

sections.heading: Separate sciences, Coordinated and Combined compared
paragraphs: This comparison is absent from every competitor page researched for this market, which is remarkable, because it is the decision that most shapes a Dubai student's science outcome. The three routes differ in how many qualifications are awarded, how deep the content goes, how many papers are sat and what remains available at 16.

Read the post-16 column first, because families usually read it last. A Combined Science award does not position a student for A Level Biology, Chemistry or Physics, or for the equivalent IB Higher Level courses, regardless of the grade. Coordinated Sciences sits in between and should be discussed explicitly with the school rather than assumed either way. Separate sciences keep everything open at the cost of the heaviest examination load.

The load question is real and should not be dismissed, particularly here. Three sciences in a timetable that also carries mathematics, English, the UAE mandatory subjects of Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and two or three options, is a great deal of examined content for a fifteen-year-old, and in this corridor several hours a week are already going to the school run. A student doing three sciences badly has worse options at 16 than one doing Coordinated Sciences well.

So the first question to put to a tutor is not about their experience; it is about which paper is on their screen. The most common avoidable error in science tutoring in Dubai is a mismatched practice set - separate-science papers worked with a Coordinated candidate, or Extended papers worked with a Core entry. Either produces a term of practice calibrated to an examination the student is not sitting, and a family here has usually spent a fortnight of hard-won weekday evenings on it before anybody notices. Confirm the award, the board and the tier before the first session, and ask the tutor to state out loud which of the three they are working from.
