sections.heading: The practical paper, which is a writing paper
paragraphs: Families arriving from systems with laboratory examinations are regularly surprised by this, and the surprise costs marks. In these qualifications practical skills are assessed in writing. The student describes a method, classifies variables, reads apparatus from a diagram, processes data and evaluates a procedure, all on paper and with no equipment in front of them.

That makes it a writing skill with a finite set of conventions, which is good news, because finite skills can be taught to completion. The method must be reproducible: a stranger reading it should be able to repeat the experiment without asking a question. Variables must be named as independent, dependent and controlled rather than merely mentioned. Readings must be given to the precision the apparatus supports. Evaluation must identify a specific weakness in this procedure rather than a generic limitation that would apply to any experiment.

It is reliably the weakest paper in the set, for a structural reason rather than anyone's fault: practising it properly means marking extended written answers rather than ticking right answers, which is slow for a department covering three sciences. Students therefore meet it in a mock, score poorly, and conclude they are weak at science when they are weak at one kind of writing.

Four sessions usually changes it substantially, and because the conventions are shared the gain applies across all three sciences at once. That makes it, along with command terms, the highest-return science work available to a DIP family, and it requires no new content at all, which also means it fits a short weekday slot after a long school run.

sections.heading: Coverage for three sciences, stated honestly
paragraphs: No competitor page in the research behind these pages discloses a coverage limit, which is implausible, since every service has one. For a three-science household the question is sharper than usual, because three simultaneous matches at compatible times is a bigger ask than one.

Here is the position. A single tutor for a shared-skills block is reliably available, usually within a few days, because the work is convention rather than deep subject specialism and any competent science teacher can deliver it. A single specialist for one science and one board is also generally available within a few days. Three specialists across three sciences at three compatible times in the same week is a materially harder ask, and in the weeks before a series it is sometimes not possible at all.

When it is not, you will be told, and the alternative offered will be a sequenced start rather than a simultaneous one: the shared block first, then one science at a time. That is usually the better plan anyway in a corridor household, because parallel plans in a shortened week produce three shallow efforts and no completed fix. But it should be your choice, made with the information, rather than something arranged quietly.

One further disclosure. Where no UAE-based specialist is available for a particular science and board, the match may be a teacher working from outside the UAE on Gulf Standard Time. That is stated rather than hidden behind a non-UAE contact number. The test stays the same for every match: has this person taught this board and code, and can they name the failure from a marked script?

sections.heading: Sequencing three sciences when the week is short
paragraphs: Three sciences cannot be revised simultaneously in eight weeks, and in this corridor the week is shorter than the calendar suggests because several hours have already gone to the school run. A rotation fixes it, and the rotation has to be written down rather than intended.

The principle is straightforward. The shared-skills block comes first if the script comparison pointed that way, because it improves all three subjects at once and makes everything afterwards more efficient. Then the weakest science takes the first and last slots of the rotation, each science gets a timed paper at planned intervals, and nothing goes more than two weeks without contact.

Writing it down matters because an unwritten plan quietly becomes a plan to revise whichever subject feels most frightening this week, which is always the same subject. The predictable result is thorough coverage of one science, adequate coverage of a second, and a visible gap in the third, usually whichever was taught first and revised last.

One rule students resist: the timed paper comes before the revision of that topic, not after. A paper taken cold tells you what to revise; a paper taken after revision tells you that you revised. The first is information and the second is reassurance, and only one of them changes a grade. In a short week, spending a slot on reassurance is an expensive choice.

Adapt the rotation to your own school's mock window, which the exams officer holds and which differs across this corridor by several weeks. A rotation copied from a neighbour at a different school is likely to be aimed at the wrong fortnight, and in an eight-week plan the wrong fortnight is a quarter of the work.

sections.heading: What it costs for three sciences, and where it goes wrong
paragraphs: A three-science household can turn a reasonable hourly rate into an unreasonable monthly total very quickly, simply by booking one weekly session per subject without first asking whether that is what the problem needs.

The market, attributed and dated October 2026. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 per hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Budget online provision starts at Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel per Bestimate's 2026 Dubai cost table, and in this corridor that travel component is doing more work than it would centrally. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support. None of these is an IB Gram price list; ours is set after the free trial.

The comparison that matters is between a shared block and three weekly sessions. A single shared-skills block of four to six sessions improves all three sciences and costs roughly a third of three parallel weekly plans. Where one science genuinely needs content work on top, a targeted single-science block is added rather than substituted. The waste is in buying three plans because three subjects looked weak, when the scripts showed one convention.

Worth setting against the rest of the household budget. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. School fees are therefore fixed for the year while tutoring is the main variable line in most education budgets - and in a three-science household the variable line is the one that quietly triples if nobody reads the scripts first. A frozen fee is not a reason to book three weekly sessions; it is a reason to find out whether one shared block would have done it.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects, and the timetable arithmetic
paragraphs: Now the subjects nobody counts when they are counting a Year 11 week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, so a Dubai Investments Park pupil sitting Cambridge or Pearson science carries them as well. KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or by April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. There is a section on this here because no competitor page in any cluster researched for this market has one, which is strange given that it applies to every Dubai private school pupil and to every hour of homework a three-science timetable has to fit around it.

The grouping rules are precise, and they are why these subjects take more of the week than their headline count suggests. KHDA requires separate classes by group for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for Arabs and non-Arabs are strictly prohibited, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between them. Standard Arabic is the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. For Social Studies, Arabic is the primary language for Arab students, while non-Arabs are taught in the language of the school's licensed curriculum. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval - which is also the answer to a question DIP parents ask us: no, a science tutor is not a back route into these subjects.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with schools able to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met and a recommendation that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. Content is tightly controlled: KHDA states that using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited, so support in these subjects works inside the school's own material.

For a three-science household in this corridor the consequence is arithmetic rather than academic. These subjects sit on top of three sciences, mathematics, English and options, and several hours a week are already going to the journey. A Year 11 student underperforming across several subjects at once is quite often out of hours rather than out of ability, and the correct first response is an audit of the week rather than the purchase of three tutors.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Investments Park
paragraphs: Send six things: the award, the board and tier for each science, the school, marked scripts from two different sciences, the next deadline the school has set, and the time your child actually gets home on a normal weekday. The two scripts are the critical item, because comparing them is what establishes whether you need one tutor or three.

The free trial lesson comes before any payment and confirms or corrects the comparison you made yourself, then estimates the block. If the honest answer is one shared block of four sessions rather than three weekly plans, that is what you will be told, and it costs us the larger booking.

And four things that will not appear in the written estimate that comes back. No grade promise, because no honest provider can make one, and a promise across three sciences would be three times as dishonest. No suggestion that tutoring is required for Ministry of Education equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, each of which would be a false claim about a regulatory process your family may genuinely have to navigate. No regulator or board approval, stated plainly: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office, centre or branch, in Dubai Investments Park or anywhere else. And no satisfaction statistics, because a figure given without its sample, its date and its method is decoration rather than evidence.

Two notes on what happens to the six things we have just asked you to send. Those marked scripts carry information about a child, so the enquiry form asks only for what the plan needs, states why it is asking, and keeps a privacy link on every page; we do not ask for a photograph, and you can ask for the record to be deleted. The second note concerns what travels the other way: we do not publish or supply Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes or syllabus documents as downloads, because that material is the boards' copyright. We cite it, we link to it, and we work from what your child's school has legitimately provided - which is one more reason the scripts matter so much.

process.title: Compare scripts from two different sciences
process.description: This is the step that decides whether you buy one tutor or three, and it is free. Read the annotations rather than the ticks and look for repetition across subjects: the same comment in biology and physics means a shared convention and one block.

process.title: Confirm the award before anything else
process.description: Separate sciences, Coordinated 0654 and Combined 0653 are three different qualifications with different papers and depths. Practising the wrong one wastes the block and dents confidence at once, and the school's assessment paperwork states which applies.

process.title: Confirm the board per science
process.description: Departments choose independently, so a student can sit Cambridge chemistry alongside Edexcel physics. Check each science separately, then tell the tutor in writing which codes they are working from and ask which series the practice papers come from.

process.title: Write the rotation down
process.description: Three sciences need a written rotation with timed papers at planned intervals, because an unwritten plan becomes a plan to revise whichever subject feels most alarming this week. Shared block first, weakest science first and last, nothing untouched for two weeks.

process.title: Verify with a timed paper, then stop
process.description: Each block ends with a paper under examination conditions in the subject worked on. If the logged error has gone, stopping is the right recommendation. A three-science household is where open-ended arrangements become expensive fastest.

whyPoints.title: A free test for one tutor or three
whyPoints.description: Comparing annotations across scripts from two different sciences settles the question before anyone quotes you, and it costs twenty minutes. If the same comment appears in both, one block of four to six sessions improves all three subjects.

whyPoints.title: The award established first
whyPoints.description: Separate, Coordinated 0654 and Combined 0653 differ in depth, papers and post-16 position. No competitor page researched for this market compares them, and practising the wrong route's papers is the most common avoidable error in Dubai science tutoring.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Practical skills are examined in writing with a finite set of conventions: reproducible method, classified variables, justified precision, specific evaluation. Reliably the weakest paper in the set and among the most improvable, and it fits a short weekday slot.

whyPoints.title: Coverage for three sciences stated plainly
whyPoints.description: One tutor for a shared block is reliably available; three specialists at three compatible times in the same week is a materially harder ask and sometimes not possible near a series. You are told, and offered a sequenced start.

whyPoints.title: Costs compared monthly, with sources
whyPoints.description: Indicative monthly AED figures from Bestimate's 2026 estimates and providers' published rates, dated October 2026, set against what each approach actually achieves rather than against an unnamed competitor.

whyPoints.title: The timetable counted honestly
whyPoints.description: Three sciences plus mathematics, English, options and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, in a week already shortened by the school run. Sometimes the right advice is to audit the week rather than buy a tutor.

faqs.question: Do we need one science tutor or three?
faqs.answer: Compare marked scripts from two different sciences and read the annotations rather than the ticks. If the same comment appears in both, such as a description offered where the question said explain or a method that assumes the reader was present, the deficit is a shared convention and one tutor fixes all three subjects in a block of four to six sessions. If the comments are unrelated, you have a specific topic gap in one science, which is a three to five session block with a specialist.

faqs.question: Can a tutor come to our DIP home for science lessons?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We teach IGCSE science one-to-one into DIP homes over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams and working annotated on a shared screen, and we send no tutors to UAE addresses; in-person home visits are an India-only service for us. For a three-science household this helps concretely: three specialists can take three evenings without three cars crossing two motorways at the same hour.

faqs.question: Our school entered our child for Coordinated Sciences. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: It is one of three quite different qualifications. Separate sciences give three full IGCSEs with three paper sets and the deepest content. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 gives two awards covering all three sciences at intermediate depth. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 gives one award at the shallowest depth. The post-16 consequence matters most: a Combined award does not position a student for A Level or IB Higher Level sciences regardless of grade, and Coordinated should be discussed explicitly with the school.

faqs.question: Our child has never sat a laboratory exam. What does the practical paper test?
faqs.answer: Writing, not laboratory work. The paper asks the student to describe a method reproducibly, classify variables as independent, dependent and controlled, read apparatus to the correct precision, process data and identify a specific weakness in the procedure. The conventions are finite, which means they can be taught to completion in about four sessions, and because they are shared across biology, chemistry and physics the gain applies to all three subjects at once.

faqs.question: How should three sciences be revised in a short week?
faqs.answer: On a written rotation, never in parallel. Put the shared conventions block first if the script comparison pointed that way, because it makes everything afterwards more efficient. Then give the weakest science the first and last slots, put a timed paper in each science at planned intervals, and let nothing go more than two weeks without contact. Write it down, because an unwritten plan becomes a plan to revise whichever subject feels most alarming this week.

faqs.question: Why does the timed paper come before the revision?
faqs.answer: Because a paper taken cold is information and a paper taken after revision is reassurance, and only one of them changes a grade. A cold paper tells you which topics and which conventions are actually costing marks, so the following sessions can be aimed. A paper sat after a week of revising the same topic confirms that the week happened. In a short week, spending a slot on reassurance is an expensive choice.

faqs.question: Can you cover all three sciences at the same time?
faqs.answer: A single tutor for a shared-skills block is reliably available, usually within a few days. One specialist for one science and board is also generally available quickly. Three specialists across three sciences at three compatible times in the same week is a materially harder ask, and in the weeks before a series it is sometimes not possible. If so you will be told and offered a sequenced start, which in a corridor household is usually the better plan anyway.

faqs.question: Which science topic gives DIP students the most trouble?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits in physics, consistently. The difficulty is reasoning rather than recall: saying what happens to current and potential difference when one component changes means holding the whole circuit in mind, and a student who has memorised every relationship can still fail the question. Chemistry's equivalent is moles and stoichiometry, where the error is usually an inverted ratio or an ignored limiting reagent. Biology's is explanation that describes a structure without linking it to function.

faqs.question: Is Combined Science a problem if our child might want medicine?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the conversation belongs before the entry is confirmed rather than in Year 12. A Combined Science award does not position a student for A Level Biology or Chemistry, or for the equivalent IB Higher Level courses, and medical and related applications commonly expect chemistry at that depth alongside biology. In this corridor, where families move schools as the area fills, that constraint can bind at a school you have not yet joined.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for three sciences?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the deficit is shared, which is why the free script comparison comes first. A shared-skills block of four to six sessions over six weeks runs roughly AED 600 to 1,200 monthly at mid-market rates and improves all three subjects. A targeted single-science block is similar. Both together in an examination year runs AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more per Bestimate's 2026 estimates. Three parallel weekly sessions is the most expensive option and frequently not the most effective.

faqs.question: Does the exam board matter for the sciences?
faqs.answer: In Year 11, considerably. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel set different papers, weight topics differently, use different tier vocabulary and frame practical skills assessment differently, even where the content overlaps heavily. Departments choose independently, so a student can sit Cambridge chemistry alongside Edexcel physics. Check the code per science on the school's assessment paperwork, and ask any prospective tutor which codes they are building practice from and from which series.

faqs.question: Our child seems weak in everything at once. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Often that they are out of hours rather than out of ability, particularly in this corridor. Three sciences sit alongside mathematics, English, options and the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and several hours a week are already going to the school run. When several subjects slip simultaneously the correct first response is an audit of the week rather than the purchase of three tutors, and we would rather say so than take three bookings.

faqs.question: Do you supply science past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider advertising them as a feature is distributing someone else's property. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes, grade boundary tables and syllabus documents are the boards' copyright. We reference them, cite the official source, link to it, and work from what your child's school legitimately provides. The subject teacher also remains the authority on exactly what this cohort sits and which tier each science is entered at.

faqs.question: If one science goes badly in June, can it be retaken alone?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel run a November series, and for a candidate sitting in Dubai that is the resit route; the February and March series is offered to India only. A November attempt is easier to plan than a first attempt because you hold the real script and the real grade, so the two or three topics that cost it can be identified precisely rather than guessed. Entry is arranged by the school's exams officer and is worth discussing as soon as results arrive.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-inves.closingHeading: Compare two scripts before you book three tutors
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-inves.closingBody: The question most science enquiries from Dubai Investments Park really contain is whether one tutor can cover three subjects, and it has a free answer. Put the last marked script from two different sciences side by side and read the annotations. The same comment in both means a shared convention and one block of four to six sessions that improves all three. Unrelated comments mean one specialist for a short block. Either way you will spend less than three parallel weekly plans. Send those scripts with the award, the boards and the real arrival time. Lessons run live online into your DIP home on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-marin.tutorsIntro: Science tutors here are matched subject by subject, not as general scientists. Biology, chemistry and physics reward different things at IGCSE, and a tutor who is excellent at one is usually only adequate at the others, so we would rather match two people than stretch one across three papers.

intro.heading: Science is three subjects, and the week only has so many evenings
paragraphs: Parents in the Marina towers and the communities around them tend to search for a science tutor rather than a chemistry tutor, and the reason is practical: the report card arrived with three science grades on it and one of them is a problem. But science at IGCSE is not one subject with three parts. Depending on the entry, a Year 11 student is sitting one, two or three separate qualifications, on different papers, with different practical arrangements, and the support for each looks different.

That is the first thing worth establishing, and it is often the thing nobody has explained. A student on three separate sciences is taking three IGCSEs: biology, chemistry and physics, each with its own papers. A student on Cambridge Coordinated Sciences is taking a double award, which counts as two IGCSEs and covers all three disciplines in less depth than the separate route. A student on Combined Science is taking a single award, which is one IGCSE. Each route leaves a different set of doors open at 16, which is why the choice made in Year 9 has consequences that surface in Year 12.

The second thing is the week. A Marina or JLT Year 11 student on three sciences has three science teachers setting homework, three sets of past papers to work through, and a bus that gets them home somewhere between 3:30pm and 4:30pm, later from the Al Barsha South schools. Adding three tutoring sessions to that week is not a plan, it is a way of making sure none of them is prepared for. The useful question is which single science is costing the most marks, and whether a sequence across the year beats three simultaneous commitments. Almost always it does.

The third is the practical component, which is the part families find hardest to picture when a lesson happens over video. Most Cambridge science syllabuses examine either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and in Dubai the alternative is common. That paper is not a test of laboratory dexterity. It tests whether a student can read an unfamiliar method, identify variables, spot a flaw, tabulate results correctly, plot a graph and evaluate a procedure. Every one of those is better taught at a shared whiteboard than at a bench, which is one of the few places where online delivery is not a compromise at all.

On that point, directly: IB Gram does not send a science tutor to a Marina address, and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India. Lessons here are one to one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, placed after the bus returns and away from the days the school already owns.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-marin.programmesIntro: Science at 14 to 16 in the schools serving this part of Dubai comes in three shapes plus the IB alternative. The shape determines how many qualifications your child ends up with and what Year 12 will let them take.

programmes.name: Three separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology, chemistry and physics taken as three independent IGCSEs, typically Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Each is tiered Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher, and each carries its own papers including a practical or alternative-to-practical component. This is the deepest route and the one that keeps every science A Level and Diploma Higher Level option open.
programmes.countryNote: The usual pattern around the Marina is that a school offers separate sciences to its upper sets and Coordinated Sciences to the rest, with the decision taken late in Year 9. Families who want the separate route for a borderline student should have that conversation before the option forms go out, because moving onto it later in the course is difficult.

programmes.name: Cambridge Coordinated Sciences, double award
programmes.description: All three disciplines examined together and awarded as two IGCSEs. Content is narrower than the separate route in each discipline but genuinely covers all three. It is tiered Core and Extended, with papers covering all three sciences in each sitting plus the practical or alternative-to-practical component.
programmes.countryNote: This is the most common science entry in British-curriculum schools near the Marina for students who are not in a top science set, and it is a sensible choice rather than a consolation. The thing to check is whether a target sixth form accepts it as the entry route into the science A Level or Diploma Higher Level your child has in mind, because policies differ between the schools in this cluster.

programmes.name: Combined Science, single award
programmes.description: All three disciplines examined together and awarded as one IGCSE. The narrowest of the three routes and generally offered to students for whom three science grades would be unachievable. It covers the foundations of each discipline and is examined on fewer papers.
programmes.countryNote: A student on a single award who later decides they want a science at Higher Level or A Level has a real gap to close, and it should be identified as early as possible rather than in the summer before Year 12. A short bridging block is usually the right answer and it is far cheaper than discovering the problem in a first-term test.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The parallel route in the continuum schools in and near this cluster. Sciences are assessed against four criteria rather than by paper, there is no tiering, and no separate practical examination exists in the IGCSE sense. Students are assessed on investigations they design and write themselves.
programmes.countryNote: Households in the Meadows and Emirates Hills frequently have one child on MYP sciences and one on IGCSE sciences at the same time, and the two need different help. An MYP student is working towards a criterion descriptor; an IGCSE student is working towards a markscheme. A tutor who conflates the two will aim at the wrong target for one of your children.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-marin.subjectsIntro: Across the three disciplines the marks go in identifiable places, and they are different places in each. Below is what each area assesses and the specific loss that recurs in marked IGCSE science papers from this cluster.

subjects.name: Biology: cells, transport and enzymes
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, active transport and enzyme-rate work. Osmosis questions are lost on imprecise language about water potential and concentration, and enzyme graphs are lost by describing the shape rather than explaining denaturation in terms of the active site.

subjects.name: Biology: human physiology
subjects.description: Circulation, gas exchange, digestion, excretion and coordination. These questions reward exact terminology, and partial marks are the norm where a student writes a near-synonym. Extended tier adds detail on hormonal control that is examined directly rather than in passing.

subjects.name: Biology: inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Genetic crosses, Punnett squares, variation and selection. The crosses are mechanical and winnable; the explanation marks sit in the account of selection, which students often write as a story about intention rather than as a process acting on existing variation.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Moles from mass and concentration, reacting masses, percentage yield and limiting reagents. This is the largest single source of chemistry marks lost at Extended tier, and the cause is almost always starting the arithmetic before working out which reagent limits the reaction.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and redox
subjects.description: Products at each electrode, half-equations and oxidation states. Predicting the product at the anode in aqueous solution is the question that separates grades, and it is a rules-based skill that improves quickly under supervised practice rather than by reading.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and the reactivity series
subjects.description: Homologous series, naming, simple reactions and the displacement patterns of the reactivity series. Marks are lost on naming conventions and on writing equations that are not balanced, both of which are mechanical and both of which are quickly fixed.

subjects.name: Physics: forces and motion
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, graphs of motion, moments and momentum. Gradient and area interpretation of motion graphs is examined constantly, and the reliable loss is reading a distance-time graph as though it were a velocity-time graph.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits and power. Circuit questions reward practice above all else, and the parallel circuit is the single most misread diagram in the IGCSE physics paper.

subjects.name: Physics: thermal physics and waves
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, changes of state, reflection, refraction and the electromagnetic spectrum. Calculation losses come from kelvin and Celsius mismatches; wave losses come from imprecise ray diagrams drawn without a normal.

subjects.name: Practical and investigative skills
subjects.description: Identifying variables, tabulating results with correct units in the headings, plotting and reading graphs, spotting anomalies and evaluating a method. This is examined as its own paper and it is the most transferable thing a science tutor can teach, because the skill is shared across all three subjects.

subjects.name: Mathematical skills for science
subjects.description: Rearrangement, standard form, significant figures, percentage change and unit conversion. A large share of science marks lost by able students is lost here rather than in the science, which is why a diagnostic should look at working rather than at recall.

sections.heading: Separate, Coordinated or Combined: what your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Before buying any science tutoring, establish which of the three routes your child is on, because it changes everything downstream: how many qualifications they leave with, how many papers they sit, how deep the content goes in each discipline and which sixth-form options stay open. The school's examinations officer will tell you the board, the syllabus code and the tier on request, and that single email is worth more than any amount of browsing.

The three routes are genuinely different products. Separate sciences means three IGCSEs and the deepest content in each discipline. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences is a double award counting as two IGCSEs, covering all three disciplines in less depth. Combined Science is a single award counting as one. There is nothing wrong with the narrower routes; they are the right choice for a great many students and a school recommending one is usually reading the evidence correctly. What is wrong is finding out in Year 12 that the route taken does not support the subject your child now wants.

That is the conversation to have, and to have early. Ask the school two things: which route is my child being entered for, and which sixth-form science options does that route support at this school and at the schools we might move to. The second half of that question matters in this cluster particularly, because families here do move between British and IB sixth forms at 16, and the entry policies for a science Higher Level or A Level differ between them. The table below sets out the comparison.

sections.heading: How the practical component is actually examined
paragraphs: The part of IGCSE science that parents find hardest to picture is the practical component, and it is also the part most often left to look after itself. Most Cambridge science syllabuses examine practical skills through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and in Dubai the alternative is widely used. Confirm which one your child's school enters, because the preparation differs and the difference is worth marks.

What matters is that the alternative-to-practical paper is not a watered-down version of a laboratory session. It tests a defined set of skills on paper: reading an unfamiliar method and working out what it is measuring, classifying independent, dependent and control variables, identifying a flaw in a procedure, completing a results table with units in the column headings, plotting a graph with a sensible scale, reading values off it, spotting an anomalous result and saying what to do about it, and writing an evaluation that identifies which source of error dominates rather than listing all of them.

Every one of those is a paper skill, which means it can be taught at a shared whiteboard as effectively as at a bench, and arguably more effectively, because the tutor sees the table being drawn and the graph being plotted and can correct the habit at the moment it forms. It is also the highest-yield block in IGCSE science, because the same skills are examined in biology, chemistry and physics. Four to six sessions aimed at this alone will frequently do more for three grades than a term of content revision in one subject.

For a student entered for the practical test rather than the alternative, the laboratory work itself remains the school's job and nothing a tutor does replaces it. What a tutor can still do is the recording, processing, graphing and evaluation that surround the measurements, which is where most of the marks on that paper sit anyway.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one timetable: when a session actually fits
paragraphs: Here is the practical arithmetic a Marina family is doing without quite articulating it. Three sciences generate three sets of homework. The bus gets home between about 3:30pm and 4:30pm from the Al Sufouh schools and later from Al Barsha South. Two evenings a week are already committed to fixtures, squads or clubs. Dinner is somewhere in there. That leaves perhaps two evenings with genuine capacity, and into those two evenings a family is contemplating putting three tutoring sessions.

It does not work, and the reason is not stamina. It is homework. A tutoring session earns its value from the work the student does between sessions. Three sessions a week generate three sets of consolidation work on top of three sets of school homework, and the consolidation is what gets dropped. At that point the tutoring has become a substitute for independent practice rather than a prompt for it, which is the precise mechanism by which families spend a lot of money and see a grade move very little.

The alternative is sequencing. Take the weakest science, judged from marked papers rather than from the report-card grades, and work on it until the error log stops changing. Then move to the next. One evening stays committed instead of three, one set of consolidation work actually gets done, and the subject that was failing gets genuine attention rather than a third of it. Across a year this covers two or sometimes all three sciences, in sequence, at a third of the weekly load.

The exception is the practical-skills block, which can run alongside a content subject because the skills are shared. A student doing weekly chemistry content work and a short parallel block on variables, tables and graphs is being supported in all three sciences at once without a third commitment. The table below sets out how a sequence typically looks against a Marina week.

sections.heading: The six-mark question, and the command words that decide it
paragraphs: A substantial share of IGCSE science marks sits in the longer extended-response questions, and this is where able students most often underperform. The pattern is consistent: the student knows the material, writes a fluent paragraph that lists correct facts, and scores perhaps half. The reason is that the markscheme is looking for a chain of reasoning with specific linking steps, not for a collection of true statements.

The command words drive this and they are defined. Describe asks what happens. Explain asks why, and a credited explanation names a mechanism rather than restating the observation. Suggest invites a plausible answer where more than one is possible, and is marked generously if the reasoning holds. Compare requires both things to be mentioned in the same sentence rather than described in turn. Calculate requires working. State requires none, so working on a state question is time spent for no return.

This is coachable and it is rarely coached, because marking forty short answers per student against published wording is beyond what a full class allows. One to one is the format where it can be done. The method is to have the student write the answer, mark it against the markscheme language, and have them rewrite it. After thirty of those the structure becomes automatic, and because the command words are shared across biology, chemistry and physics, the gain shows up in all three papers rather than one.

One practical note for this cluster. Students who have come through a continuum school or from an American curriculum are the most likely to have strong scientific knowledge and weak command-word discipline, because those systems assess differently. It is not a knowledge gap and should not be treated as one; a student in that position can lose a term to content revision they did not need.
bullets: Explain requires a mechanism; a list of correct facts is not an explanation

sections.heading: How science teaching works when the lesson is over video
paragraphs: This is the question every science-specific enquiry eventually reaches, and it deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. A video lesson cannot run a titration or set up a ripple tank. What it can do is everything the papers actually examine, which is a different list from what a laboratory does.

Take a specific example. A chemistry question gives a method for determining the concentration of an acid by titration and asks for the apparatus, the independent variable, the readings to be recorded and the improvement to the procedure. None of that requires a burette in the room. It requires the student to read the method precisely, to know what a burette reading looks like and to how many decimal places it is recorded, and to spot that the method as written has no repeat readings. A tutor with a shared whiteboard can work through that in detail and watch the student's table being built, which is more than a parent standing beside a bench could do.

Physics is similar. Circuit questions, ray diagrams and motion graphs are drawing and reasoning tasks, and drawing tasks are exactly what a shared whiteboard handles best, because the tutor sees the diagram forming and corrects the habit rather than the finished product. Biology is the most paper-based of the three to begin with: microscope drawings aside, almost the entire assessment is terminology, explanation and data interpretation.

What a video lesson cannot replace is the school laboratory, and we do not suggest otherwise. The practical work your child does in school is where measurement technique and safety habits are formed, and nothing bought from a tutoring provider substitutes for it. What a tutor adds is the surrounding skill set the paper actually marks. To be explicit about the delivery model, since the search phrase points elsewhere: IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE and no tutor will be sent to a Marina address. Home visiting is a service we run only in India.

sections.heading: The Year 10 trap: taught early, examined eighteen months later
paragraphs: A pattern repeats in this cluster often enough to be worth naming. A student does well in Year 10 science, the family relaxes, and then the autumn mock in Year 11 produces a result that makes no sense against the Year 10 reports. Nothing has gone wrong. What has happened is that Year 10 content was assessed in Year 10, shortly after being taught, and the final paper assesses it eighteen months later with no prompting about which topic a question belongs to.

That is a retention problem rather than a comprehension problem and it needs a different response. Re-teaching the content is the instinctive reaction and it is largely wasted, because the student understood it the first time. What works is retrieval: short, spaced, low-stakes recall across topics taught long ago, mixed up so the student has to identify what kind of question it is before answering. That identification step is the thing the final paper tests and the thing a topic-by-topic revision guide never practises.

For science specifically this matters more than in most subjects, because the content volume is large and split across three disciplines. A Year 11 student revising biology by rereading the biology chapters in order is practising recognition, not recall, and will feel confident while remaining unable to answer a mixed paper. The fix is unglamorous and cheap: mixed short-answer sets across all topics, weekly, with the misses logged and revisited.

The practical consequence for a Marina family is about timing. The best moment to start science tutoring is not the spring of Year 11, when most families start, but the spring of Year 10 or the summer that follows, when there is room to build retention habits rather than to fight a mock result. Support bought at that point is cheaper, calmer and does more.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs when you multiply it by three
paragraphs: The published rate figures in this market are quoted per hour per subject, and that is the arithmetic families forget. A rate that looks reasonable for one science is three times that for three, which is why the sequencing argument earlier in this page is a financial argument as well as an educational one. Supporting one science properly at a mid-market rate costs less over a year than supporting three badly.

The published figures, each attributed and recorded in October 2026, are these. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, which is the group and university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table places IB, IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350, with home tutors reaching AED 500. BartyED quotes AED 650 at the named end. Monthly estimates from the same table run AED 240 to 600 for a weekly budget session, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, and packaged offers of AED 799 a month for eight online sessions appear in the market.

Now do the multiplication. At the mid-market hourly band, one science weekly for a school year is one monthly figure; three sciences weekly is three times it, and that is before the in-home premium, which published rates put at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour against roughly AED 150 to 300 online for comparable qualifications. For a family in Al Furjan or on Bluewaters, where the journey is longest, the in-home option is both the most expensive and the least likely to survive a term of Dubai traffic.

None of the figures above is an IB Gram price and we publish no rate card on these pages. What we would say about value is narrower than price: the practical-skills block is the cheapest thing in IGCSE science that affects three grades at once, and the sequence approach costs a third of the simultaneous one. Ask whoever you speak to whether their quote includes VAT, since the published market figures are inconsistent on it, and ask what is included beyond the hour.

sections.heading: Which science route opens which sixth-form door
paragraphs: The decision made at 14 about science routes shows up again at 16, and in this cluster it shows up in an unusually complicated way, because families move between British and IB sixth forms within a few kilometres. A student who sat three separate sciences has the widest set of options in both systems. A student who sat a double award usually has most options, subject to the receiving school's own policy. A student who sat a single award has the narrowest set and should know that before Year 11 ends rather than during the Year 12 application.

The questions to put to a target sixth form are specific. What is the minimum science entry requirement for the A Level or Diploma Higher Level in question, and is a double award accepted for it? Is a grade from Core or Foundation tier accepted at all, and if so at what level? And is there a bridging arrangement for a student arriving from a different route? Schools answer these directly if asked directly, and the answers differ enough between the schools in this cluster that assuming is a bad idea.

Where a gap exists it is usually closeable, and the summer before Year 12 is the window. A student moving from a double award into a science Higher Level needs the depth the double award did not cover in that one discipline, which is a defined content list rather than a vague deficit. A short block over July and August handles it, and it is far cheaper than discovering the problem in a first-term test while new content arrives weekly.

A final note on recognition, because it is adjacent and often confused. UAE Ministry of Education equivalency for the British track is expressed as five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count of five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which is incorrect. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring provider, tutoring is not required for it, and you should verify the current requirement through the Ministry's own channel before relying on it for an application.

process.title: Find out which science route your child is on
process.description: Ask the school's examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for science. Separate, Coordinated and Combined are different products with different consequences at 16, and the answer determines what any tutoring should be aimed at. One email settles it.

process.title: Send a marked paper from the weakest science
process.description: Not the report card, the script. A marked paper shows whether the losses are content, command words, calculation or practical skills, and those four need different responses. A photograph is enough. It is the single most useful thing you can send before a first session.

process.title: Pick the evening the school does not already own
process.description: Tell us the bus return time for your address and which days carry fixtures, squads or clubs. Al Barsha South and Sports City routes push a workable start to 5:30pm or later. A slot placed on a committed day is the slot that gets cancelled until it stops being booked.

process.title: Take the free trial in one subject
process.description: One session at no cost, in whichever science is costing the most marks, spent on questions your child already got wrong. You get a written note placing the losses into categories and naming what the first few sessions should target, which may be the practical-skills block rather than the subject you expected.

process.title: Work in sequence and review after each mock
process.description: One science until the error log stops changing, then the next, with the practical block running alongside if it is needed. The mock results decide what changes rather than impressions. Where a science has stabilised, the slot moves rather than continuing from habit.

whyPoints.title: One science at a time, on purpose
whyPoints.description: Three simultaneous science sessions generate three sets of consolidation work that a Year 11 student will not do, at which point the tutoring replaces independent practice instead of prompting it. Sequencing keeps one evening committed, keeps the homework doable, and costs a third as much across the year.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper treated as its own subject
whyPoints.description: Variables, results tables with units in the headings, graph scales, anomalies and evaluation are examined in all three sciences, and almost nobody teaches them deliberately. A short block on this alone affects three grades at once and is the best-value purchase in IGCSE science.

whyPoints.title: Command words marked, not mentioned
whyPoints.description: The method is writing an extended answer, having it marked against the published wording, and rewriting it. Because the command words are shared across biology, chemistry and physics, the gain appears in three papers rather than one. A full class rarely allows that volume of individual marking.

whyPoints.title: Retention taught as a skill
whyPoints.description: Most Year 11 science shocks are retention problems rather than comprehension ones, and re-teaching content the student already understood is largely wasted. Mixed, spaced recall across old topics is what the final paper actually tests, and it is cheap to build once somebody names it.

whyPoints.title: Matched by discipline, not by the word science
whyPoints.description: Biology, chemistry and physics reward different things at IGCSE and a tutor strong in one is usually adequate in the others. Where two sciences are genuinely weak we would rather propose two specialists in sequence than stretch one person across three papers.

For an Al Furjan or Bluewaters address the in-home option is both the dearest and the least likely to survive a full term.

faqs.question: Is my child taking one science qualification or three?
faqs.answer: It depends on the route the school entered them for, and the school's examinations officer will confirm it. Three separate sciences means three IGCSEs, one each in biology, chemistry and physics, with the fullest content in each. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences is a double award counting as two IGCSEs and covers all three disciplines in less depth. Combined Science is a single award counting as one. Pearson's double award works similarly to Coordinated Sciences. None of the narrower routes is wrong, but each leaves a different set of sixth-form science options open, so the answer matters well beyond the certificate.

faqs.question: Should we book three science tutors or one?
faqs.answer: One, in sequence, for almost every family. Three weekly sessions generate three sets of consolidation work on top of three sets of school homework, and the consolidation is what gets dropped, at which point the tutoring has replaced independent practice rather than prompted it. Start with the weakest science judged from a marked paper rather than from the report card, work on it until the error log stops changing, then move to the next. Across a year this covers two or often all three, at a third of the weekly cost and with the homework actually done.

faqs.question: How are science practicals handled if the lesson happens over video?
faqs.answer: The papers mostly examine paper skills rather than bench dexterity, and those are what a tutor can teach. Reading an unfamiliar method, classifying variables, completing a results table with units in the headings, choosing a graph scale, plotting and reading off with construction lines, spotting an anomaly and saying what to do about it, and writing an evaluation that ranks the sources of error. A shared whiteboard handles all of it, and the tutor sees the table and graph being built rather than the finished version. The school laboratory remains where measurement technique is learned and nothing replaces that.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper actually testing?
faqs.answer: A defined set of investigative skills, on paper, applied to a method the student has not seen. It asks which variable is independent and which are controlled, what readings should be recorded and to what precision, what is wrong with the procedure as written, how the results should be tabulated, how the graph should be scaled and read, which result is anomalous and what should be done about it, and which source of error matters most. It is not a watered-down laboratory session. It is the most teachable paper in IGCSE science and the one most often left to look after itself.

faqs.question: My son did well in Year 10 science and badly in the Year 11 mock. What happened?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly retention rather than understanding. Year 10 content was assessed shortly after it was taught; the final paper assesses it eighteen months later, mixed up, with no cue about which topic a question belongs to. Re-teaching is the instinctive response and it is largely wasted, because he understood it the first time. What works is retrieval: short, spaced, mixed recall across topics taught long ago, so he has to identify what kind of question it is before answering. That identification step is exactly what a topic-by-topic revision guide never practises.

faqs.question: Which science is usually the weakest for students at Marina-area schools?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, and specifically the quantitative half of it. Mole calculations with limiting reagents and electrolysis products at each electrode account for a disproportionate share of lost marks at Extended tier, and both are rules-based skills that improve quickly with supervised practice rather than by reading. Physics losses are usually graph interpretation and circuits. Biology losses are usually imprecise terminology and the longer explanation questions. Even so, the report-card grade is a poor guide; the marked paper is what tells you where the money should go.

faqs.question: What time can a science session start if the bus gets back at four?
faqs.answer: Allow an hour. For most Marina and JBR addresses on the Al Sufouh routes, 5pm is the first dependable start, with 4:30pm possible only on days with no fixtures. JLT, Al Furjan and Discovery Gardens households on the Al Barsha South and Sports City routes should plan for 5:30pm or later. The bigger variable is not the average finish time but the committed days: a child in a squad or a science club will be on site until about 5pm once or twice a week, and a session placed there will be cancelled until it stops being booked.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE science tutoring cost for three subjects?
faqs.answer: Rates in this market are quoted per hour per subject, so three sciences is three times the arithmetic. Published figures recorded in October 2026: EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 an hour, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, Unitors IGCSE tuition from AED 150, TutorChase AED 270, and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table placing IGCSE and A Level specialists at AED 200 to 450 and above. Monthly estimates in that table run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for exam-year specialist support, per subject. Those are other providers' figures; IB Gram publishes no rate card here.

faqs.question: Will a double award in science stop my daughter taking chemistry at A Level?
faqs.answer: Usually not, but it depends on the receiving school and you should ask rather than assume. The questions to put are specific: what is the minimum science entry requirement for that A Level or Diploma Higher Level, is a double award accepted for it, and is there a bridging arrangement for a student arriving from a different route. Schools in this cluster answer directly and their policies differ, which matters because families here move between British and IB sixth forms at 16. Where a gap exists it is a defined content list rather than a vague deficit, and a summer block usually closes it.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on the six-mark questions despite knowing the content?
faqs.answer: Because the markscheme wants a chain of reasoning with specific linking steps, and a fluent paragraph listing correct facts is not that. Explain requires a mechanism rather than a restatement of the observation. Compare requires both items in the same sentence rather than described in turn. State requires no working at all. Students who have never had the distinction made explicit write good descriptions where explanations were asked for and score about half. Thirty answers written, marked against the published wording and rewritten will fix it, and because the command words are shared the gain appears in all three sciences.

faqs.question: Is the summer break a good time to catch up on science?
faqs.answer: It is the best window in the year for content and foundational work, because nothing competes for attention and a fortnightly cadence is enough to hold progress. It suits the second-weakest science particularly well: a discipline that has been quietly neglected during term can be rebuilt across July and August without the student having to choose between it and homework. What the summer does not suit is paper technique and timing, which fade without the pressure of assessment and belong closer to the series. Because the lesson follows the laptop, travelling families keep the slot by agreeing a time that works in both zones.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take both chemistry and physics for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and this is the better of the possible pairings, because the mathematical skills overlap: rearrangement, standard form, unit conversion and graph work carry straight across. A ninety-minute combined session usually beats two separate hours since the handover disappears. Chemistry with biology works less well than parents expect, because the two reward different things, with biology depending heavily on precise terminology and chemistry on calculation discipline. Where both are genuinely weak, two tutors in sequence is the honest answer even though it is less convenient than one.

faqs.question: When is the right time to start science tutoring, Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: The spring of Year 10 or the summer that follows is better than the spring of Year 11, which is when most families start. Early on there is room to build retention habits and rebuild foundations, the entry tier is still open, and the work is calmer and cheaper. By the spring of Year 11 the entries have closed and the useful work narrows to timed papers and technique inside a fixed tier, which is worth doing but is a smaller lever. If you are already in the spring of Year 11, buy a short, specific block rather than a general weekly hour.

faqs.question: Do you cover both Cambridge and Pearson for IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we match on the code rather than the subject name, because the two boards differ in paper structure and in how practical skills are examined. Cambridge codes are four digits, such as 0610, 0620, 0625 for the separate sciences, 0654 for Coordinated Sciences and 0653 for Combined Science. Pearson codes begin with a digit and a subject prefix, such as 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SD0 for the double award. Schools around the Marina sometimes mix boards between departments, so ask the examinations officer for the code per subject rather than assuming one board covers them all.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor need to see my child's laboratory work?
faqs.answer: Not the practical work itself, but the records are useful. A tutor working on the practical component benefits from seeing how your child tabulates and graphs results in their own school practical write-ups, because that is where the habits show: units missing from headings, scales chosen badly, construction lines never drawn. Those are the exact habits the paper penalises. Bring a couple of recent write-ups to the trial lesson along with a marked paper, and the diagnostic gets considerably sharper. The practical lessons themselves stay with the school and nothing a tutor does substitutes for them.

intro.heading: Three sciences, several awards, and the code that settles it
paragraphs: IGCSE science is not one qualification. A student in Year 10 in Dubai may be taking three separate sciences, each with its own syllabus code and its own grade; or a double award covering all three sciences and producing two grades; or a single combined award producing one. Cambridge codes the separate sciences 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, with Co-ordinated Sciences at 0654 as a double award and Combined Science at 0653. Pearson Edexcel uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the separate sciences, with a Double Award science qualification alongside.

That matters because the awards are not scaled versions of each other. The content per mark differs, the number of papers differs, the depth expected in each discipline differs, and the way practical skill is assessed differs between boards. A tutor who has taught separate Cambridge Physics for years and is handed a Co-ordinated Sciences candidate will teach good physics and misjudge the depth required, which costs marks on a paper that is pitched differently.

Finding out takes a day. Email the school's examinations officer and ask which science award your child is entered for, on which board, with which syllabus codes. Or look at the front of any past paper they have been given: the code is printed there. Then ask a prospective tutor which award they teach and when they last taught it. A specialist answers with the number. A generalist says the science is the same, which is partly true and is not an answer.

The geography side of the question has no local answer. Dubai Media City is a free zone of offices and studios in Al Sufouh between Sheikh Zayed Road and the sea, with Dubai Internet City inland and Dubai Knowledge Park along the tram line. It has residential towers and no school. Children travel out to Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School next door, into the Al Barsha cluster, or to the villa belt schools, and the nearest tuition centres are inland.

The British curriculum is the largest in this city, with KHDA's 2024-25 figures putting 37 per cent of private school enrolment on it across 387,441 students in 227 schools, so there is no shortage of adults who can teach this material. The shortage is of a match to the specific award, held in a slot the household can keep, with marking against the right scheme. That is a sourcing problem rather than a supply problem.

On delivery: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, usually between 4.30pm and 9pm on school nights, which is what lets the match be made on the award rather than on who can cross Al Sufouh before six.

programmes.name: Separate sciences

The deepest route, the usual expectation for students heading to A Level or IB sciences, and the heaviest content load in a Year 11 timetable. Preparation is paper-shaped and discipline-specific.
programmes.countryNote: Most students in this corridor who intend to take sciences at 16 are on the separate route, and the schools around Media City generally offer it to students who can carry the load. The practical consequence for tutoring is that triage matters: a student on three sciences rarely needs help in all three, and spreading one hour across them helps none.

programmes.name: Double award science
programmes.description: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson's Double Award: all three disciplines, producing two grades. Students expect it to be easier than three separate sciences and find the content per mark denser, because the breadth is retained while the time is not. It is a sensible choice for a student who needs science but is not specialising in it.
programmes.countryNote: This is the award most often misidentified by families and by tutors in Dubai, because the subject name on a report card can look like separate sciences. If your child has two science grades rather than three or one, the double award is almost certainly what they are on, and that changes the depth a tutor should be teaching to.

programmes.description: Cambridge Combined Science 0653 or an equivalent single award: all three disciplines, one grade. The lightest science route, usually taken alongside more subjects elsewhere in the timetable. It does not normally support entry to A Level or IB sciences, which is the fact families most often discover late.
programmes.countryNote: If a student on combined science wants to take a science at 16, the gap has to be addressed deliberately rather than hoped away. A short bridging block after the papers, in the final term of Year 11, is the cheap version; discovering it in Year 12 is not. Confirm the sixth form's entry expectation before assuming it is possible.

programmes.name: MYP Sciences as the alternative
programmes.description: At IB continuum schools, science at this age is marked against four criteria out of eight, with criterion B wanting a repeatable method and criterion C the processing and evaluation of the student's own data. There is no public paper in most subjects, so the tutoring job is criterion literacy rather than past-paper technique.
programmes.countryNote: Some Dubai IB schools run the MYP for all five years and others enter students for IGCSE at 16 anyway, so children in the same tower can be on different systems. A tutor matched for criterion work is a poor fit for paper practice and vice versa, which makes the examinations officer's answer worth having before you buy.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-media.subjectsIntro: These are the science subjects and components families in this corridor ask about, with codes where relevant and the specific places marks disappear.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Heavy content tested through exact command terms. Writing everything known about a process scores below answering the question asked. Data interpretation and experiment-description questions are the cheapest marks available and the ones least often practised deliberately, which makes biology the quickest science to improve in a short block.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables. Students memorise reactions and stall on an unfamiliar substance. Multi-step mole problems where the limiting reagent is not signposted are a reliable loss, and so is the qualitative analysis section, which rewards rote learning that students assume is beneath them.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity and waves are the complaints; unit handling and equation rearrangement under time pressure are the actual problems. Graph questions want a gradient with the triangle shown and units stated, and students leave both implicit. Explanation questions reward reasoning written out rather than held in the head.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: All three disciplines in a compressed award. The content per mark is denser than students expect and the depth is pitched differently from the separate sciences, which is why award-matched tutoring matters. Triage across the three disciplines produces more than an even split of the hour.

subjects.name: Experimental skills and investigations
subjects.levels: All awards, in the written papers
subjects.description: Describing a method precisely enough to repeat, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, reading instruments correctly, tabulating, plotting and evaluating limitations. Every one of these is a paper skill, examined in writing, and improves fastest with live marking against the official scheme.

subjects.name: Graph and data work
subjects.description: Axes with units, sensible scales, lines of best fit, gradients calculated with the triangle shown, and conclusions that evaluate rather than restate. Mechanical losses here are among the most common in the whole science paper and among the easiest to stop permanently with a checklist.

subjects.name: Calculations across the three sciences
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, unit prefixes, standard form, percentage and ratio work. A student whose algebra is slow looks weak in science, because every numerical question becomes an arithmetic race. Diagnosing this correctly often saves a term of misdirected science teaching.

subjects.name: Command terms
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare, calculate and evaluate each ask for a different shape and quantity of answer. Students treat explain and describe as synonyms, which costs marks in every paper of every science. One session on command terms often recovers more than a month of content revision.

subjects.name: Qualitative analysis and practical recall
subjects.description: Flame colours, precipitate colours, gas tests and the reagents that produce them. It is pure recall, it is examined, and students resist learning it because it feels unsophisticated. A fortnight of five-minute daily drilling usually handles it, and it is worth insisting on.

subjects.name: Required practicals and alternative arrangements
subjects.description: Cambridge centres run either a practical arrangement or an alternative-to-practical arrangement depending on what the centre offers, while Pearson assesses practical skills through the written papers. Ask the school which applies, because it changes what a tutor should prepare and what remains the school's responsibility.

subjects.name: Sixth-form bridging
subjects.levels: After the papers, Year 11 summer term
subjects.description: The gap between an IGCSE science grade and the start of A Level or IB science, which both assume more quantitative fluency than the IGCSE examined. A short block after the papers, when nothing else is competing for the time, is the cheapest and least popular intervention available.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-media.regionsIntro: Science requests reach us from the communities around Media City. The variables that matter are the school mix, the journey home and whether one child is on three sciences or a combined award.

regions.name: Dubai Media City and Al Sufouh
regions.note: Residential towers in a working district, nearest gates at Dubai College and GEMS Wellington International School. Requests split between separate sciences and double award, and evening slots dominate because the afternoon journey takes the early hours out of play.

regions.name: Dubai Internet City
regions.note: Sharing the Red Line Metro station, limited residential stock, the same school destinations. The recurring question here is whether a student on a double award can still move onto a science at 16, which is a sixth-form entry question rather than a grade question.

regions.name: Dubai Knowledge Park
regions.note: University and training campuses along the tram line, with residential towers and an older student profile. Science requests from here are often resit or private-candidate cases, which need a shorter and more surgical block than a first attempt.

regions.name: Barsha Heights
regions.note: Inland of the Metro line with the shortest run to the Al Barsha cluster, so children are home earlier and a 5pm slot is genuinely workable. A good share of requests are Year 10 students on three sciences deciding which one to support.

regions.name: The Greens and The Views
regions.note: Built around Regent International School, with some children walking or making a very short journey. The earliest weekday slots in this corridor are realistic here, which makes two sessions a week easier to sustain in Year 11.

regions.name: Dubai Marina and JBR
regions.note: The largest resident population in range and the slowest evening roads. Later slots and recorded lessons matter here, because science sessions are the ones students most often want to replay before a test.

regions.name: Jumeirah Lakes Towers
regions.note: Its own Metro station and a wide spread of school destinations, including Jebel Ali. Steady demand for chemistry specifically, which in this corridor is the science families most often identify as the problem.

regions.name: Al Barsha, Al Barsha South and the villa belt
regions.note: The destination for most buses out of the Media City towers and the deepest school cluster nearby. Both Cambridge and Pearson candidates come from here, sometimes within the same family on different awards.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: The main secondary destination for this corridor, mixing British, American and IB provision. Because schools sometimes use different boards for different subjects, a student can be a Cambridge candidate in the sciences and a Pearson candidate in mathematics.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the tram corridor
schoolClusters.note: The genuinely local gates. Dubai College is selective and British; GEMS Wellington International School runs both British and IB Diploma routes, so one bus can carry students on separate sciences, a double award and MYP Sciences.

schoolClusters.city: Emirates Hills, Springs, Meadows and Jebel Ali
schoolClusters.note: The longest journeys from this corridor and strong British provision. The cluster where the Year 11 to sixth-form science decision is argued about most, and where combined-award students most often discover an entry requirement late.
