dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-media.modesIntro: Three patterns of IGCSE science support that work in this corridor, all delivered one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time.

modes.title: Single-science weekly hour
modes.description: One hour a week in the one science that is actually dragging the grade, chosen by triage rather than by feeling. This is the default and the most effective purchase, because a student on three sciences who splits one hour across all three gets twenty minutes each and no momentum in any of them.
bullets: Fixed weekly hour, usually 4.30pm to 8pm Gulf Standard Time
Triage decided from marked work, not from which science feels worst
Work from the school's scheme plus board-matched past papers
Recorded, so a practical-method session can be replayed

modes.title: Experimental-skills block
modes.description: Four to six sessions on method description, variables, instrument reading, tabulation, graphing and evaluation, which is how practical skill is assessed in writing. It applies across all three sciences at once, which makes it the best-value block available to a student on a double or combined award.
bullets: Method written precisely enough for a stranger to repeat
Variables identified in every question, as a habit
Graph checklist: axes, units, scale, line of best fit, gradient with triangle
Evaluation taught as a structure rather than a list of errors

modes.title: Year 11 paper programme
modes.description: A timed paper or section every week in the target science, marked line by line with the student against the official scheme, with an error log that becomes the revision document for the series. Content reteaching happens only where the papers prove a gap exists.
bullets: One full paper or section under time every week
Marked live against the board's own scheme
Command-term drilling specific to the award
A running error log the student revises from alone

sections.heading: The first question is which science award, not which tutor
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in Dubai Media City is only useful once the award is identified. Three separate sciences, a double award and a combined award are different qualifications with different codes, different paper counts and different expected depth. A tutor teaching separate-science depth to a Co-ordinated Sciences candidate wastes the student's time on material the paper will not reward, and a tutor doing the reverse leaves marks on the table.

Parents reasonably assume the school has made this clear. In practice the award is often named once, in a letter, in Year 9, and the report card afterwards says Science. The quickest way to settle it is to count the grades: three science grades means separate sciences, two means a double award, one means combined. Then confirm it with the examinations officer and ask for the syllabus codes.

Once you have the codes, the question to a prospective tutor is short. Which award do you teach this on, which board, and when did you last teach it. A specialist answers with 0620 or 4CH1 or 0654. A generalist says the content is broadly the same across awards, which is true of the chemistry and false of the paper, and the difference is what Year 11 marks are made of.

Nothing about this is helped by proximity. Media City has no school in it, the nearest centres are inland in Al Barsha, and whether a tutor lives in Al Sufouh has no bearing on which award they know. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India, and lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time so the pool is everyone teaching in this time zone.
bullets: Count the science grades: three, two or one identifies the award
Then confirm the board and syllabus codes with the examinations officer
A specialist answers with a code; a generalist talks about content overlap
Award depth, not just content, is what a matched tutor brings

sections.heading: The awards side by side, with codes
paragraphs: The table below sets out the main options a Dubai family will encounter, with the Cambridge and Pearson equivalents and what each implies for a student heading to sixth form. Treat it as the shape of the landscape and confirm the specific syllabus version with your child's school, because specifications are revised and centres choose between options.

The most consequential row is the last one. Separate sciences are the usual expectation for A Level or IB science entry. A double award is often acceptable with a good grade. A single combined award frequently is not, and that is the fact families most often discover in Year 12 rather than Year 10. If a science at 16 is even a possibility, the award question needs asking early.

The second thing to notice is that the awards differ in depth as well as breadth. A Co-ordinated Sciences paper covers all three disciplines but does not go as deep in any of them, which changes what revision should look like: breadth with reliable basics beats depth in a favourite discipline. Students who revise their strongest science hardest are a common and expensive pattern in double-award cohorts.

Finally, the practical arrangement varies. Cambridge centres run either a practical arrangement or an alternative-to-practical arrangement depending on what the centre offers, and Pearson assesses practical skills through the written papers. Ask the school which applies to your child, because it determines what a tutor should prepare and what remains school business.

table.caption: IGCSE SCIENCE AWARDS - CODES, GRADES AND WHAT EACH SUPPORTS

A Level or IB Chemistry, including medicine routes
A Level or IB Physics, including engineering routes

sections.heading: Practical skill, and what an online tutor can honestly prepare
paragraphs: This is the reasonable objection to online science tutoring and it deserves a direct answer. A tutor over video cannot stand beside a student at a bench while they set up a titration or wire a circuit. What they can do is prepare the student for how practical skill is actually assessed, which in an examination is on paper.

Both boards test practical understanding in writing. Pearson assesses practical skills through the written papers for its International GCSE sciences. Cambridge centres run either a practical arrangement or an alternative-to-practical arrangement, and in both cases the written demand has the same shape: describe a method precisely enough to be repeated, identify independent, dependent and control variables, read a measuring instrument to its resolution, tabulate with units in the headers, plot, calculate a gradient, and evaluate the method's limitations.

Every one of those is screen-shareable, and every one improves fastest with live marking against the official scheme. The most common losses are mechanical: axes without units, a gradient quoted without the triangle shown, a conclusion that restates the trend instead of evaluating the method, a variable named as controlled without saying how it was controlled. Those are checklist items, and a student who runs the checklist stops losing those marks permanently.

The laboratory work remains the school's responsibility and should. If your child's centre runs a separate practical examination, ask the science department which apparatus the paper assumes familiarity with and treat that as school business. Tutoring covers the written assessment of practical skill, which is where the marks are, and it should say so rather than implying facilities it does not have.
bullets: Practical understanding is assessed in writing in both boards' International GCSE sciences
Method, variables, instrument resolution, tabulation, graphs and evaluation are all paper skills
The usual losses are mechanical and respond to a checklist plus live marking
Laboratory work stays with the school; tutoring should not pretend otherwise

sections.heading: Where the marks go, science by science
paragraphs: Students name topics when asked what is hard. Marked papers show something different: the losses cluster around command terms, unwritten reasoning and mechanical graph and calculation errors, and they are remarkably consistent across the three sciences.

The single most expensive misunderstanding is treating describe and explain as the same instruction. Describe asks what happens; explain asks why, with a mechanism. A student who describes when asked to explain can write a paragraph of true statements and score nothing. The same applies to suggest, which invites a reasoned proposal rather than a recalled fact, and to evaluate, which requires a judgement with both sides present.

After command terms, the pattern splits by discipline. Biology loses marks to over-writing and to unpractised data questions. Chemistry loses them to multi-step mole calculations and to the qualitative analysis tables that students decline to memorise. Physics loses them to unit handling, equation rearrangement under time pressure and gradients quoted without units. The table sets this out with the fix and the realistic time it takes.

None of these repairs requires new content, which is why a term of science tutoring can change a grade without covering fresh material. It is also why the first session should be marking rather than teaching: until you know which of these is costing the marks, any teaching is a guess, and in Year 11 a guess costs a month.

One further pattern is worth naming, because it is invisible on a report card. Students who are short of time in a science paper almost always run out in the same place: the long experimental or data question near the end, which carries more marks than anything before it. They arrive with eight minutes and write three lines. Practising that question type first rather than last in a revision session, when attention is freshest, is a free change that recovers marks nobody realised were being lost to the clock rather than to knowledge.

Command-term discipline and past data questions; two to three sessions
Multi-step moles with an unsignposted limiting reagent; qualitative analysis not learned
Calculation drills plus daily five-minute recall; two to four sessions
Unit handling, rearrangement under time, gradients without units
Rearrangement drills and a graph checklist; two to three sessions
Describe and explain treated as synonyms
One session on command terms, then enforced in every answer
Four to six sessions, and it applies to all three sciences at once

sections.heading: Triage: which science to fix first when three are wobbling
paragraphs: A student on three separate sciences with one weekly tutoring hour has a decision to make, and most families make it badly by splitting the hour. Twenty minutes a week in each science produces no momentum in any of them, and the student arrives at each session having forgotten the last one. One science, done properly, for six to eight weeks, then reassess.

The triage question is not which science feels worst. It is which one is losing the most marks for the least structural reason. A student scoring moderately in all three but making mechanical graph and calculation errors in physics should start with physics, because the errors are cheap to fix and the gain is immediate. A student genuinely behind on chemistry content needs a longer block, so starting there means the other two go unsupported for a term.

There is also an order that respects the shared skills. The experimental-skills block, covering method, variables, tabulation, graphing and evaluation, applies to all three sciences at once. Four to six sessions on it improves every science paper the student sits, which makes it the best first purchase for a student on a double or combined award, and often for one on three separate sciences too.

Reassess from marked work rather than from feeling, after about six weeks. If the targeted science has moved and another has not, swap. If nothing has moved, the issue is the match, the diagnosis or the week rather than the subject, and buying a second hour will not help. Families who rotate deliberately get more from one hour than families who split it.
bullets: One science at a time, for six to eight weeks, then reassess from marked work
Triage on marks lost for structural reasons, not on which science feels worst
The experimental-skills block improves all three papers at once

sections.heading: What IGCSE science support costs around Al Sufouh
paragraphs: Published rates in Dubai sort into clear tiers. Budget online tutoring runs from AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are published from AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Specialists in IB, IGCSE and A Level run AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium named tutoring reaches AED 500 to AED 650 and beyond, with BartyED at AED 650.

For IGCSE science, the qualified band is where almost all of the value sits. The work that moves grades is command-term discipline, experimental-skills technique, calculation drills and past-paper marking against the official scheme, and none of that requires a premium specialist. The case for the specialist band is narrower: a student on separate sciences aiming at a hard sixth-form threshold, or a chemistry candidate with a genuine content deficit rather than a technique one.

In-home visits are published between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour with travel included, and Bestimate's in-home band is AED 180 to AED 350. Monthly packages include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. For weekly paper practice, eight contacts beat four, and the in-home package costs roughly double. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to AED 600 budget, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

Those are other providers' published figures rather than IB Gram prices. The questions worth insisting on before paying anything are short: the rate, whether it is per hour or per lesson, whether travel is inside the number, the cancellation terms and the remedy if the match is wrong. Three of the six strongest-ranking Dubai tutoring pages publish no rate at all, which is why a sourced table belongs on a page like this.

sections.heading: Entries, series and the resit route
paragraphs: Two dates govern a science plan: the papers and the entry. The entry is submitted by the school months in advance, usually without much announcement, which is why a question about the award raised in March is generally too late to act on.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not a route for a Dubai candidate. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states in its exams officers' guide that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so plan only from the live official timetable.

For a science candidate, the resit calculation has an extra wrinkle. Where the practical arrangement differs by centre, a private candidate retaking may need a centre that offers the same arrangement, and that is worth checking in August rather than October. November is the recovery series for both boards, with results arriving in the new year. Plan it before you know whether you need it, because the specialists are booked by autumn.
bullets: The school submits entries and confirms the award months before the papers
Cambridge: June and November for UAE candidates; February and March is India-only
Pearson: May/June and November, with November results arriving in the new year
A private candidate resitting a science needs a centre offering the right practical arrangement

sections.heading: From IGCSE science to A Level or IB: the bridging nobody buys
paragraphs: A good IGCSE science grade and readiness for a science at 16 are related but not the same thing. Both A Level and IB sciences assume more quantitative fluency than IGCSE examines, more comfort with rearranging multi-term expressions, and in the IB a formal approach to uncertainty that IGCSE does not teach at all.

That produces a predictable autumn. A student who scored well in IGCSE Physics meets uncertainty propagation in DP1 or A Level and finds it unfamiliar, concludes the subject has become harder than expected, and spends a term catching up on something that could have been learned in four sessions during a quiet summer. The same applies to the mathematics underneath chemistry, which arrives faster and in more steps than IGCSE prepared for.

The cheap intervention is the final term of Year 11 after the papers are done, or the summer that follows. Nothing else is competing for the time, the specialists are free because nobody is asking, and four to six sessions covers uncertainty treatment, algebraic speed and the habit of explaining with a mechanism. Almost nobody buys it, because the examinations are over and the new course has not started.

This is also the moment where a combined-award student finds out whether a science at 16 is actually available to them. If it is not, knowing in June is far better than discovering it in September, and the conversation to have is with the sixth form rather than with a tutor. If it is available with bridging, that bridging has a window, and the window is now.
bullets: A Level and IB sciences assume more quantitative fluency than IGCSE examines
IB sciences add formal uncertainty treatment, which IGCSE does not teach
Four to six sessions in the Year 11 summer term covers most of the gap
Combined-award students should confirm sixth-form entry in June, not September

process.title: Identify the award and the codes
process.description: Count the science grades on the last report, then confirm with the examinations officer which award, which board and which syllabus codes. Separate sciences, a double award and combined science are different qualifications pitched at different depths, and matching without that is guesswork.

process.title: Send one marked science paper
process.description: A returned paper shows the diagnosis immediately: describe answers given where explain was asked, data questions avoided, graphs without units, multi-step calculations abandoned. That takes minutes from real evidence and is a guess without it, and in Year 11 a guess costs a month.

process.title: Triage to one science
process.description: One science at a time, chosen by marks lost for structural reasons rather than by which feels worst, for six to eight weeks and then reassessed. Where the student is on a double or combined award, the experimental-skills block usually comes first, because it improves all three disciplines at once.

process.title: Free trial lesson on a real question
process.description: One lesson at no cost, worked on a question from the actual award and board your child sits, followed by a written note naming the largest single loss and what the first four sessions would target. Nothing is paid until you have read it and agreed.

process.title: Weekly paper, live marking, error log
process.description: A timed paper or section each week, marked line by line with the student against the official scheme, and a running error log that becomes the revision document for the series. Progress is measured by whether logged errors stop recurring, which you can check yourself.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the award, not the word science
whyPoints.description: Separate sciences at 0610, 0620 and 0625, Co-ordinated Sciences at 0654 and Combined Science at 0653 are pitched at different depths, and Pearson's equivalents differ again. A tutor teaching the wrong depth wastes the hour on material the paper will not reward.

whyPoints.title: Experimental skills taught as paper skills
whyPoints.description: Method, variables, instrument resolution, tabulation, graphing and evaluation are assessed in writing in both boards' International GCSE sciences. Four to six sessions on them improves every science paper the student sits, which makes it the best-value block on a double or combined award.

whyPoints.title: Triage instead of splitting the hour
whyPoints.description: A student on three sciences with one weekly hour should spend it on one science for six to eight weeks, not twenty minutes on each. Momentum is what produces change in a procedural subject, and a split hour produces none in any discipline.

whyPoints.title: The right tier, which is usually not the top one
whyPoints.description: Nearly all IGCSE science work sits comfortably in the published AED 150 to AED 300 band, because the gains come from command terms, technique and marked papers. The specialist band at AED 200 to AED 450 is for separate sciences at a hard threshold or a real content deficit.

whyPoints.title: No travel premium and no laboratory pretence
whyPoints.description: Published in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour against AED 150 to AED 300 online, and the premium is the drive. Laboratory work stays with the school. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we run only in India.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what comes next
whyPoints.description: A combined award often does not support a science at 16, and both A Level and IB sciences assume more quantitative fluency than IGCSE examines. Saying that in Year 10, when the award can still change, is more useful than selling a Year 11 rescue.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child is doing triple, double or combined science?
faqs.answer: Count the science grades on the most recent report. Three grades means separate sciences, two means a double award such as Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, and one means a combined single award such as 0653. Then email the examinations officer to confirm the board and the syllabus codes, since a report card often just says Science. The answer matters because the awards are pitched at different depths, and a tutor teaching the wrong depth spends the hour on material the paper will not reward.

faqs.question: Is double award science easier than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Lighter in total content, denser per mark, and frequently misjudged. Students expect relief and find that the breadth is retained while the teaching time is not, which means the basics in all three disciplines have to be reliable rather than one favourite discipline being strong. The commonest and most expensive pattern in double-award cohorts is a student revising their best science hardest. Breadth with dependable fundamentals is what the paper rewards.

faqs.question: Can my child take A Level or IB science after a combined award?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it needs confirming with the sixth form rather than assuming. Separate sciences are the usual expectation, a double award is often acceptable with a good grade, and a single combined award frequently is not sufficient without bridging. The expensive version of this question is asked in Year 12; the cheap version is asked in Year 10, when the award can still be changed, or in June of Year 11, when a bridging block still fits.

faqs.question: How can an online tutor prepare my child for science practicals?
faqs.answer: By preparing them for how practical skill is assessed, which is in writing. Pearson assesses practical skills through the written papers, and Cambridge centres run either a practical or an alternative-to-practical arrangement; in both cases the written demand is the same shape. Describing a method precisely, identifying variables, reading instruments to resolution, tabulating with units, plotting, calculating gradients and evaluating limitations are all screen-shareable and all improve fastest with live marking against the official scheme.

faqs.question: Why does a page of true statements score nothing on an explain question?
faqs.answer: Describe asks what happens; explain asks why, with a mechanism. A student who describes when asked to explain can write a paragraph of entirely true statements and score nothing, which is the single most expensive misunderstanding in IGCSE science. Suggest invites a reasoned proposal rather than a recalled fact, and evaluate requires a judgement with both sides present. One session on command terms, then enforced in every written answer, often recovers more than a month of content revision.

faqs.question: My child is wobbling in all three sciences. Where should one weekly hour go?
faqs.answer: Into one science for six to eight weeks, not twenty minutes into each. A split hour produces no momentum anywhere and the student arrives at each session having forgotten the last. Choose by marks lost for structural reasons rather than by which science feels worst: mechanical graph and calculation errors are cheap to fix and give an immediate gain, while a genuine content deficit needs a longer block. Then reassess from marked work and swap if needed.

faqs.question: Which block of work improves all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: The experimental-skills block: method description precise enough to repeat, independent, dependent and control variables identified, instruments read to their resolution, tables with units in the headers, graphs with the full checklist, and evaluation tied to the actual method used. Four to six sessions covers it, and because those questions appear in every science paper on every award, the gain shows up three times over. It is the best first purchase on a double or combined award.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks on graphs when the plotting is correct?
faqs.answer: Because the marks sit around the plotting. Axes need units, scales need to be sensible, a line of best fit needs to be a line rather than a join-the-dots, a gradient needs the triangle shown and units stated, and a conclusion needs to evaluate rather than restate the trend. Each is a separate mark and each is mechanical. A student who runs the same checklist on every graph question stops losing those marks permanently, usually within three or four marked papers.

faqs.question: Does qualitative analysis in chemistry really need to be memorised?
faqs.answer: Yes, and students resist it because it feels unsophisticated. Flame colours, precipitate colours, gas tests and the reagents that produce them are pure recall, they are examined, and they are among the most reliable marks on the paper. A fortnight of five minutes a day usually handles the whole set. It is worth insisting on, because a student who refuses to learn it is choosing to lose marks that require no understanding at all.

faqs.question: How much should IGCSE science tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Nearly all of it belongs in the published qualified band of AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, because the gains come from command terms, experimental-skills technique, calculation drills and marked past papers rather than from rare expertise. Specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above are worth it for separate sciences at a hard sixth-form threshold or a real content deficit. The premium band at AED 500 to AED 650 is rarely the right call for IGCSE science.

faqs.question: Is an in-home science tutor better because of the practical side?
faqs.answer: Not in a way that affects marks. Practical skill is assessed in writing in both boards' International GCSE sciences, and a tutor at your table is no more able to run a titration than one on a screen, because neither has a laboratory. Published in-home rates run AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included against AED 150 to AED 300 online, so the premium is the drive. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; that service exists only in India.

faqs.question: When do science entries get submitted, and can the award still change?
faqs.answer: Entries go in months before the papers, submitted by the school, usually without an announcement. A change of award is a Year 10 conversation rather than a Year 11 one, and it needs evidence: marked work across all three disciplines showing whether the separate-science depth is sustainable. If a science at 16 is a possibility, raise the award question early, because by the spring of Year 11 the decision has been made for you.

faqs.question: What should a private candidate retaking a science check before entering?
faqs.answer: Which practical arrangement the centre offers, because that varies and can differ from the arrangement the student prepared for. Beyond that, the entry administration sits with the school or the examination centre rather than with a tutoring provider, and private candidates need a centre willing to enter them. November is the recovery series for both boards, with results arriving in the new year, so settle the centre and the arrangement in August rather than October.

faqs.question: Is there any point in science tutoring after the Year 11 papers are finished?
faqs.answer: It is the cheapest and least popular block available. Both A Level and IB sciences assume more quantitative fluency than IGCSE examines, and the IB adds formal uncertainty treatment that IGCSE does not teach at all. Four to six sessions in the final term or the summer covers uncertainty, algebraic speed and explaining with a mechanism, at a point when nothing competes for the time and specialists are free because nobody is asking.

faqs.question: What should I expect to see after four science sessions?
faqs.answer: A timed paper marked against the official scheme, comparable with the first session's diagnosis. Specifically: explain answers that give a mechanism, graphs with units and a gradient triangle, multi-step calculations attempted rather than abandoned, and experimental questions answered with variables named. If none of that has changed, the honest reading is that the match or the diagnosis was wrong rather than that more hours are needed, and a re-match follows.

intro.heading: Three different science awards, and nobody tells you which one you have
paragraphs: Before any tutoring conversation, a Production City family needs to know which science qualification their child is sitting. Cambridge offers Combined Science, which is a single award covering all three sciences at reduced depth; Coordinated Sciences, syllabus 0654, which is a double award covering all three at greater depth; and three separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, each a full award in its own right. Pearson has its own equivalents, including Science Double Award and the separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1.

These are not variations on a theme. They differ in content depth, in the number of papers, in how many grades appear on the certificate and in what sixth-form entry they support. A student on Combined Science who intends to take A Level Chemistry may find they have not covered material the course assumes. A student on separate sciences has three times the content to revise and three sets of papers to pace. Tutoring planned without knowing which award is in play is tutoring planned for somebody else's child.

The second question nobody asks is the practical route. Cambridge science syllabuses offer a practical test and an alternative-to-practical paper, and the school chooses which one candidates are entered for. That choice changes what needs practising entirely: an alternative-to-practical paper assesses experimental design, apparatus recognition, data handling and evaluation on paper, while a practical test assesses the student doing it. Both are teachable, and they are not the same preparation.

Dubai Production City, which residents call IMPZ, has no secondary campus inside its boundary. Students travel to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha and Jebel Ali, and those schools do not all use the same board or the same award route. In a household with two children at two campuses, both studying science, the answers can differ.

This page is written at syllabus level because that is what a parent can verify. What each award contains, which practical route does what, where marks disappear in each of the three sciences, and what past-paper practice should look like. Delivery is one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run in India only.

Everything here was reviewed in October 2026. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running to 19 November 2026. Where a timetable is involved, read the board's own live PDF rather than any restatement, including this one, because a restated date is only as current as the page it sits on.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-produ.subjectsIntro: The science content that generates the most requests in this cluster, with the specific place marks go missing. The same topics recur across combined, coordinated and separate routes at different depths.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits. The reliable loss is explaining a change in brightness without naming the quantity that changed. Calculating total resistance in parallel is the second, usually from adding resistances rather than reciprocals.

subjects.name: Physics: forces and motion
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, the equations of motion, moments and pressure. Moments questions are lost on omitting the distance from the pivot or on mixing units. Graph questions need the gradient interpreted as a named quantity, not just calculated.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles, concentration and reacting masses. This is the gate in chemistry: a student who is slow here loses marks across the whole paper. Unit confusion between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres is the most expensive single slip.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis
subjects.description: Products at each electrode, half equations and the effect of the electrolyte. Marks go missing on half equations written without balanced charges, and on predicting products without reference to the reactivity of the ions present.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and rates
subjects.description: Homologous series, addition and substitution, plus reaction rate and catalysts. Rate explanations lose marks when a student writes that particles move faster without naming collision frequency or the proportion with sufficient energy.

subjects.name: Biology: transport in plants and animals
subjects.description: Xylem and phloem, transpiration, the circulatory system and gas exchange. The volume of terminology is the difficulty. Students describe a structure where the question asked how the structure's features suit its function, which is a different answer.

subjects.name: Biology: homeostasis and coordination
subjects.description: Temperature and blood glucose control, the nervous system and hormones. Negative feedback questions need the receptor, the coordinator, the effector and the correction named in order; students name two of the four and lose half the marks.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid inheritance, genetic diagrams, variation and selection. Genetic cross questions are lost on not defining the allele symbols used, which the mark scheme requires, and on omitting the phenotype ratio when asked for it.

subjects.name: Practical and investigative skills
subjects.description: Variable control, apparatus choice, tabulating results, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient and evaluating a method. Assessed through the practical paper on Cambridge routes and inside the written papers on Pearson, and worth targeting as its own skill either way.

sections.heading: Combined, coordinated or separate: find out which award you have
paragraphs: This is the single most useful thing a Production City family can establish, and it takes one email. Cambridge Combined Science is a single award covering all three sciences at reduced depth, producing one grade. Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award covering all three at greater depth, producing two grades. The separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, are three full awards producing three grades.

The consequences run in several directions. Content depth differs, so a student on Combined Science has genuinely not met material that a separate-sciences candidate has. Grade count differs, which matters for a sixth-form application counting subjects. Revision volume differs by a factor of two or more. And sixth-form entry preferences differ, with many Dubai sixth forms preferring separate sciences for A Level science routes.

Pearson's structure is parallel but not identical. It offers Science Double Award alongside separate Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1, graded 9-1, and the International GCSE sciences are untiered rather than split into Core and Extended. A student moving between a Cambridge school and a Pearson school mid-course can meet content they were never taught and lose content they had already mastered.

So ask the exams officer for the board, the syllabus code, the tier where one applies, and the series, in writing, per science. Then bring that to any tutoring conversation. We match on the code because a Coordinated candidate and a separate Physics candidate need different depth on the same topic, and a tutor working at the wrong depth wastes the hour in both directions.

sections.heading: The practical route, and why it changes what you revise
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses offer two practical assessment routes, and the school chooses which one candidates sit. One is a practical test in which the student performs an experiment under exam conditions. The other is an alternative-to-practical paper which assesses the same skills on paper: recognising apparatus from a diagram, identifying variables, completing a results table, plotting, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient and evaluating a method.

Most Dubai families do not know which route their child is entered for, and it changes revision priorities substantially. Preparing for an alternative-to-practical paper is paper work, and it is among the most learnable components in the whole qualification because the question types repeat and the mark scheme rewards specific phrasing. Preparing for a practical test adds procedural rehearsal that only a laboratory can supply.

Pearson's International GCSE sciences take a different approach, assessing practical skills within the written papers rather than through a separate practical component. The effect is that practical skill questions are distributed through the paper, so a student cannot prepare for them as a discrete block and has to meet them wherever they appear.

Whichever route applies, the underlying skills are the same and they are badly taught almost everywhere, because they sit between topics rather than inside one. Axes labelled with quantity and unit. Scales chosen so the plotted points use most of the grid. A line of best fit drawn as a line rather than joined dot to dot. A gradient calculated and then named as a physical quantity. Variables identified as independent, dependent and controlled, with the control explained rather than listed.

sections.heading: Where marks go missing in each of the three sciences
paragraphs: Across hundreds of scripts, the losses in IGCSE science concentrate in a short list, and the list differs by subject. Knowing which applies to your child turns a vague revision plan into a specific one, and it is the first thing a timed paper reveals.

In physics, the pattern is explanation structure and unit discipline. A student who says a lamp gets dimmer because more current goes elsewhere has described the result and named nothing the mark scheme can credit. The fix is to name the quantity that changed, the relationship, the direction and then the effect. Moments questions lose marks on omitted distances; parallel resistance questions lose them on adding resistances rather than reciprocals.

In chemistry, the pattern is quantitative fluency and equation discipline. Mole reasoning underpins reacting masses, concentration and electrolysis calculations, and a student who is slow at it loses marks across the whole paper. Half equations written without balanced charges, state symbols omitted and unbalanced equations are the standard notational losses.

In biology, the pattern is terminology and command terms. The content volume is the real difficulty rather than its conceptual depth, and the mark schemes are precise about vocabulary. Students also answer the wrong question: asked how a structure's features suit its function, they describe the structure. Negative feedback questions need receptor, coordinator, effector and correction named in order, and most students supply two of the four. Genetic cross questions carry a similar requirement, since the mark scheme expects the allele symbols to be defined before the diagram is drawn, and a student who omits the definitions loses marks on a cross they completed perfectly.

sections.heading: Command terms do the same work in IGCSE as at Diploma level
paragraphs: The highest-return teaching in IGCSE science is not a topic. It is reading the instruction. State wants a fact. Describe wants an account of what happens or what features exist. Explain wants a reason or a mechanism named. Suggest wants a plausible answer where more than one is defensible. Calculate wants working shown as well as an answer. Compare wants both things referred to in the same sentence.

The arithmetic of getting this wrong is simple and brutal. A student writing a paragraph for a one-mark state question has spent two minutes earning one mark, and will be short of time on the six-mark question later. A student describing where the question said explain scores nothing, because there is no line in the mark scheme for an accurate description of the outcome.

Compare questions deserve a specific mention because they are so often half-answered. A compare question needs both items addressed in the same statement: this one is higher than that one, rather than a paragraph about one followed by a paragraph about the other. Students who write two separate accounts frequently score zero on a question they understood completely.

This is also the most transferable thing we can teach. A student sitting three separate sciences gets the benefit in all three papers, and a Coordinated candidate gets it across every paper they sit. Three to five sessions of deliberate structure work, with timed short-answer questions marked against the mark scheme, is usually enough to change it measurably.

sections.heading: Past-paper work in three subjects at once
paragraphs: For a separate-sciences candidate the hard part is not any single subject; it is managing three revision programmes and three sets of papers landing in the same study leave. Families usually respond by revising whichever subject feels worst, which concentrates effort where anxiety is highest rather than where marks are most recoverable.

The alternative is to set priority from component marks. Ask the school for component-level results across all three sciences. A student losing most marks to command-term structure across all three has one problem, cheap to fix and worth doing first because it pays three times. A student with a specific content hole in chemistry electrolysis has a different problem, confined to one paper.

Sequence within each subject follows the same rule as elsewhere. Topic questions first, while the school content is fresh. Then mixed sections under timing, because mixing exposes the traps topic practice hides. Then whole papers, late, when the student can complete one without exhaustion. For three subjects, that sequence has to be staggered rather than run in parallel, or the student does twelve weeks of topic questions and no timed papers at all.

We do not reproduce or distribute Cambridge or Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents or grade-boundary tables, which are copyright material. We reference the official source and work from papers the student or school legitimately holds. Your child's science teachers can supply past papers through the school, which is both legitimate and usually faster.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Science is where the cost question gets genuinely complicated, because three subjects can mean three tutors. A family paying for weekly biology, chemistry and physics support at the specialist band is making a substantial commitment, and in most cases it is not the right purchase.

The Dubai market bands, read in October 2026 from competitor pages and the Bestimate 2026 rate table. Budget or university-student tutors at AED 45-150, with EdFlik listing AED 45-65 and Tutopiya from AED 33-52. Qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists at AED 200-450, with TutorChase at AED 270. Premium or examiner-led from AED 500-650, with BartyED at AED 650. In-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, rising to AED 500.

The better pattern for most families is sequential rather than parallel. Identify from component marks which single science is costing the most, work on that for a defined block with a specialist, then move. Command-term and graph-skill work, which pays across all three, can be bought once rather than three times. That typically halves the spend against three concurrent weekly arrangements and produces more.

Context worth having: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. These are market figures rather than IB Gram prices. We publish no price list here and start with a free trial lesson instead.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and the honesty boundary
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are overseen by KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, with annual inspections published on a six-band scale. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah has SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Individual tutors need a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time via its app, website or e-services system. u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

On academic honesty, the boundary applies to any school-set investigation or coursework. A tutor teaches the skills, explains what the criteria reward, questions the approach, and gives feedback on drafts the student wrote. A tutor never writes, rewrites or completes assessed work or generates data. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student.

IB Gram is not KHDA approved, ADEK approved, Cambridge accredited or Pearson approved, holds no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is a specific licence issued to training institutes with physical premises, and has no UAE office. Ask any provider describing itself as approved which permit it means.

sections.heading: Starting with the code and the practical route in hand
paragraphs: Send four things and the match becomes exact: the board, the syllabus code per science, the tier where one applies, and which practical route the school entered the student for. All four come from the exams officer in one email, and they change what a tutor should be doing in the first session rather than the fifth.

Add component marks and a recent marked script if you have them. For a separate-sciences candidate, component marks across all three subjects are what set the priority order, and priority order is most of the value in the first plan. For a double-award candidate, the script usually shows which single discipline is dragging every paper.

Then take the free trial lesson, which is a real teaching hour on the current sticking point rather than a consultation, with a short written note afterwards. No card is held, nothing renews, and if the match is wrong we rematch once at no charge. Mainstream science matches usually take two to three days, longer in the four weeks around mocks when early evening slots go first.

Production City sessions usually land at 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time or later on weekdays, with weekend mornings better for graph and practical-paper work. process.title: Confirm the practical route
process.description: Ask whether the school entered your child for a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, or whether practical skills sit inside the written papers as with Pearson. The answer changes revision priorities substantially, and the alternative-to-practical paper is among the most learnable components in the qualification.

process.title: Set priority from component marks
process.description: For three separate sciences, component marks tell you which subject is costing the most and whether the losses are content or command term. process.description: Topic questions, then mixed sections, then whole papers, but staggered across the three subjects rather than run in parallel. Run in parallel, a student spends twelve weeks on topic questions and never reaches a timed paper in any subject, which is the most common revision failure at this level.

whyPoints.title: Specialists, not a science generalist
whyPoints.description: Biology, chemistry and physics have different marking conventions and different traps. Where a student needs one discipline repaired we use a specialist in it, including inside a double award, because every paper in a double award spans all three and the weak strand cannot be avoided.

whyPoints.title: Practical skills taught as their own subject
whyPoints.description: Axes labelled with quantity and unit, scales using most of the grid, a best fit line drawn as a line, a gradient named as a quantity, variables controlled with the method stated. These sit between topics and are badly taught almost everywhere, which makes them cheap marks.

faqs.question: How do I find out if my child is on Combined, Coordinated or separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Email the exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code per science, the tier where one applies and the series, in writing. Cambridge Combined Science is a single award at reduced depth, Coordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award at intermediate depth, and Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 are three full awards. They differ in content, in grade count and in what sixth forms will accept for A Level sciences, and nobody volunteers the information unless you ask for it directly.

faqs.question: Does the award route affect A Level science entry in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Often, yes. Many Dubai sixth forms prefer separate sciences for A Level science routes, because the content depth is greatest and because three grades give an admissions tutor more to work with. A Coordinated Sciences candidate can usually progress but should check the specific sixth form's stated requirement, and a Combined Science candidate aiming at A Level chemistry may find they have not covered material the course assumes. Ask the sixth form directly rather than relying on a general impression, and ask before Year 10 choices are final if possible.

faqs.question: Our school entered him for the paper practical option. What changes?
faqs.answer: It assesses practical skills on paper rather than in a laboratory: recognising apparatus from a diagram, identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables, completing a results table, plotting points, drawing a line of best fit, calculating a gradient and evaluating a method. Cambridge offers it as an alternative to a practical test and the school chooses which candidates sit. It is among the most learnable components in the whole qualification because the question types repeat, which makes targeted past-paper work on it unusually good value in the final term.

faqs.question: Why does my son lose marks on physics explain questions?
faqs.answer: Because he is describing the outcome rather than naming the mechanism. A question asking why a lamp dims when another is added awards marks for the change in total resistance, the effect on current, and then the brightness. Writing that current goes elsewhere describes the result and names nothing creditable. The structure that fixes it is mechanical: name the quantity that changes, name the relationship, state the direction, state the effect. Three to five sessions of structure work usually changes it measurably, and it transfers to the other two sciences.

faqs.question: Which chemistry topic should we fix first?
faqs.answer: Moles, almost always. Relative formula mass, moles, concentration and reacting masses underpin stoichiometry, electrolysis calculations and most quantitative questions, so a student who is slow at it loses marks across the whole paper for reasons unrelated to chemical understanding. The most expensive single slip is unit confusion between cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres, a factor of a thousand. Four to six sessions of timed mixed drill usually makes the method automatic, and that work can be supervised competently at the budget rather than specialist band.

faqs.question: Is biology really just memorising a lot of words?
faqs.answer: The content volume is the main difficulty, but the marks are lost on precision rather than volume. Mark schemes are exact about vocabulary, and students also answer a slightly different question from the one asked: told to explain how a structure's features suit its function, they describe the structure. Negative feedback questions need the receptor, coordinator, effector and correction named in order and most students supply two of four. Genetic cross questions require the allele symbols to be defined, which students omit. Each of those is a structural habit rather than more memorising.

faqs.question: Do we need three separate tutors for three sciences?
faqs.answer: Usually not, and the sequential alternative costs roughly a third as much. Ask the school for component marks across all three subjects. If the losses look similar in all three, you have a command-term and graph-skills problem, which is one intervention of four to six hours that pays in three papers. If one subject is clearly worse, buy a six to eight week block with a specialist in that subject, then reassess. Three concurrent weekly arrangements at AED 150-300 an hour each is a large commitment that rarely matches the actual diagnosis.

faqs.question: How do we revise three sciences without the papers colliding?
faqs.answer: Build the schedule against the actual exam timetable rather than a generic plan, and stagger the sequence rather than running it in parallel. Each subject needs topic questions first, then mixed sections under timing, then whole papers. Run all three in parallel and the student spends twelve weeks on topic questions and never reaches a timed paper in anything. Staggering means one subject moves to timed papers while another is still on topic work, which is uncomfortable to plan and much more effective in practice.

faqs.question: What graph mistakes cost the most in science papers?
faqs.answer: Four recur. Axes labelled with a quantity but no unit, or with neither. Scales chosen so the plotted points occupy a quarter of the grid, which loses accuracy marks on reading values off. A line of best fit drawn by joining the points dot to dot, which is a different claim about the data. And a gradient calculated correctly and then never named as a physical quantity, so the examiner cannot award the interpretation mark. All four are mechanical, all four are drilled out in a handful of sessions, and all four appear on every route.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson sciences interchangeable for revision?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered Core and Extended, with Core capped at grade C, and offer a practical test or alternative-to-practical route. Pearson's International GCSE sciences are untiered on a 9-1 scale and assess practical skills inside the written papers. Question phrasing, mark allocation patterns and topic balance all differ, so revising from the wrong board's past papers is practice for an exam your child is not sitting. A student moving between a Cambridge school and a Pearson school mid-course should expect genuine content gaps in both directions.

faqs.question: Can online lessons cover practical science work?
faqs.answer: For the assessed skills, yes, and often better than in-person because graph construction and table completion happen on a shared whiteboard that saves every step. Experimental design, variable control, apparatus recognition from diagrams, tabulation, plotting, gradient work and evaluation are all paper skills. What online tutoring cannot replace is the hours a student spends handling apparatus, which is the school's responsibility. If the school entered your child for a practical test rather than the paper alternative, the lab rehearsal has to come from the school.

faqs.question: Which exam sittings are available to a Dubai science candidate?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, warning it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam otherwise. Ask your exams officer which zone applies.

faqs.question: What time can science sessions start for a Production City student?
faqs.answer: Realistically from 5:30pm Gulf Standard Time on weekdays. With no secondary campus inside Dubai Production City, students bus to Motor City, Dubai Investments Park, Al Barsha or Jebel Ali and are typically home between four and half past, needing food and a break before anything demanding. Dubai South and Emaar South families often need six o'clock or later. Weekend mornings are better for graph and practical-paper work, which needs sustained concentration that a weekday evening after a long bus day rarely supports.

faqs.question: Does your science tutor come to our home in Dubai Production City?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers all UAE lessons as one-to-one live video, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. Across a three-subject revision programme the online format is what keeps the sessions happening when a bus is late or a road is closed, and graph work on a shared whiteboard is saved for later revision. Independent home tutors do work in this area at roughly AED 180-350 an hour on published Dubai market rates, and for a younger child needing physical supervision they can be the better choice.

faqs.question: Are private science tutors in Dubai required to be licensed?
faqs.answer: Yes. A MoHRE private tuition work permit is required, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time through its app, website or e-services. u.ae states that tutoring without the permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so distrust any amount quoted.

And which subject is actually costing the most marks, which only component marks can tell you. Get all four, send a recent marked script, and take a free trial lesson before buying anything.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one set of evenings
paragraphs: The arithmetic defeats most families before the teaching starts. A Year 11 student sitting three separate sciences has three sets of papers, and a student on a coordinated or combined award has content from all three compressed into one grade. Either way, the week contains perhaps two usable tuition evenings and a weekend morning, and three subjects do not fit into two evenings without a rule for deciding what gets dropped.

What happens in practice is that the rule is made by accident. Whichever subject had the worst recent test gets the attention, then the next worst, and by week four the plan has become a chemistry plan because chemistry produced the most alarming mark in February. The other two drift, nobody notices until the mock, and then the whole process repeats with a different subject in the leading position.

A rotation fixes this. Two subjects in any given fortnight, the third held in reserve with supervised self-study against the school's past papers, and a planned switch. The reason it works is that the three sciences fail in different ways and therefore need different quantities of attention. Chemistry's weaknesses are mostly procedural and close quickly. Physics divides into procedures that close and reasoning that does not. Biology is volume and precision, and it needs steady low-intensity work rather than bursts.

There is one preliminary that cannot be skipped. Establish whether your child sits three separate sciences, a Cambridge Coordinated Science entry at 0653, a Combined entry at 0654, or Pearson separate sciences at 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. These are structurally different qualifications with different grade consequences, and a rotation built for the wrong one wastes the term politely. One message to the school, answered subject by subject, settles it.

IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. Across Silicon Oasis, Cedre Villas, Academic City and the surrounding communities, lessons are live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time. For a rotation that matters practically: the subject in a given week can switch without renegotiating a visit, and a session can move when a mock week or a practical assessment shifts the household's timetable.

What follows is the rotation itself, the term-by-term shape, how the three sciences differ in repair speed, how practical assessment works from a UAE centre, and when the November series becomes the sensible route. Use it to decide which subject gets this fortnight, which is the decision nobody makes deliberately.

One more thing worth saying before the detail. A rotation is not a way of buying more hours; it is a way of making the same hours land somewhere useful. Families who adopt one often spend less across a term than those who respond to each alarming mark in turn, because the expensive teaching hours go only to the subject currently being taught while the other two are kept warm cheaply. The gain comes from the allocation rather than from the quantity.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-silic.subjectsIntro: This grid sorts the three sciences by how they fail and how quickly each weakness closes, which is what a rotation has to be built on. The differences between them are larger than the subject labels suggest.

subjects.name: Chemistry calculations
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, percentage yield and empirical formulae. Finite procedures that close in about four sessions, which makes chemistry the fastest-moving of the three sciences and therefore the natural first subject in a rotation.

subjects.name: Chemistry qualitative analysis
subjects.description: The tests and observations for ions and gases, which is pure drillable content that almost nobody is made to learn systematically. Two sessions and reliable marks follow, and it is the clearest single example of unclaimed marks in the whole science set.

subjects.name: Physics calculations and units
subjects.description: Multi-step calculations where units are dropped or answers left in the wrong power of ten. A standard working layout fixes it in about one session and the benefit applies across both physics papers and into chemistry calculations too.

subjects.name: Physics six-mark explanations
subjects.description: Questions wanting a causal chain that names a mechanism, where students write three restatements of the first sentence instead. A habit rather than a fact, so it needs a term of marked practice and does not close in a fortnight.

subjects.name: Biology written precision
subjects.description: Naming the structure, the process and the consequence. Biology mark schemes award nothing for general sense, and students leave the examination believing they answered. Months of marked practice rather than weeks, so biology belongs in the rotation early and steadily.

subjects.name: Biology content volume
subjects.description: Cells, transport, respiration, nutrition, coordination, inheritance and ecology. Too much to compress, which is why biology punishes a late start more than chemistry does and rewards low-intensity weekly contact across a whole term.

subjects.name: Coordinated and Combined Science
subjects.description: All three sciences in one or two grades. The rotation problem is worst here, because a gap may sit in whichever subject the tutor knows least and the content is compressed. Ask whether a prospective tutor has taught the coordinated syllabus itself, not the three subjects separately.

subjects.name: Practical reasoning in writing
subjects.description: Apparatus choice, reading scales to the right precision, systematic versus random error, and specific improvements. Cambridge offers a written alternative-to-practical paper on several syllabuses, and this reasoning is assessed on the theory papers too, so it serves more than one component.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside science
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, percentages, ratios and unit conversion. The shared gap. A student weak here appears weak in physics and chemistry simultaneously, so a single block often lifts two subjects and should usually be the rotation's first move.

subjects.name: Command words across the sciences
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, calculate and compare demand different amounts in all three subjects. One session with past papers from each science improves the whole set at once, which makes it the highest-leverage hour in a three-subject plan.

sections.heading: Establish the entry shape before building anything
paragraphs: A rotation built for the wrong qualification is a well-organised waste. Ask the school, in writing, for the board and the code for each science, plus the tier where Cambridge applies. The reply will say something like Cambridge 0620 Extended and 0625 Extended, or 0653 Coordinated Science, or Pearson 4BI1 and 4CH1. Those are different situations needing different rotations.

Three separate sciences gives three grades, which means a weakness can be isolated and the rotation can deprioritise the two subjects that are fine. Coordinated Science at 0653 is awarded as a single grade across all three subjects, so a weak area drags one grade rather than one of three and the rotation has to keep all three in play. Combined Science at 0654 is narrower again. Pearson separate sciences are single-tier with their own paper structures.

The tier question applies to Cambridge and has a hard consequence. The Core route does not reach the top grades, because the papers sat do not contain the marks needed to cross those boundaries. If your child is aiming at A Level or IB Diploma sciences, check whether the sixth-form requirement sits above the current ceiling, and check it in Year 10 while the entry is still reviewable with the school.

Ask subject by subject rather than once. Many Dubai schools enter biology with one board and physics with another, for staffing or historical reasons, and an answer about the school as a whole is not an answer about your child's three sciences. Quote the codes when requesting a tutor and ask the tutor to repeat them back with the paper structures attached.

sections.heading: The rotation, fortnight by fortnight
paragraphs: Start with the shared-gap block rather than with a subject. Four to six sessions on command words, formula rearrangement, unit handling and working layout, using past papers from all three sciences as the material. This is the only purchase in a three-subject plan that improves everything at once, and running it first means the rotation that follows is about content rather than about technique.

Then rotate in fortnights. Chemistry first, because its weaknesses are the most procedural and therefore close fastest: moles calculations and the qualitative analysis tables produce visible movement inside four sessions, and finishing a subject early frees capacity. Physics second, aimed at the procedural half of its problems, which is units, working layout and the specific topics the marked papers identified. Biology runs underneath throughout rather than in a slot of its own.

That last point is the one most families get wrong. Biology is volume and precision, and both respond to steady low-intensity contact rather than to a concentrated fortnight. Thirty minutes of marked written practice every week across a term produces more than six hours compressed into two weeks, because the precision habit forms by repetition. So biology occupies the weekend session and the self-study time rather than a weekday rotation slot.

Every switch should be driven by evidence rather than by the calendar. The weekend full paper in the non-rotating subject produces an error tally, and the tally decides whether the switch happens on schedule or whether the current subject needs another fortnight. A rotation that switches on a fixed date regardless of evidence is just a timetable; one that switches on evidence is a plan.

paragraphs: Chemistry's characteristic weaknesses are procedural. Moles and concentration calculations are a finite set of steps. The Cambridge qualitative analysis tables are drillable content that students are rarely made to learn systematically. Both close in sessions rather than terms, which is why chemistry is the natural first subject in a rotation: it finishes, and a finished subject frees the slot for the next one.

Physics divides in half. Units, standard form and working layout are procedural and close in a session or two, and they transfer into chemistry calculations at no extra cost. Six-mark written explanations are not procedural: they require a causal chain in which each step names a mechanism, and students who have spent two years writing descriptions need a term of marked practice to change that. So physics gets its procedural half in the rotation and its reasoning half across the whole term.

Biology is neither. It is volume and precision. There is more content than the other two and the mark schemes award nothing for general sense, so an answer that does not name the structure, the process and the consequence scores zero even where the student understands it. Both of those respond to steady repetition rather than to concentrated attention, which is why biology sits underneath the rotation rather than inside it.

Understanding those three profiles is what makes a rotation more than a timetable. It explains why chemistry goes first, why physics appears twice in different forms, and why biology never gets a dedicated fortnight and still improves. Families who grasp this stop treating the three sciences as interchangeable units of difficulty and start treating them as three different jobs.

sections.heading: Anchor the rotation to the mock, not the examination
paragraphs: Schools along this corridor run mocks at different points, and the mock date rather than the series date is the right anchor for a three-subject plan. A mock produces marked evidence in all three sciences simultaneously, which is exactly what a rotation needs and exactly what no amount of parental impression can supply. A plan that aims past the mock throws away the only full-length diagnostic the student gets in all three subjects at once.

So structure it as two plans. The first runs up to the mock and aims at arriving ready for it, which is a different goal from treating the mock as a rehearsal. The second is rebuilt entirely from the three error tallies the mock produces. Families who structure it this way describe the spring term as calmer, because the second rotation is evidence-led rather than driven by whichever subject most recently produced an alarming mark.

Reading the mocks takes about an hour for all three and needs no scientific knowledge. For each paper, sort every lost mark into four causes: did not know it, ran out of time, misread what was asked, or knew it and wrote an answer that did not earn the marks. Then compare the three tallies. Usually one subject is dominated by a single cause, which tells you which subject needs teaching and which needs only practice.

There is also a predicted-grade reason to care. Sixth-form and foundation applications are generally made on predictions formed partly from mock results, so performing better in the mock improves the options available regardless of what June eventually produces. Almost no family buys science tuition aimed specifically at the mock, and the cost is identical to buying it two terms later.

sections.heading: Practical assessment from a UAE centre
paragraphs: This is the question parents ask most about online science tuition and the one competing pages leave unanswered. Cambridge offers a written alternative-to-practical paper on several science syllabuses, and that is the route most candidates sitting from a UAE centre meet. It assesses apparatus selection, reading scales to the correct precision, identifying sources of error, interpreting results and suggesting specific improvements, all in writing and all based on described experiments.

That means practical marks are largely won by reasoning that can be taught without a bench, and taught in all three sciences at once, since the skills are common across them. A student who can explain why a measurement was repeated, distinguish systematic from random error, read a scale correctly and suggest an improvement that is specific rather than generic will score on that paper in biology, chemistry and physics alike. It is therefore an efficient addition to a rotation.

Where a syllabus does require school-assessed practical work, the laboratory is the school's and should be. Your child has apparatus, a teacher who knows it and technicians who maintain it, and a tutor offering to replicate that would be offering something worse than what already exists. What a tutor adds is the thinking either side: anticipating error sources before the experiment and interpreting the results honestly afterwards.

Confirm which route applies to each of your child's three sciences, because schools sometimes differ between subjects. Ask whether each entry includes a practical assessment or an alternative-to-practical paper. The answer takes one line, it determines how much of the rotation should go to practical reasoning, and it is also the question that most quickly reveals whether a prospective tutor knows the syllabus.

sections.heading: Which series, and when November becomes the answer
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no student at a Dubai school sits it, and a rotation built around a February entry deadline has imported another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so take your dates from the school's exams officer or the board's live timetable rather than from any tutoring page.

On results, Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Those backward-looking figures are the ones worth knowing, because they describe the shape of the year rather than a date that may be revised.

For a three-science family the November route has a particular use. A student short in one of three separate sciences can resit that one subject in November without disturbing the other two, which is a narrower and cheaper piece of work than a full-year repeat. A student on a coordinated award has a harder decision, because the single grade carries all three subjects. Hold an entry-fee reserve from the start either way, because fees go to the examination centre.
