sections.heading: What a rotation costs, and what to buy at which band
paragraphs: Three subjects does not have to mean three specialist bookings, and the rotation exists partly to prevent that. Published market bands, all read in October 2026: budget online tuition from AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik; a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors advertising IGCSE from AED 150; in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the figure. None of these is an IB Gram price.

The rotation allocates bands as well as weeks. The shared-gap block and the subject currently being taught belong at the qualified band, because command words, working layout and the procedural topics need someone who knows the mark scheme. The subject being kept warm belongs at the budget band or in supervised self-study with the school's past papers, because that work is practice rather than teaching.

That allocation is where the saving sits. A family paying the qualified band for three subjects simultaneously across a term is paying for teaching in two subjects that only need practice. The same total hours, distributed by the rotation, cost less and achieve more because the expensive hours land where expertise is actually required. Bestimate's monthly estimates for one weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist.

Our own terms follow the free trial lesson and the mock or paper diagnosis, because a single hourly figure across Year 10 biology recall and Extended physics explanation would be misleading in both directions. What the bands above are for is checking a quote you already hold and deciding, before you speak to anybody, which parts of your rotation genuinely need the more expensive hour.

sections.heading: Starting from Dubai Silicon Oasis, and what we will not claim
paragraphs: Send five things: the codes and tiers for each science, the entry shape, the school's mock dates, the most recent marked papers in all three subjects, and the two evenings plus weekend morning your household can realistically hold. That last item is what makes a rotation work or fail, and nobody is asked for it. We then match tutors to the codes and run a free trial lesson as live one-to-one video on Gulf Standard Time, at no cost.

Afterwards you receive a written rotation: which subject gets the first fortnight and why, what the shared-gap block will cover, which subject sits on supervised self-study, and when the plan is rebuilt from the mock. For many families the opening move is the shared-gap block rather than any subject at all, because command words and formula rearrangement are costing marks in all three. If that is the finding, we will say so.

Four limits, stated before you build a rotation around us. Nothing arrives as a download: we do not supply syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes, we reference them and link to the official source, which has the side benefit that the version your child rotates through is the current one rather than a copy of a copy. No approval sits behind the plan either, from a board or a regulator, so nobody here is KHDA approved or Cambridge accredited. There is no UAE office, centre or branch and we claim none, in Dubai Silicon Oasis or anywhere else. And IB Gram does not run home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. That last limit is why the three-science rotation described above is designed for live video rather than for a tutor driving in from Academic City on three separate evenings a week.

And no grade predictions. What a term-long rotation should produce is three error tallies that have moved, a shared-gap block that no longer appears in any of them, and a student who can say which cause is costing them marks in each subject. Those are checkable. A grade promise is not, and a provider offering one across three subjects has told you a great deal about how it sells.

faqs.question: How do we cover three IGCSE sciences with only two free evenings?
faqs.answer: With a written rotation rather than more willpower. Two fixed weekday evenings each carry one subject for a fortnight, the third sits on supervised self-study against the school's past papers, and the switch is planned in advance. A weekend morning carries a full paper in whichever subject the evenings are not touching, which produces the evidence for the next switch. Left to instinct, the plan becomes a single-subject plan by week four.

faqs.question: Which science should a Silicon Oasis student start with?
faqs.answer: Chemistry, in most cases, because its characteristic weaknesses are the most procedural and therefore close fastest. Moles and concentration calculations are a finite set of steps, and the Cambridge qualitative analysis tables are drillable content almost nobody is made to learn systematically. Four sessions produces visible movement, and a finished subject frees the slot for the next. Before any of that, though, buy the shared-gap block that lifts all three.

faqs.question: Why does biology never get its own fortnight in the rotation?
faqs.answer: Because biology is volume and precision, and both respond to steady repetition rather than concentrated attention. Thirty minutes of marked written practice every week across a term produces more than six hours compressed into a fortnight, since naming the structure, the process and the consequence is a habit that forms by repetition. So biology lives in the weekend session and the self-study time and improves throughout without occupying a weekday rotation slot.

faqs.question: What is the shared gap across all three IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Command words and mathematics. State, describe, explain, suggest, calculate and compare demand different amounts in every subject, and answering the wrong amount costs marks or time. Separately, rearranging formulae, standard form, percentages and unit conversion appear in every physics paper and most chemistry ones. A student weak there looks weak in two subjects at once, so one four to six session block often lifts the whole set.

faqs.question: Does my child sit three separate sciences or a coordinated award?
faqs.answer: Ask the school in writing, subject by subject, for the board and the code. Cambridge uses 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics for separate sciences, 0653 for Coordinated Science awarded as one grade and 0654 for Combined. Pearson uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. It matters for the rotation: separate sciences let you deprioritise the two that are fine, while a coordinated grade carries all three and keeps all three in play.

faqs.question: Do tutors come to homes in Cedre Villas for science lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists only in India. For a rotation the online format has a specific advantage: the subject in a given week can switch without renegotiating a visiting arrangement, and a session can move when a mock week or a practical assessment shifts the household timetable. Scale diagrams and graphs are also easier to teach on a shared screen than across a table.

faqs.question: How are practicals assessed if we study science online from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge offers a written alternative-to-practical paper on several science syllabuses, and that is the route most candidates sitting from a UAE centre meet. It assesses apparatus selection, reading scales to the right precision, identifying error sources, interpreting results and suggesting specific improvements, all in writing. Those skills are common across all three sciences, so one block covers the set. Where school-assessed practical work applies, the school's laboratory does that properly.

faqs.question: When should the rotation be rebuilt?
faqs.answer: At the mock window, entirely and from the evidence. Mocks produce marked papers in all three sciences at once, which is exactly what a rotation needs. Sort each paper into four causes, did not know it, ran out of time, misread what was asked, or knew it and did not earn the marks, then compare the three tallies. Usually one subject is dominated by a single cause, which tells you which needs teaching and which needs only practice.

faqs.question: Can we save money by using cheaper tutors for one of the three sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the rotation is partly designed around that. The shared-gap block and the subject currently being taught belong at the qualified band of roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, because they need somebody who knows the mark scheme. The subject being kept warm is practice rather than teaching, so the budget band of AED 33 to 65, or supervised self-study with the school's past papers, covers it adequately and the saving is real.

faqs.question: If June goes badly, can my child resit just one science?
faqs.answer: If they sit three separate sciences, yes, and it is the narrowest and cheapest fix available: the November series takes that one subject and leaves the other two alone. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, early enough for most sixth-form conversations. A student on a coordinated award has a harder decision, because the single grade carries all three subjects, so discuss that with the school before committing.

faqs.question: Which series does a Dubai Silicon Oasis science candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge candidates in the UAE sit the June series or the November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so no Dubai student sits it, and a plan built on a February entry deadline has imported another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, so take the actual timetable from the exams officer.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand biology and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Language precision. Biology mark schemes want the structure, the process and the consequence named, and an answer conveying general understanding without those three elements scores nothing. The student leaves the examination believing they answered the question. The repair is marked practice where the tutor reads the answer back and shows which clause earned nothing, repeated until the habit changes, which is why it belongs in steady weekly work rather than a burst.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three sciences for a coordinated entry?
faqs.answer: For a coordinated or combined award that is the right match, because the award is one grade and the requirement is breadth rather than depth in one subject. Ask specifically whether the tutor has taught 0653 or 0654 itself, not the three subjects separately, because the content map differs. For three separate sciences a single tutor across all three is usually weaker than a rotation using different people for the subject currently being taught.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor in Dubai Silicon Oasis need a MoHRE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no schedule of amounts is published. Since it is free, ask directly.

faqs.answer: Three error tallies that have moved, with the shared gap no longer appearing in any of them, and a student who can say which cause is costing marks in each subject. Possibly one subject finished and dropped from the rotation entirely, which is a success rather than a shortfall. No grade predictions, because nobody can honestly offer them, least of all across three subjects at once with a mock still to come.

intro.heading: Which science route is your child entered for, and why nobody told you
paragraphs: There is a question that should be asked before any science tutoring is arranged in Dubai South and almost never is. Is your child taking three separate sciences, a double award, or a single combined award? Those are different entries with different content lists, different paper structures and different numbers of grades at the end. A tutor given past papers from the wrong route will teach accurate science towards a paper the student will not sit, which is the commonest avoidable waste in IGCSE science support.

Schools make the entry decision, often in Year 9 or early Year 10, and communicate it in a sentence buried in an options booklet. Parents reasonably assume that science is science. It is not: Cambridge 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics are three separate syllabuses each with its own papers, while Combined Science and Co-ordinated Science reduce the content and restructure the examination. Checking which appears on your child's timetable takes a minute and determines everything that follows.

The second thing nobody mentions is Paper 6. In Cambridge sciences, the alternative to practical paper examines experimental skills on paper rather than in a laboratory: identifying variables, reading instruments, spotting sources of error, completing results tables and suggesting improvements. It carries real marks, its question types repeat across series, and it is reliably the last thing anyone revises because it does not feel like content. For a candidate who has worked hard and keeps underscoring, it is frequently the cheapest available improvement in the whole timetable.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script and the official mark scheme shared on screen, and diagrams and graphs drawn on a shared surface that is saved week to week. For the sciences that record matters: a graph axis unlabelled in week three and again in week nine is visible on the page rather than remembered as carelessness.

One factual note before the detail. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai, inspects schools annually and publishes the ratings. It does not accredit private tutors, and IB Gram holds no KHDA permit, approval or partnership and operates no UAE centre. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Ask to see it, then ask which syllabus codes they have taught and at which tier. The permit is a legal licence to teach privately in the UAE and says nothing about whether somebody has ever marked a Paper 6 script, which is the question that actually decides whether the hours will help your child.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-south.subjectsIntro: The components and topics a Dubai South science candidate needs work on, broken out by subject and by where marks actually go.

subjects.name: Biology 0610 theory papers
subjects.description: High recall volume, so marks come from structured note compression rather than rereading, and from command-term discipline. Describe, explain and suggest demand different answers, and writing a full explanation where describe was asked spends examination time without gaining credit. Transport, genetics and ecology reward diagram work.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620 theory papers
subjects.description: Mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables carry the widest spread of marks, and both are procedural enough to be learned in a compressed block. Ionic equations attempted without balancing charge score nothing. Organic chemistry at this level is nomenclature and reaction type rather than mechanism.

subjects.name: Physics 0625 theory papers
subjects.description: Unit prefixes and gradient interpretation account for a disproportionate share of losses. Questions asking a student to describe an experiment fail when the controlled variable is not named. Electricity questions fail on circuit reading: redrawing an awkward printed circuit before analysing it converts a hard question into a routine one.

subjects.name: Paper 6: alternative to practical
subjects.description: Examines experimental skills on paper. Candidates identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, read scales and instruments, complete results tables with correct headings and units, plot and interpret graphs, identify sources of error and suggest improvements. Question types repeat across series, which makes it the most efficient component to practise.

subjects.name: Qualitative analysis in chemistry
subjects.description: The flame tests, precipitate colours and gas tests that a candidate has to produce from memory or from the supplied tables. Pure recall with a fixed answer set, which makes it a reliable source of marks for anybody who drills it and a reliable loss for anybody who assumes it will come back on the day.

subjects.name: Graph work across the sciences
subjects.description: Axis labels with quantity and unit, sensible scales, a line of best fit through the spread rather than between endpoints, and gradients read with a large triangle. Each of these earns marks independently of the science, which makes graph technique one of the best uses of a session for a student who understands the content.

subjects.name: Required practicals and experiment description
subjects.description: Questions asking how an experiment would be carried out are marked on method rather than on outcome: named apparatus, the variable changed, the variables controlled, what is measured and how often. A student who answers in general terms loses marks that a structured four-line answer would have collected.

subjects.name: Calculations and significant figures
subjects.description: Not a topic but a marked skill across all three sciences. Early rounding in a multi-step calculation yields a final answer the mark scheme rejects. Carrying full precision through and rounding only the stated answer is a two-session habit that recovers marks on every paper the student sits.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: A reduced content list across the three sciences with its own paper structure, producing fewer grades than three separate entries. Students sometimes assume the grade ceiling is lower; it is the content coverage and the number of certificates that differ. Past papers from the separate sciences are not interchangeable with these.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel sciences 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1
subjects.description: Pearson's International GCSE sciences, used by some schools in this cluster. The content is broadly comparable to Cambridge and the question styles differ, with longer contextual stems and a different treatment of practical skills. A student transferring mid-course needs four sessions of adjustment rather than a term.

subjects.name: Command terms across the sciences
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate each demand a specific answer shape. Misreading the verb is the single commonest reason a competent candidate sits mid-band across all three sciences simultaneously, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions because the list is short and published.

subjects.name: Biology diagram and process questions
subjects.description: Questions on transport systems, the heart, the nephron and the eye reward a labelled diagram over a paragraph. Candidates who sketch before writing routinely outperform those who describe from memory, because the diagram enforces the order of the process and the order is where the marks sit.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-south.modesIntro: Four formats Dubai South families use for IGCSE science, chosen by how many subjects are in play and where in the two years the student is. All are live one-to-one video with a matched specialist.

modes.title: Single-subject weekly tuition
modes.description: One science, one session a week, with work set and marked. The right starting point when one of the three is clearly weaker than the others, which is the usual pattern rather than the exception. Adding a second science before the first is stable generally slows both.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes in a fixed weekly slot
Past papers from the correct board, tier and route
A short written note after each session naming the next target
Diagrams and graphs drawn on a shared surface and saved

modes.title: Two-science blocks with one specialist
modes.description: Common in Year 11 where weakness spans two sciences and the cause is shared, usually graph work, calculation discipline or command-term reading. One specialist who can see the common thread treats it once rather than twice, which is both cheaper and faster than two separate tutors treating two symptoms.
bullets: Two subjects, one tutor, alternating weeks or a split session
Shared diagnosis written down after the first fortnight
Graph and calculation technique treated once across both
Separate past-paper sets so each syllabus is respected

modes.title: Paper 6 technique blocks
modes.description: Four to six sessions on the alternative to practical paper alone, because its question types repeat across series and almost nobody drills them. For a student who understands the science and keeps underscoring, this is frequently the single cheapest improvement available in the whole examination timetable.
bullets: Variables, instruments and error sources worked through systematically
Results tables with correct headings and units practised repeatedly
Graph plotting and interpretation under timed conditions
Past Paper 6 questions marked against the official scheme

modes.title: Pre-series intensives
modes.description: Two or three sessions a week for four to six weeks before the June or November papers, built entirely on timed questions with no new content. The work is pacing, command words, mark-scheme vocabulary and the specific topics the student's own scripts show as weak across whichever sciences are being sat.
bullets: Every session anchored to a timed paper or section
Marked against the official scheme, wording compared line by line
Paper 6 included deliberately rather than if time allows
A written list of what still costs marks in each subject

sections.heading: Triple, double and combined: three different entries
paragraphs: This is the question that has to be settled first, because everything downstream depends on it. A triple award student takes Biology, Chemistry and Physics as three separate syllabuses, sits the full paper set for each, and receives three grades. A double award student takes a reduced combined content list, sits a different paper structure and receives two grades. A single combined award produces one grade from a further reduced content list.

The practical differences are not subtle. Content coverage differs, so a topic examined on 0625 Physics may simply not appear on the combined syllabus. Paper structure differs, so past papers from the separate sciences cannot be used to prepare a combined candidate. Timetable load differs sharply, which matters in Year 11 when three sciences each want revision hours from the same evenings. And the number of certificates differs, which can affect a post-16 entry requirement two years later.

Schools make this decision, usually in Year 9 or early Year 10, and typically on a mixture of the student's attainment and the school's timetable capacity. Families are rarely consulted in detail and frequently do not realise a choice was made. The first useful action for a Dubai South parent is to look at the child's timetable or last report and read the codes: three codes means three sciences, and anything else means a combined route.

There is one consequence worth raising early rather than at results. A combined science grade may not satisfy a sixth form's entry requirement for a science A Level or for a Higher Level Diploma science. If the student has any intention of a science or engineering route, getting that requirement in writing during Year 10 is the cheapest available insurance, because the entry route can sometimes still be changed at that point and cannot be changed later.

sections.heading: Paper 6: the component nobody revises
paragraphs: In Cambridge sciences the alternative to practical paper examines experimental skills on paper, and it is the most consistently neglected component in the whole science timetable. It does not feel like revision because there is no content to learn, which is exactly why it is cheap to improve: the question types repeat across series and a student who has worked through two past papers recognises nearly everything the third one asks.

What it actually asks is specific. Identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in a described experiment. Read a scale or instrument to the correct precision. Complete a results table with the quantity and unit in the heading. Plot points accurately, draw a line of best fit through the spread, read a gradient. Identify a source of error and distinguish it from a mistake. Suggest a practical improvement that addresses the error named rather than a general one.

Each of those is a learnable procedure with a predictable mark scheme, and each is awarded independently of whether the student understands the underlying science. A results table heading written as time rather than time in seconds loses the mark. A suggested improvement of being more careful loses the mark where naming a more precise instrument would have earned it. These are not deep failures; they are untaught conventions.

The reason this matters for a Dubai South family is arithmetic. A student taking triple award sits three of these papers. Four to six sessions of Paper 6 technique therefore pays into three subjects at once, which is a better return than the same hours spent on any single topic. For a candidate who understands the science and keeps scoring below expectation, it is usually the first place to look and almost never where anyone looks first.
bullets: Paper 6 question types repeat across series and reward recognition
Results table headings need the quantity and the unit to earn the mark
An improvement must address the named error, not urge more care
Triple award candidates sit three of these papers
Marks are awarded independently of understanding the science

sections.heading: Core against Extended across the three sciences
paragraphs: Cambridge sciences tier into Core and Extended, with Core capping the grade available and covering a reduced content list. Because science entries are made per subject, a student can be Extended in one science and Core in another, which happens more often than families realise and produces reports that look inconsistent when they are simply describing two different entries.

The decision rests with the school and is usually made in Year 10 on class performance. Over-entry and under-entry both cost marks. A student placed on Extended who cannot handle the calculation work will sit papers designed for somebody else; a student placed on Core who was always capable of Extended loses grades they could have had, and will never know, because the ceiling is invisible from inside.

Evidence is what reopens the conversation, and it has to be the right kind. A full timed Extended paper, sat under conditions and marked against the official scheme, is a document a subject lead can act on. The assertion that a child is capable is not. That is a specific, achievable goal for a term of Year 10 tutoring and it is the main reason Year 10 hours are worth more per hour than Year 11 hours in the sciences.

If the tier is discovered late, one question remains useful. The November series exists with a fresh entry, which means a student who hits a Core ceiling in June can be entered at Extended for November with an autumn term of properly aimed preparation behind them. That decision has to be made in the days after August results rather than in October, because the entry goes through the school months before the papers.

sections.heading: Where marks go in each science, specifically
paragraphs: The losses differ by subject and knowing which you are dealing with changes the plan. In Biology the volume of recall is the problem rather than the difficulty of any single idea, and the marks go on command-term discipline: describe, explain and suggest demand different answers, and writing the longest possible response to a two-mark question costs time the final question needs. Diagram-based process questions reward sketching before writing, because the diagram enforces the order of the process.

In Chemistry the spread sits in mole calculations and the qualitative analysis tables. Ionic equations attempted without balancing charge score nothing despite looking nearly right, which is a mechanical check that takes seconds and gets skipped. Early rounding in a multi-step calculation produces a final answer the scheme rejects even when the method was correct. Organic chemistry at this level is nomenclature and reaction type, which makes it one of the most recoverable topics in a short block.

In Physics the losses concentrate in unit prefixes, gradient interpretation and circuit reading. A correct calculation with a wrong power of ten is simply wrong. A question asking a student to describe an experiment fails when the controlled variable is never named. Electricity questions on deliberately awkward printed circuits are routine once the circuit is redrawn in a standard layout and hard if it is not, and the redrawing takes ninety seconds.

Across all three, command terms and graph technique are shared faults with a shared fix. That is why a student weak in two sciences is often better served by one specialist treating the common thread than by two tutors each addressing their own subject. The table collects the subject-specific traps so a student can audit their own marked scripts against the list, which is the first thing a session here does anyway.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel in the sciences
paragraphs: Schools in this cluster use both boards, sometimes differently across subjects, and the syllabus code on the timetable is the only reliable way to know. Cambridge sciences are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The content is broadly comparable at this level and the examination experience is not.

The clearest difference is practical assessment. Cambridge sets Paper 6, the alternative to practical, as a separate paper examining experimental skills on paper. Pearson integrates practical skills differently across its papers. That has a direct consequence for revision: a Cambridge candidate needs Paper 6 question practice as a discrete block, while a Pearson candidate needs practical-skills questions identified within the main papers instead.

The second difference is question style. Cambridge tends towards shorter, more compartmentalised questions. Pearson tends towards longer contextual stems where the science has to be extracted from a described situation before it can be applied. A candidate trained on one and examined on the other loses time on reading rather than on science, which is why a tutor must work from the correct board from the first session rather than discovering the mismatch in week four.

Series availability is the third. Cambridge runs June and November, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Neither offers a February or March series to UAE candidates; that one is for India only. Cambridge additionally allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable, so confirm the zone with the school.

sections.heading: Three sciences in one Year 11 timetable
paragraphs: A triple award candidate in Dubai South has a workload problem as well as a science problem, and treating only the second is why so many science plans fail. Three separate syllabuses each want revision hours, each has its own mock, and each has a Paper 6. Those demands land on the same evenings, and a plan that books three weekly sessions will usually collapse by half term because there is no time left for the independent practice that makes sessions work.

The arithmetic that helps is to find the shared faults. Command-term misreading, graph technique, calculation discipline and significant figures are faults that show up across all three sciences simultaneously. Treating them once, with one specialist, pays into three subjects. That converts what looks like a three-tutor problem into a one-tutor problem plus targeted subject work where a genuine content gap exists.

The second move is to sequence rather than parallelise. One science at a time, four to six weeks each, with the weakest first, works better than three in parallel at a third of the depth. It also produces a clearer diagnosis, because a student working on one subject's scripts with full attention reveals patterns that three simultaneous half-efforts obscure. Triple award candidates in this cluster who sequence generally finish the year ahead of those who parallelise.

The third is Paper 6. Four to six sessions on alternative to practical technique pays into all three subjects at once and is the single highest-leverage block available to a triple award candidate. It is also the easiest to justify to a reluctant student, because the work is procedural rather than conceptual and the improvement shows up quickly on past papers. The table sets out how a triple award year can be sequenced rather than spread thin.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tutoring costs in Dubai, and what three subjects imply
paragraphs: The published Dubai bands split by provider model rather than by subject, so the science-specific question is how many subjects are being bought. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33-52 an hour on Tutopiya and AED 45-65 on EdFlik, usually delivered by university students. Agencies with qualified subject tutors publish higher: Unitors lists IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200.

In-home provision sits apart. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour. TutorChase quotes AED 270 and BartyED reaches AED 650 for premium named tutors. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

For a triple award family the implication is straightforward: three weekly sessions at a specialist rate is a large commitment and usually the wrong shape anyway. Sequencing one subject at a time, with a Paper 6 and technique block paying into all three, costs considerably less than three parallel weekly sessions and produces more, because the hours concentrate rather than spread.

Published monthly packages illustrate the delivery-model difference clearly: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours. Most of that gap is the driving being paid for rather than better teaching. Every figure here belongs to the provider named; these are market bands rather than an IB Gram price list, and three of the most visible competitors in this market publish no price at all while two quote in US dollars.

sections.heading: Online delivery, and where it helps most in science
paragraphs: For IGCSE sciences the specialist pool is reasonably deep, so the online case rests less on access than it does for Higher Level Diploma subjects. Where it earns its keep instead is the working record. Diagrams, circuits, graphs and calculation chains drawn on a shared digital surface persist, which means an axis left unlabelled in week three and again in week nine is visible on the page rather than recalled as a general tendency to be careless.

The second advantage is scheduling, and for a triple award household it is decisive. A visiting tutor fits one session an evening. An online tutor fits several, which matters when two children in secondary school both need a slot, or when one child needs a science block and a maths block in the same week. Families in Discovery Gardens and Dubai Production City in particular find that the later start times their commute forces are easier to accommodate online.

Where in-home genuinely wins is a younger child who will not settle at a screen, and a parent's ability to observe from the next room. Both are real and both weigh less for a Year 11 candidate working through marked past papers, where the material is two documents best read side by side. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE at all, so there is nothing to soften in this comparison; independent in-home tutors operate in this part of Dubai if presence is the priority.

On availability, the honest position is that Biology, Chemistry and Physics at IGCSE are all reasonably well covered and a match usually takes a few days. Combined and Co-ordinated Science specifically is thinner, because fewer tutors have taught that paper structure, and a request can take longer. Where nobody suitable is free we say so and give a date rather than putting a separate-sciences tutor in front of a combined candidate with the wrong past papers.

process.title: Read the codes on the timetable
process.description: Three syllabus codes means three separate sciences; anything else means a combined route. Then note the board: 0610, 0620 and 0625 are Cambridge, while 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 are Pearson. Those two facts determine which past papers are usable, and getting them wrong wastes a term of accurate teaching.

process.title: Confirm the tier per subject
process.description: Science entries are made subject by subject, so a student can be Extended in one and Core in another. That produces reports that look inconsistent and are simply describing two entries. Each one needs confirming separately, because the tier caps the grade before revision begins.

process.title: Send marked scripts, including a Paper 6 if there is one
process.description: Theory scripts show whether losses are content, command terms, units or calculation discipline. A Paper 6 script shows something different and usually more fixable. If no scripts exist, the first session produces one from a timed section in the weakest subject.

process.title: Free trial lesson with the matched specialist
process.description: One full session at no charge and no card, taught by the person who would take the block. It returns a written diagnosis separating shared faults from subject-specific gaps, and a proposal for sequencing rather than parallelising if three sciences are in play. A wrong match is rematched.

process.title: Start with Paper 6 and the shared faults
process.description: For a triple award candidate, four to six sessions on alternative to practical technique and command-term discipline pays into three subjects at once. That is better value than any single-topic block, and it is also the easiest work to sustain because the improvement shows up quickly on past papers.

process.title: Sequence the subjects, do not spread them
process.description: One science at a time for four to six weeks, weakest first, beats three in parallel at a third of the depth. It produces a clearer diagnosis and leaves room for the independent practice that makes sessions work. Three parallel weekly sessions in Year 11 usually collapse by half term.

whyPoints.title: Matched to the route as well as the subject
whyPoints.description: Triple award, double award and combined science are different entries with different content and different papers, and past papers are not interchangeable between them. Confirming the route and the codes before the first session is what prevents a term of accurate teaching aimed at a paper the student will not sit.

whyPoints.title: Paper 6 treated as examinable content
whyPoints.description: The alternative to practical paper carries real marks, its question types repeat across series, and almost nobody drills it because it does not feel like revision. For a triple award candidate, a short block on it pays into three subjects at once, which is the best return per hour available in IGCSE science.

whyPoints.title: Shared faults treated once
whyPoints.description: Command-term misreading, graph technique, significant figures and calculation discipline appear across all three sciences at the same time. One specialist treating the common thread is faster and cheaper than three tutors each addressing their own symptom, and it is a diagnosis most plans never make.

whyPoints.title: Working that survives the term
whyPoints.description: Diagrams, circuits and graphs drawn on a shared digital surface persist, so an unlabelled axis recurring across six weeks becomes visible evidence rather than an impression of carelessness. Loose paper passed across a table does not survive the term and a tutor relying on memory treats a pattern as a one-off.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with sources, and the three-subject arithmetic
whyPoints.description: Every band here is attributed to the provider that published it, and set against what three parallel weekly sessions would actually cost. Sequencing is cheaper and more effective, which is a conclusion the published numbers support rather than a sales position.

whyPoints.title: No regulator claims and no UAE centre
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoE, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation or partnership and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Regulators appear here because explaining what they do helps a parent decide, not because the names lend us anything we do not hold.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child takes triple or combined science?
faqs.answer: Read the syllabus codes on the timetable or the last report. Three codes, such as 0610, 0620 and 0625, means three separate sciences and three grades. A single combined code means a reduced content list with its own paper structure and either one or two grades depending on the award. Schools usually make this decision in Year 9 or early Year 10 on a mixture of attainment and timetable capacity, and communicate it in one line of an options booklet, so most parents have never been told explicitly.

faqs.question: What is Paper 6 in Cambridge IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: It is the alternative to practical paper, examining experimental skills on paper rather than in a laboratory. Candidates identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, read instruments to the correct precision, complete results tables with quantity and unit in the headings, plot and interpret graphs, identify sources of error and suggest improvements that address the named error. The question types repeat across series, so working through two past papers makes most of a third recognisable. It is the single most neglected component in the science timetable.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose Paper 6 marks on questions with no science in them?
faqs.answer: Because the paper marks conventions the student was never taught. A results table heading written as time rather than time in seconds loses the mark. A suggested improvement of being more careful loses the mark where naming a more precise instrument would have earned it. A line of best fit drawn between the first and last points rather than through the spread loses the mark. None of these requires understanding the experiment, which is why four to six sessions of technique work moves the score so reliably.

faqs.question: Can my child be Extended in one science and Core in another?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it happens more often than families realise, because science entries are made subject by subject. That produces a report which looks inconsistent and is actually describing two different entries with two different grade ceilings. Each subject's tier therefore needs confirming separately before a plan is written, because the tier caps the achievable grade before any revision begins. A timed Extended paper marked against the official scheme is the evidence that reopens a conservative entry in Year 10.

faqs.question: Does combined science close off A Level or IB sciences later?
faqs.answer: It can, and that consequence is set two years before anyone notices it. Sixth forms set their own entry requirements for science A Levels and for Higher Level Diploma sciences, and a combined award grade may not satisfy them even when the grade itself looks respectable. The practical step is to get the requirement in writing from the intended sixth form during Year 10, while the entry route can sometimes still be changed. After the entry deadline it cannot, and the conversation becomes about alternatives instead.

faqs.question: Should a triple award student in Dubai South have three weekly sessions?
faqs.answer: Almost never. Three parallel weekly sessions leave no room for the independent practice that makes sessions work, and in this cluster such plans generally collapse by half term because three sciences, maths and everything else are competing for the same evenings. Sequencing works better: one science at a time for four to six weeks, weakest first, preceded by a Paper 6 and command-term block that pays into all three subjects simultaneously. It is cheaper and it produces a clearer diagnosis.

faqs.question: What are the shared faults across the three IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Four of them, and they appear simultaneously. Misreading the command term, so that describe, explain and suggest get the wrong answer shape. Graph technique, where axis labels, scales, lines of best fit and gradient triangles each earn marks independently of the science. Significant figures and early rounding, which destroy accuracy marks in correct methods. And answer length mismatched to the mark tariff, which spends time the final question needed. One specialist can treat all four once across three subjects.

faqs.question: Which board do schools near Dubai South use for sciences?
faqs.answer: Both, and sometimes differently across subjects within one school, so there is no safe generalisation by neighbourhood. Cambridge sciences are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The clearest practical difference is practical assessment: Cambridge sets Paper 6 as a separate paper, while Pearson integrates those skills across its papers. Check the code on the timetable, because it determines which past papers are usable from the first session.

faqs.question: Is there a February or March science exam series for UAE students?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative timetable zones, each with its own version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. Confirm the zone and the final timetable with the school rather than relying on any restated dates.

faqs.question: Why do ionic equations score nothing when they look nearly right?
faqs.answer: Because an equation that balances atoms but not charge is not valid, and the mark scheme treats it as wrong rather than as partially right. Students lose these marks under time pressure rather than through ignorance: the charge check takes a few seconds and gets skipped. The fix is building the check into the writing habit rather than leaving it as a final review that never happens, and that takes about one session to establish. The same discipline applies to half-equations in the redox work.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a Dubai South address?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Dubai South students are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with the marked script and official mark scheme on screen and diagrams, circuits and graphs drawn on a shared surface that is saved week to week. For the sciences that record is a real advantage, because a recurring graph or unit habit becomes visible rather than remembered differently by two people.

faqs.question: How many marks does circuit redrawing actually save in physics?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter on any paper with a series-parallel question. Examiners draw circuits that are deliberately awkward to read, and candidates who analyse the printed diagram as given will combine the wrong resistors and then carry that error through every subsequent part of the question. Redrawing in a standard layout before any calculation takes around ninety seconds and turns a hard question into a routine one. It is a habit rather than a skill, which means it can be established in two or three sessions.

faqs.question: What should a Year 10 science plan in Dubai South aim at?
faqs.answer: Two things. First, the shared technique faults: command terms, graph work, significant figures and answer length, because fixing them pays into every science simultaneously and the gains persist. Second, a timed Extended paper in any subject where the entry tier looks conservative, because that script is the evidence a subject lead can act on while the entry deadline is still ahead. By the spring of Year 11 the tiers are settled and the same hours buy less than they would have.

faqs.question: Is Combined Science harder to find a tutor for?
faqs.answer: Slightly, and it is worth knowing in advance. Fewer tutors have taught the combined paper structure, because most have worked with the separate sciences, and the past papers are not interchangeable. A separate-sciences specialist given a combined candidate will set questions on content that is not on the syllabus, which wastes sessions and shakes confidence. Where no suitable tutor is free we say so and give a date rather than making the substitution, which is the honest version of a limit most providers do not publish.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE science tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published bands split by provider model. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33-52 on Tutopiya and AED 45-65 on EdFlik. Agencies with qualified subject tutors publish higher, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, and independent home tutors are quoted up to AED 500 once travel is in the hour. For a triple award family the useful calculation is not the hourly rate but whether the plan sequences subjects or runs three in parallel. These are market bands, not IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: What time can science sessions start in Dubai South on a school night?
faqs.answer: About 16:30 for most households, because school runs ending in Dubai Investments Park put families home between 16:00 and 16:30. Green Community families can manage 16:00 since the school is minutes away, while Dubai Production City households driving to Motor City or Sports City are closer to 17:30. Science immediately after a commute produces less than science at 18:00 after a break, so the slot worth booking is the one your child can concentrate in rather than the earliest one available.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubai-sport.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE sciences to students across Sports City, Victory Heights and the Dubailand communities. A triple-science student usually works with two specialists on separate evenings rather than one tutor across all three subjects.

intro.heading: Three sciences, three completely different problems
paragraphs: Parents in Dubai Sports City tend to describe this as a single problem. Science is going badly, a tutor is needed, and the subject is treated as one thing. In the papers it is three things with almost nothing in common except the word on the timetable, and a block that treats them as interchangeable spends its time in the wrong place for at least two of the three.

Biology is a terminology and data subject. Mark schemes list the accepted words and reject near-synonyms, so a student who understands osmosis perfectly and describes it without mentioning a partially permeable membrane scores lower than they expect. The content volume is the largest of the three, and the technique that recovers marks is precision in language and care in reading graphs and tables.

Chemistry is a layout subject. Three calculation families carry most of the numerical marks — moles from mass, moles from concentration and volume, and yield or purity — and the scheme awards method marks for the structure of the working rather than for the number alone. A student who computes in their head loses marks they have earned, and ionic equations lose marks for unbalanced charge as often as unbalanced mass.

Physics is an explanation subject with algebra underneath. 'Explain why the lamp dims' wants a chain — resistance rises, current falls, power falls — and a correct formula earns nothing. Underneath that sits rearrangement, which is where most physics difficulty actually lives: a student who cannot make a quantity the subject of an equation stalls identically in motion, circuits and thermal physics.

On top of those three sits a structural question most families have not resolved: which route is the student on. Three separate sciences, a double award, or a single combined award are different entries with different papers and different progression consequences at 16. The answer is on the school's subject information sheet and it changes what a tutoring plan should aim at.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition live, one to one and online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a Sports City address, and in-home visiting is a service offered only in India. The practical consequence for a triple-science student is that each subject can be matched to a specialist in that syllabus, on separate evenings, rather than to one person who teaches the nearest approximation to all three.

What follows is the structure: the routes and their codes, how practical work is examined, where each science withholds marks, the shared mathematics behind all three, and what it costs to support two or three sciences at once rather than one. The section on the first three weeks is the one to read if money is limited, because it names the single highest-return intervention for each subject separately and they are not the same intervention.

subjects.name: Data and graph questions

subjects.name: Quantitative skills across the sciences
subjects.description: Rearrangement, ratio, percentages, standard form and significant figures. The same skill set appears in all three sciences and in mathematics, which is why a student stalling at the same step in four subjects has one problem rather than four.

subjects.name: Extended-response questions

sections.heading: What this search returns, and what is actually provided
paragraphs: An IGCSE science tutor in Dubai Sports City means one-to-one teaching in one or more of biology, chemistry and physics, arranged outside school for a student in or around the Sports City master plan. IB Gram provides that live online over video in Gulf Standard Time. No tutor is sent to a UAE address; in-home visiting is a service offered only in India, and that is stated here rather than discovered after a deposit.

The first useful thing a provider can do is refuse to treat 'science' as one subject. A request for science help has to be resolved into which science, which syllabus code, and which tier before anything sensible can be planned. The three subjects fail for different reasons, respond to different work, and are marked by schemes with different habits, so a single tutor covering all three at once will be strong in one and adequate in two.

The second is to look for the shared cause. Where a student is losing marks across all three sciences, the explanation is often not three subject weaknesses but one skill gap showing up three times: rearrangement, unit handling, command terms, or data questions answered without specific figures. Fixing that once pays in three subjects, and it is a cheaper and shorter block than three subject blocks in sequence.

What is on offer, then, is a diagnostic first and a subject block second. A marked paper from each science, read together, usually shows the pattern within one session. Where the pattern is shared, the first block is a shared-skills block. Where it is genuinely subject-specific, the block is matched to the code and the tier, and where no specialist is free for that code the answer is a stated wait rather than a substitution.

sections.heading: Triple, double award or single combined: which route is it
paragraphs: Before any teaching, establish the route. Three separate sciences gives three IGCSEs with three grades and the fullest content. Cambridge Coordinated Science 0654 is a double award with less content per discipline. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 is a single award covering all three with the least content. Pearson runs equivalent separate and double-award routes. The school makes this decision, usually in Year 9 or early Year 10.

The routes differ in more than volume. On the combined and coordinated routes the papers mix disciplines, which changes how revision has to be organised: by paper rather than by science, because a student working through biology in isolation will be surprised by the order questions arrive in. On the separate routes each paper stays within its subject, and revision by subject works.

The consequence that matters most arrives at 16. Entry to an A Level or IB Higher Level science from a single combined award is not automatic, and requirements are set by the receiving school rather than by the board. A student in Sports City intending to take Higher Level chemistry should have checked this in Year 10, because by Year 11 the entry has been made and the content covered is what it is.

The tier question sits on top of all of this. Cambridge tiers each science into Core and Extended, and Core caps the grade available. A student on Core aiming at a post-16 science has two constraints rather than one, and both are decided before the papers. The table sets the routes side by side with the question to ask about each.

sections.heading: How practical work is examined
paragraphs: Every science enquiry eventually asks about practicals, usually in the form of whether online tuition can cover them. The answer requires separating two different things that share a name. The laboratory is the school's work: handling apparatus, taking readings under supervision, and watching an experiment misbehave are experiences a tutor cannot supply in any format.

What is examined, though, is the written craft around practical work, and Cambridge sciences carry a practical component with an alternative-to-practical option precisely because those skills can be assessed on paper. The question styles are distinctive and consistent: which variable should be controlled and why, which apparatus and what precision, how to tabulate results with units in the column heading, which point is anomalous, and what is wrong with the method as described.

Each of those has a correct form that can be taught and drilled. Tables need units in headings rather than beside every value. Anomalies need identifying and then addressing, not ignoring. Method criticisms need to name the variable that was not controlled rather than saying the experiment was inaccurate. None of this requires apparatus to practise, and all of it is assessed every series.

Pearson handles the same skills within its own paper structure, which is a further reason the code matters more than the board name. A student drilled on one board's practical question style and entered for the other knows the science and misreads the task, and in a mock report that reads as carelessness. The division of labour to state plainly: the school supplies the bench, the tutor supplies the written technique, and the marks are awarded for the second.

sections.heading: Three sciences, three different fixes
paragraphs: The most useful thing on this page is the recognition that the three sciences need different first weeks. A tutor who opens every block the same way is working from a template rather than from the paper. What follows is the standard first intervention for each, drawn from the reasons the schemes withhold marks.

Biology first. The fix is vocabulary built from past mark schemes rather than from a textbook. Collect the accepted terms for the topics being examined and drill them, because the scheme rejects near-synonyms and the student has no way of knowing which words count. Alongside that, data questions: quote the figure, give the unit, name the trend with reference to specific values.

Chemistry second. The fix is calculation layout. Write the relationship, substitute with units, evaluate, round once at the end. Three calculation families cover most of the numerical marks and each can be installed as a template in two or three weeks. Then charge balancing in ionic equations, which is a two-second check that is never performed because nobody has told the student to perform it.

Physics third. The fix is the three-clause explanation: cause, mechanism, effect, written as linked clauses rather than as a conclusion alone. After that, unit conversion before substitution and direction on every vector answer. If the same algebraic step fails in motion, circuits and thermal physics, the real block is rearrangement, and the physics content is not the place to start.

sections.heading: The mathematics all three sciences assume
paragraphs: A student who is losing marks in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously usually has one problem rather than three, and it is quantitative. Rearrangement, ratio and proportion, percentages, standard form and significant figures run through all three subjects and through mathematics as well. When the same step fails in four subjects, treating it as four subject weaknesses is an expensive mistake.

The diagnostic takes twenty minutes and no specialist knowledge. Ask the student to make a named quantity the subject of three formulae, convert between units in two directions, and express two values in standard form. Watch for hesitation rather than for wrong answers: a student who arrives at the right result slowly in a quiet room will not arrive at it inside a timed paper with six other questions waiting.

Where that diagnostic fails, the first block should be quantitative, taught through science problems rather than as abstract algebra so the transfer is immediate. It is slower work than topic revision and it does not produce a visible change in the first fortnight, which is why families resist it and why providers rarely propose it. It is also the only version that lifts three subjects at once.

The corollary is worth saying for planning purposes. A triple-science student with weak quantitative skills should not be booked for three subject blocks. One shared block, then the weakest single science, is both cheaper and more effective. Families who book three tutors in a panic after a Year 11 mock usually discover this in February, having spent the money that would have funded it.

sections.heading: Which science to drop, and when that is reasonable
paragraphs: A fair number of enquiries from Arabian Ranches and Victory Heights are really asking whether a triple-science student should be carrying three sciences at all. It is a reasonable question, and the honest answer depends on the intended post-16 route rather than on current difficulty alone.

Where a student intends to take two sciences at A Level or Higher Level, three at IGCSE is the standard preparation and dropping one narrows options at 16. Where they intend to take none, three sciences is a workload decision with little return, and a double award can free real time for subjects that will matter more. Where the intention is unknown, which is common in Year 10, the safer choice is to keep options open and manage the load.

If a change is being considered, the timing matters as much as the decision. Routes and tiers are fixed at the entry deadline, which sits months before the papers, and after that point the question is academic. A conversation with the head of science in the first half of Year 10 is a decision; the same conversation in the spring of Year 11 is a complaint about something that can no longer change for that series.

The middle path is often better than either extreme. A student struggling with all three but needing science at 16 is usually better served by a shared-skills block and a double award than by three separate entries half-prepared. That recommendation costs a provider three subject blocks, which may be why it is rarely the recommendation a family receives.

sections.heading: What two or three sciences cost to support
paragraphs: Supporting one science and supporting three are different financial propositions, and families frequently commit to the second while pricing the first. The published hourly bands in this market are these. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the university-student end. Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate places specialists at AED 200 to 450 and beyond, and BartyED publishes AED 650 for premium named tutors.

In-home visiting is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and AED 200 to 500 by independent home tutors once travel is counted. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with local packages advertised around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. All of these figures are provider-published and were read in October 2026; none is IB Gram's price list.

Multiply the mid band by three subjects weekly and the monthly figure becomes a significant household decision rather than an incidental one. That is the arithmetic that makes the shared-skills block worth considering first: one weekly session addressing rearrangement, command terms and data questions costs a third of three subject blocks and can move marks in all three papers.

The sequencing advice follows from that. Diagnose first, buy the shared block if the pattern is shared, then buy the single weakest science. Add a second science only if the first block has demonstrably worked. Families who start with three tutors rarely review any of them, because reviewing three blocks at once is harder than letting all three run, and that is how a term disappears.

sections.heading: Entries, series and the regulator
paragraphs: Two administrative facts bound every science revision plan in Dubai. The first is the entry: which board, which route, which codes and which tier, all decided by the school. The second is the entry deadline, which closes months before the papers and after which the route and tier are fixed for that series.

With Cambridge there is a third administrative fact, and it is the one that costs papers. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones; Cambridge states that using the correct zone timetable is essential and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version. For a triple-science student sitting six or nine papers, a wrong-zone timetable is six or nine chances to be in the wrong place. The series themselves are straightforward: Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai Sports City candidate plans around June and treats November as the resit route.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. In the most recent completed cycles, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only version worth planning from.

On the school side, Dubai's private schools are overseen by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. ADEK covers Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority covers Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside the licensed curriculum, so the examined timetable is not the whole timetable.

sections.heading: Permits and the claims this page does not make
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

Examiner language is where science tutoring advertising strays furthest, so the rule here is explicit: no tutor is described as an examiner without evidence of current status, and examiner status is never presented as access to marking, to grade boundaries or to paper content, because it is not. Someone who has marked Paper 4 can tell your child what a mark scheme rewards in an extended-response answer. Nobody can tell you where this series' boundaries will fall. On our own standing: IB Gram holds no Cambridge, Pearson, International Baccalaureate, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education approval or accreditation, claims none, and operates no office or centre anywhere in the UAE.

Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes are referenced and linked at their official sources rather than reproduced or supplied. They belong to the boards, and for unreleased material reproduction is a more serious matter than copyright. A provider offering a library of board documents as downloads is doing something a family should be cautious about rather than impressed by.

Finally, no success statistic appears anywhere on this page. A percentage without a sample size, a date and a method cannot be checked by the reader and therefore proves nothing, however good it looks on a landing page. What can be offered instead is a stated target per block, a written review at four sessions, and an honest answer when the target has not moved.
