process.title: Send the codes, the route and a marked paper from each
process.description: 'Cambridge 0620 and 0625 Extended, Year 11, mocks 5 and 4' is answerable. Marked papers from two sciences read side by side usually show within one session whether the cause is shared or subject-specific, which decides the whole plan.

process.title: Check for a shared cause first
process.description: Twenty minutes of rearrangement, unit conversion and standard form, plus a look at how data questions were answered. Where the same step fails across sciences, the first block is shared-skills work rather than three subject blocks, which is both cheaper and faster.

process.title: Buy one block, not three
process.description: The weakest single science, or the shared block, with a stated target. Adding a second science only once the first has demonstrably moved. Families who start with three tutors rarely review any of them, and three unreviewed blocks is how a term disappears.

process.title: Weekly timed work, self-marked
process.description: Questions are set from past papers and marked by the student against the official scheme during the session, with every withheld mark named. The error log is kept across weeks so a repeated category — units, synonyms, charge balance — becomes visible rather than re-explained.

process.title: Review at four sessions
process.description: The target is measured in writing. If the categories in the error log have not changed, the diagnosis, the tutor or the frequency changes, at no cost. In a Year 11 science timetable, catching that at week four rather than week eight is a month of an exam year recovered.

whyPoints.title: Three sciences treated as three problems
whyPoints.description: Biology loses marks to rejected near-synonyms, chemistry to calculation layout, physics to explanations written as formulae. A tutor who opens every block the same way is working from a template. The first weeks differ by subject because the schemes withhold marks for different reasons.

whyPoints.title: The shared cause looked for first
whyPoints.description: Losses across all three sciences are often one quantitative gap appearing three times. Diagnosing that before buying three subject blocks saves two of them, and a single shared-skills block can move marks on three papers at once. It is slower to show and cheaper overall.

whyPoints.title: Route and tier established before teaching
whyPoints.description: Separate sciences, a double award and a single combined award are different entries with different papers and different progression at 16. Core entries cap the grade. Both are fixed at the entry deadline, so the conversation is useful in Year 10 and academic in Year 11.

whyPoints.title: Practical skills taught where the marks are
whyPoints.description: The laboratory is the school's work; the marks are awarded for variable control, apparatus and precision choice, tabulation, anomalies and method criticism. All of that is written technique, drilled on screen with real past-paper data rather than with apparatus.

whyPoints.title: Honest sequencing advice
whyPoints.description: A student struggling with all three sciences but needing science at 16 is often better served by a shared block and a double award than by three thin entries. That recommendation costs a provider two subject blocks, which is probably why it is rarely offered.

whyPoints.title: Delivery, rates and limits stated
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live, one-to-one and online in Gulf Standard Time; no tutor is sent to a UAE address and home visiting runs only in India. Every AED figure names its source and the month it was read, and no accreditation, examiner status or outcome is claimed.

faqs.question: Does my child need one science tutor or three?
faqs.answer: Usually one, and often not the one you would expect. Where marks are falling across biology, chemistry and physics at once, the cause is frequently a single quantitative gap — rearrangement, unit handling, significant figures — appearing three times. A shared-skills block addresses that in one weekly session rather than three. Where the losses are genuinely confined to one subject, a single specialist in that syllabus is the right purchase. Booking three tutors before diagnosing is how a term and a budget disappear together.

faqs.question: Is my child on triple, double award or combined science?
faqs.answer: Check the school's subject information sheet and the codes on past papers. Three separate sciences means Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, giving three grades. Cambridge Coordinated Science 0654 is a double award; Combined Science 0653 is a single award with the least content. The difference matters for revision organisation and, more importantly, for progression at 16, since entry to an A Level or Higher Level science from a single combined award is not automatic.

faqs.question: Why does biology lose marks when my child clearly understands it?
faqs.answer: Because mark schemes in biology list accepted terms and reject near-synonyms. Describing osmosis without a partially permeable membrane, or diffusion without a concentration gradient, scores lower than the student expects however sound the understanding. The fix is a vocabulary list built from past mark schemes rather than from a textbook, drilled until the accepted terms arrive automatically. Alongside that, data questions need figures quoted with units and trends described against specific values rather than in general terms.

faqs.question: Which practical skills are actually examined on the Cambridge science papers?
faqs.answer: The examined skills are written: which variable to control and why, which apparatus and what precision, how to tabulate results with units in the column headings, which point is anomalous, and what is wrong with a described method. Cambridge offers an alternative-to-practical route, and all those techniques can be drilled on screen with real past-paper data. Handling apparatus in a school laboratory remains the school's part of the work and is not something any tutor supplies.

faqs.question: Should a Sports City student drop one of the three sciences?
faqs.answer: It depends on the post-16 intention rather than on current difficulty. Two sciences at A Level or Higher Level means keeping three at IGCSE where possible. No science at 16 makes a double award a reasonable workload decision. Unknown intention in Year 10 argues for keeping options open and managing the load with a shared-skills block. Whatever the answer, routes and tiers are fixed at the entry deadline, so the conversation belongs in the first half of Year 10.

faqs.question: What is the quickest mark recovery in IGCSE chemistry?
faqs.answer: Calculation layout. Write the relationship, substitute with units, evaluate, then round once at the end. Method marks are awarded for that structure rather than for the answer alone, so a student who computes mentally loses marks they have earned. Three calculation families — moles from mass, moles from concentration and volume, and yield or purity — cover most of the numerical marks and install as templates in two or three weeks. Charge balance on ionic equations is the next cheapest.

faqs.question: Why are physics explanation questions marked so harshly?
faqs.answer: They are not marked harshly; they are marked for a specific thing. 'Explain why the lamp dims' wants a chain of consequence in words — resistance rises, current falls, power falls — and a correct formula earns nothing because the question did not ask for algebra. Writing three linked clauses instead of a single conclusion is a habit rather than an insight, and it transfers to every topic in the subject within two or three weeks of deliberate practice.

faqs.question: How do I test whether the real problem is maths rather than science?
faqs.answer: Twenty minutes, no specialist knowledge needed. Ask the student to make a named quantity the subject of three formulae, convert units in two directions, and write two values in standard form. Watch for hesitation rather than for wrong answers, because a student who gets there slowly in a quiet room will not get there inside a timed paper. If the hesitation is consistent, the first block should be quantitative, taught through science problems rather than as abstract algebra.

faqs.question: Does revision for Combined Science work differently?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this catches families out. On Combined and Coordinated Science the papers mix disciplines, so a question on energy may be followed by one on cells. A student who revises biology to completion, then chemistry, then physics, is unprepared for the order in which questions actually arrive. Revision has to be organised around paper structure rather than around subject, which usually means mixed practice sets from the start rather than at the end.

faqs.question: Which command terms matter most in science papers?
faqs.answer: Describe, explain, suggest, compare, calculate and state carry most of the traffic, and each is defined and enforced in marking. 'Describe' answered with an explanation wastes time that was needed elsewhere; 'explain' answered with a description scores nothing at all. 'Suggest' invites a reasoned possibility rather than a recalled fact, which students find counter-intuitive. Learning the handful that recur in a student's own papers is a two-week job with returns in all three sciences simultaneously.

faqs.question: How many sessions does a single science block usually need?
faqs.answer: Four to six if the losses are mechanical — terminology, layout, units, command terms — because those are habits and habits change in weeks. Around eight if one or two topics are genuinely absent and need drilling against past questions. One to two terms if the underlying problem is quantitative, because fluency is built with short frequent practice rather than taught in a lesson. Anyone quoting a session count before reading a marked paper is guessing at the diagnosis.

faqs.question: What does science tuition cost for a triple-science student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published hourly rates run from roughly AED 33 to 65 at the university-student end, where Tutopiya and EdFlik advertise, to AED 150 to 300 for qualified online subject teaching, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly hour sessions are AED 240 to 600, AED 600 to 1,200 and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more by tier. Multiply by three subjects before committing.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach biology, chemistry and physics properly?
faqs.answer: One tutor can teach all three competently at Core level and will usually be strong in one and adequate in two at Extended. The three subjects are marked by schemes with different habits and fail for different reasons, so depth matters where the marks are tight. The arrangement used here is a specialist per syllabus on separate evenings, which also keeps the homework load spread rather than landing two sets on one night.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting science tutoring in Year 10 rather than Year 11?
faqs.answer: Yes, for two reasons. The tier and route conversations are still open in Year 10 and closed in Year 11, so a diagnostic that shows whether Extended entry is realistic is actionable at that point. And mechanical habits — terminology, layout, command terms, units — are cheaper to build before a student has spent two years practising the alternatives. A four to six session block in Year 10 regularly removes the need for an intensive a year later.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubailand.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach International GCSE sciences to students across the Dubailand communities. Each profile names the board and the subjects, because a Cambridge 0620 chemistry specialist and a Pearson 4CH1 specialist prepare students for differently structured papers.

intro.heading: Does anyone near Dubailand know which science award your child is taking?
paragraphs: The honest version of this search is narrower than it looks. A parent in Motor City or Arabian Ranches wants a competent science tutor nearby. What the student actually needs is somebody who knows which of three quite different routes they are entered for, because International GCSE science is not one qualification. There are three separate sciences taken as individual subjects, a coordinated award covering all three with reduced content, and a combined award reducing it further. The three routes examine different material, and a tutor who does not establish which one applies will teach content the student will never be examined on.

Then there is the board. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel both award International GCSE sciences, with codes such as Cambridge 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics and 0610 Biology against Pearson 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1, and Cambridge coordinated and combined awards carrying codes 0654 and 0653. Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended with the tier set at entry; Pearson generally examines a single tier in the sciences. Question styles and command-term habits differ enough that generic worksheets waste a share of every paid hour.

This is where a proximity search fails a science family specifically. Three sciences means three sets of specialist knowledge, and the tutor who covers all three well at Extended tier is rarer than the tutor who covers one. Dubailand compounds it: the belt is a development zone running south-east along Al Ain Road and Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road, taking in Arabian Ranches and its two later phases, Motor City, Dubai Sports City, DAMAC Hills, Town Square, Mudon and Remraam. Two households both calling themselves Dubailand residents can be twenty-five minutes apart, so insisting a specialist lives close by narrows an already thin pool.

There is a cheap way to test a tutor before committing. Ask which award and code they have taught most recently. Ask what the student is examined on in place of a laboratory practical. Ask which topic in the student's award has been removed compared with the separate sciences. Somebody who has taught the specification answers all three without hesitation. Somebody who has not will talk about confidence and revision, which is the same answer for any subject.

IB Gram's own position is stated plainly rather than implied. We do not send a tutor to a Dubailand address; home visits are a service we operate only in India. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, matched on board, award and tier, with a free trial session first and no card required. What follows is the detail a parent needs: how the three routes differ, how the two boards differ, where science marks actually go, how practical assessment works on paper, and what the market charges.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubailand.subjectsIntro: Science marks go missing in identifiable places, and the places differ by discipline. These are the areas Dubailand students most often need rebuilt across the three sciences.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and exchange systems
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, circulation and gas exchange. Content-heavy and vocabulary-dependent, and the loss is structural: a student can recall the process and still score two of six because the answer is not organised the way the markscheme reads.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares, variation and selection. Marks are lost on genetic diagrams that omit gametes or parental genotypes, which is a presentation habit rather than a knowledge gap and closes in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Mass, moles, concentration and limiting reagents. The quantitative foundation the rest of chemistry rests on, so a gap here resurfaces in electrolysis, energetics and titration questions. Usually four or five sessions to secure.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and reactivity
subjects.description: Half equations, products at each electrode and reactivity series reasoning. Half equations unbalanced for charge are the standard loss, along with equations that balance but omit the state symbols the markscheme requires.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and rates
subjects.description: Homologous series, functional groups and rate experiments. Students describe a rate change without reference to collision frequency or activation energy, which is exactly what the explanation marks are for.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance and circuit analysis. Jointly with forces this is where the largest share of physics marks sits, and losses come from circuits worked from the formula sheet rather than redrawn properly.

subjects.name: Physics: forces and motion
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws and moments. Taught early and depended on afterwards. The reliable loss is a question attempted without the diagram that would have made it straightforward.

subjects.name: Physics: waves, energy and radioactivity
subjects.description: Reflection and refraction, energy transfer and decay. Content-light on calculation and heavy on precise description, so it rewards organised notes and exact vocabulary rather than extra problem practice.

subjects.name: Practical skills on paper
subjects.description: Variables, method criticism, scale reading, data processing, reliability and improvement. Examined through written questions across all three sciences, and the most reliably recoverable block in the whole qualification.

sections.heading: Separate, coordinated or combined: find out before paying for anything
paragraphs: This is the first question and most families cannot answer it with certainty, because schools describe the routes inconsistently in reports and option booklets. The answer sits with the examinations officer, and it comes in two parts: which award, and which syllabus code. Those two facts determine what is in scope, and therefore what every paid hour should be spent on.

The three routes reduce content in different proportions. Separate sciences carry the full specification in each discipline. A coordinated double award covers all three with content removed from each, and a combined single award removes more again. The removals are not uniform: a topic trimmed from chemistry in the coordinated award may be retained in biology, and the pattern differs between boards. A student revising a removed topic is spending time they do not have on marks that do not exist.

That is the specific waste this page is trying to prevent, and it is common. A family buys a well-reviewed separate-science revision resource, the student works diligently through it, and a meaningful share of the effort goes to content outside their award. Worse, the student concludes they are bad at science when in fact they were studying a harder qualification than the one they are entered for.

The table below sets out the three routes and what each one changes for a tutoring plan. Take it to the conversation with the school rather than treating it as an answer in itself, because the school's entry record is the authoritative document.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: codes, tiers and why generic material underperforms
paragraphs: Once the award is known, the board and the code follow. Cambridge science codes include 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0654 Coordinated Sciences and 0653 Combined Science. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses 4BI1 Biology, 4CH1 Chemistry and 4PH1 Physics among others. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole competing area-page cluster researched for this project, which is a fair measure of how rarely anyone in this market asks.

Cambridge tiers several subjects into Core and Extended, with the tier set at entry by the school. Core papers lead to grades C to G and Extended papers to A* to E, so the tier fixes a ceiling that no amount of tutoring can lift once entries close. Pearson generally examines a single tier in the sciences, which removes that particular risk and replaces it with a different planning question about the appropriate depth of preparation.

Why the code matters practically is question style. Cambridge and Pearson phrase questions differently, weight their command terms slightly differently, and present data questions in distinct formats. A student drilled on the wrong board's past questions arrives at the paper with the right knowledge and an unfamiliar interface, which costs time and confidence in the first ten minutes. Board-specific practice is not a refinement; it is the difference between prepared and nearly prepared.

One Cambridge administrative detail is worth checking and costs nothing. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Ask the examinations officer which zone your centre sits in before building a revision calendar from a timetable found online.

sections.heading: Where International GCSE science marks actually go
paragraphs: Across all three sciences the losses follow a small number of patterns, and almost none of them are failures of understanding. That is genuinely good news for a parent, because habits change faster than knowledge gaps close, and a diagnostic with marked work in front of both people identifies the pattern in a single session.

The first and largest is answer structure on longer questions. A six-mark question has a shape, and a student who writes everything they know about the topic in prose collects a fraction of the available credit. The second is command-term confusion: describe, explain, suggest and evaluate ask for different things, and answering one as another either wastes time or loses marks. The third is diagrams never drawn, which in physics means free-body diagrams and redrawn circuits, in chemistry means apparatus and in biology means genetic diagrams with gametes shown.

The fourth is quantitative discipline: units, significant figures and the arithmetic of percentage change. The fifth is the practical paper, where students who have done the laboratory work still cannot state a controlled variable precisely or criticise a method, because those are written skills nobody taught them explicitly. The sixth is timing, which is not a topic and cannot be revised, only drilled on the correct board's papers.

None of these is addressed by covering the syllabus again, which is the only plan a tutor can offer without seeing marked work. It is also the most expensive plan, because it bills by the month and converts slowly. Insisting on a diagnosis in the first session is the single most useful thing a Dubailand parent can do with a trial lesson.

table.caption: SIX SCIENCE LOSSES ACROSS ALL THREE SUBJECTS

sections.heading: Practical assessment: examined on paper, performed at school
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how a science student is supported when tuition is delivered online and science involves laboratories. The answer rests on how the qualification actually assesses practical work, and once that is understood the objection largely dissolves.

In the main International GCSE science routes, practical skills are examined through written questions about experimental method rather than through a performed experiment marked on the day. Candidates are asked to identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, criticise a given method, read an instrument scale, process data into a table, plot a graph, assess reliability and suggest a specific improvement. Those are writing and reasoning skills, and they are the single most reliably recoverable block in the qualification because almost nobody teaches them explicitly.

They are also taught better on a shared screen than at a bench. Both people can annotate the same data table and graph in real time. A tutor can display a deliberately flawed method and ask what is wrong with it, which is exactly the format the paper uses. Most usefully, a student can bring their own messy data from a school practical and have it processed properly, which turns a frustrating afternoon into transferable technique.

What a screen cannot do is build the physical competence of handling apparatus, and that part belongs to the school, which has the equipment, the technician and the safety framework. The division of labour is therefore clean and worth stating to a parent directly: the school runs the laboratory, the tutor teaches the paper. Since the marks are on the paper, that is where the tutoring should be.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the ceiling across three sciences
paragraphs: For Cambridge candidates the tier decision is the most consequential academic decision made before sixteen, and it is multiplied by three for a separate-sciences student. Core papers lead to grades C to G; Extended papers reach A* to E. The tier is set at entry by the school, usually on internal evidence, and once entries close no amount of tuition changes the ceiling.

The multiplication matters. A student can reasonably be placed at Extended in biology and Core in physics, and families often do not realise that the tier was decided subject by subject rather than as a block. If a post-16 science route requires a particular grade in physics and the physics entry is Core, that is a problem to solve before the deadline, not in the spring of Year 11.

A short diagnostic is the right purchase at that point. Three to five sessions against the actual specification produces a written assessment of whether the higher tier is realistically reachable in a given science and what closing the gap would require in weeks. Taken to a head of department, that evidence carries more weight than a parent's conviction. Occasionally it says the opposite: an honest Core entry with a strong grade serves a student better than an Extended entry producing an E, and then the money is better spent on a different subject.

For Pearson candidates there is a different lever. Where a subject permits the modular route, units can be sat across more than one series with the better result carried forward, which splits one high-stakes moment into two. Whether a centre enters modularly is a question for the examinations officer, since it is a centre decision rather than a published default.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs around the Dubailand belt
paragraphs: Science costs more to support than mathematics for a simple reason: three subjects, each with its own specialist knowledge, and fewer specialists per subject. A family wanting all three covered weekly at the specialist band is looking at a substantial monthly figure, which is why the rotation approach described above usually represents better value.

The sourced bands. Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Specialist International GCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors reaching 500. Premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

Monthly, Bestimate's Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session give AED 240 to 600 for budget provision, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and upward for specialist examination-year support. Packages circulate at roughly AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. For a three-science family the in-home comparison is particularly unfavourable, because three visiting specialists means three travel premiums while three online slots mean none.

None of these figures is an IB Gram price list. Each names the provider or source that published it so a quote can be checked, which matters in a market where three of the six most visible pages publish no price at all. One further figure should be zero: the MoHRE private tutor work permit is granted free of charge for two years, so a licensing line item in any quote is charging for something that costs nothing.

sections.heading: Coursework, board material and the honesty boundary
paragraphs: International GCSE science carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but where any assessed personal work exists the boundary is identical, and it is worth stating because one page ranking in this market sells completed assessed work outright. The penalty for that falls on the student, not the seller.

A tutor may teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, test whether a proposed approach is workable, read what the student has written and identify where it loses marks, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach citation and referencing properly. Where a school requires an authentication declaration, the student signs it, and a tutor who crossed the line has put that signature at risk.

On materials the position is firm. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure in addition. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. A provider advertising a download library of papers has an unresolved copyright problem that a family using it would be participating in.

There is a parallel rule for the mandatory UAE subjects that sit alongside the science timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students, and for those subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. Support there works from the school's own material by design.

sections.heading: Availability, permits and what a platform may claim
paragraphs: Honest availability matters more in science than in single-subject requests, because a family often wants three things at once. Single-science support at either tier matches quickly. All three sciences in the same evening is a scheduling problem rather than a supply problem, and it resolves by using two evenings or a weekend morning. The narrowest request is a specific tier in a specific board's physics at a contested hour, and where no specialist is free we give a date rather than offering a near-fit.

No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which is how families end up discovering one in week three. Lessons are also delivered by specialists who may be based in the UAE or elsewhere, including experienced Cambridge and Pearson teachers outside the Emirates, and a parent should be told that at the outset rather than infer it later.

On permits, the facts are simple. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without it are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tuition of their own school's students, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise; that reporting is press-sourced, so verify against the current ADEK text.

What none of that licenses is a claim of endorsement. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, Sharjah by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the federal Ministry of Education. IB Gram holds no approval or accreditation from any of them, nor from Cambridge, Pearson or the IB, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE.

process.title: Email the school for the award and the codes
process.description: Which route, which board, which syllabus codes, which tier where one applies. For a science family that single reply prevents the most common waste in this market: revising removed content from separate-science material on a coordinated or combined award.

process.title: Name the weakest science, not all three
process.description: A diagnostic across the three identifies where the marks are actually going. Concentrating on one at a time, reviewed every six sessions, produces more movement than splitting one hour three ways, which yields recognition rather than fluency.

process.title: Use the free trial as an interview
process.description: A full session, no charge, no card. Ask which award and code the tutor last taught, what the student is examined on instead of a performed practical, and which topic their award has removed. A specialist answers all three without hesitation.

process.title: Buy the practical-paper block early
process.description: Four to six sessions on variables, method criticism, data processing, reliability and improvement. The technique transfers across all three sciences, which makes it the most efficient purchase in the qualification and the one almost nobody teaches explicitly.

process.title: Check the tier in each science separately
process.description: Cambridge tiers are set subject by subject, so a student can be Extended in biology and Core in physics. If a post-16 route needs a grade the tier cannot deliver, that conversation belongs before entries close rather than in the spring of Year 11.

whyPoints.title: The award is established before the teaching
whyPoints.description: Separate, coordinated and combined routes examine different content, and the reductions are not uniform across the three sciences. Confirming the award and code first prevents the commonest waste in this market, which is diligent revision of removed topics.

whyPoints.title: Board-specific practice, not generic worksheets
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson phrase questions and present data differently. A student drilled on the wrong board arrives with the right knowledge and an unfamiliar interface. Exactly one syllabus code appears across the whole competing area-page cluster researched for this project.

whyPoints.title: Separate specialists for separate sciences
whyPoints.description: At Extended or Higher tier, one tutor per subject outperforms one generalist covering three, and online delivery makes consecutive slots cost nothing extra in travel. Convenience is a real benefit and it is not the same as the best arrangement.

whyPoints.title: The written practical paper taught deliberately
whyPoints.description: Variables, method criticism, data processing and evaluation are writing skills examined on paper, and they transfer across all three sciences. That makes one block serve three subjects, and it is the area most reliably left untaught by schools and tutors alike.

whyPoints.title: Rates published with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure names who published it, including the in-home band that makes the travel premium visible. For a three-science family that premium triples, since three visiting specialists means three journeys and three fees loaded with them.

whyPoints.title: No approval claimed and no outcome promised
whyPoints.description: No KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no UAE office, no grade promise, and no statistic without the number of students, the date and the method. The MoHRE private tutor permit, meanwhile, is free of charge for two years.

faqs.question: What does Coordinated Science mean compared with separate sciences?
faqs.answer: A coordinated award covers biology, chemistry and physics in one course with content reduced in each, carrying a double award on Cambridge code 0654. Separate sciences carry the full specification in each discipline and three individual grades. The reductions in the coordinated route are not uniform across the three sciences, which is why the specification itself matters. The practical consequence is that separate-science revision material over-prepares a coordinated candidate and wastes a real share of their available hours on topics they will never be examined on.

faqs.question: How do I find out which science award my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: Email the school's examinations officer and ask three things: which route, which board, and which syllabus codes. Schools describe these routes inconsistently in reports and option booklets, so a parent's impression is not reliable evidence. You are looking for something like Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 for separate sciences, 0654 for coordinated or 0653 for combined, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Ask about the tier at the same time, because Cambridge sets Core or Extended subject by subject.

faqs.question: Should one tutor cover all three sciences for a Dubailand student?
faqs.answer: For a combined or coordinated award at the lower tiers, often yes, because the content depth in each discipline is limited and the practical-paper technique is shared. For three separate sciences at Extended or Higher tier, usually not, because holding current knowledge of three specifications at that depth is a lot to ask of one person. Online delivery makes consecutive slots with different specialists cost nothing extra in travel, which removes the main practical reason families default to one tutor.

faqs.question: How are science practicals assessed if my child studies online?
faqs.answer: In the main International GCSE science routes, practical skills are examined through written questions about method rather than a performed experiment marked on the day. Candidates identify variables, criticise a method, read scales, process data, plot graphs, assess reliability and suggest improvements. Those are writing and reasoning skills, taught better on a shared annotated document than at a bench. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school, which has the equipment and the technician. Since the marks sit on the paper, that is where tutoring belongs.

faqs.question: Which science do UAE students struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Across the three, physics produces the most consistent difficulty for students in this belt, usually because electricity and forces are taught early and relied upon afterwards, and because questions are attempted from the formula sheet rather than from a diagram. Biology produces the most marks lost to answer structure, since content recall is strong and organisation is weak. Chemistry concentrates its difficulty in moles and electrolysis. The useful point is that each has a distinct failure pattern, which makes a diagnosis quick and a plan specific.

faqs.question: Can the Core tier limit a Dubailand student's post-16 science options?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this catches families out. Cambridge Core papers lead to grades C to G while Extended papers reach A* to E, and the tier is set at entry subject by subject, so a student can be Extended in biology and Core in physics without the family realising. If a post-16 science route requires a grade the Core paper cannot deliver, that must be addressed before entries close. A short diagnostic against the real specification, written up for the school, is the only intervention that works at that point.

faqs.question: How many science sessions a week does a Year 11 need in this belt?
faqs.answer: Usually one well-placed session concentrating on the weakest science, rotated after a review, plus a shared practical-paper block. Three weekly sessions across three sciences sounds thorough and rarely survives a term, because Dubailand students travel out of the belt and arrive home late, and because academy training in Sports City and Motor City occupies the early evening. Two sessions placed deliberately, one weekday and one weekend morning, produce more than three scattered ones that get cancelled.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson science papers really differ that much?
faqs.answer: Enough to matter in the first ten minutes of the paper. The underlying science is the same, but question phrasing, command-term weighting and the presentation of data questions differ, and Cambridge tiers several subjects while Pearson generally examines a single tier in the sciences. A student drilled on the wrong board's past questions arrives with the right knowledge and an unfamiliar interface, which costs time and confidence. Board-specific practice is not a refinement; it is the difference between prepared and nearly prepared.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE science tuition cost in the Dubailand communities?
faqs.answer: Market figures rather than ours. Qualified online subject tutors are quoted at AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Specialist provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, TutorChase at AED 270. Budget provision runs AED 45 to 150, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits are AED 180 to 500 including travel. For a three-science family the in-home comparison is poor, because three visiting specialists means three travel premiums against none for three online slots.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting science tutoring in Year 9?
faqs.answer: For a family in this belt, often yes, though for a different reason than in Year 11. Year 9 is where the science option block and the Core or Extended trajectory are being decided, and the skills that determine both are specific: writing an explanation rather than a description, quantitative confidence, and organising a long answer. Work on those is cheaper now than remediation later, and it is why a large share of enquiries from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon and Town Square concern the years before the examination course.

faqs.question: Which exam series will a Dubailand science candidate sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series in the UAE, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a spring window is giving you a date you cannot use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Checkable anchors from past series: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

faqs.question: Will you give us past papers for all three sciences?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider offering a paper library is showing you a problem rather than a benefit. Cambridge and Pearson past papers, mark schemes, syllabus documents and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure as well. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and difficulty. Across three sciences that is more work for the tutor and entirely manageable.

faqs.question: Does my child's science tutor need a UAE permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition runs on the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no amounts are published. Ask also whether your child attends the tutor's own school.

faqs.question: How do Arabic and Islamic Education affect a science revision plan?
faqs.answer: They make the taught week fuller than a science option block suggests. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students. KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. For a three-science student in this belt, that means fewer genuinely free evening hours than a revision timetable drawn from subject blocks alone would assume.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubailand.closingHeading: Confirm the award, then buy the hours
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-dubailand.closingBody: An IGCSE science tutor in Dubailand earns their fee by knowing which award and which board your child is entered for, and by teaching the written practical paper nobody else teaches explicitly. One email to the school settles the first; a diagnostic session settles where the marks are going. Distance settles neither, and for a three-science family a proximity search triples the travel premium while narrowing the specialist pool. Book a free trial lesson, treat it as an interview, and start with the weakest science rather than all three at once.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-emaar-beach.tutorsIntro: Our science tutors teach one subject at one tier: Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Biology 0610, the Coordinated and Combined awards, or the Pearson Edexcel equivalents. A student taking all three separate sciences should expect three names rather than one.

intro.heading: Three sciences, two boards, three routes and one phrase on the report card
paragraphs: "IGCSE science" describes at least six different arrangements. A student may be sitting Cambridge Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610 as three separate subjects, each tiered Core or Extended. They may be sitting Coordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award, or Combined Science 0653 as a single award. They may be on the Pearson Edexcel equivalents, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4BI1, or the Edexcel Double Award. Each of those produces a different number of grades, a different content selection and a different practical arrangement.

The first consequence is about resources. A student on the Coordinated double award who revises from separate-science material covers topics that will not be examined and misses treatments that will, because the coordinated syllabus is a specific selection rather than a reduced copy of three. This happens constantly, because separate-science resources are far easier to find and nothing on a report card warns against them. The exams officer can settle it in one email, and that email prevents more wasted revision than any study technique.

The second consequence is about staffing. Chemistry, physics and biology fail in different ways and a tutor strong in one is not automatically useful in another. A biologist can keep a physics student moving through topic revision and will not spot that every lost mark traces to circuits redrawn incorrectly. A student taking all three separate sciences at Extended tier should expect three tutors. That costs more per week and it is the only arrangement in which each subject gets diagnosed rather than generally revised.

Emaar Beachfront's geography decides when any of this is practical. The peninsula has one road link onto it, no school and no tuition centre inside it, and tower basements that visitors cannot enter without a resident escort. Children leave before 07:00 for Al Sufouh, Al Barsha or Jumeirah and return after 15:30. Three sciences plus mathematics in a Year 11 spring is already a crowded week, which is why the format has to be one that survives a late bus. IB Gram teaches one-to-one over live video and does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we provide only in India.

What follows goes subject by subject. Chemistry 0620 and the three areas carrying disproportionate marks. Physics 0625 and the single most expensive habit in the subject. Biology 0610 and why breadth is less dangerous than command terms. The two Cambridge practical routes, Paper 5 and the alternative Paper 6, and what each actually tests. The Pearson Edexcel codes and how their practical model differs. And a realistic method for revising three sciences at once without any of them getting the leftovers.

A final framing point. Nothing on this page is an argument that three sciences are harder than they used to be or that students are less capable. The sciences at this level are well-specified, the mark schemes are public through your school, and the losses are consistent and nameable. What makes them expensive is that they are spread across three subjects, so the same habit fails three times and gets diagnosed as three separate weaknesses. Reading all three marked scripts together is what prevents that.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-emaar-beach.programmesIntro: The science route a student is on was decided earlier than most families realise, and the three school years that matter each need different work. These are the positions we are booked from.

programmes.name: Year 9, where the route is chosen
programmes.description: The year in which separate sciences, coordinated or combined is usually decided, along with the likely tier. Students with secure arithmetic, unit handling and graph skills keep the separate-science option open; students without them are frequently routed to a combined award on evidence collected casually rather than deliberately.
programmes.countryNote: Where a school runs MYP sciences to Year 9 then switches to IGCSE, students meet written tiered papers for the first time. The investigative habits remain useful; the examination technique has to be learned from scratch.

programmes.name: Year 10, content coverage
programmes.description: Two or three sciences are delivered in parallel across this year and part of the next. This is where unit handling, equation balancing and graph reading either become automatic or become a Year 11 problem in three subjects at once. Closing topics as the school teaches them is the cheapest grade movement in the qualification.
programmes.countryNote: Ask in Year 10 which practical route the school uses for each science, because preparing for a practical test paper and preparing for the alternative paper are different jobs.

programmes.name: Year 11, technique across three subjects
programmes.description: Content finishes and the work becomes command-term literacy, calculation discipline and paper strategy, in two or three subjects simultaneously. The mock scripts are the documents of the year, because they show whether one subject is failing or whether the same habit is costing marks in all of them.
programmes.countryNote: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June or November and Pearson in May/June or November. The February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only and must not appear in a Dubai plan.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-emaar-beach.subjectsIntro: Each entry names the code, the area of the syllabus, and the error that characterises it. The errors are specific because a session plan is written at that level rather than at the level of a subject name.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The highest-value topic in the subject and the one most often half-learned. Failures are unit handling rather than the mole concept: grams against kilograms, cubic centimetres against cubic decimetres, concentration expressed more than one way. A student carrying this into titration questions loses marks across several papers.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620: ionic equations and qualitative analysis
subjects.description: The qualitative analysis tables are memorised as results rather than as reasoning, so a student can identify the salts they have seen and fails on an unfamiliar one. Ionic equations lose marks to charge imbalance and to spectator ions left in, both of which are mechanical to fix.

subjects.name: Physics 0625: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The single most expensive area in IGCSE physics. The usual loss is a circuit redrawn incorrectly before any analysis begins, producing a flawless calculation of a different circuit. Series and parallel combinations in the same question account for a disproportionate share of dropped marks.

subjects.name: Physics 0625: moments, density and pressure
subjects.description: Calculation topics where the method is usually right and the units are wrong. Converting between cubic centimetres and litres, or between kilometres per hour and metres per second, is the whole difficulty, and it is repaired mechanically in one or two sessions.

subjects.name: Biology 0610: command terms across a wide syllabus
subjects.description: Breadth is manageable; command terms are not. Describing a graph when the question said explain, or listing when it asked to outline, forfeits marks the student had already earned. This is the largest recoverable loss in the subject and it is a habit rather than a knowledge gap.

subjects.name: Biology 0610: transport, physiology and genetics
subjects.description: Where structured-question marks concentrate at Extended tier. Transport in plants and human physiology reward a sequenced answer, and students who produce correct but unordered points collect partial credit at best. Genetics questions lose marks to incomplete notation rather than to the biology.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: A double award covering all three disciplines in a coordinated selection and producing two grades. Not a reduced copy of the separate syllabuses: some separate-science topics are absent and some treatments differ, so resources must be matched to this code specifically.

subjects.name: Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single award covering all three disciplines in the narrowest selection, producing one grade. A sensible choice for a student whose strengths sit outside the sciences, and a poor choice for anyone intending to continue a science after 16.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel sciences: 4CH1, 4PH1, 4BI1
subjects.description: The Edexcel separate sciences, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical component. Question phrasing and formula provision differ from Cambridge enough that past-paper practice must match the board.

subjects.name: Practical skills across all three sciences
subjects.description: Apparatus choice, sources of error, reading a scale, tabulating results and drawing conclusions from them. Examinable whichever route a school uses, entirely teachable on paper, and routinely left until the fortnight before the papers.

sections.heading: Establish the route before anything else
paragraphs: Three separate sciences, a coordinated double award or a combined single award. Those three routes produce three grades, two grades and one grade respectively, and they examine different selections of content. The route was chosen by the school, usually in Year 9, often on the basis of sets rather than a deliberate conversation with the family, and it is frequently not stated anywhere a parent would read. The report card says "science" or names three subjects without telling you which codes sit behind them.

Getting this wrong has a specific cost. A student on Coordinated Sciences 0654 revising from 0620 and 0625 resources will spend hours on topics outside their syllabus and miss treatments inside it, because the coordinated specification selects content for coherence across the three disciplines rather than reducing each one proportionally. The separate-science resources are more plentiful online and more heavily marketed, so this is the default error rather than an unusual one.

The fix is an email to the exams officer asking for the board, syllabus code and tier for each science entry, in writing. Keep the answer somewhere the whole household can see it, because the person buying revision guides in February is rarely the person who asked the school in September. That one document determines which past papers are worth working, which mark schemes apply, and which practical component your child is preparing for.

There is one more reason to settle this early. The route determines how many grades appear on the transcript, and a post-16 provider reads that number as well as the letters. Two grades from a coordinated award is a different application from three grades in separate sciences, regardless of how good the grades are, and a family who discovers that in Year 11 has no remaining options. Ask in Year 9 or Year 10 what route the school intends and what evidence that intention rests on.

sections.heading: Chemistry 0620: the three areas that carry the marks
paragraphs: Moles and stoichiometry come first, because almost everything else depends on them. The topic is rarely misunderstood conceptually and is frequently unreliable mechanically: a student who has to pause to convert cubic centimetres to cubic decimetres, or who is uncertain whether a concentration is expressed per litre or per cubic decimetre, will lose marks in titration and reacting-mass questions that have nothing to do with chemistry. Drilling the conversions until they are automatic is unglamorous and recovers marks across several papers.

Ionic equations are the second area. The losses are specific: charge not balanced, spectator ions left in, state symbols omitted where the mark scheme wants them. Each is mechanical and each is usually taught once and never revisited. A student who can write a correct ionic equation for an unfamiliar reaction has a skill that pays in precipitation, acid-base and redox questions alike, and it takes two sessions to install properly.

Qualitative analysis is the third and the most misunderstood. Students memorise the tables as results: this reagent with this ion gives this precipitate of this colour. That works until the paper supplies an unfamiliar salt or an unexpected combination, which it reliably does at Extended tier. Taught as reasoning instead, with attention to what is actually happening in each test, the tables become reconstructable. The difference shows up as a student who can attempt an unseen identification rather than leaving it blank.

Beyond those three areas, the rest of 0620 behaves well. Rates, reversible reactions and the organic basics respond to ordinary topic work, and students who are secure on moles, ionic equations and the reasoning behind the tests tend to pick them up without special attention. That is why the order matters: three well-chosen sessions early change how productive every later session is, and three sessions spent on organic naming while stoichiometry is still shaky change nothing at all.

sections.heading: Physics 0625 and the most expensive habit in the subject
paragraphs: Electricity causes more lost marks at IGCSE physics than any other area, and the loss is almost never conceptual. A student reads a circuit, redraws it to work with, gets the redrawing wrong, and then performs correct calculations on a different circuit. The marks go not because the physics is unknown but because the question being answered is not the question that was set. Series and parallel combinations appearing in the same diagram are where this concentrates, and it is visible in a marked script immediately.

The second area is calculation topics with unit traps: moments, density, pressure, speed. Students apply the right relationship and convert the wrong way, producing answers out by a factor of a thousand that look plausible on the page because the numbers are unfamiliar. Writing down the unit at every line, rather than at the end, catches most of it. This is a two-session repair and it survives because nobody insists on it after Year 9.

The third is diagram work generally. Ray diagrams without arrows, force diagrams without labels, and graphs plotted without axes labelled all produce the same outcome: correct reasoning the examiner cannot credit. At IGCSE level the diagram is a substantial part of the available marks rather than an illustration of the answer, and students who treat it as decoration lose marks in every paper. Enforcing diagram discipline is the most reliably productive fortnight available in physics.

Waves, energy and thermal physics rarely cause trouble at this level, which is worth knowing because it tells you where not to spend sessions. A student whose script shows losses spread evenly across topics almost certainly has a technique problem rather than a content problem, and the fortnight on diagrams, units and command terms will move more marks than any amount of topic revision. The uneven script is the one that points to a genuine gap.

sections.heading: Biology 0610: breadth is not the problem
paragraphs: Biology has the widest content load of the three sciences and families reasonably assume that is the difficulty. It is not. The breadth is manageable because the content is mostly describable, and students who read the syllabus and work through it systematically cover it. The marks are lost somewhere else: in answering a cheaper command term than the one printed. A student who describes when the question said explain has written a correct answer that cannot score in the band the question was set at.

The second loss is sequence. Structured questions in transport, physiology and genetics reward an ordered answer, because the mark scheme follows a chain of events. A student who supplies all the correct points in no particular order collects partial credit, and the gap between that and full marks across several questions is substantial. Teaching students to write the sequence before writing the sentences is a short intervention with a large return.

The third is notation, concentrated in genetics. Punnett squares drawn without defining the alleles, phenotype ratios stated without the genotypes that produce them, and gametes omitted from a cross all forfeit marks on questions where the underlying biology was understood. Like most IGCSE losses these are mechanical, and they persist because they look like presentation rather than content. A marked script makes the distinction obvious within a few questions.

Ecology and the human impact material behaves differently again: it is content-light and command-term heavy, so students who have fixed their command terms score well on it with very little revision. That makes it a useful place to check whether a technique block has actually worked. If a student still loses marks there after the block, the habit has not been installed and the block needs repeating rather than extending into new content.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6: the two Cambridge practical routes
paragraphs: Cambridge assesses practical skills in the separate sciences through either a practical test paper or a written alternative, and the school chooses which. Families often do not know which applies, and the two require different preparation. The practical test is sat in a laboratory with apparatus. The alternative is a written paper that presents an experimental scenario and tests the same skills on paper: choosing apparatus, identifying sources of error, reading a scale correctly, completing a results table and drawing a supported conclusion.

The important point for families considering online tutoring is that both routes test written reasoning, and the alternative paper tests nothing else. Apparatus choice, error analysis, table construction and conclusion writing are entirely teachable over a shared page, and the alternative paper is in some ways easier to prepare for remotely than in a classroom, because every question can be worked and marked against a scheme. Where a school uses the practical test, the handling practice happens at school and the reasoning still has to be taught.

Either way, this component is routinely left until the final fortnight. That is a mistake with a measurable cost, because the skills are finite and learnable: there are only so many sources of error, so many apparatus choices, so many ways a results table can be wrong. Four to six sessions a term ahead of the papers covers it properly. Ask the school which route applies to each science, because it can differ between subjects in the same school.

sections.heading: Pearson Edexcel sciences and what changes
paragraphs: A substantial minority of schools serving this cluster enter students for Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences: 4CH1 Chemistry, 4PH1 Physics and 4BI1 Biology, with a Double Award alternative. The content overlaps heavily with Cambridge and the differences that matter to a student are structural. Practical skills are assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical component, so there is no equivalent of the Paper 5 and Paper 6 choice. Question phrasing follows a different house style, and formula provision differs.

The practical consequence is the same as it is in mathematics: practise from the board your child is entered with. A student working Cambridge 0625 papers for an Edexcel 4PH1 examination meets unfamiliar question structures under time pressure and loses minutes decoding before losing marks on content. This is a common and entirely avoidable loss, and it happens because Cambridge resources are more abundant and nobody checks the code on the entry confirmation.

The series available also differ in timing. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, with November results reaching students in January: the November 2025 series results landed on 22 January 2026 and the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026. Cambridge runs June and November for UAE candidates. Either way, link and read the awarding body's live timetable rather than relying on dates restated anywhere else, including here.

One more structural difference worth knowing. Because Edexcel does not run a separate practical component, a student on 4PH1 or 4CH1 has no equivalent of the alternative-to-practical paper to prepare for, and the practical reasoning instead appears distributed through the theory papers. That changes the revision shape rather than removing the requirement: the same apparatus, error and table skills are examined, just not in one place where they can be drilled as a block.

sections.heading: Revising three sciences at once without starving one
paragraphs: The common failure in a Year 11 spring is not that a student revises too little. It is that two sciences get attention and the third gets whatever is left, which is usually the subject they find hardest and therefore avoid. The result is two reasonable grades and one poor one, from a student who worked hard throughout. Any plan for three sciences has to allocate time deliberately rather than by inclination, and it has to be written down because inclination always reasserts itself.

The efficient structure begins with what the three subjects share. Command terms, unit conversion, graph construction and reading, results tables, and the structure of a calculation answer are tested identically in chemistry, physics and biology. A single block on those produces gains in all three, which makes it the right first purchase for a student whose scripts show the same habit failing everywhere. Three or four sessions here are worth more than three or four sessions in any one subject.

After that, allocate by cost rather than by comfort. Identify the two highest-mark losses across all three subjects, regardless of which subject they are in, and work those first. Then rotate, with the weakest subject getting the fixed slot and the stronger two sharing a second. Every fortnight, one timed paper in one subject, self-marked strictly and audited. That rotation keeps the weakest subject from being avoided, which is the single most useful structural decision in a three-science year.

With three sciences the hours are the hardest part, which is why we would rather see them honestly than be told what would be ideal. A plan built on an hour that does not exist collapses in week three and takes the family's confidence with it.

We match one tutor per subject at that tier and propose slots in Gulf Standard Time. One free trial lesson per student, no card required, producing a written breakdown of lost marks by subject and by habit. Most families start with one subject, usually the weakest, and add a second once the pattern is clear. That is a sensible order and we will say so rather than proposing three appointments in the first week.

The limits, stated plainly. Finding three Extended-tier science specialists with compatible hours for one student takes longer than finding one, and occasionally a particular code and tier combination has nobody free that week. We will say so and offer alternatives rather than putting a generalist across all three, which is the arrangement most likely to produce effort without movement. We cannot promise a grade, and the student has to do the problem sets between sessions in each subject.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child does separate or coordinated sciences?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the board, syllabus code and tier for each science entry, in writing. A report card naming three sciences does not tell you whether those are separate 0620, 0625 and 0610 entries or a coordinated award recorded by subject. The distinction decides which past papers are worth working and which specification to revise from, and getting it wrong is the commonest source of wasted revision in a Year 11 science year.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover chemistry, physics and biology?
faqs.answer: One tutor can cover all three at a level of general revision. None of them will be diagnosed. The three subjects fail in different ways: chemistry on unit handling and reasoning about tests, physics on circuits and diagrams, biology on command terms and answer sequence. A specialist in one spots their own subject's pattern in minutes and misses the others entirely. For three separate sciences at Extended tier, expect three names and start with the weakest subject.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge practical route is my child sitting?
faqs.answer: Either a practical test paper sat in a laboratory or the alternative written paper, and the school chooses. It can differ between sciences within the same school, so ask subject by subject. The alternative paper tests apparatus choice, sources of error, scale reading, results tables and supported conclusions entirely in writing, which makes it fully preparable over a shared page. Where the practical test applies, the handling happens at school and the reasoning still has to be taught.

faqs.question: Would the coordinated double award be a lighter load for our Year 10?
faqs.answer: Lighter rather than easier, and importantly different. It produces two grades instead of three and covers a coordinated selection of content across the three disciplines, which is not a proportional reduction of each separate syllabus. Some separate-science topics are absent and some treatments differ, so revising 0654 from 0620 or 0625 resources wastes effort and leaves gaps. For a student intending to continue a science after 16, the separate route is usually the better preparation.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose physics marks on circuit questions they understand?
faqs.answer: Because the circuit is being redrawn incorrectly before any analysis starts, so the calculation that follows is a flawless analysis of a different circuit. Series and parallel combinations in one diagram are where this concentrates. It is visible in a marked script immediately and it repairs in about two sessions of enforced redrawing discipline. Re-teaching the electricity topic will not touch it, which is why a script matters more than a reported grade when deciding what to buy.

faqs.question: What is the highest-value chemistry topic to work on first?
faqs.answer: Moles and stoichiometry, and specifically the unit conversions inside it. The concept is rarely misunderstood and the mechanics are frequently unreliable, so a student hesitating over cubic centimetres and cubic decimetres loses marks in titration and reacting-mass questions across several papers. Two sessions of mechanical drilling until the conversions are automatic recovers marks in more places than any other single intervention in the subject at this level.

faqs.question: Is biology just a memory subject at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way is why strong students underperform in it. The breadth is manageable with systematic coverage. The marks are lost to command terms, with students describing when the question said explain, and to answer sequence, because structured questions in transport, physiology and genetics follow a chain the mark scheme follows too. Correct points in the wrong order collect partial credit. Both are habits, both are visible in a script, and both repair quickly.

faqs.question: Should we revise from Cambridge or Edexcel science papers?
faqs.answer: Only from the board on the entry confirmation. Cambridge 0625 and Edexcel 4PH1 cover similar physics in different house styles with different formula provision, and Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate component. Practising the wrong archive trains a student to decode the wrong question format, and the time lost decoding in the exam comes out of thinking time. Confirm the board subject by subject, because it can differ within one school.

faqs.question: How do we stop one science being neglected in Year 11?
faqs.answer: By giving the weakest subject the fixed weekly slot and letting the stronger two share a second. Students avoid the subject they find hardest and the avoidance is invisible until results day, which is how a hard-working student ends up with two reasonable grades and one poor one. This is a structural fix rather than a motivational one, and it is the single most useful decision in a three-science year. Write the allocation down.

faqs.question: When should practical-paper preparation start?
faqs.answer: A term before the papers, not in the final fortnight. The examinable skills are finite: a limited number of apparatus choices, sources of error, scale-reading traps, table conventions and conclusion structures. Four to six sessions covers them properly and the marks are among the most reliably recoverable in the sciences. Families leave it late because it feels like a small component, and then discover that the written reasoning it tests also appears throughout the theory papers.

faqs.question: Our child is on a combined award and wants to take a science after 16. What now?
faqs.answer: Talk to the school before the entry deadline, because a combined single award is thin preparation for A Level or Diploma sciences and the route may still be changeable. If it is not, the realistic plan is to use the year after results to close the gap deliberately: the missing content is identifiable from the two specifications side by side, and a short block over the summer covers more than people expect. Ask the post-16 provider what they expect.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week is realistic with three sciences and maths?
faqs.answer: Two or three total, not four. More appointments than that crowd out the problem sets that actually build fluency, and a Year 11 student from this peninsula is already losing ninety minutes a day to the school run. The structure that works is one fixed slot for the weakest subject, one alternating slot for the others, and a fortnightly timed paper. Fewer, better-targeted sessions with real work between them beat a full timetable of attendance.

faqs.question: Do the sciences share any skills worth buying as one block?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is usually the best first purchase. Command terms, unit conversion, graph construction and reading, results tables and the structure of a calculation answer are tested identically in chemistry, physics and biology. Three or four sessions on those produce gains in all three subjects at once. We recommend this order when the mock scripts show the same habit failing across subjects, which is more often than families expect.

faqs.question: Can sessions work around a late school bus to the peninsula?
faqs.answer: That is most of the argument for the format. A video slot moves by thirty minutes with a message and nobody loses an evening. With two or three science appointments in a week, a format that loses sessions to a single access road compounds quickly rather than occasionally, and the sessions lost in April are the ones there is no room to replace. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, so this is the comparison that applies.
