intro.heading: Three sciences, one shortened evening, and a decision nobody makes deliberately
paragraphs: A triple award IGCSE candidate is studying three separate syllabuses: Biology, Chemistry and Physics, each with its own papers, its own content list and its own Paper 6 alternative to practical. Each sets homework. Each has a mock. Each expects revision. For a student travelling out of Emaar South to school and back, all three arrive into an evening that has already lost around ninety minutes to the road.

Most families respond by trying to support all three at once, usually with one weekly session rotating between them or with two tutors running in parallel. That is the arrangement that collapses, and it collapses around half term for arithmetic reasons rather than motivational ones. Three sciences dividing the available attention three ways means none of them receives enough independent practice between sessions to make the sessions work.

The alternative is sequencing, which feels wrong and works better. One science at a time, four to six weeks each, weakest first, preceded by a block on the faults that appear in all three simultaneously. That shared block is the part families never buy, and it is the best value in the subject: command-word discipline, graph technique, significant figures and answer-length matching show up in Biology, Chemistry and Physics at the same time, so four sessions can affect three grades.

There is a second piece of arithmetic specific to this community. A triple award candidate sits three Paper 6 papers, examining experimental skills on paper rather than in a laboratory. Those papers reward conventions rather than understanding, their question types repeat across series, and almost nobody drills them. They also happen to be the most fatigue-resistant science work available, which makes them the right content for a weekday slot after a long journey rather than the first thing to be dropped.

IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and no tutor is dispatched to an Emaar South address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams, circuits and graphs drawn on a shared surface that persists week to week. Across three sciences that record does real work, because the same unlabelled axis appearing in physics in October and in chemistry in February is one fault rather than two.

One factual note, and it matters more with three syllabuses in play than with one. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative timetable zones, stating that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable, and a triple award candidate is reading that timetable for Biology, Chemistry and Physics papers plus three Paper 6 sittings, so a single wrong zone document can misplace six dates or more at once. On the series: UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, while Cambridge's February and March series is offered to India only, which is worth holding onto because much of the free science revision material an Emaar South student finds first was written for that Indian calendar. KHDA oversees Dubai's private schools and does not accredit tutors; IB Gram holds no KHDA approval or partnership and runs no UAE centre.

Criterion B is inquiring and designing and criterion D is reflecting on the impacts of science, so a student can hold a strong grade with good investigation design while quantitative work lags.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools in this catchment run Middle Years Sciences rather than IGCSE, which means two Emaar South neighbours of the same age can face entirely different workloads: three separate syllabuses in one case, integrated criterion assessment in the other. Comparing how much tutoring each buys tells a family nothing.

programmes.name: A Level and IB Diploma sciences
programmes.description: What the IGCSE route feeds into. A triple award student has the widest options at sixteen; a combined science candidate may find a sixth form's entry requirement for a science A Level or a Higher Level Diploma science harder to satisfy. That consequence is set two years earlier by an entry decision most families were not consulted on.
programmes.countryNote: Emaar South students split between A Level sixth forms in the British-curriculum schools and Diploma cohorts in the IB continuum schools of Dubai Investments Park and the Dubailand corridor. dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-emaar-south.subjectsIntro: The science components competing for an Emaar South student's evening, each annotated by how well it survives a tired slot, because that decides what can realistically be scheduled where.

subjects.name: Paper 6: alternative to practical
subjects.description: Experimental skills examined on paper: variables, instrument reading, results tables with correct headings and units, graph plotting, error sources, improvements. Procedural, repeating across series, and the most fatigue-resistant science work available. A triple award candidate sits three of these.

subjects.name: Biology 0610 theory
subjects.description: High recall volume, so gains come from note compression and command-term discipline. Note-building is good weekend work. Command-term practice is short and survives a weekday evening, and diagram-based process questions reward sketching before writing, which also holds up when tired.

subjects.name: Chemistry 0620 theory
subjects.description: Mole calculations and qualitative analysis carry the widest spread. Qualitative analysis is pure recall with a fixed answer set, which makes it reliable late-evening drill. Mole calculations need more attention and belong earlier in the week or at a weekend.

subjects.name: Physics 0625 theory
subjects.description: Unit prefixes and gradient interpretation account for a disproportionate share of losses, and electricity questions fail on circuit reading rather than calculation. Redrawing a circuit in a standard layout is a habit, not a skill, and can be drilled in a tired slot.

subjects.name: Graph work across the sciences
subjects.description: Axis labels with quantity and unit, sensible scales, lines of best fit through the spread, gradients read with a large triangle. Each earns marks independently of the science, appears in all three subjects, and is procedural enough for any slot in the week.

subjects.name: Command terms across the sciences
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate each demand a specific answer shape. Misreading the verb is the commonest reason a competent candidate sits mid-band in all three sciences at once, and the list is short and published, so it is fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Qualitative analysis in chemistry
subjects.description: Flame tests, precipitate colours and gas tests, produced from memory or from the supplied tables. A fixed answer set, which makes it the clearest example of reliable marks available to anybody who drills it and a reliable loss to anybody who assumes it will return on the day.

subjects.name: Required practical description
subjects.description: Questions asking how an experiment would be carried out are marked on method: named apparatus, the variable changed, the variables controlled, what is measured and how often. A structured four-line answer collects marks a general description does not, and the structure is learnable.

subjects.name: Calculations and significant figures
subjects.description: A marked skill across all three sciences rather than a topic. Early rounding in a multi-step calculation yields an answer the scheme rejects. Carrying full precision and rounding only at the end is a two-session habit that recovers marks in three subjects at once.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: A reduced content list with its own paper structure and fewer grades. Past papers from the separate sciences are not usable, so confirming the route before any plan is written matters more than anything else on this list. A term of the wrong papers is unrecoverable.

subjects.name: Pearson sciences 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1
subjects.description: Used by some schools in this catchment, with broadly comparable content and different question styles, including longer contextual stems and a different treatment of practical skills. A student transferring mid-course needs about four sessions of adjustment rather than a term.

subjects.name: Biology diagram and process questions
subjects.description: Transport systems, the heart, the nephron and the eye all reward a labelled diagram over a paragraph, because the diagram enforces the order of the process and the order is where the marks sit. Sketching practice is short, procedural and suits a weekday slot.

sections.heading: Three syllabuses against the hours that exist
paragraphs: Count first. A school day, plus twenty-five to forty-five minutes of travel each way out of a community with no school in it, plus arrival, changing and eating, leaves most Emaar South Year 11 students four to four and a half usable weekday hours. Into that go homework from eight to ten subjects, revision, any co-curricular commitment and a tutoring session. Three sciences are a large share of the homework and a large share of the revision.

The comparison that makes it concrete is a family in Green Community, minutes from the school cluster: same three syllabuses, same mocks, same June series, roughly an hour and a half more usable evening every week. Across a two-year course that is a structural difference, and it means Emaar South families regularly conclude their child is working less than a classmate when they are working with less time.

What follows is not that these students need three tutors. It is that three parallel arrangements cannot be sustained, because the limiting factor is independent practice between sessions rather than teaching. A session that sets work nobody has time to do becomes a weekly explanation, which feels productive and changes nothing. Three such sessions produce three weekly explanations and a collapsed plan by half term.

The table sets the week out against the three sciences so a family can see where the pressure actually is. The honest conclusion is that one science can be properly supported at a time, with the shared faults treated once across all three, and that any plan promising more is promising attention the week does not contain.

sections.heading: Which science gets the slot, and how to decide
paragraphs: If only one science can be properly supported at a time, the choice has to be made on evidence rather than on which one feels most alarming. The three marked mock scripts answer it faster than any conversation, and they usually answer it differently from how a parent would guess.

The questions to ask of each script are the same three. Was the paper finished? An unfinished paper is a pacing problem and the fix is timing drill, not content. Are the losses concentrated in a few topics or spread evenly? Concentrated losses respond to teaching; evenly spread small losses respond to technique. Did marks go on content the student can explain aloud? That is a writing problem rather than a knowledge one.

Apply that to three scripts and a pattern usually appears. Commonly one science has genuine content gaps, perhaps because a topic was taught during a period of absence or by a succession of cover teachers, and the other two have the same technique faults. In that case the right purchase is the shared technique block first, then a sequenced block on the science with real gaps, which is both cheaper and faster than three arrangements.

Occasionally all three scripts show concentrated content losses, which usually means coverage is behind across the board. That is a different problem and the honest answer is that tutoring cannot replace a term of teaching in three subjects at once. The useful move there is a conversation with the school, plus a break intensive on the single science furthest behind, rather than spreading hours thinly across all three.

sections.heading: Paper 6, and why it fits a tired evening
paragraphs: Of everything in three science syllabuses, the alternative to practical paper is the work that holds up best at 18:30 after a long journey, and it is also the least drilled. That combination makes it the obvious first purchase for an Emaar South household and it is almost never where families start.

The reason it is fatigue-resistant is that it rewards conventions rather than sustained reasoning. Identify the independent, dependent and controlled variables in a described experiment. Read a scale to the correct precision. Complete a results table with the quantity and unit in the heading. Plot points accurately and draw a line of best fit through the spread. Identify a source of error, distinguish it from a mistake, and suggest an improvement addressing the error named rather than urging more care.

Each of those is a procedure with a predictable mark scheme, and each is marked independently of whether the student understands the underlying science. A results table heading written as time rather than time in seconds loses the mark. An improvement of being more careful loses the mark where naming a more precise instrument would have earned it. These are untaught conventions rather than deep failures, which is why four to six sessions moves the score so reliably.

The arithmetic for a triple award candidate is the clincher. Three Paper 6 papers means a single technique block pays into three subjects at once, from a slot the student can actually use, on content that repeats across series. For a household choosing where to put one weekday session, that is a stronger case than any single science's theory content can make, and it is also the easiest work to sustain because the improvement shows quickly on past papers.

sections.heading: What happens in school that no tutor can replicate
paragraphs: Worth saying plainly, because providers imply otherwise. Practical work happens in a school laboratory, with the school's apparatus, under the school's supervision, and no amount of online tutoring replaces handling a burette or wiring a circuit. A tutor who suggests they can deliver practical science remotely is overselling, and a parent should treat that claim as information about everything else they say.

What a tutor can do is prepare a student for the way practical skills are examined, which is a different and entirely legitimate thing. In Cambridge sciences that examination is Paper 6, on paper, testing whether a student can identify variables, read instruments, spot error sources and suggest improvements. Those are describable, drillable and examinable without apparatus, and most students have never been taught them explicitly.

The second thing a tutor can do is make the school's practical work count for more. A student who goes into a laboratory session knowing what the examination will later ask about it — which variable is controlled and how, what the resolution of the instrument is, where error enters — gets considerably more out of the same hour than a student following instructions. That is preparation rather than replacement, and it is the honest version of the offer.

For an Emaar South family there is a scheduling note attached. School practical sessions are fixed in the timetable and cannot move, which means they are one of the few science commitments the journey does not affect. That makes them a reliable anchor: a tutoring session placed in the same week as a practical, aimed at what that practical will later be examined on, uses the school's own work as the raw material rather than competing with it for hours.

sections.heading: The shared faults, and why treating them once is better arithmetic
paragraphs: Four faults appear in Biology, Chemistry and Physics at the same time, and they are the reason a competent student can sit mid-band in all three simultaneously. Command-word misreading, where describe, explain and suggest get the wrong answer shape. Graph technique, where axis labels, scales, lines of best fit and gradient triangles each earn marks independently of the science. Significant figures and early rounding. And answer length mismatched to the mark tariff, which spends time the final question needed.

Because they are shared, they can be treated once. Four to six sessions on all four, using past-paper questions drawn from all three sciences so the student sees the same fault in different clothes, improves three grades rather than one. That is arithmetic no single-subject block can match, and it is the purchase families in this community almost never make because it does not map onto a subject name.

It also happens to be the best work for a shortened evening. All four faults are procedural: they involve reading a verb correctly, labelling an axis, carrying precision and matching length to marks. None requires the sustained attention that a new chemistry calculation or a first encounter with electromagnetic induction does. A student off a forty-minute bus can do this work well, which is not true of most science content.

The practical sequence we recommend to Emaar South households is therefore the shared block first, then sequenced single-science blocks with the weakest first, then a Paper 6 block if the scripts show it is needed, with break intensives carrying any genuine content catch-up. That order is chosen for the hours available rather than for tidiness, and it is the arrangement that survives a term here.

sections.heading: What science revision works on a bus
paragraphs: A forty-minute journey twice a day is roughly six and a half hours a week, and for a triple award candidate that is a material amount of time. It cannot be used for everything and it can be used for something, and being specific about which is more useful than either ignoring it or pretending a bus is a desk.

What works is recall and recognition. Biology terminology and process sequences. Chemistry qualitative analysis results, which are a fixed answer set and ideally suited to flashcards. Physics equations and unit prefixes. Command-term definitions, which are short and published. Reading through a set of condensed notes made earlier at a desk. All of these are retrieval practice, which is genuinely effective and does not need a writing surface.

What does not work is anything requiring written working or sustained attention: multi-step chemistry calculations, circuit analysis, graph plotting, writing a method description to time. Attempting those on a moving bus produces frustration and the conclusion that the student cannot do them, which is a false negative with real consequences for confidence.

There is a practical version of this worth setting up once. A student who makes condensed notes and a flashcard set during the weekend session has material to use on the bus all week, which converts preparation time into retrieval time at no cost. In this community that is one of the few genuine gains available, and it works because the making of the material is desk work and the using of it is not.

sections.heading: Entry route, tier and the questions to ask the school
paragraphs: None of the scheduling above matters if the plan is aimed at the wrong papers. Triple award, double award and combined science are different entries with different content lists and different paper structures, and past papers from the separate sciences are not usable for a combined candidate. A tutor given the wrong route sets content that is not on the syllabus, which in a week this tight is a term that cannot be recovered.

Tier is the second question and it is set per subject, so a student can be Extended in one science and Core in another. That produces reports which look inconsistent and are simply describing two different entries with two different grade ceilings. Each needs confirming separately, because the tier caps the achievable grade however good the revision.

The third question is the board, because Cambridge sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625 while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, and the practical assessment differs: Cambridge sets Paper 6 as a separate paper while Pearson integrates those skills across its papers. That changes whether a Paper 6 block is the right purchase at all.

All three answers are on the timetable or come back from one email, and together they determine everything downstream. For an Emaar South family specifically there is a fourth worth asking: when is each science's mock window, because they often differ and they are the fixed points a sequenced plan should be built around. A plan aimed at the wrong mock loses a fortnight it cannot replace.

sections.heading: The travel premium, and what three sciences would cost in-home
paragraphs: If a family wanted in-home support across three sciences from this address, the published figures show what that implies. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour, with independent home tutors quoted up to AED 500 once travel is priced into the hour. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150-300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150.

From Emaar South the in-home figure sits at the top of its band, because a tutor absorbs the same twenty-five to forty-five minute journey the student just made. The sharper constraint is that a visiting tutor fits one session an evening, so three sciences in-home means three evenings committed and three travel premiums paid, in a week that already has four usable hours a night. The published monthly packages put the scale of it plainly: AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home sessions of two hours.

One science tutor is also unlikely to cover all three subjects well at Extended tier, so an in-home arrangement across the sciences usually means more than one person, each with their own route and their own available slot. At that point the household is scheduling around other people's driving rather than around their child's arrival time, which in this community is the thing that makes a plan fail.

Every figure here belongs to the provider named and is published by them. None is an IB Gram price: our conversation starts with a free trial lesson and a written sequencing plan. Bestimate's monthly estimates give the planning frame: AED 240-600 budget at one hour a week, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support.

sections.heading: Ramadan, the breaks and the final fortnight across three subjects
paragraphs: During Ramadan the school day shortens, which shortens the journey too, so an Emaar South student is home earlier even though less of the afternoon is useful. Sessions move after iftar and shorten to sixty minutes. Across three sciences the content choice matters more than usual: qualitative analysis recall, command-term work, Paper 6 conventions and flashcard retrieval all hold up late in the evening, while multi-step chemistry calculations and new physics do not.

The breaks are where a three-science plan gains most, because both the workload and the journey vanish and the student has consecutive days. That is where full timed papers belong, marked and reviewed inside forty-eight hours while the student still remembers their reasoning, and where genuine content catch-up in the weakest science belongs. In this community a break returns around fifteen hours a week of a teenager's time, which is more than any term-time rearrangement can find.

The final fortnight across three sciences is the point at which frequency beats length and selection beats coverage. Three or four sixty-minute sessions a week, timed sections only, nothing new, with each session aimed at the single highest-value remaining target in whichever science needs it. A ninety-minute session in the final week of a nine-subject year tends to end with twenty minutes of nothing happening, which is time this student does not have.

The selection discipline matters most here. With three sciences, two of them will have to accept maintenance rather than improvement in the last fortnight, and deciding which deliberately is better than discovering it by exhaustion. The scripts decide it: whichever science has the most accessible remaining marks, usually in Paper 6 conventions or in a procedural topic, gets the sessions. The others get the student's own flashcards and the condensed notes made earlier.

faqs.question: Can my Emaar South child have three science tutors at once?
faqs.answer: They can be bought and they rarely survive. A household with a twenty-five to forty-five minute school run each way has four to four and a half usable weekday hours, and three weekly sessions leave no room for the independent practice that makes sessions work. Each then becomes a weekly explanation, which feels productive and changes nothing, and the plan collapses around half term. Sequencing one science at a time, preceded by a shared-fault block, costs less and produces more.

faqs.question: Which science should get the one available slot?
faqs.answer: Whichever the three marked mock scripts say, and it often is not the one that feels most alarming. Ask the same three questions of each script: was the paper finished, are the losses concentrated or spread evenly, and were marks lost on content the student can explain aloud. Concentrated losses mean content gaps and respond to teaching. Evenly spread small losses mean technique and respond to a shared block covering all three. An unfinished paper is a pacing problem.

faqs.question: What are the faults that appear in all three sciences at once?

Graph technique, where axis labels, scales, lines of best fit and gradient triangles each earn marks independently of the science. Significant figures and early rounding in calculation chains. And answer length mismatched to the mark tariff, which spends time the final question needed. Four to six sessions treating all four improves three grades, which is better arithmetic than any single-subject block.

faqs.question: Why is Paper 6 a good choice for a weekday evening?

The questions ask candidates to identify variables, read instruments to the correct precision, complete results tables with quantity and unit in the heading, plot and interpret graphs, and suggest improvements addressing a named error. Those are procedures with predictable mark schemes. A triple award candidate sits three of these papers, so one block pays into three subjects.

faqs.question: Can practical science be taught online?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider claiming otherwise is overselling. Practical work happens in the school laboratory with the school's apparatus under the school's supervision. What a tutor can legitimately do is prepare a student for how practical skills are examined, which in Cambridge sciences means Paper 6 on paper, and make the school's own laboratory hour count for more by saying beforehand what the examination will later ask about it. That is preparation rather than replacement.

faqs.question: What science revision can my child do on the school bus?
faqs.answer: Recall and recognition work. Biology terminology and process sequences, chemistry qualitative analysis results which are a fixed answer set, physics equations and unit prefixes, command-term definitions, and reading through condensed notes made earlier at a desk. A forty-minute journey twice a day is around six and a half hours a week, which is material. What does not work is multi-step calculations, circuit analysis or anything needing written working, and attempting those there creates a false sense of inability.

faqs.question: How do I know whether my child takes triple or combined science?
faqs.answer: Read the syllabus codes on the timetable or last report. Three codes, such as 0610, 0620 and 0625, means three separate sciences and three grades. A single combined code means a reduced content list with its own paper structure and one or two grades. Schools usually decide this in Year 9 or early Year 10 on a mixture of attainment and timetable capacity, and communicate it in a line of an options booklet, so most parents were never told explicitly.

faqs.question: Does the entry route change which past papers are useful?
faqs.answer: Completely, and this is the most expensive thing to get wrong. Past papers from the separate sciences are not usable for a combined or co-ordinated science candidate, because the content lists and paper structures differ. A tutor given the wrong route sets questions on content that is not on the syllabus, and in a week with four usable evening hours that is a term nobody can recover. Confirm the route before any plan is written, in writing if possible.

faqs.question: What would three in-home science tutors cost from Emaar South?
faqs.answer: More in evenings than in money, which is the binding constraint. Published figures put in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with independent tutors up to AED 500 once travel is priced in, and from this address the quote sits at the top of the band. A visiting tutor fits one session an evening, and one person is unlikely to cover all three sciences well at Extended tier, so three sciences means three evenings and probably two or three different routes to schedule around.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send science tutors to Emaar South homes?
faqs.answer: No. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only and no tutor is sent to any UAE address. Students here are taught live one-to-one over video on Gulf Standard Time, with diagrams, circuits and graphs drawn on a shared surface that is saved week to week. Across three sciences that record does real work, because the same unlabelled axis appearing in physics in October and in chemistry in February is one fault rather than two separate impressions.

faqs.question: Why does my child's report show two different science tiers?
faqs.answer: Because science entries are made subject by subject, so a student can be Extended in one and Core in another. That produces a report which looks inconsistent and is actually describing two entries with two different grade ceilings, so each science's tier needs confirming separately. The tier caps the achievable grade however good the revision, which makes it the most consequential thing in the two years and the thing most often discovered late in a crowded Year 11.

faqs.question: How should the breaks be used for three sciences?
faqs.answer: For the work that cannot fit a weekday evening here: full timed papers, marked and reviewed inside forty-eight hours while the student still remembers their reasoning, and genuine content catch-up in whichever science is furthest behind. A break removes both the school workload and the daily journey, which in this community returns around fifteen hours a week of a teenager's time. Booking winter and spring blocks before term starts is the best-value decision available from Emaar South.

faqs.question: What should the final fortnight look like with three sciences?
faqs.answer: Short, frequent and selective. Three or four sixty-minute sessions a week, timed sections only, nothing new, each aimed at the single highest-value remaining target in whichever science has the most accessible marks left, usually Paper 6 conventions or a procedural topic. Two of the three sciences will have to accept maintenance rather than improvement, and deciding which deliberately from the scripts is better than discovering it by exhaustion in the last week.

faqs.question: Why does qualitative analysis come up as a priority in chemistry?
faqs.answer: Because it is a fixed answer set: flame tests, precipitate colours and gas tests, either known or not. That makes it the clearest example of reliable marks available to anybody who drills it and a reliable loss to anybody who assumes it will come back on the day. It is also pure recall, so it holds up in a tired evening slot and transfers well to flashcards for use on the bus, which in this community is a genuine advantage.

faqs.question: Does Pearson have a Paper 6 equivalent?
faqs.answer: Not as a separate paper. Cambridge sciences set Paper 6, the alternative to practical, as its own examination, while Pearson Edexcel International GCSE integrates practical skills across its papers instead. That changes whether a Paper 6 technique block is the right purchase at all, which is why the syllabus codes matter before anything is booked: 0610, 0620 and 0625 are Cambridge, while 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 are Pearson. Check the timetable rather than assuming.

faqs.question: What changes during Ramadan for a three-science plan?
faqs.answer: The school day shortens, which shortens the journey too, so the student is home earlier even though less of the afternoon is useful. Sessions move after iftar and shorten to sixty minutes, and the content choice matters more than usual: qualitative analysis recall, command-term work, Paper 6 conventions and flashcard retrieval hold up late, while multi-step chemistry calculations and new physics do not. Reducing rather than abandoning the arrangement is what keeps three sciences from drifting at once.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-emirates-hi.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics on both major boards, including the coordinated and combined routes. The first question each asks is which syllabus code and which paper numbers appear on the entry, because that single answer changes everything that follows.

intro.heading: Three sciences, or two grades, or one: find out which before anything else
paragraphs: Parents in this part of Dubai routinely say that their child is doing IGCSE science and assume that means the same thing everywhere. It does not. A Year 11 sitting Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 is taking three full IGCSEs and will sit nine papers. A Year 11 on Coordinated Sciences 0654 is taking one course awarded as two IGCSE grades, with six papers. A Year 11 on Combined Science 0653 is taking one course awarded as a single grade. These are not harder and easier versions of one thing; they are different volumes of content examined differently.

Getting this wrong wastes money in a predictable way. A family buys a biology tutor for a child on Coordinated Sciences and the tutor teaches the separate 0610 syllabus, which goes further than the course requires in some areas and does not cover the integration the actual papers demand. Another family hires three tutors for a child who needed one, because nobody asked whether the sciences were separate. The entry form answers it in a line, and the school exams officer will tell you if you ask.

The second thing to establish is the tier. Cambridge splits most of these syllabuses into Core and Extended, with different papers and different grade ranges. Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4. Both sit either Paper 5, a laboratory practical test, or Paper 6, an alternative-to-practical written paper, and that choice belongs to the school, not the student. The grade ceiling differs between the tiers, so a tier decision made in Year 10 shapes what is available at the end of Year 11.

The third thing, and the one almost nobody prepares for, is the practical component. It carries a fifth of the grade on the separate sciences and it is examined as a skill rather than as knowledge. Writing a method a stranger could repeat, tabulating results with consistent significant figures, plotting a graph with a sensible scale, reading a gradient as a quantity with units, and suggesting one specific improvement are all learnable in a handful of sessions. They are also the marks most commonly left on the table, because school revision tends to be content-led.

Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around the school run in Emirates Hills, The Springs and The Meadows. IB Gram does not run a UAE office and does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are offered in India only. subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-heavy and marked on precision of language. subjects.description: Moles work, the reactivity series, electrolysis and organic nomenclature. subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and the practical component account for the bulk of lost marks. Circuit questions punish students who have memorised formulae without understanding what is in series and what is in parallel, and Paper 5 punishes anyone who has never written a method for a stranger to follow.

subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two IGCSE grades, with six papers. sections.heading: What IGCSE science means on your child's entry, route by route
paragraphs: Start with the document rather than the conversation. The entry form, or the exams officer's list, names a syllabus code and a set of paper numbers for each subject. Those two pieces of information tell a tutor more than an hour of discussion about how the child is finding science. Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 means three separate IGCSEs and nine papers in total. 0654 means Coordinated Sciences, one course awarded as two grades, with six papers. 0653 means Combined Science, one course and one grade. 0652 is Physical Science, chemistry and physics without biology.

The volume difference is the thing families underestimate. Three separate sciences is roughly three times the content of Combined Science and considerably more than Coordinated Sciences, spread across three times as many papers. That matters for revision planning far more than for difficulty: a student on three separate sciences in a Dubai school that also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies has a genuinely crowded Year 11, and a revision plan that ignores the arithmetic will fail in February.

Route choice also has a tail. Some sixth forms and some university courses prefer or specify separate sciences, particularly for medicine and engineering pathways. Others accept coordinated or double-award routes without comment. The only reliable method is to read the destination's own published entry requirement before the route is chosen in Year 9 or Year 10, rather than discovering the preference after results day when the option has closed.

Pearson's structure differs enough to matter. Its separate sciences, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, are single tier, so there is no Core and Extended decision, and experimental skills are assessed inside the written papers rather than in a dedicated practical paper. The Science Double Award 4SD0 covers all three sciences and is awarded as two grades. A student transferring between boards mid-course has changed what the examination asks them to do, not merely the order of the topics.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision and what it does to the ceiling
paragraphs: On Cambridge science syllabuses, Core and Extended are not difficulty settings applied to the same paper. They are different papers. Core candidates sit Paper 1, a multiple-choice paper, and Paper 3, a theory paper. Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4, which cover additional content at greater depth. Both sit a practical or alternative-to-practical paper. The grade range differs between the two tiers, so the decision taken in Year 10 sets the best outcome available at the end of Year 11.

The decision usually rests with the school, informed by Year 9 and Year 10 performance, and schools make it carefully. Where it goes wrong is in the margins. A student placed on Core because of a weak Year 9 who then improves substantially may be capped below what they could reach, and the window to move tier is narrow because Cambridge final entries close months before the exams. An Emirates Hills candidate sits the June series or the November series, and for June the entry closes in the spring, a good four months ahead of the first paper, with the exact day printed on the school's statement of entry. Work that backwards and the tier conversation belongs in Year 10, or in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest. A conversation in May about moving to Extended is a conversation that arrives after the door has shut.

This is the single most useful thing a tutor can contribute in Year 10, and almost nobody asks for it then. A specialist sitting one Extended past paper with a student can give a reasonably honest read on whether the tier fits. If the answer is that Extended is within reach with two terms of work, there is time to make the case to the school while the entry is still open. If the answer is that Core is the right place, the family stops worrying about a ceiling that was never the problem.

Tier also changes what revision should look like. An Extended candidate needs the additional content taught and then examined, with past questions filtered to the Extended papers only; Core past papers will mislead them about the depth expected. A Core candidate practising Extended papers wastes time on material that will not appear. Downloading the wrong tier's papers is one of the most common and least noticed revision errors in Year 11.

sections.heading: Paper 5 or Paper 6: the fifth of the grade nobody revises
paragraphs: On the Cambridge separate sciences, the practical component carries around a fifth of the total grade. Schools enter candidates for either Paper 5, a laboratory practical test, or Paper 6, an alternative-to-practical written paper. The choice is the centre's and depends largely on laboratory capacity. Both examine the same underlying skills, and both are examined in a way that content revision does not touch.

What the examiner is actually testing is procedural writing. Can the student describe a method precisely enough that a stranger could repeat it, including what is measured, how often and what is kept constant? Can they produce a results table with consistent significant figures and units in the headings rather than scattered through the cells? Can they choose a scale that uses the grid, plot accurately, draw a line of best fit that is a judgement rather than a join-the-dots, and read a gradient as a quantity with units? Can they identify one specific weakness in the method and propose a realistic improvement?

Those are five discrete skills and all five are trainable. A student who has never written a method for a stranger will write one that assumes the reader was in the room. A student who has never been told that an improvement must be specific will write that they would repeat the experiment more carefully, which earns nothing. Two or three focused sessions on these habits move marks reliably, which is a rare thing to be able to say in exam preparation.

One practical note on materials. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge and are not reproduced or supplied by a tutor. They are referenced, and the work is done from what your child's school provides, which has the advantage of being the right version for the series being sat. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so confirm the zone with the exams officer before building a plan around any published date.

sections.heading: Biology 0610: precision of language is the whole game
paragraphs: Biology at IGCSE looks like the memorising subject and is marked like a writing subject. The content is large and mostly straightforward; the marks are awarded for stating things exactly. A student who writes that water moves into the cell has described the outcome. A student who writes that water moves from a region of higher water potential to a region of lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane has answered the question. Both students understand osmosis. Only one scores.

The recurring losses are predictable across cohorts. Transport in plants is answered without naming xylem and phloem or without stating a direction. Enzyme questions describe the effect of temperature without mentioning the shape of the active site. Blood glucose control is explained with the hormones in the right order and the organs omitted. Inheritance questions are answered with a correct genetic diagram and no key, which costs a mark that was already earned in the student's head.

The repair is a vocabulary discipline rather than more reading. Each topic has perhaps a dozen words the mark scheme wants, and using them is a habit built by writing answers and having them marked strictly. Students find strict marking uncomfortable for about two weeks and then start writing differently, because the pattern becomes visible. This is the single clearest case in IGCSE science where marked written work beats any amount of revision guide highlighting.

Extended candidates have one additional trap: the supplementary content arrives late in Year 11 at many schools, so it is learnt once and never revisited. A tutor starting in January should establish immediately which supplementary topics have actually been taught, because the answer determines whether the plan is revision or teaching.
bullets: Name the structures: xylem, phloem, active site, alveoli, not generalities
State a direction of movement, not just that movement happens
Label genetic diagrams and include a key, every time
Check which Extended supplementary topics have actually been taught
Have written answers marked strictly for two weeks and the habit changes

sections.heading: Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625: the two calculation bottlenecks
paragraphs: In chemistry, the bottleneck is moles. Students who can define a mole lose marks across whole papers because the procedure is loose: they round before the final line, drop units between steps, or divide before working out which reagent is limiting. The fix is mechanical. Write the balanced equation. Write what is known under each species. Convert everything to moles before doing anything else. Show the substitution line even when the arithmetic is easy. Round once, at the end. That procedure, applied for three weeks, changes the mark on every quantitative question on the paper.

Electrolysis and the reactivity series provide the other reliable chemistry losses, and both fail for the same reason: the answer describes what is seen rather than what the particles are doing. An explanation that mentions bubbles at the cathode has described an observation. An explanation that names the ion, says where it moves and what it gains or loses, has answered the question. Organic nomenclature is a smaller but entirely avoidable loss, since the naming rules are finite and can be learnt in one session.

In physics, the bottleneck is algebra, and it is frequently misdiagnosed as a physics problem. A student who cannot rearrange an equation confidently will lose physics marks on questions they conceptually understand. Ten minutes of rearrangement practice at the start of a physics session often does more for the grade than the fifty minutes that follow. Circuits are the second bottleneck: series and parallel behaviour has to be understood rather than recalled, because the examiner will combine them in a way the textbook diagram did not.

Both subjects reward showing working, and both punish the student who performs the calculation on a calculator and writes only the answer. Method marks exist precisely for the lines that a confident student thinks are beneath them. In an exam where a fifth of the grade comes from the practical paper and half from theory, the cheapest available marks are the ones awarded for writing down what you did.

sections.heading: What three sciences actually cost in this market
paragraphs: The arithmetic is worth doing explicitly, because it is different for science than for a single subject. If a Year 11 is sitting three separate sciences and a family assumes a tutor for each, the monthly figure trebles immediately. Start from the cheapest workable plan rather than the most thorough one and add only what the evidence requires.

The cheapest workable plan is one weekly session on the weakest science, with the shared skills taught inside it. Graph work, significant figures, units, command words and method writing transfer across all three sciences, so an hour of practical-skills teaching in physics improves the biology and chemistry practical papers too. On published Dubai market estimates, one weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor sits at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, based on Bestimate's rate tables, with the hourly band at AED 150 to 300. Budget online tutoring is advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, which Bestimate estimates at AED 240 to 600 a month for one session a week.

The next step up is rotating cover across all three sciences in one weekly slot, which costs the same as one subject and requires a tutor confident at IGCSE level in all three. Only after that does a second weekly session make sense, and only if marked work shows two sciences failing rather than one. An IGCSE specialist in an exam year is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above by Bestimate, with TutorChase publishing AED 270; at two sessions a week that is AED 1,000 to 2,000 and more per month.

For comparison, published in-home one-to-one rates in Dubai run from AED 180 to 500 an hour, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799, against an online package advertised at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. IB Gram does not sell in-home visits in the UAE, so that band is market context rather than an option here. All of these are rates published by named providers and read in October 2026; they are not a price list, so ask for a current quote and use the free first lesson before deciding anything.
bullets: Start with one weekly session on the weakest science, not three tutors
Teach graphs, units and method writing once; the skills transfer across all three
Add a second session only when marked work shows two sciences failing
Rotating cover in one slot costs the same as one subject
Ask whether a quoted rate includes VAT and what the replacement terms are

sections.heading: Online lessons for a Year 11 with nine papers, and the permit question
paragraphs: A Year 11 on three separate sciences in a Dubai school has a crowded week before any tutoring is added. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, advising that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Those hours are real. A tutoring plan that assumes a Year 11 evening is empty is a plan that will be abandoned by February.

That is the practical case for online delivery rather than a philosophical one. A session that needs no travel at either end can start at the hour the student is actually free, can be moved by thirty minutes when the school run runs late, and can be recorded for review during revision week. Screen-sharing a graph and annotating it live is as good as paper for this work, and better for anything the student will want to look at again. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are an India-only service and there is no UAE office.

One thing worth verifying about any tutor your family engages, online or otherwise. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so be cautious of any figure quoted to you.

A related point about asking your child's own science teacher for private lessons. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also addresses serving students affiliated with the permit holder's school. Treat that as press-reported and check the current policy document, but do not assume the arrangement is straightforward.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes from the entry
process.description: The one message that saves a week: the syllabus code and paper numbers for each science, the tier if Cambridge, and whether the centre has entered your child for the practical test or the alternative paper. The school's exams officer has all of it.

process.title: A free first lesson that reads the mock
process.description: The matched tutor works through the most recent marked science papers against the published scheme, separating content gaps from technique losses and practical-paper losses. You hear an honest read on what the remaining weeks can do, then decide whether to continue.

process.title: One science first, with shared skills inside it
process.description: The plan starts with the weakest science and teaches the transferable skills there: graphs, units, significant figures, method writing and command words. Those carry into the other two papers at no extra cost, which is why this is the first step rather than a third tutor.

process.title: Weekly sessions with marked written work
process.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video on a held Gulf Standard Time slot, with notes afterwards and a question set for the week. The tutor marks that work strictly, because loosely marked practice teaches a student that a vague answer is acceptable.

process.title: A practical-skills block before the mock
process.description: Two or three sessions aimed only at Paper 5 or Paper 6 technique, because that component carries a fifth of the grade on the separate sciences and receives a fraction of the revision. It is the most reliably recoverable mark on the page.

process.title: A tier and route review in Year 10
process.description: If your child is still in Year 10, one session sitting an Extended past paper gives an honest read on whether the tier fits while the entry window is still open. That conversation is worth more in October than any amount of revision in February.

whyPoints.title: The code before the subject
whyPoints.description: 0610, 0620 and 0625 is a different brief from 0654 or 0653, and 4BI1 is different again. Matching a tutor to the code rather than to the word science is the difference between teaching the course and teaching a neighbouring one.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: Paper 5 and Paper 6 carry roughly a fifth of a separate-science grade and are examined as procedural skills. They get dedicated sessions rather than a mention in the final week, because they are the most reliably recoverable marks available.

whyPoints.title: Tier fit tested against a real paper
whyPoints.description: Whether Core or Extended is right is answerable by sitting one Extended past paper, not by discussion. Doing that in Year 10, while the entry window is open, is worth more than months of general revision later.

whyPoints.title: Shared skills taught once
whyPoints.description: Graphs, units, significant figures, method writing and command words transfer across all three sciences. Teaching them inside the weakest subject improves the other two papers without a second or third tutor.

whyPoints.title: Board material referenced, never supplied
whyPoints.description: Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson. A tutor references them and works from what the school provides, which is also the correct version for your child's series.

whyPoints.title: Rates with sources, delivery stated plainly
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Lessons are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time; there is no UAE office and no tutor visits a UAE address.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is doing separate, coordinated or combined science?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the syllabus code on the entry. Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 means three separate sciences and three IGCSE grades. 0654 is Coordinated Sciences, one course awarded as two grades. 0653 is Combined Science, one course and one grade. 0652 is Physical Science, chemistry and physics without biology. Pearson uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for separate sciences and 4SD0 for the Science Double Award. The subject name on a school timetable frequently does not distinguish between these, and the difference in content volume is roughly threefold.

faqs.question: Is Coordinated Sciences 0654 easier than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: It is less content rather than easier content, and it brings its own difficulty. The course covers all three sciences at reduced depth and is awarded as two IGCSE grades across six papers, so there is substantially less to learn than three separate specifications. The challenge is that questions move between biology, chemistry and physics without signalling it, so a student who revises the three in isolation gets caught by the switching. Tutoring for 0654 should treat it as one integrated course, which is why matching the tutor to the code matters more than matching to a single science.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 5 and Paper 6 in Cambridge sciences?
faqs.answer: Paper 5 is a laboratory practical test sat under exam conditions; Paper 6 is an alternative-to-practical written paper examining the same thinking on paper. The school chooses which its candidates sit, largely on laboratory capacity, and the component carries roughly a fifth of the grade on the separate sciences. Both reward the same five skills: writing a repeatable method, tabulating results with consistent significant figures, plotting a sensible graph, reading a gradient as a quantity with units, and suggesting one specific improvement. Ask the exams officer which paper your child is entered for before buying revision material.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended tier in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Only while the entry window is open, and it closes months before the exam. A Cambridge candidate in Dubai sits the June or the November series, and final entries for June are made in the spring, long before the first script -- ask the examinations officer for the precise day, because it is on the statement of entry rather than in any general guide. That is why a request made once the exam season has started arrives too late. If you suspect the tier is capping a capable student, the thing to do is sit one Extended past paper with a specialist and get an honest read, ideally in Year 10. If Extended looks reachable with two terms of work, there is time to make the case to the school while the decision is still live.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose biology marks when the answer looks right?
faqs.answer: Because IGCSE biology is marked on precision rather than on gist. Writing that water moves into the cell describes the outcome; writing that water moves from a higher to a lower water potential through a partially permeable membrane answers the question. The same pattern repeats across transport in plants, enzyme activity and blood glucose control, where the named structure or the direction of movement is the mark. Each topic has about a dozen words the scheme wants. Two weeks of strictly marked written answers changes how a student writes, which no amount of highlighting achieves.

faqs.question: What are the commonest IGCSE chemistry calculation mistakes?
faqs.answer: Rounding before the final line, dropping units between steps, and dividing before identifying the limiting reagent. All three produce a confident answer to a slightly different question. The procedure that fixes them is mechanical: write the balanced equation, write what is known under each species, convert everything to moles before doing anything else, show the substitution line even when the arithmetic is trivial, and round once at the end. Applied consistently for three weeks it changes the mark on every quantitative question on the paper, which is a large share of 0620 Paper 4.

faqs.question: My child understands physics but keeps getting numbers wrong. Why?
faqs.answer: Usually because the problem is algebra rather than physics, and it gets misdiagnosed. A student who cannot rearrange an equation reliably under time pressure will lose marks on questions they understand perfectly well. Ten minutes of rearrangement practice at the start of a physics session frequently does more for the grade than the fifty minutes that follow. The second common cause is circuits, where series and parallel behaviour has been memorised from a textbook diagram rather than understood, so a combined circuit in the exam looks unfamiliar when it is not.

faqs.question: Do I need three separate science tutors for a Year 11 on three sciences?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and it is the most expensive way to start. Begin with one weekly session on the weakest science and teach the transferable skills inside it: graph work, units, significant figures, method writing and command words all carry into the other two papers. Rotating cover across all three sciences in a single weekly slot costs the same as one subject and suits a diffuse problem. Add a second session only when marked work shows two sciences genuinely failing rather than one. Three tutors should be the conclusion of evidence, not the opening assumption.

faqs.question: Does the science route affect sixth form or university options?
faqs.answer: It can, and it is worth checking before the route is chosen rather than after results. Some sixth forms and some university courses prefer or specify separate sciences, particularly on medicine and engineering pathways, while others accept coordinated or double-award routes without comment. The only reliable method is to read the destination's own published entry requirement for the year of entry. No tutoring provider is the right authority on a named institution's requirement, and tutoring is not a requirement for any admissions or equivalency process.

faqs.question: Do the three science grades count towards the five subjects the UAE equivalency rule asks for?
faqs.answer: Sciences count towards the published requirement, which on the British track is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor states six IGCSE subjects are needed, which does not match the published rule. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation authority before relying on it.

faqs.question: Will a tutor give us Cambridge past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No, and an offer to hand over a library of board material should make you cautious about a provider. Past papers, mark schemes and syllabus documents belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing or distributing them is a copyright matter. A tutor references them and works from what your child's school supplies, which also has the practical advantage of being the correct version for the series being sat. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable, so the school's copy is the authoritative one.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a house in The Springs or Emirates Hills?
faqs.answer: No. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service exists in India only, and there is no UAE office. For science specifically, online delivery has a practical advantage: a graph or a results table shared on screen and annotated live can be saved and reviewed in revision week, which a sheet of paper left behind on a dining table cannot. It also means the session can shift by half an hour when the school run runs late.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget for IGCSE science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Published market estimates, not our prices. Bestimate's Dubai tables put one weekly hour with a qualified online subject tutor at roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month, with the hourly band at AED 150 to 300. Budget online tutoring is advertised from around AED 45 to 150 an hour, estimated at AED 240 to 600 a month for one session a week. An IGCSE specialist in an exam year is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Ask whether a quoted rate includes VAT and what the replacement terms are in writing.

faqs.question: How does a full Dubai timetable affect a science revision plan?
faqs.answer: It removes hours the plan assumed were free. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advising no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. A Year 11 sitting nine science papers therefore has a genuinely crowded week before tutoring is added. Count the usable weeks after mocks, the Eid period and family travel are subtracted, then decide how many sciences the plan can realistically target.

faqs.question: What if no tutor covers the science route my child is entered for?
faqs.answer: You are told before booking rather than afterwards. Cambridge and Pearson separate sciences at evening Gulf Standard Time slots are well covered. The combinations that occasionally are not include a specific coordinated or double-award route at an awkward hour, or a request arriving in the fortnight before a series. In that case you are offered the nearest available specialist and a slot that genuinely exists, or an honest no with a suggestion of what would help instead. No competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit at all.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-emirates-hi.closingBody: One short email to your child's exams officer answers the questions that matter: which syllabus codes, which tier, which paper numbers, and whether the centre has entered them for the practical test or the alternative paper. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time for families in Emirates Hills, The Springs, The Meadows, The Lakes, The Greens and The Views.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-green-commu.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE sciences - separate, coordinated and combined - for Years 9 to 11 across Green Community, Dubai Investments Park, Jebel Ali, Al Furjan and Dubai South.

intro.heading: Science has more deadlines than any other IGCSE subject, and they are not all in June
paragraphs: Most families plan backwards from the written papers and find that the plan has already failed. Science carries more fixed dates than any other IGCSE subject area, and three of them arrive before the papers do: the final entry deadline, which fixes the route and the tier months in advance; the practical component, where a centre uses a practical test rather than an alternative-to-practical paper; and the mock window, which exists to generate diagnostic data and is usually treated as a verdict instead.

Those dates matter more in science than elsewhere because a student taking three separate sciences is carrying three sets of them. Three entry decisions, potentially three practical arrangements, three mock papers to read and three timed-paper cycles to fit into the same eight to ten weeks. The arithmetic of that is what decides whether a Year 11 in this catchment finishes the preparation they started.

A fourth date sits underneath all of them and belongs to the family rather than to the school. The content phase has to end before the timed-paper window opens, because new material introduced inside that window displaces the practice that converts knowledge into marks. For one science that is a manageable judgement. For three it is a scheduling decision that has to be taken deliberately, or the third science simply stops being prepared.

The first fact to get right is which series your child sits. UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline to a Dubai family is handing them another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window.

The second is the resit timing, which is counter-intuitive and consequential. The checkable Pearson dates show that November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. A November resit therefore confirms in late January, which is tight against spring sixth-form deadlines and worth knowing before the resit is chosen rather than after.

Green Community is a practical place to plan this from. The community sits inside Dubai Investments Park, low-rise and walkable, with schools close by, and the school run is short enough that a family's time constraint is homework rather than travel. For three separate sciences that is the relevant constraint: three tutors in-home would mean three journeys a week, which is why families this side of the city often settle for one general science tutor by default.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Laboratory work stays at school under the teacher's supervision, as the specification requires. What follows is the calendar counted backwards, the practical component's own timing, what to do with mock data, and the AED bands with their sources. Two emails come before any booking: one to the exams officer about the practical arrangement and the centre's zone, and one to us with the marked papers.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-green-commu.programmesIntro: Which configuration a student is entered for changes how many calendars they are living on, which is the practical reason it matters here.

programmes.name: Three separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry and Physics as three qualifications and three certificates, with Cambridge codes 0610, 0620 and 0625 or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The deepest route in content and the heaviest in deadlines, because every fixed date exists three times over.
programmes.countryNote: In this catchment the practical consequence is scheduling rather than difficulty. Three sciences means three mock papers to read, three timed-paper cycles and potentially three practical arrangements, all inside the same eight to ten week window as every other subject's revision.

programmes.name: Coordinated or double-award science
programmes.description: All three disciplines in one integrated course counting as two certificates, with Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 the usual form. One set of papers covering the three disciplines together, and therefore one calendar rather than three.
programmes.countryNote: The scheduling advantage is real and underrated by families weighing this route. One entry decision, one mock to read, one timed-paper cycle. For a student already carrying eight or nine subjects, that difference is often worth more than the extra depth separate sciences would have provided.

programmes.name: Combined or single-award science
programmes.description: All three disciplines in one qualification counting as a single certificate, with Cambridge Combined Science 0653 and Physical Science 0652 as examples. The lightest load in both content and deadlines.
programmes.countryNote: One science certificate contributes one subject towards the five the Ministry of Education requires for British-track equivalency, so a combined-science student needs the remaining four from elsewhere on their timetable. That arithmetic should be checked in Year 10, while the entry can still change.

programmes.name: Years 7 to 9, before the calendar starts
programmes.description: No certificates and no external deadlines, with optional Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests available in March, May and October. The only period in the whole sequence with no fixed dates attached, which is exactly why gaps formed here are invisible.
programmes.countryNote: Families in Green Community and Dubai Investments Park who start in Year 9 are using the only window with no deadline pressure. The mathematics inside science - rearranging a relationship, handling prefixes, reading a scale - is cheap to build here and expensive to build during a Year 11 mock cycle.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-green-commu.subjectsIntro: Below are the science components with the point in the calendar at which each one should be secure. Timing is the organising idea here, so the notes follow it rather than listing topics.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The most reliable weakness in this catchment and usually taught early enough to be repaired. Should be secure by the end of Year 10, because every later topic that needs formula transposition rests on the same skill.

subjects.name: Physics: moments, pressure and energy
subjects.description: Multi-step questions where an unconverted prefix invalidates the final answer. Worth drilling in the term before mocks, since the fix is a habit of writing units at every line rather than new content.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Should be automatic before the mock window, because it appears inside longer questions where an early set-up error propagates silently. Masses to moles first, always, is the enforceable rule.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and rates
subjects.description: Often taught late in Year 11, which makes it the chemistry content most likely to be unfinished at the mocks. Worth asking the school when it falls in the scheme of work.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and homeostasis
subjects.description: Content-heavy and spread across both years. The marks problem is answer structure rather than coverage, so it can be drilled at any point and is cheapest before the mock cycle begins.

subjects.name: Biology: inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Procedural once the cross is understood, which makes it one of the fastest gains available late. The explanation that follows the cross is where the marks actually sit.

subjects.name: The practical or alternative-to-practical paper
subjects.description: Assessed in writing and, where a practical test is used, often sitting earlier than the written papers. Four to six sessions of convention work is the highest-yield block in the subject and it has to happen before that date.

subjects.name: Coordinated sciences papers
subjects.description: All three disciplines interleaved in one paper, which rewards fast switching. Interleaved practice should start at least ten weeks out, because revising by discipline and then meeting them mixed costs orientation time.

subjects.name: Mathematics inside science
subjects.description: Transposition, prefixes and reading a scale. Cheapest to build in Year 9 or 10 and most often diagnosed in Year 11, where it is misread as three separate science weaknesses.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: "State", "describe", "explain" and "discuss" set different depths. A behaviour rather than content, so it moves in weeks and can be targeted even after the mocks have been marked.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the written papers, three sciences at once
paragraphs: Start at the papers and walk back. The last eight to ten weeks are the timed-paper window, and for a separate-science student that window has to accommodate three subjects plus everything else on the timetable. Before it, the mock papers, whose purpose is to generate data about habits rather than to produce a verdict. Before that, the final entry deadline, which fixes route and tier. And somewhere in the middle, the practical component, which does not wait for the written papers where a practical test is used.

Laid out that way, two things become obvious. The first is that the content phase has to end earlier than families assume. A student still meeting new chemistry content eight weeks out cannot both learn it and run a timed-paper cycle in three subjects, and one of the two will be sacrificed by default rather than by decision. The second is that the entry decision - separate, coordinated or combined; Core or Extended - is taken long before anyone feels any urgency about it.

For a coordinated or combined student the same map applies with one set of dates instead of three, and that scheduling advantage is genuinely worth weighing when the route is chosen. One mock to read, one timed cycle, one practical arrangement. For a student already carrying eight or nine subjects, that can matter more than the extra depth the separate route offers.

Our first question to a Green Community family is therefore which configuration and which series, and then where in this map they currently are. The answer determines what the available weeks can achieve, and it also determines what we should decline to promise.
