sections.heading: The practical component has its own date, and families miss it
paragraphs: Cambridge assesses practical skills in writing, through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre's arrangement. Where a practical test is used, it is a separate component with its own slot, and that slot frequently falls before the written papers. Students who have mentally filed practical preparation as something to do last find the component already behind them.

That is one of very few genuinely avoidable losses in IGCSE science, and avoiding it takes one email. Ask the exams officer which arrangement applies for each science, when each component falls, and which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one, so the zone answer is worth keeping in writing.

The preparation itself is short and high-yield, which is why the timing is frustrating rather than merely unfortunate. Four to six sessions covers it: justifying apparatus choices rather than listing them, stating each control operationally with a measurement rather than in principle, tabulating with units in the headings, choosing graph scales that use most of the grid, and describing a procedure a stranger could follow without guessing.

Each of those has an expected form the examiner is looking for. "Keep the temperature constant" earns less than "hold the water bath at 30 degrees Celsius, checked with a thermometer, for every run". Units in the table cells rather than the headings lose marks nothing in the student's understanding justifies losing. The hands-on work itself happens in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision as the specification requires, and no tutor substitutes for that.

sections.heading: The November series as a resit route, and the January gap
paragraphs: UAE candidates have two sittings a year, which makes a resit a real option rather than a theoretical one. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs a May/June window and a November window. The February/March series is offered in India only, so it is not available to a Dubai candidate whatever a page elsewhere may imply.

The timing of the November route is where families need the detail. The checkable Pearson dates give it: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results, by contrast, reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day. So a June result lands in August and a November result lands in the second half of January.

That gap matters when a resit is being used to meet a condition. A sixth-form offer that needs a particular science grade, confirmed in late January, is tight against spring deadlines and in some cases arrives after a decision has had to be taken. The question to ask the receiving school is not whether they accept a November resit but by what date they need the result, and to ask it before the resit is entered rather than after.

Practically, a November resit also compresses the preparation into the autumn term alongside a new year's work, which is a scheduling problem rather than an academic one. For a student resitting one science while starting a sixth-form programme, one focused block on the specific habits the original script exposed usually beats a second full pass through the syllabus.

sections.heading: What to do with three sets of mock science results
paragraphs: Mock results arrive and the natural response is to react to the three grades. A 4 in physics prompts a physics tutor; a 6 in biology prompts relief. The more useful response is to ignore all three grades for an hour and read the three scripts side by side, because what matters is the pattern across them rather than the ranking between them.

Read that way, the three scripts frequently say the same thing in three accents. Prefixes mishandled in physics, unit errors in chemistry, a scale misread in biology: one mathematics problem, three subjects, one fix. Or command terms answered at a single depth in all three, which is one behaviour. When that pattern appears, hiring three science tutors is the wrong purchase and one tutor working on the shared cause is the right one.

Where the scripts genuinely disagree - chemistry failing on mole set-up while biology fails on answer structure and physics is fine - then the problems are separate and the question becomes which to spend the remaining weeks on. The answer is not the lowest grade but the largest recoverable loss. A 5 hiding twelve habit marks is worth more attention than a 4 reflecting genuinely unfinished content, because habits move in weeks and content does not.

The one thing not to do with mock data is treat it as a prediction. Grade boundaries are set after each series is marked, and a mock is marked against a boundary that no longer applies. We do not publish or distribute boundary tables, which are the boards' copyright material, and anyone converting a mock mark into a confident final grade is guessing.

sections.heading: Fitting three timed-paper cycles into eight weeks
paragraphs: A separate-science student in the final run has three subjects needing timed practice, plus everything else on an eight or nine subject timetable. The arithmetic does not work if each science is given a full weekly cycle, and the usual outcome is that the third one quietly stops happening.

The workable version staggers them. One science takes the full cycle for three weeks while the other two take single timed questions; then they rotate. The marking is what makes staggering viable, because a ranked habit list from one science usually transfers: a student who stops writing units in physics is not writing them in chemistry either, and fixing the habit once improves two scripts.

The practical-style paper should be inside the cycle rather than outside it, because it is marked on conventions that decay without use. A student who drilled apparatus justification in January and has not written a control statement since April will write a vague one in the exam. One practical-style question a week through the final run costs ten minutes and protects the marks the earlier block bought.

External marking matters more as the weeks compress, not less, because the whole purpose of the cycle is to find habits. Self-marking over-rewards, since the student knows what they intended to write and reads their own shorthand generously. One paper marked properly produces more usable information than three marked by the student, and in a compressed window usable information is the scarce resource.

sections.heading: Ramadan and the UAE school year inside a science plan
paragraphs: Any plan written for a UAE family has to survive Ramadan, and almost no page in this market mentions it. School hours shorten, households reorganise their evening around iftar, and a late-afternoon tutoring slot becomes either an early-afternoon or a post-iftar one for the month. Ramadan also moves roughly eleven days earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, so it currently falls inside the spring term.

For a Year 11 science student that timing is awkward, because it can land inside the timed-paper window. The answer is not to pause. Quantitative fluency - transposition, prefixes, mole set-up - decays faster than content knowledge, so protecting frequency over length is the right adjustment: two shorter sessions a week hold more than one long one while a student is fasting, and a complete pause usually means relearning in the first week back.

The rest of the UAE year has its own shape worth planning for. The long summer break between Year 10 and Year 11 is the only stretch with no competing demands, which makes it the natural window for the practical convention block and for fixing the mathematics inside science. The winter break interrupts the term in which mocks are usually prepared. Neither is an obstacle if it is in the plan.

Because nobody is travelling to your address, all of this is a diary exercise rather than a negotiation. Moving a slot from 5pm to 2pm for a month is a change two calendars absorb. Moving an in-home tutor's commute by three hours for a month is a request they may not be able to accommodate, and that asymmetry is one of the quieter practical arguments for online delivery here.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs here, and the three-tutor arithmetic
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read October 2026 and attributed. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors advertising to AED 500. Specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

For a separate-science student the figures multiply in a way no competitor page addresses. Three disciplines done properly means three specialists, and in-home that means three journeys to the same address each week. From Green Community that is at least feasible; from Dubai South or Emaar South it is not realistic at any price, which is why families further out settle for one general science tutor by default rather than by choice.

Online the three-tutor arrangement is ordinary, and most families should still start with one. Three new tutors means three new homework streams arriving in the same week on a timetable that is already full, and the mock scripts read side by side usually show that one shared cause explains much of the pattern anyway.

Convert that to a monthly figure per discipline, because per discipline is the unit a separate-science household actually commits to. Dubai rate guidance estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Read across Biology, Chemistry and Physics, the middle band becomes AED 1,800-3,600 a month and the specialist band passes AED 3,000 before anybody has marked a paper. The published packages sharpen the comparison a Green Community parent is really making: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, against AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits, which is roughly double the monthly outlay for half the number of contact points, with a journey into Dubai Investments Park attached to each one. None of these are IB Gram prices; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Permits, equivalency and how to start on the calendar
paragraphs: The permit question usually arrives late, once an entry deadline has already fixed the route and the tier and a parent wants somebody in place this week. Answer it first instead. Private tutoring in the UAE requires a permit: the private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years - so a science tutor who will not discuss it is not avoiding a cost. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, which is why the cheapest online science hours advertised into this catchment are often legitimately held by undergraduates. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule, so any figure quoted to you for that has been invented. One line is firmer than the rest: never arrange paid tuition with your child's own class teacher, however convenient it looks with the practical component weeks away.

On equivalency, the configuration decides the arithmetic. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. Separate sciences contribute three certificates, coordinated two and combined one, which is a Year 10 check rather than a Year 12 discovery. One page ranking in this market states the requirement as six subjects, which is not what the published rule says.

What we do not claim: IB Gram is not KHDA approved, a KHDA Educational Services Permit being issued to training institutes with physical premises that we neither hold nor occupy. We claim no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation or partnership, publish no self-asserted rating, promise no grade or improvement figure, and quote no statistic without its source and date. We also do not host or distribute board papers, mark schemes or boundary tables, which are copyright material.

To start, send the configuration, the codes if you have them, the series your child is entered for, and a photograph of the most recent marked science paper - or all three papers, if there are three. A specialist reads them together, says whether the pattern is one shared cause or three separate problems, and teaches a free one-to-one trial lesson online. The written diagnosis is yours whether or not you continue, and if nobody suitable is free at your hour we say so and offer alternatives.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science exams held for a student in Green Community?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE in the June series and the November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, so any February window quoted to a Dubai family belongs to another country's calendar. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window. The written papers are only part of it: where a centre uses a practical test rather than an alternative-to-practical paper, that component has its own date, frequently before the written papers. Ask the exams officer for both.

faqs.question: Does the science practical sit on a different date from the written papers?
faqs.answer: Where a centre uses a practical test rather than an alternative-to-practical paper, yes, and it frequently falls earlier. That catches out students who have mentally filed practical preparation as the last thing to do, and it is one of very few genuinely avoidable losses in the subject. One email to the exams officer settles which arrangement applies for each science and when each component falls, and it is worth asking which Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in at the same time.

faqs.question: How late can we leave the timed-paper cycle for three sciences?
faqs.answer: Eight to ten weeks is the realistic minimum, and for three separate sciences it has to be staggered rather than run three times in parallel. One science takes the full cycle for three weeks while the other two take single timed questions, then they rotate. That also means the content phase must finish before the window opens: a student still meeting new chemistry content eight weeks out cannot both learn it and run a cycle in three subjects, and the third science quietly stops happening.

faqs.question: Is a November resit a good idea for a science grade?
faqs.answer: It can be, and the timing needs checking first. The checkable Pearson dates show November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the next day. So a November result lands in the second half of January, which is tight against spring sixth-form deadlines. The question to put to the receiving school is not whether they accept a November resit but by what date they need the result, asked before the entry rather than after.

faqs.question: How should we read three sets of mock science results?
faqs.answer: Side by side, and ignore the three grades for the first hour. Read that way, the scripts often say the same thing in three accents: prefixes mishandled in physics, unit errors in chemistry, a misread scale in biology - one mathematics problem, three subjects, one fix. Or command terms answered at one depth in all three, which is one behaviour. When that pattern appears, three science tutors is the wrong purchase and one tutor working the shared cause is the right one.

faqs.question: Which is the better use of the summer before Year 11?
faqs.answer: Practical conventions and the mathematics inside science, because the summer is the only stretch in the whole sequence with nothing competing for it. The practical component is marked on precision and its conventions are learnable in four to six sessions: apparatus justified, controls stated operationally with a measurement, units in table headings, graph scales using most of the grid. The mathematics - transposition, prefixes, reading a scale - is cheap now and expensive during a mock cycle, where it is usually misdiagnosed as three science weaknesses.

faqs.question: Does the configuration change how many deadlines we are managing?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Three separate sciences means three entry decisions, three mock papers to read, three timed-paper cycles and potentially three practical arrangements. A coordinated or double-award course covers all three disciplines in one integrated qualification, so there is one of each. For a student already carrying eight or nine subjects, that scheduling advantage is sometimes worth more than the extra depth separate sciences provide, and it is worth weighing when the entry decision is still open in Year 10.

faqs.question: When does the route decision for science actually close?
faqs.answer: At the final entry deadline, which sits months before the series and is set by the centre to board deadlines. In practice schools ask for decisions earlier than that, so the window is Year 10 rather than Year 11. That matters because the decision caps or releases the attainable grade on a Core or Foundation entry, and it also determines how many science certificates a student ends with, which feeds the Ministry of Education's five-subject equivalency rule. Ask the school when its internal deadline falls.

faqs.question: What should happen to science sessions during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: The hour moves and the frequency should be protected. School hours shorten and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot typically becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. Quantitative fluency - transposition, prefixes, mole set-up - decays faster than content knowledge, so two shorter sessions a week hold more than one long one while a student is fasting. Because nobody is travelling to your address, the change is a diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute.

faqs.question: Can one tutor realistically cover three sciences in the final weeks?
faqs.answer: For a coordinated or combined course, yes, because the qualification itself is integrated. For three separate sciences at Extended level, the honest answer is that one tutor will be strong in one discipline and approximate in the other two, and at that level the mark schemes reward discipline-specific precision. The compromise most families here should make is to start with one specialist chosen on the evidence of the three mock scripts, and to add a second only if the next set of marks supports it.

faqs.question: Why does the content phase have to end so early?
faqs.answer: Because the timed-paper cycle is what converts content into marks, and it needs eight to ten weeks for three sciences. New content introduced inside that window displaces the practice, so the student finishes knowing more and scoring the same. That is the mechanism behind the familiar pattern of a conscientious late push producing no change in the result. If you are already inside the window, the honest plan is habit repair on what the mock scripts showed rather than covering the missing material.

faqs.question: Do you provide science past papers and mark schemes to work from?
faqs.answer: We do not host or distribute them. Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and specifications are copyright material, and circulating unreleased content is a malpractice exposure for the student. We reference and link the official sources on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, and we work from the copies your child's school is licensed to provide. A service offering a complete library of papers, or material not yet released, is worth declining on that basis rather than negotiating over.

faqs.question: How many science certificates does UAE equivalency count?
faqs.answer: As many as the configuration earns: three for separate sciences, two for a coordinated or double award, one for a combined single award. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. A combined-science student therefore needs four of the five from elsewhere, which is a Year 10 check.

faqs.answer: A written diagnosis that is yours whether or not you continue. Send all three marked science papers if there are three, and the matched specialist - not a salesperson - teaches a real one-to-one lesson online built on them, finishing by writing down whether the pattern across the scripts is one shared cause or three separate failures, and what the weeks remaining before your child's series can realistically achieve. No card details are required to book it and there is no package to agree beforehand.

intro.heading: What "science" means on an IGCSE timetable, and why it changes the tutoring
paragraphs: Parents in Hor Al Anz ask for a science tutor. Cambridge and Pearson do not sell science. They sell Physics, Chemistry and Biology as separate qualifications with separate syllabus codes, separate papers and separate mark schemes, plus a Coordinated Sciences route that compresses all three into two grades. The first job of an IGCSE science tutor in Hor Al Anz is therefore to establish which of those a student is actually sitting, because the revision plan for Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 shares maybe half its content with the plan for three separate Cambridge sciences, and almost none of its paper structure.

Schools in the Deira belt split both ways. Some enter the whole cohort for Coordinated Sciences 0654 and use the spare curriculum time for a sixth or seventh subject. Others run three separate sciences for the students aiming at IB Diploma HL or A Level, and Coordinated for the rest. A student can also sit two separate sciences and drop the third. Until you know which, a tutor cannot tell you whether electromagnetic induction is on the paper or whether it was trimmed out of the Coordinated subset.

The second thing that changes the tutoring is tier. Cambridge IGCSE sciences are tiered: Core candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3 and can reach grade C at best; Extended candidates sit Paper 2 and Paper 4 and the grade ceiling opens to A*. A student put on Core in Year 10 because a baseline test went badly will carry that ceiling into results day unless somebody notices and the school agrees to move them. That decision has a deadline attached to it, and the deadline sits with the exams officer, not with the parent.

Then there is the practical. UAE candidates in a school centre sit Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, in almost every case. It is a written paper about practical work: reading a thermometer scale drawn at an angle, spotting why a result is anomalous, suggesting a control variable, naming a hazard and a sensible precaution. It is marked on laboratory thinking, not on laboratory manual dexterity, which is exactly why it can be taught over live video with a shared screen and a scanned question paper.

What an online IGCSE science tuition Dubai session looks like in practice is narrow. A tutor picks one paper, one question cluster and one error pattern, works it with the student in real time, then sets a short piece of timed work for the next session. Three subjects and four papers is far too much ground to cover generally; the only version of this that moves a grade is the version that names the topic and the paper every single week.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences (4PH1, 4CH1, 4BI1) are untiered and sat in May/June and November
Paper 6 is a written paper about practical work, not a laboratory assessment
UAE centres sit the June and November Cambridge series; the February/March series is offered to India only

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.programmesIntro: A science tutor working with a Hor Al Anz family needs to know where the student sits in the wider school structure, because the IGCSE science grade is the gatekeeper for everything above it.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: The two-year qualification most British-curriculum schools in Dubai use at 16. Cambridge sciences are tiered into Core and Extended; Pearson International GCSE sciences are untiered with one paper set for all candidates. Grades run 9 to 1 on Pearson and A* to G on most Cambridge science syllabuses, which is why a Hor Al Anz parent comparing two siblings' reports can be looking at two different scales for the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, IGCSE sits under KHDA oversight at school level while the qualification itself is awarded by Cambridge or Pearson in the UK. KHDA inspects the school; the board sets the paper. A Deira school's inspection band tells you something about teaching quality across the building and nothing about whether a particular Year 11 science set is on track for the grade it needs.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The IB alternative at the same age, assessed on four criteria rather than papers: knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, reflecting on the impacts of science. Students moving from MYP sciences into an IGCSE science set mid-course find the content familiar and the assessment alien, because nothing in MYP trains a student to answer a four-mark structured question in ninety seconds.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai schools within reach of Hor Al Anz run MYP to Year 9 then switch to IGCSE, or run both tracks in parallel. Families who transfer across the city mid-year often cross that boundary without being told it exists. The gap shows up first in Paper 2 technique and in the habit of writing paragraphs where the mark scheme wants three short labelled points.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Where strong IGCSE science students go next in Dubai if they do not choose A Level. DP Chemistry HL assumes fluency with moles and ionic equations from day one; DP Physics HL assumes algebraic rearrangement that IGCSE Core never demanded. The internal assessment is a single scientific investigation written by the student and marked against published criteria.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, which widens DP capacity for students currently in Year 10 and 11 across the older districts. A student who wants Chemistry HL two years from now needs the Extended tier now, because the Core subset omits content the HL course treats as assumed knowledge.

programmes.name: International A Level Sciences
programmes.description: The other post-16 science route, modular at AS and A2 and examined in the same June and November windows as IGCSE. A Level Physics builds directly on the IGCSE Extended treatment of forces, fields and electricity; students arriving from the Core subset meet three topics in term one they have never formally studied.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at grade E or 3 or better. Science grades count toward that five. Arabic and Islamic Education do not count toward it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.subjectsIntro: These are the science subjects and sub-topics Hor Al Anz families most often ask about by name, with the specific place marks are lost rather than a general description of the course.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Marks drain out of three places: unit conversion in moment and pressure calculations, ray diagrams where the normal is not drawn, and electricity questions where series and parallel are read the wrong way round. Extended Paper 4 rewards a student who writes the formula, substitutes, then evaluates, because method marks survive an arithmetic slip.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Mole calculations and ionic equations carry the Extended grade. The single most common avoidable loss is an unbalanced equation in a question that then asks for a calculation from it, because every downstream mark depends on the coefficients. Organic nomenclature and the homologous series are high-yield and quick to fix.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Biology looks like the memorisable one and marks are lost on command terms instead. Describe wants what happened; explain wants why; suggest wants an applied answer to an unfamiliar context. Transport in plants, enzymes and the kidney produce the most mark-scheme mismatches in Extended Paper 4.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Coordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: A compressed subset of all three sciences awarding two identical grades. The risk is revising from a single-science textbook and spending hours on content the Coordinated subset excludes. A tutor's first task here is a syllabus audit against the school's entry code, before any teaching happens.

subjects.name: Paper 6: Alternative to Practical
subjects.description: Graph plotting with a correctly chosen scale, identifying an anomalous result, naming a control variable, improving a method, and stating a hazard with a matched precaution. It is predictable to the point of being drillable, and it is the paper most students have practised least.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: No tiering, so one paper set covers the full grade range, and the formula sheet convention differs from Cambridge. Students who move school mid-course sometimes revise the wrong board's required-practical list for a term before anyone catches it.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Content overlaps heavily with Cambridge 0620 but the question style is longer-stemmed and more data-led. Titration arithmetic and the reactivity series appear in forms a Cambridge-trained student finds unfamiliar in wording rather than in substance.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Heavier on experimental interpretation than its Cambridge counterpart, with extended-response questions that need structured paragraphs. The genetics and ecology sections are where students who learned from Cambridge resources find the gaps.

subjects.name: Combined Science and Double Award routes
subjects.description: Different schools in the Deira belt use different names for similar things. Checking the entry code on the statement of entry is the only reliable way to know what a student is sitting, and it is a two-minute job that prevents a term of misdirected revision.

subjects.name: Maths support alongside science
subjects.description: A large share of lost Physics marks are maths marks: standard form, rearranging an equation with the subject on the bottom, reading a gradient off a line of best fit. Fixing those inside the science session is usually faster than a separate maths course.

sections.heading: What a Hor Al Anz parent is actually buying when they search for a science tutor
paragraphs: A search for an IGCSE science tutor in Hor Al Anz is a search for one of three different services, and getting the wrong one wastes a term. The first is remediation: the student has gaps from Year 9 or from a school transfer and needs content taught properly for the first time. The second is technique: the content is there, the mock mark is not, and the problem is command terms, paper timing and method presentation. The third is tier management: the student is on Core and needs to be on Extended, or is on Extended and is drowning.

These need different tutors and different session shapes. Remediation is slow and sequential and needs a tutor willing to go back two years. Technique work is fast, paper-driven and can move a grade in six to eight weeks because nothing new is being learned. Tier management is mostly a conversation with the school's exams officer, and the useful thing a tutor does is produce evidence from timed papers that makes the case one way or the other.

Diagnosing which one applies takes a marked mock paper and about forty minutes. A student losing marks evenly across every topic has a content problem. A student scoring well on recall questions and badly on four-and-five-mark structured questions has a technique problem. A student capped at grade C on every paper they sit is on the Core tier and no amount of tutoring changes the ceiling. That diagnosis is what the free trial lesson is for, and it should happen before anybody buys a block of sessions.

The honest version of this is that the third case is the most urgent and the least often spotted. A Core entry made in Year 10 on the basis of one baseline test follows a student to results day. If the IB Diploma or an A Level science is the plan, a grade C ceiling closes that door, and the window to change the entry closes months before the exam.
bullets: Content gap: marks lost evenly across topics, needs sequential reteaching
Technique gap: recall fine, structured questions weak, fixable in weeks
Tier cap: every paper capped at C, needs a school-level entry decision
Diagnosis needs one marked mock paper, not a general conversation

sections.heading: The syllabus codes behind the word "science", and why the code matters more than the subject name
paragraphs: Every IGCSE science question paper is tied to a numbered syllabus. The number is printed on the statement of entry the school issues, and it is the single most useful piece of information a parent can bring to a first tutoring session. Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, IGCSE Chemistry 0620 and IGCSE Biology 0610 are the three separate sciences. Coordinated Sciences 0654 is the double award. Pearson Edexcel runs 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 for the same three subjects with a different paper structure and no tiering.

The practical consequence is that two students in the same Hor Al Anz building, both described by their parents as doing IGCSE science, can have almost nothing in common in their revision. One is revising four papers across three subjects with a tiered grade ceiling. The other is revising two papers for a double award that excludes several topics the first student must know. Buying generic science tutoring for either one produces a tutor teaching to the wrong specification.

Board differences are smaller in content than in presentation, and presentation is where marks live. Cambridge supplies a formula sheet with a particular set of relationships; Pearson supplies a different one. Cambridge Extended Paper 4 is structured, multi-part and tightly marked; Pearson's untiered papers run longer stems with more data interpretation. A student who switched schools between Year 10 and Year 11 may have been taught one and entered for the other, and the first time anyone notices is a mock where the paper looks unfamiliar.

The fix is clerical and takes ten minutes. Find the statement of entry, read the syllabus codes, and tell the tutor. Everything downstream, from which past papers to use to which topics to ignore, follows from those four digits.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks are actually lost, paper by paper
paragraphs: Mark schemes are published, which means the places students lose marks are knowable rather than mysterious. Across the three Cambridge sciences the pattern is consistent enough to plan against. On multiple-choice Paper 1 and Paper 2, losses cluster on questions with a negative in the stem and on questions where two options are both defensible and one is more precise. The fix is slow reading, not more content.

On the theory Papers 3 and 4, the dominant loss is command-term mismatch. A question that says state wants a short factual answer and gives no credit for explanation. A question that says explain gives no credit for a description. A question that says suggest expects the student to apply known science to an unfamiliar situation and accepts several answers. Students who write more than the question asks lose time and gain nothing; students who write less than it asks lose marks they knew the content for.

Physics adds a numerical layer. Method marks are awarded for the correct relationship and correct substitution even when the final number is wrong, which means a student who writes nothing but an answer loses everything on an arithmetic slip. Writing the formula, substituting, then stating the answer with a unit is worth training as a reflex, because it converts a zero into two marks several times a paper.

Chemistry's single biggest avoidable loss is an unbalanced equation feeding a calculation. Biology's is the enzyme, transport and excretion cluster, where students reproduce a memorised paragraph instead of answering the specific question asked. Both are diagnosable from one marked past paper and both respond quickly to targeted work.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the grade ceiling
paragraphs: The Core and Extended tier choice in Cambridge sciences is the most consequential decision in a student's IGCSE science career and it is often made by someone the family never speaks to. Core candidates sit the easier paper pair and the maximum grade available is C. Extended candidates sit the harder pair and can reach A*. The content differs too: the Extended syllabus includes material simply absent from Core, so a Core student has not merely been assessed more gently, they have not been taught several topics.

The case for Core is real. A student who would score poorly across the whole Extended paper can come out with a secure C on Core rather than an insecure E on Extended, and for a student heading to a vocational route or a subject where science is not a prerequisite, that is a sensible trade. The case against is equally real: a C ceiling closes IB Diploma HL sciences and most A Level science options, and the student usually does not understand that at the time.

What makes this a tutoring question rather than a school question is evidence. A school moves a student between tiers on the strength of timed-paper performance, not on a parent's request. Six weeks of Extended past papers under timed conditions, marked honestly, produces exactly the evidence a head of science needs to see. If the papers say Extended is viable, the conversation becomes easy. If they say it is not, the family has made an informed decision instead of a hopeful one.

Timing matters because entries are submitted months before the exam window and the school's internal deadline sits earlier still. A tier conversation started in the spring term of Year 11 is usually too late for the next series. Started early in Year 11, it is straightforward. Parents in Hor Al Anz whose children are currently in Year 10 have the most room to act.

sections.heading: Paper 6 and the practical question: how experimental skills are examined without a laboratory
paragraphs: The question every parent asks about online science tutoring is the practical one. If lessons happen over video, how does a student prepare for the practical? The answer is that for almost every UAE candidate in a school centre, the practical is already a written paper. Cambridge offers a practical test option, but the Alternative to Practical paper is what the overwhelming majority of international centres enter candidates for, and it tests reasoning about experiments rather than the performance of them.

What that paper actually asks is narrow and repetitive across series. Read a measuring instrument shown in a diagram, sometimes deliberately drawn at an awkward angle. Record results in a table with correct headings and units. Choose a sensible scale and plot points accurately. Draw a line or curve of best fit. Identify an anomalous result and say why it is anomalous. Name the independent, dependent and control variables. Suggest one improvement to the method and explain why it helps. State a hazard and give a precaution that actually addresses it.

Every one of those is drillable on a shared screen, and most are better drilled that way than in a busy school laboratory, because the tutor can mark a plotted graph point by point against the mark scheme while the student watches. Students lose marks on this paper for small, repeatable reasons: a scale that uses awkward intervals, a line of best fit drawn through the anomaly, a precaution that is really just a restatement of the hazard.

The practical work a student does at school still matters for understanding. But the marks come from the written paper, and the written paper rewards a student who has practised the specific question types rather than one who has handled the most apparatus. That is the honest reason online delivery does not disadvantage a science candidate here.

sections.heading: The exam calendar counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. The February/March series exists but Cambridge offers it to India only, so a Dubai parent reading a revision schedule built around a spring sitting is reading a plan for a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November each year.

Counting backwards from the June series is how a tutoring plan gets built. The school's internal entry deadline comes first and is usually set weeks before the board's own final-entry date, because the exams officer has to collate a whole cohort. Then mocks, typically in the winter term. Then the specification-coverage checkpoint, where any topic not yet taught becomes a known risk. Then the timed-paper phase, which is where most of the grade movement happens. Then the exam window itself, then results.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable per zone. Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a Dubai family, that means the timetable to trust is the one the school's exams officer issues, not one found through a search.

Pearson's published dates give a useful illustration of how long the tail is. Its November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November results have historically reached students in January; November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. Always open the live official timetable rather than relying on a restated date, because provisional timetables are revised.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs around Hor Al Anz, read as a monthly figure
paragraphs: Most published tutoring prices in Dubai are hourly, which is the least useful way for a family to think about them. A parent is deciding whether to add a recurring line to the household budget, so the number that matters is the monthly one. Bestimate's Dubai tutoring rate work puts weekly one-hour sessions at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are market figures, not IB Gram's price list.

The hourly bands behind them are published by the providers themselves. EdFlik advertises online tutoring from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52, which is the university-student and group-adjacent end of the market. Unitors publishes IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 an hour and IB from AED 200. TutorChase lists around AED 270 for specialist work, and Bestimate's specialist band runs AED 200 to 450 and above. BartyED sits at AED 650 for premium named tutors. Monthly packages circulating in the market include roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions.

Three separate sciences changes the arithmetic in a way single-subject pricing hides. A triple-science student in Year 11 needing weekly support in all three is buying three sessions a week, not one. At mid-band market rates that is a materially different monthly commitment from one maths session, and it is the point at which families usually decide to prioritise the two weakest sciences rather than cover all three thinly.

What a parent can verify before paying anything: the hourly figure, whether it is per sixty minutes or per lesson of some other length, whether VAT is included in the quoted number, what happens to a cancelled session, and whether a trial lesson exists and on what condition. Those five questions catch most of the surprises, and a provider who will not answer them in writing has told you something useful.

sections.heading: Online rather than in-home, and the plain statement of what IB Gram sells
paragraphs: A family in Hor Al Anz searching for a science tutor often pictures someone at the dining table. That model exists in Dubai and the published in-home band is AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, against AED 150 to 300 for a comparably qualified tutor working online. The gap is not a quality premium. It is the cost of a round trip across the city and the dead time inside it.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no tutor will arrive at an address in Dubai. Every UAE lesson is delivered one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for the paper and the mark scheme. Saying that plainly is more useful to a parent than discovering it after a booking.

The argument for online delivery on a science page is specific rather than general. A Hor Al Anz family hiring locally is choosing from the specialists who will travel to Hor Al Anz on a Tuesday at five. A family hiring online is choosing from specialists who teach Cambridge 0620 Extended every week, regardless of where they live. For a student who needs mole calculations rather than science in the abstract, that difference is the whole point.

There is also a practical gain that matters in this part of Dubai. A video session can start fifteen minutes after the school bus arrives, can move to a later slot during Ramadan without renegotiating a driver's route, and can be rescheduled for a mock week without anyone writing off a journey. Across the older northern districts, where traffic on Abu Hail Road and the Ittihad corridor is at its worst exactly at tutoring o'clock, that flexibility is worth more than it sounds.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: what a science tutor may and may not do with assessed work
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences carry less assessed coursework than the IB Diploma, but the boundary still matters, and it matters more as a student moves upward into DP or A Level investigations. The rule a serious tutor works to is simple: the student produces the work, the tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on it. A tutor who hands back a corrected version in their own words has not helped; they have substituted their judgement for the student's and created an honesty problem.

In practice this means a tutor can explain why an experimental method has a flaw, can ask what the student thinks the control variable should be, can mark a practice answer against the published mark scheme, and can show a worked example of a similar question. A tutor should not write a student's answer for them, should not edit a piece of assessed work to completion, and should not supply a model answer to be submitted.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the UAE search results for IB and IGCSE support include operations that sell completed Internal Assessments outright. One competitor page found in this market lists finished IAs at a fixed price. For an IB student that is a malpractice trigger with consequences that follow the student, not the seller. A family evaluating any tutoring provider is entitled to ask directly what the provider will and will not produce, and to walk away from a vague answer.

The adjacent boundary is copyright. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the IB. A tutor should reference and link them at their official source rather than distributing copies, and a provider offering a downloadable library of board materials is telling you about its standards.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects sitting alongside the science timetable
paragraphs: A science-focused revision plan built for a Hor Al Anz student has to fit around subjects that exist in Dubai and nowhere else on a Cambridge timetable. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and its requirements were set to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. These are not optional add-ons a family can deprioritise during exam term.

KHDA also sets how they are organised. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and schools may vary lesson length so long as the weekly total is met.

For tutoring planning the consequence is arithmetic. A Year 11 student in a Dubai school carries these subjects on top of a full IGCSE science load, which means the hours available for Physics, Chemistry and Biology revision are fewer than the same student would have in a UK school. Any plan that assumes a UK timetable will overcommit the student by several hours a week.

It also means a family sometimes needs Arabic support alongside science rather than instead of it, particularly for a non-Arab student who arrived in Dubai mid-school and is now several years behind the stream they were placed in. That is a separate conversation from the science one, and worth having separately rather than folding into a science session.

process.title: Send the syllabus codes and a marked mock
process.description: The useful first message names the school, the year group and the syllabus codes from the statement of entry, and attaches a photograph of a marked mock paper. That is enough to tell whether the problem is content, technique or tier, and it saves a session of general questions.

process.title: Free trial lesson with a diagnosis
process.description: The trial is a working session on a real past-paper question, not a sales call. The tutor marks live against the published scheme and says plainly which of the three problem types they are looking at and roughly how long it takes to shift. No payment is taken before this happens.

process.title: Agree the paper order and the weekly slot
process.description: One science per session, named in advance, in an order set by mock marks rather than by what the student enjoys. The slot is fixed to the school run and adjusted for Ramadan or a mock week rather than abandoned, because a moved session is easier to recover than a cancelled habit.

process.title: Timed papers from week one
process.description: Short timed tasks between sessions, full papers as the series approaches, every piece marked against the real scheme. Mark-scheme marking is the measurement; a student who feels more confident but scores the same has not improved yet, and the papers say so before results day does.

process.title: Review against the calendar, not the calendar month
process.description: Every four weeks the plan is checked against how far the series is away and what the timed papers show. Topics still uncovered become named risks. If a tier conversation with the school is needed, the paper evidence is already assembled by then.

whyPoints.title: Taught by syllabus code, not by subject name
whyPoints.description: A tutor who knows they are teaching Cambridge 0620 Extended rather than chemistry generally can tell a student which topics are off the paper. That saves hours, and it is the first question we ask rather than the last.

whyPoints.title: Mark schemes used in the session
whyPoints.description: Work is marked against the published scheme while the student watches, so they see where a four-mark answer earned two. Feeling clearer and scoring higher are different things, and only one of them appears on results day.

whyPoints.title: Paper 6 treated as a paper, not an afterthought
whyPoints.description: The Alternative to Practical paper is predictable and most students arrive having practised it least. Drilling scale choice, anomaly explanation and hazard-precaution pairs is some of the cheapest grade movement available in IGCSE science.

whyPoints.title: Honest about the tier ceiling
whyPoints.description: If a student is on Core and aiming at an HL science, we say so early and produce the timed-paper evidence a head of science needs. Tutoring cannot lift a Core entry past grade C, and pretending otherwise costs a family a year.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated up front
whyPoints.description: Every UAE lesson runs live over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE, and a family learns that on this page rather than after booking. Home tutoring is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science syllabus is my child in Hor Al Anz actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Read the statement of entry the school issues. It carries the syllabus code, and the code settles everything: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 are three separate qualifications, while Coordinated Sciences 0654 awards two grades from a compressed subset of all three. Pearson Edexcel runs 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1 with no tiering. Two students on the same street can be revising entirely different content under the word science. Bring the codes to the first session; a tutor working from the wrong specification will teach topics that are not on the paper and skip ones that are.

faqs.question: What does the Core and Extended tier mean for my child's final science grade?
faqs.answer: On Cambridge sciences, Core candidates sit the easier paper pair and the highest grade available is C. Extended candidates sit the harder pair and can reach A*. The Extended syllabus also contains content Core students are never taught, so the difference is not only in marking severity. A Core entry closes IB Diploma HL sciences and most A Level science routes. Schools move students between tiers on timed-paper evidence rather than on request, so if the tier looks wrong, start collecting marked Extended papers early in Year 11 rather than in the final term.

faqs.question: How is the practical examined if science lessons are taught over video?
faqs.answer: Most UAE school centres enter candidates for Paper 6, the Alternative to Practical, which is a written paper about experimental work rather than a laboratory assessment. It asks the student to read an instrument from a diagram, tabulate results with units, choose a scale and plot accurately, identify and explain an anomalous result, name control variables, improve a method and pair a hazard with a real precaution. Every one of those is drillable on a shared screen, and marking a plotted graph point by point against the scheme is easier online than across a laboratory bench.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit Cambridge IGCSE science exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE centres sit those two. The February/March series exists but Cambridge offers it to India only, so any revision plan built around a spring sitting belongs to a different country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable per zone, stating that using the correct zone timetable is essential, so the dates to trust are the ones your school's exams officer issues.

faqs.question: My child is doing triple science and is behind in all three. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: Start with the marked mocks and rank the three by how far each is from its target, then weight sessions towards the two furthest behind rather than covering all three thinly. Three separate sciences means three plans, three sets of past papers and three mark schemes, and a single weekly session rotating between them moves nothing. Most families in this position pick two subjects for weekly work and bring the third in for a short block before the series. Covering everything equally is the most common way a term of tutoring produces no grade movement.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE science tutoring cost around Deira and Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: Published market figures give the range. Bestimate's Dubai rate work puts a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Hourly, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, Unitors publishes IGCSE from AED 150, TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED AED 650 for premium tutors. Those are the providers' own published figures, not ours. Ask any provider whether the rate is per sixty minutes and whether VAT is included.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to our home in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one, live over video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the past paper and mark scheme shared on screen. The published in-home market band in Dubai runs AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 for a comparably qualified tutor online, and the gap mostly buys a round trip rather than better teaching. Online also means choosing a specialist in your child's syllabus code rather than whoever travels to the district.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a science investigation my child has to submit?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the underlying science, question the experimental design, point out where a method is uncontrolled, explain what the published criteria reward and mark practice work against them. A tutor cannot write the investigation, edit it to completion or supply a model answer for submission. The work has to be the student's own. This boundary matters because some providers in this market sell completed Internal Assessments outright, and for a student that is a malpractice risk with consequences that follow them rather than the seller.

faqs.question: Which science topics cost Hor Al Anz students the most marks?
faqs.answer: In Chemistry 0620, unbalanced equations feeding a calculation, because every downstream mark depends on the coefficients, plus mole arithmetic and organic naming. In Physics 0625, unit conversion in pressure and moment questions, ray diagrams drawn without the normal, and series-versus-parallel misreading. In Biology 0610, command-term mismatch in the enzyme, transport and excretion cluster, where students reproduce a memorised paragraph instead of answering what was asked. All three are diagnosable from one marked past paper and all three respond to targeted work faster than general revision does.

faqs.question: Is there a difference between Cambridge and Edexcel for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: The content overlaps heavily; the structure does not. Cambridge sciences are tiered into Core and Extended with four papers plus Paper 6, and grade on an A* to G scale on most science syllabuses. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are untiered, use two papers and grade 9 to 1, with longer question stems and more data interpretation. The supplied formula conventions also differ. A student who changed school mid-course may have been taught one and entered for the other, which usually surfaces at a mock where the paper simply looks unfamiliar.

faqs.question: My child's school report says the KHDA rating is good. Does that tell me about the science teaching?
faqs.answer: Only indirectly. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and the judgement covers the whole school across many measures. It is a useful signal about the building and close to useless as a prediction for one Year 11 science set. The thing that predicts a science grade is a marked timed paper. If you want to know whether your child is on track for a 7 or a grade A, look at what they score on a full past paper under exam conditions, not at an inspection band.

faqs.question: What time can a science session realistically start for a student in Hor Al Anz?
faqs.answer: It depends on the school rather than the neighbourhood. Students at schools inside the Deira grid are often home by around half past three and can take a four o'clock slot. Students bussed to Al Garhoud, Oud Metha or across to Bur Dubai frequently arrive back nearer five, which pushes a realistic start to six. Families with a Sharjah-side commute through Al Nahda or Al Mamzar tend to prefer later evening or weekend slots. Because lessons are online, the slot can move for a mock week or shift after Iftar during Ramadan without losing a journey.

faqs.question: Do we still need five IGCSE subjects for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, the Ministry requires a pass in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at grade no lower than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Science grades count towards the five. One competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which is wrong. Verify your own case with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority; we describe the process and do not perform it.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start science tutoring eight weeks before the exams?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem you have. Eight weeks is enough for technique work, because nothing new is being learned: command-term discipline, writing the formula before the answer, Paper 6 drills and two timed papers a week per subject can move a grade when the content is broadly there. Eight weeks is not enough to reteach two years of missing content across three sciences, and a tutor who says otherwise is selling. The honest plan at that distance is to triage: pick the subject closest to a grade boundary and spend the hours there.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Physics, Chemistry and Biology for the same student?
faqs.answer: Some can and most should not. A tutor with a physical-sciences background can usually handle Physics and Chemistry to IGCSE Extended standard; Biology is a different vocabulary and a different style of marking. For Coordinated Sciences 0654, a single generalist is often the right answer because the content is a compressed subset. For three separate Extended entries aimed at HL or A Level sciences, subject specialists per paper produce better marks, and the cost of that is three sessions a week rather than one.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for our slot and syllabus?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot with whoever is available. Niche combinations, a particular Edexcel code at a particular hour on a particular evening, do occasionally come up empty. In that case the options are a different time, a different tutor with a short handover, or a wait with a date attached. A provider who never has a coverage gap is either very large or not being straight with you, and the cost of a mismatched tutor in Year 11 is a term, which is not recoverable.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingHeading: Start with one marked paper, not a package
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-hor-al-anz.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE science tutor in Hor Al Anz, the fastest useful step is to find the statement of entry, note the syllabus codes, and photograph the most recent marked mock paper. From those two things a specialist can tell you whether you are looking at a content gap, a technique problem or a tier ceiling, and roughly how many weeks each one takes to shift. The trial lesson is a working session on a real past-paper question with live mark-scheme marking, and no payment is taken before it. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits in the UAE.

intro.heading: Three sciences, three tutors, and why that is usually wrong
paragraphs: A student taking three separate IGCSE sciences presents the most expensive tutoring question in this market, because the obvious response is three tutors and the correct response almost never is. Report cards name a subject area rather than a subject. A profile that reads badly across science usually has one of the three carrying the problem, and one timed paper in each identifies which within a single session.

The arithmetic is worth doing before anything is bought. At the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, one weekly session in one subject is roughly AED 600 to 1,200 a month on Bestimate's mid-range estimates. Three of them is three times that. For a household in these clusters watching a monthly figure, the diagnosis is not a formality - it is the difference between an affordable arrangement and an unaffordable one.

The route matters too, and families are rarely told how. Three separate sciences means up to three potentially tutorable subjects. A double award - Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SC1 - compresses all three into one entry with papers that move between biology, chemistry and physics, so the tutoring follows the paper rather than the subject. A single combined science such as Cambridge 0653 is one entry, one grade and one plan.

Then there is what is actually worth paying for within a science. Command-term discipline, because 'describe' and 'explain' carry different allocations and students answer both the same way, losing marks on every extended question. The written practical skills, because they are examined directly and almost never taught as a lesson. And in chemistry, mole calculations at the higher tiers, which sit inside questions across the whole paper.

Every AED figure on this page was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram rate - ours is quoted after the free trial. Three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote United States dollars, which is not a currency any household in International City transacts in.

One more cost worth naming before the detail. The hourly rate in this market does not rise in February, but the better-matched tutors are committed by then, so the same money buys a weaker arrangement. Booking in the first term of Year 10 or Year 11 is the only real discount available here, and it is obtained by planning rather than by negotiating.

IB Gram delivers this online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, because home visits are an India-only service for us. Published in-home rates run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel against AED 150 to 300 online, and from these clusters that premium of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour buys a long journey rather than better science teaching.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-internation.programmesIntro: What each route costs to support, and how many tutors it can reasonably absorb.

programmes.name: Three separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology, chemistry and physics as individual subjects with individual grades. The heaviest content load and the route that keeps every onward option open. Students who struggle usually struggle in one of the three rather than across all, which makes targeted tutoring unusually efficient and untargeted tutoring unusually expensive.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the diagnosis saves the most money for a family in these clusters. Three tutors at the qualified band is a substantial monthly commitment; one tutor in the right subject is a third of it. The paper should decide which, not the pattern - though chemistry is the most common culprit in this cluster, usually because of stoichiometry.

programmes.name: Double award: Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SC1
programmes.description: All three sciences compressed into the equivalent of two subjects with two identical grades. Content is reduced and breadth retained, but the papers move between biology, chemistry and physics inside one booklet, and students lose real time re-orienting between them.
programmes.countryNote: The double award suits a single tutor better than the triple route does, because the revision follows the paper rather than the subject. The specific thing worth paying for is practice at switching between subject areas under timed conditions, which is a technique nobody teaches and which costs a weekend session to establish.

programmes.name: Single combined science
programmes.description: All three sciences in one subject with one grade and substantially reduced content. Appropriate for a student who needs a science qualification rather than a science future, and the cheapest route to support because there is one plan and one set of papers.
programmes.countryNote: Before spending anything on this route, check what it permits afterwards. Combined science frequently closes A Level and Diploma Higher Level sciences, and those rules belong to the receiving sixth form rather than the board. If a science at sixth form matters, the money may be better spent on a Year 10 case for moving up to the double award.

programmes.name: November resit
programmes.description: A subject retaken in the November series. For separate sciences this means resitting the one subject that failed, decided on the component breakdown. For a double award or combined science it usually means resitting the whole award, which is a much larger and more expensive undertaking.
programmes.countryNote: That distinction decides whether a November entry makes financial sense. Request the component breakdown as soon as results arrive. Note the timing too: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, after most sixth-form courses had started, so ask the receiving school in writing whether a conditional place survives a January result.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-internation.subjectsIntro: Each area is described by what it costs to fix as well as what it demands, because those vary enormously across the three sciences.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline across all three sciences
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest, compare and calculate each specify a different answer with a different mark allocation. Students answer nearly all as describe. Two or three sessions, transferable across every science, and the cheapest decisive purchase on this list.

subjects.name: Written practical and experimental skills
subjects.description: Variables, range and interval, repeats, precision, significant figures, plotting, lines of best fit, and evaluations naming a specific limitation. Examined in the Cambridge alternative-to-practical and inside Pearson's written papers, and almost never taught as a lesson of its own.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Mass to moles, concentration, reacting masses and percentage yield. Sits inside questions across the whole chemistry paper rather than in one section, so six to eight sessions of short calculation sets improves several parts of it at once.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and redox
subjects.description: Products at each electrode, half-equations and the reasoning behind which ion is discharged. Marks go on half-equations and on predictions stated without the justification, which is where the marks sit. Mechanical and inexpensive to drill.

subjects.name: Chemistry: practical vocabulary
subjects.description: Exact terminology for filtration, crystallisation, distillation, chromatography and gas tests. Vague descriptions score nothing even when the method is understood. Memorisable in a fortnight, which makes it one of the better returns in the subject.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits. The heaviest mark load in IGCSE physics and the largest source of confusion. Marks go on circuit reasoning stated as assertion rather than derived from the relationships.

subjects.name: Physics: graphs and motion
subjects.description: Speed and acceleration graphs, forces, moments and energy transfer. Graph questions dominate, and the recurring error is calculating a gradient from two data points rather than from widely separated points on the line of best fit.

subjects.name: Physics: numerical discipline
subjects.description: Unit prefixes, powers of ten and conversions applied consistently inside one calculation. Cheap to fix and worth marks the student believes they already earned, which makes it a frustrating loss and a satisfying repair.

subjects.name: Biology: explanation structure
subjects.description: Mark schemes credit the link from a feature to what it achieves - large surface area for faster diffusion, thin wall for a shorter path. A student who names the structure without that link has described rather than explained, which costs marks on every extended question.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and data questions
subjects.description: Monohybrid crosses drawn on paper rather than attempted mentally, and data questions where the axes are read before anything is written. Both are habits rather than content, and both move within a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Double-award paper navigation
subjects.description: Switching between biology, chemistry and physics inside a single paper without losing time to re-orientation. Practised by paper section under timed conditions, which is the opposite of how most students revise, and worth one weekend session to establish.

subjects.name: Bridging into A Level or Diploma sciences
subjects.description: The algebra, unit handling and graph skills the next course assumes from its first week. Six to eight summer sessions when the commute disappears, and the cheapest genuinely useful science tutoring a family in these clusters buys.

sections.heading: What each route costs to support
paragraphs: The route your child is on sets the maximum sensible spend, and most families never see it laid out. Three separate sciences can absorb three tutors, which is why the diagnosis matters most on that route. A double award has one entry and papers that move between subjects, so it absorbs one tutor well and three badly. A single combined science has one plan and is the cheapest route to support.

Get the route from the examinations officer rather than inferring it: three entries with three syllabus codes means separate sciences; one entry such as Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SC1 means a double award; one entry such as Cambridge 0653 means combined science. It takes minutes and it changes both the plan and the budget.

The table below sets the routes against what they can reasonably absorb and what the monthly figure looks like at the qualified online band. The rates are market figures attributed to the providers publishing them and read in October 2026, with Bestimate's monthly estimates used for the per-month column. None of them is an IB Gram rate.

One route-specific warning that is about money rather than marks. If your child is on combined science and may want a science at sixth form, the most valuable spend may not be tutoring the current course at all - it may be a Year 10 block aimed at producing marked evidence at the double-award level, because combined science frequently closes those options entirely.

sections.heading: Science purchases ranked by what they return
paragraphs: If the monthly figure is fixed, the order of spending matters more than the hourly rate. Science is well suited to this kind of ranking, because two of the highest-return purchases transfer across all three subjects at once and a third is examined directly while being almost never taught.

Command terms come first. The mark schemes in all three sciences credit different things for describe, explain and suggest, and students answer all of them as describe. Two or three sessions fixes it across biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously, and the habit transfers to the humanities as well. It is the cheapest decisive purchase available in the whole subject area.

Written practical skills come second, because they are examined directly in the Cambridge alternative-to-practical and inside Pearson's written papers, and because they are taught properly nowhere. Variables, range, repeats, precision, significant figures, plotting, lines of best fit, and an evaluation that names one specific limitation and one realistic improvement. Three or four sessions on real datasets.

Chemistry stoichiometry comes third but only for students at Extended or Higher tier, where it sits inside questions across the whole paper. After those three, you are into ordinary content teaching with ordinary returns, which is where an open weekly arrangement belongs if it belongs anywhere. Note also what sits at the bottom of the ranking and at the top of most sales conversations: general weekly support in a named subject, which is the easiest thing for a provider to describe and the hardest thing for a parent to evaluate afterwards.
