sections.heading: What each AED band contains for IGCSE science
paragraphs: The useful exercise is matching a band to a job rather than looking for the cheapest hour, because for science the bands differ in what they can actually deliver. Every figure here was published by the provider named and read in October 2026, and none is an IB Gram rate - ours is quoted after the free trial against the work the diagnosis identifies.

Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. For combined-science and Core-tier content, and for drilling command terms once somebody has taught the distinction, that band is genuinely usable. What it less often contains is fluency with Extended-tier chemistry calculations or with alternative-to-practical technique.

Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. This is where most useful IGCSE science tutoring in Dubai happens, and where all three ranked purchases above belong. Specialists run AED 200 to 450 or more, with TutorChase at AED 270, which is defensible for a Higher-tier subject that gates a sixth-form place and hard to justify for combined-science revision.

The monthly view is what decides whether a science plan survives contact with the household budget. Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist examination-year support, with published online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions - and eight sessions a month is the figure to hold onto, because it is roughly two a week, which is what one science discipline in real difficulty needs rather than one. An International City family weighing that against school fees has one piece of certainty to plan with: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, so tutoring is the line that moves this year. One discipline at the mid band is a recognisable monthly commitment; three at the specialist band is a second set of school fees, which is the arithmetic the rest of this page exists to prevent.

sections.heading: Why one timed paper per science is the best money you will spend
paragraphs: It costs nothing beyond the time, and it routinely changes the monthly figure by two thirds. The method is simple: one timed paper in biology, one in chemistry and one in physics, marked question by question against the published mark scheme, with the reason for every lost mark written down in the student's own words rather than summarised by an adult.

What emerges is almost always a concentration. One subject will account for most of the deficit, and within it three or four recurring reasons will account for most of the loss. In this cluster chemistry is the most frequent culprit, usually because of mole calculations at the higher tiers, but physics carries it often enough that assuming would be a mistake.

The second thing that emerges is the kind of loss. Marks lost with correct final answers mean method. Marks lost in clusters mean a topic. Marks lost heavily in the final third mean pacing. Marks lost on extended-response questions across all three sciences mean command terms, which is the cross-subject block rather than three separate arrangements.

For a double-award or combined-science candidate the exercise is slightly different but just as useful: look at whether the losses cluster in one of the three subject areas within the paper. A student can lose most of their marks in chemistry sections while appearing uniformly weak overall, and that distinction decides whether you need a chemistry tutor or a paper-navigation session. Either way the exercise costs nothing beyond the time it takes, which makes it the only step in this process with no downside at all.

sections.heading: The four ways science budgets disappear
paragraphs: These patterns account for most of the science spending families in this district later regret, and all four are diagnosis failures rather than teaching failures. The first and largest is buying three tutors when one subject is carrying the problem, which triples the monthly figure for thinner progress in each subject than a single focused arrangement would deliver.

The second is buying content teaching when the loss is technique. A student who understands osmosis and loses marks for describing rather than explaining does not need osmosis re-taught; they need two sessions on command terms, which also improves their chemistry and physics. Content teaching is the default sale in this market because it is the easiest thing to describe, not because it is usually the right purchase.

The third is buying apparatus-focused revision for a board that does not examine practical work directly. Pearson's 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SC1 have no practical examination; Cambridge sciences may sit a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical depending on the school's choice. Revising apparatus technique for a Pearson candidate is weeks spent on something unexamined, and nobody checks because nobody asks for the entry list.

The fourth is starting after the mock results, when demand across the emirate peaks and the better-matched tutors are committed. The hourly rate is identical in October and in February; what differs is who is still available. That is the only genuine discount in this market and it is obtained by booking early rather than by negotiating.

sections.heading: Practical skills, and why online costs nothing here
paragraphs: A family paying for science tutoring reasonably asks whether online delivery is a compromise. For practical work the honest answer in this district is that it costs nothing, because the thing a tutor cannot provide is the thing a travelling tutor cannot provide either: access to the school's laboratory. From these clusters, once the bus has gone, the apparatus is out of reach for the day whoever is sitting in your living room.

What is examined, meanwhile, is mostly not apparatus handling. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical examination or the alternative-to-practical paper depending on the school's choice. Pearson candidates sit neither: 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and the Science Double Award 4SC1 assess experimental skills inside the written papers as method-design and data-analysis questions.

Both routes test the same underlying skills and all of them are taught on a shared screen with a real dataset. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables. Choosing a sensible range and interval. Justifying a number of repeats. Reading a scale to appropriate precision. Recording to consistent significant figures. Plotting with a sensible scale. Drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points. Writing an evaluation naming one specific limitation and one realistic improvement.

So the sensible purchase for a student here is a short block on exactly that list, matched to the board their school entered them for. Three or four sessions, on datasets, with the official specimen material cited rather than supplied - we link cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com rather than distributing board papers, which is both the correct copyright position and the only way to be sure the version is current.

sections.heading: A two-year science spend plan
paragraphs: Spreading a modest budget across two years produces a better outcome than concentrating it in Year 11, and the reason is availability as much as pedagogy. Demand for IGCSE science tutoring in Dubai spikes after mock results and again in the final weeks, and those are precisely the periods when the better-matched tutors have no slots left.

The order that works is: command terms in the first term of Year 10, because the block is short and improves all three sciences at once while nothing is urgent. Then the written practical skills block, timed so the technique is in place before the first school assessments that test it. Then, if the papers justify it, a targeted subject block on whichever science the diagnosis names. Then timed-paper work in the final two terms.

That totals somewhere between twelve and twenty sessions across two years for most students, which at the qualified band is a defined and modest commitment with a known end. The alternative - three open weekly arrangements through Year 11 - costs several times as much and leaves nobody able to say afterwards what the money changed.

On the calendar: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, with the February and March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and in November - its November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

sections.heading: What to ask before paying, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Five questions, deliberately about money and accountability rather than teaching philosophy. Does the individual teaching my child hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit, and may I see it? Is the figure per hour or per session, and does it include VAT? Which subject, board and tier have you taught, and for how many cohorts? What is the replacement policy if the match fails? And what will you do with internally assessed work, and what will you refuse to do?

On the permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so disregard any amount quoted at you. Because the permit is free, it cannot legitimately be priced into a rate.

On coursework: several IGCSE subjects carry internally assessed components, and wherever a mark is awarded for work submitted as the student's own, a tutor may teach the skill, explain the criteria, question a draft and give written feedback - and may not supply text, rewrite paragraphs, choose topics or generate data. The search results this page sits in include an operator selling completed coursework, and a malpractice finding from that falls on the candidate.

And what we do not claim: no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE; no KHDA Educational Services Permit, which is issued to training institutes with premises in Dubai; no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson; no promises about grades and no published predicted scores; no ratings we cannot evidence with countable dated reviews; and no board material supplied as downloads.

process.description: Three entries with three codes means separate sciences; one entry such as 0654 or 4SC1 means a double award; one such as 0653 means combined science. It also tells us which board, which decides whether apparatus revision belongs in the plan at all.

process.description: Marked question by question against the published mark scheme, with the reason for each lost mark written down. This is the step that usually shows one subject carrying the problem, and it routinely changes the monthly figure by two thirds.

process.description: A real lesson on real science with the student working. Afterwards a plain summary: which subject needs the money, whether the losses are technique or content, and which of the ranked purchases to buy first. Say no and nothing is owed.

process.title: Buy in order, not all at once
process.description: Command terms first because one block improves all three sciences. Then written practical skills. Then a targeted subject block if the papers justify it. Then timed papers. A defined plan with a known end beats three open weekly arrangements.

whyPoints.title: We mark before we quote
whyPoints.description: One timed paper in each science usually shows that a single subject is carrying the problem, which cuts the monthly figure by around two thirds. It costs nothing but the time, and it is the first thing we do rather than the last.

whyPoints.title: Purchases ranked, not hours sold
whyPoints.description: Command terms improve all three sciences in two or three sessions. Written practical skills are examined directly and taught almost nowhere. Those come before content teaching, which is the default sale in this market because it is easiest to describe.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure attributed and dated
whyPoints.description: Three of the six leading pages in this market publish no price at all and two quote dollars. Ours name the provider and the month they were read, and none of them is presented as our own rate.

whyPoints.title: The board checked before apparatus revision
whyPoints.description: Pearson's 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SC1 have no practical examination. Revising apparatus technique for a Pearson candidate is weeks spent on something unexamined, and it happens constantly because nobody asks for the entry list.

whyPoints.title: No travel line on the bill
whyPoints.description: In-home rates carry roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour of travel, and from these clusters that buys a long journey. It also cannot buy laboratory access, which is the one thing a science student here actually cannot get from home.

whyPoints.description: If combined science would close a science at sixth form, the best spend may be a Year 10 block producing marked evidence at the double-award level rather than tutoring the current course. That is a different purchase and we would rather name it.

faqs.question: Can I get an IGCSE science tutor in International City?
faqs.answer: Yes, as one-to-one online tuition rather than a tutor coming to your flat, since IB Gram offers home visits only in India. For science from this district online delivery costs nothing in practical terms, because the thing a tutor cannot provide is laboratory access - and a travelling tutor cannot provide that either. The written practical marks sit in skills taught on a shared screen with real data, which is where a short block of sessions belongs.

faqs.question: Will my child taking biology, chemistry and physics need three tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost never. A weak science profile usually has one of the three carrying the problem, and one timed paper in each - marked question by question against the published mark scheme - identifies which within a single session. At the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, three tutors is three times the monthly figure for thinner progress in each subject. Chemistry is the most frequent culprit in this cluster, usually because of mole calculations at the higher tiers.

faqs.question: What does science tutoring cost per month for a family here?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put mid-range support at AED 600 to 1,200 a month per subject and specialist examination-year support at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more, with published online packages at AED 799 a month for eight sessions. Hourly, qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Those are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026, not IB Gram rates.

faqs.question: Which science purchase gives the best return?
faqs.answer: Command terms, by a clear margin. The mark schemes in all three sciences credit different things for describe, explain and suggest, and students answer nearly all of them as describe, which costs marks on every extended-response question. Two or three sessions fixes it across biology, chemistry and physics at once, and the habit transfers to the humanities too. Nothing else in science improves three subjects for the price of one block.

faqs.question: Is the budget rate band usable for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: For some jobs. Budget and university-student online tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from 33 to 52, and that band is genuinely usable for combined-science and Core-tier content, and for drilling command terms once somebody has taught the distinction properly. What it less often contains is fluency with Extended-tier chemistry calculations or with alternative-to-practical technique, which is where the qualified band earns its money.

faqs.question: Does the route my child is on change the cost?
faqs.answer: Substantially. Three separate sciences can absorb three tutors, which is why the diagnosis matters most there. A double award such as Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SC1 has one entry and papers that move between subjects, so it absorbs one tutor well and three badly. A single combined science such as Cambridge 0653 has one plan and is the cheapest route to support. Get the route from the examinations officer rather than inferring it from the report.

faqs.question: Is it worth spending money if my child is on combined science?
faqs.answer: It depends on what comes next, and this is a money question rather than an academic one. Combined science frequently closes A Level and Diploma Higher Level sciences, and those rules belong to the receiving sixth form rather than to the board. If a science at sixth form matters, the most valuable spend may be a Year 10 block aimed at producing marked evidence at the double-award level, rather than tutoring the current course. Ask two sixth forms in writing first.

faqs.question: Why would apparatus revision ever be wasted money?
faqs.answer: Because Pearson's International GCSE sciences - 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and the Science Double Award 4SC1 - have no practical examination at all, and assess experimental skills inside the written papers instead. Cambridge sciences may sit a practical paper or the alternative-to-practical, and the school chooses which. A Pearson candidate revising apparatus technique is preparing for something unexamined, and it happens constantly because nobody asks the examinations officer for the entry list first.

faqs.question: What exactly does the written practical component assess?
faqs.answer: Not dexterity. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables; choosing a sensible range and interval; justifying a number of repeats; reading a scale to appropriate precision; recording to consistent significant figures; plotting with a sensible scale; drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points; and writing an evaluation naming one specific limitation and one realistic improvement. Three or four sessions on real datasets covers that list, and all of it works on a shared screen.

faqs.question: Does starting later in the year cost more?
faqs.answer: The hourly rate does not change, but what you can buy with it does. Demand for IGCSE science tutoring in Dubai spikes after mock results and again in the final weeks, and in those windows the better-matched tutors are fully committed, so a family booking then pays the same money for a less suitable arrangement. Booking in the first term of Year 10 or Year 11 is the only genuine discount available in this market.

faqs.question: How should we spread a modest budget across two years?
faqs.answer: Command terms in the first term of Year 10, because the block is short and improves all three sciences while nothing is urgent. Then the written practical skills block, before the first school assessments that test it. Then a targeted subject block if the papers justify one. Then timed-paper work in the final two terms. That totals roughly twelve to twenty sessions across two years rather than three open weekly arrangements through Year 11.

faqs.question: Does practice between sessions change the value of the money?
faqs.answer: Considerably. Command-term discipline, numerical habits and graph technique change through repetition rather than through explanation, so an hour of teaching followed by nothing delivers perhaps a third of its value at the full price. Twenty minutes of past-paper questions on two evenings costs nothing and roughly triples the return on the session. We agree the practice and the evening it happens in, because otherwise it reliably does not happen.

faqs.question: Is a November resit affordable on the double award route?
faqs.answer: It is a bigger financial decision than for separate sciences, because resitting a double award usually means resitting the whole award rather than the one science that went wrong. For separate sciences you can ask for the component breakdown and resit the single weak subject, which is a far shorter and cheaper job. Request the breakdown either way as soon as results arrive, and check that a sixth-form place survives a result arriving in late January.

faqs.question: Is the tutor's permit something that affects the price?
faqs.answer: No, and that is worth knowing. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, so no tutor can legitimately price it into a rate. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any figure quoted at you as unverified. Ask to see the permit.

faqs.question: What if the money would be better spent elsewhere?
faqs.answer: Then we say so after the trial lesson rather than taking the booking. A student not completing the work the school already sets will not be rescued by more teaching, and a difficulty that is organisational rather than scientific usually needs a conversation with the school instead. Most schools in Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Silicon Oasis also run free after-school subject support that nobody advertises, and trying that for a month costs nothing at all.

Each names the award and the papers they have taught, and each keeps a slot inside the window a JBR school run actually leaves on a weekday.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one timetable, and one afternoon to fit it into
paragraphs: Science is the only part of an IGCSE timetable that can arrive as three subjects at once, and that is what makes it expensive to get wrong. A JBR family whose child is sitting Biology, Chemistry and Physics separately is carrying three syllabuses, three sets of papers and three practical components, and when a report arrives saying science is weak the honest first question is which science. Buying three weekly hours because the word on the report was plural is the most common way money is wasted in this subject in Dubai.

The second thing to establish is the award. Cambridge entries split three ways. A triple entry means Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as separate syllabuses producing three certificate grades. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines and produces two grades. Combined Science 0653 produces one. Pearson runs the equivalent split with 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 as separate subjects or Science Double Award 4SD0 for two grades. Those are genuinely different qualifications with different content depth, and what they open at 16 differs too.

The third is tiering, which behaves differently across the boards and catches parents out. Cambridge sciences are tiered Core and Extended, and a Core entry cannot be awarded above a grade C. Pearson's international sciences are untiered and graded 9 to 1, so there is no ceiling to discover. If your child sits Cambridge, the tier is the single most important fact on the statement of entry, and it is fixed at the final entry deadline rather than negotiable in the spring.

Then there is the practical component, which differs by board in a way that changes what tutoring can do. Each Cambridge science carries a practical element worth 20 per cent, sat as a Practical Test or as the Alternative to Practical paper. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead. Either way the question grammar is learnable: variables and control, precision and uncertainty, the conventions for drawing a graph, identifying the source of an anomalous result. The bench work itself belongs to the school and stays there.

The local constraint is simple and it shapes everything above. No school sits inside the JBR towers, so every student here commutes: a short run to Al Sufouh and the Media City edge, a longer one to Al Barsha and Al Barsha South, the longest out to the villa belt around Emirates Hills and The Meadows. That return journey decides how many science hours the week can hold, which is usually one and occasionally two, never three. Lessons are delivered one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jbr.programmesIntro: The science decisions that matter are taken a stage before the one a family is worrying about, which is why this ladder starts in Year 9. These are the four stages as a JBR household meets them.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary science and Checkpoint
programmes.description: Three years of general science, assessed internally and in many schools through Cambridge Checkpoint tests, which run in March, May and October. Checkpoint carries no certificate weight but schools use it to recommend the award and the tier. This is the stage at which a student either learns to record a method separately from a result or does not, and that habit decides practical marks for the next four years.
programmes.countryNote: Around JBR the Year 9 options sheet is where the science award is effectively chosen, usually in the spring term. A family reading that sheet carefully and asking two questions, which award and which board, is doing the highest-value work available in this subject. It costs nothing and it is the decision that is hardest to reverse later.

programmes.name: International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Two years ending in either three separate science certificates, two from a co-ordinated double award, or one from a combined entry. Cambridge codes are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences and 0653 Combined Science. Pearson codes are 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and Science Double Award 4SD0. Each route carries its own content depth and its own number of papers.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A triple science entry contributes three of those five on its own, which is one of the practical arguments for triple that nobody makes on an options evening.

programmes.name: A Level and International A Level sciences
programmes.description: The commonest post-16 science route in the British-curriculum schools around JBR. Departments publish a minimum IGCSE grade for entry, usually in the same science, and that threshold is where the award decision comes back. A student with a co-ordinated double award can often still proceed, but the published requirement is worth reading rather than assuming.
programmes.countryNote: Ministry equivalency on the British track also requires one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E, or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, on top of the five IGCSE passes. Families reducing to two A Levels for workload reasons should confirm that arithmetic on the Ministry's own guidance before the decision is made.

programmes.name: IB Diploma sciences
programmes.description: The alternative route, where a student takes one or at most two sciences from Group 4 at Higher or Standard Level. The current syllabus organises each science into concept-based themes with Higher Level material embedded, and 20 per cent of the grade comes from an individual scientific investigation. Students arriving from triple science cope with the content; students from a combined award meet a wider gap in the first term.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools around Al Barsha and the villa belt run IGCSE sciences to 16 and then offer both the Diploma and A Level, so a JBR family often faces the choice inside their existing school. Higher Level science places usually carry a published IGCSE grade requirement, which again makes the Year 11 result matter beyond the certificate.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jbr.subjectsIntro: Below are the science entries JBR families most often ask about, with the codes. If the award or the code against your child's science differs from these, that single detail is the most useful thing to tell a prospective tutor.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Three components: a multiple-choice paper at 30 per cent, a theory paper at 50 and the practical element at 20. Marks leave on terminology precision, because a named process earns credit where a description of something increasing earns none, and on water-potential and osmosis questions where the direction of movement is reasoned backwards.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The same three-component structure. Mole calculations, ionic equations and the qualitative analysis tables are the recurring difficulties, and the analysis section rewards the exact observation the mark scheme names rather than a general description of a colour change.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: Again three components. Electricity and waves account for more lost marks than anything else, usually through circuit reasoning rather than arithmetic, and units and significant figures cost marks silently across every paper. Ray diagrams lose marks on construction convention rather than on understanding.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three disciplines in one syllabus producing two certificate grades. It is not an easier science so much as a shallower one, which matters at 16: students moving into Higher Level Diploma sciences or A Level from a double award meet a wider content gap in the first term and usually need a short bridging block.

subjects.name: Cambridge Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: All three disciplines compressed into a single certificate grade. It is the right choice for a student who needs a science pass and whose timetable is better spent elsewhere, and the wrong choice for a student with any intention of a science route at 16. The decision is made on the Year 9 options sheet and is difficult to reverse.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: A long first paper and a shorter second, with no separate practical examination: practical skills are assessed inside the written papers. Because the specification is untiered there is no grade ceiling to discover, which removes one of the two things that most often surprises a Cambridge family in the spring of Year 11.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: The same two-paper structure. The longer first paper rewards sustained multi-step calculation, so students who are comfortable with chemistry and uncomfortable with arithmetic are exposed differently here than they would be under Cambridge. Practical skills appear as written questions about method, precision and anomalies.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers, no practical examination, and a formula support position worth checking on the specimen paper rather than assuming. Circuit reasoning and graph interpretation carry the same weight of lost marks as under Cambridge; the difference is in the paper length and the distribution of the harder questions.

subjects.name: Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: The Pearson equivalent of a co-ordinated double award, producing two certificate grades across the three disciplines. As with Cambridge 0654, the consideration is not difficulty but what it opens at 16, and that question is answered by the post-16 department's published entry requirement rather than by the award's reputation.

subjects.name: The practical component, both boards
subjects.description: Cambridge sets a Practical Test or the Alternative to Practical paper; Pearson assesses the same skills inside the written papers. Either way the assessed skills are identical: variables and control, precision and uncertainty, graph conventions, identifying and explaining an anomalous result. All four are teachable over video; the bench work is the school's.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jbr.regionsTitle: The JBR school runs, and how many science hours each one leaves
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jbr.regionsIntro: With three sciences on a timetable, the only local fact that matters is how much of the afternoon survives the commute. These notes set out the runs JBR families actually make and what each leaves room for in a week.

regions.name: Al Sufouh and the Media City edge
regions.note: The shortest run from the towers, back early enough for a 16:15 start. These are the only JBR families for whom two science hours in a week is realistic without pushing one of them to a weekend, and even then the second hour should be a different subject rather than more of the same.

regions.name: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
regions.note: Where most JBR secondary students study, on a return leg of thirty to forty-five minutes that coincides with the wider Al Barsha exodus. One science hour at 16:45 is comfortable; a second in the same week needs a weekend slot rather than another weekday evening.

regions.name: Dubai Marina
regions.note: Across Al Mamsha Street, sharing tram stops and school buses with JBR, so Marina and JBR students usually sit in the same science sets and the same windows. Useful to know because the award and the board will also be identical, which makes a tutor match transferable between neighbours.

regions.name: JLT
regions.note: A highway crossing away, adding minutes at the worst point of the afternoon. For a three-science student those minutes matter, because the practical-skills work that most needs an alert student is exactly the work that gets pushed to the end of the hour.

regions.name: Emirates Hills, The Meadows and The Springs
regions.note: The villa belt, with the longest commutes in this set and often the broadest option structures, which means more students here carry triple science. One weekend session plus one short weekday hour is the pattern that works for that load.

regions.name: Jumeirah Village Triangle and Circle
regions.note: Newer schools absorbing New Dubai demand, several running Pearson specifications across the sciences. The return leg runs against the afternoon flow, so a 16:45 start holds up here more reliably than the distance from JBR suggests.

regions.name: Al Safa and Umm Suqeim
regions.note: Older British schools with long IGCSE histories and settled science department board choices, which makes the award and the codes easy to confirm with one email. Students joining mid-course from another board need a short conversion on practical question grammar rather than content.

regions.name: Bluewaters Island
regions.note: JBR timings plus the bridge crossing. For a student carrying three sciences the practical answer is to book fifteen minutes later than the map suggests, so the session starts settled rather than at a run with the hardest material last.

schoolClusters.city: Al Barsha and Al Barsha South
schoolClusters.note: The main destination for JBR secondary students and the hardest cluster in which to guess the science award, because triple, double and combined entries all appear and the board can differ between the three sciences in one school. Confirm the codes before buying any hours.

schoolClusters.city: Al Sufouh and the short-commute schools
schoolClusters.note: Settled departmental choices and the shortest run from the towers. This is the one cluster where a triple-science student can realistically hold two weekday science hours across Year 11, which changes what a sensible budget looks like for these families.

schoolClusters.city: The villa belt, Jumeirah Village and the older British schools
schoolClusters.note: Broader option structures, more triple-science entries and longer commutes, which together argue for one weekend session covering the weakest science and one short weekday hour on the second. Mock timetables here are usually published early enough to plan a pre-series block around.

sections.heading: Triple, double or single: the award that sets the next four years
paragraphs: Before anything else, establish which science award your child is entered for, because it determines how many certificate grades the two years produce and how much content was covered to produce them. A Cambridge triple entry means Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as three separate syllabuses, three sets of papers and three grades. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines in one syllabus and returns two grades. Combined Science 0653 returns one. Pearson mirrors the split with separate 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 entries or Science Double Award 4SD0.

The honest framing is not that one is harder. Triple is wider and deeper and takes more timetable; double covers the three disciplines at less depth; single covers least. What differs most is what each opens at 16, and that question is answered by the published entry requirement of the post-16 department rather than by the award's reputation. A student from a double award can often still take A Level biology, but the requirement is a document to read, not a thing to assume.

There is one practical argument for triple that rarely gets made at an options evening in Dubai. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. A triple science entry supplies three of those five by itself, where a combined entry supplies one. For a family planning on a UAE university route that is worth knowing before the options sheet is returned.

The table sets the five common awards side by side on the things that actually differ. Read it against your child's statement of entry rather than against what the school said in Year 9, because entries are sometimes adjusted and the document is the authority.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one week: the hour arithmetic a JBR household faces
paragraphs: This is where the commute stops being background and becomes the constraint. A triple-science student in Year 11 carries three syllabuses, and a parent reading a disappointing report naturally wants all three covered. The week does not contain three science hours, at least not three useful ones, once the return journey from Al Barsha or the villa belt is subtracted and the other six or seven subjects are given any time at all.

The arithmetic works out roughly like this. A JBR student on the Al Sufouh run is home early enough for a 16:15 start and can hold two weekday hours in a week without the second one being wasted. A student on the Al Barsha run has one comfortable weekday hour at 16:45 and needs a weekend slot for anything beyond that. A student commuting to the villa belt, where the return can reach fifty minutes, is better served by one longer weekend session than by two tired weekday ones at the same total cost.

That means the real decision is not how many hours but which subject gets them, and the practical-skills block is the exception that resolves it. Because the assessed practical skills are identical across Biology, Chemistry and Physics, and identical in substance between the two boards even though the assessment route differs, six to eight hours on that material lifts marks in all three subjects at once. For a triple-science student with one hour a week available, that is the highest-return block on this page.

Read the table as a planning tool rather than a rule. The point of the right-hand column is to stop a family buying three subject hours they cannot sustain and to spend the same money on the one thing that transfers across all three.

sections.heading: Which science is actually weak? A twenty-minute diagnosis
paragraphs: A report saying science needs attention is not actionable, and the fastest way to make it actionable is a short diagnostic rather than a term of general revision. The three sciences fail in recognisably different ways, and once you know the signature you know which subject to pay for and which two are coping.

Biology fails on precision of language. A student who understands a process perfectly and writes that something increases, where the mark scheme wants a named mechanism, loses the mark every time. The signature is a script full of reasonable-sounding sentences scoring well below what the student knows. Biology also fails on the small number of genuinely quantitative topics, water potential and genetics crosses in particular, where the reasoning runs in a direction students find counter-intuitive.

Chemistry fails on arithmetic discipline. The signature is a student who can explain bonding fluently and cannot complete a mole calculation under timing, or who reaches the right number and loses the mark to premature rounding or a missing unit. Qualitative analysis is the second signature: students describe a colour change in their own words rather than giving the observation the mark scheme names, and the marks go without the chemistry being wrong.

Physics fails on reasoning about systems rather than on calculation. The signature is circuits: a student who can use every formula and cannot say what happens to the current elsewhere in a circuit when one component changes. Ray diagrams are the second signature, and the losses there are construction conventions rather than optics. Twenty minutes with an unseen question from each of the three sciences, marked honestly, will usually tell you which one to buy.

sections.heading: The topic that breaks each science, and what fixes it
paragraphs: Each of the three sciences has one or two topics that account for a disproportionate share of lost marks in this cohort, and they are not the topics students say they find hard. Students report finding whichever topic they met most recently hardest. The mark schemes report something steadier, and it is worth working from the second rather than the first.

In Biology it is movement across membranes and the genetics crosses. Osmosis and water potential questions require reasoning about the direction of movement from a concentration statement, and students routinely reverse it. Genetics crosses are mechanical once learned and are lost instead to notation: gametes not shown, the key not stated, phenotype ratios given where genotypes were asked for. Both are drill-fixable in a handful of sessions.

In Chemistry it is the mole and the qualitative analysis tables. Mole fluency underpins every quantitative question in the paper, so slowness there reads as weakness everywhere. The analysis tables are pure recall of specified observations, and students lose marks writing goes cloudy where the scheme wants a white precipitate. In Physics it is circuits and ray diagrams: the first needs reasoning about a whole system, the second needs construction conventions followed exactly.

sections.heading: The Year 9 options sheet, read properly
paragraphs: Most science difficulty in Year 11 was decided in Year 9, on a sheet most families read as a menu rather than as a set of consequences. Three questions make that sheet far more useful. Which award is this, triple, double or single. Which awarding body, and is it the same for all three sciences. And how many timetable periods does triple science take, and which subject is being given up to pay for them.

The third question is the one nobody asks. Triple science is wider and deeper and it costs periods, which have to come from somewhere: often a humanities subject, sometimes a language, occasionally the subject a student is best at. A student who takes triple science and drops the subject they would have scored highest in has not obviously improved their transcript, and for Ministry equivalency, which counts five accredited passes excluding Arabic and Islamic education, the arithmetic of what is dropped matters.

The second question matters because a school may run different boards in different science departments. It is entirely normal for physics to be entered with one board and biology with another, and a parent who assumes a single answer will get the specification wrong for two of the three subjects. Ask each department, or wait for the statement of entry and read the codes off it.

The first question has a reversal deadline attached. Moving between awards is usually possible during Year 10 and effectively impossible once entries are made, and the final entry deadline for a series sits months before the papers. Pearson shows it most plainly, because its windows are published as dates you can check: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and entries for that sitting had closed well before the autumn term began. Cambridge works the same way across its June and November series -- those are the two series a JBR candidate can sit -- with the June entry closing in the spring. Ask your examinations officer for the equivalent date in writing at the start of Year 10.

sections.heading: Practical skills in a written question: the grammar nobody teaches
paragraphs: Each Cambridge science carries a practical component worth 20 per cent of the grade, sat either as a Practical Test or as the Alternative to Practical paper. Pearson's international sciences have no separate practical examination and assess the same skills inside the written papers. The assessment route differs; the skills being tested do not, and that is the useful insight for a family with one hour a week and three sciences.

Four skills account for nearly all of it. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar experiment, and saying how each would be controlled. Discussing precision, resolution and uncertainty, including which instrument would improve a measurement and why. Presenting results to convention: axes labelled with units, sensible scales, a line of best fit drawn as a line of best fit rather than joined dots. And explaining an anomalous result as a specific procedural cause rather than dismissing it as human error.

All four are teachable over video, and all four transfer across the three sciences, which is why this block is the best value available to a triple-science student whose week only holds one hour. A student who learns the question grammar once is better at it in Biology, Chemistry and Physics simultaneously, and the improvement shows on the written papers as well as the practical component because the same language appears throughout.

What a tutor does not do is replace the school's bench work. The practical scheme belongs to the school, the apparatus is there, and students should be doing it. The tutoring contribution is the thinking either side of the bench: designing properly before, and analysing honestly afterwards. sections.heading: Where three sciences lead at 16, and what each route wants
paragraphs: The award and the grades open or close post-16 doors, and the useful thing a family can do in Year 10 is find out which doors and what they cost. Two routes dominate around JBR: A Level or International A Level sciences, and IB Diploma Group 4 sciences at Higher or Standard Level. Both are often available inside the same school, which makes the choice feel administrative when it is in fact consequential.

A Level science departments publish a minimum IGCSE grade, usually in the same science, and sometimes a mathematics condition alongside it. IB coordinators set their own threshold for Higher Level science places and are also looking at the whole six-group transcript rather than at the science alone. For a student from a co-ordinated or combined award, both routes may still be open, but the published requirement is the document to read and the bridging gap is real: those students typically need a short content block in the first term.

On the Ministry side, equivalency on the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. IB Gram does not perform, submit, expedite or guarantee equivalency; it is a Ministry process with an official channel. Tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency.

sections.heading: What three sciences cost around JBR, per subject and in total
paragraphs: This is the subject where the published hourly rates are most misleading, because the hourly rate is the wrong unit. Three sciences means the figure gets multiplied, and the multiplication is what families fail to do before committing. One mid-tier hour a week per science, at a market rate of AED 150 to AED 300, is AED 450 to AED 900 a week before anything else in the week is paid for, which is why the first task is deciding that only one of the three actually needs it.

The published figures, read in October 2026 from the providers' own pages, run as follows. Tutopiya's comparison panel opens at AED 33 to AED 52, with a revision date around twenty-one months old. EdFlik publishes an entry tier at AED 45 to AED 65. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table places subject specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to AED 350 and independent home tutors quoted at AED 200 to AED 500. BartyED quotes AED 650 at the examiner end.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour give AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year. Those are per subject. For a triple-science family the practical conclusion is to buy one subject hour and one practical-skills block rather than three subject hours, because the practical block raises marks in all three subjects for the price of one.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card here. The sequence is a free trial lesson, one per student with no card details taken, then a quote once the award, the codes and the weakest subject are known. For budget context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai will not rise for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package, valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are the fixed line this year; three sciences' worth of tutoring is the line that can quietly triple.

faqs.question: My child's report says science is weak. Do we need three tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost certainly not. The three sciences fail in different ways and one usually carries most of the deficit. Biology fails on precision of language, chemistry on arithmetic discipline, physics on reasoning about whole systems. One unseen question from each, marked honestly, identifies the subject to pay for in about twenty minutes. Three weekly hours at market rates runs to AED 450 to AED 900 a week before anything else in the week is paid for, which is rarely necessary.

faqs.question: What is the difference between triple science and a co-ordinated double award?
faqs.answer: Triple science means three separate syllabuses, Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with three sets of papers and three certificate grades. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, or Pearson 4SD0, covers the same three disciplines at less depth and returns two grades. Combined Science 0653 returns one. The difference that matters is not difficulty but what each opens at 16, which the post-16 department's published entry requirement answers.

faqs.question: Does a double award stop my child taking A Level or Higher Level science?
faqs.answer: Usually not, but it creates a real bridging gap and the requirement is a document to read rather than a thing to assume. Departments publish a minimum IGCSE grade, often in the same science, and IB coordinators set their own threshold for Higher Level places. Students arriving from a double or combined award typically need a short content block in the first post-16 term, because the depth covered in two years was narrower than the course now assumes.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge sciences tiered, and are Pearson's?
faqs.answer: Cambridge sciences are tiered Core and Extended, with a Core entry capped at grade C and Extended graded A* to E. Pearson's international sciences are untiered and graded 9 to 1, so there is no ceiling to discover in the spring of Year 11. If your child sits Cambridge, the tier on the statement of entry is the single most important fact there, and it is fixed at the final entry deadline rather than negotiable afterwards.

faqs.question: How many science hours a week does a JBR school run actually allow?
faqs.answer: One for most families, two for the shortest commute. Students on the Al Sufouh run are home early enough for a 16:15 start and can hold two weekday hours on different subjects. The Al Barsha run leaves one comfortable hour at 16:45 and needs a weekend slot for anything more. From the villa belt, where the return can reach fifty minutes, one longer weekend session buys more than two tired weekday hours at the same cost.

faqs.question: Which single block of tutoring helps all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: The practical-skills block. The assessed skills are identical across Biology, Chemistry and Physics under both boards: identifying and controlling variables, discussing precision and uncertainty, presenting results to convention, and explaining an anomalous result as a specific procedural cause. Six to eight hours on that grammar raises marks in all three subjects simultaneously, and the same language also appears throughout the written papers, so the improvement is wider than the practical component alone.

faqs.question: My daughter sits Paper 6 rather than a practical test. What will it ask her?
faqs.answer: The thinking either side of the bench rather than manual skill. Typical questions ask you to name the independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar experiment and say how each would be controlled, to identify which instrument would improve a measurement and why, to plot results and draw a proper line of best fit, and to explain why one result does not fit the trend. It assumes real laboratory experience, which the school provides, and it rewards precise language.

faqs.question: Can online lessons teach practical science without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: They can teach the assessed practical skills, which is not the same as replacing the laboratory and should not be presented as such. The bench work, the apparatus and the scheme of practical work belong to the school and should stay there. What a tutor contributes is experimental design before the practical and honest analysis afterwards, both of which are where most of the assessed marks sit. We do not claim to run experiments over video.

faqs.question: Which biology topics cost the most marks in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Movement across membranes and genetics crosses, consistently. Osmosis and water-potential questions require reasoning about direction of movement from a concentration statement and students regularly reverse it. Genetics crosses are mechanical once learned and are lost instead to notation: gametes not shown, the key not stated, phenotype ratios given where genotypes were asked for. Both respond quickly to drilling, which makes them unusually good value for a short block of hours.

faqs.question: Why does my son know the physics and still lose marks?
faqs.answer: Because physics marks go on reasoning about systems rather than on using formulae. The characteristic case is circuits: a student who can apply every relationship and cannot say what happens to the current elsewhere when one component changes. Ray diagrams are the second case, where losses come from construction conventions rather than from misunderstanding optics. Both are teachable as technique, and both show up on a mock script in a recognisable pattern.

faqs.question: How early should the Year 9 options sheet be discussed?
faqs.answer: Before it is returned, with three questions asked in writing. Which award is this, triple, double or single. Which awarding body for each science, since a school may use different boards in different departments. And how many timetable periods does triple science take, and which subject is being dropped to pay for them. That third question is the one nobody asks, and it is the one that decides whether a stronger transcript or a weaker one results.

faqs.question: Does a triple science entry help with UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: It contributes usefully. Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. A triple science entry supplies three of those five on its own, where a combined entry supplies one. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency, and tutoring is not a requirement for it; the Ministry's own channel is the one to use.

faqs.question: Do science tutors working with Dubai students need a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 on private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 are eligible. Working without one attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws.

faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home visiting is a service we operate only in India. UAE lessons are one to one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with a shared canvas for diagrams and graph work, screen sharing for annotating the student's own script, and saved worked solutions. The in-home band of AED 180 to AED 500 an hour appears on this page so you can multiply it across three sciences and see the result.

faqs.question: What does three sciences' worth of tutoring actually cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Multiply the single-subject figure by three, which is the arithmetic families skip. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for one weekly hour give AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist support in an examination year, all per subject. Three sciences at the middle tier is therefore AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month, which is why diagnosing one subject matters.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for my child's science code in our slot?
faqs.answer: We say so before anything is paid. Separate Biology, Chemistry and Physics at the common tiers are usually matched within the week. A narrower request, such as Cambridge 0654 Extended with a practical focus in one fixed weekday slot, can take longer or occasionally cannot be staffed. In that case we offer the nearest workable time, propose a weekend session, or tell you plainly we cannot cover it rather than placing a tutor who does not know the award.

intro.heading: Three ways to sit IGCSE science, and they are not interchangeable
paragraphs: A parent in Al Furjan and a parent in Jebel Ali Village can both say their child is taking IGCSE science and mean quite different things. One child may be sitting Biology, Chemistry and Physics as three separate qualifications. Another may be on a coordinated or double-award route that covers all three and counts as two certificates. A third may be on a single combined science award counting as one. The content depth, the paper count and the number of certificates all differ.

That difference has consequences beyond the timetable. The number of IGCSE certificates matters for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency, where the published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count. A student on a single combined award has one science certificate towards that five; a student taking three separate sciences has three.

It also decides what tutoring can usefully do. Three separate sciences at Extended level is a heavy load with deep content in each; one specialist cannot carry all three well and should not pretend to. A combined award is broad and shallow, and the failure mode is different: breadth without the depth to answer a six-mark question. Hiring a tutor for "science" without knowing which of these you have is the most common expensive mistake in this subject.

Then there is the board. Cambridge runs separate sciences as Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, with coordinated and combined alternatives such as Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, Combined Science 0653 and Physical Science 0652. Pearson Edexcel runs separate sciences as 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 alongside double and single award routes. Topic coverage diverges between boards, and the practical assessment is handled differently.

Geography is why this page also compares delivery. Jebel Ali sits at the industrial western edge of Dubai, with its residential communities spread through Al Furjan, Discovery Gardens, Dubai Investments Park, Green Community, Dubai South and Emaar South. Three separate-science tutors visiting one household is three journeys. One of those tutors existing at all, within driving distance of Emaar South on a weekday evening, is already optimistic.

IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time. We do not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Laboratory work stays at school under the teacher's supervision, as the specification requires. What follows is the route comparison, the board comparison, where marks go in each science, the AED bands with their sources, and the calendar counted backwards. Read it with the exam entry statement and one marked science paper beside you, because those two documents answer most of the questions a first phone call would otherwise take twenty minutes to establish.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jebel-ali.subjectsIntro: Below is where marks actually go in each IGCSE science, drawn from the marked papers our tutors see from the schools serving this catchment. The patterns differ by discipline, which is the argument against a single general science tutor.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and homeostasis
subjects.description: Content-heavy and command-term sensitive. Six-mark answers written as unlinked bullet lists cap the mark regardless of how much the student knows, because the question wanted a connected account.

subjects.name: Biology: inheritance and variation
subjects.description: Genetic crosses are procedural and therefore trainable quickly. Marks go missing on the explanation that follows the cross, where a probability is stated without the reasoning the question asked for.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Set-up order decides the mark. Students who apply the ratio before converting to moles produce a plausible answer from the wrong proportion, with no visible error to find on the script.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and rates
subjects.description: Functional groups, uses and reaction conditions, plus the factors affecting rate. Explanations that name a factor without saying how it changes collision frequency lose the second half of the mark.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The single weakest topic across this catchment. Marks go on circuit diagrams never drawn and on relationships recognised but not transposed quickly enough to reach the later parts of a question.

subjects.name: Physics: moments, pressure and energy
subjects.description: Multi-step questions where a missing unit or an unconverted prefix invalidates the final answer. The fix is a habit of writing units at every line rather than at the end.

subjects.name: Coordinated sciences papers
subjects.description: All three disciplines in one paper, which rewards fast switching between them. Students who revise by discipline and then meet them interleaved lose time orienting themselves question by question.

subjects.name: Combined and physical science
subjects.description: Broad coverage with less depth. The characteristic failure is a recall-level answer where the question asked for an explanation, because the course gave less practice at extended reasoning.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical papers
subjects.description: Assessed in writing and marked on precision: apparatus justified, variables controlled in operational terms, units in table headings, graph scales sensible. Four sessions of convention work usually produces the fastest mark gain available.

subjects.name: Mathematical skills inside science
subjects.description: Rearranging relationships, handling prefixes, reading a scale and calculating a percentage. Weak maths shows up as weak science on a science script, and it is frequently misdiagnosed as a content problem.

sections.heading: Separate, coordinated or combined: the comparison nobody sets out
paragraphs: The first question to answer is not which topic is hard but which configuration your child is entered for, because that decides the content depth, the number of papers, the number of certificates and what sixth-form doors stay open. Schools in this catchment use all three, sometimes within the same year group, and the choice is often made for timetable reasons rather than announced as a decision.

Three separate sciences gives three certificates and the deepest content. It is the standard route for a student heading into A Level or IB Diploma sciences, and it is also the heaviest load on a Year 11 already carrying eight or nine subjects. The tutoring implication is specific: three separate sciences are three specialisms, and a general science tutor covering all three will be competent in one of them and approximate in the others.

A coordinated or double-award route covers all three disciplines in one integrated course counting as two certificates. It is the middle option most UAE schools use to keep progression open at a lower timetable cost, and it is generally accepted for sixth-form entry - though each school publishes its own requirement and that is the thing to read rather than to assume. Its characteristic weakness is interleaving: papers ask all three disciplines in sequence, and students who revise by discipline lose time reorienting.

Combined or single-award science is one certificate and the lightest load. Its weakness is depth: less practice at extended reasoning, so a question asking for explanation gets a recall answer. And its constraint is arithmetic rather than academic - one science certificate contributes one subject to the five the Ministry of Education requires for British-track equivalency.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel in the sciences
paragraphs: Both boards award International GCSEs in science and both are accepted by UAE and overseas universities. For a tutor planning eight weeks of work the differences are material: the codes differ, topic coverage diverges in places, and the practical component is assessed differently, which changes what preparation looks like.

Cambridge separate sciences are Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, each including a practical component assessed in writing - either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, depending on the centre's arrangement. The integrated routes include Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, Combined Science 0653 and Physical Science 0652. Pearson's separate sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with double and single award routes alongside and a different approach to practical skills.

The administrative differences matter as much. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct timetable version for your zone, and says plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and then revises them, so the live official PDF is the only safe reference for either.

Our first question to a Jebel Ali family is therefore the code rather than the subject, and the code is printed on the exam entry statement and on the front cover of any past paper the school has issued. One photograph settles both the board and the route, and it prevents the single most expensive mistake available in science tutoring.

sections.heading: Where marks go, discipline by discipline
paragraphs: The argument against a general science tutor is empirical rather than snobbish. The three disciplines fail differently, and the fixes do not transfer. A tutor who is excellent at the biology failure mode will not necessarily spot the chemistry one, because they are not the same kind of error.

Biology fails on command-term depth and answer structure. The content is largely present; the six-mark question is answered as a list of true statements with nothing connecting them, and the mark scheme wanted a connected account. The fix is structural: write the chain, then check each link earns something. It is a writing discipline applied to biological content.

Chemistry fails on set-up order and convention. Converting to moles after applying a ratio produces a plausible answer from the wrong proportion with no visible mistake. Naming a rate factor without explaining its effect on collision frequency earns half the mark. These are mechanical rules and they respond to enforcement rather than to understanding.

Physics fails on rearrangement and diagrams. A student who recognises a relationship but cannot transpose it quickly loses every part of a multi-step question after the first. A circuit or free-body diagram never drawn means forces and currents are summed from a mental picture, which produces sign and direction errors the diagram would have prevented. Underneath all three sits mathematics: weak arithmetic and prefix handling show up as weak science, and are regularly misdiagnosed as a content gap. Testing for that before hiring three tutors is the cheapest hour a science parent can spend.

sections.heading: The practical paper, which is where the cheapest marks are
paragraphs: Cambridge assesses practical skills in writing, through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and this is where science candidates in this catchment lose the most marks per hour of available effort. Students treat it as the easy paper because there is nothing to memorise. The mark scheme treats it as a test of precision, and precision has conventions.

What it actually asks for: apparatus chosen and the choice justified; the independent, dependent and controlled variables identified in the scenario given; each control stated in operational terms with a measurement rather than in principle; results tabulated with units in the headings; a graph with scales using most of the grid and a line that respects the data; and a procedure another person could follow without guessing.

Each of those has an expected form. "Keep the temperature constant" earns less than "hold the water bath at 30 degrees Celsius, checked with a thermometer, for every run". Units placed in the table cells instead of the headings lose marks nothing in the student's understanding justifies losing. A graph line drawn through the origin because it looks tidier, when the data does not support it, costs the analysis mark.

Four to six sessions on these conventions is typically the highest-yield block in IGCSE science, and the division of labour is clear: the hands-on practical work happens in the school laboratory under the teacher's supervision as the specification requires, and a tutor prepares the written skills and reviews the student's own write-ups. We link the official sources rather than distributing board papers or mark schemes, which are copyright material.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs around Jebel Ali, and the three-tutor problem
paragraphs: Published Dubai figures, read October 2026, attributed to whoever published them. Tutopiya advertises from about AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65, both online. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 online. Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500. Specialist exam-year work is published at AED 200-450 and above, TutorChase quotes around AED 270, and BartyED publishes AED 650.

For a separate-science student the arithmetic multiplies in a way no competitor page addresses. Three disciplines done properly means three specialists, and in-home that means three journeys to the same address each week. From Jebel Ali Village or Emaar South, three tutors willing to make that drive at a usable hour is not a realistic expectation at any price, which is why families in this catchment so often end up with one general science tutor by default rather than by choice.

Online, the three-tutor arrangement is ordinary. Each discipline gets its own specialist, each has its own slot, and the household has no journeys to accommodate. Most families still start with one discipline - the one the marked papers say is leaking most marks - and add a second only if the evidence supports it, because a Year 11 with three new tutors has three new sets of homework.

Per term is the more useful unit around here, because the route decides how many of these columns you are buying. Dubai rate guidance estimates a weekly one-hour session at roughly AED 240-600 a month at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support; across a three-month term that reads as AED 720-1,800, AED 1,800-3,600 and AED 3,000-6,000. A coordinated or double-award student needs one of those columns. A separate-science student, done properly, needs three. The advertised packages price the format rather than the teaching: around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions lands near AED 100 a contact hour, while AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits is closer to AED 200 an hour for the same eight hours, and from Jebel Ali Village or Emaar South a good part of that gap is the drive rather than the tutor. None of these are IB Gram prices; our fee is quoted after the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: The series calendar for a science candidate, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit Cambridge IGCSE science in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline to a Dubai family is handing them another country's dates. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in a May/June window and a November window.

Counting backwards is what makes a plan honest. Final entries close months before the papers, and the route and tier are fixed at that point - which means the separate-versus-coordinated question and the Core-versus-Extended question are both settled long before the exams. Mocks land about a term ahead and exist to produce data. A timed-paper cycle needs the final eight to ten weeks, which implies the syllabus has been covered once already.

Science has one extra edge the other subjects do not. Where the specification includes a practical test rather than an alternative paper, that component sits on its own date and is often earlier than the written papers, so it can be upon a student who is still planning to revise for it later. Ask the centre which practical arrangement applies and when it falls.

The checkable Pearson dates show the length of the tail: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Work from the live official timetables and confirm your centre's Cambridge administrative zone in writing.
