sections.heading: Equivalency, permits and online delivery from this catchment
paragraphs: The certificate count is where science meets the Ministry of Education. The published British-track equivalency rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than grade E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five. One page ranking in this market tells UAE parents the figure is six, which is not what the published rule says.

That matters for a combined-science student, who has one science certificate towards the five rather than two or three. It is an arithmetic check worth doing in Year 10 while the entry can still be changed, not in Year 12. Equivalency is a Ministry process that IB Gram neither performs nor influences, and tutoring is not a requirement for it; we describe it and point you to the official channel.

On permits: private tutoring in the UAE requires the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, issued through MoHRE, and the UAE government states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published schedule.

On delivery: IB Gram teaches live, one-to-one, over video on Gulf Standard Time and offers no home visits in the UAE, with in-home tutoring running only in India. The honest limitations are a student who will not begin work without an adult present, a weak connection that shortens the hour, and a shared study space the tutor cannot manage. Laboratory time belongs to the school in every case. We are not KHDA approved, hold no ADEK, MoE, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson accreditation, and publish no self-asserted ratings or outcome promises.

sections.heading: Starting with the evidence rather than the anxiety
paragraphs: Send three things: which configuration your child is entered for, the codes if you have them, and a photograph of the most recent marked science paper. If you do not know the configuration, the exam entry statement does, and the code on the front of a past paper settles the board as well.

The marked paper is what makes the first session useful, and in science it often changes the plan entirely. A family convinced the problem is chemistry frequently turns out to have a mathematics problem appearing in all three sciences: prefixes, rearrangement, reading a scale. That is one fix rather than three, and it is cheaper and faster than the three-tutor arrangement they came expecting to buy.

Matching takes about a day for the separate sciences on either board and for the coordinated routes. Where a family needs two or three disciplines at once we usually recommend starting with one, chosen on the evidence of the marked papers, and adding a second only if the next set of marks supports it. A Year 11 with three new tutors has three new homework streams and one timetable.

The trial lesson is free, taught by the matched specialist rather than a salesperson, and built on the paper you sent. It ends with a written note of what the paper showed and what the first month should target, and that note is yours whether or not you continue. When no suitable specialist has a slot at the hour you want, we say so and offer a different weekday, a short block, or an honest suggestion to look locally with the permit question in hand.

process.title: Identify the configuration
process.description: Separate sciences, coordinated or double award, or combined single award. It decides the content depth, the number of certificates and whether your child needs one tutor or three. The exam entry statement states it plainly.

process.title: Confirm the codes
process.description: 0610, 0620 and 0625 are Cambridge separate sciences; 0654, 0653 and 0652 are the integrated routes; 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 are Pearson. The code appears on the entry statement and on the front of any past paper.

process.title: Send one marked science paper
process.description: This is what most often changes the plan. A problem presented as three weak sciences frequently turns out to be one mathematics problem showing up three times, which is a single cheaper fix rather than three separate ones.

process.title: Start with one discipline, on evidence
process.description: The one the marked papers say is leaking most marks. A Year 11 with three new tutors acquires three homework streams at once, and the second discipline should be added only if the next set of marks supports it.

process.title: Free diagnostic trial, then a weekly slot
process.description: A real one-to-one online lesson with the matched specialist, ending in a written note that is yours either way. Then a fixed Gulf Standard Time slot each week, reviewed against mock results and the live series.

whyPoints.title: The configuration question gets asked first
whyPoints.description: Separate, coordinated and combined routes count for different numbers of certificates and imply different tutoring plans. No competitor page in this market asks which one a family actually has before quoting a rate.

whyPoints.title: Three disciplines, three specialists
whyPoints.description: Biology fails on answer structure, chemistry on set-up order, physics on rearrangement and diagrams. The fixes do not transfer, which is why a general science tutor is strong in one discipline and approximate in the others.

whyPoints.title: Three tutors without three journeys
whyPoints.description: In-home, a separate-science student in Emaar South would need three cross-city drives a week, which is why families here settle for a generalist by default. Online, three specialists with three slots is ordinary.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper treated as a subject
whyPoints.description: Assessed in writing and marked on precision, it is the cheapest set of marks in IGCSE science and almost nobody revises for it separately. Four to six sessions of convention work is the highest-yield block available.

whyPoints.title: The certificate arithmetic checked early
whyPoints.description: A combined-science student has one science certificate towards the five the Ministry of Education requires. That is worth checking in Year 10, while the entry can still change, rather than during a university application.

whyPoints.title: Figures and rules cited, not asserted
whyPoints.description: AED bands are attributed to their publishers with the month we read them, the equivalency rule is quoted from its source, and we claim no KHDA, ADEK, MoE, Cambridge or Pearson approval because we hold none.

faqs.question: What is the difference between separate, coordinated and combined IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Separate sciences means Biology, Chemistry and Physics entered as three qualifications with three certificates and the deepest content. Coordinated or double award covers all three in one integrated course counting as two certificates. Combined or single award covers all three in one qualification counting as one certificate, with the least depth. The configuration decides paper count, content load, sixth-form options and how many subjects count towards the five the Ministry of Education requires for British-track equivalency. The exam entry statement tells you which your child is on.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three sciences for a Jebel Ali Year 11?
faqs.answer: For a coordinated or combined course, yes, because the qualification itself is integrated. For three separate sciences at Extended level, we would usually say no. The disciplines fail differently: biology on answer structure at depth, chemistry on mole set-up order and convention, physics on rearrangement and diagrams. A tutor who is genuinely strong in one of those is approximate in the others, and at Extended level the mark schemes reward discipline-specific precision that approximation does not reach.

faqs.question: Which science topic causes most trouble in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits in physics, consistently, followed by moles and stoichiometry in chemistry. In biology it is less a topic than a habit: six-mark questions answered as a list of true statements with nothing connecting them. Beneath all three sits mathematics - prefixes, rearrangement, reading a scale - which appears on the script as weak science and is regularly misdiagnosed as a content gap. That last one is worth testing for before buying three tutors, because it is a single fix.

faqs.question: How is the practical assessed if my child studies science online?
faqs.answer: The practical component is assessed in writing in any case, through either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper depending on the centre's arrangement, and it is marked on precision rather than on laboratory skill. Hands-on work happens at school under the teacher's supervision with the school's apparatus and risk assessment, as the specification requires. What a tutor prepares is the written skills: justifying apparatus, stating controls operationally with a measurement, table and graph conventions, and describing a procedure a stranger could follow.

faqs.question: Does a combined science award limit sixth-form options?
faqs.answer: It can, and the only reliable method is to read the stated entry requirement for the specific sixth form and subject your child wants. Science entry grades are usually among the higher ones on a school's list, because the step up in the first term is steep. Within this catchment both A Level and IB Diploma routes are available, and each publishes its own requirement. Check it in Year 10 while the entry can still be changed rather than in Year 11 after results are predicted.

faqs.question: How many science certificates count towards UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: As many as your child's configuration earns: three for separate sciences, two for a coordinated or double award, one for a combined single award. The published British-track rule requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects. A combined-science student therefore needs four of the five from elsewhere on their timetable.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel sciences interchangeable for tutoring?
faqs.answer: No, and the gap is wide enough to waste a term. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610, 0620 and 0625, with integrated routes such as 0654, 0653 and 0652; Pearson runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 plus double and single awards. Topic coverage diverges in places and the practical component is handled differently, which changes the past-paper diet and the preparation. The code on the exam entry statement or the front of a past paper settles the board in seconds, and it should be confirmed before any tutor is assigned.

faqs.question: My child is weak in all three sciences. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With a marked paper from each, before buying anything. A pattern of weakness across all three disciplines very often points to one shared cause rather than three independent ones, and the usual culprit is mathematics inside science: prefix handling, rearranging a relationship, reading a scale, calculating a percentage. That is one fix, delivered by one tutor, and it is substantially cheaper and faster than three discipline specialists. If the marked papers show genuinely different failures, then the three-tutor conversation is the right one.

faqs.question: Is it realistic to have three in-home science tutors in Emaar South?
faqs.answer: Honestly, no, and that is why families this far south often end up with one general science tutor by default rather than by choice. Three specialists in-home means three cross-city drives to the same address each week, at an hour when a student is already tired, and Dubai rate guidance puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180-350 with independents to AED 500 before that multiplication. Online, three specialists with three separate slots is an ordinary arrangement, though most families should still start with one chosen on evidence.

faqs.question: When should a Year 10 start IGCSE science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is the cheapest useful point, for two reasons. First, the route and tier decisions - separate against coordinated, Core against Extended - are made at entry and they cap or release the attainable grade, so evidence collected in Year 10 influences a decision that cannot be undone later. Second, the conventions that carry practical-paper marks and the habit of writing units at every line are far cheaper to build than to repair. By Year 11 the same work competes with a mock cycle.

faqs.question: Do you provide science past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: We do not host or distribute them. Cambridge and Pearson papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and specifications are copyright material, and circulating unreleased material is a malpractice exposure for the student. We reference and link the official sources on cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, and we work from the copies the school is licensed to provide. Any service offering you a complete library of papers, or material not yet released, is worth declining on those grounds alone.

faqs.question: Does the practical test sit on a different date from the written science papers?
faqs.answer: Where a centre uses a practical test rather than an alternative-to-practical paper, that component has its own date and it is frequently earlier than the written papers. Students who plan to revise practical skills last are sometimes caught by that, and it is one of the few genuinely avoidable losses in the subject. Ask the exams officer which arrangement applies and when the component falls, and confirm the centre's Cambridge administrative zone at the same time, since the zone determines which timetable version applies.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor follow my child's school scheme of work?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we ask for it at the start, because running a parallel syllabus is one of the quieter ways tutoring fails. If the class is three weeks from starting electricity, the useful work is preparation for electricity, not revision of a topic the class finished in September. The scheme of work is usually available from the subject teacher on request, and it is the single most useful document a science parent can have, because it tells you when the difficult units arrive.

faqs.question: How do science sessions change during Ramadan in this catchment?
faqs.answer: The hour moves and the shape changes. School hours shorten and households reorganise their evening around iftar, so a weekday 5pm slot usually becomes early afternoon or post-iftar for the month. For science we suggest protecting the frequency over the length: quantitative fluency decays fastest when sessions stop, and two shorter sessions hold it better than one long one while a student is fasting. Because nobody is travelling to your address, moving a slot is a calendar change rather than a renegotiation of someone's commute.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingHeading: Answer the configuration question, then send a paper
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jebel-ali.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE science tutor in Jebel Ali, the two questions that save the most money are which configuration your child is entered for and which board. Separate sciences, coordinated or combined decides whether you need one specialist or three; the code decides the papers. Send both, plus a photograph of the most recent marked science paper, and a specialist on that specification will read it, tell you whether the problem is one shared mathematics gap or three different failures, and teach a free one-to-one trial lesson online at a Gulf Standard Time hour that works from Jebel Ali, Al Furjan or Dubai South.

intro.heading: Does anyone near JLT actually know your child's science syllabus?
paragraphs: JLT is a dense residential pocket between Sheikh Zayed Road and the Marina, served by the DMCC and Sobha Realty metro stations, with almost no schools inside its own cluster grid. Children living in the towers travel out: to The Greens, to Emirates Hills, to Al Barsha, to Al Sufouh, to Jumeirah Village. That geography is the whole reason the search for an IGCSE science tutor in JLT is harder than it looks. A tutor who lives four minutes away is easy to find. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0620 Extended to the current syllabus, knows which topics are supplement-only, and can mark a Paper 6 answer the way an examiner would, is a much smaller pool, and that pool is not organised by postcode.

So this page answers the question honestly rather than flattering it. There is no shortage of people in New Dubai who will teach science to a fifteen-year-old. There is a real shortage of people who can tell you, without looking it up, that your child's Extended entry means Papers 2, 4 and either 5 or 6, that the practical component is a fifth of the grade, and that a Core entry caps the result at a C whatever happens in the exam hall. Those three facts change what a tutoring plan should look like. A tutor who does not know them is teaching science in general, which is not the same subject as the one being examined.

IB Gram is a matching platform rather than a local agency, and it is worth being plain about what that means in practice. Lessons for UAE families are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not run home visits in Dubai; a tutor arriving at a JLT tower is not something on offer here, and home tutoring as a physical service is an India-only part of the business. What a JLT family gets instead is a wider shortlist: the search is for someone who teaches 0625 Extended and has marked Paper 4 answers for years, not for someone who happens to be free and within a twenty-minute drive of Cluster X at five in the afternoon.

The practical consequence is that a parent in JLT can stop screening by location and start screening by syllabus. The questions that matter are which code, which tier, which practical route, and which topics the last mock exposed. A tutor who answers those four crisply will be more useful than one who is physically closer and vaguer. Later on this page there is a table of seven questions that separate the two kinds of answer, and you are welcome to use it on anyone, including us.

The rest of the page covers the four science specifications a JLT student might actually be sitting, the Core and Extended tier decision and what it costs to get wrong, how practical skills are taught when nobody shares a laboratory bench, where marks go missing in 0610, 0620 and 0625, what the Dubai market charges for science tuition, and how the mandatory UAE subjects fit around a Year 11 science timetable. Nothing here requires you to book anything to be useful.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jlt.programmesIntro: A JLT family's science question is rarely only about this year. Most of the schools this neighbourhood feeds run a British route into IGCSE at sixteen and then split towards A Level or the IB Diploma, so the tutoring brief usually spans two stages rather than one.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE entry is made. Schools teach science as one subject or as three, often setting students by Year 9 on internal data and Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint results. This is where the habits that decide a Core or Extended entry are formed: unit handling, graph plotting, rearranging equations, writing a method somebody else could follow. Tutoring here is cheaper per hour and far cheaper per mark than repair work in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October, which means a Year 9 student in a JLT-area school usually has a graded external benchmark before any IGCSE tier decision is made. Ask the school whether its setting uses that benchmark or its own internal assessments, because the two do not always agree and the tier a child is placed in has a hard grade ceiling attached.

programmes.name: IGCSE sciences, Years 10 and 11
programmes.description: The two-year run to the June or November series. Cambridge candidates sit Paper 1 or 2, Paper 3 or 4, and Paper 5 or 6 in each science. Pearson candidates sit two written papers per subject with the practical skills assessed inside them. Work splits three ways: unseen content, recall under time pressure, and the specific question styles that separate a grade 6 from a grade 8. A tutor who has read the examiner reports for the code knows which of the three is actually costing your child marks.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools run both boards, sometimes within the same building for different cohorts, and the entry code on the statement of entry is the only reliable answer. Cambridge centres are allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the zone determines which version of the timetable applies, so a JLT family checking exam dates should take them from the school's exams officer rather than from a generic online timetable.

programmes.name: AS and A Level sciences, Years 12 and 13
programmes.description: Where IGCSE science choices land for students staying British. The jump is not in difficulty of recall but in the amount of reasoning asked per mark, and in practical endorsement work that has no IGCSE equivalent. Students who coasted through Extended on memory tend to stall in the first term. Tutoring at this stage works best as a weekly habit started in the September of Year 12 rather than a rescue in the spring of Year 13.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools serving JLT families offer A Level and the IB Diploma side by side, so the Year 11 decision is live rather than automatic. Students who want to keep both doors open are usually advised to hold Extended science entries and strong maths, since a Core science entry closes off the A Level route at most Dubai schools regardless of the grade achieved.

programmes.name: IB Diploma sciences after IGCSE
programmes.description: The other common exit from IGCSE around New Dubai. IB science replaces tiered papers with a syllabus split into standard and higher level, plus an internally assessed scientific investigation that is marked against published criteria. Students arriving from Extended IGCSE usually have the content base but not the investigative writing, which is the part that decides the internal assessment mark. Bridging work in the summer between Year 11 and Year 12 is cheap and unusually effective.
programmes.countryNote: The IB Diploma accounts for a smaller share of Dubai private-school enrolment than the UK curriculum, but it is growing: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A JLT family weighing the two routes should look at which schools in reach actually run Diploma science at higher level, not just which run the Diploma.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jlt.subjectsIntro: Science is not one subject on a statement of entry. Each code below has its own paper structure, its own supplement content and its own examiner habits, and the first job in a match is working out which one your child is sitting.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Recall-heavy, which misleads students into thinking it is the easy science. Marks go missing on the applied questions: enzyme and transport experiments, the detail required in a named-process answer, and the difference between describing a graph and explaining it. Extended adds supplement content across most topics.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The paper that punishes gaps in moles and equations hardest, because the same arithmetic reappears in energetics, electrolysis and titration questions. Organic chemistry is usually learned too late. Paper 6 answers lose marks on precision of method rather than on knowledge of chemistry.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: The most mathematically exposed of the three. Students who cannot rearrange a formula under time pressure cap out regardless of understanding. Electricity and waves produce the widest spread of marks, and unit errors quietly remove marks that students never see on a returned paper.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three sciences in two award slots. The content is reduced but the paper covers everything in one sitting, so revision has to be organised across subjects rather than inside them. Students often prepare as if it were three separate exams and run out of time in the one paper that matters.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One award for all three sciences, with the smallest content load of the Cambridge science routes. It suits students loading elsewhere in the timetable, but it limits science progression afterwards, so the choice deserves a conversation before Year 10 rather than after results.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Environmental Management 0680
subjects.description: Two papers, no tiering, and a syllabus that rewards data interpretation and case-study detail rather than recall. It is a genuinely useful science-adjacent option, and it is also one of the codes where a local specialist is hardest to find, which is where online matching earns its keep.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers, the longer carrying the larger share of the marks, with practical skills assessed inside them rather than in a separate test. Students moving from a Cambridge school mid-course notice the question style shift more than the content shift.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: No Core and Extended split, so there is no grade ceiling to design around, but also no reduced route for a struggling student. Calculation questions carry more marks per question than many families expect, and that is where a term of targeted work shows up fastest.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Formula handling, standard form and unit conversion decide a large share of the available marks. The absence of a separate practical paper does not mean practical reasoning is absent; it means it arrives inside written questions about apparatus, variables and sources of error.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: Three sciences across two awards on the Pearson route, taken by several British-curriculum schools in Dubai. It is a common entry on JLT-area statements of entry and a frequent source of confusion, because parents search for Cambridge paper numbers that do not exist on this specification.

sections.heading: The four science specifications a JLT student might be sitting
paragraphs: Before anything else, find the code. It is printed on the statement of entry the school issues, and it is the single most useful piece of information a parent can bring to a first conversation with a tutor. Cambridge and Pearson both call their qualification an International GCSE, both are taught in Dubai, and they are not the same examination. The paper structure differs, the tiering differs, and the practical arrangements differ enough that preparing for one while sitting the other wastes most of the preparation.

Cambridge separates its sciences into Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, with Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award and Combined Science 0653 as a single award. Each of the separate sciences is tiered. A Core candidate sits the multiple-choice Paper 1, the theory Paper 3 and either the practical test Paper 5 or the written Alternative to Practical Paper 6. An Extended candidate sits Paper 2, Paper 4 and the same practical choice. The theory paper carries half the marks, the multiple-choice paper thirty per cent, and the practical component the remaining fifth.

Pearson runs International GCSE Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 and a Science Double Award 4SD0. There is no Core and Extended split, so there is no grade ceiling built into the entry, and there is no separate practical examination. Practical reasoning is assessed inside the two written papers through questions about apparatus, variables, anomalous results and improvements to a method. Families who move a child between a Cambridge school and a Pearson school mid-course usually find the content maps across reasonably well and the question style does not.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision with a grade ceiling attached
paragraphs: On the Cambridge route, the tier your child is entered for sets the highest grade available before a single question is answered. A Core entry in 0620 can produce a grade C at best. Nothing in the exam hall changes that. An Extended entry runs the full range. This is the most consequential science decision a Dubai school makes about a fourteen-year-old, and it is frequently made on Year 9 set placement and then never revisited.

The case for a Core entry is real where it applies. A student whose school data sits well below a C is better served by a syllabus with less supplement content and a realistic chance of a solid pass than by an Extended entry that produces a grade 3 and a demoralised year. The case against is that the ceiling is permanent for that series, it closes off A Level science at most Dubai schools, and it is sometimes applied to a student whose problem was a single missing skill rather than a general weakness in science.

The practical question for a JLT parent is therefore when to look at it, and the answer is the first term of Year 10, not the spring of Year 11. By Year 11 a tier change may be administratively possible but pedagogically awkward, because supplement topics the Core group never covered have to be taught alongside revision of everything else. A term of focused work in Year 10 on the one or two skills holding a student back, typically rearranging equations, handling moles, or writing a method with a measurable variable, is often what the tier decision actually turns on.
A tutor matched by code can look at the school's own data with you and say which of those it is. That is a different conversation from a general offer of science help.

sections.heading: Paper 6, Paper 5 and teaching practical skills without a shared bench
paragraphs: A fifth of a Cambridge IGCSE science grade comes from the practical component, and most students arrive at it undertrained. Schools choose between Paper 5, a timed practical test under supervision, and Paper 6, a written Alternative to Practical. The two are not interchangeable in preparation. Paper 5 rewards hands in the right place: setting up apparatus, taking readings cleanly, recording to a consistent precision. Paper 6 rewards the written description of experimental thinking: identifying the independent and dependent variable, naming a control, spotting an anomalous point, suggesting a specific improvement rather than a general one.

Paper 6 is the more common route for private candidates and for several Dubai centres, and it is the one that online teaching handles well, because the entire assessment is written. A tutor can put a past Paper 6 on a shared screen, mark it against the published mark scheme, and show a student that saying repeat the experiment earns nothing while saying repeat the readings at each mass and take a mean earns the mark. That is a trainable skill with a short learning curve, and it is cheap marks for a student who has never had it taught deliberately.

Where a school enters students for Paper 5, online work covers the reasoning, the recording conventions and the data analysis, and the physical handling stays where it belongs, in the school laboratory. A tutor should say that plainly rather than pretending a video call can replace a bench. The useful contribution is preparing the student to use their laboratory time well: knowing before the session what a good table of results looks like, what precision the instrument supports, and what the examiner will ask them to conclude.

Pearson candidates have no separate practical paper, which does not remove practical skill from the examination. It relocates it. Questions about apparatus, error, variables and method improvements sit inside the written papers, and they are often the questions where the grade boundary between a 6 and a 7 is actually decided.

sections.heading: Seven questions that reveal whether a tutor knows the syllabus
paragraphs: This is the section to use before you pay anybody, including us. The questions below are not a test of intelligence or warmth. They test whether the person in front of you has worked with the specific examination your child is entered for, recently enough to answer without looking anything up. A good tutor will enjoy being asked. A tutor who deflects all seven is offering general science help, which has its place, but not at specialist rates in the February before a June series.

The pattern to listen for is specificity. A generalist answers in categories: it counts towards the grade, it is a bit easier, they need more practice. A specialist answers in numbers and paper names: twenty per cent, Paper 6, grade C ceiling, supplement content, command terms. Neither answer tells you whether the person is kind or whether your child will like them, and both of those matter. But only one tells you the tutoring will be aimed at the examination.

One more question worth asking, which is not in the table because it has no right answer: what will you do if my child is not improving after six weeks? The useful reply names something checkable, a change of approach, a different diagnostic, an honest recommendation to stop. The unhelpful reply is reassurance. No tutor can promise a grade, and anyone who does is telling you something about their honesty rather than their teaching. The seven questions take about ten minutes to ask and they are the cheapest diligence available to a JLT parent, because every one of them has a verifiable answer.

sections.heading: Where marks actually go missing in 0610, 0620 and 0625
paragraphs: Parents are usually told their child needs to revise more. That is occasionally true and rarely diagnostic. On marked papers from Dubai cohorts, the same handful of losses recur, and almost all of them are technique rather than knowledge. Fixing technique is faster than relearning a syllabus, which is why a marked mock paper is worth more to a first tutoring session than a report card.

In Physics 0625 the recurring losses are arithmetic and units. A student who understands that resistance rises with length still loses the mark by leaving an answer in centimetres, or by rearranging a formula in their head and transposing a term. The second cluster is waves and electricity, where diagrams have to be read precisely and where partial credit depends on showing the working that the student did silently. The fix is mechanical practice with formula rearrangement and a habit of writing the unit before the number is calculated.

In Chemistry 0620 moles are the load-bearing wall. Energetics, electrolysis, titration and yield questions all rest on the same calculation, so a student shaky on moles loses marks in four topics while appearing to have four separate problems. Organic chemistry is the second cluster, usually because it is taught late in Year 11 and revised once. In Biology 0610 the losses are verbal: naming a process rather than describing it, confusing describe with explain, and writing about a graph trend without quoting the figures that earn the mark.

Across all three, the Alternative to Practical paper is the most reliably underprepared component, and the multiple-choice paper is the most reliably untrained. Neither requires new content. Both respond quickly to deliberate work, which makes them the first place a sensible tutoring plan looks.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs around JLT, and what the money buys
paragraphs: Dubai tutoring prices are unusually opaque. Of the competitor pages reviewed for this project in October 2026, three published no price at all and two quoted in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The bands below are market rates gathered from providers' own published figures and from the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are not an IB Gram price list, and they are included so that a quote you receive can be placed somewhere sensible.

The pattern across the bands is that the hourly rate mostly buys depth of subject knowledge and, in the in-home case, a share of somebody's travel time. A JLT family paying the in-home band is paying a Dubai driving premium twice over: once in money and once in the session being scheduled when the tutor can get across Sheikh Zayed Road rather than when the student is capable of concentrating. Removing travel from the equation is the main financial argument for online delivery, and it is also the scheduling argument.

Where money is genuinely wasted is easier to name than where it is well spent. It is wasted on a cheap hour with somebody who does not know the code, because the student practises the wrong question style. It is wasted on three sciences crammed into one weekly session, which produces an hour of coverage and no depth. It is wasted on starting six weeks before a June series, when the available gain is technique only. And it is wasted on a tutor who never asks for a marked paper, because without one the first month is spent discovering what the school report already said.

Ask any provider for the rate per sixty minutes, whether it includes written feedback, and what happens if you stop after one lesson. Those three answers price a service more honestly than a headline figure does.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies around a Year 11 science timetable
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies alongside its licensed international curriculum, whatever that curriculum is. KHDA's published guidelines for mandatory subjects set this out, require the requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and go further than most parents realise into how the subjects are organised. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

The language rules matter for anyone planning a tutoring timetable. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab students in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length if the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises a minimum of twenty-five minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

For a Year 11 student working towards three science entries, the practical effect is that the week has less room in it than a science-only plan assumes. These lessons are not optional and they carry assessment. A tutoring schedule that ignores them tends to collapse in the second month. The more useful approach is to count the actual weekly hours already committed, including the mandatory subjects and the commute out of JLT, and then decide how many science slots the week can genuinely hold. For most Year 11 students that is two, occasionally three, almost never four.

One constraint is worth knowing before anybody offers to tutor these subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so support here means working with the school's own material rather than importing a parallel course.

sections.heading: Getting started from JLT, including what happens if nobody is free
paragraphs: The honest version of starting is short. You tell us the code, the tier, the school and the time of day that actually works once the bus has arrived. We look for a tutor who teaches that code, not merely that subject. A trial lesson runs before any payment, and it is a real diagnostic lesson rather than a sales call: the tutor should come out of it able to name two specific things your child is losing marks on. If the match is wrong, you say so and we change it, which is a less awkward conversation than it sounds.

The part most platforms leave out is what happens when the match is not available. Some codes have thin coverage. Environmental Management 0680, Pearson Double Award 4SD0 at short notice, and a request for a specific tier in the eight weeks before a series are the three cases where we may not have somebody suitable immediately. The disclosure is simple: if there is no UAE-based specialist free in your slot, we will say so, and the alternative is a tutor elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, which is how a great deal of this platform's teaching already happens. If neither works, that is a no rather than a holding pattern.

Two other things are worth saying plainly. A tutor here teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced; assessed work must be the student's own, and no part of it comes from a tutor's hand. And individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit from MoHRE, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years, with those operating without one subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. You are entitled to ask any tutor, anywhere, whether they hold one.

If you want the shortest possible next step: find the statement of entry, photograph the most recent marked science paper, and bring both. Those two documents make a first session roughly twice as useful as a conversation about how your child is finding science.

process.description: A photographed mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it is the most useful thing you can send. It shows where marks are going, which is almost never where a report card says the problem is, and it lets the first session start with a diagnosis.

process.description: JLT children travel out of the cluster to school. Choose a time based on when your child is actually home and able to think, not on when school finishes. Slots after 17:30 on weekdays are the ones that hold through a term.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One lesson, no payment, with a tutor matched to the code. The test is not whether it felt pleasant but whether the tutor can name two specific mark losses afterwards and say what the first month will address. If not, ask for a different match.

process.title: Review at six weeks against the paper
process.description: Six weeks in, look at a fresh timed section rather than at how the lessons feel. If the same marks are still going, the plan changes or the tutor does. This is a scheduled checkpoint rather than something you have to raise.

process.description: School reports, mocks and tier reviews each change what tutoring should be doing. A plan built in October for a Year 10 student should not still be running unchanged in February of Year 11.

whyPoints.description: The match starts from 0610, 0620, 0625, 0654, 0680, 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 or 4SD0, not from the word science. It is the difference between a tutor who teaches the examination your child is sitting and one who teaches the subject it belongs to.

whyPoints.title: A tutor pool that is not limited by driving distance
whyPoints.description: A JLT family is not restricted to whoever can reach Cluster X by five o'clock. Removing travel from the search widens the shortlist to specialists in a specific code and tier, which is the whole point when the code is an unusual one.

whyPoints.title: Practical components taught deliberately
whyPoints.description: Paper 5 and Paper 6 are treated as separate skills, and the Alternative to Practical is taught against the published mark scheme rather than assumed. A fifth of a Cambridge science grade sits there, and most students arrive at it untrained.

whyPoints.title: Prices placed in the market, not asserted
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are other providers' published figures with the source named, so a quote you receive can be compared with something. No invented statistics, no self-awarded ratings, no claim about how many families use the platform.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on what a tutor does with assessed work
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning, reviewing and feedback on work the student has produced. Assessed material must be the student's own, and that boundary is stated rather than left ambiguous, which is not true of every provider in this search.

whyPoints.title: Delivery stated once, plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. There is no home-visit service in Dubai and no UAE office, and saying so up front is more useful than discovering it after a booking.

faqs.question: Is there an IGCSE science tutor near JLT who actually knows my child's syllabus code?
faqs.answer: Within walking distance of a JLT tower, probably not reliably. The pool of people who have taught Cambridge 0620 Extended or Pearson 4CH1 recently enough to mark a paper the way an examiner does is small, and it is not distributed by cluster number. That is why the match here starts from the code rather than from a map. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the shortlist is specialists in your child's exact specification instead of whoever can reach your tower by five o'clock on a school night.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry the school issues carries the code, and the school's exams officer can confirm it in a sentence. Do not rely on the subject name: both boards call the qualification an International GCSE and both are taught across Dubai, sometimes in the same school for different cohorts. The codes matter because Cambridge physics is tiered and has a separate practical paper, while the Pearson specification has neither. Preparing for the wrong one wastes most of the preparation, so this is the first question to settle before booking anything.

faqs.question: What is the Alternative to Practical paper, and can it be taught over video?
faqs.answer: Paper 6 is Cambridge's written alternative to the supervised practical test, and it is worth twenty per cent of the science grade. It asks students to identify variables, read apparatus, spot anomalous results and suggest specific improvements to a method. Because the whole paper is written, it teaches well over video: the tutor marks past questions on a shared screen against the published mark scheme and shows where a vague answer earns nothing while a precise one earns the mark. It is usually the fastest available improvement in a Cambridge science grade.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended science during Year 11?
faqs.answer: Administratively it is often possible up to the entry deadline, and pedagogically it is awkward. The Extended papers include supplement content a Core group has never been taught, so a late change means learning new material alongside revising everything else. The better window is the first term of Year 10, when a term of work on one or two specific skills, usually formula rearrangement or moles, can change the picture the school is deciding from. Ask the school for the data behind the placement before asking for the change.

faqs.question: How many science subjects should a Year 10 student in a JLT-area school take?
faqs.answer: That is set by the school's option blocks more than by preference. Three separate sciences suit a student heading for A Level or Diploma science and able to carry the content load. A double award covers all three in two slots and frees timetable space, which can be the better choice for a student whose strengths sit elsewhere. A single award limits science progression afterwards. The decision deserves a conversation before Year 10 begins rather than after the first set of results arrives.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science topics cost Dubai students the most marks?
faqs.answer: On marked papers the same clusters recur. In physics it is unit handling and formula rearrangement, concentrated in electricity and waves. In chemistry it is moles, which quietly damages energetics, electrolysis, titration and yield questions at the same time, plus organic chemistry taught too late to revise properly. In biology it is the difference between describing and explaining, and graph answers that omit the figures carrying the marks. Almost all of these are technique rather than missing knowledge, which is why they respond faster than general revision does.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Biology, Chemistry and Physics for a double-award entry?
faqs.answer: For Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson 4SD0 a single tutor across all three is workable, because the content is reduced and the examination is sat in combined papers, so organising revision across subjects is part of the skill. For three separate science entries it is usually a false economy: an hour split three ways produces coverage without depth. Most families who try it end up with one weekly slot per subject for the subjects that matter to the next stage and school support for the third.

faqs.question: How long before the June series should science tutoring start?
faqs.answer: Earlier buys more. Started in Year 10, tutoring prevents gaps and costs less per mark gained, because it runs alongside school teaching rather than repairing it. Started six to twelve weeks out, the realistic gain is technique: paper timing, command terms, multiple-choice strategy and Paper 6 method detail. That is a genuine gain and it is not nothing, but it is not the same as content recovery. If exams are close, pick the two papers with the most recoverable marks rather than attempting the whole syllabus.

faqs.question: Do you cover Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Environmental Management 0680?
faqs.answer: Both, though coverage for 0680 is thinner than for the mainstream codes and a match can take longer. Environmental Management is untiered, sits across two papers and rewards data interpretation and case-study detail rather than recall, which makes it a genuinely different teaching job from the separate sciences. If no specialist is free in your slot, we will say so rather than offer a general science tutor and hope. Thin coverage on a niche code is a scheduling fact, not something to discover in week three.

faqs.question: What do science tutors charge around JLT and Dubai Marina?
faqs.answer: Published market bands in Dubai for 2026 run roughly AED 45-150 an hour for a university-student tutor online, AED 150-300 for a qualified subject teacher online, AED 180-500 for an in-home visit including the tutor's travel, and AED 200-450 or more for an IGCSE and A Level specialist. Those figures come from providers' own pages and from the Bestimate Dubai rate table, not from us. Ask any provider for the rate per sixty minutes, whether written feedback is included, and what happens if you stop after one lesson.

faqs.question: Will an online science tutor replace the practical work my child does at school?
faqs.answer: No, and a tutor who suggests otherwise is overselling. Physical laboratory work belongs in the school laboratory. What online teaching does well is the reasoning around it: predicting what a result should look like, designing a table before the readings are taken, choosing a precision the instrument supports, identifying an anomalous point and writing an improvement an examiner will credit. For Paper 6 candidates that is the whole assessment. For Paper 5 candidates it is the preparation that makes their supervised laboratory time count.

faqs.question: Do private science tutors in the UAE need a permit from MoHRE?
faqs.answer: Individuals offering private lessons do. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system under the service named Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Any parent may ask a tutor about it.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the UAE Ministry count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that, the requirement is one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. At least one competing site in this search publishes a six-subject figure. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel before relying on it.

faqs.question: Can lessons move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan for a Year 11 student?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for a Year 11 science cohort it is often the sensible arrangement. School hours shorten during Ramadan, afternoon concentration drops, and a late-evening slot after Iftar tends to be more productive than an earlier one that nobody is awake for. Because tutors work to Gulf Standard Time rather than travelling, a timetable shift for a few weeks is straightforward. Tell us before the month starts so the slot can be moved rather than cancelled, and move it back afterwards if the earlier time worked better.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is available for my child's code and time slot?
faqs.answer: You get told. Some combinations are thin: an unusual code, a specific tier, or a request made in the last two months before a series. If there is no UAE-based specialist free in your slot, the alternative offered is a tutor elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, which is already how much of this platform's teaching runs. If neither option fits, the answer is no rather than a waiting list that never resolves. Concealing a coverage limit is what makes families distrust platforms, so it gets stated.

faqs.question: How do we book a trial lesson for IGCSE science from JLT?
faqs.answer: Send the syllabus code, the tier, the school and the days and times that work once your child is home from school, and add a photograph of the most recent marked science paper if you have one. The trial lesson is free and runs before any payment. It should end with the tutor naming two specific things costing marks and outlining what the first month would address. If that does not happen, ask for a different tutor, which is a normal request rather than a complaint.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jlt.closingHeading: Start from the code, not the postcode
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jlt.closingBody: The useful move for a JLT family is to stop searching by distance. Find the statement of entry, note the code and the tier, photograph the last marked science paper, and look for somebody who teaches that specification rather than somebody who lives nearby. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the commute out of the towers rather than around a tutor's driving route. The trial lesson is free and comes before any payment, and if the first match is wrong it gets changed. Bring the two documents and the first session will do real diagnostic work instead of introductions.

intro.heading: Hiring against a date, not a hunch
paragraphs: Most searches for an IGCSE science tutor in Jumeirah 1 begin after a specific piece of paper arrives home: a mock grade, a predicted grade sheet, or a parents' evening comment that the practical paper is pulling the average down. The useful question at that point is not whether tutoring works in general. It is how many teaching weeks remain before the paper, what those weeks can realistically cover, and which part of the course is costing the most marks per hour of effort. That is a calendar problem before it is a teaching problem, and it has a different answer in October than it does in March.

The dates are public and they are not flexible. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, and those are the two open to a candidate in Dubai -- the February and March series is offered to India only. Final entries for a June series close in the spring, months ahead of the first paper, with forecast grades following a few weeks later and results in August; a November entry runs on the same shape and reports in January. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Everything a tutor does has to fit inside that frame.

Jumeirah 1 sits in the densest private-school market in the country. KHDA's 2024-25 figures put 387,441 students across 227 private schools in Dubai, running 17 different curricula, with the UK curriculum accounting for 37% of enrolment and the Indian curriculum 26%. In practice that means a Jumeirah 1 street can hold three families sitting three different science specifications in the same term, which is exactly why a tutor who asks for the syllabus code first is worth more than one who asks for the year group.

There is also a delivery fact to state early. IB Gram teaches UAE families one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send tutors to addresses anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a science subject that turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise, because the person who knows where the Extended paper hides its marks is rarely the person who happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of Beach Road.

The rest of this page is built as a countdown. It names the courses and their codes, separates the two practical papers, counts the exam calendar backwards from the paper to the entry deadline, lists the topics where marks actually disappear, sets out what the Dubai market charges, and states plainly what a tutor may and may not touch in a piece of assessed science work. Read the calendar section first if your child sits a paper this academic year.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE Science
programmes.description: A two-year course examined by terminal paper. Cambridge offers Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as separate subjects, plus Combined Science 0653 and Coordinated Sciences 0654 as compressed routes. Pearson offers Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 and Science Double Award 4SD0. Each written paper carries its own command-term vocabulary, and the mark scheme is unforgiving about the difference between describe, explain and suggest.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai centres sit under KHDA licensing for the school but under Cambridge or Pearson rules for the exam itself, and the centre's administrative zone decides which version of the timetable applies. Cambridge is explicit that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used, so a Jumeirah 1 family should confirm the zone with the exams officer rather than with a search engine.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The science route several Jumeirah and Umm Suqeim campuses run instead of IGCSE. Assessment is criterion-based across knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science, each marked out of eight. Students arriving at IGCSE from MYP usually hold strong investigation skills and weak timed-recall habits, because the MYP rarely asks for a two-mark definition under clock pressure.
programmes.countryNote: The transfer matters locally because families in Jumeirah 1 frequently change route rather than district, moving between a British campus in Al Safa and an IB campus in Umm Suqeim without relocating. A student moving from MYP Year 5 into IGCSE Year 11 needs the specification content audited topic by topic in the first fortnight, since criterion-marked work does not map onto a syllabus checklist.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Where a strong IGCSE science grade is usually spent. Biology, Chemistry, Physics and Sports, Exercise and Health Science run at Standard and Higher Level, each with an internally assessed scientific investigation and a collaborative sciences project. HL demands a level of quantitative confidence that an IGCSE Extended grade predicts far better than an IGCSE Core grade does.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places across the emirate. For a Jumeirah 1 family that widens the DP options within a short drive, and it makes the Year 11 science decision more consequential: a Core-tier IGCSE grade can quietly close an HL science door that was open in Year 9.

programmes.name: International A Level Sciences
programmes.description: The other common destination from IGCSE science in Dubai, run by most British-curriculum campuses in the Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster. Cambridge International A Level and Pearson International A Level both expect fluency with the IGCSE Extended content as a starting point, and both front-load the first term with the material an Extended candidate has already met once.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which is the detail that quietly changes which sciences are worth funding.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-1.subjectsIntro: Science is not one subject with one failure mode. Below are the courses a Jumeirah 1 student is likely to be sitting, with the part of each that most often costs marks. The tutoring plan for an eight-week countdown differs sharply between them.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-heavy and vocabulary-sensitive. Marks go on transport in plants, homeostasis and the genetics calculations, and on the difference between an answer that names a process and one that explains a mechanism. Extended candidates lose most in the longer data-interpretation items where the stem supplies a graph and asks for a reasoned conclusion.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Three predictable pressure points: moles and reacting-mass calculations, electrolysis products at each electrode, and organic chemistry naming and reaction types. Extended papers reward candidates who show working line by line, because method marks survive an arithmetic slip while a bare final answer does not.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism dominate the lost marks, followed by the equations-of-motion graph work and thermal physics. The recurring error is not conceptual but procedural: unconverted units, missing prefixes and answers quoted to a precision the data does not support.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Three disciplines compressed into a double award. The syllabus is narrower than three separate subjects but the papers still sample across all three, so a student who is strong in biology and weak in physics has nowhere to hide. Revision has to be rationed by discipline rather than by topic order.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single-award route taken where timetable space is tight. It is the course most often misread by families, because a good grade here does not carry the same weight into A Level sciences as a separate-subject grade. Worth checking against the destination sixth form before Year 11 begins.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Untiered, with two written papers and no separate practical exam; practical skills are assessed inside the written papers. Candidates coming from Cambridge notice the longer extended-response items and the heavier emphasis on experimental design, which has to be practised in writing rather than discussed.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Calculation-dense, with titration arithmetic, yield and atom economy appearing reliably. The command terms differ from Cambridge in small but costly ways, so a student switching boards mid-course needs a mark-scheme comparison before they need more content.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Formula-sheet discipline is the differentiator. Students who learn which equations are provided and which must be recalled convert several marks a paper. The practical-skills questions ask for variables, control and sources of error in specific wording that rewards rehearsal.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: Three papers, one per discipline, graded as two IGCSEs. A common Dubai choice where a student needs science breadth without three full subject slots. The risk is uneven preparation: the double award grade is pulled down by whichever discipline is neglected in the final six weeks.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics as a science dependency
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, percentage change and gradient work are maths skills examined inside science papers. Where a physics grade is stuck below target despite good content recall, the diagnostic is usually algebraic fluency rather than physics knowledge, and it is faster to fix.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term time
modes.description: A fixed sixty or ninety-minute slot on the same day each week, running from October through to the paper. This is the format that repairs content gaps, because it allows work to be set between sessions and marked at the start of the next one. For three separate sciences it usually means two slots a week, not three.

The work is almost entirely past-paper based, with each session ending in a timed section done unaided. sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor can change in the weeks that are left
paragraphs: The honest answer to the opening question depends on the number of teaching weeks before the paper. With twenty weeks, content can be rebuilt from the specification upwards, including the topics a student has never really understood. With eight weeks, the work is triage: identify the three highest-yield topics, drill them to a reliable standard, fix the command-term habits that leak marks across every question, and deliberately abandon what cannot be fixed. With three weeks, the only honest offer is exam technique, timing and the most frequently examined content.

That distinction matters because the wrong plan at the wrong distance wastes the budget. A family that starts an IGCSE science tutor in Jumeirah 1 six weeks out and asks for full syllabus coverage will get thin coverage of everything and improvement in nothing. The same hours spent on three named topics and twenty past-paper sections move a grade boundary far more reliably. A tutor who will not tell you which topics are being dropped is not running a countdown; they are running a syllabus tour.

The table below is the shape of an eight-week block, which is the most commonly requested length in this district between the November mocks and the spring papers. Each week carries one focus, one piece of evidence that it worked, and a session split. It is written for a single discipline. For a double award or three separate sciences, the block runs twice as long or covers one discipline at a time rather than compressing all three.

Evidence is the part families most often skip. A week without a measurable output is a week nobody can audit. A marked past-paper section, a timed topic test, or a corrected set of six-mark answers gives both the tutor and the parent something to compare against the following week. Without that, the only available signal is the school report, which arrives too late to change anything.

sections.heading: Which science course your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: The first thing worth establishing is the syllabus code, because the subject name alone does not identify the course. Two Jumeirah 1 students can both be studying IGCSE Physics and sit entirely different papers with different tiering rules, different practical arrangements and different command-term conventions. The code appears on the school's option booklet, on the exam entry confirmation and on the front page of any past paper the school has issued.

Cambridge separates its sciences into Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, each tiered into Core and Extended, and offers two compressed routes: Combined Science 0653 as a single award and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 as untiered single subjects, plus Science Double Award 4SD0, which is three papers graded as two qualifications. The structural difference that catches families out is tiering: a Cambridge Core entry caps the available grade, while the Pearson papers do not tier at all.

That distinction is the single most consequential piece of information in a Year 10 science conversation, and it is frequently discovered too late. A student entered for Core sciences cannot reach the top grades regardless of how well they perform, and the entry decision sits with the school and its exams officer rather than with the family. Any plan built with an IGCSE science tutor in Jumeirah 1 should start by confirming the tier in writing, because it determines whether the ceiling being worked towards actually exists.

The table sets the courses side by side. Paper numbering and practical arrangements are given as the structural shape rather than as a substitute for the syllabus document; the live specification on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com is always the reference, and no awarding-body material is reproduced or supplied here.

sections.heading: The practical component, and what each version actually rewards
paragraphs: Practical assessment is where the two boards diverge most, and where online tuition is most often questioned. Cambridge offers centres a choice between a timetabled practical test sat in a laboratory and an alternative-to-practical written paper that examines the same skills on paper. Pearson assesses practical skills inside its written papers rather than through a separate component. In all three arrangements, what is actually being marked is written: the identification of independent, dependent and control variables, the recognition of sources of error, the reading of apparatus to an appropriate precision, and the drawing of a conclusion the data can support.

That is the part families misunderstand. A student does not lose practical marks because they have not held a burette; they lose them because they wrote that the experiment should be repeated without saying what repetition achieves, or because they named a variable without saying how it was controlled. Those are writing habits, and they respond quickly to being drilled against a mark scheme. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school, which has the apparatus, the technicians and the safety arrangements.

Where the practical test is the chosen component, the school runs it and prepares candidates for it. Tuition in that case concentrates on the recording and analysis half: tabulating readings with consistent significant figures, plotting with a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, and calculating a gradient with units. All of that can be done on a shared screen with real data, and most of it is the same skill set the written papers examine anyway.

A practical point about format: a student who has to demonstrate a graph-drawing habit is better served by a session where the tutor can see the page. Sessions here use a document camera or a photographed worksheet so the working is visible, which is a lower-friction arrangement than it sounds and is how most of the marked work on this page's countdown gets reviewed.
bullets: Variables named, and the method of control stated for each
Significant figures consistent with the instrument, not the calculator
Anomalies identified before averages are taken

Improvements that change the result, not just repeat it

sections.heading: The IGCSE exam calendar counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: No competitor page in this market publishes an exam calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is the thing that makes every other decision urgent. Entry deadlines sit months before the paper. Forecast grades are due weeks before it. Results arrive months after. A family that discovers the entry deadline once the exam season has started has lost that series whether or not the tutoring was working.

Start with what a Dubai candidate can actually sit, because that is where most published advice goes wrong. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series; the February and March series exists but is offered to India only, and the Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests that run in March, May and October are a different product entirely and are not IGCSE. So the choice in Jumeirah 1 is June, with November as the resit route. Counted backwards from a June paper that means final entries in the spring, roughly four months earlier, forecast grades a few weeks after that, results in August and certificates later in the autumn. The exact days belong to your school's statement of entry rather than to any page like this one, and the implication is the same either way: the tier and subject decisions are effectively made in the autumn term, before most schools have issued mock results.

Pearson's pattern is different and worth knowing separately. International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November series roughly a year ahead of the first paper, and those provisional dates can be revised, so the live timetable page is the reference rather than any restatement of it.

One Cambridge administrative detail deserves its own line, because it has cost candidates entire papers. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A Jumeirah 1 family should get the zone and the zone timetable from the school's exams officer, in writing, and should not infer it from a published timetable found online.
