sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks are actually lost
paragraphs: Lost marks cluster, and the clusters are consistent enough to be worth naming. In chemistry, the reliable losses are reacting-mass and mole calculations where no working is shown, electrolysis questions where the product at each electrode is guessed rather than reasoned, and organic chemistry where the reaction type is named but the conditions are omitted. In physics, electricity and magnetism carry the heaviest losses, followed by motion graphs read as pictures rather than as gradients, and unit conversion errors that turn a correct method into a wrong answer.

In biology, the pattern is different: the content is usually known and the answer is usually too short. A six-mark question on transport in plants or on homeostasis wants a sequence of linked statements, and a student who writes three correct facts without connecting them collects half the marks. Genetics crosses lose marks on notation rather than understanding, and data-interpretation items lose them on conclusions that go further than the graph allows.

Across all three disciplines, the largest single recoverable category is command-term handling. Describe, explain, suggest, compare, state and calculate each have a settled meaning in the mark scheme, and each has a shape the answer must take. A student who answers every six-mark question with a description, whatever the verb, will cap out several grades below their knowledge. This is the cheapest thing to fix in a short countdown, because it transfers across every topic at once.

The diagnostic that makes any of this usable is the student's own marked script. Not a prediction, not a report comment, but the actual mock paper with the examiner's or teacher's marks on it. From that, a loss table can be built in a single session, and the rest of the block has a target. Any tutoring plan written before that script has been read is a guess.
bullets: Working not shown, so method marks are unavailable after an arithmetic slip
Command term ignored: a description offered where an explanation is required
Units unconverted, prefixes dropped, precision overstated
Six-mark answers that list facts without linking them causally
Conclusions drawn beyond what the supplied data supports

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the Year 10 decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Cambridge tiering is a quiet constraint that families often meet only when results arrive. Core and Extended entries sit different papers, and the Core route caps the grade available. A student performing well on Core papers can still be holding a grade that closes the door to an A Level science or an IB Higher Level science two years later, which is a route decision disguised as an exam-entry formality.

The decision belongs to the school, and it is normally made on mock evidence during Year 10 or early Year 11. That timing is the reason an autumn countdown matters more than it looks: the work done between September and the November entry deadline is not only preparation for the paper, it is the evidence base for the tier the student is entered at. A family that wants an Extended entry should be asking what evidence the school needs to see, and by when.

The reverse case is just as real. A student entered for Extended who cannot reliably access the harder items may collect a lower grade than a confident Core entry would have produced, and that grade sits on the transcript for Ministry of Education equivalency purposes as well as for sixth-form admission. The honest advice sometimes runs against the ambitious one, and a tutor who has read the marked script is better placed to say which case applies.

Pearson's untiered structure removes this decision but replaces it with a different one: subject count. Because the Double Award route grades three papers as two qualifications, it occupies fewer option slots, and families trade science depth for a second language or a humanities subject. Both trades are defensible; neither should be made without checking what the destination sixth form expects.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs around Jumeirah 1, and the home-visit question
paragraphs: Parents in this district ask about in-home tutoring first, and the question deserves a straight answer rather than a redirection. In-home one-to-one tutoring in Dubai is a real market with real prices. Published market figures put in-home visits at roughly AED 180-500 an hour with travel built in, against roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts the in-home band at AED 180-350 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A Level tutors at AED 200-450 or more; monthly packages seen in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

The premium buys travel, not teaching. An hour of in-home tuition in Jumeirah 1 includes the tutor's drive along Beach Road or Al Wasl Road in the late afternoon, and the pool of people willing to make that drive is defined by geography rather than by specialism. That is the structural problem with proximity as a selection criterion for a science subject: the number of tutors who know where Cambridge 0620 hides its marks is small, and the number of those who also live within twenty minutes of Jumeirah 1 is smaller still.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; our UAE teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visiting is a service we run only in India. Stated plainly, that is a narrower offer than some agencies advertise. It is also why a Jumeirah 1 family can be matched to a Chemistry specialist who teaches the exact specification rather than to whoever was available on that side of the city on a Tuesday.

sections.heading: Ramadan, half term and the revision weeks that genuinely exist
paragraphs: A countdown written on a calendar that ignores the UAE academic year will not survive contact with it. Between an October start and a February paper sit a half-term break, a winter break, school mock weeks, and in most years a period of shortened school days. Counting those out of an eight-week plan often leaves five or six weeks of usable teaching time, which changes the triage substantially.

Ramadan matters for scheduling rather than for content. School hours shorten, afternoons are quieter and evenings reorganise around Iftar. Many Jumeirah 1 families move a weekday session to a post-Iftar slot, which works well for an older IGCSE candidate and poorly for a tired fourteen-year-old. The practical rule is to decide the Ramadan schedule in advance rather than week by week, because a slot that is renegotiated every week tends to disappear.

School mock weeks are the other structural interruption, and they are the most useful one. A mock paper is the single best diagnostic available, and a countdown should be built to arrive at the mock with something to test and to resume immediately afterwards with the marked script in hand. Pausing tuition during mocks and restarting with the script is usually better value than running sessions through a week when the student has no capacity to absorb anything.

The winter break is where a short intensive earns its place. Four sessions across a two-week break, concentrated on one discipline, cover ground that term-time weeks cannot, because there is no competing homework. Families in this district often use the break for the discipline that is furthest behind, then return to a single weekly slot on the other two.
bullets: Count the actual teaching weeks before agreeing a plan length

sections.heading: Academic honesty in a science course, and the line a tutor holds
paragraphs: Science at IGCSE has less assessed coursework than it once did, but the honesty question still arises: around practical write-ups, around investigation tasks set by the school, and around any work that will be submitted as the student's own. The boundary is not subtle. A tutor may teach the content, model a method on a different example, explain the mark scheme, and give feedback on work the student has already produced alone. A tutor may not author any part of a piece that will be submitted for assessment, and may not supply text, data or analysis for it.

This matters commercially as well as ethically, because the UAE search results for IGCSE and IB help include operations that sell finished assessed work outright. One of them lists completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. For a student, submitting that work is a malpractice matter with consequences that reach well beyond a single grade. Any tutor or agency willing to discuss producing assessed work should be treated as a risk to the student rather than as a convenience.

There is a related boundary around materials. We reference the official syllabus, past papers and mark schemes and point families to cambridgeinternational.org and qualifications.pearson.com, and we do not reproduce or distribute those documents. Schools hold legitimate access to them, and the exams officer is the right route for a student who needs a specific past series. A tutor who offers an unlimited private library of board material is usually offering something they are not entitled to distribute.

Stating the boundary makes the service narrower and more useful at once. What a family is buying is teaching, diagnosis and feedback on the student's own work, which is the only form of help that survives contact with a terminal written exam. The grade on the paper has to be produced by the student in a hall with no support in the room, and the preparation should look like that.

process.title: Send the marked script and the syllabus code
process.description: Not the report card. The actual marked mock paper and the syllabus code from the option booklet. Those two documents let a tutor build a loss table and tell you honestly how many weeks the plan needs. Without them, the first paid session is spent on diagnosis you could have had free.

process.title: Confirm the exam series and the tier
process.description: Ask the school's exams officer, in writing, which series the student is entered for, which Cambridge administrative zone the centre sits in, and whether the entry is Core or Extended. All three change the plan. The zone matters because Cambridge publishes six different timetables and will not accept responsibility for a missed paper.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One free 45-minute lesson per family, no card details collected. The tutor works on a real topic from the marked script, not a general assessment, and you get written feedback afterwards. If the match is wrong, say so and a different tutor is proposed before any payment is made.

process.title: Agree the block and the evidence
process.description: A number of weeks, a fixed weekly slot on Gulf Standard Time, and a named output each week: a timed topic test, a marked past-paper section, a rewritten set of six-mark answers. The evidence is what makes the block auditable rather than reassuring.

process.title: Review at the halfway point
process.description: Compare the loss table from week one against the current scripts. Topics that have been fixed come off; topics still leaking marks either get more time or get deliberately dropped. This is also the point to decide whether a second discipline joins the plan or waits until after the paper.

whyPoints.title: The specification comes first
whyPoints.description: Every plan starts from the syllabus code and the student's own marked script, because IGCSE Physics 0625 and 4PH1 are different papers with different conventions. A tutor who teaches generic physics to a specific specification loses marks the student has already earned.

whyPoints.title: Specialism over proximity
whyPoints.description: A Jumeirah 1 address limits a driving tutor to whoever is within range in late-afternoon traffic. Teaching over live video removes that filter, so the selection criterion becomes whether the tutor knows the paper rather than whether they know the postcode.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is part of the service
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, forecast-grade dates and results dates are published, and they decide what is possible. Any plan here is costed against the actual number of teaching weeks left after breaks and mock weeks, not against an idealised term.

whyPoints.title: Written evidence every week
whyPoints.description: Each session produces something markable: a timed section, a corrected calculation set, an experimental-design answer. Progress is read from those, which is why a mid-block review can show what changed rather than asserting it.

whyPoints.title: Honest limits, stated early
whyPoints.description: No home visits anywhere in the UAE, no assessed work produced on a student's behalf, no board material redistributed, and no grade promised. Where no specialist is free for a niche course in a given week, we say so and give a date rather than substituting someone who does not know the paper.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry a source
whyPoints.description: Market rates on this page are attributed to the organisation that published them and dated October 2026. Regulatory statements are attributed to u.ae, KHDA, Cambridge International or Pearson. Nothing here is presented as our own statistic without the underlying data.

faqs.question: How late in Year 11 can an IGCSE science tutor still change the grade?
faqs.answer: Later than most families expect, but what changes depends on the distance. With twenty weeks, content can be rebuilt from the specification. With eight, the work is triage: three named topics drilled properly, command-term habits fixed across every question, and the rest deliberately set aside. With three weeks, the honest offer is exam technique, timing and the most frequently examined material. The one thing that does not work at short range is full syllabus coverage, which produces thin familiarity with everything and reliability in nothing. Ask any tutor at short notice which topics they intend to drop; if they will not name them, there is no plan.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science syllabus codes does my child's Jumeirah 1 school use?
faqs.answer: The school's option booklet and the exam entry confirmation both carry it, and so does the front page of any past paper the school has issued. Cambridge uses Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Combined Science 0653 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. Pearson Edexcel uses Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 and Science Double Award 4SD0. The Al Safa and Umm Suqeim cluster around Jumeirah 1 contains both Cambridge and Pearson centres, so two neighbours studying the same named subject can be sitting different papers with different tiering rules. Confirm the code before agreeing a tutoring plan.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if the lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: What is marked in every arrangement is written work, not laboratory performance. Cambridge centres choose between a timetabled practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper; Pearson assesses practical skills inside its written papers. In all three cases the marks go on naming variables and stating how they were controlled, reading instruments to an appropriate precision, identifying anomalies, plotting and calculating gradients, and limiting conclusions to what the data supports. Those are writing habits and they drill well on a shared screen. The laboratory work itself belongs to the school, which holds the apparatus, the technicians and the safety arrangements.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a Cambridge practical test and the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: One is sat in a laboratory with apparatus, the other is a written paper that examines the same skills on paper. The centre decides which route its candidates take, so a family cannot choose between them; the exams officer can confirm which applies. For tuition the difference is small, because both assess the recording and analysis half of practical work: tabulating readings with consistent significant figures, spotting anomalies, plotting sensibly, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, and evaluating sources of error. Preparation for either should centre on written answers marked against the published scheme.

faqs.question: Should my child take Co-ordinated Sciences or three separate IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: It is a timetable trade rather than an ability question. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 compresses three disciplines into a double award, occupying fewer option slots and leaving room for another subject. Three separate subjects cover more content and carry more weight into A Level or Higher Level sciences. The risk with the double award is that papers sample across all three disciplines, so weakness in one is visible in the overall grade with nowhere to hide. Check what the destination sixth form expects before the option form is signed, because that expectation is the only decisive input.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge entries close for the series my Jumeirah 1 child will actually sit?
faqs.answer: Months before the papers, and the series matters: a Dubai candidate sits the Cambridge June series or the November one, never the February and March series, which Cambridge offers to India only. Final entries for June are made in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first script, with forecast grades a few weeks before the exam period and results in August; a November entry closes earlier in the year and reports in January. Pearson gives you a date you can check against a published timetable -- its November 2026 International GCSE window ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read backwards, that means the tier and subject decisions are effectively made in the autumn term, often before mock results are issued. A family planning autumn tuition should treat the entry deadline as the first fixed point in the plan and confirm both the series and the entry with the school's exams officer in writing.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge timetable zone is my child's Dubai exam centre in?
faqs.answer: The school's exams officer is the only reliable source for that. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for the centre's zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. That makes the zone a piece of information worth getting from the school's exams officer in writing rather than inferring from a timetable found online. It is also why revision schedules built from a generic timetable can quietly put a paper on the wrong day.

faqs.question: My child is entered for Core science — can they still move to Extended?
faqs.answer: Possibly, but the decision sits with the school and its exams officer, and it is made on evidence before the entry deadline. The practical consequence of a Core entry is that the grade available is capped, which can close an A Level or Higher Level science route two years later. If an Extended entry is the goal, ask the school what evidence it needs to see and by when, then build the autumn work to produce exactly that: marked topic tests and timed past-paper sections at Extended demand. After entries close, the tier is fixed for that series regardless of later progress.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of IGCSE science tuition make sense in Year 11?
faqs.answer: For one discipline, a single sixty or ninety-minute weekly slot with work set between sessions is usually enough during term time, rising to two sessions a week in a six to eight week countdown. For three separate sciences, two slots a week rotating between disciplines works better than three slots that collapse under homework pressure. The limiting factor is rarely the tutor's availability; it is the number of hours the student can give to independent work between sessions. A plan that leaves no room for that produces attendance rather than progress.

faqs.question: Do the three sciences need three different tutors?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Many tutors teach two disciplines to IGCSE depth comfortably, and biology and chemistry pair more often than physics and biology. Where a grade is tier-critical or a specific component is failing, a specialist in that single discipline is usually better value than one person covering all three thinly. The practical approach is to start with the discipline losing the most marks, establish a pattern there, and add a second only if the student's independent-study time can absorb it. Three concurrent tutors in Year 11 is rarely a workable schedule.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE science tuition cost around Jumeirah 1 and Al Safa?
faqs.answer: Published market bands for Dubai put budget online tutors at roughly AED 45-150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at AED 150-300, in-home visits at AED 180-500 with travel included, and IGCSE or IB specialists at AED 200-450 or more. Bestimate's Dubai rate table gives in-home at AED 180-350; TutorChase publishes AED 270. Monthly packages seen in the market include roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are other organisations' published figures as at October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Our own rate is quoted after a free trial lesson against the subject and the number of weeks.

faqs.question: How should a Jumeirah 1 science revision schedule change during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Most families move the session to a post-Iftar slot, and for an older IGCSE candidate it often works better than a shortened afternoon. School hours contract during Ramadan and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so a fixed post-Iftar slot is usually easier to protect than a 4pm one. The practical advice is to set the Ramadan schedule before the month begins rather than renegotiating weekly, because a slot that moves every week tends to disappear. For younger students the opposite often applies: a shorter session earlier in the day, with less content and more review, holds attention better than a late one.

faqs.question: Do IGCSE sciences count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which changes which subjects are worth funding. Sciences count like any other accredited subject. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring platform performs or influences, and the requirements should be verified on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority before any decision rests on them.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to help with a school science investigation task?
faqs.answer: Only within a clear boundary. A tutor may teach the underlying content, model a method on a different example, explain what the mark scheme rewards, and give feedback on work the student has already produced alone. A tutor may not author any part of a piece that will be submitted for assessment, or supply text, data or analysis for it. That line matters in this market, because some operations in these search results sell finished assessed work outright, and a student who submits it faces a malpractice matter rather than a bad grade. Teaching and feedback are the only forms of help that survive a terminal exam.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for Pearson Double Award science that week?
faqs.answer: We say so and give a date rather than substituting somebody who does not know the specification. Science Double Award 4SD0 sits across three disciplines, so the match has to cover the discipline actually losing marks, and the pool for a specific component in a specific week is finite. Where the wait is longer than the countdown allows, the useful options are to start with the discipline that is covered now, or to begin with a single-topic repair block on the strongest available match. Both are stated before any payment, with the limitation named.

faqs.question: Does a tutor working with a Jumeirah 1 family need a MoHRE work permit?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this applies to online work as well. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted. The application route is MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service, stated as a two-working-day completion.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics as separate sciences and as a combined or co-ordinated award, across Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel. Each one works from the specific paper structure your child's school has entered them for.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one afternoon, and a drive back from Al Safa
paragraphs: The science problem in Jumeirah 2 is arithmetic before it is academic. A Year 10 or Year 11 student on triple award is carrying three separate GCSE subjects that between them occupy roughly a fifth of the school timetable and produce three sets of homework, three sets of end-of-unit tests and, at Cambridge, three practical components. A family that decides to add tuition is not deciding what to study. They are deciding which of three subjects gets the single weekly hour that the afternoon can actually hold.

That afternoon is shorter than it looks. Jumeirah 2 has no secondary school within its boundaries, so every student here is driven out and back. A child at Jumeirah College in Al Safa finishes around 3:05pm and is home by about 3:25pm. A child at Dubai College in Al Sufouh finishes around 3:20pm and, with Sheikh Zayed Road backed up at the Safa interchange on a Sunday, is not home before 4:10pm. A child at Kings' School Dubai in Umm Suqeim 3 with a commitment until 4:30pm walks in at 5pm. Add swimming on Mondays and an Arabic class on Sundays and there are typically two usable evenings a week, not five.

So the honest answer to a search for an IGCSE science tutor here starts with triage. Which of the three sciences is actually losing marks, and is it losing them for the same reason in all three? In our experience it usually is. A student weak on ratio and proportion loses marks on mole calculations in chemistry, on density and pressure in physics, and on magnification and rates in biology. One hour of ratio work shows up in three subjects. A student whose problem is command-term discipline — answering "explain" with a description, answering "suggest" with a recall — loses marks in all three for the same reason as well.

The second thing worth establishing is the award structure and the codes, because they change the paper count. Cambridge separate sciences are Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, three papers each. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award covering all three in two GCSEs, and Combined Science 0653 is a single award. Pearson runs Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 as separate sciences with two papers each, and Science Double Award 4SD0 with six. A tutor planning revision for a triple-award candidate as if they were on a double award will leave a third of the content untouched.

IB Gram delivers all UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-home visiting is a service we run only in India. For a three-science household the practical gain is the half hour an arriving tutor needs: the student closes the front door, opens a laptop and the hour starts, which with two usable evenings a week is not a small thing.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.programmesIntro: Schools serving Jumeirah 2 structure science at 16 in three different ways, and the number of GCSEs at the end differs. This is what each route involves.

programmes.name: Separate sciences: Biology, Chemistry and Physics
programmes.description: Three distinct IGCSE qualifications. At Cambridge that is 0610, 0620 and 0625, each assessed by a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component, with Core and Extended tiers available. At Pearson it is 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, each with two written papers and practical skills examined within them. This is the route most selective British schools in this catchment take for students heading to A Level sciences.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools account for 37% of Dubai private-school enrolment, the largest single share across 227 private schools serving 387,441 students in 2024-25. Triple award is the standard offer at the selective end of that group, which is why a Jumeirah 2 family often finds their child carrying three sciences without having consciously chosen it.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated or Double Award Science
programmes.description: All three sciences taught and examined together for two GCSE grades rather than three. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences is 0654, with Core and Extended tiers; Pearson Science Double Award is 4SD0, assessed across six papers split by discipline. Content is reduced in each subject rather than one subject being dropped, so a student still meets all three but in less depth.
programmes.countryNote: Double award is the sensible route for a Jumeirah 2 student who wants a broad sixth form rather than three A Level sciences, and it leaves a timetable with genuine space in it. It does not close the A Level door, but a student moving from double award into A Level Chemistry should expect a summer of catching up on the depth the separate course would have covered.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The post-16 route for students at the IB schools in this ring. Diploma sciences are assessed by Paper 1 at 36% of the grade, Paper 2 at 44%, and an internally assessed scientific investigation at 20%. The step up from IGCSE is less about content than about writing reasoning the mark scheme can credit, and about handling an independent piece of experimental work.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students are 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment, and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 places. A Jumeirah 2 student on triple award at a British school who then moves to a Diploma sixth form arrives better prepared in content and short on the investigation skills, which is a predictable and cheap gap to close in the summer between.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson International A Level Sciences
programmes.description: The other post-16 route in this catchment, where triple-award students usually continue into two or three sciences. A Level sciences assume the separate-science content in full, including the practical skills examined in the Cambridge Paper 5 practical test or the equivalent Pearson component.
programmes.countryNote: For a Jumeirah 2 family the cheap intervention point is the Year 11 summer. Six to eight hours spent on the quantitative skills that A Level sciences assume — rearranging equations, logarithms, standard form, uncertainty — costs the IGCSE rate now and prevents remedial work at the specialist rate in the spring of Year 12.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-2.subjectsIntro: A science booking in this district usually covers two or three subjects and often picks up maths as well. These are the components each one is actually assessed on.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: A multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either the Paper 5 practical test or the Paper 6 alternative to practical, which carries a fifth of the marks. The theory paper rewards working shown in order with units; the practical component rewards graph discipline and recognising a systematic error in a described method.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Same three-component structure. Mole calculations, titration arithmetic, percentage yield and empirical formulae carry most of the quantitative marks, and organic reactions carry most of the recall. A student weak on ratio loses marks here and again in physics.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Less arithmetic, far more command-term dependence. Describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different answer shape, and a correct biological idea written in the wrong shape earns nothing. Magnification, surface-area-to-volume ratios and rate calculations are the quantitative exceptions.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: All three disciplines examined for a double award. The content in each is reduced rather than removed, so a revision plan has to be built from the 0654 syllabus itself rather than by partially covering three separate ones, which is the most common planning error on this route.

subjects.name: Biology (Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, with the larger carrying the greater share of the marks and practical skills examined within the written components rather than separately. Pearson's question style leans more on applied scenarios than Cambridge's, which changes the past-paper diet a student needs.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them. The quantitative content overlaps heavily with Cambridge 0620 but the mark schemes differ in how much credit the method attracts, which matters for a student who is strong on answers and weak on working.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers covering forces and motion, electricity, waves, energy, magnetism, radioactivity and astrophysics. The astrophysics content has no Cambridge 0625 equivalent at the same depth, which is a real gap for any student who changes board mid-course.

subjects.name: Science Double Award (Pearson 4SD0)
subjects.description: Six papers split across the three disciplines for two GCSE grades. The paper count surprises families who assume a double award means less assessment; it means less content per paper, not fewer sittings.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: Booked with science more often than anything else in this district, because the overlap is causal rather than coincidental. Ratio, proportion, standard form, rearrangement and reading a gradient are maths skills examined inside science papers.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken by triple-award students heading for A Level sciences. It introduces calculus and trigonometric identities a year early and is the single best predictor of a comfortable Year 12 in physics and chemistry.

sections.heading: Which award your child is on, and how many papers that means
paragraphs: Parents in this district routinely tell us their child is "doing science" without knowing whether that is one GCSE, two or three. It is worth establishing in writing, because the paper count, the content volume and the revision plan all follow from it. The phrase to ask the school is which award and which syllabus codes, and the answer should be a list of numbers.

Cambridge separate sciences are Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625. Each one is assessed by a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper at Core or Extended tier, and a practical component which is either the Paper 5 practical test or the Paper 6 alternative to practical. That practical component carries a fifth of the subject's marks, and it is the one most often neglected in revision because it does not look like the rest of the course. Three separate sciences therefore mean nine components in total.

Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines for two GCSE grades, with Core and Extended tiers. Combined Science 0653 covers them for one. On the Pearson side, Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 each have two written papers, with practical skills examined inside them rather than in a separate component, and Science Double Award 4SD0 has six papers split across the three disciplines. A family on 4SD0 is sometimes surprised that a double award involves six sittings; the reduction is in content per paper, not in the number of papers.

The reason the code matters more than the subject name is that past papers are the main currency of revision and they are code-specific. A triple-award Cambridge student working through 0654 papers is practising a reduced syllabus and will be short on the Extended content. A 4PH1 student working through 0625 papers will never meet the astrophysics material that Pearson examines and Cambridge does not cover to the same depth.

sections.heading: Building a science week around the Jumeirah 2 school run
paragraphs: The table below is the planning document most families in this district actually need. It sets out the schools a Jumeirah 2 science student is likely to attend, the typical end of a normal day, the realistic door-to-door return, and the earliest hour a science session can begin once the child is home and fed. These are normal days without a fixture or a rehearsal; one of those pushes everything back by an hour and a half.

The pattern that emerges is a two-tier one. Students at the Al Safa gates have a usable 4pm to 4:15pm slot. Students at Dubai College, Kings' School Dubai and the Al Sufouh schools do not, and for them 4:45pm is the first honest option. Booking the earlier time for a second-ring student is a decision to miss the session twice a month, which is how tuition quietly stops in this neighbourhood.

Day of week matters as much as time of day. Sunday afternoons are the slowest on Al Wasl in this district, and Thursday is the day most families would rather keep clear. Monday, Tuesday and Wednesday are where the two usable evenings almost always sit, and the practical recommendation is to take one of them and hold it for the whole term. A science session that moves every week has stopped happening by about week six.

There is a particular argument for a video lesson on a three-science timetable. On a triple-award schedule the homework load is already three streams deep, and the half hour that an arriving tutor needs — the knock, the settling, the offer of a drink, the leaving early to beat the traffic — comes out of the only hour available. Removing the travel from both sides converts a 45-minute lesson into a 75-minute one without anybody paying for extra time.

sections.heading: The practical component, and how it works without a school lab
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how practical science can be supported over video, and the answer is more encouraging than it sounds, because of how the practical component is actually assessed. At Cambridge, separate-science candidates sit either the Paper 5 practical test or the Paper 6 alternative to practical, and the great majority of international candidates sit Paper 6. Paper 6 is a written paper about practical work: it describes an experiment and asks the candidate to read a scale, plot and interpret data, identify a variable that should have been controlled, spot the systematic error in the method, and suggest an improvement. No apparatus is required to be good at it.

That is fortunate, because Paper 6 is worth a fifth of the subject's marks and it is the component where the most marks are available for the least teaching. The skills are finite and listable: reading a measuring instrument to the correct precision, choosing axes that use most of the grid, drawing a line of best fit rather than joining points, calculating a gradient with units, distinguishing a random error from a systematic one, and writing an improvement that would actually change the result rather than a platitude about repeating the experiment.

On the Pearson side, practical skills are examined inside the written papers rather than in a separate component, which changes where they appear but not what they require. The same graph discipline and the same method critique show up as parts of longer questions, often carrying several marks each. A student who has drilled the Cambridge Paper 6 skills handles those Pearson questions well, which is one of the few places where the two boards converge usefully.

What a video lesson cannot do is give a student the physical experience of handling apparatus, and we would not pretend otherwise. That experience comes from the school's own laboratory, which every school in this catchment has. What tuition adds is the part the school lab tends not to teach explicitly: the written technique that converts having done an experiment into marks on a Paper 6 script.

sections.heading: Where marks go missing in each of the three sciences
paragraphs: Physics loses marks on units and on rearrangement. A student who knows that pressure is force over area will still lose the mark by giving an answer in newtons, or by rearranging an equation with a square root in it and dropping the root. Beyond that, the recurring physics failures are moments and the principle of moments stated without the pivot identified, electrical circuits where the student computes a total resistance correctly and then applies the wrong potential difference to a branch, and radioactivity questions where half-life arithmetic goes wrong because the student counts intervals rather than halvings.

Chemistry loses marks on moles and on reasoning. The mole calculations themselves are rarely the problem; the problem is the chain — grams to moles, moles to moles by the equation ratio, moles back to grams or volume — where students take one step correctly and skip the ratio. After that: ionic equations written with charges unbalanced, electrolysis answered at the wrong electrode, and rates questions where the student describes the graph rather than explaining the collision-theory reason for its shape. Organic chemistry at IGCSE is mostly recall and is the cheapest part of the subject to fix.

Biology loses marks almost entirely on command terms and precision of language. "Explain" answered with a description is the single most common error in the subject. "Suggest" answered with recall rather than applied reasoning is the second. After those: osmosis described without the words water potential or concentration gradient used correctly, genetic crosses where the Punnett square is right and the ratio is misread, and enzyme questions where the student says the enzyme "dies" rather than that it denatures.

The useful observation for a family triaging three subjects is that two of these three lists are dominated by a single shared failing. Ratio reasoning covers the physics rearrangement and the chemistry mole chain. Command-term discipline covers most of biology and a large part of the explanation marks in the other two. An hour a week on those two things improves three papers, which is why the shared-skills pattern is often better value than one subject at a time.

Chemistry: the mole chain skipping the equation ratio; unbalanced ionic equations

Two shared failings, ratio and command terms, account for most of all three

sections.heading: What three sciences cost to support, rather than one
paragraphs: Pricing a science booking in this district means pricing a subject count, and most published rate cards are written for one subject. Taking the market as published in October 2026: Unitors quotes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour; Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table puts specialist IGCSE, IB and A Level rates at AED 200 to 450 and above; TutorChase quotes around AED 270; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from roughly AED 33 to 52 at the university-student tier; BartyED sits at around AED 650. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors.

Against those figures, three separate weekly sessions is a large commitment and very few families in Jumeirah 2 run it. What most do instead is one of three things. They rotate one subject per term, which costs one session a week across the whole year. They buy a shared-skills hour that serves all three, which costs the same and covers more. Or they buy nothing in Year 10 and two sessions a week from January of Year 11, which concentrates the spend into one term.

Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour arrangement are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Monthly packages advertised in this market include roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Those are the figures to hold in mind when a provider quotes you three subjects, because three separate arrangements at the mid band is a commitment on the scale of a school activity fee rather than a small addition.

One useful point of leverage: because maths underlies the quantitative marks in all three sciences, a family already paying for maths tuition may get more science marks from asking that tutor to work explicitly on ratio, standard form and rearrangement in science contexts than from adding a fourth subject. We will say so when it applies, including when it means a smaller booking.

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Those are the two series UAE candidates sit. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a parent reading an Indian tutoring page and planning a science revision timetable around a March exam will be planning for the wrong country.

Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. For a three-science candidate that is a real operational risk: nine components across three subjects, spread over several weeks, and a zone-specific ordering that determines which subject needs to be ready first.

Working backwards from the June series, the fixed points are the tier and entry decision in the autumn term, mocks in January or February, and then the only question that matters: how many complete timed papers, marked against the official mark scheme, before the first real one. For a triple-award candidate that means papers in three subjects plus three practical components, and a realistic target is two full sets. Most students manage one.

The November series is the resit route. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January — November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, so a resit decision taken in late August leaves roughly eight teaching weeks. That is enough for one science, possibly two, and not enough for three. Always work from the live official timetable on the board's own site rather than from a date restated on any tutoring page, including this one.

sections.heading: KHDA inspection bands and what a science department rating tells you
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and which inspects every private school annually on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak. Parents in Jumeirah 2 reasonably use those ratings when choosing a school and then rarely look at them again, which is a missed opportunity, because the published inspection report usually says something specific about subject departments rather than only awarding an overall grade.

What to look for in the report, if you are trying to work out whether your child's science difficulty is theirs or the school's, is the attainment and progress judgement for science at the secondary phase rather than the headline band. A school rated Very Good overall can have a science judgement a band lower, and that is a far more useful signal about whether a Year 10 class is likely to be well taught than any overall label. Ratings should only ever be read from the regulator's own published report, not from an aggregator.

The regulator map across the country is worth knowing too, because families in this district move between emirates more often than they expect. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Two further KHDA facts that bear on a science timetable. Dubai's private school sector served 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 different curricula, and KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for the 2026-27 academic year under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Separately, the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 new places, with enrolment having risen 6% in 2025-26. A growing cohort means larger science sets, and larger sets are the context in which a quiet student with a ratio problem goes unnoticed.

sections.heading: What a science tutor may and may not do with your child's work
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences on the specifications used in this catchment carry no coursework component, which removes the sharpest academic-honesty risk from this page. It does not remove the issue. Homework handed in for a school grade is the student's own work under every school's policy, and students on triple award have three streams of it, which is exactly the situation in which a well-meaning adult starts filling in answers.

The boundary we hold, and state to the student in the first session, is that the tutor teaches a method and works a parallel example while the student does the question that gets submitted. In practice, on a science homework set, that means the tutor takes the first structured question and the student takes the rest, with the tutor watching rather than dictating. It is slower and it is the only version in which the hour has been worth paying for.

We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and reproducing them is a copyright problem rather than a grey area. We link the official source and work from material the student legitimately holds through their school, which in practice is most of what they need.

One more honesty point specific to science advertising. No tutor can promise a grade, and a page that attaches a guaranteed outcome to a price is making a claim it cannot stand behind. What a plan can honestly offer is a diagnosis, a named set of skills to fix, timed papers marked against the official scheme, and a recorded score that either moves or does not. That is a thing a parent can check.

faqs.question: My child takes three IGCSE sciences. Which one should get the tutoring hour?
faqs.answer: Decide it from three marked unit tests rather than from which subject feels hardest. Sort the lost marks in each into content gaps, missing reasoning, arithmetic slips and misread questions. In most cases one category dominates across all three sciences, and then the answer is not a subject at all: it is an hour a week on ratio and proportion, or on command-term discipline, which shows up in three papers rather than one. If one subject genuinely has a content hole, take that subject for a term and review at the end.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE science session start for a Jumeirah 2 student?
faqs.answer: It depends which gate they come out of. Al Safa schools finish between about 2:45pm and 3:05pm with a fifteen to twenty-five minute run home, so 4pm or 4:15pm Gulf Standard Time works. Dubai College, Kings' School Dubai and the Al Sufouh schools finish around 3:10pm to 3:20pm with a twenty-five to forty-five minute run, so 4:45pm is the first honest slot. Booking the earlier time for a second-ring student means missing it twice a month, which is how science tuition quietly stops in this district.

faqs.question: What is the difference between triple award and co-ordinated sciences at IGCSE?
faqs.answer: Triple award is three separate qualifications: at Cambridge that is Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, each with a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and a practical component, so nine components in total. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 covers all three disciplines for two GCSE grades across three components, with content reduced in each subject rather than one subject removed. Pearson's equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for separate sciences and Science Double Award 4SD0, which has six papers despite awarding two grades.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: Most international Cambridge candidates sit Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is a written paper about practical work rather than a laboratory exam. It asks the candidate to read a scale to the correct precision, plot and interpret data, identify a variable that should have been controlled, spot a systematic error in a described method and suggest an improvement that would actually change the result. Those skills are taught perfectly well over a shared screen. The physical handling of apparatus comes from the school laboratory, which every school in this catchment has.

faqs.question: Why does the alternative to practical paper matter so much?
faqs.answer: Because it carries a fifth of the marks in each Cambridge separate science and it is the component most often left out of revision, on the assumption that it is somehow covered by doing experiments at school. It is not: it is a written technique with a finite and listable skill set. Choosing axes that use most of the grid, drawing a line of best fit instead of joining points, calculating a gradient with units, and distinguishing random from systematic error are each worth marks every series, and a few focused hours visibly change the score.

faqs.question: Which syllabus codes do schools near Jumeirah 2 use for science?
faqs.answer: The Al Safa and Al Sufouh ring uses a mixture. Cambridge separate sciences 0610, 0620 and 0625 are the standard offer at the selective British schools; Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 appears where a broader sixth form is expected; and Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and Science Double Award 4SD0 are used by a growing number of schools. Ask the head of science to confirm the award and the codes by email before booking anything, because past papers are code-specific and practising the wrong set leaves content untouched.

faqs.question: Is a single tutor across biology, chemistry and physics realistic for a Jumeirah 2 student?
faqs.answer: At IGCSE level, usually yes, and for a shared-skills hour it is the better arrangement. The failings that cost most marks across all three are ratio reasoning and command-term discipline, and one tutor seeing the same error in three different papers fixes it once rather than three times. Where a single subject has a genuine content hole, particularly in Extended-tier physics or organic chemistry, a subject specialist for a term is worth it. At A Level and IB Higher Level the three subjects need separate specialists.

faqs.question: What does supporting three sciences cost compared with one?
faqs.answer: Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates put a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour. Three separate weekly sessions multiplies that by three, and almost no family in this district runs it. One shared-skills hour or one subject rotated per term costs the same as a single subject and covers more of the problem.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a villa in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not provide home visits anywhere in the UAE; in-home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video with a shared screen. In-home science tuition is a real option in Dubai, quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 with independent tutors, including travel. On a triple-award timetable with two usable evenings a week, removing the arrival and departure from both ends recovers most of a session.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit their IGCSE science exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Those are the two series UAE candidates sit. The February/March series is offered to India only, so a timetable copied from an Indian page will be eleven weeks wrong. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: How many science papers can realistically be resat in November?
faqs.answer: One subject comfortably, two with effort, three rarely. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, so a decision taken in late August leaves roughly eight teaching weeks. Three sciences means nine Cambridge components or six Pearson papers, and eight weeks cannot carry that. Pick the subject where the gap between the grade awarded and the grade needed is smallest.

faqs.question: Where do IGCSE physics students in this area lose the most marks?
faqs.answer: Units and rearrangement, before anything topic-specific. A student who knows pressure is force over area still loses the mark by answering in newtons, or by rearranging an equation containing a square root and dropping the root. After that the recurring failures are moments stated without identifying the pivot, circuit questions where the total resistance is right but the wrong potential difference is applied to a branch, and half-life arithmetic where the student counts time intervals rather than the number of halvings.

faqs.question: What is the most common biology mistake in IGCSE scripts from Dubai?
faqs.answer: Answering "explain" with a description. A student writes what happens, accurately, and never says why, and the mark scheme awards credit only for the reason. The second most common is answering "suggest" from recall instead of applying knowledge to the unfamiliar scenario in the question. After those: osmosis described without using water potential or concentration gradient correctly, genetic crosses where the Punnett square is correct and the ratio is misread, and saying an enzyme dies rather than denatures.

faqs.question: How do I read a KHDA inspection report to judge a science department?
faqs.answer: Look past the overall band. KHDA inspects every Dubai private school annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak, and the published report normally carries attainment and progress judgements by subject and phase. The science judgement at secondary phase tells you far more about whether a Year 10 class is likely to be well taught than the headline grade, and a school rated Very Good overall can sit a band lower in science. Read it on KHDA's own site rather than from an aggregator.

faqs.question: Can science sessions carry on through Ramadan in Jumeirah 2?
faqs.answer: Yes, with a different slot. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the household day reorganises around iftar, so an afternoon session that worked in February usually will not. Most families here move to a post-iftar evening session, and some prefer a short weekend morning instead. We agree the arrangement in writing before the month begins rather than improvising, because improvised weeks are the ones that get skipped. Since lessons run over video, changing the time involves no travel to renegotiate.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor complete my child's homework if it is due tomorrow?
faqs.answer: No. The tutor teaches the method and works the first structured question as a parallel example, and your child does the rest while the tutor watches. That boundary is stated to the student in the first session and it is not negotiable, because work handed in for a school grade must be the student's own under every school's policy. We also do not supply past papers or mark schemes as downloads, since those belong to Cambridge and Pearson; we link the official source instead.

intro.heading: Three sciences, two grades or one: the entry decides everything else
paragraphs: Science is the subject where Dubai families most often buy the wrong amount of tutoring, and the cause is almost always a misunderstanding about the entry. A student taking Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 is sitting three separate courses and will receive three grades. A student taking Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is sitting one course covering all three disciplines and will receive two grades from a double award. A student taking Combined Science 0653 receives a single grade. The content, the volume and the paper structure differ in each case.

The practical consequence is money. Parents of a co-ordinated or combined candidate frequently hire three separate science tutors, one per discipline, because that is the shape the subject appears to have. They then pay three times the rate to cover material that is not all on the paper, while the actual difficulty, which is the breadth of a single syllabus, goes unaddressed. Conversely, a triple-science candidate given one generalist science tutor usually gets thin coverage of all three and depth in none.

The second thing to establish is the practical component. Cambridge science entries include either a practical test or a written alternative to practical, and the two require quite different preparation. The alternative to practical is a written paper about experimental method, data and evaluation, and it can be prepared for thoroughly without a laboratory. A practical test cannot, and no honest tutor will claim otherwise. Laboratory time belongs to the school; what a tutor adds is the analysis, the evaluation and the writing.

The third is the tier. Core entries sit the lower-numbered papers and are graded C to G; Extended entries sit the higher-numbered papers and are graded A* to E. A student working towards a grade the entry does not permit is a specific, avoidable waste, and in science it is discovered more often than in any other subject because the papers feel similar from the outside. Ask which tier your child sits, on what evidence the decision was made, and what the school's internal cut-off is for changing it. All three answers cost nothing, and all three are a great deal easier to obtain in October than they are in April.

Everything here is delivered one-to-one online over live video on Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around the Jumeirah 3 school run. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India. For science in particular, the honest statement is that online tuition is where the written marks are won and the school laboratory is where the practical skills are built, and a good plan uses both rather than pretending one replaces the other.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-3.subjectsIntro: Science tutoring in Dubai is most effective when it targets named topics rather than whole subjects, because the topics that lose marks are remarkably consistent. These are the ones families ask about most, with the specific failure in each.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Series and parallel circuits, potential dividers, and calculations involving current, voltage and resistance. The reliable failure is treating a parallel branch as a series one, and losing every subsequent mark in a chain calculation. Drawing and labelling the circuit before calculating fixes most of it.

subjects.name: Physics: electromagnetism and induction
subjects.description: Motor effect, generators, transformers and the relationship between turns and voltage. Marks are lost on direction: which way the field points, which way the force acts. Students who have learned the rules as mnemonics without a diagram usually apply them inconsistently under pressure.

subjects.name: Physics: waves and optics
subjects.description: Refraction, total internal reflection, critical angle and wave calculations. Ray diagrams are a mark-scheme requirement with specific conventions, including arrows and construction lines, and a diagram that looks right but omits the conventions scores below one that is drawn properly.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The single largest source of lost chemistry marks in this market. Calculations involving masses, concentrations and gas volumes require a visible route from the equation to the answer, and students who jump to a number forfeit the method marks even when the number is right.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic chemistry
subjects.description: Homologous series, functional groups, addition and substitution, and polymers. Marks go on naming and on drawing structures to the convention the mark scheme expects, including showing all bonds where the question requires a displayed formula.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis and tests
subjects.description: The tests for cations, anions and gases, with their observations. These are learnable facts that students consistently decline to learn, then lose four or five easy marks on. A fortnight of drilled recall is among the highest-return science revision available.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and gas exchange
subjects.description: Circulatory and respiratory systems, transpiration, and the structure-function links the mark scheme rewards. Students describe a structure accurately and never connect it to a function, which is the difference between a describe mark and an explain mark.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares, dominant and recessive alleles, and the vocabulary of genotype, phenotype and heterozygosity. The usual loss is imprecise language: using the word gene where the answer requires allele, which a mark scheme will not accept.

subjects.name: Biology: enzymes and photosynthesis
subjects.description: Rate graphs, limiting factors and the effect of temperature and pH. These questions almost always ask for an explanation of a trend rather than a description of it, and the explanation requires naming the mechanism, not restating the shape of the curve.

subjects.name: Practical skills across all three sciences
subjects.levels: Practical test or alternative to practical
subjects.description: Identifying independent, dependent and control variables, tabulating results with units in the heading, plotting with sensible scales, drawing a line of best fit, evaluating sources of error and suggesting improvements. These are the most transferable marks in the whole science entry and the least practised.

sections.heading: Separate, co-ordinated or combined: find out before you buy anything
paragraphs: This is the first question and most families have never been asked it. Cambridge offers three routes through IGCSE science and they produce different numbers of grades from different volumes of content. Separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, are three independent subjects with three grades. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is one syllabus covering all three disciplines and awarding two grades. Combined Science 0653 is one syllabus awarding one grade.

The error that follows from not knowing is expensive in both directions. Parents of a 0654 candidate hire a biologist, a chemist and a physicist, pay three times the rate, and have each of them teach beyond the syllabus boundary because none of them is working from the co-ordinated specification. Parents of a triple-science candidate hire one general science tutor and get three shallow passes instead of one deep one. Both are common, and both are resolved by one email to the exams officer.

Pearson runs an equivalent set of routes with its own codes and its own question styles. A Pearson candidate practising Cambridge papers will meet differently constructed questions and a different balance of marks, which is not catastrophic but is a waste of preparation time that was available for something else.

The table sets the Cambridge routes against each other on the points that decide what tutoring should look like. Exact paper durations and mark totals are published on Cambridge's own syllabus pages and held by your school's exams officer, and should be read from there, because they are revised between series and a number copied from a web page is not evidence.

sections.heading: The practical component, answered honestly
paragraphs: Every Cambridge science entry carries a practical element, and it takes one of two forms: a practical test carried out in a laboratory, or a written alternative-to-practical paper about experimental work. Which one your child sits is decided by the school and appears on the entry. It is worth knowing because the two need completely different preparation and because several providers in this market are vague about what they can and cannot do.

The honest position is this. An alternative-to-practical paper is a written examination, and it can be prepared for completely without a laboratory. It asks candidates to identify variables, read a measuring instrument, complete a results table, plot and interpret a graph, draw a conclusion, identify sources of error and suggest improvements. Those are written skills, they follow mark-scheme conventions, and they are the most reliably recoverable marks in the entire science entry because almost nobody practises them.

A practical test is different. Manipulating apparatus, making an accurate measurement and working safely are built in a laboratory, and that laboratory is the school's. What online tutoring contributes to a practical test is the analysis and the writing: the plan, the table design, the graph conventions, the conclusion and the evaluation. Any provider claiming to replace laboratory hours over a video link is overstating what the format can do.

The practical skills table below is the one to work through with a marked script beside it. In our experience with Dubai candidates, the losses cluster in three places: units omitted from a table heading, a graph scale chosen so the points occupy a quarter of the grid, and an evaluation that lists what went wrong without proposing a specific improvement.

sections.heading: Command words, and how long an answer should be
paragraphs: More science marks are lost to command words than to content, and the fix takes about an hour to teach and a term to embed. Each command word in a Cambridge science paper obliges a specific kind of answer, and writing the wrong kind means the correct science scores nothing. A student who writes a beautiful description in answer to an explain question has not been careless; they have not been told what the word means.

The second half of the problem is length. The mark allocation tells a candidate how many distinct points are wanted, and students routinely write one point at great length for a three-mark question or three points in a single clause for a one-mark question. Teaching a student to count the marks and produce that many separate, scoreable statements recovers marks across every topic simultaneously, which is why it is the first thing we do rather than the last.

The third element is precision of vocabulary. In biology, gene and allele are not interchangeable and a mark scheme will not accept one for the other. In chemistry, an observation is not a conclusion. In physics, a force and a field are different things and the answer has to name the right one. These distinctions feel pedantic until a parent sees three or four marks lost to them on one paper.

The table below lists the command words that appear most often in Cambridge science papers alongside what the scheme expects in return. It is the kind of reference no competitor in this market publishes, and it is worth printing and keeping beside the desk for the rest of Year 11.

sections.heading: One tutor for three sciences, or three tutors?
paragraphs: This is the question that decides the bill, and the right answer depends entirely on the entry. For a co-ordinated or combined candidate, one tutor working from the single syllabus is both cheaper and better, because the useful work includes knowing what the specification excludes. For a triple-science candidate, the honest answer is usually one or two tutors rather than three, chosen for the disciplines actually losing marks.

The arithmetic is worth seeing. At the published Dubai band for a qualified online subject teacher, roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, one weekly hour across a term of twelve weeks is in the region of AED 1,800 to 3,600. Three weekly hours across the same term is three times that. Very few Year 11 students are genuinely weak in all three sciences at once; the usual pattern on a marked set of mocks is one subject well below the others and a shared weakness in command words and practical-paper technique.

That shared weakness is the argument for a different kind of booking. A command-word and practical-skills block, taught once, improves answers in all three sciences simultaneously, because the conventions are the same across biology, chemistry and physics. Six sessions on answer structure and the practical paper will often do more for a triple-science candidate's total than twelve sessions spread thinly across three content syllabuses.

The market figures behind that arithmetic are these, each from the provider's own published material rather than from us. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 at the budget online end. Unitors publishes online IGCSE rates from AED 150. TutorChase publishes AED 270. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table puts a subject specialist at AED 200 to 450 and upwards, in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors to AED 500, and BartyED publishes AED 650. Monthly packages of AED 799 for eight online sessions circulate widely in the emirate.

sections.heading: Where a marked science mock really goes wrong
paragraphs: Ask for the mock scripts rather than the mock grades and the pattern is usually visible within ten minutes. Across Dubai candidates the losses fall into four groups, and only one of them is a content gap. The first group is command-word failures: the right science written in the wrong form. The second is calculation presentation: a correct value with no working, no unit or an accuracy the question did not ask for. The third is the practical paper, often barely attempted because it was never practised.

The fourth group is genuine content, and it is usually narrower than parents fear. In physics it concentrates in electricity and electromagnetism. In chemistry it concentrates in moles and in the qualitative tests, the second of which is pure recall and therefore the cheapest fix available in the entire subject. In biology it concentrates in genetics vocabulary and in explaining rate graphs rather than describing them.

Working out which group dominates changes the purchase completely. A student losing twenty marks to command words and presentation needs six sessions on answer construction, not a term of content revision. A student losing twenty marks to electromagnetism needs the opposite. A student losing marks evenly across all four groups usually needs to sit two more timed papers before anybody decides anything, because one mock is a small sample.

This is also where honesty about timing matters. With two terms left all four groups can be addressed. With four weeks left, command words, calculation presentation and the practical paper are reachable and a broad content rebuild is not. Saying so is more useful than selling a plan that cannot be completed.

sections.heading: Fitting science sessions into a Jumeirah 3 week
paragraphs: School days along this stretch of coast end between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm, and the journey home adds twenty to fifty minutes depending on direction and traffic on Jumeirah Beach Road. From Jumeirah 3 the first weekday session that holds up across a term starts at about 5pm, and the 5pm to 6pm window is the most reliable. Slots at 7pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time are widely available and often better for a triple-science candidate who needs a longer, calmer session.

Science has a specific scheduling requirement that mathematics does not: the practical paper rewards working through a full data set, and that does not compress neatly into the last fifteen minutes of a session. Families who book a longer slot once a fortnight for practical-paper work, alongside a shorter weekly content session, tend to get more from the same total hours than those who book an identical hour every week.

The winter break is the best uninterrupted window in the Dubai school year for sitting timed science papers, and it is the point at which a triple-science candidate can realistically complete one full paper per subject and have them marked properly. Two or three papers sat across that fortnight produce a far better diagnosis than six squeezed into term time with help.

Ramadan shortens school hours and moves the usable window to the early afternoon or to after Iftar. Both work over live video and both are difficult for anyone driving in Dubai at those hours. Agreeing the month's slot a fortnight in advance, keeping the same tutor and the same weekday, is what keeps a practical-skills block intact rather than losing half of it.
