sections.heading: Coursework, lab reports and the boundary a tutor keeps
paragraphs: Where a science entry includes any internally assessed or submitted work, the boundary around tutoring support is the same as it is everywhere else in this market and worth stating before any session is booked. A tutor may teach the technique, explain what the marking criteria reward, model a method or a graph on a different data set, read a draft and say which criterion it is failing, and ask questions that make a student re-examine their own reasoning.

A tutor may not write up an experiment on the student's behalf, supply conclusions to be copied, choose the investigation, or process the data and hand over the results. No tutor on this platform produces a lab report, an Internal Assessment or any assessed science writing for a student. That is a genuine differentiator in a market where research found a provider selling completed Internal Assessments outright, and where the exposure of buying one falls entirely on the candidate.

The same applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge and Pearson, and we link to the boards' own pages rather than reproducing or distributing them. Your school's exams officer has access to more than is published publicly, and both routes cost nothing.

A parent can test any science session afterwards without knowing the subject. Ask your child to explain what they changed in an answer and why the mark scheme required it. A student who can describe the rule has been taught something portable. A student who can only point at the corrected text has been given an answer, and it will not be there in the examination hall.

sections.heading: Starting, with the three things that make the first session useful
paragraphs: Three items turn a general request for a science tutor near Jumeirah 3 into a brief that works from the first hour. The entry confirmation, showing the board, the route, the codes and the tier, and which practical component your child sits. The marked mock scripts for each science, with the marks visible. And a count of the teaching weeks genuinely left once the school breaks are removed.

With those in hand, use the free trial lesson for diagnosis rather than introduction. A productive first session produces a categorised list of where the marks went, a judgement about whether the problem is one discipline or a shared technique weakness, and an honest statement about what is reachable in the time available. If the trial produces reassurance instead, you have learned what you needed to know about that tutor.

Expect specificity about availability. Separate-science specialists at the exact tier and board are not free at every hour, and for a narrow request close to a paper date the honest answer is sometimes a different weekday or a short wait. We prefer saying that to putting a generalist into a chemistry booking where the whole value depends on knowing how the moles calculations are marked.

One last suggestion that costs nothing. Before buying anything, ask the school whether departmental revision sessions, past-paper clinics or practical catch-up time already exist. In many Dubai schools they do, they are free, and they cover exactly the practical-paper technique that is otherwise the first thing a parent pays for.

faqs.question: Is my child taking three separate sciences or a co-ordinated award?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer for the entry confirmation; it is the only reliable source. Cambridge separate sciences are Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, and they produce three grades. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a single syllabus awarding two grades, and Combined Science 0653 is a single syllabus awarding one. The distinction decides how many tutors a family needs, and parents of co-ordinated candidates commonly hire three when one is both cheaper and more effective, because the useful work includes knowing what the syllabus excludes.

faqs.question: Who covers the laboratory side if the tutoring happens over video?
faqs.answer: The practical element of a Cambridge science entry is either a laboratory practical test or a written alternative-to-practical paper, and which one your child sits is on the entry. Laboratory work belongs to the school and no video link substitutes for it; we say that plainly. The written paper, however, can be prepared for completely online, because it asks for variables, tables, graph plotting, conclusions, error sources and improvements, all of which follow written mark-scheme conventions and are rarely practised.

faqs.question: Does my child need three science tutors for a triple-science entry?
faqs.answer: Usually not. On a marked set of mocks the normal pattern is one science clearly below the others plus a weakness in command words and practical-paper technique that is shared across all three. Three weekly tutors at the published Dubai band of AED 150 to 300 an hour runs to roughly AED 5,400 to 10,800 over a twelve-week term. One discipline plus a six-session technique block is a fraction of that and frequently recovers more marks, because answer structure transfers across biology, chemistry and physics at once.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science topics do Dubai students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: In physics, electricity and circuits followed by electromagnetism, usually because a parallel branch was treated as a series one or a direction rule was applied without a diagram. In chemistry, moles and stoichiometry, where correct answers lose method marks for having no visible route, and the qualitative-analysis tests, which are pure recall and therefore the cheapest fix available. In biology, genetics vocabulary, where gene is written for allele, and rate graphs, where a trend is described rather than explained.

faqs.question: Why does my child write a full answer and still score one mark out of three?
faqs.answer: Almost always because of the command word or the mark allocation. Describe asks what happens; explain asks for the mechanism, and a description in answer to explain scores nothing however accurate it is. The mark allocation also tells a candidate how many separate scoreable points are wanted, and students routinely write one point at length for three marks. Counting the marks and producing that many distinct statements recovers marks across every topic simultaneously, which is why it is the first thing we teach rather than the last.

faqs.question: Which written skills carry the marks on the practical component?
faqs.answer: Written experimental skill. Candidates are asked to identify independent, dependent and controlled variables as measurable quantities, read values to the precision of a scale, complete a results table with quantity and unit in the heading, plot a graph with a sensible scale and a line of best fit, draw a conclusion in the terms of the question, identify specific sources of error and propose a specific improvement for each. Every one of those is a convention, and conventions are teachable in a handful of sessions without any apparatus.

faqs.question: Does Core or Extended limit the science grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Yes. A Core science entry sits the lower-numbered components and is graded C to G; an Extended entry sits the higher-numbered components and is graded A* to E. The tier is set at entry, usually a term or more before the papers, and the real deadline for changing it is the school's internal cut-off rather than the board's published date. If your child is working towards a grade the entry does not permit, that is a conversation with the school rather than something tutoring can resolve.

faqs.question: Can a combined science grade still lead to A Level or IB science?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but it narrows the options at most Dubai schools, and the decision needs taking before entries close rather than after results. Post-16 science courses publish grade conditions and some specify a separate-science background. If A Level or Higher Level Diploma science is the intention, ask the school directly what their own entry conditions are for a combined-award candidate and get the answer in writing, because it varies between schools in this emirate.

faqs.question: How many science sessions a week should a Year 11 candidate in Dubai have?
faqs.answer: One weekly hour on the weakest discipline, plus a short block on command words and the practical paper, covers most cases. That is around twelve to eighteen hours across a term, or roughly AED 2,700 to 5,400 at the published AED 150 to 300 band. Two weekly disciplines is sometimes justified. Three almost never is, and families who book three usually discover at the end of term that one subject accounted for most of the gap all along.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor visit our home in Jumeirah 3?
faqs.answer: Not through IB Gram. We deliver one-to-one tuition online over live video everywhere in the UAE, and we do not provide home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates; home visiting is a service we run only in India. Independent in-home tutors operate in the emirate and are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the figure. For science specifically the thing a home visit cannot supply either is a laboratory, which remains the school's.

faqs.question: What time can a science session start from Jumeirah 3 during term?
faqs.answer: Around 5pm is the first weekday start that holds up across a whole term, because school days here finish between roughly 2.30pm and 3.30pm and the run home adds twenty to fifty minutes. Slots at 7pm and 8pm Gulf Standard Time are widely available and often better for a triple-science candidate. Science also benefits from a longer fortnightly slot for practical-paper work with a full data set, which does not fit into the last quarter of an hour of a weekly session.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write up a science investigation or lab report?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the technique, explain what the criteria reward, model a method or a graph on different data, read a draft and name what it is failing, and ask questions that force the student to re-examine their reasoning. A tutor may not write up the experiment, supply conclusions to be copied, choose the investigation or process the data and hand over results. The work has to be the student's, and a parent can test it afterwards by asking their child to explain each change and the rule behind it.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE science papers and results fall for candidates in the UAE?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit the June and November series. Pearson's final November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, and June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge also runs June and November series and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so confirm your zone's timetable with the exams officer and plan against the live official version.

faqs.question: Is a tutor teaching science to a Dubai student required to hold a permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. Private tuition in the UAE requires a MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published, so treat specific figures quoted at you as unverified. This is a MoHRE permit, not a KHDA school licence.

faqs.question: What should we send before the free science trial lesson?
faqs.answer: The entry confirmation showing board, route, codes, tier and which practical component your child sits; the marked mock scripts for each science with the marks visible; and a count of the teaching weeks genuinely left after school breaks are removed. With those, a first session can produce a categorised list of lost marks and a judgement about whether this is a one-discipline problem or a shared technique problem. The trial is free, needs no card details and carries no obligation to continue.

intro.heading: "Science" is not a subject, and that is where the trouble starts
paragraphs: Parents in Jumeirah Golf Estates ring asking for a science tutor, and the first thing worth establishing is that no such qualification exists. Your child is sitting one of several genuinely different things. Three separate awards in Biology, Chemistry and Physics. Or Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, a double award covering all three disciplines at Extended depth in two grades. Or Cambridge Combined Science 0653, a single award. Or Pearson Double Award Science 4SD0, which is structured differently again. Each has its own papers, its own content list and its own practical route.

This matters because of who you then need. A triple-award student sitting 0610, 0620 and 0625 has three subjects and, properly, needs a biologist for one, a chemist for another and a physicist for the third. A coordinated-science student has one timetabled subject covering all three disciplines, which is a different and in some ways harder teaching problem, because the content is broad and shallow and the examination skips between disciplines inside a single paper.

The honest answer to whether anyone near Jumeirah Golf Estates can do this is: it depends which part. A capable general science tutor exists within a short drive and can help a Year 9 student or a Core-tier candidate. Somebody who knows that 0654 is assessed differently from three separate awards, who can mark an alternative-to-practical question against the scheme, and who teaches Extended-tier physics electricity properly — that person is scarce, and the pool inside one gated community is close to empty.

So this page does the work a parent would otherwise do over six phone calls. It identifies the codes and what each one means, explains the two practical routes and what each actually tests, sets out the Core and Extended ceiling in the sciences specifically, names where marks go in each discipline, and prices the market with attribution. Then it says what to ask a prospective tutor to find out in two minutes whether they know the difference.

There is one more structural fact worth having in mind, because it governs how much you should buy. A triple-award student has the fullest timetable in the school, and in this community they also have one of the longest afternoons. Three weekly science slots on top of that leaves no evening for the unaided practice that actually consolidates anything, which makes it both the most expensive and the least effective arrangement available. One discipline at a time, finished before the next begins, fits a Jumeirah Golf Estates week and produces more.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-go.subjectsIntro: The sciences fail in discipline-specific ways, and knowing which discipline is costing the marks is more useful than knowing the overall grade. These are the areas Jumeirah Golf Estates families ask about most.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The single largest source of lost marks across all science routes. Series and parallel reasoning holds up on a familiar diagram and collapses on an unfamiliar one, and formula rearrangement fails under time pressure. Three or four sessions usually produces a visible change.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and energy
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws and energy transfers. Marks are lost by writing numbers without naming the energy stores involved, which is what the mark scheme asks for, and by treating velocity as a number rather than a vector.

subjects.name: Physics: waves and radioactivity
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum, half-life and decay equations. Content-dense and self-contained, so it is efficient to tutor: two or three sessions and it is usually secure for the paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Carries weight far beyond its apparent size and is routinely rushed. A student who cannot read an equation as a ratio loses marks in energetics, electrolysis and titration questions as well. The highest-value chemistry block available.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis and ion tests
subjects.description: Pure recall marks for the tests and observations for cations, anions and gases, and students leave them blank with remarkable consistency. One session, learned properly, is worth several marks on the practical route paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and bonding
subjects.description: Functional groups, homologous series, ionic and covalent bonding and structure. The common failure is vocabulary: answers about bond strength where the question asks about intermolecular forces, which forfeits the mark entirely.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: The quantitative end of biology and where marks are most often lost on precision of language. An osmosis answer that never says partially permeable membrane, or an enzyme answer that says the enzyme died, scores poorly despite understanding.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid crosses, Punnett squares, variation and selection. Highly teachable because the question shapes are predictable, and students lose marks by omitting the genotype key or the gamete row rather than by misunderstanding the biology.

subjects.name: Practical skills and the practical paper
subjects.levels: All routes, by either practical test or alternative-to-practical
subjects.description: Planning, variable control, reading instruments, tabulating and drawing conclusions. Taught unevenly and assessed in its own right, which makes two or three dedicated sessions one of the better returns across every science route.

subjects.name: Mathematical fluency for science
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, unit conversion, percentage change and reading graphs. Not a syllabus topic and frequently the actual problem. A marked paper shows it immediately: the science is understood and the arithmetic fails.

sections.heading: Which science is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: Start here, because everything else depends on it and most families cannot answer it on the first call. Look on the last school report or the examination entry confirmation for a syllabus code. With Cambridge it is four digits: 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry, 0625 Physics for three separate awards, 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences for the double award, 0653 Combined Science for the single. With Pearson the codes read differently: 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the separate sciences and 4SD0 for Double Award Science.

The difference is not administrative. A triple-award student has three subjects, three sets of papers and three grades. A coordinated double-award student has one timetabled subject assessed across all three disciplines in shared papers, worth two grades, with content that is broader and shallower. A single-award student has one grade and less content again. Past-paper material does not transfer between these routes, so a tutor working from the wrong set is testing your child on content they will never be asked.

There is a second question underneath it: Core or Extended, Foundation or Higher. In the sciences as elsewhere, a Core or Foundation entry caps the available grade at 5. For a student intending IB Diploma Higher Level sciences or science A Levels, that ceiling is decisive, and the entry is set by the school in Year 10 on Year 10 evidence.

If no code appears anywhere in the paperwork, one email to the head of year settles it. It is the single most valuable two minutes a Jumeirah Golf Estates parent can spend before buying any science tuition, and the answer determines the tutor, the papers and the realistic session count.

sections.heading: The practical paper, decoded
paragraphs: Almost every science route assesses practical skills, and almost no parent knows which way their child's school does it. There are two models. A practical test is sat in a laboratory with apparatus, under examination conditions. An alternative-to-practical paper is a written paper that assesses the same skills on paper: reading a scale from a diagram, spotting the flaw in a described method, completing a results table, plotting and drawing a conclusion. Which one applies depends on the school's entry, and it changes what revision should contain.

The important point is that the skills assessed are the same either way, and they are taught unevenly. Tabulation conventions carry marks: column headings with units, consistent decimal places, dependent variable on the correct axis. Variable control carries marks, and it has to be phrased as the scheme wants — naming what was held constant, not asserting that the experiment was fair. Conclusions carry marks for referring to the data rather than to expectation.

In chemistry there is an additional, purely recallable component on some routes: the qualitative analysis tests. Cation, anion and gas tests with their observations are a finite list, and students leave those marks blank with striking regularity. One session of memorisation work and they are secure, which is as close to free marks as this qualification offers.

For a Jumeirah Golf Estates student, two or three sessions on the practical route is one of the better returns available in science, and it is nearly always underbought because it does not feel like real content. Ask the school which route your child is entered for, then ask any prospective tutor what they would drill differently for each. A specialist answers in a sentence.

sections.heading: Where each science loses its marks
paragraphs: Physics first, because it is the discipline that most often decides a science grade. Electricity is the problem area: series and parallel reasoning that works on a textbook circuit collapses on an unfamiliar diagram, and formula rearrangement fails under time pressure. Alongside that sit vector errors — velocity and force treated as plain numbers — and energy answers that give figures without naming the energy stores involved, which is exactly what the mark scheme asks for.

Chemistry loses marks in two places. The first is quantitative: mole calculations rushed, equations read as sentences rather than ratios, and unit or significant-figure slips carried through multi-step answers. The second is vocabulary: explanations given in terms of bond strength where the question is about intermolecular forces, or in terms of temperature where particle behaviour was wanted. Both patterns are visible on a marked paper in minutes.

Biology loses marks almost entirely on precision of language rather than on understanding. An osmosis answer that omits partially permeable membrane, an enzyme answer that says the enzyme died rather than denatured, a transport answer that describes diffusion without naming the concentration gradient. Students who clearly understand the biology score below their ability for want of four or five phrases used exactly.

Across all three disciplines there is a common fifth failure: command terms. Describe, explain, suggest and compare carry different mark allocations and ask for different things, and students answer the one they prefer. All of this is why we ask for one marked paper before quoting anything. The script names the pattern, and the pattern names the session count.

sections.heading: The tier ceiling in the sciences
paragraphs: The Core and Extended decision matters more in the sciences than in most subjects, because science is where post-16 plans most often depend on a specific grade. A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5, and a Pearson Foundation entry does the same. A student aiming at IB Diploma Higher Level Chemistry or at science A Levels generally needs more than that, and no quantity of tuition lifts a ceiling.

On a coordinated double award the tier decision applies to the whole subject, which means it covers all three disciplines at once. That is worth noticing: a student who is strong in biology and weak in physics may be placed on Core because of physics, with the biology grade capped as collateral. Where that is the situation, a single-discipline physics block early in Year 11 is the intervention that might change the entry, and it is a much smaller spend than a year of general support.

Schools make these decisions for defensible reasons. A borderline candidate entered for Extended can score below the lowest Extended grade and come away with nothing, where Core would have produced a secure 4 or 5. That is a genuine risk. But the placement is made on Year 10 evidence, and a student whose work changes materially in the first term of Year 11 can sometimes be moved — if a parent asks.

Where the tier cannot change and the post-16 plan requires more, the honest options are to revise the plan or to enter the November series on the higher tier, potentially as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre. Both are legitimate. Paying for thirty sessions against a ceiling is not, and we will say so before taking the booking.

sections.heading: One tutor for three sciences, or three tutors?
paragraphs: This is the practical question for triple-award families and the answer depends on the tier. At Core level, a strong general science tutor can reasonably cover all three disciplines, because the content depth is manageable and the common failures are mathematical and linguistic rather than discipline-specific. That is a legitimate and cheaper arrangement and we will say so when it applies.

At Extended level it stops being true. Extended-tier physics electricity, chemistry mole calculations with electrolysis, and biology genetics are three different teaching problems with three different mark-scheme vocabularies, and somebody adequate at all three is rarely good at any. A tutor covering three Extended sciences for the same student is usually covering one well and two approximately.

The efficient compromise is almost always to buy one discipline at a time. A marked paper in each science shows where the grade is actually being lost, which is usually one discipline rather than three, and a four to six session block with a specialist in that one is a far smaller purchase than a weekly slot covering everything. When it is done, look again; often nothing further is needed.

For coordinated double-award students the same logic applies more strongly, because one weak discipline pulls two grades down at once. Targeting it is both the cheapest and the most visible intervention available in this qualification, and it is rarely what gets sold.

A reasonable test of a prospective tutor, then, is to ask which discipline they would start with for your child and why. An answer drawn from the marked papers is the right one. An offer to cover all three weekly, at Extended tier, from the beginning of the syllabus, is the answer that costs the most and delivers the least.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs around Jumeirah Golf Estates
paragraphs: Rates in this market are set by format and tutor category rather than by discipline, so each science costs roughly what any specialist subject costs. Published Dubai rates for a qualified subject tutor working online run about AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. Specialist IGCSE, IB and A-Level provision is quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, one UK-based agency at AED 270, and premium named or examiner-led provision as high as AED 650. Budget online tuition is advertised from AED 45 to AED 150, with one platform listing from AED 33 to AED 52 and another from AED 45 to AED 65.

Where science differs from other subjects is the multiplication risk. A triple-award family that buys a weekly slot in each discipline is committing to three simultaneous arrangements, which at a mid-band rate is in the region of AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month and leaves the student no time for unaided practice. That is the most expensive mistake available in this qualification, and it is also the least effective, because practice between sessions is the mechanism that works.

The block structure is what keeps it sane. Four to six sessions in one discipline is roughly AED 800 to AED 1,200 at a mid-band rate. A practical-paper block of two or three sessions is AED 400 to AED 600. One qualitative-analysis session is a couple of hundred dirhams and is worth several marks. A June-series rotation across three sciences for eight weeks is a larger but finite commitment with a clear stop date.

In-home visits in Dubai are advertised at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour including travel, with one provider publishing AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions against AED 799 for eight online sessions. Every figure here was read from the provider's own published page in October 2026 and describes the market, not IB Gram, whose fee follows the free trial lesson.

sections.heading: Scheduling three sciences in a Jumeirah Golf Estates week
paragraphs: Triple-award students have the fullest timetables in Year 11, and in this community they also have the longest afternoons. Campus finish runs from about 2.45pm to 3.30pm, the gate queue costs ten to twenty minutes, the drive is twelve to thirty-five minutes depending on whether the school sits in JVT or out towards Arabian Ranches, and clubs in Dubai Sports City take a good proportion of children out again until after six.

What follows is a planning rule rather than a preference: do not try to run three weekly science slots. A student with three tuition sessions, a full timetable and training has no evening left for the unaided practice that actually consolidates anything. One block at a time, finished before the next begins, fits the week and produces more.

In the final eight weeks before the June series, rotate instead. One discipline a week, a whole timed paper, and a marking session on it — which gives each science a proper hearing every three weeks and keeps the total commitment at one session a week. Online delivery is what makes that rotation practical, since no travel has to be rearranged each time the discipline changes.

Weekend mornings are the most underused slot in this community and the right one for whole papers and practical-route work, both of which need an uninterrupted ninety minutes that a weekday evening here rarely provides. Sessions can also shift post-Iftar during Ramadan and pause through mock weeks, and a stop date agreed at the start keeps the arrangement from running on unreviewed.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor science in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category is worth knowing when comparing the AED 45 to AED 150 band to a specialist rate: the low figure is usually a legitimate tutor in a different category, not an unlicensed one. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted.

One boundary applies with particular force in the sciences, where the qualified teacher pool at any school is small. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being relied on as exact wording. Either way, do not engage your child's own science teacher privately.

And what nobody holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA. IB Gram holds no such permit, has no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. We also do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes; tutors reference and link to the official source.

faqs.question: What does my child's IGCSE science code actually mean?
faqs.answer: It tells you which qualification they are sitting, and the differences are substantial. Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 are three separate awards in Biology, Chemistry and Physics producing three grades. Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences is one timetabled subject covering all three disciplines and worth two grades. Cambridge 0653 Combined Science is a single award. Pearson uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the separate sciences and 4SD0 for Double Award Science. Past-paper material does not transfer between these routes, which is why the code matters more than the subject name.

faqs.question: Is triple science or coordinated science better for my child?
faqs.answer: It depends on the post-16 plan and on capacity. Three separate sciences give the greatest depth and are the most useful preparation for IB Diploma Higher Level sciences or science A Levels, at three times the content. Coordinated double award 0654 is broader and shallower, produces two grades, and is widely accepted. The question to ask is specific: contact the sixth form or IB coordinator your child is likely to go to and ask what they expect for Higher Level sciences. Do not assume either way from what friends have chosen.

faqs.question: Does my child sit a practical exam or a written practical paper?
faqs.answer: One of the two, and the school decides which. A practical test is sat in a laboratory with apparatus under examination conditions. An alternative-to-practical paper assesses the same skills in writing: reading a scale from a diagram, identifying a flaw in a described method, completing a results table, plotting and concluding. Ask the school which route your child is entered for, because it changes what two or three of the most cost-effective revision sessions should contain. The skills assessed are the same either way and are taught unevenly.

faqs.question: Which science topic costs Jumeirah Golf Estates students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Physics electricity, consistently and across every route. Series and parallel reasoning that works on a textbook circuit collapses on an unfamiliar diagram, and formula rearrangement fails under time pressure. On a coordinated double award this is particularly costly, because one weak discipline pulls two grades down at once. Three or four sessions with a physicist on unfamiliar circuits and rearrangement usually produces a visible change at the next assessment, which makes it the best-value single block in the qualification.

faqs.question: Should one tutor cover all three sciences?
faqs.answer: At Core tier, often yes, and we will say so when it applies: the content depth is manageable and the common failures are mathematical and linguistic rather than discipline-specific. At Extended tier, no. Electricity, mole calculations with electrolysis, and genetics are three different teaching problems with three different mark-scheme vocabularies, and somebody adequate at all three is rarely strong in any. The efficient approach is one discipline at a time, chosen from marked papers, which usually turns out to be one rather than three.

faqs.question: My child is on Core science but wants Higher Level chemistry in the IB. Is that possible?
faqs.answer: It depends on the tier, and the tier is the problem. A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum grade at 5, and most Higher Level science routes expect more. Three honest options: ask the school about a tier review early in Year 11, which a short diagnostic block can inform; enter the November series on the higher tier, potentially as a private candidate through an approved Dubai centre; or discuss Standard Level with the IB coordinator. What does not work is buying sessions against a ceiling that cannot move.

faqs.question: How many science sessions can a Year 11 student actually absorb?
faqs.answer: One a week, almost always, and never three. A triple-award student has the fullest timetable in the school, and in this community they also have one of the longest afternoons: campus finish to 3.30pm, gate queue, drive, then often training in Dubai Sports City. Three tuition slots on top of that leaves no evening for the unaided practice that consolidates anything. One block at a time, finished before the next begins, fits the week and produces more for considerably less money.

faqs.question: What is the cheapest useful science session we could buy?
faqs.answer: Probably one session on chemistry qualitative analysis, where that is part of your child's code. The cation, anion and gas tests with their observations are a finite, memorisable list carrying real marks, and students leave them blank with striking regularity. One session of structured memorisation work secures them. After that, a two or three session practical-paper block on tabulation conventions, variable control phrasing and writing conclusions from data is the next best return, and both are usually underbought.

faqs.question: Why does my child understand biology and still score poorly?
faqs.answer: Because biology marks turn on precision of language far more than on understanding. An osmosis answer that omits partially permeable membrane loses the mark. An enzyme answer that says the enzyme died rather than denatured loses the mark. A transport answer that describes diffusion without naming the concentration gradient loses the mark. A student who clearly grasps the biology can score a grade or two below their ability for want of four or five phrases used exactly, and that is fixable in a short block rather than a term.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE science tutor cost in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Rates are set by format rather than discipline, so each science costs about what any specialist subject does: AED 150 to AED 300 an hour for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for specialist provision, and up to AED 650 for premium examiner-led work. In blocks: four to six sessions in one discipline is roughly AED 800 to AED 1,200, and a practical-paper block is AED 400 to AED 600. Market rates researched October 2026, not IB Gram's prices, which follow the free trial.

faqs.question: Can my child take different sciences with different exam boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in Dubai it is common, because schools choose per department. A student can be a Cambridge biologist and a Pearson physicist in the same Year 11. It is not a problem in itself, but it has a practical consequence: the past-paper material, the tier names and in some cases the practical route differ between them, so one tutor covering both is managing two sets of conventions. This is another reason to establish every code before any tuition starts rather than afterwards.

faqs.question: With eight weeks left before June, what should science tuition even attempt?
faqs.answer: Not too late to be useful, but the plan should change. Eight weeks is enough to secure recallable marks — qualitative analysis, half-life calculations, genetics question shapes — and to fix technique: command terms, tabulation, conclusions written from data. It is not enough to teach two missing topics and polish technique simultaneously, and a provider promising both is selling optimism. The honest plan secures what is reachable, and treats the November series as the second attempt if the target grade needs one.

faqs.question: Is there a science specialist close to Jumeirah Golf Estates?
faqs.answer: It depends which part. A capable general science tutor who can help a Year 9 student or a Core-tier candidate does exist within a short drive. Somebody who knows that 0654 is assessed differently from three separate awards, can mark an alternative-to-practical question against the scheme, and teaches Extended-tier electricity properly is scarce, and the pool inside one villa community of a few thousand households is close to empty. That is why we match online by code and discipline rather than by distance.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor need a UAE permit to teach online?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE requires a private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE, granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it and under which category. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no amounts are published.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-is.tutorsIntro: These tutors cover Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE biology, chemistry and physics, plus combined and coordinated science, for families around Jumeirah Islands. Each is briefed on the exact award, code and tier your child is entered for.

intro.heading: Nobody can teach a science entry they have not identified
paragraphs: There is no single IGCSE science qualification, and that is where most wasted spending in this market begins. Your child may be entered for three separate sciences with three syllabus codes and three sets of papers, or for a coordinated double award, or for a combined single award covering all three with reduced content. The tutor's job changes completely between those.

Then the board. Cambridge IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics are 0610, 0620 and 0625; the Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Content overlaps heavily and assessment does not, and past papers are not interchangeable. A tutor working from the wrong set teaches competently and moves nothing, which parents typically discover after a term.

Then the tier, where a science subject is tiered. Core and Extended in Cambridge, Foundation and Higher in some Pearson subjects. The tier does more than cap a grade: it removes content, and the removed content is disproportionately what post-16 science courses assume a student has met. Teaching the wrong tier wastes the hour in one direction or leaves the student under-prepared in the other.

Then the practical route, which almost nobody asks about until it is late. Some candidates sit a practical examination in a laboratory; others sit a written alternative-to-practical paper testing the same skills on paper. Both assess method writing, variables, instrument precision, tabulation, graphing and criticising a method, and the preparation differs between them more than the shared skill list suggests.

And then the question only a parent can answer: which of the three sciences is actually failing? Families say science. Marked papers usually say that one subject is secure, one has a content gap and one has a technique problem. Those are three different jobs, needing different responses over different numbers of weeks, and an hour split across all three completes none of them and marks no paper in any of them.

Two further facts belong in the first conversation. The series: UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November, Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November, and the February/March Cambridge series is offered to India only. And the timetable: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version, and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong one. The school holds the version that applies.

IB Gram matches a tutor briefed on that exact entry and teaches live online, one to one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service, and with no school or tuition centre inside the Jumeirah Islands gates, online removes a journey from the day rather than adding one.

programmes.description: Biology, chemistry and physics as three qualifications, each with its own papers and practical assessment route. The standard route towards A Level sciences or the Diploma's Higher Level sciences, and the heavier of the two options in workload terms.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-is.subjectsIntro: What a specialist should be able to say about each area, and the question that tests it. These are the answers to listen for rather than a list of topics.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: A specialist names this as the topic usually rebuilt rather than revised, because students learn the relationships without a model of what a circuit does. They will say it takes about three sessions and that the work runs from the physical situation towards the calculation rather than the reverse.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, moments and motion
subjects.description: A specialist says moments questions reward drawing the situation and marking distances from the pivot, and that students working from the formula alone fail anything non-standard. Motion graph interpretation is the other recurring loss and responds to practice rather than teaching.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: A specialist identifies reliability rather than comprehension as the problem and prescribes one fixed layout with units at every step. They will say two or three sessions, and that the same discipline then carries into energetics and any calculation-heavy question.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis and separation
subjects.description: A specialist calls these the fastest marks in the whole science programme, because the tests and observations are finite and students drop them only through never having been drilled systematically. One or two sessions, and measurable immediately.

subjects.name: Chemistry: bonding and structure
subjects.description: A specialist says explanation marks are lost when a student states a property without connecting it to the bonding that causes it, which is what the question is asking for. It is answer construction against real mark schemes rather than more content.

subjects.name: Biology: precision of written answers
subjects.description: A specialist names this before content, every time, and can give the example: the scheme wants a named variable and a direction where students write that something improved. Examiner reports repeat it each series, and it takes three or four sessions to shift.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: A specialist points at osmosis and water potential language as the place precision matters most, and notes that students who learn the processes as narratives rather than mechanisms lose the explanation marks while appearing to know the topic.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: A specialist says genetic diagrams score only when laid out fully with gametes shown, and that partial diagrams score partially. A one-session procedural fix, and a reliable source of recovered marks that no amount of general revision would find.

subjects.name: Practical skills across all three
subjects.description: A specialist asks which practical route applies before planning anything, then describes the same list for either: repeatable method, variables, instrument precision, tabulation with units in headings, sensible scales, line of best fit, and criticising a method rather than reporting success.

subjects.name: Command terms and exam conduct
subjects.description: A specialist distinguishes state, describe, explain, suggest and compare as different answer shapes, and adds showing working, time management and answering the question asked. They will call these the cheapest marks in science, and they are rarely taught because they look too obvious.

sections.heading: Seven facts to get from the exams officer
paragraphs: This is one email and it is the most valuable thing you can do before spending anything. Without these, a tutor can only teach science in general, which is rarely the problem. With them, the work becomes specific enough to plan and to evaluate.

One: the award. Three separate sciences, a coordinated double award, or a combined single award. Two: the syllabus code per science, because departments within one school sometimes use different boards. Three: the tier per science, where the subject is tiered. Four: the practical assessment route, laboratory or written alternative.

Five: the series your child is entered for, which for a UAE Cambridge candidate is June or November, and for Pearson May/June or November. Six: any internal coursework or controlled-assessment deadlines, which the school sets and which arrive without warning. Seven: the zone-specific timetable, which the school holds and which Cambridge says must be the correct version for the centre's zone.

A tutor given all seven can tell you in the first session which past papers apply, what depth to teach, how the practical will be examined and when the work has to be done by. A tutor given only the year group and the word science is going to guess, and the guess will usually be the course they know best rather than the one your child sits.
The table sets out each fact with what it changes and the cost of not asking. None of these questions is unusual and an exams officer answers all seven in a single reply.

sections.heading: How to test a science tutor without being a scientist
paragraphs: You do not need subject knowledge for this. The test is whether a tutor asks the right questions and names specific failures rather than general ones, and both are audible in ten minutes. Run it in the trial session, before price comes up.

The opening signal is what they ask you for. A specialist wants the award, the codes, the tiers, the practical route and a marked paper per science. A general tutor asks for the year group and the topic list. That difference tells you what the next term would look like before any teaching has happened.

The second signal is how they talk about biology. If a tutor says biology needs more revision, they have not taught it recently. If they say biology marks are lost to precision of language, and give the example of a named variable and a direction where the student wrote that something improved, they have read mark schemes.

The third is whether they ask about the practical route before planning anything. A written alternative-to-practical paper is not theory, and a student who has never been required to criticise a method on paper performs badly on it whatever their content knowledge. A tutor who does not raise this has not prepared candidates for it.

The fourth is the three-sciences question. Ask whether you should tutor all three. A specialist says no, explains that marked papers usually show three different problems, and recommends one subject done properly plus a transferable practical or command-term block. A tutor who agrees to cover three sciences in one hour is selling convenience rather than teaching.

sections.heading: What the tier takes away in science specifically
paragraphs: A parent cannot judge a tutor's claim to know the tier without knowing roughly what the tier contains, so here is the shape of it. The higher tier in a tiered science is not the lower tier with harder questions; it includes material the lower tier never teaches, and that material is disproportionately what post-16 science courses assume.

In physics the higher tier extends the quantitative treatment and adds topics that A Level and Diploma physics build on directly. In chemistry it adds the mole and stoichiometric work that decides most of the grade, along with more demanding bonding and organic content. In biology it adds detail and quantitative handling across several topics rather than whole new areas.

The practical consequence runs in two directions and both are expensive. A lower-tier candidate taught higher-tier content has their hour wasted and their confidence knocked. A higher-tier candidate whose tutor works at the lower tier arrives at the paper under-prepared on exactly the content that separates the grades.

It matters for the tier decision itself as well. If your child needs a science for sixth form and is near the boundary, the argument for the higher tier is made in Year 10 with marked evidence aimed specifically at the separating content, followed by strong marks on the school's own assessments. A request without evidence does not move a head of department.

Specifications are revised and the school holds the version your child is actually sitting, so treat any list as a prompt to confirm rather than as the specification. The table sets out what the tier changes and what follows at sixteen.

sections.heading: The practical route, and why it is asked too late
paragraphs: Every IGCSE science assesses practical skills, and how yours are assessed depends on the entry your school has made rather than on the subject. Some candidates sit a practical examination in a laboratory. Others sit a written alternative-to-practical paper testing the same skills on paper. A tutor who does not establish which applies prepares your child for the wrong thing.

Both routes test the same competences: writing a method precise enough for someone else to repeat exactly, identifying the variable changed and the ones that must be controlled, reading an instrument to an appropriate precision, tabulating with units in the headings, plotting with a sensible scale, drawing a line of best fit, and criticising a method rather than reporting that it worked.

The trap in the written route is that students revise it as theory because it is a written paper. It is not theory. It asks about apparatus, precision, anomalous results and improvements, and a student who has never been required to criticise a method on paper performs poorly on it however well they know the content of the subject.

This is also the best-value block available in science tutoring, because the skills transfer. Four to six sessions earn marks in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously, and again in whichever practical route applies. Almost no family buys it, because on an invoice it does not look like a subject.

Online delivery suits the work well: the method is written, the table drawn, the graph plotted and then criticised, all on a shared screen. The hands-on laboratory work stays at school with the school's apparatus, where it belongs and where it would be in any case.

sections.heading: Which of the three sciences is really the problem
paragraphs: Parents say science. Marked papers say something narrower, and collecting three of them costs nothing. In most households one science is secure, one is weak for a content reason and one is weak for a technique reason, and those are three different jobs needing three different responses over different timescales.

The pattern we see from this part of Dubai is consistent: physics weak on electricity and moments, chemistry weak on mole reliability, biology weak on the precision of written answers. Electricity needs a conceptual rebuild over about three sessions. Mole work needs one layout drilled in two or three. Biology needs answer construction against real mark schemes over three or four.

The temptation is to buy one weekly hour and ask the tutor to cover all three. That produces twenty minutes each, no completed piece of work, no marked past paper and no measurable change. Parents defend it on grounds of fairness between subjects, which is understandable and is not a teaching principle.

The better approach is to pick one science for a term, usually the one that most affects sixth-form options or has the clearest fixable problem, and add a transferable block on practical skills or command terms. In many households the second science then needs no tutoring, because the technique work carries across.

In a community where every child travels out to school and arrives home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50, the week is a scarcer resource than the money. Three tutoring sessions on top of three sciences' homework collapses by about week six, usually with the homework stopping first.

sections.heading: Boards, series and the zone timetable
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson examine the sciences differently even where the content is similar, which is why the code decides the past papers. Cambridge IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics are 0610, 0620 and 0625. The Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Confirm current codes with your exams officer, since specifications are revised.

On series the rule for a UAE family is simple and frequently misstated. Cambridge candidates here sit the June and November series, with Checkpoint tests at lower secondary in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

The zone system has no UK equivalent and matters because it decides the dates your child sits. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

The November series is the resit route, and its cost is in timing. The Pearson precedent: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026.

So a November resit means a sixth-form application season carried out with a provisional grade. Where a June grade sits just below a boundary, the alternative is an enquiry about results, submitted by the school within a short window after results for a fee set by the board. Plan from the live official timetable the school holds rather than from any tutoring page.

sections.heading: What we can honestly staff
paragraphs: Biology, chemistry and physics at either tier are well covered and usually matched within the same week, including combined and coordinated award candidates once we know which award applies. That is the honest position, and no competitor in this market publishes a coverage limit at all.

The scarce resource is the hour rather than the subject. Weekday slots between 17:00 and 19:00 in the spring term are what every Year 11 household in Dubai wants, and they fill from September onwards. A family booking in the autumn holds the slot all year; a family asking in February chooses from what remains at the same hourly figure.

From these gates the arrival pattern narrows it further. With no school inside Jumeirah Islands, every child travels out and comes home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50, which makes 17:00 the dependable start and 17:30 safer for a child returning from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. A 16:30 slot is nominally available and loses its first twenty minutes.

For the mandatory UAE subjects we are candid about the constraints. Support means working with the school's own material, because KHDA prohibits the use of different or additional content for those subjects without prior Ministry of Education permission, and schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them.

Where a tutor covering a UAE family is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book. Two ranking competitors in this market route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning it, which is the same fact handled badly.

sections.heading: Rates, mandatory subjects and what we do not claim
paragraphs: The published Dubai rates are better read as a staffing ladder than as a price list. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65 an hour, which buys availability and not much else. A qualified subject tutor online is quoted at AED 150-300, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150, and that is the first band at which somebody has actually read the specification your child is entered against. Specialist work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270, and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650. In-home visits are the band this district distorts: they run AED 180-350, with independent home tutors at AED 200-500, and across a villa community spread this thinly a real share of that upper figure is paying for the drive in and out rather than for a Physics specialist.

The specific trap in science is multiplication: pricing three weekly hours produces a monthly figure no household sustains for three terms, and the arrangement then stops in week six. Bestimate's monthly estimates are AED 240-600 budget, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, per subject. One science done properly is better value than three started.

Two UAE facts shape the week around any science timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, with KHDA calculating instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requiring separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them.

And on equivalency: the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3 on the British track, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or better or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five, which changes the arithmetic for a student taking ten subjects.

We do not perform or guarantee equivalency, publish no ratings, distribute no past papers, and write no coursework.

faqs.question: What exactly should we ask our school before hiring a science tutor?
faqs.answer: Seven things in one email: the award, meaning three separate sciences or a coordinated or combined one; the syllabus code for each science, because departments sometimes differ; the tier for each; whether the practical is assessed in a laboratory or on a written alternative paper; the series your child is entered for; any internal coursework deadlines; and confirmation of the zone-specific Cambridge timetable the school holds. An exams officer answers all seven in a single reply, and every later decision rests on them.

faqs.question: How can we judge a science tutor if we are not scientists ourselves?
faqs.answer: Listen for four things. What they ask you for: a specialist wants the award, codes, tiers, practical route and marked papers, while a general tutor wants the year group and topic list. How they describe biology: precision of language with a concrete example, not a need for more revision. Whether they raise the practical route before planning. And what they say about tutoring all three sciences, where the right answer is no, with a reason.

faqs.question: Our child does combined science. Does that limit A Level options?
faqs.answer: Often, and the decision sits with the receiving school rather than the board. A coordinated double award is accepted by some sixth forms for a science at A Level and not by others, and a combined single award more frequently is not. That is a Year 10 question to ask in writing, not a post-results discovery. If a separate entry is still possible and your child is capable of it, ask whether the school can accommodate it.

faqs.question: Do your science tutors come into the community?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. Science tuition for families inside these gates is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers and graph work on a shared screen. The hands-on practical work stays at school with the school's apparatus in any case. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences should we spend the hour on?
faqs.answer: Collect one marked paper per science and decide from those rather than from a feeling. Most households find one subject is secure, one has a content gap and one has a technique problem. Pick the science that most affects sixth-form options or has the clearest fixable problem, usually physics if electricity is the issue, and add a practical skills or command-term block that pays into all three. The second science often then needs nothing.

faqs.question: Why does our child lose marks in biology despite knowing the content?
faqs.answer: Because biology is marked on precision of language. The scheme wants a named variable and a direction; students write that something improved or the rate increased. Examiner reports make this point every series and nobody teaches it explicitly. State, describe, explain and suggest each demand a different answer shape. The work is answer construction against real mark schemes over three or four sessions, and it usually shows up immediately on the next timed paper.

faqs.question: Is the written practical paper just theory with a different name?
faqs.answer: No, and treating it that way is the commonest preparation error in IGCSE science. The alternative-to-practical paper asks about apparatus, precision, anomalous results and improvements, and it requires a student to criticise a method on paper rather than recall content. A student who has never been made to do that performs badly on it whatever they know. Ask your exams officer which route applies, then make sure the tutor prepares for that route specifically.

faqs.question: How long does the electricity problem in physics take to fix?
faqs.answer: About three sessions, and it is usually the best use of early time if physics is the weak subject. Students learn the relationships without a mental model of what the circuit is doing, so anything non-standard defeats them and revision does not touch it, because the gap is conceptual rather than factual. The work runs from the physical situation towards the calculation rather than the reverse. Moments in physics and mole reliability in chemistry are the next two candidates.

faqs.question: Can we really not tutor all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: You can buy it and we will advise against it, for two reasons. An hour split three ways produces twenty minutes each, no completed work and no marked paper, so nobody can say whether it worked. And in a community where every child travels out to school and gets home between roughly 15:40 and 16:50, three tutoring sessions on top of three sciences' homework collapses by about week six, usually with the homework stopping first.

faqs.question: When will our child actually sit the science papers?
faqs.answer: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only, despite appearing in content aimed at Gulf parents. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong one, so plan from the version your school's exams officer holds.

faqs.question: Our child is on Core and wants a science at A Level. What should we do?
faqs.answer: Contest it in Year 10 with marked evidence, because the tier removes content as well as capping the grade and post-16 courses assume the higher-tier material. A term of weekly work aimed specifically at the separating content, followed by strong marks on the school's own assessments, is what changes a head of department's view. If the cap stands, ask the receiving sixth form directly what bridging they expect rather than assuming the subject is closed.

faqs.question: Which single purchase gives the most back across all three sciences?
faqs.answer: The practical skills block: four to six sessions on writing a repeatable method, identifying and controlling variables, reading instruments to an appropriate precision, tabulating with units in the headings, plotting with a sensible scale and criticising a method. It earns marks in biology, chemistry and physics at once and again in whichever practical route applies. Almost no family buys it because on an invoice it does not look like a subject.

faqs.question: What should the summer before Year 11 be used for?
faqs.answer: A short block, and it is the best-timed science tutoring available. With nothing else competing for the time, four to six sessions can rebuild electricity properly, drill a mole layout until it is automatic, or establish practical method writing across all three sciences. That removes work the autumn term would otherwise need weekly support to do, and it secures a weekly slot before Year 11 demand fills the early evenings across the city.

faqs.question: Can you help with the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons?
faqs.answer: We can support a student with their school's own material, within real limits worth knowing. Those subjects are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, KHDA calculates their instructional time on a forty-minute lesson unit and requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them, and using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. They are also excluded from the five subjects equivalency counts.

faqs.question: What time should science sessions be from these gates?
faqs.answer: 17:00, or 17:30 if your child travels back from Al Barsha or Al Sufouh. With no school inside Jumeirah Islands every pupil travels out, and the return leg usually serves two or three other communities first, so arrivals run from roughly 15:40 to 16:50. A 16:30 slot loses its first twenty minutes. Ask your transport office for your own route's timings, because households inside the same gates differ by twenty minutes, and keep Saturday morning for a full paper.

intro.heading: What 'IGCSE science' means in your child's case
paragraphs: There is no single IGCSE science qualification, and that is the source of most of the confusion families arrive with. Your child may be entered for three separate sciences, each with its own syllabus code and its own papers. Or for a combined or coordinated award covering all three in one or two qualifications with reduced content. Those are different courses with different paper counts, and a tutor needs to know which before the first session.

The second variable is the board. Cambridge IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics are 0610, 0620 and 0625; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The content overlaps heavily and the assessment does not, including how practical skills are examined. Past papers are not interchangeable, and a tutor working from the wrong set will teach well and move nothing.

The third is tier, where the subject is tiered. Cambridge offers Core and Extended in the sciences; Pearson uses Foundation and Higher in some subjects. The tier caps the grade and removes content, and it is normally set on Year 9 and early Year 10 evidence. If your child needs a science for sixth form, a Core entry is worth questioning in Year 10 rather than accepting silently.

Once those three facts are in hand the work becomes specific, and there is a fourth question only a parent can answer: which of the three sciences is actually failing? Families routinely say 'science' when the marked papers show chemistry is secure, biology is weak on language precision and physics is weak on electricity. Three different problems, three different interventions, and spreading one hour across all three fixes none of them.

For a Jumeirah Park household the constraint is the week. The community's own school runs the British curriculum and students at other schools travel out, with the bus returning most children between about 15:20 and 16:40 depending on district and route. Three sciences plus homework does not fit alongside three tutoring sessions, so the choice of which science gets the hour is the real decision.

There is a fifth question most families never ask, and it is the one with the best return: how are practical skills examined for your child's entry? Some candidates sit a practical examination in a laboratory and others a written alternative-to-practical paper. Both test method writing, variables, instrument reading, tabulation and graphing, and a short block on those skills earns marks in all three sciences at once.

IB Gram delivers this as live online tuition to Jumeirah Park, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers shared on screen. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are an India-only service. We target the local search phrase because it is what parents type, and then tell you plainly what the service is.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-pa.subjectsIntro: What an IGCSE science tutor should be working on, with the specific place each topic costs marks. Use these as test questions for any tutor you are considering.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel circuits. The single most frequently rebuilt topic in IGCSE science, because students learn the formulae without a mental model of what a circuit is doing. It needs reasoning about the physical situation first, then calculation, and it usually takes three sessions.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, moments and motion
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws, moments and pressure. Moments questions reward students who draw the situation and mark the distances from the pivot; those who work from the formula alone lose marks on anything non-standard. Graph interpretation is the other recurring loss.

subjects.name: Chemistry: mole and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Relative masses, moles, concentration, limiting reagents and percentage yield. The Extended grade turns substantially on these, and the problem is reliability rather than comprehension: a layout improvised each time fails under exam pressure. One fixed layout, drilled with units, fixes it quickly.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis and separation
subjects.description: Identifying ions and gases, chromatography, distillation and filtration. These carry straightforward marks that students drop simply because the tests and observations were never systematically learned. Among the fastest returns available in the whole science programme.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and bonding
subjects.description: Covalent and ionic bonding, structure and properties, homologous series and basic reactions. Explanation marks are lost where students state a property without connecting it to the bonding that causes it, which is what the question is actually asking for.

subjects.name: Biology: precision of language
subjects.description: The defining difficulty in IGCSE biology is not content but wording. Mark schemes want a named variable and a direction, where students write that the plant grew better. Examiner reports repeat this every series, and it responds to answer construction against real schemes rather than more revision.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, active transport, gas exchange and the two core processes. Osmosis questions in particular reward precise use of water potential language. Students who learn the processes as stories rather than as mechanisms lose the explanation marks.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid crosses, genetic diagrams, variation and selection. Genetic diagrams score only when laid out fully with gametes shown, and partial diagrams score partially. A procedural fix rather than a conceptual one, and a reliable source of recovered marks.

subjects.name: Practical skills across all three
subjects.description: Writing a repeatable method, identifying variables, reading instruments, plotting with a sensible scale and drawing a line of best fit. Assessed through a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper depending on the entry, and the single most transferable skill in science tutoring.

subjects.name: Command terms and exam conduct
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest and compare each demand a different answer. Add showing working so method marks survive, managing time across a paper, and answering the question asked rather than the one revised. The cheapest marks in science and the least often taught.

sections.heading: Separate, combined or coordinated: find out which
paragraphs: This is the first question and most families cannot answer it. Separate sciences means three qualifications, three sets of papers and three syllabus codes. Combined science means one qualification covering all three with reduced content. Coordinated science, in the Cambridge form, covers all three as a double award. The paper count, the content depth and the sixth-form consequences differ in each case.

It matters for tutoring because the tutor's brief changes completely. A combined-science candidate does not need the depth a separate-sciences candidate needs, and teaching them the separate-science content wastes the hour while making the student feel behind. The reverse error is worse: a separate-sciences candidate taught combined-level content arrives at the paper under-prepared.

It matters even more for what comes next. Sixth forms and Diploma schools differ in whether a combined award supports a science at A Level or at Higher Level, and the expectation is set by the receiving school rather than by the board. That is a Year 10 conversation with your child's school, not a post-results discovery, and it is worth having in writing.

Sometimes the route is a timetable constraint rather than a judgement about the student. Schools build option blocks around staffing, and a child capable of three separate sciences occasionally ends up on a combined award because of how the week was constructed. If that is your situation, it is worth asking directly whether a separate entry is possible.

The table sets out the three routes and what each implies. Confirm the specific award and codes with your school's exams officer, because the naming varies between boards and the detail matters more than the label.
