sections.heading: Which of the three sciences is actually failing
paragraphs: Parents say science; marked papers say something narrower. In most cases one of the three is secure, one is weak for a content reason and one is weak for a technique reason, and those need different responses. Finding out which costs nothing except the effort of collecting three marked papers, and it is the step that decides whether the tutoring money works.

The typical pattern in this community is that physics is weak on electricity and moments, chemistry is weak on mole reliability, and biology is weak on the precision of written answers. Those are three separate jobs. Electricity needs a mental model rebuilt over about three sessions. Mole calculations need a fixed layout drilled. Biology needs answer construction against real mark schemes.

The commonest mistake is to buy one weekly hour and ask the tutor to cover all three sciences inside it. That produces twenty minutes on each, no complete piece of work, no marked past paper and no measurable change. Parents defend the arrangement because it feels fair between subjects, and fairness between subjects is not a teaching principle.

The better approach is to pick one science for a term, usually the one that most affects sixth-form options or the one with the clearest fixable problem, and run it properly. Then reassess. In many households the second science never needs tutoring, because the practical and command-term work from the first transfers to it.

A tutor should be able to tell you in the first session, from marked papers, which of the three categories applies to each science and roughly how many sessions each would need. If the answer is a general plan to revise all three from the beginning, the papers have not been read.

sections.heading: How practical skills are examined, and what that means
paragraphs: Every IGCSE science assesses practical skills, and how it does so depends on the entry your school has made. Some candidates sit a practical examination in a laboratory; others sit an alternative-to-practical written paper that tests the same skills on paper. Which applies to your child is a question for the exams officer, and the answer changes how a tutor should prepare them.

Both routes test the same underlying things: can the student write a method precise enough for someone else to repeat, identify the variable being changed and the ones that must be controlled, read an instrument and record to an appropriate precision, tabulate results sensibly, plot a graph with labelled axes and a sensible scale, and draw a line of best fit that ignores an obvious outlier.

That list is the most valuable thing in science tutoring because it is transferable. Four to six sessions on practical technique earn marks in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously, and again in whichever practical route applies. No other block of science tutoring pays into three subjects at once, and almost no family buys it because it does not feel like a subject.

An alternative-to-practical paper has a particular trap: because it is written, students revise it as theory. It is not theory. It asks about apparatus, precision, anomalous results and improvements, and a student who has never been made to criticise a method on paper performs badly however well they know the content.

Online delivery suits this work well. The method is written, the table is drawn, the graph is plotted and critiqued, all on a shared screen. The hands-on laboratory work remains at school with the school's apparatus, as it would in any case, and that is where it belongs.

sections.heading: Fitting three sciences into a Jumeirah Park week
paragraphs: This is where science tutoring usually breaks, and it is a logistics problem rather than an academic one. Dubai schools finish between roughly 14:30 and 15:30. A Jumeirah Park bus route serving Al Barsha or Jumeirah Village returns most students between 15:20 and 16:40, depending on the district and which schools share the route. There is no metro station inside the community.

What remains is around four usable hours per weekday evening, into which homework for three sciences plus other subjects, dinner and sleep all have to fit. Adding three tutoring sessions to that week does not work, and families who try it discover by the fourth week that the sessions are being cancelled or the homework is not being done.

The workable pattern is one tutored science on one weekday evening, a second weekday left clear for the student's own work, and a Saturday morning slot for a full past paper when the examination year arrives. Students at the school inside Jumeirah Park can hold a 16:00 weekday slot; bussed students should take 17:00 or 17:30 rather than squeezing in unfed at 16:30.

Bus routes are built around schools rather than communities, so two households a few streets apart genuinely have different windows. Ask your school's transport office for your own route timings rather than copying a neighbour's slot, because twenty minutes is the difference between a session that works and one that is spent waking up.

During Ramadan the pattern shifts: school hours shorten, households run later, and a post-Iftar session or a late-morning weekend slot works better than anything at five in the afternoon. We reschedule rather than cancel, because the June series does not move to accommodate the calendar.

sections.heading: Boards, codes and the two UAE series
paragraphs: Cambridge and Pearson examine the sciences differently even where the content is similar, so the syllabus code decides which past papers a tutor should be using. Cambridge IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics are 0610, 0620 and 0625. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE equivalents are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Confirm the current codes with your exams officer, since specifications are revised.

There are structural differences worth knowing. Cambridge tiers many science subjects into Core and Extended and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong zone's timetable. Pearson publishes provisional and then final timetables per series and offers modular entry in some subjects.

On series, the rule for a UAE family is simple and frequently misstated in tutoring content. Cambridge candidates here sit the June and November series. The February/March series is offered to India only and is not available to a UAE candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

The November series is therefore the resit route, and the Pearson precedent shows its timing cost: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students in January; November 2025 results arrived on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026.

Always plan from the live official timetable your school holds rather than from any date on a tutoring page, including this one. Dates are revised, zone versions differ, and a parent acting on a wrong date pays a cost no refund covers.

sections.heading: What science support costs here
paragraphs: Published Dubai rates put a qualified subject tutor online at AED 150-300 an hour, with Unitors quoting IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and IB work sits at AED 200-450 or more on Bestimate's survey, with TutorChase around AED 270 and BartyED's premium examiner-led tier at AED 650. Budget providers advertise from AED 33-65: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 and EdFlik from AED 45-65.

In-home visits carry a travel premium, at AED 180-350 on Bestimate's figures and AED 200-500 for independent home tutors. On a monthly basis Bestimate estimates AED 240-600 for a weekly budget arrangement, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Packages run from about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

The specific trap in science is multiplication. A parent who decides all three sciences need support and prices three weekly hours arrives at a monthly figure that no household sustains for three terms. The arrangement then stops in week six, which is the worst outcome of all. One science done properly for a term is better value and more likely to finish.

The best-value purchase in science is the practical skills block, because four to six sessions pay into all three subjects and into the practical or alternative-to-practical paper. Almost nobody buys it, because it does not look like a subject. The second best is a single-science block chosen from a marked paper with a defined target and an end point.

Every figure above is the provider's or survey's own, read in October 2026, and none of them is an IB Gram price. We publish no rate card because the right number depends on the science, the tier and the weeks remaining.

sections.heading: Mandatory UAE subjects, equivalency and the week
paragraphs: A science timetable in Dubai does not sit in isolation. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required its current guidance to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with the advice that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes.

KHDA also requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, which is why support there means the school's own material.

The consequence for a Year 10 or 11 science student is a fuller week than the subject list suggests, and it strengthens the argument for one tutored science rather than three. Prioritisation is not a compromise here; it is the only arrangement that fits.

Equivalency is the other thing worth knowing while choosing science entries. On the British track the Ministry of Education requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at grade E or better or two Advanced Subsidiary Level subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

That exclusion changes the arithmetic. A student taking ten subjects including Arabic and Islamic Education has eight that count, and if the sciences are weak the five-subject threshold is less comfortable than it looks. IB Gram does not perform or guarantee equivalency, and no tutoring is required for it; verify current requirements with the Ministry of Education.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child takes separate or combined science?
faqs.answer: Ask the exams officer, by email, for the award and the syllabus codes. Separate sciences means three qualifications with three sets of papers; a coordinated double award or a combined single award covers all three with reduced content. The answer changes the depth a tutor should teach and, more importantly, what sixth forms will accept afterwards. Schools sometimes place a capable student on a combined award for timetable reasons, so it is also worth asking whether a separate entry is still possible.

faqs.question: Can we get all three sciences tutored in one weekly hour?
faqs.answer: You can buy it and we will advise against it. An hour split three ways produces twenty minutes each, no completed piece of work and no marked past paper, which means no measurable change. Pick the science that most affects sixth-form options or has the clearest fixable problem and run that one properly for a term. In many households the second science then needs no tutoring at all, because the practical and command-term work transfers across subjects.

faqs.question: Which single science topic most often needs rebuilding from scratch?
faqs.answer: Electricity and circuits in physics. Students learn the formulae without any mental model of what a circuit is doing, so anything non-standard defeats them, and no amount of revision fixes it because the problem is conceptual rather than factual. It takes about three sessions to rebuild properly, working from the physical situation towards the calculation rather than the reverse. Moments in physics and mole calculations in chemistry are the next two on the list.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in biology when they know the content?
faqs.answer: Because biology is marked on precision of language. The scheme wants a named variable and a direction; students write that the plant grew better or the rate increased. Examiner reports make this point every series. State, describe, explain and suggest each demand a different answer shape, and nobody teaches that explicitly. The work is answer construction against real mark schemes, which usually takes three or four sessions and then shows up immediately on timed papers.

faqs.question: Is the practical assessed in a laboratory, or on paper, for our entry?
faqs.answer: It depends on the entry your school has made, so ask the exams officer. Some candidates sit a practical examination in a laboratory; others sit an alternative-to-practical written paper testing the same skills on paper. The distinction matters because students revise the written paper as theory, and it is not theory: it asks about apparatus, precision, anomalous results and improvements. A student who has never been made to criticise a method on paper performs poorly on it regardless of content knowledge.

faqs.question: Do science tutors visit homes in Jumeirah Park?
faqs.answer: Not through us. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; that service runs in India only, and there is no centre here either. Science tuition for Jumeirah Park families is live online, one tutor to one student, on Gulf Standard Time, with past papers and graph work on a shared screen. Practical work stays at school with the school's apparatus in any case. Published in-home rates in Dubai run AED 180-500 an hour including travel if presence in the room is essential.

faqs.question: What is the best-value science tutoring we could buy?
faqs.answer: A practical skills block of four to six sessions: writing a repeatable method, identifying and controlling variables, reading instruments to an appropriate precision, tabulating with units in the headings, plotting with a sensible scale and drawing a line of best fit. It earns marks in biology, chemistry and physics at once and again in whichever practical route applies. Almost no family buys it, because it does not look like a subject, and it is the clearest return available.

faqs.question: Our child is on Core science but wants to study a science at A Level. What now?
faqs.answer: Talk to the school in Year 10, with marked evidence, because the tier removes content as well as capping grades and sixth forms set their own entry expectations. A term of weekly work aimed specifically at the content separating the tiers, followed by strong marks on the school's own assessments, is what changes a head of department's view. If the cap stands, ask the receiving sixth form directly what bridging they expect rather than assuming the door is closed.

faqs.question: When will my child actually sit the science papers?
faqs.answer: UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series; the February/March series is offered to India only and is not available here, despite appearing in tutoring content aimed at Gulf parents. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version and states it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who used the wrong one, so use the version your school holds.

faqs.question: How many sciences should we be paying for in Year 11?
faqs.answer: Usually one, occasionally two, almost never three. The limiting factor is the week rather than the money: three sciences plus other subjects already fills the evenings in a household where the bus arrives at 16:30, and adding three sessions means either the sessions or the homework stops happening. Two is viable if one science is already secure and you use two separate evenings. Three collapses by about week six in our experience.

faqs.question: Is chemistry or physics harder to catch up at this level?
faqs.answer: Physics, usually, because its difficulties are conceptual and compound: a student without a model of a circuit cannot build on it. Chemistry's common weaknesses -- mole reliability, qualitative analysis, bonding explanations -- are procedural or factual and respond quickly, often within two or three sessions each. Biology sits in between: the content is accessible and the language precision takes longer to change. That ordering is why we usually recommend starting with physics if all three are weak.

faqs.question: What should we do in the summer before Year 11?
faqs.answer: A short block, and it is the best-timed science tutoring available. With nothing else in the diary, four to six sessions can rebuild electricity properly, drill a mole layout until it is automatic, or establish practical method writing across all three sciences. That removes work the autumn term would otherwise need weekly support to do. It also secures a weekly slot before the Year 11 demand arrives and the early-evening hours fill up.

faqs.question: Do you help with the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education subjects too?
faqs.answer: We can support a student with their school's own material, and there are real limits worth knowing. Those subjects are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in several of them, and using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. So support means working with what the school teaches, not substituting an alternative course. They are also excluded from the five subjects equivalency counts.

faqs.question: How quickly can you start, and what if the slot we want is taken?
faqs.answer: For most science subjects, within the same week. The scarce combination is a weekday 17:00 to 19:00 slot in the spring term, which is when every Year 11 family in Dubai wants the same hour. If it is not free you are told, with a date, and offered an off-peak or weekend alternative or an interim tutor with a stated handover. Where a tutor is based outside the UAE and teaches on Gulf Standard Time, we say so before you book.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover two sciences if we use two evenings?
faqs.answer: Often yes at this level, and it has a real advantage: one person sees the whole science workload and can tell you which paper to prioritise in a crowded fortnight. Chemistry and biology pair comfortably, as do physics and maths. What we avoid is one tutor covering all three in a single hour. Ask which syllabus codes they have taught and whether they know the practical route your child is entered for before combining subjects.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-vi.tutorsIntro: Science tutors matched to Jumeirah Village Circle students are discipline specialists working to a named syllabus code, proposed with a block sized to the weeks remaining. A biologist teaches 0610 and a physicist teaches 0625, and nobody is asked to cover all three at Extended depth.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one evening, and a calendar that decides everything
paragraphs: A triple-award IGCSE student has the fullest timetable in the school and, in Jumeirah Village Circle, one of the busiest afternoons: a short school run to JVT or Al Barsha South, then academies in Dubai Sports City next door taking them out again between four and six. Three sciences competing for the remaining evening is the central planning problem of this qualification, and the usual response — a weekly slot in each — is both the most expensive arrangement available and the least effective, because it leaves no time for the unaided practice that actually consolidates anything.

The way out is sequencing, and sequencing requires knowing when each discipline's hardest content arrives. Schools teach the three sciences in broadly predictable orders. Physics electricity, which decides more science grades than any other topic, typically lands in the middle of the two years. Chemistry's quantitative work — moles, concentration, electrolysis calculations — builds across both. Biology's genetics and the harder transport and respiration content tend to arrive later. So a student who seemed fine in Year 10 and struggles in Year 11 has usually just reached the parts their foundation could not carry.

Then there is a category of marks that can be secured at literally any point in the year and almost always is not. Chemistry's qualitative analysis ion tests are pure recall. Physics half-life calculations are a fixed procedure. Biology genetics question shapes are predictable. The practical route — whether your child sits a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper — is drillable in two or three sessions at any time. Those are the cheapest marks in the qualification and they are routinely left until there is no time left for them.

Above all of it sits the tier decision, made by the school during Year 10 on Year 10 evidence and closing at the final entry deadline. A Core or Foundation entry caps the available grade at 5, and on a coordinated double award that cap applies to all three disciplines at once — so a student strong in biology can have that grade capped because of physics.

One more calendar item deserves naming because it is routinely discovered too late: the practical route. Every science route assesses practical skills, either through a practical test sat with apparatus or through an alternative-to-practical paper, and which applies depends on the school's entry. The skills it rewards — tabulation with units in column headings, variable control phrased as what was held constant, conclusions written from the data table — transfer across all three sciences at once, which makes them unusually efficient for a student with one usable evening. They should be drilled by January of Year 11, not in May.

IB Gram teaches Jumeirah Village Circle students one-to-one over live video at a fixed weekly time in Gulf Standard Time, matched to a named syllabus code. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; in-person home tutoring is a service we run only in India. Our fee follows a free trial lesson, because the honest number depends on the weeks remaining and what marked papers show.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-vi.subjectsIntro: Here are the science clusters tuition is actually bought for, with when each one usually arrives and whether it can be fixed late.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Lands mid-course and decides more science grades than any other topic. Series and parallel reasoning collapses on unfamiliar diagrams and formula rearrangement fails under time pressure. Fixable late in three or four sessions, and worth more earlier.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and energy
subjects.description: Taught early, so a gap here is visible in Year 10 and cheap to close then. Marks are lost by giving numbers without naming energy stores, which is what the scheme asks for.

subjects.name: Physics: waves and radioactivity
subjects.description: Usually Year 11, content-dense and self-contained. Half-life calculations are a fixed procedure and among the most reliably recoverable marks at any point in the year.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Builds across both years and underpins electrolysis, energetics and titration questions. The earlier this is secured the more of the rest of chemistry it carries, which makes it the best Year 10 purchase in the sciences.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis and ion tests
subjects.description: Pure recall for cation, anion and gas tests with their observations. A finite list, learnable in one session, and left blank on papers with striking regularity. The single cheapest marks in the qualification, available at any time.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic, bonding and electrolysis
subjects.description: Spread across Year 11 in most schemes. Bonding answers lose marks to vocabulary — bond strength used where intermolecular forces were wanted — and electrolysis depends on the mole work underneath it.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: The quantitative end of biology, usually mid-course. Marks lost on precision: osmosis answers omitting partially permeable membrane, enzyme answers saying the enzyme died rather than denatured.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Typically Year 11 and highly teachable, because the question shapes are predictable. Students lose marks by omitting the genotype key or the gamete row rather than by misunderstanding the biology — recoverable in two sessions whenever taken.

subjects.name: Practical skills and the practical paper
subjects.levels: All routes, practical test or alternative-to-practical
subjects.description: Tabulation conventions, variable control phrasing, scale reading, graphing and writing conclusions from data. Assessed in its own right, taught unevenly, drillable in two or three sessions at any point, and almost always left too late.

subjects.name: Mathematical fluency for science
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, unit conversion, percentage change and reading graphs. Not a syllabus topic and frequently the real problem, particularly in physics. Best addressed in Year 10, before it compounds across three subjects.

sections.heading: When each discipline's hardest content arrives
paragraphs: Schools teach the sciences in broadly predictable orders, which makes the timing of problems predictable too. Physics starts with forces, motion and energy, which are relatively approachable, then moves to electricity in the middle of the course — and electricity is where more science grades are decided than anywhere else, because circuit reasoning that works on a textbook diagram collapses on an unfamiliar one.

Chemistry builds its quantitative spine across both years: moles, concentration, limiting reagents and then electrolysis calculations that depend on them. That is why the earlier chemistry mole work is secured, the more of the rest of the subject it carries. Organic chemistry, bonding and electrolysis tend to be spread through Year 11, and bonding losses are vocabulary rather than content.

Biology front-loads cells and classification, which are manageable, and places transport, respiration and photosynthesis mid-course and genetics typically in Year 11. Genetics is the single most teachable late topic in the sciences because the question shapes are predictable and the marks are lost to omissions — a missing genotype key, an absent gamete row — rather than to misunderstanding.

So a student who looked fine in Year 10 and struggles in Year 11 has usually not deteriorated. They have reached electricity, or electrolysis, or the parts of biology that assume the earlier work. The table below is what to take to a prospective tutor: ask which cluster they would start with for your child, and expect an answer drawn from the marked papers rather than from the start of the syllabus.

sections.heading: Why three weekly science slots is the wrong plan
paragraphs: This is the arrangement families in Jumeirah Village Circle most often arrive asking for and the one we most often argue against. A triple-award student has the fullest timetable in the school. In this community they also have a short school run that looks generous and an adjacent Dubai Sports City that takes them out again between four and six. What is left of the evening is one usable working block.

Fill that block with a tuition session three times a week and the student has no unassisted practice time at all. The unassisted attempt is the mechanism by which anything gets learned: it is where a method becomes automatic and where the student discovers what they cannot yet do. Remove it and you have bought attendance. At a mid-band market rate three weekly slots also runs to roughly AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month, which makes it the most expensive way to achieve less.

The alternative is sequencing in the long middle and rotation at the end. Through Year 10 and early Year 11, run one discipline at a time in a four to six session block, chosen from marked papers, and finish it before starting the next. Marked papers almost always show the grade is being lost in one discipline rather than three, so often only one block is needed.

In the final eight weeks, rotate: one discipline a week, a whole timed paper and a marking session, which gives each science a full hearing every three weeks at one session a week. That is the plan the table sets out, and online delivery is what makes it administratively possible, because no travel has to be rearranged every time the discipline changes.

sections.heading: The eight-week rotation, laid out
paragraphs: Here is the plan we propose to triple-award families in this community, written out rather than described. Weeks one to three: one discipline each, a whole timed paper in each, marked against the scheme, producing a named list of losses per subject. That first cycle is diagnostic as much as remedial and it tells you where the remaining five weeks should be weighted.

Weeks four to six: the second cycle, weighted towards whichever discipline the first cycle showed as weakest, with the other two getting a shorter paper each. This is also where the recallable marks get secured — the chemistry ion tests, the half-life procedure, the genetics question shapes — because they are quick and they bank reliably.

Week seven: the practical route, whichever the school uses. Tabulation conventions with units in column headings, variable control phrased the way the scheme wants, conclusions written from the data table rather than from expectation. These skills transfer across all three sciences, which is why they belong in a single week rather than being split.

Week eight: re-sit one of the week-one papers under timed conditions to measure the change, then triage. Deciding what not to revise in the final days is one of the more valuable things a specialist does and almost never what a family expects to pay for. Sessions can shift post-Iftar through Ramadan, and there is a hard stop at study leave agreed on day one.

The reason the rotation works where three weekly slots do not is simply that it leaves four evenings a week free. Those evenings are where the papers set between sessions actually get attempted, and the attempt is the part that changes anything.

sections.heading: The marks you can bank at any point in the year
paragraphs: Some science marks do not depend on where you are in the course, and they are the cheapest in the qualification. They are left until the end so reliably that it is worth listing them explicitly.

Chemistry qualitative analysis is first. The cation, anion and gas tests with their observations are a finite, memorisable list carrying real marks on the practical route paper, and students leave them blank with striking consistency. One session of structured memorisation work secures them, in October of Year 10 just as well as in April of Year 11.

Physics half-life is second. It is a fixed procedure, it appears reliably, and once a student can read a decay curve and apply the procedure it stays. Biology genetics question shapes are third: Punnett squares and monohybrid crosses have a predictable architecture, and the marks lost are omissions — the genotype key, the gamete row, the ratio stated — rather than misunderstanding.

The practical route is fourth and the largest of the group. Tabulation conventions carry marks: column headings with units, consistent decimal places, the dependent variable on the correct axis. Variable control carries marks, and it must be phrased as naming what was held constant rather than asserting the experiment was fair. Conclusions carry marks for referring to the data collected. Two or three sessions covers all of it and the skills apply to all three sciences at once.

Taken together these four groups are perhaps a week of tuition and a measurable number of marks. They are also the part of the plan a family can commit to without waiting for a specialist in a particular discipline to free up, which makes them the sensible thing to start with while a tighter match is being arranged.
bullets: Chemistry ion tests: a finite list, one session, real marks
Physics half-life: a fixed procedure that stays once learned

sections.heading: The practical route, and when to drill it
paragraphs: Every science route assesses practical skills and almost no parent knows which way their child's school does it. There are two models: a practical test sat in a laboratory with apparatus under examination conditions, or an alternative-to-practical paper that assesses the same skills in writing — reading a scale from a diagram, identifying the flaw in a described method, completing a results table, plotting and concluding.

Which applies depends on the school's entry, and it varies across the campuses this cluster uses. It is a single question to the school and it changes what two or three sessions should contain: a practical test needs timed practice with real apparatus, which has to happen at school, while an alternative-to-practical paper needs past-paper practical questions marked against the scheme, which works perfectly well online.

The timing point is that this is drillable at any stage and is almost always left too late. The skills are taught unevenly because they sit between subject teaching and laboratory time, and they are worth real marks on every route. A family that books a practical-route block in January of Year 11 is buying marks that a family booking in May will not have time to collect.

There is also a sequencing argument. Practical-paper skills transfer across all three sciences simultaneously, which makes the block unusually efficient for a triple-award student with one usable evening. Two or three sessions improving tabulation, variable control phrasing and conclusion writing lifts three subjects at once, which nothing else in this qualification does.

sections.heading: The tier decision, and the deadline that closes it
paragraphs: This is the date that matters most in the sciences, because science is where post-16 plans most often depend on a specific grade. A Cambridge Core entry caps the maximum available grade at 5, and a Pearson Foundation entry does the same. A student aiming at IB Diploma Higher Level sciences or science A Levels generally needs more, and no quantity of tuition lifts a ceiling.

On a coordinated double award the decision applies to the whole subject, covering all three disciplines together, which produces a specific injustice worth noticing: a student strong in biology and weak in physics may be placed on Core because of physics, with the biology grade capped as collateral. Where that is the case, a physics block early in Year 11 is the intervention with the most leverage available on this route, and it is a far smaller spend than a year of general support.

Schools make the decision for a defensible reason: a borderline candidate entered for the higher tier can score below its lowest available grade and come away with nothing, whereas the lower tier produces a secure 4 or 5. But it is made on Year 10 evidence, and a student whose work changes materially in the first term of Year 11 can sometimes be moved — if a parent asks before the final entry deadline.

So ask the school two questions in the first weeks of Year 11: which tier is my child entered for in each science, and when is the final entry deadline. A five or six session block on higher-tier material taken immediately produces a clear answer and written evidence a head of year can act on. The same block taken in February has nothing left to influence.

sections.heading: Mocks, and the fortnight that follows
paragraphs: Mock examinations sit roughly a term before the June series and a full set of marked science papers is the best diagnostic the two years produce. Read together they answer the question that determines the whole plan: is the grade being lost in one discipline or spread across three, and within each one is it content or technique.

In our experience of this community, marked papers usually show one discipline carrying most of the loss — physics, more often than not, and electricity within it. That turns a proposed three-slot weekly arrangement into a single four to six session block with a specialist, which is roughly a third of the cost and produces more. Families who skip this step buy a term of general support aimed at a problem nobody diagnosed.

The fortnight after mocks is therefore the highest-value booking window in the calendar and also the busiest, since every family in Dubai receives marked papers at roughly the same time. Mock timetables across the schools this cluster uses differ by up to a fortnight, which helps a little: a Motor City family and a JVT family may not be competing for the same slot in the same week.

Keep the papers. Re-sitting one of them under timed conditions four to six weeks into a block gives a direct measure of whether the work is landing, which is considerably more useful than discussing how the sessions are going. We build that re-sit into the eight-week rotation for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: The November series for sciences, decided in the spring
paragraphs: Both boards run a November series, so a second attempt sits roughly five months after June rather than a year, and private candidate entry through an approved Dubai centre is possible. For the sciences this is particularly useful, because a single discipline can be retaken without disturbing the other two on a triple-award route.

The arithmetic is worth doing in March. Thirty weeks of general support before June, at a mid-band market rate, is in the region of AED 6,000. A focused block of eight to ten sessions after results, aimed at one discipline and one tier, is roughly AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 plus the centre's entry fee. If the realistic spring view is that physics will land a band short while biology and chemistry are secure, the second plan is both cheaper and better targeted.

Two timing cautions. The November entry deadline falls well before the examination and often before a family has absorbed August results, so the date needs finding in the spring term. And entry fees for a private candidate are paid to the centre rather than to a tutor, which belongs in the comparison.

The November window is also the only realistic route past a tier ceiling, including on a coordinated double award where the ceiling currently covers all three disciplines. A student entered for Core in June can be entered for Extended in November, which converts a fixed grade 5 into a possibility. For a science student whose post-16 plan needs a 6 or 7, that is a spring-term conversation with the school.
bullets: A single discipline can be retaken in November without disturbing the others

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the usable evening
paragraphs: The UAE academic year runs in three terms from late August to early July, with a winter break around the turn of the year and a spring break later. For a Year 11 science student those breaks fall usefully: the winter break sits between the mock period at many schools and the final run-in, and the spring break sits inside the eight to ten weeks before the June series. Four or five sessions across either one buys ground term time cannot, because there is no homework competing for the hours.

Ramadan adds a layer. School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and household energy changes for everybody including students who are not fasting. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, in the current period it falls close to the June run-in. Plan for it: shorter sessions, post-Iftar timing, and whole timed papers moved to weekend mornings for that month.

On the ordinary week, this community has a particular shape. Most students travel five to fifteen minutes to JVT or Al Barsha South, or eight to fifteen to Motor City, and are home by 3.45pm. Dubai Sports City is adjacent and its academies take students out between four and six. So the workable slots are around 5.30pm without a club and 7pm to 8.15pm with one, later again from Arabian Ranches 3, Mudon or Town Square.

Place the session after a first attempt at the school's work. A student who has tried the questions arrives with a specific sticking point, which is what a specialist resolves quickly; scheduled earlier it becomes supervised homework at a specialist rate. Weekend mornings are the right slot for whole timed papers, which need ninety uninterrupted minutes a weekday evening here rarely offers.

sections.heading: Who is permitted to tutor science here
paragraphs: Science tuition here is bounded by the same single document as every other subject, and it is a lighter document than most parents expect. The private tuition work permit is administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, having been introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and it is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own listing for issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. Note what the permit does not do. It does not certify that the holder can teach physics to the same standard as biology, and in a Jumeirah Village Circle household running all three disciplines at once that distinction matters a great deal more than the permit does.

Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. That last category explains much of the AED 45 to AED 150 band, where a very low rate usually reflects tutor category rather than anything improper. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so no amount can honestly be quoted.

One boundary becomes tempting in the fortnight after mocks, which is exactly when it should not be crossed, and it applies with force in the sciences where the qualified teacher pool at any school is small. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. That is press-reported and should be verified against the current ADEK policy document before being treated as exact wording.

And what nobody holds. A tutoring business with premises in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute from KHDA — which a tuition centre may legitimately hold and an individual tutor cannot. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no UAE office or centre, and is not accredited, licensed, approved by or partnered with KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge, Pearson or the IB. We also do not reproduce or distribute syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes.

process.title: Find the codes and the tiers
process.description: 0610, 0620, 0625 for three separate Cambridge sciences; 0654 for the coordinated double award; 0653 for combined; 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 or 4SD0 for Pearson. Then the tier in each. process.title: Send marked papers from all three
process.description: This is the step that saves the most money in this subject. Read together, marked papers almost always show the grade being lost in one discipline rather than three, which turns a proposed three-slot arrangement into a single four to six session block with a specialist.

process.title: Buy the block that matches the date
process.description: Chemistry moles work and mathematical fluency belong in Year 10, because they compound. A tier-evidence block belongs in the first weeks of Year 11. The practical-route block works at any point and should not wait until May. The rotation belongs in the final eight weeks.

process.title: Take the free trial on a lost question
process.description: You and your child meet the proposed discipline specialist over live video. Hand them a question the mock lost. Afterwards you get their read, a session count sized to the weeks remaining, and the fee. No payment is required to reach that point and nothing is conditional.

process.title: Run one discipline at a time, then rotate
process.description: Sequence through the long middle and rotate at the end. Never three weekly slots: the student needs the evening for unaided practice, and in this community there is only one usable working block once the school run and the academy are done.

whyPoints.title: We argue against three weekly slots
whyPoints.description: Three science sessions a week runs to roughly AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month at a mid-band rate and leaves a Jumeirah Village Circle student no evening for unaided practice, which is the mechanism that works. Sequencing and then rotating costs a third as much and produces more.

whyPoints.title: Blocks timed to the syllabus
whyPoints.description: Chemistry mole work pays in Year 10 because it compounds; the practical route pays at any time and is usually left too late; the rotation belongs in the final eight weeks. We ask which clusters the school has covered before proposing anything.

whyPoints.title: Recallable marks named explicitly
whyPoints.description: Chemistry ion tests, half-life procedure, genetics question shapes and practical-paper conventions are finite, learnable and routinely left blank. We list them and secure them deliberately, because they are the cheapest marks in the qualification and nobody sells them.

whyPoints.title: Discipline specialists, matched by code
whyPoints.description: At Core tier one competent general science tutor is often enough and we will say so. At Extended tier, electricity, mole calculations and genetics are three different teaching problems, and we staff by syllabus code because past-paper material does not transfer between routes.

whyPoints.title: Mocks used as diagnosis, with a re-sit
whyPoints.description: One session per discipline on the marked mock before buying anything, then a paper re-sat weeks later to measure change. That is a harder and more honest review mechanism than discussing progress, and it is why we ask families to keep the scripts.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery and attributed figures
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time; IB Gram makes no home visits in the UAE, as in-person home tutoring exists only in our India service. Every AED figure here belongs to a named provider or survey with the research date stated, and no grade is ever promised.

faqs.question: Should my triple-award child have a weekly session in each science?
faqs.answer: No, and it is the arrangement we argue against most often. A triple-award student has the fullest timetable in the school, and in Jumeirah Village Circle the adjacent Dubai Sports City academies take them out between four and six, so there is one usable working block in the evening. Filling it three times a week leaves no unassisted practice time, which is the mechanism by which anything gets learned. At a mid-band rate it also costs AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month to achieve less.

faqs.question: What should a final eight weeks across three sciences look like?
faqs.answer: A rotation at one session a week. Weeks one to three: one discipline each, a whole timed paper marked against the scheme, producing a named list of losses per subject. Weeks four to six: a second cycle weighted towards the weakest discipline, with recallable marks secured alongside. Week seven: the practical route, whose skills transfer across all three sciences. Week eight: re-sit a week-one paper to measure the change, then decide what not to revise in the final days.

faqs.question: Which science marks can we secure at any point in the year?
faqs.answer: Four groups, and they are the cheapest in the qualification. Chemistry qualitative analysis — the cation, anion and gas tests with observations — is a finite list learnable in one session and left blank on papers with striking regularity. Physics half-life is a fixed procedure that stays once learned. Biology genetics question shapes are predictable, with marks lost to omissions rather than misunderstanding. And the practical route, at two or three sessions, which lifts all three sciences simultaneously.

faqs.question: My child was fine in Year 10 and is struggling now. What changed?
faqs.answer: Probably nothing about the child. Physics electricity lands mid-course and decides more science grades than any other topic, because circuit reasoning that works on a textbook diagram collapses on an unfamiliar one. Chemistry electrolysis calculations arrive in Year 11 and depend on mole work secured earlier. Biology genetics and the harder transport content also tend to be Year 11. A student who looked fine in December has usually reached the parts their foundation could not carry, which a marked paper shows clearly.

faqs.question: When should we drill the practical paper?
faqs.answer: Earlier than almost everybody does, and by January of Year 11 at the latest. The skills — tabulation with units in column headings, variable control phrased as what was held constant, conclusions written from the data table — are taught unevenly because they fall between subject teaching and laboratory time, and they carry real marks on every route. They also transfer across all three sciences at once, which makes the block unusually efficient for a student with one usable evening a week.

faqs.question: How do I find out which practical route my child's school entered them for?
faqs.answer: One of the two, and the school decides. A practical test is sat in a laboratory with apparatus under examination conditions; an alternative-to-practical paper assesses the same skills in writing — reading a scale from a diagram, spotting a flaw in a described method, completing a results table, plotting and concluding. It varies across the campuses this cluster uses, so ask the school. The answer changes what two or three sessions should contain and whether the practice has to happen at school.

faqs.question: How does the tier decision work on a coordinated double award?
faqs.answer: It applies to the whole subject, covering all three disciplines together, which produces a specific problem. A student strong in biology and weak in physics may be placed on Core because of physics, with the biology grade capped as collateral at 5. That makes a physics block early in Year 11 the intervention with the most leverage on this route, because fixing one discipline can lift the entry for all three. Ask the school which tier is entered and when the final deadline falls.

faqs.question: What should we do with marked mock papers from three sciences?
faqs.answer: Read them together before buying anything, ideally with one session per discipline. In this community they usually show one discipline carrying most of the loss — physics more often than not, and electricity within it — which turns a proposed three-slot weekly arrangement into a single four to six session block at roughly a third of the cost. Then keep the papers: re-sitting one under timed conditions four to six weeks into a block measures whether the work is landing.

faqs.question: On a triple-award route, can we retake just the weak discipline?
faqs.answer: Yes, and on a triple-award route that is the main attraction. Both boards run a November series, so a second attempt in one discipline sits roughly five months after June without disturbing the two that went well, and private candidate entry through an approved Dubai centre is possible. A focused block of eight to ten sessions aimed at one paper and one tier is roughly AED 1,600 to AED 2,000 at a mid-band rate plus the centre's entry fee, paid to the centre rather than to a tutor.

faqs.question: When should we decide about a November science entry?
faqs.answer: In the spring term, not in August. The November entry deadline falls well before the examination and frequently before a family has absorbed June results, so it needs finding early. The spring is also when a realistic view is possible: if physics looks likely to land a band short while chemistry and biology are secure, a targeted November plan is cheaper and better aimed than extending general support through to June in all three subjects.

faqs.question: Which Year 10 science block is worth the most?
faqs.answer: Chemistry mole work, closely followed by mathematical fluency for physics. Both compound: moles underpin electrolysis, energetics and every titration question that comes later, and rearranging formulae, standard form and unit conversion underpin physics throughout. Four sessions on either in Year 10 prevents a visible share of the Year 11 repair work across more than one subject. Both are also unglamorous, which is why families rarely request them and usually ask about the topic that looks hardest instead.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change a science revision plan?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, evenings restructure around Iftar, and the household's energy pattern changes including for students who are not fasting. Because Ramadan moves earlier each year against the Gregorian calendar, in the current period it falls close to the June run-in. What works is shorter sessions, post-Iftar timing, and moving whole timed papers to weekend mornings for that month, since a paper needs ninety uninterrupted minutes. Online delivery makes the rearrangement trivial, with no travel to renegotiate.

faqs.question: Is the winter break useful for a Year 11 science student?
faqs.answer: More than most families expect. The UAE academic year runs in three terms from late August to early July, and the winter break sits between the mock period at many schools and the final run-in — exactly where four or five sessions buy ground term time cannot, because there is no homework competing for the hours. The spring break sits inside the eight to ten weeks before the June series and is more valuable still. Families rarely plan either, because holidays feel like time off.

faqs.question: What if no specialist is free in the discipline we need?
faqs.answer: You get the realistic wait rather than a general science tutor at Extended tier. Availability is thinnest for Pearson science codes and tightest in the eight weeks before the June series, when every family in Dubai wants the same hours. In the meantime the practical-route block or a recallable-marks session can usually run with a different specialist, and both are genuinely useful rather than filler. Where the available tutor is based outside the UAE, we say so, including the time zone, before any payment.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-vi.closingBody: Three IGCSE sciences and one usable evening is a scheduling problem before it is a teaching one. Send us the syllabus codes, the tiers, which practical route the school uses, and marked papers from all three. Marked papers usually show the grade being lost in one discipline rather than three, which turns a proposed three-slot arrangement into one short block. Then rotate in the final eight weeks, one discipline a week with a timed paper each. You can test the proposed specialist in a free trial lesson over live video. No home visits in the UAE and no promised grades.

Most work with students from the British-curriculum schools across Jumeirah Village Triangle and the Dubailand belt.

intro.heading: First find out which science qualification your child is taking
paragraphs: There is no such thing as a single IGCSE in science, which is why the first question a competent tutor asks is which route the student is on. Separate sciences means three IGCSEs: Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610, each with its own full syllabus and its own pair of papers plus a practical component. Coordinated Science is a double award covering all three disciplines with reduced content. Combined Science is a single award covering all three with further reduced content. Pearson offers its own equivalents again with different codes.

Those routes are not interchangeable and they do not lead to the same places. Three separate sciences keeps every A Level and IB Higher Level science open without argument. A double or single award covers less content in each discipline and some receiving schools treat it as insufficient preparation for a Higher Level science. For a child who might read medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, veterinary medicine or an engineering route, that distinction is the most consequential thing on this page.

The second thing most families do not know about is the practical component. Many Cambridge science entries use an alternative-to-practical paper, which assesses experimental method on paper rather than in a laboratory: choosing apparatus, identifying control variables, judging the resolution of an instrument, spotting anomalous results, drawing and reading graphs. It carries real marks and it is almost always the last thing a school revision programme reaches, because the theory papers are bigger. For a student a grade short of their target, it is frequently the best four sessions available.

The third is recall. IGCSE sciences contain a surprising amount of content that is pure memory rather than reasoning, and chemistry's qualitative analysis — the tests for cations, anions and gases, with the observation each produces — is the clearest example. It is a table. A student who learns the table to blank recall picks up marks on every paper that includes an identification question, and most students revise it by recognition instead, which does not work under examination conditions. The same is true of biology definitions, which are credited against specific wording, and of the physics formulae that are not printed in the examination. None of that is interesting work and all of it is cheap, which is the combination that makes it get skipped.

What follows is the route comparison, the paper structure for each science, the alternative-to-practical skill set, the recall tables worth learning, where marks are lost topic by topic, what tutoring costs in this market with sources, the examination calendar including the series UAE candidates never sit, and how to schedule around a Jumeirah Village Triangle school night. Teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

A student weak on those arrives at IGCSE looking like they have a science problem when they have an arithmetic and precision problem.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-vi.subjectsIntro: The IGCSE science subjects and components most requested from the Jumeirah Village Triangle area, with the Cambridge code and what each one actually tests. Ordered by where marks are lost.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and electromagnetism produce the heaviest loss, followed by graph work where axes are mislabelled or a gradient is read from the wrong points. Moments, pressure and thermal physics are reliable mark sources once the formula handling is secure. Units and prefixes are assessed throughout rather than separately.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: Moles arithmetic and ionic equations without state symbols cost the most on Extended. Qualitative analysis is pure recall and the fastest recoverable block of marks in the subject. Organic chemistry at this level is about functional groups and reaction types rather than mechanisms.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Content volume rather than depth is the difficulty. Answer length must match the mark allocation, and command terms decide what is wanted. Transport in plants, genetics and the human digestive and circulatory systems are the recurring weak topics across Dubai cohorts.

subjects.name: Coordinated Science (double award)
subjects.description: All three disciplines with reduced content in each, awarded as two IGCSEs. A sensible load for a student who needs science qualifications without three full syllabuses, but check the sixth-form policy before assuming it supports an A Level or Higher Level science.

subjects.name: Combined Science (single award)
subjects.description: All three disciplines in one IGCSE with the most reduced content. Appropriate where science is not the destination, and frequently insufficient as preparation for a post-16 science course. The decision should be made against the sixth-form requirement rather than against timetable convenience.

subjects.name: Alternative to practical
subjects.description: Experimental method assessed on paper: apparatus selection, control variables, instrument resolution, anomalous results, tabulation and graph work. A closed skill set, which makes it unusually teachable, and routinely the least practised paper in a school revision programme.

subjects.name: Qualitative analysis
subjects.description: Tests for cations, anions and gases with the observation each produces. Entirely recall, entirely predictable, and worth learning to blank recall rather than to recognition. Students who can only recognise the right answer in a list lose the marks when asked to state the test.

subjects.name: Graph and data skills
subjects.description: Choosing scales, plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit, reading intermediate values and calculating a gradient with units. Assessed in every science and in the alternative-to-practical paper, and improved faster than any content topic because it is procedural.

subjects.name: Calculation and unit handling
subjects.description: Rearranging formulae, standard form, prefixes and significant figures. Weakness here presents as a problem with whichever topic is current rather than as itself, which is why a diagnosis built on topics alone frequently misidentifies the cause.

subjects.name: Command terms across the sciences
subjects.description: 'State' takes a phrase with no working. 'Describe' takes what happens. 'Explain' takes why. 'Suggest' takes applied reasoning in an unfamiliar context. Mismatching these is the single largest category of avoidable loss across all three sciences and is teachable in about one session.

sections.heading: Separate, coordinated or combined: which one is your child on?
paragraphs: Ask the examinations officer for the board, the syllabus code and the tier for each science entry. The answer tells you how many IGCSEs are being awarded, how much content is being covered, and what doors remain open at sixteen. Families frequently assume they know and are wrong, because school communications tend to say 'science' where the entry says something more specific.

Separate sciences is three codes, three syllabuses and three IGCSEs: Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620, Biology 0610 on the Cambridge route. It is the heaviest option on any timetable and the only one that keeps an A Level or IB Higher Level science open without a conversation. Coordinated Science is a double award covering all three with reduced content in each, awarded as two IGCSEs. Combined Science is a single award with the most reduced content, awarded as one.

The policy at the receiving school is what matters, and it varies. Some sixth forms accept a double award for A Level Chemistry; some do not. Some will accept it conditionally with a bridging requirement. IB schools offering Higher Level sciences generally expect full content coverage, because the Diploma sciences move quickly from the first term and carry an internally assessed investigation worth 20% of the grade. The only way to know is to ask the school your child is likely to attend, in writing, before the Year 9 option form is signed.

On top of the route sits the tier, on the Cambridge separate sciences. Core covers less content and caps the grade, commonly at 5 on the 9-1 scale or C on the letter scale; Extended covers the full syllabus and reaches 9. A student entered for Core cannot be awarded above the cap however well they perform, and the entry decision sits with the school months before the examination.

sections.heading: The alternative-to-practical paper, properly
paragraphs: This component gets less revision attention than any other part of an IGCSE science entry, and the reason is simple: the theory papers carry more marks, so a school running out of time cuts the practical paper. The consequence is whole cohorts sitting a paper they have barely practised, losing marks on a skill set that could have been taught in four sessions with no new content involved.

What it assesses is experimental method expressed on paper. Choosing the right apparatus for a measurement and justifying it. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables in a described experiment. Judging the resolution of an instrument and the precision it permits. Constructing a results table with correct headings and units before any data is collected. Identifying an anomalous result and saying what to do about it. Plotting a graph to the scheme's tolerance, drawing a line of best fit, and reading an intermediate value accurately.

Every one of those is procedural and markable, which means it is teachable and testable. A student who has worked through eight real alternative-to-practical questions with the published schemes read afterwards will not be surprised by a ninth. A student who has worked through none is improvising on the day, usually with reasonable scientific instincts and no idea what the paper credits.

The other thing this component does is prepare a student for something later. The Diploma sciences carry an internally assessed investigation worth 20% of the grade, marked on research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The habits the alternative-to-practical paper rewards — defined variables, justified apparatus, honest treatment of anomalies, sensible precision — are the same habits that investigation credits. Work done here is not wasted at sixteen.

sections.heading: The recall content: qualitative analysis as a table
paragraphs: Chemistry 0620 contains a block of content that is pure memory, and it is the most efficient marks in the whole science entry. The tests for cations, anions and gases, with the observation each produces, appear in identification questions on every series. There is no reasoning to construct; there is a table to know. Students who revise it by recognition — reading the table and feeling familiar with it — cannot reproduce it under examination conditions, and lose marks they had every opportunity to hold.

The method is blank recall. The student writes the table from nothing, three or four times a week, and it is marked for completeness rather than for effort. Three to four weeks of that and it holds. The same approach applies to biology definitions, which are also marked against specific wording, and to the physics formulae that are not provided in the examination.

Why this gets neglected is worth naming. Recall work is dull, it does not feel like understanding, and both students and tutors prefer the satisfaction of explaining a concept. But an examination credits the right answer, and for identification questions the right answer is a remembered observation. A tutor who spends every session on explanation and never tests recall is giving the student the more enjoyable hour and the lower grade.

The table below is a working summary of the kind of content involved. It is there to show the shape of the task rather than to replace the official syllabus content, which should be taken from the current Cambridge syllabus document directly — we reference and link the awarding body's own material rather than reproducing it.

sections.heading: Where marks go in each science, and what it costs to fix
paragraphs: Loss patterns are consistent across Dubai cohorts, which means a marked script tells a specialist what to do within a few minutes. The useful output of a diagnosis is a list of habits with a session count against each, not a list of weak topics, because habits repeat on every paper and a topic list does not say what to do differently.

In Physics 0625 the recurring losses are circuits and electromagnetism, where students recall rules without applying them to the network in front of them; graph work, where gradients are read from plotted points rather than from the drawn line; and formula rearrangement under time pressure. In Chemistry 0620 it is moles arithmetic, ionic equations missing state symbols, and the recall content discussed above. In Biology 0610 it is command-term mismatch and answer length, where a student writes a paragraph for a two-mark question and then runs short of time.

Across all three the single largest avoidable category is command terms. 'State' wants a phrase. 'Describe' wants what happens. 'Explain' wants why. 'Suggest' wants reasoning applied to an unfamiliar context and is where the strongest students gain separation. A student who annotates the command term before writing changes their mark profile across every science paper, and it takes about one session to install as a habit.

sections.heading: What science tutoring costs in Dubai, and how to buy less of it
paragraphs: Three separate sciences is the most expensive subject block on an IGCSE timetable to support privately, and the useful question is not the hourly rate but how to need fewer hours. The answer usually involves buying the cheap components first: the alternative-to-practical block at four sessions, the recall programme at three or four weeks of short daily work, and the command-term habit at one session. Those three together typically cost less than a term of weekly content teaching and move more marks.

The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IGCSE and IB specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 including travel; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end.

Monthly, Bestimate's estimates for one weekly hour come to roughly AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or above for exam-year specialist support, with published packages around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. A family supporting all three sciences at a weekly hour each is therefore looking at three times those numbers, which is exactly why component-first buying matters.

One question worth asking any tutor who offers to cover all three sciences: which codes have you taught, and which have you marked. Many specialists cover two of the three to a high standard; few cover all three at Extended level with equal command of the mark schemes. Where one tutor genuinely covers two, continuity improves and the student repeats less context each week. Where they cannot, splitting is the better outcome even at the cost of a second slot.

sections.heading: The science examination calendar for a UAE candidate
paragraphs: Two things are worth getting right about the calendar, and both are commonly got wrong on pages aimed at UAE families. The first is which series applies. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, plus Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February/March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it and a revision plan built around a March window is built on a date that does not exist for them. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November.

The second is the zone rule. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and notes that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a student with three science entries plus everything else, a clash check against the wrong zone's timetable is a genuine risk. Get the zone from the examinations officer before printing anything.

Results timings give a sense of the lag. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the right habit is to open the live official timetable rather than to trust a restated date anywhere, including on this page.

Counted backwards, a science year looks like this: route and tier settled by the end of Year 10, full syllabus seen once by the autumn of Year 11, mocks in the winter, the alternative-to-practical block in the spring, recall programme running continuously from the spring, and full timed papers from the mock onwards with an error log kept throughout.

sections.heading: Format, scheduling and what we do not claim
paragraphs: A family supporting three sciences needs three slots, which makes the format question practical rather than philosophical. From Jumeirah Village Triangle, children at Sunmarke School or Arcadia Global School inside the community can take 16:30, and online sessions run to 21:00 on Gulf Standard Time, so three 45-minute sessions a week across different evenings is straightforward to arrange. A visiting tutor needing a two-hour minimum and finishing by about 18:30 cannot offer that shape for three subjects.

Home visits are nonetheless a legitimate choice for some students and the market provides them: AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table, up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. A younger student who needs an adult in the room, or one whose written method needs correcting as it is produced, is well served by presence. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE — that is an India-only service — so the comparison here is offered to inform rather than to argue.

Scheduling notes for this cluster. Families driving back from Motor City, Dubai Hills or the Dubailand schools usually want 17:30 or later. Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00 and often at 45 minutes, which suits recall work well. Mock weeks are generally paused, then resumed with a session spent reading the marked scripts, which for three sciences is the most informative hour of the year.

And the claims we do not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. We are not an examination centre and cannot enter a candidate; entries go through your school or an approved private-candidate centre. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit and have no UAE office. Separately, the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount appears here.
