process.title: Confirm the route, the codes and the tiers
process.description: One email to the examinations officer returns whether your child is on separate, coordinated or combined science, which codes, and which tier per entry. That answer determines how much content is being covered and what the grade ceiling is, and it is the prerequisite for any sensible plan.

process.title: Check the sixth-form policy in writing
process.description: Ask the school your child is likely to attend at sixteen whether the route they are on supports the post-16 sciences they may want. Policies differ on double and single awards, and a written answer in Year 9 is worth more than an assumption in Year 11.

process.title: Free diagnostic lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge spent reading the student's own errors across the sciences they are weakest in. The output is a list of habits with session counts, not a list of topics, because habits repeat on every paper and are what can be changed on a known timescale.

process.title: Buy the cheap components first
process.description: The command-term habit is one session. The alternative-to-practical block is four. The recall programme is three or four weeks of short daily work with weekly marking. Together these cost less than a term of content teaching and usually move more marks, which is why they come first.

process.title: Weekly slots reviewed on school marks
process.description: Separate sessions per science, 45 or 60 minutes, scheduled across different evenings around the JVT school run, with post-Iftar timing in Ramadan. Progress is judged on the school's next marked papers, read against the original diagnosis rather than against our own exercises.

whyPoints.title: The route question asked first
whyPoints.description: Separate sciences awards three IGCSEs with full content; coordinated two with less; combined one with least. That decision determines post-16 access and it is made in Year 9, so we ask about it before discussing any lessons.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper treated as a component
whyPoints.description: The alternative-to-practical paper assesses a closed set of procedural skills with no new content attached, and school revision programmes routinely reach it last. Four sessions covers it, and the habits it rewards also prepare a student for the Diploma investigation at sixteen.

whyPoints.title: Recall taught as recall
whyPoints.description: Qualitative analysis, biology definitions and the unprovided physics formulae are memory tasks. We test them to blank recall rather than recognition, because recognition does not survive an examination hall, and three to four weeks of short daily sets is enough.

whyPoints.title: Habits with session counts
whyPoints.description: The diagnosis names each habit and how long it takes to change: one session for command terms, two for ionic equations, three for circuit reasoning, four for the practical paper. That is a plan with an endpoint rather than an open commitment.

whyPoints.title: Component-first buying for three subjects
whyPoints.description: Supporting all three sciences weekly is the most expensive block on an IGCSE timetable. We tell families to buy the cheap components first because it costs less and moves more marks, even though it bills less than a term of content teaching.

faqs.question: Is my child taking one science IGCSE or three?
faqs.answer: Ask the examinations officer, because school communications often say 'science' where the entry is more specific. Separate sciences means three IGCSEs on three codes: Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 on the Cambridge route, each with a full syllabus. Coordinated Science is a double award covering all three with reduced content, giving two IGCSEs. Combined Science is a single award with the most reduced content, giving one. The number matters for the certificate and the content matters for what a sixth form will accept at sixteen.

faqs.question: Will a double award science get my child into A Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the only reliable answer comes from the school your child will attend. Policies genuinely differ: some sixth forms accept a coordinated double award for an A Level science, some refuse it, and some accept it conditionally with a bridging requirement. IB schools offering Higher Level sciences generally expect full content coverage because the Diploma sciences move fast from the first term and carry an internally assessed investigation worth 20%. Get the policy in writing during Year 9, while the option form can still be changed.

faqs.question: What is actually on the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Experimental method expressed on paper. Choosing and justifying apparatus by its resolution and range. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables in a described experiment. Judging the precision an instrument permits. Constructing a results table with correct headings and units. Identifying an anomalous result and stating what to do about it. Plotting a graph to the scheme's tolerance, drawing a line of best fit and reading intermediate values or a gradient from the line rather than from plotted points. It is a closed skill set and four sessions normally covers all of it.

faqs.question: Why does my child know the chemistry tests but still lose the marks?
faqs.answer: Because they know them by recognition rather than by recall. A student who reads the qualitative analysis table and feels familiar with it cannot reproduce the reagent and the observation when asked to state a test with nothing in front of them. The method that works is blank recall: write the whole table from nothing, three or four times a week, marked for completeness. Three to four weeks of that and it holds under examination conditions. The same applies to biology definitions, which are credited against specific wording, and to unprovided physics formulae.

faqs.question: Which science do Dubai students most often need help with?
faqs.answer: Physics 0625, usually, and specifically electricity and electromagnetism, where students recall the rules without applying them to the circuit in the question. Chemistry 0620 comes second, on moles arithmetic and ionic equations missing state symbols. Biology 0610 generates fewer enquiries but a particular pattern: answer length not matched to the mark allocation, so time runs short on later questions. Across all three, command-term mismatch is the largest avoidable category and it is teachable in roughly one session plus a fortnight of marked practice.

faqs.question: Can one tutor teach all three sciences at Extended level?
faqs.answer: Many specialists cover two of the three to a high standard; few cover all three at Extended with equal command of the mark schemes. Where one tutor genuinely covers two, continuity improves and the student spends less time re-explaining context each week. Where they cannot, splitting across two tutors is the better outcome even though it costs a second slot. Ask directly which codes a tutor has taught and which they have marked, and treat a general answer about being good at science as a no.

faqs.question: How do we support three sciences without paying for three weekly hours?
faqs.answer: Buy the components rather than the subjects. The command-term habit is one session. The alternative-to-practical block is four and covers the practical paper for all three sciences at once in method terms. The recall programme is three or four weeks of short daily work with weekly marking. Those three together cost less than a term of weekly content teaching in one subject and typically move more marks. Weekly content support is then reserved for the single science where the marked work shows a genuine content gap.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor come to the house in Jumeirah Village Triangle?
faqs.answer: Independent tutors and agencies in Dubai do, at AED 180-350 an hour on Bestimate's 2026 rate table and up to about AED 500 for independent home tutors with travel included. IB Gram does not, anywhere in the UAE. For a family supporting three sciences the scheduling arithmetic favours the online format strongly: three 45-minute sessions across different evenings, with starts from 16:30 and slots to 21:00, against a visiting tutor's two-hour minimum and a realistic finish by about 18:30.

faqs.question: Is Core tier science a problem if my child wants a science A Level?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, because of the ceiling. A Cambridge Core entry is commonly capped at grade 5 on the 9-1 scale or C on the letter scale, and an A Level science typically asks for grade 6 or 7. No performance lifts a result above the cap, so the entry closes the door before the paper is sat. The entry decision sits with the school on internal evidence and closes months before the series, which is why a Year 10 block of marked Extended-standard questions is the useful response rather than a Year 11 conversation.

faqs.question: Which series will my child sit for IGCSE science in the UAE?
faqs.answer: June or November on the Cambridge route, and May/June or November on the Pearson route. The February/March series is offered to India only, so no UAE candidate sits it, and any plan built around a March examination window is built on a date that does not apply. Cambridge also runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which is a different assessment entirely and is sometimes what has been half-remembered. Confirm the series and the entry with the examinations officer.

faqs.question: How does the Cambridge zone timetable affect three science entries?
faqs.answer: It raises the stakes on a clash check. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and notes it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A student with three science entries plus everything else has more papers to coordinate, so checking against the wrong zone's timetable is a real risk. Ask the examinations officer which zone the centre is in before printing a timetable.

faqs.question: Does the alternative-to-practical work help later in the IB?
faqs.answer: Directly. The Diploma sciences each carry an internally assessed scientific investigation worth 20% of the grade, marked out of 24 across research design, data analysis, conclusion and evaluation. The habits the alternative-to-practical paper rewards are the same ones that investigation credits: variables defined and justified, apparatus chosen for its resolution, anomalies treated honestly, precision quoted sensibly, graphs drawn and read properly. A student who took that paper seriously at sixteen arrives in DP1 able to design an investigation rather than learning how during one.

faqs.question: How much should a Dubai family budget for one science subject per term?
faqs.answer: At published market bands, twelve weekly sessions over a term comes to roughly AED 1,800-3,600 at the AED 150-300 qualified band and AED 2,400-5,400 at the AED 200-450 specialist band. Three sciences at that frequency triples those figures, which is why component-first buying matters. Published packages in this market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. Those are other providers' figures read in October 2026. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27.

faqs.question: Can sessions shift during Ramadan or a mock week?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for three sciences both are worth planning at the start of term. During Ramadan sessions move to post-Iftar timing, typically 20:30 to 22:00 on Gulf Standard Time and often at 45 minutes, which suits recall work particularly well because short and frequent is the right shape for it. Through a school mock week most families pause teaching and keep one session to read the marked scripts across all three sciences, which is usually the most informative hour of the year. Every session is recorded, so a pause costs nothing.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-vi.closingHeading: Route first, components second, content last
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-jumeirah-vi.closingBody: Science is the subject block where buying in the right order saves the most. Find out whether your child is on three separate sciences, a double award or a single one, and check in writing whether that route supports the post-16 sciences they may want. dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-karama.tutorsIntro: These tutors teach IGCSE biology, chemistry and physics on Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses, across separate sciences and the combined and co-ordinated routes. Each starts from the syllabus code on the entry and marks against the published scheme.

intro.heading: Four different qualifications all called science
paragraphs: Ask ten Karama parents what their child is studying for science at IGCSE and most will say science. Ask the school and the answer will be one of four quite different things. Three separate subjects, each with its own syllabus code and its own papers. A co-ordinated sciences course that covers all three disciplines in one qualification worth a single grade. A combined science course covering less content for a single grade. Or a double award covering all three for two grades. These are not interchangeable, the papers differ, and revision material for the wrong one is money spent on confusion.

The board matters as much as the route. Cambridge biology is 0610, chemistry 0620 and physics 0625, with co-ordinated sciences at 0654 and combined science at 0653. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the separate subjects and a double award option. The content overlaps substantially between the boards, but the paper structures, the formulae supplied and the way practical skills are assessed differ, which is exactly where marks are won and lost. A tutor who does not ask for the code is planning from guesswork.

Then there is the tier. Cambridge separates Core and Extended; Pearson's separate sciences are untiered while other routes differ. The lower tier caps the attainable grade, and in this belt a student is sometimes sitting Core because a class was split in Year 9 and nobody revisited the decision. If a tier change is still possible, that is the most consequential conversation available to a family this term, and it has an administrative deadline attached rather than an academic one.

The fourth variable is the practical component, and it is the one parents understand least. Cambridge assesses practical skills either by a practical test or by an alternative-to-practical written paper, and schools choose. That choice changes revision completely: the alternative-to-practical paper is a written examination about experiments, rewarding precise language about variables, apparatus and sources of error rather than laboratory dexterity. Students who are strong in the laboratory and weak at writing about it lose marks there routinely.

Once those four facts are settled, the teaching is specific rather than general. Biology marks are lost to command words and imprecise terminology. Chemistry marks are lost to moles, state symbols and significant figures. Physics marks are lost to rearrangement, units and graph gradients. Each science fails in its own way, and a tutor covering all three for a co-ordinated candidate has to teach three different sets of habits rather than one general approach to science.

What follows is the detail: the routes compared, the papers, the practical component, the command words, and the specific traps in each discipline. Lessons are delivered one to one, live online. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-karama.programmesIntro: Science at IGCSE in this belt is entered in several different ways, and students arrive from several different places. These are the stages a science tutor works across around Karama.

programmes.name: Separate sciences: biology, chemistry and physics
programmes.description: Three qualifications, three grades. Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625; Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Each has its own content, its own papers and its own practical assessment arrangement. This is the route schools use for students heading towards A Level or Diploma sciences, and it carries the most content of the four routes by a considerable margin.
programmes.countryNote: Separate sciences take three option slots, which in a nine-subject timetable squeezes everything else. Families in this belt sometimes discover in Year 11 that the workload is unsustainable alongside additional mathematics. Reviewing the subject count at the end of Year 10, with marked evidence, is more useful than reviewing it in March.

programmes.name: Co-ordinated sciences
programmes.description: Cambridge 0654: all three disciplines in one qualification worth a single grade, covering roughly two thirds of the separate-science content. It occupies two option slots rather than three and remains acceptable for many post-16 science routes, though the receiving school's own entry requirement decides that. Papers assess all three disciplines, so a weakness in one pulls the single grade down.
programmes.countryNote: The hidden risk in co-ordinated sciences is a student who is strong in biology and weak in physics. One grade means the weak discipline drags the whole result, and schools report progress by discipline rarely enough that parents sometimes do not see it coming. Ask for discipline-level marks from the last internal assessment.

programmes.name: Combined science and double award routes
programmes.description: Cambridge 0653 combined science covers all three disciplines for a single grade with less content again, taking one option slot. Pearson offers a double award covering all three for two grades. Both suit students whose strengths sit elsewhere, and both can restrict post-16 science options, so the decision needs checking against where the student intends to go.
programmes.countryNote: Before choosing a reduced-content route, ask the post-16 destination for its own published entry requirement for A Level or Diploma sciences. Guidance varies noticeably between Dubai schools even within the same curriculum, and a route that is acceptable at one is not always acceptable at the next.

programmes.name: MYP sciences, as the alternative route to sixteen
programmes.description: The IB continuum alternative, assessed on four criteria out of eight each rather than by terminal examination. Students transferring from MYP into an IGCSE science cohort usually bring strong investigation skills and weaker timed-paper technique, because MYP assessment is not built around an examination at the end.
programmes.countryNote: A mid-course transfer into Year 11 IGCSE science from MYP needs a fast audit of specific content the student has never met, particularly on the Extended tier. In chemistry the usual gap is quantitative work; in physics it is rearrangement and electrical circuits.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-karama.subjectsIntro: Science at IGCSE is three disciplines plus the practical component, and students in this belt usually need help in one or two rather than all three. These are the subjects our IGCSE specialists cover.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy and terminology-sensitive. Marks are lost to command words and to imprecise language: a student who writes that something gets bigger where the scheme wants increases in surface area loses marks they understood the biology for.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, concentration, titration arithmetic, electrolysis and organic families. The recoverable marks sit in state symbols, significant figures and applying a ratio from the balanced equation to the right species rather than the convenient one.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Forces, electricity, waves, thermal physics and magnetism. Marks go to rearrangement done correctly, units stated, and gradients read from a best-fit line rather than from two adjacent data points.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: All three disciplines in one grade. Tutoring here has to be triaged by discipline, because the single grade is pulled down by whichever discipline is weakest and that is usually visible in marked work long before it shows in a report.

subjects.name: Combined Science
subjects.description: Reduced content across all three disciplines for one grade. The right objective is usually securing every accessible mark rather than stretch work, because most of the paper's marks sit in straightforward recall and simple calculation.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The hidden prerequisite for science marks. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and percentage work and graph skills are all examined inside science papers, so weak mathematics costs marks twice.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Taken by some students heading for A Level sciences. It introduces calculus and more advanced trigonometry early, and its workload needs sequencing against three separate sciences rather than stacked on top of them.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Binary, logic gates and pseudocode tracing. Students who enjoy the systematic side of physics often take it well, and the data-representation content overlaps with number work in mathematics.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Data response and graph interpretation marked much as the science data questions are, so graph skills built for science transfer here. Case-study specificity is what separates grades.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The transferable skill with science is reading what was actually asked and allocating time by marks available. Students who over-write cheap questions in English do the same thing in a science paper.

sections.heading: Which science qualification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the first question and it decides everything downstream. A school can enter a student for separate sciences, giving three grades from three syllabuses; for Cambridge co-ordinated sciences 0654, giving one grade across all three disciplines at roughly two thirds of the separate content; for Cambridge combined science 0653, giving one grade with less content again; or for a double award covering all three disciplines for two grades. Each route has a different paper structure and a different content load.

The differences have consequences beyond revision. Separate sciences occupy three option slots, which in a nine-subject timetable is a significant commitment and is the usual reason a Year 11 workload becomes unmanageable. Co-ordinated sciences occupy two and remain acceptable for many post-16 science routes, though that is decided by the receiving school's published entry requirement rather than by a general rule. Combined science occupies one and can close doors that a family did not know were open.

The risk specific to the single-grade routes is concentration. With one grade covering three disciplines, a student who is strong in biology and weak in physics has their whole science result pulled down by the weak discipline, and schools report by discipline rarely enough that this can arrive as a surprise in a mock result. The remedy is simple and worth doing this term: ask for discipline-level marks from the last internal assessment rather than an overall science grade.

For a tutor the practical consequence is that session time cannot be split evenly. A co-ordinated candidate losing forty marks in physics and eight in biology should not be having one session each. Our tutors start with a full past paper from the correct syllabus, marked and broken down by discipline, then allocate the block in proportion to the marks actually available. That sounds obvious and it is the opposite of how all-three science tutoring is usually sold.

sections.heading: The papers, the tiers, and the practical component schools choose
paragraphs: Cambridge science syllabuses are tiered into Core and Extended, with the Core tier capping the attainable grade. Pearson's separate sciences are structured differently. A student entered for Core cannot reach the top grades, and in this belt that entry is sometimes a leftover from a Year 9 class split rather than a current judgement. If a tier change is still administratively possible, that conversation beats any amount of revision planning, and it has a school deadline attached that usually falls earlier than the board's.

The practical component is the part families understand least and it changes revision completely. Cambridge assesses practical skills either through a practical test or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses which. Where the alternative paper applies, the examination is written: it asks about variables, apparatus, measurement precision, sources of error and how to describe a method someone else could repeat. Laboratory confidence is not what is being tested; precise written description is.

That distinction produces a specific and common failure. A student who is competent and confident in the laboratory, who gets good results and enjoys practical work, can score poorly on the alternative-to-practical paper because they have never been taught to write about an experiment in the language the scheme rewards. Naming the independent, dependent and control variables precisely, justifying an apparatus choice by the precision it offers, and distinguishing a source of error from a mistake are all taught skills with predictable question styles.

Because they are bounded and predictable, these are among the best-value tutoring sessions available in IGCSE science. A student who cannot touch these questions at the start of a short block will usually answer them competently after three or four focused sessions on real past papers. The same is not true of a genuine content gap across a whole discipline, which is why our tutors front-load the practical component in a run-in and tackle content gaps in order of marks available afterwards.

sections.heading: Command words: the single cheapest source of recovered marks in science
paragraphs: Science papers are written around command words, and a student who answers in the wrong shape loses marks on content they knew. State wants a bare fact with no reasoning. Describe wants what happens, in order, with no causes. Explain wants causes, with the word because doing real work. Suggest wants a plausible answer applied to an unfamiliar context, and is marked generously provided the science is sound. Compare wants both sides in the same sentence. Calculate wants the working shown.

The commonest expensive error is describing where the scheme asked for an explanation. A student writes a fluent paragraph about what the graph does and earns no marks, because every mark on offer was for why. The second commonest is answering suggest questions as though they were recall questions, which produces a blank where a reasoned guess from the given information would have scored. The third is giving one side of a comparison.

This is drillable in two sessions and it does not require any new science. Take twenty real past-paper stems from the correct board, identify the command word in each, write the required shape of answer without doing the science, then check against the published scheme. Students find it tedious and the marks move faster than they do for any content work, which is why our tutors do it early in a block rather than saving it for revision.

Terminology sits alongside command words, particularly in biology. Mark schemes award specific words: diffusion rather than moves, surface area rather than size, enzyme rather than chemical. A student who understands the biology perfectly and writes it in everyday language loses marks steadily across a whole paper, and the fix is a vocabulary discipline built through marked practice rather than a reading list.

sections.heading: Three disciplines, three different failure modes
paragraphs: Treating science as one subject is the mistake that wastes tutoring hours. Biology, chemistry and physics fail differently at IGCSE, and a tutor who teaches all three for a co-ordinated candidate has to switch habits as well as content between them.

Biology fails on language and volume. The content is large, mostly recall, and marked against specific terminology, so the student who loses marks here is usually not confused about the biology but imprecise in writing it. Alongside that sits the data-handling element: graph reading, table interpretation and drawing a conclusion that the data actually supports. Both are fixed by marked practice rather than by rereading notes, and rereading notes is what most students default to because it feels like revision.

Chemistry fails on quantitative work. Moles, concentration, titration arithmetic, percentage yield and empirical formulae are where the available marks concentrate, and the errors are specific: a ratio taken from an unbalanced equation, moles applied to the wrong species, state symbols omitted, significant figures carried wrongly, a unit left off a concentration. Each of those is a habit. A student who fixes the habits usually recovers more marks than one who rereads the periodic table trends.

Physics fails on mathematics. Rearranging an equation where the subject is not already isolated, converting between units and prefixes, reading a gradient from a best-fit line rather than from two adjacent points, and stating a unit with every numerical answer. Students who relied on a formula triangle at Year 9 hit this wall in Year 11, and it reads as a physics problem while being an algebra problem. Diagnosing which of the three disciplines is actually costing the marks, and why, is the work of the first session rather than the tenth.

sections.heading: Graphs, tables and calculations: the skills shared across all three sciences
paragraphs: A cluster of skills appears in every science paper regardless of discipline, and improving them moves marks in biology, chemistry and physics at once. That makes them the most efficient thing to teach a co-ordinated or separate-science candidate who is short of time, and they are routinely compressed out of a crowded school year.

Graph work comes first. Plotting points accurately, choosing a scale that uses the grid, drawing a line that fits the data rather than connecting the first and last points, labelling both axes with quantity and unit, and reading a gradient from two widely separated points on the line. Each of those carries marks and each is mechanically checkable. A student who loses a mark per graph question across three sciences is losing more than most content gaps cost them.

Table and data interpretation comes second. Reading a value correctly from a table with mixed units, spotting a trend and stating it in the direction the question asked, identifying an anomalous result and saying why it is anomalous rather than simply that it is. The discipline here is to answer the question asked rather than the question the student expected, which in data questions is a frequent and expensive divergence.

Calculation discipline comes third and overlaps with mathematics. Show the substitution before the answer. Carry full precision through intermediate steps and round once at the end. State the unit. Use an appropriate number of significant figures rather than everything the calculator displayed. Convert prefixes carefully, especially between milli, micro and kilo. None of this is science, all of it is marked in science papers, and all of it can be fixed in a handful of sessions with marked practice.

sections.heading: The series, the deadlines and what a short run-in can realistically do
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit IGCSE sciences in two series: June and November. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for international candidates and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, stating plainly that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026.

Results arrive long after the papers, and that gap drives the resit decision. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Because the window between a result and the next entry deadline is short, a November resit has to be considered before the June result lands rather than after it. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so every date should be checked against the board's live official timetable rather than a saved copy.

With a short run-in — six to ten weeks — a science plan has to be built backwards from the papers. Week one is a full past paper from the correct syllabus and tier, marked and split by discipline, producing a breakdown of marks lost to content, to command words, to calculation and to the practical component. Those four categories have four different remedies, and the proportions decide everything that follows.

What a short block can do is recover accessible marks: command-word technique, calculation discipline, graph skills and the practical paper's written language. What it cannot do is teach a discipline from scratch, which is why a co-ordinated candidate who has effectively not learned physics is a different proposition from one who has learned it and keeps losing marks. We will say which case we think yours is after the diagnostic rather than before it.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tutoring costs around Karama, counted three ways
paragraphs: Science is where the per-subject arithmetic bites, because a family helping with all three disciplines is buying three times as much tutoring as a family helping with one. Published Dubai rates divide by tier. Budget online tutoring runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya quoting from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors working online are quoted at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. IGCSE and IB specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table giving AED 200 to AED 450 and upwards.

Counted monthly, Bestimate's estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 mid-band and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist examination-year work. Packages advertised in Dubai include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. In-home one-to-one is quoted separately at AED 180 to AED 350 by Bestimate, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500, because travel is priced inside the hour.

Counted by discipline, the sensible approach for most Karama families is narrower than three tutors. Start with the discipline the marked work identifies as weakest, run six weeks, measure, and only then decide whether a second is needed. A family paying mid-band rates for one discipline for twelve weeks usually gets more movement than one paying budget rates for three disciplines for four weeks, because single-discipline work can go deep enough to change habits rather than merely covering ground.

What a parent can check for themselves is the useful filter. Ask which syllabus code and tier the tutor has taught and when. Ask them to mark one data question or one calculation from your child's last paper and explain where each mark went. Ask whether the school enters students for the practical test or the alternative paper, and whether the tutor has prepared candidates for that specific component. A tutor who answers those three well is worth the mid-band rate. For IB Gram's own arrangements, start with the free trial lesson and the consultation.

sections.heading: Why a science tutor does not need to be in the room, even without a laboratory
paragraphs: The objection families raise about online science tutoring is the laboratory, and it is worth answering directly. A private tutor does not provide laboratory access in any delivery model. A visiting tutor in a Karama flat has no fume cupboard, no data logger and no supply of standard solutions either. The practical component is prepared by the school in its own laboratory, and where the school enters students for the alternative-to-practical paper, the examination itself is written rather than practical.

That reframes the comparison. What science tutoring actually needs is a shared surface where graphs can be drawn and corrected, a way to send a script for marking and get it back annotated, and the ability to work through a past paper question by question with the mark scheme alongside. A tablet and a shared whiteboard do all three better than two people over one exercise book, and the annotated work is retained rather than lost in a margin.

The pool argument applies here as strongly as anywhere. A Karama family hiring someone who can attend is choosing from tutors living nearby and free at the student's hour. For Extended-tier physics on a specific Pearson specification, prepared for the alternative-to-practical paper, that is a narrow requirement and the local pool may contain nobody who meets it. Online changes the constraint from postcode to diary. The in-home band is also higher, at AED 180 to AED 500 against AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified online tutor, and in this neighbourhood that premium buys a short drive.

The honest exception is a younger or very distractible student, where someone physically present helps in a way video does not replicate. For a Year 10 or Year 11 candidate working to a fixed series date it rarely decides anything. IB Gram does not offer in-home visits anywhere in the UAE — home tutoring is a service we provide only in India — so where a child genuinely needs a person in the room, we will say so rather than sell an online session as a substitute.

sections.heading: Permits, materials and the limits we work inside
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is lawful and regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via the smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit face fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific amount quoted is unverified.

Dubai's private schools are regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which on the UAE government's own description is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA also requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, organised in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, with instructional time calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit and a recommendation that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes. For a science tutoring plan this is timetable arithmetic: the free hours in a Year 11 week are fewer than a subject list suggests.

No permit or regulator is an endorsement of anybody. IB Gram is not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge or Pearson. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation for training institutes operating premises in Dubai, which we neither hold nor claim. We do not describe tutors as examiners without evidence of current status, and examiner status gives nobody access to marking decisions, boundaries or unseen papers.

On materials and outcomes the limits are firm. We will not supply Cambridge or Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads, because they belong to the boards; a tutor references them, teaches from them in a session and points you at the official source. We will not predict a grade, though a specialist will tell you which of the four mark-loss categories is currently costing most and what looks reachable. And we will not complete any assessed work for a student.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science route my child is on?
faqs.answer: Ask the school for the entry confirmation with syllabus codes, not for a subject list. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610 biology, 0620 chemistry and 0625 physics; co-ordinated sciences is 0654 and combined science 0653. Pearson separate sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with a double award option. Also ask for the tier and whether the school enters students for the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper. Those details decide which past papers are useful, and revision material bought for the wrong route is money spent on confusion.

faqs.question: Co-ordinated Sciences versus separate sciences: which one is my Karama child taking?
faqs.answer: Co-ordinated sciences, Cambridge 0654, covers all three disciplines in one qualification worth a single grade, at roughly two thirds of the separate-science content, and occupies two option slots. Separate sciences give three grades from three syllabuses and occupy three slots with considerably more content. Co-ordinated remains acceptable for many post-16 science routes, but the receiving school's own published entry requirement decides that rather than any general rule, so ask the destination directly before treating it as equivalent.

faqs.question: My child is strong in biology and weak in physics. Does that matter on one grade?
faqs.answer: A great deal, and it is the specific risk of the single-grade routes. With one grade covering all three disciplines, the weakest discipline pulls the whole result down, and schools report by discipline rarely enough that this sometimes first appears in a mock result. Ask for discipline-level marks from the last internal assessment rather than an overall science grade. Tutoring should then be weighted towards the weak discipline in proportion to the marks actually being lost, not split evenly across three subjects.

faqs.question: What is the alternative-to-practical paper and how is it revised?
faqs.answer: It is a written examination about experiments, used where a school chooses it instead of a practical test. It asks about independent, dependent and control variables, apparatus choice and the precision it offers, sources of error as distinct from mistakes, and how to describe a method another person could repeat. Laboratory confidence is not what is tested; precise written description is, which is why students who enjoy practical work sometimes score poorly. It is a bounded body of technique with predictable question styles and it responds quickly to focused practice.

faqs.question: Which command word costs IGCSE science students the most marks?
faqs.answer: Explain, because students answer it as though it said describe. A fluent paragraph about what a graph does earns nothing when every mark on offer was for why it does it. Suggest is a close second: students leave it blank because the answer was not in their notes, when the question rewards reasoning from the information given. Comparisons lose half their marks when only one side is given. Drilling twenty real past-paper stems for the command word, without doing the science, moves marks faster than content revision.

faqs.question: Why does my child lose marks in chemistry calculations they say they understand?
faqs.answer: Usually one of five specific habits. Taking a ratio from an equation that was not balanced. Calculating moles correctly then applying them to the wrong species. Omitting state symbols. Carrying significant figures wrongly from a titration. Leaving the unit off a concentration. Each of those is a habit rather than a knowledge gap, and each is found by marking the student's own script against the published scheme rather than by revising the topic. Rebuilding mole reasoning from limiting-reagent problems, rather than from a memorised formula, fixes most of them.

faqs.question: Is physics actually a maths problem for most IGCSE students?
faqs.answer: For a large share of lost marks, yes. Rearranging an equation where the subject is not already isolated, converting between prefixes, reading a gradient from a best-fit line rather than two adjacent points, and stating a unit with every answer are mathematics skills marked inside a physics paper. Students who relied on a formula triangle in Year 9 hit this in Year 11, and it presents as weakness in physics. Twenty equations rearranged for every variable, drilled over two or three sessions, removes most of the friction.

faqs.question: Should we hire one tutor for all three sciences or one at a time?
faqs.answer: Start with one, chosen from marked evidence. Six weeks deep on the weakest discipline usually moves more marks than four weeks spread thinly across three, because the failures are discipline-specific habits and habits only change with depth. It is also cheaper: three disciplines at once simply triples the hourly figure, and nothing about that arithmetic is a discount. Add a second discipline when the first has moved in raw marks, and treat all-three triage as a decision for a co-ordinated candidate with a genuinely even spread of weakness.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science series will my child in Karama sit?
faqs.answer: June or November. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for international candidates and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, with the zone deciding which version of the timetable applies; Cambridge states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's timetable. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. The February series some providers mention is offered to India only.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE science results arrive and is a resit worth planning early?
faqs.answer: Plan it before the result arrives. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. The window between a result and the next entry deadline is short, so a resit decision made after results has already lost time. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and revises them, so confirm every date against the board's live official timetable rather than a copy saved from a previous year.

faqs.answer: Published rates divide by tier rather than by neighbourhood. Budget online tutoring is advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik at AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. Qualified subject tutors online are quoted at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, TutorChase listing AED 270. faqs.question: Can online science tutoring work without a laboratory?
faqs.answer: Yes, because no private tutor provides laboratory access in any delivery model. A visiting tutor in a Karama flat has no fume cupboard or data logger either. Practical work belongs to the school, and where the school enters students for the alternative-to-practical paper the examination itself is written. What tutoring needs is a shared surface for graphs, annotated script marking between sessions and the ability to work through a past paper with the scheme alongside, all of which online delivery does well and retains afterwards.

faqs.question: Is it too late to start science tutoring eight weeks before the papers?
faqs.answer: No, with the plan built backwards from the examination. Week one is a full past paper from the correct syllabus and tier, marked and split by discipline, giving a breakdown of marks lost to content, command words, calculation and the practical component. Weeks two to five address those in order of marks available; weeks six to eight are full timed papers with review focused only on marks lost. What eight weeks cannot do is teach a discipline from scratch, so the realistic target is recovering accessible marks rather than moving the ceiling.

Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Applications go through MoHRE's own private tutor licensing service. Ask any tutor directly whether they hold it. Tutoring without one carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, although no fine schedule has been published.

Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, and distributing them as downloads is someone else's copyright handed to you. A tutor references them, works from them inside a session and points you at the official source so you can obtain them properly. We also will not predict a grade, though a specialist will tell you which mark-loss category is currently costing most, and we will not complete any assessed work for a student.

intro.heading: Three sciences, two award structures, and one decision that caps everything
paragraphs: The first thing to establish when a family searches for an IGCSE science tutor in Dubai Knowledge Park is which award structure the student is on. Triple award means three separate qualifications - biology, chemistry and physics, each with its own syllabus code and its own grade. Double award, Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award, means all three disciplines at reduced depth producing two grades. Single award produces one. Those are different qualifications with different post-16 consequences, and the choice was usually made in Year 9.

That decision is the one worth checking before any tutoring money is spent, because it sets a ceiling nothing else can lift. A Diploma Higher Level science or an A Level science normally expects the separate subject at IGCSE, and departments in this belt are frequently reluctant to accept a double-award student into Higher Level chemistry or physics. A student who intends to apply for medicine, engineering or any health-science route and who is sitting double award has a problem that is structural rather than academic.

Once the award structure is settled, the three sciences need separating rather than treating as one. Biology fails on content volume and on specification vocabulary - a correct answer in everyday words frequently scores nothing because the mark scheme lists the term. Chemistry fails on mole calculations and on the qualitative analysis tables, with organic taught last and revised least. Physics fails on electricity and on anything requiring an equation to be rearranged under time pressure, which is a maths weakness presenting as a physics grade.

There is a fourth component families almost never plan for. Cambridge assesses practical skills either through a practical test or through an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on the syllabus and the centre, and Pearson assesses practical skills within the written papers in several subjects. The written practical component is a writing skill as much as a science one - describing a method precisely, identifying variables, reading apparatus to the right precision - and it is marked generously for students who have practised it and harshly for those who have not.

Knowledge Park itself is an education free zone off Al Sufouh Road, with university campuses and training institutes rather than homes, so families running this search live in Al Sufouh, Media City, Barsha Heights, The Greens or the Marina towers. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor attending a UAE address is a service we run only in India. For three sciences that matters in a specific way: a single visiting tutor rarely covers all three well, while an online match can put a chemistry specialist and a physics specialist on the same timetable without anyone driving anywhere.

sections.heading: Triple award against double award: what the entry actually caps
paragraphs: This is the decision that matters most and gets examined least. Triple award means three separate syllabuses with three separate grades: biology, chemistry and physics. Double award - Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson's Science Double Award - covers all three disciplines at reduced depth and produces two grades. Single award produces one. The content coverage differs substantially, and so does what each one opens at sixteen.

The consequence lands at post-16 entry. A Level chemistry and physics departments, and Diploma Higher Level sciences, generally expect the separate subject, and many in this belt are reluctant to admit double-award students at all. Where they do, the student arrives with materially thinner content coverage and less practical experience, and the first term closes that gap at speed while also teaching new material. A student aiming at medicine, dentistry, pharmacy or engineering with double award has a structural problem rather than an academic one.

The decision can still be revisited, and the window is Year 10 into very early Year 11. It moves on evidence rather than argument: a timed separate-science paper sat cold, marked strictly, with a topic-level breakdown of the gap and a realistic estimate of the weeks needed to close it. Schools respond to that far better than to parental conviction, and timetabling constraints mean the request has to be made while a place can still be created.

If the award structure is right for the student, that is worth hearing too. A secure pair of strong double-award grades serves a student heading for humanities or business far better than three mediocre separate-science grades, and the timetable space freed up can be spent on subjects that actually matter to the application. sections.heading: The papers, by syllabus code, and the practical component nobody plans for
paragraphs: Parents in this catchment frequently do not know which board or which papers their child's science departments use, and in a triple-award timetable there can be different answers for different subjects. The syllabus code is the thing to collect: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 for the separate sciences, 0654 for Co-ordinated Sciences, or the Pearson equivalents 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Revision guides, past papers and mark schemes are code-specific, and buying for the wrong one produces work without marks.

Within a Cambridge science syllabus the paper structure is tiered. Core candidates sit one multiple-choice paper and one theory paper; Extended candidates sit the harder versions of both. Then comes the practical component, and this is where centres differ: some enter candidates for the practical test, others for the alternative-to-practical written paper. The two require different preparation, and a student who has prepared for the wrong one has prepared for nothing.

The alternative-to-practical paper is the most under-prepared component in IGCSE science. It asks a student to describe a method precisely, identify independent, dependent and control variables, read apparatus to the correct resolution, spot a flaw in a described procedure, and suggest an improvement. All of that is precision writing applied to science, and the mark schemes are specific about the words that earn marks. Students who have practised it score well; students who assume laboratory experience is enough do not.

Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers in several subjects rather than through a separate paper, which changes the preparation but not the underlying skill. For any family considering a period of online schooling or entry as a private candidate, the practical arrangements are the decisive difference between the two boards and should be checked before a move rather than after.

sections.heading: Where each science drains marks, and why it is usually not three problems
paragraphs: A report showing three weak science grades looks like three problems and is usually one and a half. The common factor is quantitative: proportion, rearrangement, standard form, unit conversion and graph reading are examined inside all three sciences, and a student weak there loses marks everywhere and concludes they are bad at science. Testing it takes five minutes - hand over an unfamiliar formula and ask for a given symbol to be made the subject, with no science attached.

Beyond that shared weakness, each science has its own signature. Biology loses marks to specification vocabulary: the mark scheme lists the term, and a biologically correct answer in everyday language scores nothing. It also loses marks to content volume, because there is simply more to know than in the other two and revision tends to be broad and shallow. The fix is active recall against the specification itself rather than re-reading notes.

Chemistry loses marks to the mole system and to the qualitative analysis tables, which are a memorisation task that students keep deferring. Organic is taught last and revised least. Physics loses marks to electricity - circuit analysis on an unfamiliar network, where students have learned worked examples instead of a reduction method - and to graph interpretation, where a gradient is calculated correctly and its physical meaning never stated.

The practical consequence is an order of operations. Fix the quantitative weakness first, because it pays in all three subjects at once. Then take the science where the marked paper shows the cheapest marks available. Then the next. A plan that works on all three sciences simultaneously produces six hours of tuition a week, which is more than any Year 11 can absorb alongside a full timetable, and the first casualty is the independent practice that makes tutoring work at all.

sections.heading: Command terms and the six-mark questions, across all three sciences
paragraphs: The extended-response questions at the end of a science paper carry a disproportionate share of the volatile marks, and they are lost for reasons that have nothing to do with science knowledge. A student who knows the content writes everything they know in the order it occurs to them, and the mark scheme awards points for specific linked statements that may or may not appear. Structure, not content, is what separates two marks from five.

The command terms are a closed list and they behave consistently. 'State' wants a single fact with no elaboration. 'Describe' wants what happens, in sequence. 'Explain' wants why, in causal steps - and an explanation delivered as a description sits in the lower band however accurate it is. 'Compare' wants both sides against the same criteria, ideally in the same sentence. 'Suggest' invites a plausible answer the student has not been taught, with a justification. 'Calculate' requires working. 'Determine' usually means take something from a graph or table first.

Teaching these takes about two sessions and it is the cheapest improvement available in IGCSE science, because it collects marks on content the student already holds. It also transfers completely between biology, chemistry and physics, which makes it unusually efficient for a triple-award student. A single block on command terms and six-mark structure can lift all three grades, which no amount of additional content can do at the same price.

The method is simple and uncomfortable. Write a six-mark answer, mark it against the official scheme without generosity, and count how many of the scheme's listed points actually appear. Most students find they wrote four correct things and scored two, because two of the four were not on the list and the other two were not linked. Doing that five or six times changes how a student reads a long question for good.

sections.heading: A past-paper routine when there are three sciences to cover
paragraphs: Three sciences means three sets of past papers, three mark schemes and a practical component, and the commonest failure is doing a little of everything badly. The routine that works treats papers as diagnostic instruments rather than as practice, which means fewer papers, marked more strictly, with the results acted on.

Sit one whole paper per science, to time, with no notes and no mark scheme in reach. Then mark each strictly, and categorise every lost mark into five buckets: content not known, quantitative error, command term misread, practical technique, or ran out of time. The totals matter far less than the distribution. A student losing most marks to quantitative errors across all three sciences has one problem to fix; a student losing them to content in biology and to command terms in physics has two separate ones.

Then rotate deliberately rather than evenly. Spend two weeks on whichever bucket is largest, re-sit a paper, and compare the distribution rather than the total. A student whose quantitative errors have fallen from twelve marks to three has made real progress even if the overall score moved only a little, because the next paper will convert that. Chasing the total instead of the distribution is how months disappear.

Keep the practical paper in the rotation from the start, not at the end. It is the component students most reliably postpone, it is marked on precise wording, and it improves faster than content work because the body of technique is small. Two sessions on method description, variables and apparatus resolution, practised against official schemes, generally recovers more marks per hour than anything else available to a triple-award student.

sections.heading: The arithmetic of paying for three sciences
paragraphs: Three sciences changes the cost conversation, because the obvious plan - a tutor for each - is rarely affordable or advisable. Published market rates in Dubai start at roughly AED 33 to 52 an hour with Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 with EdFlik at the budget end, which generally means a university student. A qualified subject tutor online is published from around AED 150 to 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150. Specialist rates run AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home one-to-one is quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price.

Three weekly sessions at the qualified-tutor band is a monthly commitment most families in this belt will not want to sustain for two years, and they should not have to. The sequence approach - one science at a time, chosen from marked papers, finished before the next begins - costs a third as much per month and usually produces more, because the student retains the independent practice time that makes any tutoring effective. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work.

There is one case where paying for two at once is right: when two sciences are both genuinely weak and the student is in the final two terms of Year 11. Even then, two specialists on different evenings beats one generalist covering both, and with online delivery the second appointment adds no travel for anybody. Advertised in-home packages in this market run around AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions, which is the clearest illustration of what the travel premium costs when more than one subject is involved.

IB Gram publishes no rate card on this page, because a figure quoted without knowing the award structure, the number of sciences and the frequency is not information. The trial lesson and the consultation are free. For budgeting context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year.

sections.heading: Practical work, materials and the limits worth stating
paragraphs: Science is the subject where online delivery has a real boundary, and it is worth naming rather than arguing around. Apparatus cannot be handled together over video. A student cannot be shown how a burette feels at the point of a titration, how a micrometer behaves when over-tightened, or why an ammeter reading is drifting. Those skills are learned in the school laboratory, and that is the right place for them.

What the written practical component assesses, though, is mostly not dexterity. It is the ability to describe a method precisely, to identify and control variables, to read apparatus to the correct resolution, to spot a flaw in a described procedure and to suggest a targeted improvement. All of that is analysis and precision writing, and it works better on a shared screen where the sentence can be written, marked against the scheme and rewritten in the same five minutes.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai; a tutor attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. So the honest comparison is between a subject specialist on a screen and a generalist in the room, and for a triple-award student needing chemistry and physics taught properly, the specialist wins on the thing that matters. For a student who cannot settle on a screen, it may not, and that is a limitation rather than an objection to be handled.

On materials, we reference Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes, cite them and link to the boards. We do not reproduce them or supply them as downloads, because they are the boards' copyright and, for unreleased material, a malpractice exposure. On permits, the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no fine schedule published - so ask any tutor whether they hold it.

sections.heading: KHDA, the timetable and why triple award gets squeezed
paragraphs: Private schools in Dubai are overseen by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The sector ran 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across seventeen curricula, with UK curriculum schools at 37 per cent of enrolment. Inspection reports are public and name subject-level strengths, which makes them the best available comparison of science teaching between two schools in this belt.

The timetable pressure that pushes students towards double award is partly structural. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated against a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and at least twenty-five minutes is advised for any mandatory subject lesson.

Three separate sciences need roughly half again as many periods as a double award, and in a Year 10 timetable that also has to fit mandatory subjects, mathematics, English and two or three options, something has to give. That is the mechanism behind a pattern families notice without identifying the cause: triple award is offered to fewer students than want it, and where it is offered the periods are sometimes tighter than the content needs.

One part of that squeezed timetable is closed to a science tutor entirely, and it is worth being clear about the boundary. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ between the two groups, and combined classes are prohibited. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval, which schools are responsible for ensuring. In those subjects the use of different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is also prohibited. So when periods are tight, the hours that can be bought back sit in biology, chemistry and physics, not in the mandatory block that created the pressure.
