process.title: Establish the award structure first
process.description: Triple, double or single, and the syllabus codes for each science. That single answer determines the post-16 ceiling and the past papers, and it takes one email to the school. Any plan built before it is known is a guess.

process.title: Test the quantitative work separately
process.description: An unfamiliar formula, a symbol to be made the subject, no science attached. If that is slow, the first two sessions are quantitative sessions - and they pay in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously rather than in one.

process.title: Send marked papers from each science
process.description: Three marked scripts tell us whether this is one problem or three. The distribution of lost marks across content, quantitative error, command terms, practical technique and time is what sets the order of work.

process.title: A free trial on a live topic
process.description: The tutor teaches whatever is currently stuck in the science that matters most, at the correct tier and board. That shows how explanations land, and there is nothing to unwind if the pairing is wrong.

process.title: Sequence, do not parallelise
process.description: One science at a time unless two are genuinely critical and the papers are close. Three sciences in parallel means six hours of tuition a week, and the independent practice is always the first thing to go.

process.title: Review by distribution, not by total
process.description: Re-sit a paper and compare where the marks were lost, not just how many. Quantitative errors falling from twelve marks to three is real progress even when the total barely moves, because the next paper converts it.

whyPoints.title: Award structure before content
whyPoints.description: We establish triple, double or single award first, because it sets a ceiling that no amount of teaching lifts. A double-award student aiming at A Level chemistry has a structural problem that needs a different conversation.

whyPoints.title: One problem, not three
whyPoints.description: Three weak science grades usually share a quantitative cause. Fixing proportion, rearrangement and graph reading first pays in all three subjects at once, which no subject-specific work can do.

whyPoints.title: A specialist per science
whyPoints.description: Biology, chemistry and physics fail for different reasons and are taught best by people who teach them. Online delivery makes a second specialist on a second evening cost nothing extra in travel.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper taken seriously
whyPoints.description: The written practical component is precision writing marked on specific words, and it is the most reliably under-prepared paper in IGCSE science. Two sessions on it transfer across all three subjects.

whyPoints.title: Command terms as a closed list
whyPoints.description: State, describe, explain, compare, suggest, determine. Taught explicitly, they collect marks on content the student already holds, in all three sciences at once.

whyPoints.title: Sequenced to be affordable
whyPoints.description: One science at a time, chosen from marked papers, finished before the next starts. It costs a third of the obvious plan and protects the independent practice that makes tutoring work.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child is on triple or double award science?
faqs.answer: Ask the school office or the head of science for the syllabus codes on the entry. Three codes - Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 - means triple award. A single code such as Cambridge 0654 Co-ordinated Sciences, or a Pearson Science Double Award entry, means two grades from one qualification covering all three disciplines at reduced depth. Do this in Year 10, because that is when the decision can still be revisited and Year 11 is when it is being locked in.

faqs.question: My son is on double award and wants to study engineering. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: It is a structural problem rather than an academic one, which makes it more serious than a weak grade. A Level physics and chemistry departments and Diploma Higher Level sciences generally expect the separate subject, and many in this belt will not admit double-award students at all. The options are to make an evidence-based case for moving to triple award while a place can still be timetabled, or to plan a route that accepts the double-award outcome. Discovering it in Year 13 leaves neither option open.

faqs.question: Why is my daughter losing marks in all three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Almost always because of one shared cause rather than three separate ones. Proportion, equation rearrangement, standard form, unit conversion and graph reading are examined inside every science paper, and a student weak there loses marks everywhere and concludes they are bad at science. The test takes five minutes: hand over an unfamiliar formula and ask for a given symbol to be made the subject, with no science attached. If that is slow, fix it first and all three grades move.

faqs.question: Nobody has mentioned the written practical paper all year - what is on it?
faqs.answer: Cambridge assesses practical skills either through a practical test or through a written alternative, and which one applies depends on the syllabus and the centre, so confirm with the school first. The written paper asks a student to describe a method precisely, identify independent, dependent and control variables, read apparatus to the correct resolution, spot a flaw in a described procedure and suggest a targeted improvement. It is precision writing applied to science, marked on specific wording, and it improves quickly with two sessions of practice against official schemes.

faqs.question: Why does biology seem harder than chemistry for my child when everyone says the opposite?
faqs.answer: Because biology's difficulty is volume and vocabulary rather than conceptual depth. The content is larger than in the other two sciences, so revision tends to go broad and shallow, and extended-response questions on transport in plants, homeostasis or inheritance require the specification's own terms. A biologically correct answer in everyday language frequently scores nothing because the mark scheme lists the word. Active recall against the specification itself, using its vocabulary, is what shifts this - not re-reading notes.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover biology, chemistry and physics for a triple-award student?
faqs.answer: One tutor can cover all three at Core tier or in Year 10 reasonably well. At Extended tier in Year 11, the three fail for different reasons and are taught best by people who teach them: chemistry's mole system and qualitative analysis, physics's circuit reduction, biology's specification vocabulary. Where two sciences genuinely need attention at once, two specialists on different evenings works better than one generalist across both, and with online delivery the second appointment adds no travel for anyone.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our home in Al Sufouh or The Greens?
faqs.answer: Not from us. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; tutors attending a student's address is a service we run only in India. Every lesson here is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. In-home tutoring exists in this market at published rates of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and for a family needing two sciences a week that travel overhead is paid twice. What the premium buys is presence, not subject expertise.

faqs.question: How much should three sciences cost us a month, and is that even the right plan?
faqs.answer: Three weekly sessions at the qualified-tutor band is a commitment most families here will not sustain for two years, and usually should not. Published monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions in Dubai run roughly AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. One science at a time, chosen from marked papers and finished before the next begins, costs a third as much and protects the independent practice that makes any of it work.

faqs.question: How many marks are really at stake in the six-mark questions?
faqs.answer: Enough to move a grade, and they are lost for non-scientific reasons. A student who knows the content writes everything they know in the order it occurs to them, while the mark scheme awards specific linked statements. Most students who mark their own long answers strictly discover they wrote four correct things and scored two, because two were not on the list and the other two were not connected. Two sessions on structure and command terms collects marks on content already held, in all three sciences at once.

faqs.question: Can online lessons really work for science when so much of it is practical?
faqs.answer: For what the papers assess, mostly yes - with one honest exception. Apparatus handling cannot be taught over video and belongs in the school laboratory, and we say so rather than claiming otherwise. The written practical component, though, tests method description, variable identification, apparatus resolution, flaw-spotting and improvement suggestion, all of which are precision writing and analysis. Those work better on a shared screen, where a sentence can be written, marked against the official scheme and rewritten inside five minutes.

faqs.question: Does it matter whether the sciences are Cambridge or Pearson for revision purposes?
faqs.answer: Yes, substantially. Question style, paper structure and the practical arrangements all differ, so past papers from the wrong board teach technique that will not be rewarded. Cambridge tiers the separate sciences into Core and Extended and assesses practical skills through a practical test or a written alternative. Pearson assesses practical skills within the written papers in several subjects, which is the decisive difference for anyone considering online schooling or entry as a private candidate. Collect the codes before buying anything.

faqs.question: Is it worth starting science tutoring in Year 10 rather than waiting?
faqs.answer: It is the better value by a wide margin, for two reasons. The quantitative work that underlies all three sciences takes a term to repair and pays for the remaining eighteen months rather than the remaining eight weeks. And Year 10 is when the triple-award decision can still be revisited on evidence, which is the single most consequential thing about IGCSE science. Year 11 tutoring is triage within a ceiling already set; Year 10 tutoring can still move the ceiling.

faqs.question: Which series will my child sit in Dubai - June, November, or the India-only February one?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International offers its February/March series to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Confirm the series with your school's exams officer, and also ask which of Cambridge's six administrative zones the centre sits in, because Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct timetable for your zone and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

faqs.question: What if we need a science specialist and none is available at our hour?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting someone who does not teach the subject. Some requirements are thin - a particular Cambridge syllabus version mid-revision, or practical-paper technique in the fortnight before the papers. When that happens you get three straight answers: how long a match realistically takes, whether a closely related specialist could cover part of the need, and whether the school's own department is the better route for now. No competitor page in this market publishes a coverage limit.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-knowledge-p.closingHeading: Collect the codes, then decide what to buy
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-knowledge-p.closingBody: If you are looking for an IGCSE science tutor in Dubai Knowledge Park, the useful first step costs nothing. Email the school and ask for the syllabus codes, the tier for each science and which practical route the centre enters. Then test the quantitative work for five minutes at home. With those answers the plan is usually obvious: fix the arithmetic first, take the science where the marked paper shows the cheapest marks, and keep the practical paper in the rotation from the start rather than leaving it until April.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one Jumeirah week, and two usable slots
paragraphs: The honest starting point for science tutoring in LA Mer is an arithmetic problem rather than a teaching one. A Year 11 student in this cluster finishes school between about 2:45pm and 3:30pm, reaches home between 3:15pm and 4:15pm after the Jumeirah Beach Road or Al Wasl Road exit, and then has an activity programme that in most of these schools runs until about 6pm. The evening that remains has to hold food, eight or nine subjects' worth of homework, and whatever revision the school has set. Two tutored hours a week is a realistic ceiling for most families. Three sciences do not divide neatly into two hours.

Most families discover this by trying the other thing first. Three weekly science hours are booked in September, the student keeps them for about six weeks, and then one quietly stops happening because there was never room for it. The hour that falls away is rarely the one that mattered least; it is the one scheduled latest in the evening, which is usually physics. Deciding which two hours exist is therefore better done deliberately in September than accidentally in November. That means the first decision is triage, not timetabling. Which science is actually costing marks, and in which paper? Parents frequently arrive asking for science tutoring in general, when the marked mock shows a clear pattern: strong biology, adequate chemistry, and physics losing marks specifically on the calculation questions. Tutoring all three equally in that situation spends two thirds of the budget maintaining subjects that were already fine.

The second decision is which specification the school uses, because it changes what a session should contain. Cambridge separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, carry a practical component worth 20 per cent: either Paper 5, a practical test, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences, 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, have no separate practical paper and assess practical skills inside the written papers instead. A tutor who assumes the wrong one of those will prepare a student for a paper they are not sitting.

The third is whether the student is doing three separate sciences at all. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award, producing two grades from one set of papers that covers all three disciplines, and Combined Science 0653 is a single award. A student on 0654 does not need three subject specialists; they need one person who can move across all three at the level the paper actually demands, which is shallower than the separate sciences but broader.

IB Gram teaches LA Mer families one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE, since home visits are offered only in India. For a two-slot week that matters practically: a session can be switched from physics to chemistry between one week and the next without anyone rearranging a drive, which is what makes triage a live tool rather than a decision made once in September.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-la-mer.subjectsIntro: These are the science blocks that generate the most tutoring hours among LA Mer families, with the paper each tends to be examined in and what it actually demands.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Series and parallel behaviour, resistance calculations and circuit reasoning. The most requested single topic in this cluster. Students who can recite the rules often cannot apply them to an unfamiliar circuit diagram, which is a practice problem rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and energy calculations
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting is the real skill, and it is a mathematics habit rather than a physics one. Marks are lost through unit errors and through writing a final answer with no working the examiner can award method marks for.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The dividing line between a grade 6 and a grade 8 in Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1. Multi-step problems involving limiting reagent and percentage yield reward sequencing practice, and they appear every series without fail.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic chemistry and reaction types
subjects.description: Homologous series, naming and the reactions linking functional groups. Recall volume rather than conceptual difficulty, which means frequent short testing produces more than long explanation ever will.

subjects.name: Chemistry: acids, bases, salts and preparation methods
subjects.description: Students lose marks on the practical detail: which method prepares which salt, how a product is separated, what observation confirms a reaction. These are exactly the details the practical and alternative-to-practical papers probe.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: High-mark-density content that rewards precise language. Explanation questions ask for a mechanism in order, and students who know the biology lose marks by giving the right ideas in the wrong sequence.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares, ratios and the vocabulary around alleles and phenotypes. Procedural once the convention is learned, and a reliable source of recoverable marks within two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Biology: human physiology and homeostasis
subjects.description: Negative feedback, hormonal control and the detail of specific organ systems. The common failure is describing what happens without naming the controlling mechanism, which is where the marks sit.

subjects.name: Practical skills and experimental design
subjects.levels: Cambridge Paper 5 or Paper 6, inside written papers for Edexcel
subjects.description: Reading a measuring instrument, identifying variables, spotting a flaw in a method and suggesting an improvement. Worth 20 per cent on Cambridge separate sciences and routinely the least-practised component in a tight Year 11 timetable.

subjects.name: Graph and data handling across all three sciences
subjects.description: Plotting accurately, drawing a line of best fit, reading an intercept and describing a trend in the words the mark scheme expects. One skill that pays in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously, which makes it the best single use of a shared session.

sections.heading: What fits into a LA Mer Year 11 week, and what has to be dropped
paragraphs: Start with the hours that exist rather than the hours you would like. The table below maps a typical Year 11 afternoon in this cluster from the school bell to the point where productive science work stops, which is the calculation every science tutoring plan here has to survive.

What falls out of that map is that two tutored hours a week is the ceiling for most students, and that both have to sit in the 6:30pm to 8:30pm window unless the activity programme leaves an early slot free. A family trying to fit three weekly science hours into this week is either removing independent study time or scheduling a session at an hour when nobody learns anything. Both are worse than choosing.

So the choice has to be made deliberately, and it should be made from a marked paper. A mock script shows which science is losing marks and, more usefully, which kind of question is losing them. Lost marks concentrated in calculation questions across physics and chemistry point to one shared session on quantitative technique rather than two separate subject sessions. Lost marks concentrated in six-mark explanation questions across biology and chemistry point to a session on writing to the mark allocation.

That is the useful reframing for a tight week. The unit of tutoring is not the subject; it is the failure mode. Two hours spent on the two failure modes a student actually has will cover all three sciences, while two hours spent on two of the three subjects will leave the third untouched and the failure modes unaddressed.

sections.heading: Which science specification is your child actually sitting?
paragraphs: This is the question that most changes what a session should contain, and it takes one email to the school to answer. The code appears on the exam entry statement. Getting it wrong means preparing a student for a paper that does not exist on their timetable, and it happens often enough to be worth checking before hiring anybody.

Cambridge separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, tier into Core and Extended. Core candidates sit a multiple-choice Paper 1 and a theory Paper 3; Extended candidates sit a multiple-choice Paper 2 and a theory Paper 4. Both tiers then add a practical component worth 20 per cent, taken either as Paper 5, a practical test carried out with apparatus, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which asks the same skills in written form. Which of those two a school enters for varies by school and sometimes by cohort.

Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award. One set of papers covers biology, chemistry and physics and produces two grades, with a theory paper that is longer than the separate-science equivalent and the same practical component at 20 per cent. Combined Science 0653 is the single-award version. Students on either are examined across all three disciplines at less depth than the separate sciences, so a tutor needs breadth rather than specialism.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences work differently again. Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 each have two written papers at Foundation or Higher tier, with practical skills assessed inside those papers rather than in a separate practical component. For a family comparing tutors, that single structural difference is worth more than any claim about experience: a tutor who has only taught Cambridge will have spent years preparing students for a practical paper your child may not sit.

sections.heading: The practical component is the cheapest 20 per cent to recover
paragraphs: On Cambridge separate sciences and Co-ordinated Sciences, the practical component carries 20 per cent of the grade, and in a crowded Year 11 timetable it is the component schools have least time to rehearse. That combination makes it the best value target in a two-slot week, because the marks are concentrated and the skills are small in number.

What the practical and alternative-to-practical papers actually test is narrow and learnable. Reading a scale correctly and to the right precision. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar method. Spotting the flaw in a described procedure. Suggesting a specific improvement rather than saying be more careful. Plotting a graph with sensible axes, drawing a line of best fit through scattered points, and reading a value off it. Describing a trend in the language the mark scheme rewards.

None of those requires apparatus to learn. The alternative to practical paper is written in any case, and the practical test rewards a student who knows what the examiner is looking for far more than one who has handled the equipment a few extra times. A session spent marking past practical questions against the published scheme will typically move a student further than a session spent revising content they already partly know.

There is a second reason this component rewards attention. It is the same skill set in all three sciences, so an hour spent on it serves biology, chemistry and physics at once. For a LA Mer family with two slots and three subjects, that is the only part of the syllabus where a single hour genuinely counts three times.

Tests a small, learnable set of skills rather than content

sections.heading: The science year counted backwards from the June series
paragraphs: Planning the two slots is easier against a calendar, and this is ground no competitor page in this search covers. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any February or March dates quoted to a Dubai family should be disregarded. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

Checkable reference points are worth having. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and they give the shape of a year reliably, but the live official timetable is what should be checked before acting, because provisional timetables get revised.

One Cambridge administrative point matters for any family in the Gulf. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the timetable differs by zone, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone it sits in rather than working from the first timetable a search returns.

Counted backwards, the two slots have a natural sequence. Through the autumn term they carry whatever the school is teaching. The mock window produces the only honest diagnostic of the year. The weeks after the mocks are the highest-value hours available, spent on a diagnosed list rather than on revision in general. Practical paper work fits best in the term before the series, when content is largely covered. The last fortnight belongs to the student's own timed practice.

sections.heading: Online delivery against a visiting tutor, for a family with two slots
paragraphs: Home tutoring is the usual search term and it deserves a direct answer rather than a deflection. In-home one-to-one science tuition in Dubai is widely available and is quoted at AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel included, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. Online qualified subject tutors are published at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors listing IGCSE rates from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. Those are market figures belonging to the providers named, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list.

For a three-science family the specific problem with the visiting model is flexibility. If the mock shows physics calculation failures in January and chemistry stoichiometry failures in March, the sensible move is to switch what a slot is used for. With a visiting tutor that means either finding a second person who can reach LA Mer at the same hour or asking a biologist to teach stoichiometry. With online delivery it means changing who joins the call.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. LA Mer families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared past papers and recorded sessions. The relevant gain for this page is that a slot can carry a different science from one week to the next without a logistics negotiation.

The second gain is subject match. Requiring a person to reach the Jumeirah coast by 6:45pm on a given weekday narrows the field to those who live nearby and are free then, and narrows it again if you need someone who has taught Pearson 4PH1 rather than Cambridge 0625. Removing the distance condition is what lets the match be made on the specification instead.

sections.heading: Honest limits: what a science tutor should and should not be doing
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences are examined by terminal papers, so the coursework question that dominates Diploma subjects does not arise in the same form. The integrity question still does, in two specific places that matter for families hiring in this market.

The first concerns materials. Nobody should be offering you downloaded syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as a package. Those materials belong to Cambridge International and to Pearson, and the proper route is the official site or the school's own licensed access. A tutor who turns up with a folder of copied mark schemes has told you something about their standards before teaching anything.

The second concerns school assessments. A tutor should not be sitting alongside a student during a timed school assessment, should not be supplying answers to a paper the school is still using with its cohort, and should not be completing any work that will be submitted as the student's own. For students who go on to the IB Diploma the same principle hardens into a formal rule: the scientific investigation is 20 per cent of the grade and must be the student's own work, with a tutor limited to teaching the criteria and giving feedback on drafts. At least one operator in this search sells completed Internal Assessments, which is a malpractice risk carried entirely by the student.

The third limit is on promises. No tutor can honestly guarantee a grade or a specific improvement, and nobody offering one should be taken seriously. What can be offered is a diagnosis from marked work, teaching aimed at named papers, a written record of what each session covered, and a clear recommendation when the right answer is to buy fewer hours rather than more.

sections.heading: Checking that a Dubai science tutor is permitted to teach
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the checks a parent needs are short. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Because there is no fee, there is no cost reason for a working tutor to lack one.

Eligibility is broad, which surprises many families. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service listing is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, any specific amount quoted to you should be treated with caution.

Two adjacent facts are worth knowing in Dubai specifically. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal entity from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, a restriction the MoHRE permit's code of conduct echoes.

Reduced to what a parent actually asks: does this person hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and is my child enrolled at the school where they teach? Both answers should arrive without hesitation.

process.title: Send the specification codes
process.description: Tell us whether the school enters for Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, for Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, or for Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, and whether Paper 5 or Paper 6 applies. That one answer determines what every session should contain, and it is on the exam entry statement.

process.title: Send a marked paper, not a wish list
process.description: A recent mock or class test script shows which science is losing marks and which kind of question is losing them. That is what turns two weekly hours into a plan. Without it, the hours get split evenly across three subjects and address nothing in particular.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: A full session at no charge, taught rather than pitched, with the student. The tutor works from the marked script and starts teaching. One trial lesson per student, before any booking is made; if the match is wrong, say so and nothing is owed.

process.title: Assign the slots to failure modes
process.description: The two weekly hours are allocated to the two things actually going wrong, which is often quantitative technique and writing to the mark allocation rather than two of the three sciences. Slots are reallocated when the mark pattern changes.

process.title: Add the practical paper block, then taper
process.description: In the term before the series, one slot moves to practical and alternative-to-practical paper work, which is the same skill set in all three sciences. In the final weeks the sessions reduce deliberately so the student practises alone under timed conditions.

whyPoints.title: The week is sized before anything is sold
whyPoints.description: Two tutored hours is the realistic ceiling for a Year 11 student in this cluster, and saying so is more useful than selling three. Everything on this page is built around what actually fits between a 3:30pm finish and the point where calculation work stops holding.

whyPoints.title: Specification first, subject second
whyPoints.description: Cambridge separate sciences carry a practical paper worth 20 per cent; Pearson Edexcel assesses those skills inside the written papers. A tutor matched without that information may spend months preparing a student for a component they will never sit.

whyPoints.title: Slots follow the failure mode
whyPoints.description: Lost marks concentrated in calculation questions across two sciences call for one quantitative session, not two subject sessions. Treating the failure mode as the unit of tutoring is how two hours end up covering all three sciences.

whyPoints.title: A slot can change subject without a logistics problem
whyPoints.description: Because teaching is one-to-one over live video, moving a slot from physics to chemistry after the mocks means a different tutor joins the call. With a visiting tutor it means finding a second person who can reach the Jumeirah coast at the same hour.

whyPoints.title: Rates quoted with their sources
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure here is attributed to the provider who published it and dated to when it was read. Three of the six pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars, which is not the currency these families transact in.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees and no copied mark schemes
whyPoints.description: No grade or improvement is promised, because none can honestly be. Syllabus documents, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson and are referenced rather than supplied, which is a standard worth checking before hiring anyone.

faqs.question: Can a LA Mer family realistically fit three sciences into one tutoring week?
faqs.answer: Not as three separate hours, for most students. School in this cluster ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, activity programmes run to about 6pm, and Year 11 carries eight or nine subjects of homework. Two tutored hours a week is the ceiling before independent study time starts disappearing. The way three sciences fit into two hours is by treating the failure mode as the unit rather than the subject: one hour on quantitative technique covers physics and chemistry at once.

faqs.question: Which science should we prioritise if we can only book two hours?
faqs.answer: Decide from a marked mock script rather than from the subject that feels hardest. The script shows both which science is losing marks and which kind of question is losing them. Lost marks clustered in calculation questions across physics and chemistry point to one shared session on quantitative technique. Lost marks clustered in six-mark explanation questions point to a session on writing to the mark allocation. Either way the two hours then address something specific instead of being split evenly across three subjects.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: 0654 is a double award: one set of papers covering biology, chemistry and physics produces two grades, with a longer combined theory paper and the same practical component at 20 per cent. The three separate sciences, 0610, 0620 and 0625, each produce their own grade and go deeper in each discipline. A student on 0654 does not need three subject specialists; they need one tutor comfortable moving across all three at the depth the combined paper actually demands.

faqs.question: Does Pearson Edexcel IGCSE science have a practical exam like Cambridge?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the single most useful thing to establish before hiring. Cambridge separate sciences and Co-ordinated Sciences include a practical component worth 20 per cent, taken as Paper 5, a practical test with apparatus, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical in written form. Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 have no separate practical paper and assess those skills inside the written papers. A tutor prepared for the wrong structure will waste months.

faqs.question: Is the Cambridge practical paper worth tutoring if we have no laboratory at home?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it does not need apparatus. The practical and alternative-to-practical papers test a narrow, learnable set of skills: reading a scale to the right precision, identifying variables in an unfamiliar method, spotting a flaw in a procedure, proposing a specific improvement, plotting a graph with sensible axes, drawing a line of best fit and reading a value from it. All of that is taught by marking past practical questions against the published scheme. It is also the same skill set in all three sciences.

faqs.question: Why is electricity the most requested physics topic among Jumeirah families?
faqs.answer: Because it is where the gap between knowing the rules and applying them shows most sharply. A student can recite how current and potential difference behave in series and parallel and still fail a question built on an unfamiliar circuit diagram, because the question requires reading the circuit rather than recalling the rule. That is a practice problem rather than a knowledge problem, and it responds quickly to marked past-paper work on progressively less familiar diagrams.

faqs.question: Our mock results were bad across all three sciences. Where do we start?
faqs.answer: With the scripts rather than the grades, and with one diagnostic session. Marks lost uniformly across three sciences almost always share a cause: either quantitative technique, or writing to the mark allocation, or the practical and data questions. Each of those is one session a week rather than three. Booking three separate subject tutors in that situation triples the cost and addresses the shared cause only incidentally. Start with the pattern, then decide how many hours the pattern actually needs.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE science exams run for students in Dubai?
faqs.answer: UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so disregard any February or March dates quoted by a tutor or a website. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. As checkable reference points, the Pearson November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026. Confirm current dates on the official timetable, since provisional versions get revised.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge zone timetable applies to a school on the Jumeirah coast?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, because it varies and the consequence of guessing is serious. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and the exam timetable differs between them. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. A tutor building a revision schedule should be working from the school's zone timetable rather than a generic one found through a search.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to homes in LA Mer?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. LA Mer families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with screen-shared past papers and recorded sessions. For a three-science family that format solves a real problem: when the mark pattern changes after the mocks, a slot can move from physics to chemistry by a different tutor joining the call rather than by finding a second person who can reach the area.

faqs.question: How much does IGCSE science tutoring cost in the Dubai market?
faqs.answer: Published rates for qualified online subject tutors run AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase publishing AED 270 for specialist work. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the usual range at AED 180 to AED 350. Budget online options start lower, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65. Those figures belong to the named providers and were read in October 2026.

faqs.question: Do the two Co-ordinated Sciences grades both count towards MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: On the British track a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not included among those five. One provider ranking for these searches states that six subjects are required, which is not what the published rule says. A double award in Co-ordinated Sciences contributes two of the five. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than relying on any tutoring website.

faqs.question: Should we switch from Core to Extended tier, and what does that cost in hours?
faqs.answer: The tier sets the grade ceiling, so it is the most consequential decision in the course: Cambridge Core is graded C to G and Extended A* to E. The honest way to decide is a single diagnostic hour on a marked Extended past paper, which shows whether the student is short of content or short of technique. Short of technique is recoverable within a term. Short of content across several topics, with the series close, usually is not, and protecting a strong Core grade is the better plan.

faqs.question: Can a tutor give us past papers and mark schemes for all three sciences?
faqs.answer: They should not, and a tutor who offers a folder of them has told you something useful. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge International and to Pearson, and the correct route is the official site or the school's own licensed access. A tutor references and links those materials rather than redistributing them. Working through a paper the student has legitimately obtained, marked against the published scheme, is the actual job and it does not require copying anything.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-la-mer.closingHeading: Find the codes, size the week, then choose what the two hours do
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-la-mer.closingBody: Three things settle a science tutoring plan for a LA Mer family, and none of them is an hourly rate. First, the specification codes, because Cambridge and Pearson differ on whether a practical paper exists at all. Second, the honest size of the week, which in this cluster is two tutored hours between a 3:30pm finish and the point where calculation work stops holding. Third, a marked mock script, which shows which failure mode those two hours should address. Take the free trial lesson, which is taught rather than pitched. Teaching is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-living-lege.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach International GCSE sciences to students in Living Legends and the surrounding communities. Each profile names the board and the subjects, and availability is listed by hour, because for a three-science family the hour is the binding constraint.

intro.heading: Three sciences and one usable evening
paragraphs: A family taking three separate sciences at International GCSE has three times the content, three sets of command-term habits and three sets of practical conventions to learn, inside the same week as everybody else. In Living Legends that week is shorter than most, because there is no secondary school inside the community. Students travel out, most often to Al Barsha South, Dubai Hills Estate or the Al Khail Road corridor, and arrive home between four and half past four. By the time they have eaten, one usable evening slot remains.

That produces the central planning question, and most families answer it wrongly. Faced with three subjects and one slot, the instinct is to divide the hour: twenty minutes of biology, twenty of chemistry, twenty of physics. It feels fair and it produces recognition rather than fluency, because twenty minutes is enough to revisit a topic and not enough to fix anything. The alternative, which works, is rotation: one science at a time, concentrated, reviewed every six sessions and changed when the evidence says so.

There is one genuine exception to that rule, and it is the most valuable thing on this page. The written practical paper skills, identifying variables, criticising a method, processing data, assessing reliability and suggesting improvements, are examined across all three sciences and are largely transferable between them. A single block on those serves biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously. For a family with one slot and three subjects, that is the only purchase that genuinely multiplies.

Scheduling has a second layer here. Dubai Sports City sits immediately next door, and many households in Living Legends have children in academy programmes training between five and seven on several weekdays. Where that applies, the weekday evening is effectively gone and the weekend morning becomes the serious window. Add the mandatory UAE subjects, which Dubai private schools must teach alongside the licensed curriculum with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and the taught week is fuller than a science option block suggests.

IB Gram removes travel from the arrangement so the remaining hours can be used properly. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so a session starts minutes after arrival, consecutive slots cost nothing extra, and a weekend block can be used without anybody rearranging a car. Home visits are a service we operate only in India, so nobody is sent to a Living Legends address. What follows is the scheduling detail, the rotation logic, the shared practical block, and what a three-science plan costs. Taken in that order it produces a plan a family can still run in February, which is more than can be said for the three-sessions-a-week arrangement most households start with in September and abandon by half term.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-living-lege.programmesIntro: Four routes cover nearly every science enquiry from this community, and the route determines how much there is to schedule in the first place.

programmes.name: Three separate sciences
programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry and Physics as individual International GCSE subjects, each with its own papers and grade. The fullest content load and the standard route toward two or three sciences post-16. Three subjects also means three sets of command-term habits and three sets of practical conventions, which is what makes the scheduling hard rather than simply busy.
programmes.countryNote: Students from this community heading toward IB Higher Level or A Level sciences are usually on this route, and they are the ones for whom rotation planning matters most. One slot divided three ways is the default arrangement here and the least effective one.

programmes.name: Coordinated Sciences (double award)
programmes.description: All three sciences in one course carrying a double award, Cambridge code 0654, with content reduced in each. The reductions are not uniform across the three sciences, so the specification matters. The commonest error is revising from separate-science material and spending hours on topics removed from the award.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of families in this area are on this route without being certain of it, because schools describe it inconsistently in reports. Confirming it with the examinations officer before booking tuition is the cheapest piece of planning available and takes one email.

programmes.name: Combined Science (single award)
programmes.description: All three sciences in one course carrying a single award, Cambridge code 0653, with content reduced further again. Appropriate where a student needs a broad science qualification rather than a route into science at sixteen. Scope discipline is where the efficiency comes from on this route.
programmes.countryNote: For Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, five accredited International GCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count. How a single or double award counts toward that total is a question for the attestation authority rather than a tutoring page.

programmes.name: Post-16 science routes
programmes.description: A Level or IB Diploma sciences, with entry constrained by the International GCSE route and tier. Separate sciences at Extended or Higher tier are the comfortable foundation; a combined single award is usually not sufficient for a demanding post-16 science. That constraint is set at fourteen and discovered at sixteen.
programmes.countryNote: Families here with a medicine or engineering ambition should check it in Year 9. Published entry requirements for the intended post-16 programme are the document to read, and reading them costs nothing and prevents an expensive surprise.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-living-lege.subjectsIntro: In a rotation plan, each science needs its own diagnosis. These notes name where the marks go in each and how much concentration the work requires, which is what decides the slot.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and exchange
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, circulation and gas exchange. Content-heavy and vocabulary-dependent, with marks lost to answer structure on long questions rather than to recall. Tolerates a tired slot better than the physical sciences, which makes it useful after training.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares, variation and selection. Marks go missing on genetic diagrams that omit gametes or parental genotypes, which is a presentation habit rather than a knowledge gap and closes in two or three sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Mass, moles, concentration and limiting reagents. The quantitative foundation the rest of chemistry rests on, so a gap resurfaces in electrolysis, energetics and titration questions. Needs a sharp hour and four or five sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and reactivity
subjects.description: Half equations, products at each electrode and reactivity reasoning. Half equations unbalanced for charge are the standard loss, along with equations that balance but omit the state symbols the markscheme requires.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and rates
subjects.description: Homologous series, functional groups and rate experiments. Students describe a rate change without reference to collision frequency or activation energy, which is precisely what the explanation marks reward.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance and circuit analysis. Jointly with forces this carries the largest share of physics marks, and losses come from circuits worked from the formula sheet rather than redrawn properly. Needs a reasonably sharp hour.

subjects.name: Physics: forces and motion
subjects.description: Motion graphs, Newton's laws and moments. Taught early and depended on afterwards. The reliable loss is a question attempted without the diagram that would have made it straightforward, which is a draw-first habit.

subjects.name: Physics: waves, energy and radioactivity
subjects.description: Reflection and refraction, energy transfer and decay. Light on calculation and heavy on precise description, so it rewards organised notes and exact vocabulary and is the best physics topic for a depleted slot.

subjects.name: Practical skills on paper
subjects.levels: All routes, both boards, all three sciences
subjects.description: Variables, method criticism, scale reading, data processing, reliability and improvement. The one block that transfers across all three sciences, and the most reliably recoverable marks in the qualification because almost nobody teaches it explicitly.

sections.heading: The scheduling arithmetic: three subjects, one evening
paragraphs: Start with what the week actually leaves. A Year 11 student from this community commuting to Al Barsha South or the Al Khail corridor is home between four and half past four, needs thirty to forty minutes before they can concentrate, and has school homework across every subject plus the mandatory UAE subjects. That leaves one reliable weekday evening study slot and, for most households, one weekend morning. Three sciences do not fit into that by division.

The instinctive response is to split: twenty minutes per subject. It is the most common arrangement in this area and the least effective, for a reason worth stating precisely. Twenty minutes is enough to revisit a topic and remind a student of something they half knew. It is not enough to work through a multi-step chemistry calculation, diagnose why a physics circuit question went wrong, or restructure a six-mark biology answer and have the student rewrite it. Those take the better part of a session each, and without them nothing changes.

Rotation works instead. Pick the science currently losing the most marks, give it the whole slot for six sessions, measure against the same question types, and then decide whether to continue or move. Over a Year 11 that produces three or four concentrated runs rather than ninety fragmented ones, and the student can feel the difference by the second block. It also makes the spend legible, because each block has a start, an end and a result.

The one place rotation does not apply is the shared practical block, because that technique transfers across all three sciences. Scheduling it early means every subsequent block starts from a higher base. The table below sets out a rotation plan across a Year 11 for a three-science student in this community.

sections.heading: The journey, and what it leaves for science homework
paragraphs: It is worth doing the arithmetic rather than assuming it, because the result changes what a parent should book. There is no secondary school inside Living Legends, so the journey is a given rather than a choice. School finishes between half past two and half past three across Dubai's private sector. A journey to Al Barsha South or Dubai Hills runs twenty to thirty minutes in free traffic and longer on a bus that serves several communities, because the route rather than the distance sets the time.

Home between four and half past four, then. Thirty to forty minutes to eat and stop being a passenger. That puts the start of usable study time at around five, and a three-science student has school homework in all three subjects plus everything else. A tutoring session placed at five competes with the homework rather than supporting it; a session at six works, and leaves the earlier hour for the school's own tasks.

Then the evening has to absorb the mandatory UAE subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes required for Arab and non-Arab students, and KHDA calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit while advising that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. The homework that follows is real, and a science plan that ignores it is planning for a week the student does not have.

For academy households next door in Sports City the calculation is different again: training occupies five until seven on several weekdays, so the weekday science slot either sits immediately after school, before training, or it does not exist. In those households the weekend double slot is not an alternative arrangement but the main one, and recognising that in September avoids three months of cancelled sessions.

sections.heading: Which science belongs in a tired hour
paragraphs: Not all science work needs the same concentration, and knowing the difference lets a family use a depleted slot productively instead of writing it off. This matters more for a three-science student than for anyone else, because they have more subjects than good hours.

Biology tolerates tiredness best. Much of the work is vocabulary, structured recall and answer organisation, all of which can be done with a tutor guiding rather than the student generating. Restructuring a six-mark answer about gas exchange is a worthwhile use of a Thursday evening after training. So is working through model answers on genetics and tightening the language.

Physics is the least forgiving at the calculation end and among the most forgiving at the descriptive end, which makes it two subjects for scheduling purposes. Circuit analysis and forces problems need a reasonably sharp hour. Waves, energy and radioactivity are description-heavy and precision-dependent rather than calculation-heavy, which makes them perfectly reasonable in a tired slot.

Chemistry sits in the middle and divides sharply. Moles and stoichiometry need concentration, because they are multi-step arithmetic where one slip invalidates the rest. Reactivity trends, electrolysis products and the vocabulary of rates are more descriptive and survive a later hour. The practical consequence is simple: a rotation plan should place the quantitative chemistry and the physics calculations in the best window available, and use the depleted window for biology and for the descriptive parts of the other two. Doing that costs nothing and recovers an hour a week that most families write off entirely.

sections.heading: The practical block that serves all three subjects
paragraphs: This is the most useful paragraph on the page for a three-science family. In the main International GCSE science routes, practical skills are examined through written questions about experimental method rather than through a performed experiment marked on the day. Candidates identify independent, dependent and controlled variables, criticise a given method, read an instrument scale, process data into a table, plot a graph, assess reliability and suggest a specific improvement.

The decisive point is that those skills are substantially the same in biology, chemistry and physics. The context changes and the reasoning does not. A student who learns to name a controlled variable precisely, to spot that a method has no repeats, to plot with sensible axes and to write an evaluation that names a specific error and its specific effect, carries that into all three papers. One block of four to six sessions therefore improves three subjects, which is the only purchase in this market that genuinely multiplies.

It is also the most commonly untaught area in the qualification, and not through any failure by schools. Laboratory time is limited and is spent on apparatus, procedure and safety, with the data treatment set as homework and rarely taught explicitly. The result is a widespread gap that is both high-value and procedural, which is the ideal combination for tutoring.

And it suits online delivery particularly well, which matters in a community where a visiting tutor is expensive and loses minutes at the gate. Both people annotate the same data table and graph in real time. A tutor can display a deliberately flawed method and ask what is wrong with it, which is the format the paper itself uses. The most valuable single session is one where the student brings their own messy data from a school practical in any of the three sciences and watches it processed properly. The laboratory work stays with the school, which has the equipment and the technician.

sections.heading: Mocks, Ramadan and the series: planning three subjects around the calendar
paragraphs: A three-science student meets the calendar three times over, because mock periods, internal assessments and the series itself hit all three subjects at once. Planning around that is the difference between a rotation that holds and one that collapses in February.

The series first, because the rule for a UAE page is firm. Cambridge International runs International GCSE in a June series and a November series; the February and March series is offered to India only, so any page quoting a spring window is handing parents a date they cannot use. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. Backward-looking anchors can be checked: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Mock periods are the local hazard. Schools typically run them in one block, which means all three sciences are examined within days of each other and tutoring capacity should be planned to pause rather than intensify. A family that books extra sessions during mocks is buying hours the student has no room to use. The weeks immediately after mocks, by contrast, are the single most productive period in the year, because there is marked evidence across all three subjects and a diagnosis can be made properly rather than guessed.

Ramadan shortens school days across the Emirates and moves energy to the evening. Sessions typically shift later, often after Iftar, and shorten while holding frequency. For a three-science rotation that argues for using the Ramadan weeks on the description-heavy material, biology vocabulary, waves and radioactivity, reactivity trends, and front-loading the quantitative work before the month begins. Non-fasting students in the same household are affected too, since the shortened school day changes the week's rhythm for everyone.

sections.heading: What a three-science plan costs
paragraphs: Three subjects is the point at which tutoring budgets break, so the arithmetic deserves stating plainly. Every figure below names the provider or source that published it, which matters in a market where three of the six most visible pages publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars.

Budget online provision runs AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified online subject tutors sit at AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing International GCSE from AED 150. Specialist International GCSE and A Level provision runs AED 200 to 450 and upward, with TutorChase at AED 270. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, and premium named provision reaches AED 650 with BartyED.

Now apply three subjects. Weekly support in all three at the qualified band is three times the monthly figure, and Bestimate's estimate for a single weekly session is already AED 600 to 1,200 mid-range. For most households that is not sustainable across a Year 11, which is exactly why rotation is the right structure rather than merely the cheaper one. A diagnosis, a shared practical block and two concentrated single-subject blocks across a year costs a fraction of three standing weekly arrangements and usually produces more.

The in-home comparison is worse for three sciences than for any other request. Three visiting specialists means three travel premiums and three gate waits, and a tutor booked for six who clears security at ten past has delivered fifty minutes of a paid hour. Monthly, four two-hour in-home sessions are advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799 against roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions. IB Gram does not sell UAE home visits at all; the service exists only in India, and the MoHRE private tutor permit is free of charge, so no licensing cost belongs in any quote.

sections.heading: Coursework, board material and the honesty boundary
paragraphs: International GCSE science carries less internally assessed work than the IB Diploma, but where any assessed personal work exists the boundary is the same across all three subjects, and it is worth stating because one page ranking in this market sells completed assessed work outright. The penalty for that falls on the student, not the seller.

A tutor may teach the content, explain what the assessment criteria reward, test whether a proposed approach is workable, read what the student has written and identify where it is losing marks, demonstrate a technique on different material, and teach citation and referencing properly. Where a school requires an authentication declaration, the student signs it, and a tutor who crossed that line has put the signature at risk along with the qualification behind it.

On materials the position is firm. Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade boundary tables are their copyright, and unreleased material carries a malpractice exposure in addition. A tutor cites the official source, works from what the school has legitimately issued, and writes equivalent practice questions in the same style and at the same difficulty. Across three sciences that is more work for the tutor and entirely manageable, and a provider advertising a download library of papers is offering an unresolved problem rather than an advantage.

A parallel rule applies to the mandatory UAE subjects sitting alongside the science timetable. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are compulsory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and for those subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. Support there works from the school's own material by design, which is a constraint rather than a preference.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and honest availability for three subjects
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE is regulated by permit, and the facts are short enough that every page should carry them. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee, states a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the smart app, website and e-services system.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule has been published. There is also a conduct rule worth knowing: Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from paid private tuition of students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct does likewise. That reporting is press-sourced, so verify against the current ADEK document before relying on exact wording.

Because Living Legends has no secondary school of its own, the body inspecting your child's biology, chemistry and physics teaching is attached to the campus they travel to rather than the community they sleep in, and every one of those campuses sits in Dubai, so it answers to KHDA. KHDA oversees the quality of private education and inspects on six bands from Outstanding to Very Weak, and one band covers all three sciences together, which is why an Outstanding school can still have the physics department described in section two. Cross an emirate boundary and the body changes. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. None of them has approved or accredited IB Gram, and neither has Cambridge nor Pearson; we operate no office, centre or branch anywhere in the UAE, which is the same reason the three-science evening above is built online rather than around a van.

On availability, single-science support at either tier matches quickly. All three sciences in the same evening is a scheduling problem rather than a supply problem, and it resolves with a weekend double slot or two evenings. The narrowest request is a specific tier in a specific board's physics at short notice, and where no specialist is free we give a date rather than offering a near-fit. No competitor in the clusters researched for this project discloses a coverage limit anywhere, which is why families keep finding one in week three.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-meydan.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE sciences by specification rather than by subject name, which is the distinction that matters when a Meydan student is entered for a double award on one board and a single science on another. You meet the tutor before any payment is taken.

intro.heading: The code comes before the tutor
paragraphs: Most parents searching for an IGCSE science tutor in Meydan can name the subject and not the specification, and that gap is where a term of tutoring gets wasted. The phrase science covers at least five different purchases at this level. A student may be sitting Cambridge Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625 and Biology 0610 as three separate subjects. They may be sitting Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award, which covers all three disciplines across a smaller set of papers and earns two grades. They may be on the Pearson Edexcel equivalents instead. Each of those routes examines different material through differently structured papers.

The second decision hidden inside the same phrase is the tier. A Cambridge entry is either Core or Extended, and the tier sets the ceiling before any teaching happens: Core entries access grades C to G, Extended entries A* to E. A student entered for Core cannot earn a grade above C no matter how well they are taught, and families discover this at exactly the wrong moment. The equivalent decision on the Pearson side is Foundation against Higher. A tutor who starts work without knowing the tier is guessing at which content is even on the paper.

Then there is the practical question, which in Dubai is nearly always answered one way. Cambridge sciences offer a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres enter candidates for the alternative. That paper asks a student to read apparatus diagrams, describe method, identify variables and spot sources of error without touching equipment. It is a paper about laboratory thinking rather than laboratory skill, which is why it tutors extremely well online and why a student who enjoys practical work can still lose marks on it.

Meydan's geography makes the usual proximity argument weak. There is no secondary school inside Meydan. The students sit in Nad Al Sheba at Repton School Dubai, Kent College Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy or North London Collegiate School Dubai, or across Ras Al Khor Road at Hartland International School, Deira International School and Dubai English Speaking College. A tutor living in District One is no better placed to know which specification your child's school entered than one teaching from elsewhere. One of those facts affects the grade. The other affects nothing.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Science support for Meydan families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with apparatus diagrams and past papers shared on screen. For the alternative-to-practical paper in particular, that is not a compromise: the paper itself is a written exercise, and marking a student's own attempt on a shared screen with the scheme open is the most direct form of preparation there is.

programmes.description: The years in which the habits that decide an IGCSE science grade are formed, and almost nobody buys tutoring for them. The skills that transfer are unit handling, rearranging a formula, drawing a line of best fit and writing a method somebody else could follow. None of that is on a specification yet, which is exactly why it is cheap to fix here and expensive to fix in Year 11.
programmes.countryNote: For a Meydan family this is the highest-value science tutoring available and the least purchased. A short block in Year 9 on calculation fluency and method writing costs a fraction of a Year 11 rescue term in the same Dubai market.

programmes.name: Where the science route leads next
programmes.description: A double-award grade is accepted for many sixth-form science courses but not all, and some A Level and IB Diploma science entries expect a separate single-science grade. That makes the Year 9 option choice a post-16 decision in disguise. It also means a November resit can matter for sixth-form entry in a way a parent does not anticipate in June.
programmes.countryNote: The Meydan schools split between A Level and the IB Diploma at sixth form, sometimes within the same campus, so ask the school directly what its own sixth form expects from a science entry before deciding between a double award and three single sciences.

programmes.name: Ministry of Education equivalency
programmes.description: For a UAE certificate equivalency on the British track, a student must pass five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-meydan.subjectsIntro: What a Meydan family actually buys under the word science varies. These are the components, named by what they assess rather than by subject label, because that is the level at which a tutor is either useful or not.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0620 or Pearson 4CH1
subjects.description: Reactions, moles, rates and organic families. Extended-tier marks disappear on stoichiometry that requires two steps and on explanations of trends where the student states the trend and omits the reason the mark scheme pays for.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0625 or Pearson 4PH1
subjects.description: Formula-driven and calculation-heavy. Marks go missing on unit prefixes, on rearranging before substituting, and on circuit questions where a student can recite the rule for current and not apply it to an unfamiliar arrangement.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0610 or Pearson 4BI1
subjects.description: The highest content volume of the three and the one most often under-revised because it reads as easy. Extended questions want precise terminology, and an answer that is broadly right in everyday language earns nothing.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences, double award
subjects.description: All three disciplines across a reduced set of papers, awarded as two grades. Less content than triple science but the same demand for precision, and a student needs to know which of the three disciplines is actually weak rather than treating it as one subject.

subjects.name: Combined Science, single award
subjects.description: A single grade covering all three disciplines, entered by a smaller group. Worth confirming with the school whether this is the entry, because the content coverage differs from the double award and past-paper practice does not transfer cleanly.

subjects.name: Alternative to Practical
subjects.description: Apparatus diagrams, method description, variable identification and sources of error, examined on paper. The paper most Dubai centres enter and the one most students have never practised separately, which makes it an unusually productive target.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, Cambridge 0580 or Pearson 4MA1
subjects.description: The subject that silently limits a physics grade. Rearranging formulae, handling standard form and reading gradients are maths skills examined inside science papers, and a science tutor who identifies that saves a family a wasted term.

subjects.name: Science practical skills
subjects.description: Writing a method another person could repeat, tabulating results with units in the heading, plotting sensibly and distinguishing anomaly from error. Examined across every science paper and taught explicitly almost nowhere.

subjects.name: Extended writing in science
subjects.description: The six-mark explain questions where most Extended candidates lose their margin. The fix is structural rather than factual: name the thing, state the mechanism, state the consequence, in that order, every time.

subjects.name: Past-paper technique
subjects.description: Reading command words, allocating minutes by marks, and knowing when to abandon a question. Worth more in the final term than any further content coverage, and genuinely teachable in a handful of sessions.
