sections.heading: How to find the specification and tier your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: The document you want exists and your school will give it to you. Email the examinations officer, not the science teacher, and ask for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the components your child is entered for. The reason to ask the examinations officer is that entries are their job, and a science teacher may know the course without knowing which tier an individual pupil was finally entered for. Ask for it in writing and keep it, because every subsequent decision about tutoring depends on it.

If you want to check before the reply arrives, look at the student's own materials. The front of a past paper carries the code and the component number. An exercise book or revision guide issued by the school usually names the board. A mock paper is the most reliable artefact of all, since schools normally mock on the specification they have entered. The combination of code and component tells a tutor almost everything: Cambridge 0620 with a Paper 4 is Extended-tier chemistry theory, and Cambridge 0654 is the double award whatever else is said about it.

The tier is the part worth being insistent about. A Cambridge Core entry accesses grades C to G and an Extended entry accesses A* to E, and that ceiling is set by the entry rather than by the teaching. A family paying for Extended-level tutoring for a child entered at Core is buying content that will not appear on the paper, and a family discovering in April that the entry was Core has lost the window to ask about changing it. Schools will discuss a tier change where the evidence supports it, but the conversation has to happen in time.

Once you hold the code, tier and components, send them to any tutor you are considering before the first lesson. It is a reasonable test as well as useful information: a tutor who asks what the components are and plans around them is working professionally, and one who says they cover all the boards without wanting the detail is telling you something about how the sessions will go.

sections.heading: Triple science or a double award, and what the choice closes
paragraphs: A Meydan family usually meets this decision in Year 9 and treats it as a workload question, which it partly is. Three separate sciences means three full specifications, three sets of theory papers and three practical components, and for a student carrying nine or ten subjects that is a genuine load. A double award covers all three disciplines across a reduced content set and awards two grades, which lightens the week considerably without removing any discipline from the student's education.

Where the decision bites is afterwards. Sixth-form science courses vary in what they will accept: many are content with a strong double-award grade, some expect a separate single-science grade in the discipline being continued, and the position differs between A Level and the IB Diploma. The Meydan corridor contains both routes, sometimes inside one campus, so the question cannot be answered in general. Ask the school's own sixth form what it expects, and if your child might move schools, ask the likely destination too.

The tutoring consequence is specific. A double-award student who needs help does not need three tutors; they need one person who can find out which of the three disciplines is actually costing marks, which is usually invisible from a single overall grade. A triple-science student is in a different position, because a weak discipline shows up as a weak subject grade and can be targeted directly. Diagnosing the double-award student takes a timed paper and a marking session rather than a conversation.

One further point families underestimate: dropping from triple to double after the course has started is not always possible and not always free of consequence, since entries and teaching groups are already set. If the workload is the problem, raise it with the school early in Year 10 rather than in the spring of Year 11, when the realistic options have narrowed to tier changes and resits.

sections.heading: The alternative-to-practical paper, and why it tutors so well
paragraphs: Cambridge sciences offer either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres enter the alternative. That means a Meydan student's practical marks are earned on paper: reading an apparatus diagram and saying what it measures, writing a method precise enough for somebody else to repeat, naming the independent, dependent and controlled variables, reading a scale correctly, spotting an anomalous result and explaining what probably caused it, and proposing a specific improvement rather than a general one.

Those are procedural skills, which is why they respond so quickly to teaching and why so many marks are available to a student who has practised them. The usual failure is not ignorance. It is vagueness: a method that says heat the liquid and record the temperature, where the mark scheme wanted the volume stated, the heating described and the measurement interval specified. A student who has had three of their own methods marked against a published scheme generally stops writing vague ones, and the improvement transfers across all three disciplines at once.

This paper is also the clearest case against the assumption that science must be tutored in person. The assessment is written. Working through apparatus diagrams on a shared screen, with the student annotating and the scheme open alongside, is a closer match to the exam than standing at a bench would be. A student who enjoys laboratory work and dislikes writing method frequently scores worse here than a cautious classmate, which surprises parents and is entirely consistent with what the paper measures.

Practically, this is the block we would recommend first to a Meydan household unsure where to start. It is short, it is cheap relative to a term, the marks are recoverable, and the gain applies to chemistry, physics and biology simultaneously. Ask the school to confirm which practical component your child is entered for before booking it, since the small number of centres running the practical test need something different.

sections.heading: The two series a Meydan candidate sits, counted backwards
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series. UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, and it is worth saying plainly because material written for Indian candidates circulates freely online and a Dubai family acting on a February entry deadline would be acting on the wrong calendar. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit separately in March, May and October and are not part of this.

Cambridge also allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone. Cambridge warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. So the only timetable worth planning around is the one your school's examinations officer confirms for your centre. Printing a timetable found through a search engine is a real risk rather than a theoretical one.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in a May and June window and in November each year. The November final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Results dates give a sense of the lag: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the document to work from rather than any restatement of it.

Counted backwards, the planning points are clear enough. Final entries sit months before the papers, which is why a tier conversation has to happen early. Mocks land in the winter term at most Meydan-area schools and are the best diagnostic data a family will get for free. A November resit is a real option, but its results arrive in the January window, so check whether that timing works for a sixth-form offer before relying on it.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the permit, and the claims we will not make
paragraphs: Families on the British track in Dubai eventually meet the Ministry of Education equivalency requirement, and the sourced position is specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. Alongside that, the requirement names one accredited Advanced Level subject at a grade of no less than E, or two accredited Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market tells UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the published clarification says.

No IB points threshold for equivalency appears in that source, so none is published here. Nor should anyone treat these pages as the authority on an individual case: equivalency and attestation are processes run by the Ministry and the attestation authorities, and IB Gram neither performs them, guarantees them, nor has any role in them. Check your own position on moe.gov.ae or with the relevant authority, and be sceptical of any tutoring provider that implies tutoring is required for a regulatory outcome.

On who may teach: private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and because no schedule of amounts is published, no figure should be quoted at you.

For completeness: IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing here should be read as claiming one. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA; Abu Dhabi and Al Ain by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there; Sharjah by SPEA; Ras Al Khaimah by its Department of Knowledge; and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah by the Ministry of Education. Naming them is useful to a parent. Implying they endorse us would not be.

sections.heading: A nearby science tutor against an online specialist
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison turns on what the paper actually tests. For a student who will not sit down without an adult present, a person at the table is worth paying for and that is a real need rather than a weakness. For a Year 11 student entered for Extended-tier papers and an alternative-to-practical component, the thing that moves the grade is somebody who knows that specification's question style and can mark the student's own attempt against the published scheme. Those two qualities have no relationship to each other.

In Meydan the geography makes the trade worse than it looks. The approach from Al Quoz or along Al Khail Road between four and six o'clock is slow, so a local tutor's earliest offer tends to be later than the family wanted, and the set of people who clear both the specification bar and the commute bar is small. Online delivery drops the commute condition and keeps the one that matters. That is the argument, and it is about logistics rather than about screens being superior.

The published Dubai rates frame the money. Qualified online subject tutoring runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors stating an IGCSE rate from AED 150. In-home one-to-one is quoted at AED 180 to 500, with Bestimate's table at 180 to 350 and independent tutors asking 200 to 500. Budget online tutoring advertises much lower, from around AED 33 to 65 at EdFlik and Tutopiya. Those are each provider's own published figures, read in October 2026, and none of them is our price.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service runs only in India. What a Meydan family gets instead is one-to-one live video on Gulf Standard Time, with apparatus diagrams and the correct board's papers on a shared screen, and a recording the student can return to before a test. For the alternative-to-practical paper specifically, that is a closer match to the examination than a bench would be.

sections.heading: Starting from Meydan, with the limits stated
paragraphs: Send three things first: the school, and the board, code and tier from the examinations officer. With those we can say whether a specialist in that specification is free in your hour. Without them any provider is guessing, and a plan built on a guess about the tier is the most expensive mistake available in this subject. If you do not have the details yet, ask us anyway and we will tell you exactly what to request from the school.

Then take the free trial lesson with the named tutor who would teach your child. No card, no commitment, no automatic enrolment. The useful thing to watch is whether the tutor asks about components and tier unprompted and whether the questions they set look like the right board's questions. A written note follows the session describing the gap found, and that note is worth having even if you stop there.

Coverage limits deserve saying out loud, since nobody else in this market does. Specialists for a particular board and tier in the late-afternoon Gulf window are finite, and triple-science households often need two slots rather than one. Sometimes the honest answer is a different hour, sometimes a different weekday, sometimes a short wait. You will get which one, with a date, rather than a generalist seated in the slot.

After that the pattern is unexciting by design. Weekly sessions aimed at a named target, a written note each time, a practical-skills block early, and a deliberate switch to timed paper marking once the mocks are back. If the gap closes, we say so and stop. A provider who never reaches that point is selling a subscription rather than teaching a specification.

faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science specification my child in Meydan is sitting?
faqs.answer: Email the school's examinations officer rather than the science teacher and ask for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the components. Entries are the examinations officer's responsibility, and a teacher may know the course without knowing which tier an individual pupil was finally entered for. While you wait, look at the front of a past paper or a mock, which carries the code and component number. Keep the reply, because every later decision about tutoring, resits and tier changes depends on it.

faqs.question: What is the difference between triple science and the Cambridge double award?
faqs.answer: Triple science means three separate specifications, three sets of theory papers and three practical components, awarded as three grades. The Co-ordinated Sciences double award covers all three disciplines across a reduced content set and is awarded as two grades. The double award lightens a crowded Year 11 considerably without dropping a discipline. The catch is afterwards: sixth-form science courses vary in whether they accept it, and the position differs between A Level and the IB Diploma, so ask the destination sixth form directly.

faqs.question: Does the Core or Extended tier limit the grade my child can get?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the most important thing to establish early. A Cambridge Core entry accesses grades C to G; an Extended entry accesses A* to E. The ceiling comes from the entry rather than the teaching, so a child entered at Core cannot exceed grade C regardless of how well they are taught or tutored. Schools will discuss a tier change where the evidence supports it, but the conversation must happen before final entries close. Ask which tier your child is entered for in writing, this term.

faqs.question: What does the alternative-to-practical paper ask a Meydan student to do?
faqs.answer: It is a written paper that replaces the laboratory practical test, and most international centres in Dubai enter it. It asks a student to read apparatus diagrams, describe a method precisely enough to be repeated, name independent, dependent and controlled variables, read scales with units, identify an anomalous result with a plausible cause, and propose a specific improvement. The marks are procedural rather than factual, so three or four sessions of having their own method answers marked against a published scheme usually produces a visible change.

faqs.question: Why does my child enjoy laboratory work and still lose practical marks?
faqs.answer: Because the paper most Dubai centres enter tests laboratory thinking on paper, not laboratory skill at a bench. A confident practical student often writes a vague method, such as heat the liquid and record the temperature, where the scheme wanted the volume stated, the heating described and the measurement interval specified. A cautious classmate who writes carefully scores higher. The repair is to have several of their own written methods marked against the published criteria until precision becomes the habit rather than the exception.

faqs.question: Which exam series will an IGCSE science candidate in Meydan sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so material written for Indian candidates circulates online with entry deadlines that do not apply here. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in a May and June window and in November. Confirm the series with your school's examinations officer rather than a search result, and work from the live official timetable rather than any restatement of it.

faqs.question: Our examinations officer mentioned a timetable zone. What does that mean?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones worldwide, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. Practically, that means the only timetable worth printing is the one your centre confirms. A timetable found through a search engine may belong to another zone entirely, and the consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Should my child resit a science in November or wait for the next June?
faqs.answer: It depends on what the grade is for. A November entry returns a result in the January window, which can be in time for some sixth-form arrangements and too late for others, so check with whoever holds the offer before deciding. November also gives a short, focused preparation period, which suits a student who missed a grade narrowly and knows which paper cost them. Waiting for June gives more teaching time, which suits a student with a broader content gap rather than a technique problem.

faqs.question: How many science subjects should we tutor in the final term of Year 11?
faqs.answer: Fewer than most families start with. Three weekly science hours in the final term is a large commitment that usually diagnoses nothing, because the household cannot tell which change produced which result. The better sequence is one timed paper per discipline, marked together, to find out where the marks are actually going, then concentrate on the weakest one plus a shared practical-skills block. That pattern costs less and produces information, which is what the final term is short of.

faqs.question: Can my child practise with past papers from the other board?
faqs.answer: Sparingly, and only for content. Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel examine similar science through different question styles, mark scheme conventions and command word usage, so a student who practises mostly on the wrong board builds fluency in the wrong format and then meets the real paper cold. Use the entered board's papers for timed practice and technique work. The other board's questions are a reasonable source of extra content drilling once the specification and style are secure, and not before.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE passes does UAE equivalency actually require on the British track?
faqs.answer: The published clarification for the British track states five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one accredited Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two accredited Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market tells UAE candidates six subjects are required, which does not match the source. Verify your own case on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority rather than relying on any tutoring site.

faqs.question: Which schools do Meydan science students usually attend?
faqs.answer: There is no secondary school inside Meydan, so the cohort sits elsewhere. The nearest belt is Nad Al Sheba, with Repton School Dubai, Kent College Dubai, GEMS Modern Academy and North London Collegiate School Dubai within a short drive. Across Ras Al Khor Road families use Hartland International School, Deira International School, Dubai English Speaking College and Swiss International Scientific School Dubai. They do not all enter the same board or tier, which is why the specification question comes before the tutor question. No affiliation with any of them is implied.

faqs.question: Can science really be tutored online when the laboratory is at school?
faqs.answer: For the paper most Dubai centres enter, yes, and arguably better. The alternative-to-practical component is a written exercise about apparatus diagrams, method, variables, anomalies and improvements, so annotating diagrams on a shared screen with the mark scheme open is a close match to the examination itself. The laboratory work remains the school's job and the school does it. What tutoring adds is the written precision the paper pays for, which is exactly the part a bench session would not address.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a science tutor to a house in Meydan?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; that service runs only in India. Science support for Meydan families is one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the correct board's papers and apparatus diagrams on a shared screen and a recording the student keeps. Meydan also makes the practical case: the approach from Al Quoz or Al Khail Road between four and six is slow, so a local tutor's earliest offer is usually later than the hour a family wanted.

faqs.question: What does a block of IGCSE science tutoring cost in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Published rates put qualified online subject tutoring at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors stating an IGCSE rate from AED 150. Budget online tutoring advertises much lower, from around AED 33 to 65 at Tutopiya and EdFlik. In-home one-to-one is quoted separately at AED 180 to 500 because travel sits inside the figure. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not our price list.

faqs.question: What if no specialist in our board and tier is free at our Meydan hour?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a date. Specialists in a particular specification and tier within the late-afternoon Gulf window are genuinely finite, and a triple-science household frequently needs two slots rather than one. Sometimes the answer is a different hour, sometimes a different weekday, sometimes a short wait. What we will not do is put a generalist in the slot and present them as a specialist. No competitor page we examined in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor in Mirdif is actually being asked to fix
paragraphs: A parent in Mirdif rarely searches for an IGCSE science tutor because their child dislikes science. They search because a report has arrived with a number on it that nobody can explain. The predicted grade says 6 and the mock says 4. The teacher's comment says 'needs to apply knowledge more carefully', which is true and also useless as an instruction. Somewhere between what the student knows and what the paper rewards, marks are leaking, and the point of a tutor is to find the leak rather than to teach the whole syllabus again from Chapter 1.

IGCSE science is unusually diagnosable, because the assessment is public. Cambridge publishes the syllabus, the specimen papers and the mark scheme for every component. That means a competent tutor can take a student's own mock script, lay it next to the mark scheme, and tell you in one sitting whether the problem is recall, calculation, command-term reading, practical write-up, or simply running out of time on Paper 4. Those five faults need five different terms of work. Buying generic 'science tuition' for a command-term problem is how families in Mirdif spend AED 4,000 and move a grade by nothing at all.

The second thing a Mirdif parent is often asking without saying it is which syllabus their child is on. Mirdif and the eastern suburbs feed a mixed set of schools: British-curriculum schools entering Cambridge IGCSE, a Taaleem IB school running MYP sciences before the Diploma, and Indian-curriculum schools where a cousin or neighbour is sitting something else entirely. Two Year 11 students on the same street can be sitting Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Extended and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1, which have different papers, different practical arrangements and different past-paper banks. A tutor who teaches 'IGCSE chemistry' in the abstract will waste the first month working from the wrong specification.

Then there is the Core and Extended question, which is the single most consequential decision in IGCSE science and the one least often explained to parents. A Core entry means the student sits Paper 1 and Paper 3, is not examined on the supplement content, and cannot be awarded a grade above C. That is a ceiling, not a difficulty setting. A student heading for IB Diploma Chemistry or A Level Physics who has been entered on Core has a progression problem that no amount of revision in April will solve, because the grade itself will not go high enough. Finding that out in Year 11 is common. Finding it out in time to ask the exams officer to change the entry is less common.

So this page is written from the subject rather than from the neighbourhood. It sets out the syllabus codes a Mirdif student might be sitting, the weighting of every component, where the mark scheme actually takes marks away, how the practical papers are taught without a school laboratory, and what the local market charges for all of it. Lessons from IB Gram are delivered one to one over live video. We do not send a tutor to a Mirdif address; home visits are a service we run only in India, and the comparison table further down sets out honestly what that choice costs and what it buys.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-mirdif.programmesIntro: Mirdif families usually arrive at IGCSE science from one of three directions: a British-curriculum school running Cambridge, an IB school where MYP sciences come first, or a transfer from another system mid-Key Stage 4. Each needs a different starting diagnosis.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Sciences
programmes.description: The route most Mirdif British-curriculum students take. Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 each run a Core tier and an Extended tier, with three assessed components: a multiple-choice paper, a structured theory paper, and either a live practical test or the written alternative to practical. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 compresses all three subjects into a double award, and Combined Science 0653 into a single award.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai schools enter candidates through their own Cambridge centre, and the centre sits in one of six administrative timetable zones. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask your school's exams officer which zone it sits in before you plan revision around any published date.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Sciences
programmes.description: The other board a Mirdif student may be sitting: Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 and Science Double Award 4SD0. The structure is different in a way that matters for revision. There is no separate practical examination; experimental skills are assessed inside the written papers, so a student needs to be able to describe, criticise and improve a method in prose rather than perform it under timed conditions.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson runs International GCSE exams in May and June and again in November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always work from the live timetable on the Pearson support site rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Uptown School in Mirdif runs the Middle Years Programme, so some students in the area meet sciences through MYP criteria rather than an exam board. Assessment is criterion-referenced on a 1-8 scale across knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. The content overlaps IGCSE heavily; the assessment language does not.
programmes.countryNote: An MYP 5 student in Mirdif who transfers to a British-curriculum school for Year 11 arrives with strong investigation skills and no experience of a timed multiple-choice paper. The gap is almost never knowledge. It is pace, command-term convention and the habit of writing to a mark allocation, and it usually takes six to eight weeks of past-paper work to close.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme Sciences
programmes.description: Where a strong IGCSE science student in Mirdif often goes next. DP Biology, Chemistry and Physics run at Standard and Higher Level with a shared internal assessment: a single scientific investigation marked against published criteria. The jump from IGCSE is less about new topics than about uncertainty, error analysis and sustained independent write-up.
programmes.countryNote: If Diploma science is the plan, the IGCSE entry tier decides whether it is available. Schools commonly expect a grade 6 or 7 at IGCSE for Higher Level science, which a Core entry cannot produce. A Mirdif family thinking about the Diploma should settle the Core and Extended question in Year 10, not in the spring of Year 11.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-mirdif.subjectsIntro: These are the science components Mirdif students ask for most often, with what each one actually assesses and where the mark scheme takes marks back. A tutor who cannot name the loss point is not diagnosing anything.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: Moles and stoichiometry carry the calculation load, and electrolysis plus organic chemistry carry the recall load. Extended adds the supplement content that most higher-mark questions sit on. The commonest loss is a correct method with an unbalanced equation underneath it, which takes the method marks away with it.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Electricity is where Mirdif students lose most marks, usually because series and parallel reasoning is memorised as rules instead of understood as current and potential difference. Momentum, moments and the thermal topics reward clean working. Units and prefixes alone account for a steady drip of single marks across Paper 4.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Heavier on recall than the other two, which misleads students into thinking it is the easy one. The marks are in precision: transport in plants, the nitrogen cycle and inheritance are all marked on named structures and named processes. A vague answer that is not wrong still scores nothing.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three sciences in one qualification worth two grades. The content per subject is reduced but the paper is longer and switches discipline without warning, so revision has to be interleaved rather than blocked. Students who revise one science at a time typically underperform on this syllabus.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade covering biology, chemistry and physics. Suited to students who need a science qualification rather than a science pathway. Worth checking against progression plans early, because it is rarely accepted as a prerequisite for Higher Level Diploma science or A Level.

subjects.name: Paper 6: Alternative to Practical
subjects.description: A one-hour written paper about experiments: reading apparatus, tabulating results, plotting, identifying variables, spotting the flaw in a described method. It is teachable entirely online because it is a paper about experimental reasoning, not a test of hands. Most students have never been taught it as a separate skill.

subjects.name: Paper 5: Practical Test
subjects.description: A timed hour and a quarter at a bench, where marks go to significant figures, sensible axis scales, controlled variables and honest anomalies. Online work cannot replace bench time, but the recording, graphing and evaluation marks are the majority of the paper and they can be drilled from the student's own school practicals.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Same chemistry, different examination architecture. Practical skills sit inside the written papers, so a student must be able to criticise a method in writing. The question style is less heavily scaffolded than Cambridge, which rewards students who can structure an answer without being prompted step by step.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Formula handling is more exposed than in Cambridge, with more multi-step calculation inside single questions. Students who are used to being given the rearranged equation lose marks here. The fix is mechanical: rearrange before substituting, every time, and carry units through the working.

subjects.name: MYP Sciences, criteria A to D
subjects.description: Knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on impacts, each marked out of 8. Criterion B and C work is where most of the marks and most of the deadline pressure sit, and both are assessed on the student's own design decisions rather than on the result they got.

subjects.name: Maths skills inside science
subjects.description: Standard form, significant figures, rearranging, gradients from graphs and percentage change. A surprising share of lost science marks are arithmetic, not science. Diagnosing this early stops a family paying for chemistry lessons to fix a maths problem.

subjects.name: Exam technique for science papers
subjects.description: Command-term reading, mark-allocation budgeting, and the discipline of answering the question asked rather than the question revised. State, describe, explain, suggest, calculate, determine and compare each have a defined expectation, and treating them as synonyms is the single most common cause of a predicted 7 becoming an actual 5.

sections.heading: The science routes a Mirdif student could be on, and why it decides everything else
paragraphs: Before any tutoring starts, one question has to be answered precisely: which syllabus, which tier, which board. In Mirdif this is not a formality. A single Year 11 cohort in the eastern suburbs will contain students sitting three separate Cambridge sciences, students sitting Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award, students on Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers, and students finishing MYP 5 who will not sit an external science paper at all. The revision material, the past-paper bank and the practical arrangements differ in each case.

The answer is on the student's statement of entry, which the school issues before the series, and the exams officer can confirm it sooner. Ask for the syllabus code, not the subject name. Chemistry 0620 and Chemistry 4CH1 are both called IGCSE Chemistry in conversation and are different examinations. A tutor who starts work without that code is guessing, and the guess is usually Cambridge because it is more common, which leaves Edexcel students doing the wrong style of question for a month.

Tier matters as much as board. The table below sets out the papers each Cambridge route actually sits and what grades the route can award. Read the last column first. A Core entry is not an easier version of the same qualification; it is a different qualification with a lower ceiling, and that ceiling is set by the entry, not by the student's performance. So the first job in any Mirdif enquiry is to establish the route and the tier from the school in writing, because a term of well-planned work aimed at the wrong ceiling still ends at that ceiling.

sections.heading: Component weightings, and the specific place each paper takes marks back
paragraphs: The three-component split is the most useful number in IGCSE science and the least known among parents. On the Cambridge single sciences, the multiple-choice paper carries 30 per cent of the grade, the structured theory paper carries 50 per cent, and the practical component carries 20 per cent. A student revising only content is optimising the 50 per cent and ignoring half of the rest.

That arithmetic changes what a term of tuition should contain. A student two grades short on theory needs structured-question drilling. A student whose theory is fine and whose overall mark is still short is almost always losing it on the multiple-choice paper through careless elimination, or on the practical paper because nobody taught it. Twenty per cent of a grade is roughly a grade and a half of movement on its own, and it is the cheapest 20 per cent in the qualification to improve, because the skills are finite and repeat every series.

The table names where each component loses marks. These are not general observations. They are the faults that recur across scripts: command terms read as invitations to write everything known, significant figures carried inconsistently from a table into a graph, methods described without a control or a repeat, and calculations substituted before rearrangement so that an arithmetic slip takes the whole question down. Each of those faults has a fixed remedy, which is why they are worth naming: the remedy is a habit drilled to the point of boredom rather than a concept explained once and forgotten by the following week.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: Every Cambridge science syllabus runs two tiers, and the entry is made by the school. On Core, the student sits Paper 1 and Paper 3, is examined only on the core content, and can be awarded grades C to G. On Extended, the student sits Paper 2 and Paper 4, is examined on the core plus the supplement, and can be awarded A* to E. A student entered on Core who answers every question perfectly receives a C.

This is where Mirdif families most often discover a problem too late. A school may place a student on Core in good faith after a weak Year 10, and nobody connects that decision to a Year 12 plan that assumes a grade 6 in Chemistry for Higher Level Diploma science. By March of Year 11, after the final entry deadline has passed, the conversation is no longer about revision. It is about whether the student resits in the November series or changes their Diploma subject choices.

The practical advice is unglamorous. Ask, in Year 10, which tier each science is entered at and what the school needs to see to move a student up. Supplement content is a finite list, published in the syllabus, and six to ten weeks of focused work on it is often enough to make an Extended entry defensible. The table sets out what the two tiers differ on so that a parent can have that conversation with evidence rather than with worry.

sections.heading: How the practical papers are taught without a school laboratory
paragraphs: Parents reasonably ask how an online IGCSE science tutor can help with a practical component. The honest answer begins by separating the two practical routes. Paper 5 is a live bench test, and nothing delivered over video replaces time with apparatus. Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is a written paper about experiments and is in no sense a test of manual skill. Most Mirdif schools enter candidates for Paper 6.

Even on Paper 5, the majority of available marks are not awarded for handling equipment. They are awarded for recording readings to a consistent precision, building a results table with correct headings and units, plotting with sensible scales, drawing a line of best fit that respects the data, identifying and commenting on anomalies, and writing an evaluation that names a real limitation and a real improvement. Every one of those is a paper skill and every one can be taught and marked remotely using the student's own school practical sheets.

The method is simple and repeatable. The student brings the write-up from the practical their school ran that week. The tutor marks it against the published criteria, shows which marks were available and not taken, and then hands over a past-paper question on the same apparatus. Over six sessions the student stops producing a description of what happened and starts producing a document an examiner can award marks to. For Edexcel candidates the same reasoning is worth more, because it is assessed inside the written papers rather than quarantined in one component.

sections.heading: Command terms: the cheapest marks in IGCSE science to recover
paragraphs: If one change moves an IGCSE science grade faster than any other, it is teaching the student to read the command term and answer that term only. State means give a fact with no reasoning. Describe means say what happens, in order, without explaining why. Explain means give a cause, and an answer with no causal link scores nothing however correct it is. Suggest means apply known science to an unfamiliar situation and will not be in any revision guide. Calculate requires working. Determine usually requires reading a value off something first. Compare requires both sides in the same sentence.

Students who have never had this taught treat all seven as a general instruction to write what they know about the topic. Examiners do not reward that, and the student experiences the result as unfairness, which makes it worse because effort stops feeling connected to outcome. Showing a student two of their own answers, one that scored and one that did not, usually fixes the misunderstanding in a single session. Making the habit stick takes a term of marked practice.

The second half of the same skill is mark budgeting. A four-mark question wants four distinct creditable points, not one point expressed four ways. A two-mark calculation wants the working and the answer with a unit. Teaching a student to glance at the mark allocation before writing is unexciting and recovers a steady stream of marks across every paper in the series, which is exactly the kind of gain that shows up in a mock score three weeks later.
bullets: State, describe and explain are three different instructions, not three registers of the same one
A suggest question is deliberately unfamiliar; the content is not missing from revision
Mark allocation tells you how many separate points the examiner is counting
Units and significant figures are marked separately from the method on calculation questions

sections.heading: Sequencing a term of past-paper work, rather than doing papers at random
paragraphs: Most families already know that past papers matter. Fewer know that doing them in the wrong order wastes them. There is a finite bank of Cambridge past papers for each syllabus, and a student who burns through whole papers in October on content the school has not taught yet learns mostly that they cannot do it. By March, when the papers would be diagnostic, the bank is used up and every question is half-remembered.

The sequence that works in a Mirdif Year 11 runs in three phases. Until the Christmas break, questions are drawn by topic from papers, not whole papers, and only on content already taught, so each one is a fair test. From January, whole sections are attempted under time to build pace, with the practical component drilled as its own strand. From the mock results onward, whole papers under full exam conditions, marked by the tutor against the mark scheme with a written loss analysis each time.

The loss analysis is the part that converts practice into movement. Every marked paper produces a short list: three question types that cost marks, with the specific reason. The next two sessions attack that list. Then another paper. A student who repeats this cycle five or six times before the June series arrives at the examination with a known, shrinking list of weaknesses rather than a vague sense that there is a lot of chemistry. It also gives a parent something checkable. Ask to see the latest loss analysis rather than asking whether the lessons are going well, because the list is evidence and the answer to the question is only an opinion.
bullets: Topic-level questions first, whole papers later, timed papers last
Never sit a paper on content the school has not yet taught
Every marked paper ends with three named loss points and a plan for each
Keep two unseen whole papers in reserve for the final fortnight

sections.heading: What IGCSE science tuition in Mirdif costs, and what the figures mean
paragraphs: Start from the cheapest end, because that is where most Mirdif searches begin. Online lessons from university-student tutors are advertised in Dubai from around AED 45 to 150 an hour; EdFlik lists rates from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52, both published on their own sites and read in October 2026. At that price a tutor can supervise homework and keep a student company through revision. What that tier generally cannot do is mark a Paper 4 script against the published scheme and name the three question types costing a grade, because that requires someone who has taught the specification.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online is quoted in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE rates from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. Named IGCSE and Diploma specialists sit at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table putting specialists at AED 200 to 450 plus. A premium named tier exists above that, where BartyED publishes AED 650. All of these are other providers' published prices, quoted with their source and date; they are the market, not an IB Gram price list.

The in-home column is the one worth reading carefully on a Mirdif page, because Mirdif is a long drive from most of Dubai's tutor supply. Bestimate puts in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors are quoted at AED 200 to 500, with monthly packages seen at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits against AED 799 a month for eight online sessions. sections.heading: Checking that a science tutor is legally permitted to teach in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a Mirdif parent is entitled to ask about it directly. Private tuition work permits were introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the permit is issued through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. It is granted free of charge for two years. Anyone telling you there is a fee, or that permits do not apply to private lessons, is wrong on a point of public record.

The eligible categories are broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. The application route is MoHRE's own service, 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time and is accessed through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you.

Two further points are specific to a parent in Dubai. A tutoring operation with premises and staff is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, so a centre and a freelancer are not interchangeable in regulatory terms. And in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, with the MoHRE code of conduct carrying a similar bar. IB Gram holds no regulator licence or accreditation and does not describe itself as having one; what we can tell you is which tutor is teaching your child and what their subject background is.

sections.heading: Why online beats a local visit for a science specialist in Mirdif
paragraphs: The case for online delivery on this page is not that it is cheaper, although it is. It is that the thing a Mirdif family needs is specific, and specificity does not survive a geographic filter. The population of tutors who can teach Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 Extended well, mark Paper 4 against the scheme and drill Paper 6 technique is not evenly spread across Dubai. Filtering that population down to those willing to drive to Mirdif on a Tuesday at 5pm leaves a much smaller group, and the binding constraint becomes the traffic rather than the chemistry.

Science tuition also happens to suit the format unusually well. Working is written on a shared screen and saved, so the student has every derivation afterwards. Past-paper scripts are annotated live in a document both people can see. Graphs are plotted and measured rather than eyeballed. A three-minute clip of an electrolysis demonstration can be paused mid-reaction, which is more than a bench can offer. Nothing about a shared whiteboard is a compromise for a subject that is examined on paper.

To be plain about what IB Gram does and does not sell: lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a tutor to a Mirdif address, and home visits are a service we offer only in India. The table of market rates above is there so you can price that choice yourself rather than take our word for it, and the free first lesson exists so you can judge the teaching before any money changes hands.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and what a science tutor may and may not do
paragraphs: IGCSE science carries less assessed coursework than the Diploma, but the boundary still matters, particularly for students who are also finishing MYP projects or starting Diploma internal assessments. The rule is simple to state. A tutor teaches, explains, questions, sets practice and gives feedback on work the student has produced. A tutor does not produce assessed work, and does not edit a piece of assessed work to the point where the words are no longer the student's.

In practice that means a tutor can teach the structure of a good evaluation, mark a student's own practical write-up against the criteria, explain why a limitation is weak and ask what a better one might be. A tutor cannot supply the limitation in finished prose for the student to copy. On a Diploma internal assessment or an Extended Essay the same line applies with sharper consequences, because an academic-honesty finding by the IB sits on the student's record, not on the tutor's.

This is worth saying plainly because parts of this market do not observe the line at all. One UAE-facing site in this search space sells completed Internal Assessments outright. That is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student who submits it. We will not do it, we will say so to a student who asks, and if a deadline is genuinely unmanageable the right conversation is with the school's coordinator rather than with a tutor. A coordinator can extend a deadline or arrange support; a tutor who writes the work can only create a problem that outlasts the assignment and follows the student into the next qualification.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge science syllabus is my child in Mirdif actually sitting?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the syllabus code, which appears on the statement of entry. The common ones are Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as a double award and Combined Science 0653 as a single award. Some Mirdif students sit Pearson Edexcel International GCSE instead, coded 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The distinction is not academic. The boards set different papers, assess practical work differently and have separate past-paper banks, so the code decides which tutor is the right match and which questions the revision should come from.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Paper 5 and Paper 6 in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Paper 5 is a live practical test lasting an hour and a quarter, taken at a bench with apparatus. Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is a one-hour written paper about experiments: reading instruments, tabulating results, plotting graphs, identifying variables and criticising a described method. Both carry 20 per cent of the Cambridge grade, and a school enters candidates for one or the other. Most Dubai schools use Paper 6. Either way, the majority of available marks go to recording, graphing and evaluation rather than to handling equipment, which is why the component is teachable online.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really prepare my child for the practical paper?
faqs.answer: For Paper 6 the answer is straightforwardly yes, because it is a written paper about experimental reasoning rather than a test of manual skill. For Paper 5, bench time has to come from school, but the marks that students most often drop are not the handling marks. They are significant figures carried inconsistently, axis scales chosen badly, lines of best fit forced through the origin, anomalies left uncommented and evaluations that name no real limitation. All of that is marked on paper and can be taught, practised and corrected over a shared screen using the student's own school write-ups.

faqs.question: My child is entered on Core science but wants Higher Level Diploma Chemistry. Is that possible?
faqs.answer: It is possible, but the Core entry is the obstacle rather than the ability. A Core entry can only award grades C to G, and most schools expect a 6 or 7 at IGCSE before admitting a student to Higher Level Diploma science. The first step is a conversation with the school about moving the entry to Extended, which is realistic if it happens before the final entry deadline. The supplement content is a finite published list and six to ten weeks of focused work on it is often enough to make the case. Ask in Year 10 if you can.

faqs.question: How many weeks of 0620 past papers does a Year 11 in Mirdif need?
faqs.answer: Fewer whole papers than most families expect, and much earlier topic-level work than most families do. A workable shape is topic-selected questions until the Christmas break, timed sections from January, and five or six full papers under exam conditions between the mock results and the series, each one marked against the published scheme with a written list of three loss points. The value is in the loss analysis rather than the volume. Keep two unseen papers back for the final fortnight so there is still a fair test left at the end.

faqs.question: Is Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610 easier than Chemistry 0620 because it has more recall?
faqs.answer: It has more recall and it is not easier, which catches out a lot of capable students. Biology marks are awarded on precision: named structures, named processes, the correct direction of a gradient, the specific hormone. An answer that is broadly right and vaguely worded scores nothing. Chemistry concentrates its difficulty in stoichiometry and electrolysis, where a student can at least see the problem coming. In Biology the difficulty is distributed, so students revise confidently and then lose single marks everywhere. Precision drills on the student's own answers are the fix.

faqs.question: Why does my child keep losing marks on explain questions in IGCSE Physics?
faqs.answer: Almost always because the answer describes instead of explaining. Describe asks what happens, in order. Explain asks why, and an answer without a stated cause scores nothing however accurate the description. Physics compounds this because the causal chain is often two steps long: current increases because resistance falls, so the potential difference across the other component drops. Students write the first half and stop. Showing a student two of their own answers, one credited and one not, usually corrects the misunderstanding in one session; making the habit automatic takes a term of marked practice.

faqs.question: Is Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 a lighter option than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: The content per subject is reduced and the award is worth two grades rather than three, so for a student who needs science rather than a science pathway it can be a sensible choice. It is not an easy option. The papers move between biology, chemistry and physics without warning, which punishes students who revise one subject at a time in blocks. Interleaved revision matters more here than on any other science route. Check progression plans too, because some A Level and Diploma Higher Level courses expect the separate single-subject award.

faqs.question: Do you cover Pearson Edexcel International GCSE science as well as Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the difference is worth understanding before lessons start. Edexcel International GCSE sciences, coded 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SD0 for the double award, run two written papers with no separate practical examination. Experimental skills are assessed inside those papers, so the student has to criticise and improve a method in prose rather than perform it. Question scaffolding is lighter than Cambridge, which rewards students who can structure an answer unprompted. Tell us the code and the tutor is matched to that specification and works from that board's papers.

faqs.question: When do IGCSE science exams actually happen for a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs its IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. The February and March series is offered to India only, so ignore any date you see for it. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. Every Cambridge centre sits in one of six administrative timetable zones, and Cambridge is explicit that using the wrong zone's timetable is the candidate's risk. Ask your school which zone it is in.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE science tutor cost per hour in Mirdif?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai market rates read in October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel priced in, and AED 200 to 450 and above for an IGCSE or Diploma specialist. A premium named tier exists above that. Those are other providers' own published figures, not ours. For IB Gram the sensible next step is the free first lesson and a short consultation rather than a rate quoted before anyone has seen a script.

faqs.question: Will a tutor come out to our villa in Mirdif for science lessons?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families one to one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, and home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation we are apologising for. Filtering the pool of tutors who teach Cambridge 0620 Extended well down to those who will drive to Mirdif on a weekday evening leaves a much smaller group, and the market rate for a visit carries the travel inside the hourly figure. The comparison table on this page sets out both sides with numbers.

faqs.question: How do I check that a science tutor is legally allowed to tutor in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tuition work permits were introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and are issued through MoHRE, free of charge, for two years. Eligible categories include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. The official route is MoHRE's 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing' service, which lists a two-working-day completion time. Ask a prospective tutor directly whether they hold the permit. Anyone who tells you it costs money, or does not apply to online lessons, is not a reliable source.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks before the science papers. Is it too late to start?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks is short but it is not nothing, and what matters is spending it on the right thing. In that window the highest-return work is usually the practical component, because it carries 20 per cent of the grade and is often the least taught, followed by command-term discipline on structured questions. Attempting to recover a whole syllabus in eight weeks produces thin coverage everywhere. A diagnostic first lesson on a recent script identifies the two or three question types costing the most marks, and the remaining weeks go there rather than back to Chapter 1.

faqs.question: Would one tutor handle all three sciences for a Mirdif student, or do we need three?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and only where the tutor genuinely has the background for each. A physical scientist can often cover Chemistry and Physics credibly at IGCSE level; Biology more often needs a biologist, particularly on the precision of named processes. Where one tutor can cover two or three, a rotation weighted towards whichever paper is furthest from target works better than splitting time evenly. Where they cannot, we say so and match a second tutor rather than stretching one person across a subject they would be learning alongside your child.

faqs.question: What should the free first science lesson actually tell me?
faqs.answer: Three things. Which syllabus and tier your child is on, stated as a code rather than a subject name. Where the marks are going, named by question type: recall, multi-step calculation, command-term reading, practical write-up or pace. And what a term of work would contain, in order, with the school's mock dates and the exam series in it. If a trial lesson ends with warm impressions and no diagnosis, you have learned very little, and that is worth knowing before you commit to a term.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-mirdif.closingBody: The fastest way to know whether tuition will help is to put a real piece of your child's work in front of someone who teaches the specification. Send a mock paper or a class test with the teacher's marks on it, tell us the syllabus code, and we will match a specialist and book a free first lesson at a time that fits a Mirdif school day. In that hour your child goes through their own script with the tutor and you get a named loss pattern and a proposed sequence of work. If it does not convince you, nothing has been spent and you still know more than you did.

Matching starts with the syllabus code on your child's entry, because the paper structure differs between them and so does the price of covering it.

intro.heading: Three sciences, two sciences, or one: the question behind the quote
paragraphs: An IGCSE science quote in Dubai is meaningless until somebody establishes what your child is actually entered for. There are three common routes through the British-curriculum schools around Mohammed Bin Rashid City. Triple award means three separate subjects, three sets of papers, three grades on the certificate: Cambridge 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, or Pearson Edexcel 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Co-ordinated Sciences, Cambridge 0654, covers all three disciplines across one set of papers and awards a double award grade. Combined Science, Cambridge 0653, awards a single grade.

That distinction is the biggest single variable in the cost. Supporting triple award means three bodies of content, three practical traditions and three sets of command-term habits. Supporting a double award means one set of papers with less depth in each discipline. A tutor who quotes an hourly rate without asking which route your child is on is quoting for an unknown quantity, and the number will be revised later.

The second variable is tiering. Cambridge entries are Core or Extended. Core papers cap the available grade; Extended papers open the full range and carry materially more content. A student entered for Core needs a different kind of support from one entered for Extended, and the honest advice for some students is to secure the Core grade rather than pay for an Extended rescue. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE does not tier its sciences the same way, which is one reason the two boards cost different amounts to support even at the same hourly rate.

The third variable is the practical component, and it is the one families almost never budget for. Cambridge IGCSE sciences include a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper worth roughly a fifth of the grade. Pearson Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead. A child moving between schools can move between those systems mid-course, and the practical paper is where that shows up as lost marks.

There is a fourth variable, and it is the one that decides how big the bill gets: scope. A triple-award student with one weak science does not need three tutors, and reading the most recent set of marked papers usually says which subject is the problem within twenty minutes. Families who buy the full set are often paying three times over for something that was one third the size. Any provider quoting a three-subject programme before seeing the marked work is quoting a scope rather than diagnosing one, and the scope is the expensive part.

Delivery, stated plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in Mohammed Bin Rashid City or anywhere else in the UAE. Visiting tutors are an India-only service. IGCSE science support here is one-to-one live video in Gulf Standard Time. For a subject where diagrams, apparatus sketches and graph work carry marks, a shared whiteboard that keeps the work after the lesson is a practical advantage, and removing travel from the price is a direct saving.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-mohammed-bi.subjectsIntro: Below are the science and science-adjacent IGCSE courses families in this district ask about, with the syllabus code where it is useful and the place marks reliably go missing.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations are the recurring failure, followed by organic nomenclature and ionic equation balancing. Extended adds the quantitative depth that Core avoids, which is where the tiering decision bites hardest.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: Electricity is the topic that breaks most students, usually because series and parallel circuits were learned as rules rather than as consequences of conservation. Unit prefixes and rearrangement cost marks on every paper.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Content volume rather than difficulty is the problem. Marks are lost on command terms, on describing a graph instead of explaining it, and on experimental design questions where control variables are omitted.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: All three disciplines in one paper set. The practical risk is uneven revision, with one discipline neglected until the mock reveals it. A single tutor across the whole syllabus is the sensible shape here.

subjects.description: One grade across the sciences. Needs breadth coverage rather than depth, and responds well to a short block built on past-paper questions by topic rather than a long teaching programme.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Underpins the science papers more than families expect. Rearrangement, ratio, standard form and graph interpretation are science marks dressed as maths, and fixing them lifts all three sciences at once.

subjects.name: Alternative to Practical
subjects.description: A written paper about experiments, worth roughly a fifth of the grade in Cambridge sciences. It rewards knowing apparatus, reading scales, identifying variables and spotting sources of error, and it is almost never revised specifically.

subjects.description: Relevant to science marks because extended-response questions are marked on whether the explanation is clear. Students who know the science and cannot structure a three-mark explanation lose marks in every science paper.

sections.heading: Triple, double or combined: the arithmetic behind the quote
paragraphs: Work out the route before you compare prices. The number of papers, the number of grades and the amount of content differ enough between the three routes that a single hourly rate produces three very different bills.

Triple award at Extended is the heaviest. Three syllabuses, each with its own multiple-choice paper, theory paper and practical component, assessed and graded separately. If a student needs support across all three, that is three weekly sessions or one long weekend block, and no honest provider will tell you otherwise. The saving available here is not a lower rate but a smaller scope: in most triple-award students one science is dragging and the other two are adequate, and a diagnostic reading of the last mock will say which.

Co-ordinated Sciences, Cambridge 0654, is the middle route. All three disciplines, one paper set, a double award grade. Depth in each discipline is lower, which means one tutor can realistically hold the whole syllabus. The weekly cost is roughly a third of a three-subject triple programme for a student who genuinely needs broad coverage.

Combined Science, Cambridge 0653, is the lightest and cheapest to support. One grade, breadth rather than depth, and a course that responds well to a short block of topic-by-topic past-paper work rather than sustained teaching.

One thing to establish in writing before any of this is priced: which route the school has actually entered your child for. Parents are frequently certain their child sits triple award when the entry says Co-ordinated Sciences, or the reverse, and the mistake usually comes to light at the mock. The examinations officer can confirm the codes in a single email. The table sets out what each route involves so you can see where your child sits before anyone quotes you an hour.

sections.heading: Core or Extended, and the decision that changes the bill
paragraphs: Cambridge IGCSE sciences are entered at Core or Extended tier. The distinction is not cosmetic: Core papers cover less content and cap the grade available, Extended papers cover more and open the full range. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are not tiered the same way, which is one reason two students at the same hourly rate can need very different numbers of hours.

The tiering decision usually arrives in Year 10 or early Year 11, set by the school on the basis of internal assessment. It is reviewable, and that is where tutoring money is sometimes well spent and sometimes wasted. A student sitting just below the Extended threshold, with a clear single weakness, is a good candidate for a short targeted block that moves them up a tier. A student well inside Core, with gaps across every topic, is not — and paying for an Extended rescue there buys a worse outcome than securing a strong Core grade.

The honest version of this advice is unpopular because it sounds like giving up. It is not. A secure Core grade on the certificate serves MoE equivalency and most university entry requirements. An attempted Extended paper that produces an unclassified result serves nothing. Ask the school what the student's internal marks say, ask what the threshold is, and make the decision on evidence rather than ambition.

What a tutor should do with this is simple. In the first session, establish the tier, confirm it against the last marked paper, and say plainly whether a tier change is realistic. If it is not, the hours go into securing the grade available rather than chasing one that is not.

sections.heading: The practical paper nobody budgets for
paragraphs: In Cambridge IGCSE sciences there is a component worth roughly a fifth of the grade that most students never revise specifically, because it does not feel like content. It is either the practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper, and it is written, not performed.

What it rewards is a narrow and entirely teachable set of skills. Reading a scale correctly, including the half-division. Naming apparatus precisely rather than approximately. Identifying the independent, dependent and control variables in somebody else's experiment. Explaining why a result is anomalous. Suggesting one improvement that would actually reduce the error described rather than a generic improvement. Drawing a table with units in the headings rather than in the cells.

None of that requires a laboratory, which is the point worth making for families considering online support. A student can learn to read a burette diagram, identify a control variable and critique a method on a shared screen as well as in a room, and arguably better, because the diagrams stay on the whiteboard afterwards for revision. Where a school's own laboratory time is limited, this is the component online support most reliably improves.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE handles this differently, assessing practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate component. A child who moves school mid-course can move between the two systems, and that transition is where marks quietly disappear. Establish which board and which component your child is entered for before anyone plans a revision programme around it.

sections.heading: What IGCSE science support costs in Dubai, cheapest route first
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, which is where most families start and where some should stay. Tutopiya advertises online tutoring from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. For a Year 10 student needing homework support and a bit of structure on a combined science course, that band can be entirely sufficient, and paying more for it buys nothing.

The next band up is where IGCSE science support usually belongs. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150 an hour against IB from AED 200 — a useful signal, since it is the only competitor in this market with a published hourly rate, and it prices IGCSE below IB for the same reason we would: the content ceiling is lower and the tutor pool wider. Qualified online subject tutors across the market sit roughly AED 150 to 300.

Above that sit the specialist and premium bands, published at AED 200 to 450 or more by Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650. For IGCSE science specifically, those bands are harder to justify than they are at IB Higher Level. There are more IGCSE science teachers than DP science specialists, and an Extended paper is a less rarefied thing to teach than Higher Level organic chemistry.

In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent home tutors. Monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home visits. All of those are the providers' own published figures, not IB Gram prices. We quote after a free trial, because the right number depends on the route, the tier and the weeks remaining.

sections.heading: The exam series counted backwards from the entry deadline
paragraphs: Families plan science revision from the exam date. The deadline that actually constrains them is the entry deadline, which sits months earlier and is set by the school rather than by the board.

In the UAE, Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so it is not a route available to a student in Dubai — a point worth stating because it circulates in parent groups as though it were. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year.

Two Cambridge administrative facts matter to a Dubai family. Every examination centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. That is a school responsibility, but it is worth confirming with the examinations officer rather than assuming.

For Pearson, the published pattern gives a useful shape: the November 2026 International GCSE final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so any session table should be checked against the live official timetable rather than a restated date.
