sections.heading: What MoE equivalency actually asks of your child's science grades
paragraphs: This is the part of the picture nearly every tutoring page in this market omits, and one ranking competitor gets wrong outright.

For the British track, the UAE Ministry of Education equivalency requirement is that a student passes five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

The figure to be careful about is the subject count. One ranking competitor in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced requirement is five accredited subjects at grade E or 3 or better, excluding Arabic and Islamic education. Publishing the correct number matters more than it sounds: a family planning around six when five is the requirement may pay for a subject and a tutor they did not need.

What this means for a science budget is concrete. A double award in Co-ordinated Sciences contributes two of the five. Triple award contributes three. Combined science contributes one. If the five-subject count is tight, the route your child is entered for is part of the equivalency arithmetic as well as the university one, and that is worth knowing before Year 10 choices are finalised. Verify every requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority; the process is theirs, not ours, and we neither perform nor guarantee any part of it.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science tuition money is wasted in this district
paragraphs: Three patterns account for most of it, and all three are visible before you spend.

Buying three sciences when one is the problem. A triple-award student with a weak chemistry grade and solid biology and physics does not need three tutors. Reading the last set of marked papers takes twenty minutes and usually identifies a single subject, sometimes a single topic within it. Families who buy the whole set are frequently paying three times for a problem that was one third that size.

Buying content teaching when the issue is paper technique. A student who can explain the science at the kitchen table and scores poorly on the theory paper has a structure problem, not a knowledge problem. Three-mark explanations need three distinct points, extended responses need the command term obeyed, and graph questions need the axis read before the answer is written. None of that is new content and all of it is faster to fix.

Ignoring the practical component until the mock. It is roughly a fifth of a Cambridge science grade, it is written rather than performed, and it is almost never revised specifically because it does not look like revision. A handful of sessions on apparatus, scales, variables and error critique is the highest-yield spend available in IGCSE science, and it is the one families reach for last.

There is a fourth, less common but more expensive: buying a tutor who does not know which board the child sits. A tutor teaching Cambridge 0620 habits to a Pearson 4CH1 candidate will produce confident answers to questions the student will not be asked. Establish the code on the entry, in writing, before the first session.

sections.heading: Online science support versus a visiting tutor, on cost and on pool
paragraphs: The in-home comparison for IGCSE science is less lopsided than it is at IB Higher Level, because there are more IGCSE science teachers living in Dubai than there are DP specialists. It still goes the same way, for two reasons.

The first is the arithmetic. In-home visits are published at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors, and the in-home monthly package advertised in this market works out at roughly AED 210 per session hour against roughly AED 100 for the online equivalent. The difference is travel, which a family pays for whether it is itemised or absorbed into the rate. A forty-minute round trip to District One at 17:00 has a real cost whoever carries it.

The second is the code. A triple-award student on Pearson 4PH1 needs someone who knows that specification, not someone who knows physics. Online, the constraint on matching is the clock. In person, it is the clock plus a drivable radius, and for a specific syllabus code that intersection in one evening slot gets small quickly.

There is a third consideration that is specific to science. Much of the teaching is diagrammatic: circuit diagrams, apparatus sketches, reaction schemes, graphs with gradients marked. A shared whiteboard records all of it and keeps it after the lesson, so a student revising in May can scroll back to the circuit they half-understood in January. A notebook on a kitchen table does not offer that, and for the practical and alternative-to-practical component the retained diagrams are most of the revision material.

To be unambiguous: IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE. Visiting tutors are an India-only service. The in-home figures on this page describe what the Dubai market charges for something we do not sell, and they are here because the comparison is the argument.

sections.heading: Agreeing the scope before the rate
paragraphs: The sequence is short and the first lesson is free. Tell us the school, the year group, the board, the syllabus codes and the tier. Send the most recent marked science papers, with per-question marks visible if possible. We will come back with a view on scope — which sciences actually need support and roughly how many hours — and a proposed tutor.

The trial lesson is taught by that tutor on a real topic, not by a salesperson. A useful thing to ask in it: get the tutor to walk through an alternative-to-practical question. A tutor who knows the component will talk about scale divisions, control variables and error sources within a minute. One who does not will talk about the science in the question instead.

Two things we will decline. We will not sell three sciences where the marked papers show one. And we will not promise a grade or a tier change, because nobody can, and a provider who does is selling you something they cannot deliver. If no tutor is free in your window for your specific syllabus code, we will tell you rather than substitute someone who knows the other board.

Scheduling is worth settling at the same time as scope. Secondary schools serving this district finish between 15:00 and 15:45, and a bus from District One or Business Bay adds twenty to forty minutes, so the first slot that reliably happens is around 16:45. A triple-award student needing two sciences is better served by one ninety-minute weekend session than by two rushed weekday hours, and that choice costs the same. Tell us the two windows that genuinely survive your week and we will build the sequence around them rather than around a timetable that looks neat.

faqs.question: How much does an IGCSE Science tutor in Mohammed Bin Rashid City cost?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai rates put qualified online subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Budget online options are advertised from AED 33 to 52 by Tutopiya and AED 45 to 65 by EdFlik. Specialist bands of AED 200 to 450 and above, published by Bestimate and TutorChase, are harder to justify at IGCSE than at IB Higher Level. Those are providers' own figures, not IB Gram prices. The honest number depends on whether your child sits triple, double or combined science, so we quote after a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Does tutoring three separate sciences cost three times as much?
faqs.answer: It can, which is why scope matters more than rate. A triple-award student has three syllabuses, three sets of papers and three grades, so genuine support across all three means three weekly sessions. In most cases, though, one science is dragging the set down and the other two are adequate. Reading the most recent marked papers usually identifies that single subject, and sometimes a single topic within it. Families who buy the whole set often pay three times for a problem that was one third that size. Ask for the scope to be justified from the marked work.

faqs.question: Co-ordinated Sciences or three separate sciences - which costs more to support?
faqs.answer: Co-ordinated Sciences, Cambridge 0654, covers biology, chemistry and physics across one set of papers and awards a double award grade. Separate sciences means three independent subjects, each with their own papers and their own grade: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The double award has less depth in each discipline, which means one tutor can realistically hold the whole syllabus and the weekly cost is far lower. Triple award is the expected foundation for A Level or Higher Level IB sciences; double award suits a student who needs science grades rather than a science pathway.

faqs.question: How does the Core or Extended decision change what we pay?
faqs.answer: The school decides on internal evidence, and the decision is reviewable. Core covers less content and caps the grade available; Extended covers more and opens the full range. A student sitting just below the Extended threshold with one clear weakness is a reasonable candidate for a short targeted block. A student well inside Core with gaps across every topic is not, and chasing Extended there risks a worse result than a secure Core grade. Ask the school what the internal marks say and what the threshold is, then decide on the evidence rather than on ambition.

faqs.question: Is there a separate practical paper to budget revision time for?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board. Cambridge IGCSE sciences include either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, worth roughly a fifth of the grade, and the alternative paper is written rather than performed. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE assesses practical skills inside the written papers instead, with no separate practical component. Confirm which your child is entered for with the school, because it changes what revision looks like. The alternative paper rewards naming apparatus, reading scales, identifying variables and critiquing sources of error, all of which can be taught without a laboratory.

faqs.question: Can online lessons prepare my child for the alternative-to-practical paper?
faqs.answer: Yes, and this is the component online support most reliably improves. The paper is written, not performed: it asks a student to read a scale including the half-division, name apparatus precisely, identify independent, dependent and control variables in someone else's method, explain an anomalous result and suggest an improvement that would actually reduce the error described. All of that is taught through diagrams and worked examples, and on a shared whiteboard the diagrams remain available for revision afterwards. Where a school's own laboratory time is limited, this is often the quickest few marks available.

faqs.question: Do your tutors cover both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: Yes, and we match on the syllabus code rather than the subject name. Cambridge 0620 Chemistry and Pearson 4CH1 are different papers with different practical arrangements and different mark schemes, and a tutor who teaches Cambridge habits to a Pearson candidate produces confident answers to questions the student will not face. Ask your school, in writing, which board and which codes your child is entered for. A child who has changed school mid-course is the most common case where the family and the entry no longer agree.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science do UAE students struggle with most?
faqs.answer: In the cohorts we see across Dubai, chemistry and physics generate most requests and biology the fewest, though biology trips students up on volume rather than difficulty. In chemistry the recurring failure is mole calculations, followed by ionic equations and organic nomenclature. In physics it is electricity, usually because series and parallel circuits were learned as rules rather than as consequences. In biology it is command terms and experimental design questions where control variables are left out. All three lose marks to the same underlying issue: explaining when the question asked them to explain, not describe.

faqs.question: When are IGCSE science exams held in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE examinations in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The February and March series exists but is offered to India only, so it is not a route available in Dubai, despite circulating in parent groups as though it were. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and must use the correct zone timetable, so confirm the version with your school's examinations officer rather than relying on a generic published date.

faqs.question: Do our science entries count towards the MoE equivalency subject total?
faqs.answer: For the Ministry of Education British-track equivalency, the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One ranking competitor in this market states six IGCSE subjects are required, which does not match the sourced rule. Triple award contributes three of the five, a double award two, and combined science one. Verify your own position on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority.

faqs.question: Is a monthly package better value than paying by the hour for science?
faqs.answer: Do the arithmetic before deciding. An online package advertised in this market at AED 799 a month for eight sessions works out around AED 100 per session hour. An in-home package at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits works out around AED 210 an hour. The second is not more teaching; the gap is largely travel, which the family pays for whether or not it is itemised. Ask what happens to unused sessions, whether the named tutor is guaranteed, and whether the rate holds if you drop from three sciences to one after the mock.

faqs.question: My child is in Year 11 with the series a few months away. Is it worth starting?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the shape should change. The first session ought to be diagnostic rather than instructional: a marked paper read for patterns, not for a score. In most late starts the fastest marks are technical rather than topical — obeying the command term, giving three distinct points in a three-mark explanation, reading the axis before answering a graph question, and the practical or alternative paper, which is roughly a fifth of a Cambridge grade and is usually unrevised. Content gaps then get triaged by paper weighting rather than covered in order.

faqs.question: Is one tutor across all three sciences cheaper than three specialists?
faqs.answer: For Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Combined Science 0653, yes, and it is the sensible arrangement: one tutor holding one syllabus across all three disciplines, one weekly slot, one rate. For triple award at Extended it is less realistic, because the depth in each subject is greater and a single tutor strong in all three at that level is uncommon. The usual and cheaper answer for triple award is to identify the one weak science from the marked papers and support that properly rather than spreading one tutor thinly across three.

faqs.question: Is online science tuition cheaper than a tutor who comes to the villa?
faqs.answer: On published figures, yes. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 350 by Bestimate and up to AED 500 by independent tutors, and the in-home monthly package in this market works out at roughly double the online equivalent per hour. The gap is travel, a genuine cost whoever absorbs it, and a round trip to District One at 17:00 is not short. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere in the UAE; visiting tutors are an India-only service, so those figures describe the market rather than anything we sell.

faqs.question: How do I know whether the problem is the science or the exam technique?
faqs.answer: Sit one full theory paper to time and have it marked properly. If your child can explain the content at the kitchen table but the paper comes back with marks lost on explanation structure, command terms and unfinished questions, the problem is technique and it is the faster of the two to fix. If the content itself is missing, the paper will show gaps clustered by topic rather than by question type. One timed paper and one honest marking session distinguishes these, and it costs a single session rather than a term.

faqs.question: What if no tutor is free for our board and our evening slot?
faqs.answer: We will say so. Matching on a specific syllabus code in a specific weekday window is a narrower request than it sounds, particularly for Pearson specifications and particularly in the weeks before a series. The realistic options then are a different evening, a weekend morning, or a short wait for a slot. We would rather disclose that than put your child with a tutor who knows the other board, because the mark schemes differ and the student would be practising the wrong habits. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all.

intro.heading: Three sciences is a sequencing problem
paragraphs: A student taking Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 as three separate IGCSEs is carrying three full syllabuses, three sets of papers and, on most entries, three practical components. That is the heaviest block on any IGCSE timetable and it is also the one most families try to support with a single generic plan. The result is predictable: all three get revised a little, none gets secured, and the student arrives at the series with three partially prepared subjects rather than two solid ones and one in progress.

The problem is not effort and it is rarely ability. It is sequencing. Three sciences cannot peak simultaneously, cannot all carry a weekly tutoring slot in a congested week, and do not need the same work at the same time. Chemistry's recall content wants a schedule running for months. Physics' electricity and electromagnetism want teaching when the school covers them. Biology's volume wants steady rotation rather than concentrated blocks. Treating them as one subject called science wastes most of the advantage of taking them separately, and it is the reason a family can spend heavily on science support across a whole year and see two of the three grades move.

Motor City is a favourable place to run a proper sequence, because GEMS Metropole School sits inside the community and the school run is short. Students are often home by about half past three, which makes a 16:30 session realistic and makes short frequent contact practical. Across most of the Dubailand corridor a student is not at a desk before half past five, and three sciences in that window is considerably harder to arrange. The sequence below assumes the Motor City timings; families further out in the corridor should expect to run it on one slot rather than two.

This page lays out the sequence: what each science needs in Year 10 and what it needs in Year 11, a weekly rotation that keeps all three alive without paying for three slots, what each mock in the cycle should be used for, and the entry and timetable checks that three science entries make more consequential than one. It also prices the whole thing by stage, because three subjects at a weekly hour each is the most expensive pattern available and almost never the right one.

Two practical notes. UAE candidates sit the June series and the November series; Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so a plan built around a March window is built on a date that does not apply. And teaching for UAE families is delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, sessions run 45 or 60 minutes from 16:30 to 21:00, and there are no home visits anywhere in the UAE.

sections.heading: Sequencing three sciences across two years
paragraphs: The useful question is not how to revise three sciences but when to do what in each. They have different shapes. Chemistry has a large block of pure recall that rewards a long schedule. Physics has two or three topics that account for most of its loss and are best taught in term, while the school is covering them. Biology is broad and shallow, which makes rotation the right approach and concentrated blocks the wrong one. A plan that treats all three identically is working against the structure of each.

Year 10 is where sequencing pays. Moles arithmetic in chemistry, graph and formula skills across all three, and the start of the chemistry recall schedule all belong here, because each one underpins something later and because a recall schedule started in the spring of Year 10 is still running at the series. A family that uses Year 10 well needs considerably less in Year 11, which is the opposite of how most spending is distributed.

Year 11 autumn is coverage and the physics loss topics. Every science should have been through its syllabus once before the winter mocks, because a mock sat on partially taught content produces a misleading score and wastes the most useful diagnostic of the year. Electricity and electromagnetism should have been taught properly rather than skimmed, because they are the single heaviest loss area across Dubai cohorts.

Year 11 spring is technique and the practical block, with the recall schedule continuing underneath. Full timed papers begin after the mocks and run to the series, one per science on a rotating fortnightly cycle rather than three a week, which is unsustainable. If Ramadan falls in that window, the long papers move earlier and the Ramadan weeks become recall and review, which the chemistry and biology content suits particularly well.

sections.heading: A rotation that keeps three subjects alive on one slot
paragraphs: Three weekly sessions for three sciences is the most expensive pattern available and, in a congested Dubai week, usually the least sustainable. By week four something has been displaced by a fixture, by week six the between-session work has stopped, and the family is paying for three slots and getting two. A rotation solves the scheduling problem and, done properly, loses very little.

The mechanics are simple. One weekly slot rotates between the three sciences on a fixed cycle, so each gets taught every third week. The two not being taught get short work set and marked — recall sets, a few past questions, a graph to plot — which the student does alone and which the tutor reviews at the start of the next session in that subject. A running error log per subject means nothing is forgotten across the gap, which is the thing families fear about a rotation and the thing a log removes.

What makes it work is that most of what three sciences need between sessions is short, repetitive and does not require a tutor present: recall testing, formula practice, plotting a graph, marking an answer against a scheme. Those are exactly the tasks that should not be consuming paid session time anyway. The session is for diagnosis, teaching and marking; the volume happens between sessions.

The rotation breaks down in one specific case, which is when one science is materially behind the other two. Then the right answer is a single-science intensive of six to ten sessions instead of the rotation, returning to rotation once the gap has closed. What does not work is adding an intensive on top of a rotation, because that creates four science commitments in a week and the between-session work — which is where most of the learning happens — stops immediately.

sections.heading: What each mock in the cycle is actually for
paragraphs: Most Dubai schools run at least two rounds of internal examinations across Year 10 and Year 11, and in three sciences that produces six or more marked scripts. Those scripts are the best data a family will ever get and most of it is read once, for the score, and then filed. Each round has a different job and knowing which changes what you do with it.

A Year 10 end-of-year examination is a coverage check and a tier indicator. It tells you whether the student is keeping pace in each science and it is the evidence the school will use when deciding Core or Extended entries. If a family wants an Extended entry that the school is hesitant about, this is the round where marked evidence matters, and the window to produce it is the term before.

The Year 11 winter mock is the diagnostic round and the most important one. Sat on a fully taught syllabus, it produces a list of habits per science: answering without working, rounding partway, command-term mismatch, running out of time on the long paper. That list, not the three scores, is what the spring plan should be built from. One session spent reading all three scripts together is usually the most productive hour of the year, because the same habit frequently appears in all three.

Any later internal round is a check on whether the habits have changed, and it should be read against the winter list rather than for its score. Habits that are closing confirm the plan; habits that repeat mean either the between-session work is not happening or the diagnosis was wrong. Both are better established in March than in June, which is the whole argument for treating a mock as data rather than as a verdict.

sections.heading: Entry, tiers and the clash risk of three science entries
paragraphs: Three science entries make the administrative side of an IGCSE year more consequential than it is for a student taking one. There are more papers to fit in the window, more tier decisions to track, and more opportunity for a timetable misreading to cost something real. All of it is checkable with one email to the examinations officer, and almost nobody sends it.

Ask for four things per science: the board, the syllabus code, the tier of entry, and whether the practical component is the alternative-to-practical paper or a laboratory assessment. The tier matters because a Cambridge Core entry is commonly capped at grade 5 or C, and a student aiming at an A Level or IB Higher Level science generally needs Extended. The board matters because Pearson's science codes have their own paper structures. And the practical component matters because it determines whether the four-session practical block is relevant.

The Cambridge zone rule is where three entries raise the stakes. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and notes that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong one. A student with three science papers plus everything else has more dates to coordinate, so checking against the wrong zone's timetable is a genuine risk rather than a theoretical one.

On the series themselves: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and the February/March series offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so open the live official timetable rather than trusting any restatement.

sections.heading: Ramadan, study leave and the final six weeks with three sciences
paragraphs: The last stretch of a three-science year has two features that a generic revision plan does not account for: the Ramadan period, where it falls before a June series, and study leave, where a student suddenly has unstructured time and three subjects to divide it between. Both reward planning and punish improvisation.

During Ramadan, school hours shorten, afternoon concentration is lower, and the productive window moves to after Iftar. For three sciences that is actually workable, because a large share of what remains to be done at that stage is recall: the chemistry qualitative analysis tables, biology definitions credited against specific wording, and the physics formulae not provided in the examination. All of it is short, repetitive and well suited to a post-Iftar session between 20:30 and 22:00. What does not fit is a full-length timed paper, which means those have to be front-loaded into the earlier spring.

Study leave is the opposite problem: too much unstructured time and no external schedule. The failure mode is a student who revises whichever science feels most urgent that morning, which means the subject they are worst at gets avoided. The remedy is a written rotation with a fixed allocation per science per day and one timed paper per science across the period, so the distribution is decided in advance rather than by mood.

A specific caution about the final fortnight with three sciences: no new topics. A topic started that late competes for attention with consolidating everything already learned across three subjects, and the trade is almost never worth it. The last two weeks should be recall spot-checks, marked paper review and the error logs. If a topic is genuinely untaught at that point, the honest conversation is about which grade is reachable rather than about covering it.

sections.heading: What three sciences cost, and the order to buy in
paragraphs: Three sciences at a weekly hour each is the most expensive support pattern available on an IGCSE timetable and almost never the right one. The published Dubai bands, read in October 2026: Tutopiya from AED 33-52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45-65 at the entry level; Unitors IGCSE tuition from AED 150 and IB from AED 200; Bestimate's 2026 rate table at AED 150-300 for qualified online subject tutors, AED 180-350 for in-home one-to-one and AED 200-450 or above for IGCSE and IB specialists, with independent home tutors reaching AED 500 once travel is included; TutorChase at AED 270; BartyED at AED 650.

At the AED 150-300 band, three weekly hours across a twelve-week term is AED 5,400-10,800. The same term as a rotation on one slot is AED 1,800-3,600, with the between-session work doing the volume. The shared practical block is a further AED 600-1,200 and serves all three sciences at once. That is the arithmetic that should drive the decision, and it is why buying order matters more than hourly rate.

The sensible order is: the command-term session first, because it is one session and transfers across all three sciences; then the shared practical block, because it is four sessions and also serves all three; then the rotation, which keeps all three alive on one slot; and only then a single-science intensive if the marked scripts show one subject materially behind. Broad content review across three sciences is the most expensive pattern per mark recovered and the one most often requested.

IB Gram publishes no fixed hourly rate on this page because subject, tier and urgency move it, and a quote follows the free diagnostic lesson. Published monthly packages in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions, which maps onto a rotation plus the practical block. For context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in Dubai private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total.

sections.heading: Scheduling three sciences from Motor City
paragraphs: Motor City is the easiest postcode in this corridor for a three-science plan, and the reason is the school run. GEMS Metropole School sits inside the community, so students are often home by about half past three and a 16:30 session is realistic. Early sessions are better than late ones for recall and procedural work, which is most of what three sciences need between teaching.

That also makes a 45-minute slot practical, which matters more here than it looks. The rotation described above works on one weekly session, but a family who wants two — the rotation plus a timed paper review in the final term — can fit both into a week at 16:30 and 18:00 on different days without displacing anything. From Arabian Ranches 3, Town Square or DAMAC Hills, where students are not at a desk before half past five, the same pattern is considerably harder.

A visiting tutor cannot offer either shape. Forty to sixty minutes of travel each way means a two-hour minimum booking and a latest workable start of roughly 18:30, so three sciences become one long appointment rather than a rotation with short between-session work. The published premium for the visit is AED 30-150 an hour over the equivalent online band, and in a three-science plan it buys presence at the cost of the session structure the plan depends on.

Home visits remain the right purchase for some students — a younger child who needs an adult present, or one whose written method needs correcting as it is produced. IB Gram does not offer them anywhere in the UAE; that is an India-only service, and we have no UAE office, centre or branch. The comparison here is informational rather than persuasive.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we do not claim
paragraphs: Send the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the practical component type for each science, plus marked mocks if there are any. A specialist runs a free diagnostic lesson that reads all three scripts together, because the same habit frequently appears in all three, and a written note follows within a working day with a habit list per science and a proposed rotation. Nothing is charged before you read it.

Availability is deep for Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 at UAE evening slots, and a match normally takes one to three working days. A tutor who covers two of the three to a high standard is common and worth asking for, because the rotation runs better with fewer relationships; one who covers all three at Extended level with equal command of the mark schemes is rarer. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free, the tutor comes from our India-based faculty teaching on Gulf Standard Time, and we say so before the booking.

On materials: Cambridge and Pearson specifications, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright. We work through them on screen in session and link the official sources so you can obtain them legitimately. And the claims we do not make. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership from Cambridge, Pearson, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education or MoHRE. We are not an examination centre and cannot enter a candidate; entries go through your school or an approved private-candidate centre, which sets its own fees and deadlines. We hold no KHDA Educational Services Permit and have no UAE office. Private tutoring is regulated: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws — no fine schedule has been published, so no amount appears here.

process.title: Confirm four things per science
process.description: Board, syllabus code, tier of entry and practical component type, from the examinations officer. With three entries that is twelve pieces of information and one email, and it determines which past papers are worth doing and whether the shared practical block applies.

process.title: Read all three marked scripts together
process.description: The same habit — answering without working, rounding partway, command-term mismatch — frequently appears in all three sciences. Reading them together finds that, and one session fixing a shared habit is worth three sessions fixing it separately in each subject.

process.title: Buy the shared things first
process.description: The command-term session is one session and serves all three sciences. The alternative-to-practical block is four sessions and also serves all three in method. Together they cost less than a term of one weekly slot and usually move more marks across the whole science block.

process.title: Run a rotation, not three slots
process.description: One weekly session rotating between the three sciences on a fixed cycle, with recall and short work set and marked in the other two. A running error log per subject means nothing is lost across the three-week gap, which is the only real objection to a rotation.

process.title: Switch to an intensive only when one science falls behind
process.description: If the marked scripts show one subject materially behind the others, replace the rotation with a six to ten session intensive in that subject and return to rotation afterwards. Adding an intensive on top of a rotation produces four commitments and the between-session work stops.

whyPoints.title: Three sciences treated as a sequence
whyPoints.description: Chemistry has a recall block that wants months, physics has loss topics best taught in term, and biology wants steady rotation. A plan that treats all three identically works against the structure of each, and we sequence them across both years instead.

whyPoints.title: One slot, three subjects
whyPoints.description: A rotation with short between-session work and a running error log per subject keeps all three alive on one weekly session. At published bands that is AED 1,800-3,600 a term against AED 5,400-10,800 for three weekly hours, and it survives a congested Dubai week.

whyPoints.title: The shared blocks bought first
whyPoints.description: The command-term session is one session for all three sciences. The alternative-to-practical block is four sessions for all three in method. Both come before any single-subject teaching because they are the cheapest marks on the whole route.

whyPoints.title: Mocks read as data per round
whyPoints.description: A Year 10 end-of-year paper is a tier indicator. The Year 11 winter mock is the diagnostic round. Later rounds are habit checks against the winter list. Each has a different job, and reading them for the score alone discards most of the information.

whyPoints.title: Three entries checked administratively
whyPoints.description: Three science papers plus everything else makes the Cambridge zone timetable check consequential rather than clerical. Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone version, so the zone comes from the examinations officer first.

whyPoints.title: Ramadan and study leave planned, not improvised
whyPoints.description: Front-load the long papers, use short post-Iftar sessions for the recall that three sciences are full of, and write a fixed daily allocation for study leave so the weakest science does not get avoided. No new topics in the final fortnight.

faqs.question: How do we support three IGCSE sciences without paying for three slots?
faqs.answer: Run a rotation. One weekly session cycles between physics, chemistry and biology on a fixed three-week pattern, with short recall and practice work set and marked in the two not being taught, and a running error log per subject so nothing is lost across the gap. At published Dubai bands that is roughly AED 1,800-3,600 for a twelve-week term at the AED 150-300 band, against AED 5,400-10,800 for three weekly hours — and it survives a congested week, which three separate slots usually do not.

faqs.question: Does a three-week gap between physics sessions lose progress?
faqs.answer: Not if the gap is managed. The reason it works is that most of what three sciences need between sessions is short, repetitive and does not require a tutor present: recall testing, formula practice, plotting a graph, marking an answer against a scheme. Those should not be consuming paid session time anyway. The error log per subject is what prevents drift, because the next physics session starts by reviewing the log rather than by rediscovering where the student was.

faqs.question: Which science should we put first in the rotation?
faqs.answer: Whichever the marked scripts show furthest behind, and then rebalance each half term. The sequencing differs by subject too: chemistry's recall block wants a schedule running from the spring of Year 10 onwards, physics' electricity and electromagnetism want teaching in term while the school covers them, and biology's volume wants steady rotation rather than concentrated blocks. If one science is materially behind the other two, a single-science intensive replaces the rotation until the gap closes.

faqs.question: Is the alternative-to-practical block worth it for all three sciences?
faqs.answer: It is the best-value purchase on the three-science route, because the skill set is shared in method across all three. Apparatus selection and justification, control variables, instrument resolution, tabulation, anomalous results, and graph drawing and reading are the same disciplines whichever science is asking. Four sessions covers them with no new content involved, and school revision programmes routinely reach this paper last because the theory papers carry more marks. One block, three subjects.

faqs.question: What should we do with a Year 11 winter mock in three sciences?
faqs.answer: Read all three scripts together in one session, and extract a habit list per science rather than three scores. The same habit frequently appears in all three — answering without working, rounding partway through a calculation, command-term mismatch, running out of time on the long paper — which means one session fixing it is worth three. That habit list, not the marks, is what the spring plan should be built from, and it is usually the most productive hour of the whole year.

faqs.question: When does the chemistry recall schedule need to start?
faqs.answer: The spring of Year 10, not May of Year 11. Qualitative analysis — the tests for cations, anions and gases with their observations — is pure recall and has to be reproduced from nothing in the examination, which is a different ability from recognising it on a page. The method is blank recall at increasing intervals: next day, three days, a week, a fortnight, then monthly through to the series. Each attempt is five to ten minutes, and started early the whole schedule costs under three hours of a student's time.

faqs.question: Why does the Cambridge zone timetable matter more with three sciences?
faqs.answer: Because there are more dates to coordinate and therefore more opportunity for a misreading to cost something. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and notes that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. A student with three science papers plus everything else should have the zone confirmed by the examinations officer before anyone prints a timetable or books travel.

faqs.question: Should all three sciences be on the same tier?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. Schools decide tiers per subject on internal evidence, so a student can reasonably be entered Extended in biology and Core in physics if the evidence points that way. What matters is the post-16 consequence: a Cambridge Core entry is commonly capped at grade 5 or C, and an A Level or IB Higher Level science generally needs more than that. Ask for the tier per science in Year 10, while marked evidence can still change a decision.

faqs.question: How should three sciences be revised during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: By using the period for what suits it. School hours shorten, afternoon concentration drops and the productive window moves to after Iftar, which works well for the large amount of recall three sciences contain: chemistry test tables, biology definitions credited against specific wording, and physics formulae not provided in the examination. Short post-Iftar sessions between 20:30 and 22:00 are ideal for that. Full-length timed papers do not fit, so front-load them into the earlier spring rather than planning them into the period.

faqs.question: How do we stop study leave being wasted across three subjects?
faqs.answer: Write a fixed daily allocation before study leave begins. The failure mode is a student revising whichever science feels most urgent that morning, which in practice means the subject they are worst at gets avoided for a fortnight. A written rotation with a set number of hours per science per day, plus one timed paper per science across the period, removes the decision from the moment. One timed paper per science is the right volume; three a week is not sustainable.

faqs.question: Does a rotation work better with one tutor or with three?
faqs.answer: Covering two of the three to a high standard is common and worth asking for, because a rotation runs better with fewer relationships and the student re-explains less context. Covering all three at Extended with equal command of the mark schemes is rarer. Ask directly which syllabus codes a tutor has taught and which they have marked, and treat a general claim about being good at science as a no. Where one tutor covers two, the third can run as a separate shorter arrangement.

faqs.question: Does GEMS Metropole School being in Motor City make this easier?
faqs.answer: Considerably, and it is the main local advantage. A short school run means students are often home by about 15:30, so a 16:30 session is realistic — early sessions being better than late ones for the recall and procedural work three sciences depend on. It also makes two short sessions a week feasible in the final term, a rotation session plus a timed paper review. From Arabian Ranches 3, Town Square or DAMAC Hills, where students are not at a desk before 17:30, the same pattern is much harder to arrange.

faqs.question: What is the first thing to buy for a three-science student?
faqs.answer: The command-term session, because it is one session and transfers to all three sciences at once. 'State' takes a phrase, 'describe' takes what happens, 'explain' takes why, and 'suggest' takes applied reasoning in an unfamiliar context — and mismatching them is the largest avoidable loss category across all three subjects. After that, the four-session alternative-to-practical block, which also serves all three. Those five sessions cost less than a term of one weekly slot and usually move more marks across the whole science block.

faqs.question: Can we start a new topic in the last fortnight if one was missed?
faqs.answer: With three sciences, almost never. A topic started that late competes for attention with consolidating everything already learned across three subjects, and the trade is rarely worth it. The final two weeks should be recall spot-checks, marked paper review and the error logs. If a topic is genuinely untaught at that point, the honest conversation is about which grade is reachable with what is secure, rather than about covering it — and that conversation is more useful than a rushed attempt at the content.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-motor-city.closingHeading: Sequence the three, share what can be shared
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-motor-city.closingBody: Three separate sciences is the heaviest block on an IGCSE timetable and the one most often supported with a single generic plan. Sequence it instead. Start the chemistry recall schedule in Year 10 and the physics loss topics in term, keep biology on rotation, and buy the shared things first: one command-term session and one four-session practical block, both of which serve all three subjects at once. Then run a rotation on one weekly slot rather than three. Send the board, code, tier and practical type for each science and take the free diagnostic lesson.

intro.heading: Three sciences, one calendar, and a decision made years ago
paragraphs: Science revision is harder to plan than any other part of an IGCSE timetable, for a structural reason. A student taking separate physics, chemistry and biology is sitting three sets of papers with three sets of practical content, and mock season arrives in all three in the same fortnight. A student on a combined award is sitting fewer papers covering content from all three, which sounds easier and is often less forgiving, because one weak area has nowhere to hide across fewer questions.

Either way the calendar is the thing that organises the work. The award decision was taken in Year 9 or Year 10 and is effectively fixed. Tier placement, where the subject is tiered, happens late in Year 10. Entries are lodged months before the papers. Mocks land about six months out and produce the only real diagnostic a family gets. The final stretch is timed papers and nothing else. Work that fits the phase pays; work that ignores it duplicates the school day.

Mudon makes the evenings short. The community sits off Al Qudra Road in Dubailand with no secondary school inside its own boundary, so students travel to Jebel Ali School in DAMAC Hills, GEMS Metropole in Motor City, South View School towards Remraam, GEMS FirstPoint in The Villa or further along Al Khail Road. A Year 11 home after four, with homework from three sciences and the mandatory UAE subjects alongside, has perhaps two usable hours and three subjects wanting them.

The exam calendar itself is simple provided the right document is read. Cambridge runs its International GCSE exams in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered in India only, so an Indian timetable circulating in a parents' group is the wrong paper for a Dubai centre. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, stating it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

One more calendar fact shapes a Dubailand science plan, and it is not on any board timetable. The mandatory UAE subjects run alongside the IGCSE courses in every Dubai private school, with their own assessments and their own deadlines, and they land on the same evenings as science revision. A plan that treats the week as empty space outside school hours will collide with them, which is why the sequencing advice further down this page is about choosing one or two sciences rather than fitting all three in.

Delivery is one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, so a session can sit at half past four for a student home early or after eight where both parents commute. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only. The laboratory stays with the school, and this page is explicit about what that means for the practical component rather than quietly skipping it.

sections.heading: The science year in a Dubai Year 11, counted backwards
paragraphs: Take the series the student is entered for and count back. Twelve months out, in Year 10, tier placement is being decided where the subject is tiered, and the harder topics should be met then rather than left for revision. Nine months out, entries are lodged and the zone timetable is set, so the board and code for each science become fixed facts worth writing down. Six months out, mocks arrive in all three sciences at once and produce the only real diagnostic of the year.

Three months out the work should have switched from topics to papers. In science this switch is harder than in maths, because science revision feels productive when it is reading and most students keep reading. A student who has sat six full timed science papers under conditions behaves differently in the hall from one who has reread six chapters, even when the two know the same content.

Six weeks out, the only useful work is error patterns from marked scripts plus the practical and method questions, which respond quickly because they are formulaic. New content at this stage is a poor investment: anything genuinely unlearned will not be secure enough to deploy under pressure, while a habit such as always stating the because in an explanation can still be installed.

The dated anchors are worth recording, since they make the lag concrete. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Always read the live official timetable rather than a restated date, because provisional timetables can be revised.

sections.heading: Separate sciences or combined: the decision and its consequences
paragraphs: The award decision usually happens in Year 9 or Year 10 and is treated as administrative, which it is not. Separate sciences produce three qualifications with greater content depth and keep the widest sixth-form options open. A combined award produces fewer qualifications covering content from all three, with a different paper pattern and a different revision problem.

Families assume combined is easier. It is narrower, which is not the same thing. With fewer questions covering three subjects, each question carries proportionally more of the grade and a weak topic is more exposed than it would be across three separate papers. A student who is strong in biology and weak in physics can hide that imbalance better in separate sciences, where the biology grade stands alone.

What matters more than difficulty is what each permits afterwards. Some sixth forms set different entry thresholds for an A Level or Higher Level Diploma science from a combined award than from a separate one, and those thresholds are set by schools rather than by boards. For a Mudon family planning a sixth form at a different school from the current one, that is worth checking a year before applications rather than after results.

If the decision is still open, the question to put to the school is narrow: which route is my child on, what grades does each route make available, and what would the intended sixth form require from each. Three answers in writing, and the rest of the planning follows.

sections.heading: Practical skills when the lessons are online
paragraphs: Science papers assess practical skills, and an online tutor cannot run an experiment. Saying so plainly matters, because the alternative is a page that implies otherwise and a family that discovers the gap late. The practical work belongs to the school: its equipment, its safety rules and its scheme of work. What remains, and it is substantial, is everything the paper actually asks about practical work.

Practical-style questions follow patterns that are learnable away from a bench. A method has to be written so another person could repeat it, with quantities, control variables and a measurable outcome specified. A table has to be ruled with units in the headings rather than beside the values. A graph has to use a sensible scale, with the dependent variable on the correct axis and a line of best fit rather than dot-to-dot. Each of those is a rule, and rules are teachable on a screen.

The commonest losses are equally formulaic. Students name apparatus instead of describing a procedure. They identify a variable as controlled without saying how it would be controlled. They read a value from a graph without using the axes they drew. They describe a result as accurate when the question asked about precision. A fortnight of practical-question drilling moves these marks reliably, and they appear in every science paper.

Where a school offers an alternative-to-practical style paper, the same logic applies with more force, because that paper is entirely about the skills rather than the doing. Confirm with the school which paper the student sits, since it changes what the eight weeks before a series should contain.

sections.heading: Which science to fix first, and when
paragraphs: With three sciences and limited evenings, sequencing matters more than effort. The decision should come from the marked mock scripts rather than from which subject feels worst, because the feeling usually tracks the teacher rather than the marks.

Physics is typically the subject where a small intervention moves the most, because its losses concentrate in a few topics and in mathematical execution. If rearrangement and standard form are failing, fixing them raises marks in physics and in chemistry simultaneously, which makes it the efficient first move. Chemistry comes next in most cases, because its losses are mechanical: equations, state symbols, and qualitative analysis marks left unclaimed.

Biology is often last in the order and it is not the least important. Its losses are about command-term reading and terminology precision, which respond to drilling but take a steady few weeks rather than a sharp intervention. A student who starts biology work six weeks out will get less from it than one who started three months out, which is the opposite of the physics pattern.

The rule of thumb that survives contact with reality: fix shared mathematical skills first, then mechanical notation, then terminology and command terms. And resist taking all three sciences at once in tutoring. Three hours a week of input leaves no time to practise any of it, which produces three sets of homework and no improvement.

A final word on which subject the student says is worst. That judgement usually tracks the teacher, the classroom and how recent the last bad lesson was, rather than the marks. Scripts do not care about any of that, which is why the sequence should come from them. Where a student's own sense and the scripts agree, the plan is easy; where they disagree, start with the scripts and explain why.

sections.heading: Mock season across three sciences
paragraphs: Mock season is the densest fortnight of a Year 11 year and the most wasted. Three science papers come back with three grades, a conversation happens about effort, and the scripts go into a drawer. Those scripts are the only specific information anyone has about where the marks went, and they arrive at exactly the point in the calendar when there is still time to act on them.

Read properly, each script separates four failures that feel identical to a student. Content absence shows as questions untouched. Technique loss shows as right method and lost marks. Timing collapse shows as a strong first half and an abandoned final page. Misreading shows as a good answer to a question the paper did not ask, usually because a command term was skipped.

Across three sciences the pattern is often the same in all three, which is useful news. A student who skips command terms does it in physics, chemistry and biology alike, and a single fortnight of command-term drilling lifts all three. A student whose losses are content-based in only one subject has a narrower and clearer problem. Reading all three scripts together is what reveals which case you are in.

One caution on the grades themselves. Schools set mocks at different severities, and a paper marked harshly to motivate a cohort is not a forecast. Treat the number as a position and the annotations as the information, and compare any school boundary against the board's most recently published boundaries for the same paper rather than assuming they match.

sections.heading: Resits, the November route and the January lag
paragraphs: A resit is a legitimate option and it needs to be costed in time rather than only in money. UAE Cambridge candidates sit June and November, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. A student disappointed by a summer result can sit again in the autumn series, which means a term of preparation alongside the start of sixth form.

The dated lag is the part families miss. November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which means an autumn resit returns a grade in the middle of the following academic year. If a sixth-form place or a course choice depends on that grade, the receiving school needs to know the timing in advance and may need to hold a place conditionally. That conversation belongs with the school before the entry, not after the result.

The preparation itself is different from first-time revision. The content has been taught, the student has sat the real paper, and there is a script from the actual series available through the centre in some cases. The work is therefore narrow: the specific topics that failed, plus the technique that lost marks across the paper. Six to eight focused weeks is usually a better plan than restarting the syllabus.

One practical point on entries. The resit is lodged through a centre, and a student who has left the school may need to find a centre willing to enter them as a private candidate. Ask the current school early about whether it will continue to act as the centre, because arranging that late is considerably harder than preparing for the paper.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs in this market
paragraphs: Three sciences invite a budgeting mistake, which is to assume three subjects means three times the cost. In practice a well-sequenced plan buys one or two subjects at a time, so the monthly figure stays in the same band as a single-subject arrangement for most of the year and rises only for a short block before a series.

The bands themselves are published and worth checking. Budget online tutors and university students advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour in Dubai, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED.

In-home visits carry travel inside the quote at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour, Bestimate's range being AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to 500. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 budget, AED 600 to 1,200 mid and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more specialist.

For household context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year. All the figures above are market rates with their sources named rather than IB Gram prices, and a free trial lesson comes before any payment is taken.

sections.heading: Permits, coursework and the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Three administrative points sit behind a science tutoring plan in Dubai. The first is the tutor's permit. An individual giving private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service listing shows no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

The second is coursework honesty. Where a centre runs assessed practical work or a project, it must be the student's own. A tutor may teach the science, explain what the criteria reward, say that a method will not produce usable data and mark a student's own draft against descriptors. A tutor may not write, draft, complete or edit the work to completion, or supply data the student did not collect. Board material stays with its publishers and is linked rather than circulated.

The third is the mandatory UAE subjects, which compete for the same evenings. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

For those subjects, instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit with at least 25 minutes advised per lesson, and the use of different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is prohibited. The practical consequence for a science plan is scheduling: avoid putting timed science papers on the same evening as an Arabic assessment.

faqs.question: How do we plan three sciences across one Year 11 evening?
faqs.answer: By sequencing rather than splitting. Three hours of weekly tutoring leaves no time to practise any of it, which produces three sets of homework and no improvement. Read all three marked mock scripts together, identify whether the same failure runs through all of them, and start with shared mathematical skills if they are failing, because fixing rearrangement and standard form raises marks in physics and chemistry at once. Then mechanical notation in chemistry, then terminology and command-term reading in biology, which needs weeks rather than days.

faqs.question: Is a combined science award easier than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Narrower, which is not the same thing. A combined award covers content from all three sciences across fewer papers, so each question carries proportionally more of the grade and a weak strand is more exposed than it would be inside one subject's own papers. Separate sciences give three independent grades, so strength in biology can stand alone. What matters more than difficulty is what each route permits afterwards, since sixth forms set their own entry thresholds for A Level and Higher Level sciences from each.

faqs.question: When should a Mudon family switch from revising topics to doing papers?
faqs.answer: About three months before the series, and the switch should be complete by six weeks out. Science revision is unusually good at feeling productive while changing nothing, because reading a chapter feels like work and sitting a timed paper feels like a test. A student who has completed six full papers under conditions behaves differently in the hall from one who has reread six chapters, even where the two know identical content. Put a date on the switch rather than leaving it to feel right.

faqs.question: How are practical skills examined if tuition happens on a screen?
faqs.answer: The experiment belongs to the school; the paper examines the skills, and those are rules that can be drilled anywhere. A method must be repeatable by a stranger, with quantities and control variables specified. Units belong in table headings rather than beside values. Graphs need sensible scales, the right axis for the dependent variable and a line of best fit. Accuracy and precision are different questions. A fortnight of practical-question drilling moves marks that appear in every science paper.

faqs.question: What should we do with the three mock scripts the school returned?
faqs.answer: Read them together before any tutoring is booked. Each script separates content absence, visible as untouched questions, from technique loss where the method was right, from timing collapse showing as an abandoned final page, from misreading where a good answer addressed the wrong question. Students skip command terms consistently across subjects, so the same fortnight of drilling can lift all three sciences. Treat each grade as a position rather than a forecast, since schools set mocks at different severities.

faqs.question: Which science usually gives the fastest improvement?
faqs.answer: Physics, in most cases, because its losses concentrate in a few topics and in mathematical execution. If rearrangement, standard form or gradients are failing, repairing them raises marks in physics and chemistry at the same time, which makes it the efficient first move. Chemistry follows, since its losses are mechanical: unbalanced equations, missing state symbols and unclaimed qualitative analysis marks. Biology responds more slowly because it depends on terminology precision and command-term reading, so it should be started earlier than families expect.

faqs.question: Can a student sit an IGCSE science resit in the autumn?
faqs.answer: Yes. UAE Cambridge candidates sit the June and November series, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. The lag is the part to plan for: November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, so an autumn resit returns a grade in the middle of the following academic year. If a sixth-form place depends on it, tell the receiving school before the entry. Also confirm early which centre will enter the student, since arranging that late is harder than the revision itself.

faqs.question: Do the sciences at my child's school use the same exam board?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily, and assuming so is the most common revision error in this market. Several Dubailand schools run Cambridge for one science and Pearson Edexcel for another, and the papers are not interchangeable: question styles, scaffolding and mark-scheme conventions all differ. Ask for a written list of subject, board and code for each science. Then check the code on the front of any past paper the student has been given against that list. It takes one message and it protects an entire term of practice.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the papers should a science block start?
faqs.answer: Six to eight for technique work, which is the right length for drilling practical questions, command terms and working shown while leaving time to practise between sessions. Longer blocks are for content, and content needs three months or more to become secure enough to use under pressure. The marked mock script tells you which you need: scattered small losses across many questions point to technique, while whole questions abandoned point to content. A provider who proposes a block before seeing a script is guessing.

faqs.question: Does the mandatory Arabic timetable affect a science revision plan?
faqs.answer: Mainly as a scheduling constraint. Every Dubai private school teaches Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies whatever curriculum it is licensed for, with KHDA's requirements implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, and those lessons and assessments compete for the same evenings as science revision. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. The practical move is simply not to schedule a timed science paper on the same evening as an Arabic assessment, which sounds obvious and is routinely overlooked.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for science tuition in Year 10 rather than Year 11?
faqs.answer: Often, and it is the least popular advice in this market. Year 10 is when tier placement is decided where a subject is tiered, and the harder topics are met for the first time. Work done then raises the available ceiling, whereas work done in the spring of Year 11 can only recover marks inside a fixed entry. One weekly hour in Year 10 aimed at the harder end of the syllabus is better value than three hours of urgent revision fifteen months later.

faqs.question: What does three sciences cost per month at market rates?
faqs.answer: Less than three times one subject, if the plan is sequenced. Buying one or two sciences at a time keeps the monthly figure comparable to a single-subject arrangement, rising only for a short block before a series. For the bands themselves, a qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band. These are published market figures rather than IB Gram prices.

faqs.question: Can one tutor take all three sciences for a Year 11?
faqs.answer: At IGCSE level, often yes, and there are advantages: shared calculation technique, shared graph and data skills, and one review conversation rather than three. The question to ask is which papers they have marked in each subject, not whether they can cover all three. Where the sciences sit with different boards, confirm the tutor is comfortable with both sets of conventions. If the honest answer is that one subject is a stretch, two tutors is better and costs the same per hour.

faqs.question: Our child is on a combined award and failing one strand. What now?
faqs.answer: Identify the strand precisely from the marked script, because a combined award exposes a weak strand across fewer questions and therefore costs more per weakness than separate sciences would. Then treat it as a single-subject problem: the topics inside that strand that carry the most marks in the actual paper pattern, drilled with timed questions from the award route specifically rather than from separate-science papers. Using the wrong past papers is a common error here, since the paper pattern for a combined route is its own.

intro.heading: The three-subject problem, and what it does to a budget
paragraphs: The request that arrives from this catchment most often reads something like: my child is in Year 11, struggling in science, can you help with all three. It is a completely reasonable thing to ask and it is also the most expensive way to buy IGCSE science support. Three subjects at a qualified online rate of AED 150 to 300 an hour works out at roughly AED 13,500 to 27,000 across a thirty-week year, and in practice it produces three thin efforts rather than one solid one, because the student has nine or ten other subjects and no spare evenings.

The first useful question is therefore not who to hire but what your child is actually entered for. A student taking Cambridge Coordinated Sciences, syllabus 0654, is sitting one double-award qualification that covers all three sciences at reduced depth. A student taking separate Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 is sitting three qualifications. A student on Pearson's Science Double Award 4SD0 is on a third arrangement again. The content depth, the paper count and the realistic tutoring requirement differ substantially between them, and families are frequently unsure which applies.

The second question is which of the three sciences is actually costing the grade. In our experience of this catchment it is rarely all three equally. Physics is the most commonly requested and the most commonly genuinely weak, usually because of the algebra it assumes. Chemistry difficulty is often really a mole-arithmetic problem. Biology is often a command-term problem dressed as a content problem, which is the cheapest of the three to fix and the one families least often identify. A marked script answers this in minutes; a conversation almost never does.

The third is how practical skills are being examined, because this changes what the tutoring hour should contain. Cambridge offers both a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and most international centres use the written route. Pearson assesses practical knowledge inside the written papers. Either way the marks go to planning, variables, instrument reading, tabulation, graph work and evaluation, and all of those are paper skills that can be taught on a shared screen.

On delivery, plainly: IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run only in India, and the published Dubai market rate for in-home visits is roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, which is the figure to compare against if that is the route you are considering. For a Muhaisnah family we match a subject specialist for one science at a time and teach one-to-one over live video, with a free trial lesson before anything is charged.

Nothing below is a promise about a grade. The papers are marked externally, the tier was set by the school, and the performance on the day belongs to the student. What a correctly matched tutor changes is the number of marks lost for reasons unconnected to understanding, and across three science papers that number is usually bigger than one subject's worth of content teaching could ever recover.

programmes.name: Key Stage 3 science
programmes.description: Integrated science with no external examination, which is where the quantitative foundations are either built or missed. Rearranging formulae, proportional reasoning, unit conversion and reading scales are the four that determine whether IGCSE physics and chemistry are accessible later.
programmes.countryNote: Almost nobody in this catchment buys science support at this stage and it is the cheapest point to do it, at the lower end of every published band. A Year 8 student can also take a half past five session, which a Year 11 here generally cannot.

programmes.name: Year 10 IGCSE science
programmes.description: The first examined year across either separate sciences or a double award, with tier placement being confirmed. The available work is foundational, which means one subject supported properly through the autumn and spring can change tier evidence as well as content.

programmes.name: Year 11 IGCSE science
programmes.description: The examination year. Tiers are fixed, content largely delivered, and the available work is paper technique: practical-skills questions, command terms, timed calculation and graph work. programmes.countryNote: Where most demand arrives and where three-subject requests originate. The honest advice is to pick the one science where the marked script shows the largest fixable gap, buy a bounded block, and let the school's revision programme carry the others.

programmes.name: Transition into AS sciences
