dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-muhaisnah.subjectsIntro: These are the science subjects and components Muhaisnah families name, with an honest note on which need a specialist and which do not.

subjects.name: Physics, separate award
subjects.description: The most commonly requested and most commonly genuinely weak of the three here. Electricity and waves do the most damage, and the underlying cause is frequently algebraic rather than physical. Needs a specialist if the gap is conceptual; needs a mathematics tutor if it is rearrangement.

subjects.name: Chemistry, separate award
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic families carry the paper. A student who can write equations and cannot explain a trend has a conceptual gap; a student who stalls on calculations has an arithmetic one. The two need different tutors and cost different amounts.

subjects.name: Biology, separate award
subjects.description: The cheapest of the three to improve and the least often identified correctly. Volume of content makes it feel manageable, but the marks sit in command-term precision and in reading unfamiliar methods, both of which respond within a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Coordinated Sciences, double award
subjects.description: All three sciences at reduced depth, awarded as a double qualification. Tutoring here is usually about identifying which of the three strands is weak rather than teaching all of them, because the depth is lower and the strands are examined together.

subjects.name: Combined Science, single award
subjects.description: A single award covering all three sciences, with less content again. Families sometimes assume it is the same as Coordinated Sciences and it is not: the award size and the depth both differ, which affects both university routes and tutoring need.

subjects.name: Science Double Award
subjects.description: Pearson's double-award route covering all three sciences. Paper structure and the way practical knowledge is examined both differ from the Cambridge equivalent, so a tutor familiar with 0654 is not automatically useful here.

subjects.name: Practical skills on paper
subjects.description: Planning an investigation, identifying variables, reading instruments, tabulating, plotting, interpreting and evaluating. Examined either in an alternative-to-practical paper, a practical test, or inside the written papers. Among the most efficient marks to target and entirely teachable remotely.

subjects.name: Command-term discipline
subjects.description: Describe, explain, suggest, state and compare each want a different answer. The single cheapest set of marks available across science, and the one most students are losing without knowing it, because the content was right and the answer shape was not.

subjects.name: Graph and data handling
subjects.description: Scale choice, plotting accuracy, line of best fit, gradient meaning and anomaly identification. A shared screen is a better teaching surface for this than an exercise book, because the tutor annotates the student's actual graph while they watch.

subjects.name: Quantitative skills across science
subjects.description: Rearrangement, proportional reasoning, unit conversion, standard form and significant figures. A student weak here will look weak at two sciences simultaneously, and the fix is one piece of work rather than two subject blocks.

subjects.name: Required practical knowledge
subjects.description: Specific procedures students are expected to know and describe. Learned from the specification rather than discovered at a bench, which makes it readily teachable online and a reliable source of marks in the final weeks.

subjects.name: Core and Extended tier content
subjects.description: Extended candidates sit additional content and harder question styles with a higher grade ceiling. Knowing which tier each science is entered at matters, because a student can be on different tiers in different sciences within one school.

sections.heading: Separate sciences, Coordinated Sciences or a double award: what each costs to support
paragraphs: Begin here, because the answer changes the budget by a factor of three. Separate sciences means three qualifications, each with its own full content, its own papers and its own revision requirement. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences, 0654, is a double award covering all three at reduced depth in a shared set of papers. Cambridge Combined Science, 0653, is a single award with less content again. Pearson's Science Double Award, 4SD0, is a different double-award arrangement with its own paper structure.

Families often do not know which applies, and schools do not always make the distinction clear in reports. It is worth one email to the exams officer, because the tutoring implication is direct: a double-award student usually needs help identifying which of the three strands is weak, at reduced depth, and can be served by one tutor across a bounded block. A separate-sciences student with a genuine gap in physics needs a physics specialist, and if they also have a gap in chemistry that is a second engagement rather than an extension of the first.

The table below sets out the routes with what each involves and a realistic annual cost at published qualified rates. Read the final column as the planning instruction: for a double award, one tutor and a diagnosis is usually sufficient, and for separate sciences the question is which single subject to buy rather than whether to buy all three.

One further note on grades and progression. Award size matters for later routes: a single-award qualification is not equivalent to two separate science grades, and families planning towards AS sciences should check what the sixth form requires before assuming a double or single award suffices. That is a conversation with the school rather than with a tutor, and it is free.

sections.heading: The codes, and why a science tutor must be matched to one
paragraphs: Ask the exams officer for the syllabus codes in writing, for each science separately, because a student can be on different boards for different sciences within the same school. That sounds unlikely and it is common: Cambridge sciences with Pearson mathematics is the usual split in this catchment, but Pearson sciences with Cambridge everything else happens too.

The table gives the codes you are most likely to be told, with the paper structure in outline and the practical route. Take the code to any tutor you are considering and ask them to describe its papers and how practical skills are examined on it. A specialist answers in under a minute. Someone who says the sciences are broadly the same across boards is describing the content, which is largely true, and ignoring the papers, which is where the final weeks of preparation live.

Two distinctions catch families out specifically. Cambridge separate sciences offer both a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses; which one your child sits changes what the tutoring should contain. And Cambridge offers 9-1 graded versions of its sciences alongside the letter-graded ones, which are the same content reported differently, so a report showing a numeral rather than a letter is not evidence of a different syllabus.

Confirm paper numbers, durations and practical arrangements against the board's published syllabus for your child's cohort rather than against any tutoring page, including this one, because syllabuses are reissued. What does not change is the matching principle: one subject, one code, one tutor who teaches it habitually.

sections.heading: Practical skills: examined on paper, teachable on a screen
paragraphs: The reasonable objection to online science tutoring is laboratory work, and it deserves a precise answer rather than reassurance. Hands-on apparatus time belongs to the school, which has the equipment. What the boards assess, however, is practical knowledge and reasoning expressed in writing, and that is a different thing from manipulating a burette.

Cambridge separate sciences offer two routes: a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper, with most international centres using the written route. Pearson assesses practical knowledge inside the written papers rather than separately. In both cases the marks go to planning an investigation, identifying independent, dependent and control variables, choosing a sensible range and interval, reading instruments to an appropriate precision, tabulating with consistent units and significant figures, plotting with a sensible scale, drawing and using a line of best fit, identifying anomalies, and suggesting a specific improvement rather than a generic one.

Every item on that list is a paper skill, and several are taught considerably better remotely. Plotting is the clearest example: a tutor annotating the student's actual graph live, pointing at the scale choice that cost a mark, achieves in five minutes what a written comment in an exercise book achieves in a week. Identifying a dependent variable in an unfamiliar method is reading comprehension applied to science. Suggesting an improvement is a learnable formula rather than an inspiration.

The table sets out the two routes side by side so you can establish which your child is on and what the tutoring should therefore contain. Where the school uses a practical test, the focus shifts towards recording conventions and towards rehearsing method sequences so the student is not reading a procedure for the first time under pressure. Where the written alternative applies, the focus is squarely on the question types in that paper, which are highly patterned and therefore highly drillable.

sections.heading: Where science money is wasted in this catchment
paragraphs: Five patterns, and the first dwarfs the others. Buying all three sciences at once. It triples the cost, consumes three of a Year 11 student's remaining evenings, and in practice yields three mediocre efforts because nobody has time to do the work between sessions. The student also has mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in a Dubai school, on top of nine or ten subjects, and there simply is not room.

Second, buying subject content when the loss is cross-science technique. If a student is losing marks on command terms, tabulation, graph scale and evaluation phrasing, those losses appear in all three papers and can be fixed in one short block. A family who buys three content tutors to solve a technique problem pays roughly ten times what the fix costs.

Third, paying specialist rates to repair quantitative skills. A student who cannot rearrange a formula or convert units will look weak in physics and chemistry simultaneously. That is one piece of Key Stage 4 mathematics, available at the mid band, and buying two science specialists to work around it is paying twice for a problem that is neither of theirs.

Fourth, starting after the spring mocks. By then the content window has shut, the better weekday slots are taken by school revision clinics, and only technique work remains, at the highest point of the demand curve. Fifth, buying a tutor who does not know the code. A Cambridge 0654 specialist teaching a Pearson 4SD0 candidate will cover correct science and prepare them for the wrong paper structure, and a material share of the final weeks is about paper structure.

sections.heading: Core and Extended across the sciences, and the mixed-tier surprise
paragraphs: Tiering in science works as it does in mathematics: the lower tier covers less content and caps the grade that can be awarded, while the higher tier covers additional material, asks harder question styles and opens the full range. What surprises families is that a student can be entered at different tiers in different sciences within the same school, and the report does not always make that obvious.

That matters for a budget in two ways. If the target grade in a subject sits above the ceiling of the tier your child is entered at, no amount of tutoring reaches it and the conversation belongs with the head of science rather than with a tutor. And if a student is Extended in biology and Core in physics, those are two different kinds of engagement, and treating them as one science problem will produce the wrong plan for both.

The decision belongs to the school, is based on evidence from the student's work, and is usually taken during Year 10. The sequence for a family who wants it reviewed is to ask the subject teacher what evidence would change the entry and by what date the decision must be made, then work on exactly that. A tutor promising to move a child up a tier without having seen a marked script is guessing, and in science the evidence the school looks at is usually quantitative accuracy and the ability to handle unstructured questions.

One honest word in the other direction. A secure Core grade is a better outcome than a struggling Extended one, and families who force Extended entries on borderline students in all three sciences simultaneously frequently end up with worse results across the board. The tier is a judgement about what a student can sustain across a full paper under time pressure, not a statement about their ability or their ambition.

sections.heading: Realistic monthly spend for one, two or three sciences
paragraphs: Published rates are per hour and households budget per month, so here is the translation. The figures use the published Dubai bands: budget online provision from roughly AED 33 to 65 an hour as published by two providers, qualified subject tutors at roughly AED 150 to 300, specialists at roughly AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home visits at roughly AED 180 to 500 with travel included. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a weekly hour are AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support.

The table converts configurations into monthly figures so the comparison is concrete. The row worth studying is the last one: a six-session cross-science skills block, bought once, costs a fraction of any monthly configuration and affects marks in all three papers. For a family with a genuine technique problem rather than a content problem, it is the highest-return purchase on this page by a wide margin.

The row to be wary of is three weekly hours. At the qualified band that is roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month, which is a significant household commitment, and it is the configuration most likely to be abandoned by February because the student cannot sustain it alongside everything else. An abandoned engagement costs the same as a completed one for the months it ran.

Our own figure is agreed at the consultation once the codes, tiers and diagnosis are known. We sit in the qualified-specialist part of those bands rather than the budget part, the trial lesson is free, and nothing is charged before it. Where the mock scripts say one subject and a skills block will do, that is what we quote, which is a smaller sale than three weekly slots and is the recommendation we would want for our own children.

sections.heading: Which science topics actually need a specialist
paragraphs: Not all of them, and knowing the difference is how a family in this catchment buys well. Some topics need somebody who teaches that subject at that tier habitually. Others are quantitative problems that a good mathematics tutor fixes faster and cheaper. A third group is answer-shape work that any competent science teacher can drill. Spending specialist money on the second and third groups is the commonest avoidable overspend in science.

Needs a specialist: electricity and magnetism in physics, where the conceptual model matters and misconceptions are stubborn. Moles and electrolysis in chemistry where the gap is conceptual rather than arithmetic. Organic chemistry families and reaction patterns. Genetics and inheritance problems in biology, where the reasoning is formal and students pattern-match wrongly. And anything at the top of the Extended tier where questions combine topics without signalling which.

Does not need a specialist: rearranging formulae, unit conversion, standard form, significant figures and percentage calculations. All of those are mathematics, they underpin two sciences at once, and a mathematics tutor at the mid band resolves them faster than two science specialists working around them. If your child is losing marks on the arithmetic inside science questions rather than on the science, buy the mathematics.

Drillable by any competent science teacher: command terms, tabulation conventions, graph scale and fit, anomaly identification, evaluation phrasing and required practical knowledge. These are patterned, they repeat across papers and across subjects, and they are the marks a six-session cross-science block targets. They are also, in our experience of mock scripts from this catchment, where the largest share of recoverable marks sits.

sections.heading: Year 10 foundations or Year 11 triage: where the money works
paragraphs: Almost all the science demand in this catchment arrives in Year 11 and almost all the value sits in Year 10. The reason is structural. In Year 10 the tier is still movable, the content is being taught for the first time, quantitative foundations can be rebuilt without competing against revision, and the evening slots are uncontested. One science, one weekly hour, two terms: that is the configuration that changes outcomes, and it costs roughly a third of a three-subject Year 11 engagement.

Year 11 support is not pointless but it is a narrower product and should be bought as such. After the autumn mocks you have the best diagnostic the school will ever give you, free, in the form of three marked scripts. Read them, or have them read, and buy the one subject and the one skills block that the scripts justify. Bought that way, Year 11 science support is excellent value. Bought as three open-ended weekly slots in March, it is the most expensive thing on this page.

There is a third window families almost never use: the summer between Year 10 and Year 11. No competing homework, no fatigue from the school run, and the ability to rebuild rearrangement and unit work without also keeping up with a current unit. For a student whose physics and chemistry both look weak, that summer block is frequently the whole fix, because the common cause was quantitative and it was never two problems.

And if you are reading this in Year 9, the cheapest intervention in this entire page is available to you: a term of work on proportional reasoning, rearrangement, unit conversion and reading scales, at the lower end of the published bands, before any of it is attached to an examined grade. Families who do that generally never buy science tutoring again, which is a strange thing for a tutoring page to recommend and is nonetheless true.

sections.heading: Starting science support from Muhaisnah
paragraphs: Send four things. The syllabus codes and tiers for each science, from the exams officer rather than the student. The most recent mock or marked script for each subject. The school's weekly timetable, including which afternoons finish late. And the two evening slots you genuinely believe will survive until June.

If you have three mock scripts and no clear view, buy the three-session diagnostic rather than any hours. It ends with a written recommendation naming which subject is genuinely weak, which losses are cross-science technique, and which the school's revision programme will carry. It frequently recommends buying less than you asked for, which is the point of it.

Then buy one thing. One science as a weekly hour or a bounded block, or a cross-science skills block, with a stated target checkable on a marked paper. Good science targets are mechanical: tabulating and plotting without losing presentation marks, matching answer length to the command term, or suggesting a specific rather than generic improvement in an evaluation question.

Finally, the advice we would give regardless of whether you use us. If your child is in Year 10, buy the autumn and buy one subject. If they are in Year 11 with mocks done, read the scripts before you spend. If physics and chemistry both look weak, check the arithmetic before concluding you have two science problems. And if the target grade sits above a tier ceiling, go and see the head of science first, because that conversation is free and no tutor substitutes for it.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three IGCSE sciences for my child?
faqs.answer: For a double-award route such as Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson 4SD0, usually yes, because the depth is lower and the strands are examined together; the work is mostly identifying which strand is weak. For three separate sciences, a single tutor covering all three at Extended tier is a generalist, and the depth shows by the spring of Year 11. The better plan is one specialist for the one subject your mock scripts name, plus a short cross-science skills block that earns marks in all three papers at once.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Coordinated Sciences and Combined Science?
faqs.answer: Cambridge Coordinated Sciences, 0654, is a double award covering biology, chemistry and physics at reduced depth, reported as two grades. Cambridge Combined Science, 0653, is a single award with less content again, reported as one. They are frequently confused, and the distinction matters both for later routes, since a single award is not equivalent to two separate science grades, and for tutoring, since the content depth differs. Ask the exams officer which your child is entered for and check what your sixth form requires for AS sciences.

faqs.question: Which of the three sciences do students here struggle with most?
faqs.answer: Physics, consistently, in enquiries from this catchment, and the underlying cause is frequently algebraic rather than physical: a student who cannot rearrange confidently will look weak at physics regardless of how well they understand it. Chemistry difficulty is often really a mole-arithmetic problem. Biology is the one most often misdiagnosed: it feels manageable because the content is familiar, but the marks sit in command-term precision and in reading unfamiliar methods, which makes it the cheapest of the three to improve.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if we study online?
faqs.answer: On paper, in both main routes. Cambridge separate sciences offer a practical test and an alternative-to-practical written paper, with most international centres using the written route; Pearson assesses practical knowledge inside the written papers. The marks go to planning, variables, instrument reading, tabulation, plotting, interpretation and evaluation, all of which are written skills. Apparatus time belongs to the school, which has the equipment. Several of these skills are taught better on a shared screen, because a tutor can annotate your child's actual graph while they watch.

faqs.question: What does supporting all three sciences cost across a year?
faqs.answer: At the published qualified band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, three weekly hours across a thirty-week school year works out at roughly AED 13,500 to 27,000, or roughly AED 1,800 to 3,600 a month. At specialist rates it is higher. That configuration is also the one most likely to be abandoned by February, because a Year 11 student with nine or ten subjects plus mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies does not have three spare evenings. One diagnosed subject plus a skills block costs a fraction.

faqs.question: What is a cross-science skills block and why is it cheaper?
faqs.answer: Four to six sessions on the things that earn marks in all three science papers simultaneously: command terms, tabulation conventions, graph scale and fit, anomaly identification, evaluation phrasing and quantitative technique. Because those losses are not subject-specific, the block is bought once rather than three times, and at published qualified rates a six-session block is roughly AED 900 to 1,800 in total. For a student whose mock scripts show technique losses rather than content gaps, it is the highest-return purchase available.

faqs.question: My child is Extended in biology and Core in physics. Does that change anything?
faqs.answer: Yes, considerably, and families are often unaware it is even possible. Mixed tiering across sciences within one school is common. It means two different kinds of engagement: Extended work focuses on multi-topic questions and the harder question styles that only appear on that tier, while Core work focuses on securing the content within a capped grade range. Treating both as one science problem produces the wrong plan for each. Ask the exams officer to confirm the tier for every science separately, in writing.

faqs.question: Can tutoring move my child from Core to Extended in a science?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, but the decision belongs to the school and is usually taken during Year 10 on evidence from the student's work. Ask the subject teacher two questions: what evidence would change the entry, and by what date must the decision be made. Then work on exactly that, which in science is usually quantitative accuracy and the ability to handle unstructured questions. Be realistic about the trade: a secure Core grade is a better outcome than a struggling Extended one, and forcing the higher tier across all three sciences at once rarely ends well.

faqs.question: Is my child's science problem actually a maths problem?
faqs.answer: Frequently, and the distinction saves real money. Rearranging formulae, unit conversion, standard form, significant figures and percentage calculation underpin both physics and chemistry, so a student weak in those appears weak in two sciences at once. That is one piece of work, available from a mathematics tutor at the mid band, rather than two science specialists working around it. A specialist reading a marked script can tell you within minutes whether the science reasoning is sound and the arithmetic is collapsing.

faqs.question: When is the best time to buy IGCSE science support?
faqs.answer: Year 10, or the summer between Year 10 and Year 11, and almost nobody does either. In Year 10 the tier is still movable, content is being taught for the first time, and the evening slots are uncontested. The summer offers something better still: quantitative foundations can be rebuilt with no competing homework, and for a student whose physics and chemistry both look weak that block is frequently the whole fix. After the spring mocks of Year 11 is the most expensive window with the least to work with.

faqs.question: Do we need separate sciences for a UAE university application?
faqs.answer: That depends on the programme and the university, and it should be checked on the institution's own admissions page rather than assumed. What is published and checkable is the Ministry of Education equivalency rule for the British track: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One ranking tutoring site in this market publishes a six-subject figure, which is incorrect. No tutoring is required for equivalency.

faqs.question: What should a science tutor set between sessions?
faqs.answer: Past-paper questions from the board, selected to match the diagnosed loss, marked before the next session. Most of the consolidation in science happens between lessons, so a tutor who sets nothing is selling an hour of company rather than a course of study. Ask explicitly whether work is set and marked and whether that is inside the quoted rate. Ask also where the papers come from: they should be the board's published material or what the school supplies, not a pack being sold to you.

faqs.question: How quickly can you match a science specialist for a Muhaisnah student?
faqs.answer: Biology and chemistry typically reach a trial lesson within three to five days, because the specialist pool is reasonably deep. Physics takes a little longer, four to seven days, and Extended-tier physics longer again. Double-award routes depend on the code: Cambridge 0654 is well covered and Pearson 4SD0 takes longer because fewer tutors have taught that specific paper structure. We will tell you the wait rather than filling the slot with a tutor from an adjacent subject, because the gap surfaces in the final term.

faqs.question: Why should we pay more for online lessons than a local tutor charges?
faqs.answer: You probably will not. Local science tutoring around Muhaisnah is plentiful and inexpensive, and most of it teaches Indian-curriculum science, which is genuinely useful for Key Stage 3 foundations and insufficient for Extended-tier IGCSE paper technique. The published in-home band of roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour includes travel through the afternoon peak. What online delivery buys is a tutor matched to your child's actual syllabus code rather than whoever is nearby, at a rate that pays for teaching rather than a drive.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-nad-al-hama.tutorsIntro: The science tutors here name a single subject and a board rather than offering science generally. For a student sitting three separate sciences, one strong specialist in the weakest subject beats one generalist across all three, and the page below explains why.

intro.heading: Three sciences, three codes, and one calendar they all sit on
paragraphs: The first question is structural rather than academic. A Dubai IGCSE candidate may be sitting three separate sciences, each with its own certificate; a coordinated double award, which yields two grades across all three disciplines; or a single combined award, which yields one. The three routes carry different numbers of papers, different depth and, critically, different practical arrangements. A parent who does not know which route their child is on cannot sensibly judge how many tutoring hours the sciences deserve.

The second question is the board, because the codes differ and so do the papers. Cambridge International runs Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as separate sciences, with Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as the double award and Combined Science 0653 as the single. Pearson Edexcel runs Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1, with a double award alternative. A student practising past papers from the wrong code is practising the right science in the wrong format, and in the last eight weeks the format is what is being prepared.

The third is practical assessment, which is where the two boards genuinely diverge. Cambridge separate sciences offer a practical route and an alternative-to-practical written paper, and schools choose between them. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences assess practical skills inside the written papers rather than through a separate practical component. That difference changes what revision looks like: one route needs apparatus familiarity and the other needs practice at answering experimental questions in writing.

Then there is the calendar, which is the same for all three sciences and unforgiving. Content is delivered through Year 10 and the first half of Year 11, mocks land after the winter break, entries close months before the papers, and the series arrives in June with a November resit route. A family carrying three sciences plus six or seven other subjects has to triage, and the honest arithmetic of that triage is set out below rather than hidden behind a package.

Nad Al Hamar is a residential district on the eastern side of Dubai, between the Ras Al Khor sanctuary and the Dubai-Al Ain Road, with no secondary school inside it. Children travel out to Festival City, Mirdif, Al Warqa, Al Qusais and Academic City, coming home between about 3.50pm and 4.35pm, which leaves a narrower evening than a three-science timetable really needs. Teaching is one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run in India only. What follows is the three routes compared, the practical arrangements by board, every syllabus code in one table, the Year 11 countdown, and the triage arithmetic for a family that cannot buy three subjects.

programmes.name: Three separate sciences

programmes.name: Coordinated or double award science
programmes.description: All three disciplines taught and examined together, yielding two grades, under Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or a Pearson double award. Less depth per discipline than the separate route and substantially less timetable load, which can free time for other subjects. Accepted for many post-16 routes but checked carefully by competitive A Level science programmes.

programmes.name: Combined single award science
programmes.description: One grade covering all three disciplines, under Cambridge Combined Science 0653 or an equivalent. The lightest science load, appropriate for students whose strengths and intended route lie elsewhere. It counts as one subject toward a subject total, which matters for any requirement expressed as a number of passes.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-nad-al-hama.subjectsIntro: What a science tutor should be able to take apart, discipline by discipline and skill by skill.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Current, potential difference, resistance, series and parallel reasoning. The most requested topic in the eastern suburbs and almost always a reasoning problem rather than a formula problem: students cannot say what happens to the rest of a circuit when one component changes.

subjects.name: Physics: waves and radiation
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, the electromagnetic spectrum and radioactive decay. Definitions must be stated precisely and students paraphrase them, which costs marks on questions they believed they had answered correctly.

subjects.name: Physics: forces and motion
subjects.description: Speed, acceleration, graphs of motion, moments and pressure. Graph interpretation does most of the work here, and a student who cannot read a gradient as a rate will struggle across the whole paper rather than in one topic.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and calculations
subjects.description: Relative formula mass, moles, concentration, percentage yield and gas volumes. The single biggest discriminator on an Extended chemistry paper, and almost entirely a matter of drilling rather than understanding.

subjects.name: Chemistry: electrolysis and reactivity
subjects.description: Electrode products, half-equations and the reactivity series. Half-equations reward a fixed routine and punish improvisation, which is why a student either scores nearly all of these marks or very few.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic and polymers
subjects.description: Homologous series, nomenclature, addition and condensation polymerisation. Largely recall, which makes it one of the fastest areas to recover in a short block before a series.

subjects.name: Biology: transport and respiration
subjects.description: Circulation, gas exchange, respiration and photosynthesis as linked processes. Students know each process and lose marks when asked to connect two of them, because the connection was never explicitly taught.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Monohybrid crosses, genetic diagrams, variation and selection. A procedural topic with a reliable question format, so practice volume converts directly into marks, making it a sensible target in a short block.

subjects.name: Shared skill: experimental questions
subjects.description: Variables, controls, repeats, anomalous results, graph plotting and conclusions drawn from data. Examined in every science, through a practical paper, an alternative-to-practical paper or inside the written papers, and the best value hour in science revision because it pays across all three subjects.

sections.heading: Separate, coordinated or combined: find out which before anything else
paragraphs: These are three different qualifications and they generate three different conversations. Separate sciences mean three full courses, three sets of papers and three grades, and they are the normal expectation for a student intending A Level sciences, medicine or engineering. A coordinated or double award covers all three disciplines in less depth and produces two grades. A combined single award produces one. The timetable load differs enormously, and so does the number of subjects your child's certificate will show.

The practical consequence for a tutoring decision is about allocation. A separate-sciences candidate who is weak in physics has one subject to fix out of three, and the other two can be left to school and self-study. A coordinated candidate who is weak in the physics content has a problem inside a single qualification, so the weakness drags both awarded grades rather than one. That changes the priority: the same weakness is more expensive on the coordinated route.

The route also interacts with post-16 plans in ways families discover late. Some sixth forms accept a double award for entry to their own A Level sciences and some require separate sciences, and the requirement is set school by school rather than nationally. The question to ask, in Year 10 rather than after results, is simply whether your school's A Level science courses accept the route your child is on and at what grade.

And it interacts with subject counting. UAE certificate equivalency requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the count. Three separate sciences contribute three subjects toward a total of that kind; a combined single award contributes one. For a student with a narrow subject set that arithmetic is worth checking against the Ministry's published requirements before the entries are finalised.

sections.heading: The practical papers, and the route your school chose for you
paragraphs: This is the part of IGCSE science that parents understand least, partly because the two boards handle it differently. For Cambridge separate sciences, schools choose between a practical test, sat with apparatus under examination conditions, and an alternative-to-practical written paper, which asks about experimental work without requiring the student to perform it. Both assess the same underlying skills and they demand quite different preparation.

For Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences, practical skills are assessed within the written papers rather than through a separate practical component. The questions ask about variables, methods, data and conclusions in the context of experiments the student may have performed in class. The revision implication is that experimental questions appear throughout the papers rather than being confined to one, so a student who treats practical work as a separate topic to be revised last will meet it everywhere.

Whichever route applies, the underlying skill set is identical and it is the best-value thing to revise in science. Identifying the independent, dependent and control variables. Explaining why a variable must be controlled rather than simply listing it. Justifying a number of repeats. Spotting an anomalous result and saying what to do about it. Plotting a graph with sensible axes and a line that reflects the data rather than joining the points. Drawing a conclusion the data supports and no more.

Those skills pay in all three disciplines simultaneously, which is why a short block on them is the rational first purchase for a three-science candidate who cannot afford three subjects of tutoring. Four to six sessions, practised on unfamiliar data from biology, chemistry and physics in turn, improves marks across every science paper rather than in one.

sections.heading: The codes, and why practising the wrong ones costs the last eight weeks
paragraphs: Syllabus codes look like administrative trivia and are the most practical piece of information a science family can hold. Cambridge International runs Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653. Pearson Edexcel runs Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1. A school may use Cambridge for one science and Pearson for another, which sounds unlikely and happens.

The cost of getting this wrong is concentrated in the final weeks, which is exactly when it is most expensive. A student revising Cambridge physics from Pearson papers will meet the same physics in an unfamiliar question style, will feel either falsely confident or needlessly alarmed, and will have spent the scarcest hours of the year on a format they will not sit. Research across this market found that exactly one syllabus code appeared anywhere in an entire cluster of competitor pages, which tells you how rarely this is checked.

Codes also carry the tier. Cambridge separate sciences are entered at Core or Extended, with a grade ceiling on the lower tier that no amount of tutoring lifts. Pearson sciences have their own tier arrangements. Confirming the tier matters as much as confirming the code, because the topics examined differ and because a parent who wants to argue for the higher entry has to do it before the entry closes, months before the papers.

Finally, the series. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only, so a Dubai parent reading advice about a February science examination is reading advice for another country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with different timetables, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone's version.

sections.heading: The Year 11 science countdown
paragraphs: Science has more content than almost any other subject block on a Year 11 timetable, which makes the calendar tighter here than elsewhere. August and September are for establishing facts: the route, the codes, the tier, the practical arrangement and the school's mock dates. They are also the last stretch in which content can be taught comfortably rather than squeezed, and the cheapest point at which to fix a weakness in one discipline.

October to the winter break is content completion plus the first serious revision, and it is when entries are being prepared. The tier conversation, if there is to be one, has to happen here. After the break come the mocks, which in science are unusually informative because they expose the difference between a student who has not learned the content and a student who cannot answer experimental and graph questions about content they do know.

January and February are therefore diagnostic months rather than buying months. Read the marked scripts across all three sciences and look for the pattern. If experimental questions are being lost in every subject, the problem is a shared skill and one short block fixes it in all three. If one discipline is far behind the other two, that is a single-subject block. If everything is low with time left on the paper, the problem is content and the honest answer may be that only one subject can be rescued.

March onward is technique and targeted recovery. Timed papers in the correct codes, the experimental skill set drilled, and the recall-heavy topics in each science swept in short bursts because they are the fastest marks available late. Organic chemistry and polymers, genetics and inheritance, and radiation definitions are all high-recall and respond to drilling in the final weeks in a way that circuit reasoning does not.

sections.heading: Which of the three sciences to pay for, and which to leave alone
paragraphs: Three sciences cannot all be tutored, and attempting it is both expensive and self-defeating, because taught hours displace the independent practice that actually consolidates science content. The triage question is not which subject feels worst but which has the most recoverable marks in the weeks available, and the answer is frequently counter-intuitive.

Biology is the most content-heavy and the most recall-driven, which makes it the most recoverable late, provided the student will do the memorisation. A biology deficit two months out is usually fixable with drilling and past questions rather than teaching. Chemistry depends heavily on calculations at Extended level, and a student who cannot do moles will be losing marks across the paper, so a short calculation block has high leverage. Physics is the most reasoning-dependent, especially circuits, and is the least recoverable in a hurry.

That suggests a rough order of priority when time is short: fix the chemistry calculations, drill the biology recall, and accept that physics reasoning needs longer. When there is more time, the order reverses, because physics reasoning built in the autumn pays across the whole paper and biology recall can wait until it is fresh. The right answer depends on how many weeks exist, which is why the calendar and the triage are the same conversation.

One more factor: the practical and experimental questions are shared across all three sciences. A block on that skill set is the only science purchase that improves three papers at once, and for a family that can only afford one block it is frequently the best choice available, ahead of any single-subject work.

sections.heading: Three sciences and one evening: scheduling the week
paragraphs: A Year 11 student in Nad Al Hamar comes home between about 3.50pm and 4.35pm depending on direction, later on activity days, and then has to fit homework from nine or ten subjects plus revision. Science is the heaviest of those loads. The practical consequence is that a tutoring slot has to be chosen for the week it is hardest to keep rather than the week it is easiest, and that one tutored subject plus structured self-study usually beats two tutored subjects with no time left to practise.

Session length should follow the problem rather than convention. Content teaching in a weak discipline needs ninety minutes, because explanation plus practice plus checking does not compress. Experimental skills and calculation drilling work better at forty-five minutes twice a week, because both are habits. A full timed paper plus its review needs two clear hours, which on a weeknight does not exist, so that belongs on a weekend morning.

For households with two candidates, consecutive slots on one evening work better than separate evenings. One-to-one means one student in the session, so an hour cannot be shared, but an evening can, and giving up one weeknight is easier to sustain through a whole term than giving up three. In practice a 6pm and a 7.15pm pair holds well in this part of Dubai.

Ramadan reshapes the month: school hours shorten, door times come forward by an hour or more, and families split between early-afternoon and post-Iftar slots. Both work over video, which they would not with a tutor crossing the eastern suburbs at Iftar. For a Year 11 science candidate the planning move is to front-load content work into the weeks before and treat the month as recall and retention work, which suits biology particularly well.

sections.heading: What science help costs, and the three-subject mistake
paragraphs: The expensive error in science is buying three subjects because there are three sciences. At the qualified online band of AED 150 to 300 an hour, three weekly sessions runs to roughly three times the mid monthly estimate, which Bestimate puts at AED 600 to 1,200 for a single weekly hour. That is a substantial monthly commitment for a result that is often worse than one well-chosen block, because the student loses the evenings they needed for memorisation and past questions.

Set the same published bands against a twelve-week term in a single science and the decision sharpens further. A weekly hour with a qualified subject tutor online, quoted at AED 150 to 300 and published by Unitors at IGCSE from AED 150, is AED 1,800 to 3,600 a term for Biology on its own. Move to the IGCSE specialist band of AED 200 to 450 and above, where TutorChase publishes AED 270, and the same term costs AED 2,400 to 5,400. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 an hour once travel out to Nad Al Hamar is absorbed, with Bestimate at AED 180 to 350, which is a term between AED 2,160 and AED 6,000 for one subject on one evening. Budget online platforms advertise from AED 33 to 65, with Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, and a full term there costs less than a single specialist month, which is precisely why families buy three of them and end up with three shallow subjects. Every figure is the provider's own, read in October 2026.

Packages seen in the Dubai market include about AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which for a science family is worth noting because eight shorter sessions can cover a twice-weekly drilling pattern in one subject rather than one session each in three. In-home monthly packages appear at AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits, where part of the money is paying for travel across the eastern suburbs rather than for teaching.

A tuition centre group class remains the cheapest taught option per head and genuinely suits a science student whose problem is practice volume rather than a named gap, which in science is more often the case than in mathematics. And the school's own science clinics are usually included in fees and aligned exactly with the codes your child sits. A family paying for three sciences without having used those is almost certainly overspending.

sections.heading: Coursework, data and the line a science tutor does not cross
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences on these routes do not carry a written internal assessment in the way the Diploma does, but practical work still produces data that students write up, and schools set assessed tasks of their own. The boundary therefore still matters. A tutor may teach the content, explain what an experimental question rewards, demonstrate a full worked analysis on an entirely different data set, and read your child's own work to ask questions about variables, repeats, anomalies and whether a conclusion is supported.

A tutor may not design the method for the student, process their data, write or rewrite a write-up, or produce material the student submits as their own. In science specifically the temptation is data rather than prose: adjusting an awkward reading, dropping a point without justification, or inventing repeats that were never done. Each of those is falsification, and the honest treatment scores better anyway, because an anomaly identified and discussed earns credit while one quietly deleted earns nothing.

We also do not supply syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. They belong to Cambridge International and Pearson, the boards publish specifications on their own sites, and your child's school has legitimate access to the assessment material. A tutor working from that material inside a session is ordinary practice; hosting a download library of it is distributing somebody else's property.

And we claim no approval from anyone. IB Gram holds no accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, Cambridge International or Pearson, and operates no office or centre in the UAE. Individual tutors in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which is free of charge and valid for two years; if you hire independently, ask to see it.

faqs.question: Is our child sitting three separate sciences or a double award?
faqs.answer: The statement of entry says, and the exams officer will confirm it in one email. Separate sciences means three full courses under Cambridge codes 0610, 0620 and 0625 or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with three grades. A coordinated or double award covers all three disciplines in less depth under Cambridge 0654 and yields two grades. A combined single award yields one. The routes differ in timetable load, in depth, and in how many subjects your child's certificate shows.

faqs.question: Does a double award science limit sixth-form options in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It can, and the rule is set school by school rather than nationally. Some sixth forms accept a double award for entry to their own A Level sciences, sometimes at a higher grade, and some require separate sciences. Ask your school's own published criteria in Year 10 rather than after results. There is also a subject-counting effect: three separate sciences contribute three subjects to a total, while a combined single award contributes one, which matters for any requirement expressed as a number of passes.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if my child studies partly online?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself happens at school, with apparatus, as it must. What differs is the assessment route. Cambridge separate sciences offer a practical test with apparatus or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and the school chooses. Pearson Edexcel assesses practical skills inside the written papers. Online tutoring supports the parts that are desk work: variables, controls, repeats, anomalous results, graph plotting and conclusions from data, which is where most of the marks actually sit in every route.

faqs.question: Which syllabus codes should we be downloading past papers for?
faqs.answer: Whichever ones appear on the statement of entry, and check per subject because a school can use different boards for different sciences. Cambridge runs Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 and Combined Science 0653; Pearson runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Practising the wrong code means meeting the right science in an unfamiliar question style during the scarcest weeks of the year. We do not host board material ourselves; your school has legitimate access.

faqs.question: If we can only afford one science, which should we pay for?
faqs.answer: Often none of them individually. The experimental skill set, variables, controls, repeats, anomalies, graphs and conclusions, is examined in all three sciences whichever practical route applies, so a four to six session block on it improves three papers at once. If a single subject must be chosen, pick on recoverable marks in the weeks available: chemistry calculations have the highest leverage per hour, biology recall is the most recoverable late, and physics circuit reasoning is the least recoverable in a hurry.

faqs.question: Why is our child fine in science lessons and weak on science papers?
faqs.answer: Usually experimental and graph questions, which are examined in every science and taught as an afterthought in many schemes. A student can know respiration thoroughly and still lose marks explaining why a variable had to be controlled, justifying a number of repeats, or drawing a line of best fit rather than joining the points. Read the marked scripts: if experimental questions are shedding marks in all three subjects, it is a shared skill gap rather than three content gaps.

faqs.question: Can biology really be rescued in the last two months?
faqs.answer: More readily than physics, yes, provided your child will do the memorisation. Biology is the most content-heavy and most recall-driven of the three, which makes it the most responsive to drilling and past questions late in the year. Genetics and inheritance in particular has a reliable question format where practice volume converts directly into marks. What does not respond the same way is physics circuit reasoning, which needs understanding built over longer than eight weeks.

faqs.question: Our school entered the Core tier for science. Can tutoring change the grade?
faqs.answer: Only within the tier. The Core entry at Cambridge carries a grade ceiling that is a property of the paper rather than the candidate, so a student who performs outstandingly on a Core paper still receives a capped grade. Tutoring can maximise the result inside the tier, and more usefully, if there is still time, build the case for an Extended entry. That case has to be made before entries close, months before the papers, which in practice means Year 10 or very early Year 11.

faqs.question: Is there a February science series our child could sit in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, and the February and March series is offered to India only. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May and June and again in November. Any page offering a Dubai parent a February examination window has copied guidance written for another country. Note also that Cambridge allocates centres to one of six administrative zones with different timetables and cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong version.

faqs.question: Which schools near Nad Al Hamar enter students for separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Mostly the larger British and Indian curriculum schools in Al Warqa and the Festival City cluster, including GEMS Our Own English High School, Deira International School and Universal American School Dubai, with the Mirdif and Al Mizhar belt running a mix of separate, coordinated and American high-school routes. Boards differ between schools and sometimes between subjects within a school. Schools are named here as local context only, with no affiliation or endorsement implied.

faqs.question: How should three sciences fit into a Nad Al Hamar weeknight?
faqs.answer: They mostly should not. Door times run from about 3.50pm to past 4.35pm depending on direction, and a Year 11 candidate carries nine or ten subject homeworks plus revision. One tutored science plus structured self-study in the other two beats two tutored subjects with no practice time left. Content teaching needs ninety minutes once a week; calculation and recall drilling works better at forty-five minutes twice a week; a full timed paper plus review needs a weekend morning.

faqs.question: What happens to science revision during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: School hours shorten, so the Nad Al Hamar door time comes forward by an hour or more and the evening changes shape. Families generally move to an early-afternoon slot or a post-Iftar one, and both work over video in a way they would not with a tutor travelling across the eastern suburbs at Iftar. The planning move for a science candidate is to front-load content work into the preceding weeks and use the month for recall and retention, which suits biology particularly well.

faqs.question: Would a group science class at a Mirdif centre be good enough?
faqs.answer: In science, more often than in mathematics. A centre class is the cheapest taught option per head and supplies structure, pace and practice volume, which is the actual problem for a large share of science candidates: they know roughly what to do and have not done enough questions. Where a class fails is the named gap, such as a student who cannot reason about circuits, because the class moves at the scheme's pace. Try the school's own science clinic first, since it is usually included in fees.

faqs.question: Should the same person teach all three of our sciences, or just one?
faqs.answer: For experimental skills and graph work, yes, and that is a genuinely good use of one tutor because those skills are identical across the three. For Extended content at depth, treat the claim cautiously: a tutor offering strength in all three disciplines at the higher tier is claiming three specialisms. The useful pattern is one tutor for the shared experimental block, then a subject specialist for whichever single discipline the marked mocks identify as furthest behind.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-nad-al-hama.closingBody: Science decisions go wrong at the start rather than at the end. Find out whether your child sits separate sciences, a coordinated double award or a combined single award, get the syllabus code and tier for each, and check which practical route the school entered. Then read all three marked mock scripts together and look for the pattern across them, because if experimental questions are shedding marks everywhere, one short block fixes three papers. intro.heading: Three science routes, and the one your child is on
paragraphs: Parents in Nad Al Sheba comparing science tutoring options usually begin with the wrong comparison. They compare tutors, or they compare their district against Meydan and Sobha Hartland, when the comparison that decides the outcome is between the three science routes a school offers. Single award science produces one IGCSE grade. Double award, or Co-ordinated Sciences, produces two. Three separate sciences produce three. The content overlaps heavily; the papers, the volume and the post-16 doors do not.

The choice was made in Year 9, often quickly, sometimes by default, and it is frequently not revisited. A student taking three separate sciences is carrying roughly a third more examined content than a double award student and sitting six papers rather than four. If that student is struggling, the first question is whether they are struggling with science or with the load, and those have different answers. Dropping to double award, where the school permits it and before the entry deadline, is sometimes the right answer and is almost never discussed.

The district context: Repton School Dubai, Kings' School Nad Al Sheba and GEMS Modern Academy sit inside Nad Al Sheba, with Hartland International School and North London Collegiate School Dubai in Sobha Hartland and Safa Community School a short drive away. Dubai held 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25 across seventeen licensed curricula, with UK-curriculum schools accounting for 37% of enrolment — the largest single share. UK curriculum, though, does not mean one board or one science route, and schools within a few kilometres of each other differ on both.

That is why the geographic comparison turns out to be the least useful one. What differs between Nad Al Sheba, Meydan, Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City is the school run and therefore the time a session can start. What differs between the schools in them is the board, the science route and the practical arrangement, and none of that follows a map. A family should ask their school for the syllabus codes before hiring anybody, and the codes are the one piece of information almost nobody arrives with.

IB Gram delivers tuition to UAE families as one-to-one lessons over live video, and does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a student taking three sciences that matters practically: three subjects can mean three tutors or two, and a travelling arrangement that works for one subject becomes three car journeys a week once the exam year starts.

Two things are worth collecting before any first conversation about science tutoring. The syllabus codes, which the exams officer or head of science can give you in one email, and the most recent marked piece of written science work from each subject. The codes tell a tutor which papers your child will actually sit. The scripts tell them whether the lost marks are command terms in biology, missing state symbols in chemistry, or algebra abandoned halfway through a physics calculation. Those are three different problems with three different prices, and treating them as one problem called science is how a term gets spent without a grade moving.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-nad-al-sheb.subjectsIntro: Three sciences, two boards and three routes produce a long list of possible combinations. Below are the courses and components Nad Al Sheba students bring, with the syllabus code and the characteristic place marks go in each.

subjects.name: Cambridge Biology 0610
subjects.description: Content-dense and command-term sensitive. Describe and explain earn different marks here more sharply than in the other two sciences, and six-mark extended answers need a rehearsed structure. Transport, homeostasis and inheritance questions reward sequencing an answer in order rather than listing facts about the topic.

subjects.name: Cambridge Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The mole and organic chemistry decide most grades. Students who balance equations confidently still drop marks on state symbols, on ionic equations, and on explaining a trend rather than stating it. Qualitative analysis questions are mechanical and reliably available once the test results are learned properly.

subjects.name: Cambridge Physics 0625
subjects.description: Multiple choice, theory and a practical route. Unit conversion, describing a graph rather than using its gradient, and experimental-design questions that never name a control are the three recurring losses. Formula recall matters less than recognising which rearrangement the given data invites.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: All three sciences in one course awarding two grades, with genuinely reduced content rather than the same syllabus compressed. The papers move between disciplines, so the examined skill includes switching register quickly — a biology explanation and a physics calculation can sit on facing pages.

subjects.name: Cambridge Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade covering all three sciences at a lighter depth, suited to students for whom science is a requirement rather than a direction. Tutoring here is usually about securing a grade floor rather than reaching a ceiling, which changes what a sensible number of sessions looks like.

subjects.name: Pearson Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers with practical skills assessed inside them rather than in a separate practical paper. Extended-response questions carry significant marks and reward a planned structure. The absence of a standalone practical paper does not remove experimental questions; it moves them into the theory papers.

subjects.name: Pearson Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Two written papers, practical skills assessed within them. Calculation questions on moles, concentration and yield are reliable marks and are often rushed. As with Cambridge, state symbols and complete ionic equations are the quiet losses that cost marks on every paper.

subjects.name: Pearson Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers with experimental method assessed inside them. The mathematical demand is the highest of the three Pearson sciences, so a student weak on rearrangement will show it here first. Graph questions reward taking a gradient properly, with a large triangle and labelled values.

subjects.name: Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: Three sciences in one course awarding two grades, with papers covering each discipline. Suits students carrying a wide subject list who need science grades without three separate revision programmes, and it keeps most non-specialist post-16 routes available.

subjects.name: Practical and alternative-to-practical components
subjects.description: Cambridge separate sciences include either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on what the centre offers. The alternative paper is highly predictable in structure — method, variables, tables, graphs, improvements — which makes it one of the best returns on tutoring time available.

subjects.name: Experimental method and variables
subjects.description: Independent, dependent and control variables, fair tests, repeat readings and improvement suggestions. Assessed somewhere on every science route in some form, taught once in most schools, and the single most transferable set of marks across all three sciences.

subjects.name: Mathematical skills for science
subjects.description: Rearrangement, proportion, percentages, standard form, significant figures and gradient work. Not a science topic and the cause of a large share of lost science marks, particularly in physics and in chemistry calculations. Worth testing separately before buying subject hours.

sections.heading: Single award, double award or three separate sciences
paragraphs: This is the comparison that decides a science outcome, and it is almost never on the page when families research tutoring. The three routes are different qualifications. Single award produces one IGCSE grade covering all three sciences at a lighter depth. Double award — Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0 — produces two grades with genuinely reduced content. Three separate sciences produce three grades, six or more papers, and roughly a third more examined material.

What follows is a workload difference, not a prestige one. A Nad Al Sheba student taking nine or ten subjects including three separate sciences is carrying a revision programme that is physically larger than a classmate's on double award, and in the final term that difference is measured in hours they do not have. Where a student is struggling with one science, the honest first question is whether the route is right rather than whether the teaching is wrong.

The route also sets the post-16 doors, and this is where a decision made casually in Year 9 has consequences. A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences assume separate-science content in their first term. Double award keeps most other routes open, including plenty of competitive degrees that require no science at all. Single award narrows the science-specific options considerably. None of those is a wrong choice; choosing one by default is.

Where a change is possible it has a deadline, held by the school's exams officer rather than by the board, and it sits in the autumn of Year 11 at the latest. The practical move for a family with doubts is to ask two questions in writing: can my child move between routes, and by when. Both have short answers and both cost the school nothing to give.

paragraphs: Families in this part of Dubai compare four communities as a block: Nad Al Sheba, Meydan, Sobha Hartland and Mohammed Bin Rashid City. For tutoring the comparison reduces to one variable, and it is not quality of provision. It is what time a session can start on a weekday, which matters disproportionately for a student taking three sciences because three subjects need three slots.

Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland have schools inside their own boundaries, so a child can be home and settled by 15:30. That makes three weekday science sessions genuinely schedulable without pushing any of them past 19:00. Meydan sits at 16:00 to 16:30 depending on which school the child travels to. What does not follow a map at all is the thing that actually matters: the board, the science route and the practical arrangement. Schools a few kilometres apart in this block differ on all three, and some differ by subject within one school. A family that works out their session window and never establishes their syllabus codes has solved the easy problem and left the hard one.

Nothing has to arrive, so a District One family and a Sobha Hartland family can both hold a 16:00 slot. What remains is the match: a tutor who teaches the specific code and route rather than science in general, which is a selection question rather than a location one.

sections.heading: The practical component, board by board
paragraphs: Science practical assessment is the part of IGCSE that varies most between boards and routes, and the part parents most often get wrong when they compare two children at two schools. It is worth establishing exactly what your child sits, because one of the available components is among the easiest sources of marks in the whole qualification and the other does not exist.

Cambridge separate sciences include either a practical test, sat in a laboratory under exam conditions, or an alternative-to-practical written paper, depending on what the centre offers. The alternative paper is the interesting one. It asks about method, variables, tables, graphs and improvements in a structure that barely changes from series to series, which makes it highly predictable and therefore highly coachable. Students neglect it because it looks like a paper about experiments they did not do.

Pearson International GCSE sciences take a different approach: there is no standalone practical paper, and experimental skills are assessed inside the written papers instead. That does not reduce the demand, it relocates it. A 4PH1 or 4CH1 student still meets questions about method and variables, and still loses marks for not naming a control, but the questions arrive mixed among theory rather than gathered in one place.

The practical implication for a Nad Al Sheba family is a single question to the school: which component does my child sit, and is it a laboratory test or a written paper? Then, if it is the alternative-to-practical route, buy three or four sessions on it specifically. Across three separate sciences the same template applies to all three, which makes it the best-value block available on this page.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson for the three sciences
paragraphs: Both boards award International GCSEs in biology, chemistry and physics, both are accepted wherever UK-curriculum qualifications are accepted, and both run June and November series available to UAE candidates. Underneath that they differ in ways that change a term of preparation, and a tutor who does not know which one a student sits will use the wrong practice material.

Cambridge uses codes 0610, 0620 and 0625 for the separate sciences and tiers them into Core and Extended, with the tier setting the grade ceiling. It also zones its timetables: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one.

Pearson uses 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, single-tier rather than tiered, and assesses experimental skills inside the written papers rather than in a separate practical component. Its results pattern is a useful checkable anchor: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so the live official timetable is the only reliable source for dates.

One correction worth making plainly because it has reached UAE parents in error before. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit June and November on both boards, and November is the standard resit route. Any revision plan built around a February exam window or a late-November entry deadline is using another country's calendar.

sections.heading: What three sciences costs in tutoring, honestly
paragraphs: A single-subject tutoring budget and a three-science one are different conversations, and the market's hourly bands disguise that. Three separate sciences can mean three tutors, three slots and three times the monthly figure, which is why the first useful question is not the rate but whether all three subjects actually need support.

In most cases they do not. The common pattern is one science clearly weaker than the other two, usually physics where the problem is mathematical or chemistry where the problem is precision. Working the weakest subject properly for a term moves a grade; spreading the same hours thinly across three moves nothing and costs the same. A diagnostic across all three in one session is the cheapest way to establish which case you are in.

The market bands, read in October 2026 and belonging to whoever published them: budget online or undergraduate tutoring AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; a qualified subject tutor online AED 150 to 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; an IGCSE specialist AED 200 to 450 or more, TutorChase publishing AED 270; in-home one-to-one AED 180 to 500 including travel, Bestimate at 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at 200 to 500; and a premium end reaching AED 650 at BartyED.

Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Published packages include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, which for a three-science student is often the efficient shape: two subjects covered weekly rather than one subject twice. Ask about session length, VAT and what happens if you stop after one lesson.

sections.heading: Three sciences, three different failure modes
paragraphs: A student who says they are bad at science is almost always bad at one of them in a specific way, and the three sciences fail differently enough that the distinction is worth making before any hours are bought. Lumping them together is how a term of generic science tutoring produces no movement in any of the three.

Biology fails on command terms and on structure. The content is dense but mostly learnable, and the marks go missing when a student explains where the paper said describe, or writes a six-mark answer as a list of facts about the topic rather than a sequenced account of the process. The fix is answer structure and command-term drilling, which is quick and highly transferable.

Chemistry fails on precision. State symbols, ionic equations, trends described rather than explained, and calculation units left unconverted. The chemistry is usually understood; the expression is incomplete. Drilling this means marking the student's own written answers strictly against the official scheme while they watch, which lands harder than any explanation and holds afterwards.

Physics fails on mathematics. Rearrangement, unit conversion, proportional reasoning and taking a gradient properly from a graph. A student who understands the physics and cannot execute the algebra loses the back half of every calculation question. The test is cheap: give them a physics question with the setup already done and ask only for the algebra. If that is where it breaks, the purchase is maths inside physics rather than more physics.
