sections.heading: Sequencing revision across three sciences
paragraphs: A separate-science student in Year 11 has three subjects competing for the same evenings, and the usual approach is to revise whichever one has an assessment next. That produces a rolling emergency rather than a plan, and in the final term it means the third science gets whatever is left over, which is nothing.

The approach that works is a rotation set in advance and written down. Decide at the start of each fortnight which of the three gets the larger share and which gets maintenance, and rotate deliberately so no subject goes three weeks without being touched. Maintenance is not nothing: twenty minutes of recall on the subject not currently in focus prevents the three-week gap that makes a topic feel unlearnt.

The second move is to run the shared work once rather than three times. Experimental method, variables, graph skills and command terms apply to all three sciences. A block on those is one purchase that improves three subjects, which no amount of content revision in a single subject can do. In the final term it is also the only remaining lever available for a student who cannot cover everything.

The third move is to write down what is being abandoned, in each of the three subjects, and show it to the student. Students resist this more than parents do, because a written list of what they will not know feels like failure. It is what makes the remaining revision concentrated enough to move a boundary. A Year 11 student with three sciences cannot revise everything, and choosing deliberately beats choosing at random.

sections.heading: Three sciences on a shared screen
paragraphs: For science tutoring the honest comparison between formats has to acknowledge what video cannot do: it cannot run a practical. The school's laboratory programme, the equipment and the supervised work are the school's job, and no outside tutor in any format replaces them. Anyone claiming otherwise is selling something that is not available.

What the examined components actually require is different. The Cambridge alternative-to-practical paper asks about method, variables, tables and graphs in writing. Pearson assesses experimental skills inside written papers. Both are desk skills, and a shared screen handles them better than a notebook: a graph can be plotted live, a gradient taken with a large triangle while both people watch, and a results table built together so the student sees why the column headings carry units.

The practical scheduling point is sharper for three sciences than for one. Three in-home visits a week in exam term means three return journeys through pick-up traffic and three travel premiums of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour each. For a Mohammed Bin Rashid City family that is not a close call. For a Nad Al Sheba family with a short school run it is a genuine choice, and presence has real value for a younger student.

sections.heading: How the science route meets MoE equivalency
paragraphs: Equivalency converts a school-leaving qualification into something UAE authorities recognise, and it governs applications to universities inside the country. It is also the place where a science-route decision taken in Year 9 can have an administrative consequence nobody mentioned at the time, which is why it belongs on this page.

The published British-track rule is specific: a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Alongside that, one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. One ranking competitor publishes six as the IGCSE subject count; the published figure is five.

What this page will not do is tell you how a double award counts towards that five. It is a reasonable question — two grades from one course is exactly the sort of case an administrative rule has to handle — and no source this project could verify states the answer. Rather than guess, ask the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority directly, and ask your school's exams officer what they have seen in practice. An invented answer on a page like this one would be a liability for the family that acted on it.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Verify everything on moe.gov.ae before acting.

sections.heading: Two questions to ask before paying anybody
paragraphs: Everything on this page reduces to a short set of checks, and across the four communities the checks are identical because the differences between them are not the ones that matter. Running them takes a few minutes and separates providers more reliably than any website copy, this page included.

The first question is for the school: what are my child's syllabus codes, which tier are they entered at, and which practical component do they sit? Three facts, one email, and they determine what correct practice looks like. A family that knows them can test any tutor in a single conversation; a family that does not is relying on the tutor to work it out, usually during paid sessions.

The second question is for the tutor: where do marks go on that specific paper? A specialist answers in command terms, state symbols, gradients and controls. A generalist answers in topic names. The difference is audible within a few minutes and it is the single most reliable signal available before money moves. Then use the free trial lesson, which exists so that judgement is yours rather than ours.

Two things worth knowing about credentials in this market. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, with eligible applicants including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18 — so anybody describing it as costly or optional is misinformed. And IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none.

Ask the tutor where marks go on that exact paper, and listen for specifics

process.title: Send the codes, the tier and the practical route
process.description: The useful opening message names the board and syllabus codes, the tier if the board tiers, the school, the year group and which practical component the child sits. Add the most recent marked script if there is one. Those facts decide which of three sciences actually needs support and what correct practice looks like.

process.title: A free diagnostic across the three
process.description: One live session that samples all three sciences rather than teaching one, usually with a short written answer from each marked strictly against the official scheme. The purpose is to find out whether one subject is clearly behind, which is the usual case, or whether the problem is shared method and timing. No payment is involved.

process.title: Buy the weakest subject, not all three
process.description: Where one science is behind, a term of weekly work on that subject moves a grade. Spreading the same hours across three moves nothing and costs the same. Where the diagnostic points at shared skills instead, the purchase is one experimental-method block that improves all three at once.

process.title: Weekly sessions on the correct code and tier
process.description: Practice is always on the student's own syllabus code and tier, with notes naming the topic, what was set and which question type comes next. Extended-tier practice given to a Core candidate demoralises them; Core practice leaves an Extended candidate unready for the back half of the paper.

process.title: Set the rotation for the exam year
process.description: A fortnightly rotation written in advance, with one subject in focus and the others on twenty-minute recall, beats revising whichever subject has the next test. A written abandoned-topic list for each of the three is part of the plan, because a Year 11 student with three sciences cannot cover everything.

process.title: Paper blocks for the final weeks
process.description: Content coverage stops and sessions become timed sections marked against official schemes, rotating across subjects deliberately rather than finishing one before starting the next. Papers come from the school's licensed access or the board's own platform, and the time goes on the marking.

whyPoints.title: The route checked before the teaching
whyPoints.description: Single award, double award and three separate sciences are different qualifications with different volumes and different post-16 doors. Where a student is drowning, the first question is whether the route is right, which is a conversation most providers skip entirely.

whyPoints.title: Three sciences, three diagnoses
whyPoints.description: Biology fails on command terms, chemistry on precision of expression, physics on mathematical execution. Generic science tutoring treats them as one subject and moves none of them. The diagnostic samples all three before any hours are committed.

whyPoints.title: The practical paper treated as the opportunity it is
whyPoints.description: Where the student sits Cambridge's alternative-to-practical paper, its structure barely changes between series and the same template serves all three sciences. Three or four sessions on it improves three subjects, which no content block can do.

whyPoints.title: Codes and tiers confirmed, not assumed
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 need different practice, and Cambridge tiers set the grade ceiling. We ask for the codes and tier before matching a tutor, because wrong-tier practice is the most common wasted hour in this subject.

faqs.question: Is the IGCSE science tutoring based in Nad Al Sheba or delivered online?
faqs.answer: Online, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a student taking three separate sciences the format decides whether three sessions a week are schedulable at all: three video slots are three slots, while three in-home visits mean three return journeys through pick-up traffic and three travel premiums of roughly AED 50 to 150 an hour above the online band.

faqs.question: What is the difference between double award and three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Double award — Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0 — covers all three sciences in one course and awards two IGCSE grades, with genuinely reduced content rather than the same syllabus compressed. Three separate sciences award three grades, require six or more papers and carry roughly a third more examined material. Separate sciences are needed for A Level and IB Higher Level sciences; double award keeps most other routes open, including many competitive degrees that require no science.

faqs.question: Can my child change science route if they are struggling?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deadline is the school's internal entry deadline rather than the board's, which sits in the autumn of Year 11 at the latest. Ask the exams officer two questions in writing: can my child move between routes, and by when. Both have short answers and cost the school nothing to give. Where a student on three separate sciences is drowning, the route is sometimes the problem rather than the teaching, and that conversation is worth having before buying hours.

faqs.question: Which practical paper does my child actually sit?
faqs.answer: It depends on the board and the centre. Cambridge separate sciences include either a laboratory practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, and which one is offered is decided at centre level, so ask the exams officer. Pearson International GCSE sciences have no standalone practical paper and assess experimental skills inside the written papers instead. If your child sits the Cambridge written alternative, that is among the most coachable papers in the qualification and worth three or four dedicated sessions.

faqs.question: Why is my child good at biology and poor at physics?
faqs.answer: Because the three sciences fail differently. Biology is content-dense but mostly learnable, and its marks go missing on command terms and answer structure. Physics is mathematical, and a student who understands the concepts but cannot rearrange fluently or convert units loses the back half of every calculation. Test it directly: give them a physics question with the setup already done and ask only for the algebra. If that is where it breaks, the purchase is maths inside physics rather than more physics content.

faqs.question: Do we need three tutors for three sciences?
faqs.answer: Usually not. The common pattern is one science clearly behind the other two, and a term of weekly work on that subject moves a grade while the same hours spread across three move nothing. Where the diagnostic points at shared skills instead — experimental method, graph work, command terms, timing — one block of three or four sessions improves all three at once. Three separate weekly tutors is the right answer occasionally and is usually a sign of a route problem.

faqs.question: Which exam board does my child's school use for science?
faqs.answer: Ask for the syllabus codes rather than the board name, because some schools split boards by subject. You are looking for Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or 0654 for Co-ordinated Sciences, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 or 4SD0. Also ask which tier, because Cambridge tiers into Core and Extended and the tier sets the grade ceiling. Those two facts determine what correct practice looks like, and wrong-tier practice is the most common wasted hour in IGCSE science.

faqs.question: How much should we expect to pay for science tutoring in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Hourly bands read in October 2026: AED 45 to 150 for budget online tutoring, with EdFlik from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52; AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150; AED 200 to 450 or more for a specialist, TutorChase publishing AED 270; AED 180 to 500 for in-home including travel; and up to AED 650 at BartyED. For three sciences the monthly arithmetic matters more than the rate, so decide first whether all three need support.

faqs.question: How should a Year 11 student revise three sciences at once?
faqs.answer: Set a fortnightly rotation in advance rather than revising whichever subject has the next test, which produces a rolling emergency. One subject takes the larger share while the others get twenty minutes of recall, then rotate, so no subject goes three weeks untouched. Run the shared work — method, variables, graphs, command terms — once rather than three times. Then write an abandoned-topic list for each subject, because three sciences cannot all be covered and choosing deliberately beats choosing at random.

faqs.question: When are the IGCSE science exams for UAE candidates?
faqs.answer: Both Cambridge and Pearson run series available to UAE candidates in June and November, with November the standard resit route. The February and March Cambridge series is offered to India only, so any plan built around a February exam window is using another country's calendar. For exact dates use your school's timetable: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong one.

faqs.question: Does a double award count as two subjects for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: That is a fair question and this page will not guess at it. The published British-track rule requires five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, and no source we could verify states how a double award is counted within that. Ask the Ministry of Education or your emirate's attestation authority directly, and ask your school's exams officer what they have seen in practice. An invented answer here would be your liability.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the practical coursework or lab write-ups?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the thinking: variables, fair tests, how to build a results table with units in the headings, how to take a gradient properly, and what an improvement question is asking for. A tutor cannot run a practical — the school's laboratory programme, equipment and supervision are the school's job and no format replaces them — and will not produce data, results or written work for submission. Any provider offering to supply results is offering something that puts the student at risk.

faqs.question: Is a science grade enough to get into A Level sciences here?
faqs.answer: Read your own school's published entry requirement for its sixth form or Diploma, because they differ between schools and are revised. What is consistent is that A Level sciences and IB Higher Level sciences assume separate-science content in their first term, so a double award student entering either is starting with a gap to close. That is worth knowing in Year 10, while the route can still change, rather than in August of Year 11 when it cannot.

faqs.question: Do tutors in Dubai need any kind of licence?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

faqs.question: What is the fastest improvement available in IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: Experimental method, if the student has not been taught it properly. Variables, fair tests, repeat readings, tables with units in the headings, graphs with proper gradients and improvement questions appear somewhere on every science route on both boards, and most schools teach the topic once in Year 10 and never return. Three or four sessions on it improves all three sciences at once, which no amount of content revision in one subject can do.

faqs.question: Does it matter that we live in Mohammed Bin Rashid City rather than Nad Al Sheba?
faqs.answer: Only for timing, and only if a tutor has to drive. District One's internal roads and single exit onto Al Khail absorb twenty minutes at pick-up, which makes three in-home science sessions a week impractical and three video sessions ordinary. Nad Al Sheba and Sobha Hartland have schools inside their boundaries and can take a 15:30 start. What actually varies between the communities is the board and science route their schools use, and that follows no map at all.

intro.heading: The question behind the search, answered properly
paragraphs: A family in Oud Metha looking for science help has almost always had the same experience. They ask around the building, somebody recommends a tutor two streets away, the tutor says yes to IGCSE science, and three weeks later the Year 11 student is being taught material that is not on their paper. Nobody involved was dishonest. The word science covers at least five distinct Cambridge qualifications and three Pearson ones, and the difference between them is not a matter of emphasis.

So the first thing this page does is tell you how to find out what your child is actually sitting. It is on the exam entry statement the school issues, and it is a four-digit number for Cambridge or a code beginning with four for Pearson. Cambridge Biology is 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Combined Science 0653 and Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. Pearson International GCSE Biology is 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1 and Double Award Science 4SD0. Ask the school office for the statement if you have not seen it. Everything that follows depends on it.

The second thing is the honest part. The pool of people within a short drive of Oud Metha who have taught a specific one of those codes to examination, repeatedly, and know where its mark scheme is unforgiving, is not large. Oud Metha sits in a dense and well-schooled part of Dubai, but it is a British, Indian and IB mix rather than a single-board cluster, and science is three subjects not one. A Chemistry 0620 specialist who is also fluent in Physics 0625 practical papers is a particular person, and geography is a poor way to find them.

Delivering lessons online solves that, and IB Gram delivers to Oud Metha families one-to-one over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. The practical gain is specific to this search. Instead of choosing between the two or three science tutors who can reach your building by 5pm, you choose from everybody who can teach your child's code at 5pm Gulf Standard Time. The shortlist stops being a map problem and becomes a syllabus problem, which is the problem you actually have.

The rest of this page is the working. It sets out the board differences with codes and papers, explains the Core and Extended tier decision and what it does to the grade ceiling, describes how practical science is assessed when there is no laboratory in the room, names where marks are lost paper by paper, gives the June and November series dates from Cambridge's and Pearson's own pages, prices the Bur Dubai market in AED with attribution, and sets out what the Ministry of Education equivalency rules actually require. No figure here is unattributed and no exam date is restated without its source.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-oud-metha.programmesIntro: An IGCSE science course does not sit alone. It follows a lower-secondary stage that decides how ready a student is, and it feeds a post-16 route that decides which tier they needed. These are the stages either side of it, and what each one changes.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary
programmes.description: Science at this stage is taught as one subject with three strands, assessed through Checkpoint tests rather than public examinations. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The strand that predicts IGCSE difficulty most reliably is not recall. It is handling data: reading a table, plotting it, and saying what it shows without being told.
programmes.countryNote: In the Bur Dubai belt this stage is where a parent can act cheaply. A Year 8 student in Oud Metha who cannot plot a graph unaided is a Year 11 student who will lose practical-paper marks, and the repair at Year 8 is a handful of sessions rather than a term. Almost nobody buys tuition here, which is why almost everybody buys it later.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE sciences
programmes.description: Three separate sciences at 0610, 0620 and 0625, or the combined routes at 0653 and 0654. Each separate science is tiered into Core and Extended, with a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. The tier decision is made by the school, usually in Year 10, and it sets the grade ceiling for the whole course.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs its IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Your child's Oud Metha or Bur Dubai school knows its zone; ask.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences
programmes.description: Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 each sit in a single tier with two written papers, and Double Award Science is 4SD0. There is no separate practical examination: practical knowledge is assessed inside the written papers, which changes how apparatus and method should be revised. A student who prepares for a practical paper that does not exist has wasted weeks.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always check the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com rather than a restated date.

programmes.name: IB Diploma and International A Level, post-16
programmes.description: Where the tier decision shows its consequences. A student who took Core tier, or Combined Science, arrives at Diploma Chemistry or International A Level Physics with a genuine content gap rather than a confidence gap. Extended tier, or the Co-ordinated double award, is the route schools in this belt expect before they timetable a science at Higher Level.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma provision reachable from Oud Metha sits mainly in Al Jaddaf and Dubai Festival City, while the British post-16 route is available closer to home in Bur Dubai. If the Diploma is the plan, ask the receiving school in Year 10 which tier and which code it expects, and make the tier decision with that answer in hand rather than after results day.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-oud-metha.subjectsIntro: Science is three subjects and two boards, and each combination examines differently. These are the courses we teach for students in Oud Metha, written as what each one actually assesses rather than as a list of topics.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620)
subjects.description: The mole concept is the hinge of the whole course and the place a weak start is hardest to repair later. Electrolysis and the organic families follow it. Extended-tier questions ask for calculation chains where Core asks for recall, so the tier changes the kind of practice needed, not only the amount.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and waves take the largest share of lost marks, and almost all of it is unit handling and rearrangement rather than concept. A student who writes the right physics in the wrong unit loses the mark, every time, and no amount of content revision changes that.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610)
subjects.description: Deceptively verbal. The content reads easily and the marks are lost in precision: the difference between diffusion and osmosis stated exactly, the genetics cross set out fully, the extended response that answers all three parts of the question rather than the first.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0654)
subjects.description: Covers all three sciences and counts as two qualifications. The common failure is treating it as three light courses rather than one examined whole: the papers move between sciences without warning, and students who revise in silos lose time switching.

subjects.name: Combined Science (Cambridge 0653)
subjects.description: One qualification across all three sciences at reduced depth. A reasonable choice for a student heading to a non-science post-16 route, and a real problem for one who later wants Diploma Chemistry, because the mole and electrolysis coverage is thinner than the Diploma assumes.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Two written papers, no separate practical examination, and practical knowledge examined inside the theory. Apparatus, method and expected observations therefore have to be revised as content, which is a different habit from preparing for a Cambridge practical test.

subjects.name: Physics (Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Single-tier entry means no grade ceiling set in Year 10, which suits a student who improves late. The formula handling is the same discipline as Cambridge; the difference is in how practical method appears in the written papers.

subjects.name: Biology (Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Extended-response marks reward structure heavily. Students who have been taught to answer in bullet points lose marks they knew the content for, and that is a technique fix rather than a revision fix.

subjects.name: Double Award Science (Pearson 4SD0)
subjects.description: Pearson's two-qualification route across the three sciences. Useful where a school timetable cannot fit three separate sciences, and it keeps most post-16 doors open, but confirm the receiving school's entry expectations before relying on that.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: Included because science marks depend on it. Standard form, ratio, rearrangement and percentage change appear in every science paper, and a student on Foundation-tier maths will hit a ceiling in Extended-tier science that looks like a science problem.

sections.heading: Step one: find out which syllabus your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: There is a document that answers this and most parents have never been shown it. The exam entry statement issued by the school lists each subject with its board and its syllabus code. For Cambridge the code is four digits: Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Combined Science 0653, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. For Pearson it begins with a four: Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1, Physics 4PH1, Double Award Science 4SD0. Ask the school office for the statement. It takes one email and it removes the single largest cause of wasted tuition in this market.

Why it matters is not administrative. The two boards examine differently in ways that change what a student should practise. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered and carry either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper. Pearson sits in one tier with two written papers and assesses practical knowledge inside them. A student revising apparatus diagrams for a Cambridge practical test is doing necessary work; the same student on 4CH1 is preparing for a paper that does not exist, and losing the weeks they needed for extended response.

The table below sets the two boards side by side for the same three subjects. Use it with the entry statement in front of you, not instead of it, and confirm paper structure and weightings with your child's school, because boards revise specifications between cycles and a figure found online can be a cycle out of date. One syllabus code appears across the entire seven-page area cluster researched for this project. Knowing yours is already an advantage.

sections.heading: Is there anybody near Oud Metha who really knows this code?
paragraphs: This is the question the search is really asking, and it deserves a direct answer rather than reassurance. Within a short drive of Oud Metha there are certainly people who can teach secondary science. The number who have taught one specific code to examination, repeatedly, and know where its mark scheme refuses to give credit, is much smaller. Narrow it further to somebody free in the one weekday window your family can use, and in a dense but board-mixed neighbourhood the list can come down to nobody.

That is not a criticism of the area. It is arithmetic. Oud Metha and the Bur Dubai belt serve British, Indian and IB provision simultaneously, so the local tutoring pool is spread across boards rather than concentrated in one. KHDA's 2024-25 figures describe a Dubai market of 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering seventeen curricula, with UK 37%, Indian 26%, US 14% and International Baccalaureate 7%. A mixed market produces mixed tutors, and a mixed tutor is exactly the wrong person for a specific paper.

Online delivery is the honest fix, and it is why IB Gram works this way. The constraint stops being who lives nearby and becomes who is free at the hour you need, which is a far larger pool and one you can filter by code. IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are offered only in India. If no specialist in your child's exact code is available in your window, we say so and tell you when one is, rather than putting a general science tutor in the slot and letting the term pass.
bullets: Ask any prospective tutor which code they have taught to examination, and how often
Ask what the alternative-to-practical paper requires, and listen for whether it applies
Ask where that paper's mark scheme refuses credit; a specialist answers instantly
A tutor who says all IGCSE science is the same has answered the question

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the decision that sets the ceiling
paragraphs: For Cambridge separate sciences the school enters each student at Core or Extended tier, usually during Year 10. Core covers less content and reaches a lower maximum grade; Extended covers the full content and reaches the top of the scale. The decision is made on predicted performance, and once made it is difficult to reverse late in Year 11 because the papers differ. Many parents in this belt learn the tier exists only when a mock result arrives with an unexpected cap on it.

The academic consequence is clearest for a student intending a science post-16. Extended tier, or the Co-ordinated double award, is what schools in Bur Dubai and across the Creek expect before timetabling a Diploma science at Higher Level or an International A Level. A Core-tier student can still progress, but arrives with a content gap that takes four to six weeks of focused work to close, and that work is cheapest in the summer before Year 12 rather than in the middle of it.

Where tuition helps most is not in arguing about the tier. It is in making the tier decision on evidence. Three weeks of Extended-tier past-paper questions, marked honestly, tells a family more than a term of predicted grades. If the student can handle the calculation chains, make the case to the school with the papers in hand. If they cannot, the Core decision is correct and the money is better spent elsewhere.

sections.heading: How practical science is examined when nobody is in a laboratory
paragraphs: This is the most common worry about online science tuition and it rests on a misunderstanding of how the qualification works. Neither board asks a tutor to supervise an experiment. Cambridge examines practical work either through a practical test sat under examination conditions at the centre, or through an alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson examines practical knowledge inside its two written papers. In every case the thing being assessed is written: a method described, a reading interpreted, a source of error identified.

That makes the practical component unusually well suited to one-to-one work over video. The student shares the question, the tutor watches the answer being written, and the errors show up immediately: a method with no stated control variable, a table without units in the header, a graph with an awkward scale chosen to avoid the arithmetic, a conclusion that restates the data rather than explaining it. Those are visible on a shared screen in a way they are not visible across a kitchen table while somebody waits.

The school remains responsible for the laboratory work itself, and a tutor should never offer to replace it. What a tutor can do is make sure the student can describe what they did and evaluate it in the language the mark scheme rewards. For Pearson candidates this matters more than parents expect, because apparatus and expected observations have to be revised as content rather than recalled from a lesson. A Bur Dubai student who has done the experiments and cannot write them up is losing marks for writing, not for science.

sections.heading: Where IGCSE science marks are actually lost, paper by paper
paragraphs: Multiple choice is lost to speed and to misread stems rather than to ignorance. Students who know the material arrive at the last five questions with four minutes left and guess. The fix is volume under a clock, which needs no insight and can be done late in the course, so it is the cheapest thing on this list and the thing to leave until last.

Theory papers are lost to answer length. The mark allocation is a set of instructions and students treat it as a suggestion: three marks, one sentence. In Biology this is the single largest source of lost marks, because the content reads easily and the precision is where the credit is. In Chemistry it is calculation chains abandoned halfway, where a student who shows the first two steps earns more than one who shows a wrong final answer alone. In Physics it is units and rearrangement, relentlessly.

Practical and alternative-to-practical papers are lost to method vocabulary. Control variable, range, repeat, anomaly, resolution and systematic error are words with precise meanings in a mark scheme and approximate meanings in ordinary speech. A student who writes I did it three times to be accurate has said something the scheme cannot credit. Teaching those six words properly is perhaps two sessions and moves marks in all three sciences at once, which makes it the best value work available on an IGCSE science course.

One further loss is invisible until a paper is marked honestly: question selection order. Students work front to back, spend eleven minutes on an early six-mark question they half know, and reach the final structured question with no time. Teaching a student to scan, bank the questions they can finish, and return to the rest is a technique session rather than a science one. It is also the only intervention on this list that works equally well in Biology, Chemistry and Physics without any subject knowledge changing hands.
bullets: Multiple choice: timed volume, left to the final weeks
Theory: answer length matched to the mark allocation
Chemistry: show every step of a calculation chain
Physics: units and rearrangement before content

sections.heading: The June and November series, counted backwards
paragraphs: UAE candidates sit two series, and the planning value of knowing which one comes next is considerable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. The February and March series is offered to India only and is not an option for a UAE candidate, so a plan built around it is a plan built around the wrong country.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For results timing, June 2026 Pearson results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, including the International GCSE November series months before entries for it close, so the live timetable on qualifications.pearson.com is the document to work from rather than any date restated on a page like this one.

One Cambridge administrative detail is worth a parent's attention because it has real consequences. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. If your child is revising from a timetable found online rather than from the one the school issued, check the zone. Then build the eight weeks before the series backwards from the real dates.

sections.heading: What science tuition costs in the Bur Dubai market
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market rather than the top, because that is where most Oud Metha enquiries start. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, both at the budget online tier, typically delivered by university students. For a Year 10 student who needs company and structure rather than paper expertise, that tier can be reasonable. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from a series, a tutor who does not know whether the alternative-to-practical paper applies is not cheap at any price.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online is quoted across Dubai at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, reviewed October 2026, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE and from AED 200 for IB. Specialist IB and IGCSE support is quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 650, as BartyED publishes. In-home one-to-one sits at AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table, with independent home tutors advertising up to AED 500.

The one figure that explains the rest is the monthly package comparison. Advertised rates in Dubai include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. The teaching can be identical; the second price includes a car crossing Bur Dubai twice. None of these are IB Gram prices. Ours follows a free trial lesson and a look at the actual mark breakdown, which is the only basis on which an hourly figure means anything. For context on the wider household budget, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai do not rise for 2026-27.

sections.heading: How many IGCSE subjects the Ministry of Education actually counts
paragraphs: Families in Oud Metha planning a UAE university route need the equivalency rules, and the rules are more generous than the rumour. For the British track, students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That five-subject figure is worth stating because it is commonly got wrong. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced position is five, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from the count. Nothing on this page should be treated as the authority, though: verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority before making a subject decision on them, and treat any page restating them, including this one, as a pointer to the official source.

For completeness on the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. No IB points threshold is published in that source, so no IB equivalency figure appears here. Two further points matter for a tutoring decision: equivalency is a process the Ministry runs, not something a tutor performs or influences, and tutoring is not required for it. Anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency.

process.title: Send the syllabus code, or ask the school for it
process.description: The exam entry statement names the board and the code for each science. With 0620 or 4CH1 in the first message, a match takes a fraction of the time it takes from the word science. If you cannot find the statement, one email to the school office produces it, and it is the most useful thing you can do before spending anything.

process.title: Free trial lesson used as a diagnostic
process.description: The tutor sets questions across the whole paper rather than the current topic, watches where the method breaks, and reports what they found. If the match is wrong you say so and nothing is owed. The condition is one trial lesson per student. This is the step that catches a board mismatch before it costs a term.

process.title: A written plan naming the paper and the target
process.description: After the trial you get the topics, the order, roughly how many sessions and what the block should achieve, stated against the paper rather than the syllabus. A plan that cannot name its objective becomes a standing weekly slot, which is the most expensive way to buy tuition in this market.

process.title: A fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Lessons run live over video at a time chosen around the Bur Dubai school run, usually between 4.30pm and 7pm on a weekday. No travel is added at either end, so a 5pm session starts at 5pm. Ramadan timings can move to post-Iftar slots on request.

process.title: Review against the plan, including the option to stop
process.description: At the end of the block you get the mark evidence and a recommendation, which may be to stop. For many IGCSE students the right answer after eight focused weeks is that the gap has closed and the money is better spent on a different subject next term.

whyPoints.title: Matched by code, not by subject word
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0620 and Pearson 4CH1 are different courses with different papers. We match on the code from the exam entry statement, which removes the commonest and most expensive failure in local tutoring: a good tutor teaching the wrong specification very well.

whyPoints.title: The pool is everybody free at that hour
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means your shortlist is not drawn from the people who can reach Oud Metha by 5pm. It is drawn from everybody who can teach your child's paper at 5pm Gulf Standard Time, which is how a specific specialism becomes findable at all.

whyPoints.title: Dates taken from the boards, not restated loosely
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates on this page carry their source, and the February and March series is named as India-only because it is. A plan built on a wrong exam window is worse than no plan, and it is a mistake that has been published to UAE parents before.

whyPoints.description: Every AED band here names the provider that published it and the month it was read. Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and one asks the price in its own FAQ and then declines to answer it.

whyPoints.description: If nobody is free in your window for your child's exact code, we tell you, and tell you when somebody will be. faqs.question: How do I find out which IGCSE science syllabus my child is taking?
faqs.answer: It is on the exam entry statement the school issues, which lists each subject with its board and code. Cambridge codes are four digits: Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625, Combined Science 0653, Co-ordinated Sciences 0654. Pearson International GCSE codes begin with a four: 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SD0 for Double Award. If you have not been sent the statement, one email to the school office produces it. Do this before paying for anything, because the two boards examine practical work differently and a tutor preparing your child for a paper they will not sit is the most expensive mistake available in this market.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE sciences cover the same material?
faqs.answer: They overlap substantially in content and differ in structure, which is what matters for revision. Cambridge separate sciences are tiered into Core and Extended and carry either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson sits in a single tier with two written papers and assesses practical knowledge inside them, with no separate practical component. So a Pearson candidate has to revise apparatus, method and expected observations as content, while a Cambridge candidate prepares for a specific paper about them. Confirm the paper structure and weightings with your child's school, since both boards revise specifications between cycles.

faqs.question: Can an online tutor really help with practical science?
faqs.answer: Yes, because neither board assesses the experiment itself through a tutor. Cambridge examines practical work through a practical test sat at the centre or through an alternative-to-practical written paper; Pearson examines it inside the written papers. In every case the assessed thing is written: a method described, a reading interpreted, a source of error named. Those errors are visible immediately on a shared screen, which is why one-to-one video work suits this component well. The school stays responsible for the laboratory work, and no tutor should offer to replace it.

faqs.question: My child is on Core tier. Does that limit what they can do afterwards?
faqs.answer: It limits the grade available and it creates a real content gap for post-16 sciences, but it does not close the route. Core tier covers a reduced subset of the syllabus and caps the maximum grade below the top of the scale; Extended covers the full content and reaches the top. Schools in Bur Dubai and across the Creek generally expect Extended tier, or the Co-ordinated double award, before timetabling a Diploma science at Higher Level. If Core is the entry, budget four to six weeks of focused work in the summer before Year 12 rather than discovering the gap in October.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science do UAE students lose the most marks on?
faqs.answer: Across the three, the largest single cause is answer length rather than any one subject. Students treat the mark allocation as a suggestion and write one sentence for three marks. In Biology that is the dominant loss, because the content reads easily and the credit sits in precision. In Chemistry it is calculation chains abandoned halfway, where showing two correct steps earns more than a bare wrong answer. In Physics it is units and rearrangement, consistently. Fixing answer length is technique work rather than content revision, and it moves marks in all three papers at once.

faqs.question: When do UAE students sit IGCSE science exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series; Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November, and the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. The February and March series is offered to India only and does not apply to UAE candidates. Work from the timetable your school issued rather than one found online, and check it on cambridgeinternational.org or qualifications.pearson.com.

faqs.question: Why does Cambridge ask about an administrative zone?
faqs.answer: Because the same exam runs at different local times around the world. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a timetable version per zone. Its own guidance states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Your child's school in Oud Metha or Bur Dubai knows which zone it sits in. If revision is being planned from a timetable found online, check the zone before trusting any date on it.

faqs.question: How many sessions does one IGCSE science usually need?
faqs.answer: For a Year 11 student with a defined gap, eight to twelve weekly sessions is a realistic block, and the honest answer at the end of it is often that no more are needed. For a student behind in all three sciences, rotating one weekly session across Biology, Chemistry and Physics usually produces more movement than three separate slots, because the method work on units, graphs and answer length transfers between them. Avoid open-ended weekly arrangements with no stated objective; they run for two years and nobody involved has to judge whether they worked.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE science tutor cost in Oud Metha?
faqs.answer: Dubai market rates, reviewed October 2026, start at the budget online tier where Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 to 52 an hour and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65, usually delivered by university students. A qualified subject tutor working online is quoted at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing from AED 150 for IGCSE. Specialist support runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. In-home one-to-one is AED 180 to 350 in Bestimate's 2026 table. Those are other providers' figures. IB Gram sets pricing after a free trial lesson and a look at the mark breakdown.

faqs.question: Is a cheap tutor a false economy for IGCSE science?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on the job. For a Year 9 or Year 10 student who needs structure, homework discipline and somebody to sit with, the budget online tier at AED 33 to 65 an hour can be perfectly sensible and is what many Oud Metha families should buy. For a Year 11 student eight weeks from a series, a tutor who cannot say whether the alternative-to-practical paper applies to their entry is expensive at any rate, because the weeks are not replaceable. Match the tier to the task rather than to the anxiety.

faqs.question: Do my child's IGCSE sciences count towards UAE equivalency, and how many subjects are needed?
faqs.answer: Five subjects are counted. Students on the British track must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects, which is not what the sourced guidance says. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, because equivalency is the Ministry's process and no tutor performs or influences it.

faqs.question: Which schools near Oud Metha teach IGCSE sciences?
faqs.answer: The British-curriculum provision closest to an Oud Metha address includes St Mary's Catholic High School and Dubai Gem Private School, with Ambassador School in Al Mankhool and Dubai English Speaking School nearby. Across the Creek, Deira International School and Al Ittihad Private School in Al Mamzar also run IGCSE before splitting into post-16 routes. Boards vary between them, and some run Cambridge while others run Pearson, so never assume from the school name. Check the current KHDA inspection report alongside the school's own subject list, both of which are published.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover Biology, Chemistry and Physics?
faqs.answer: Some can, and the honest test is whether they can name where each paper's mark scheme refuses credit. A tutor fluent in all three at Extended tier exists but is uncommon, and claiming the range is easier than holding it. Where one tutor genuinely covers all three, rotation is efficient and cheaper than three separate slots. Where they do not, it is better to take one specialist for the weakest subject and leave the others to school support than to buy shallow coverage across three papers. Ask for the codes they have taught to examination.

faqs.question: What happens if nobody is available for my child's exact syllabus?
faqs.answer: We tell you, and we tell you when somebody will be. The alternative, putting a general science tutor into the slot and hoping, is the quiet failure that costs a family a term, and no competitor page researched for this project discloses a coverage limit at all. If your window cannot be covered, the realistic options are to move the slot, to start with a defined block on the work any strong science teacher can move such as method vocabulary and answer structure, or to wait. We will say which of the three we think applies to you.

faqs.question: Do you supply past papers or mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge, Pearson and IB syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables are copyright material, and reproducing or distributing them is infringement. A tutor works with material the student legitimately holds through their school, cites the official source and links to it: cambridgeinternational.org for Cambridge qualifications and qualifications.pearson.com for Pearson Edexcel. Your child's school is the proper route to released papers and current specifications, and the school also holds the correct zone timetable, which matters more than any copy circulating online.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingHeading: Get the code, then get the right tutor
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-oud-metha.closingBody: The useful order for an Oud Metha family is short. Ask the school office for the exam entry statement and read the board and code against each science. Send that code with your enquiry. Take the free trial lesson and let the tutor set questions across the whole paper rather than the topic the student is currently on, then read what they report. Choose a block with a named objective and an end date. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, timed around the Bur Dubai school run, with Ramadan slots available after Iftar. If nobody is free for your code in your window, we will tell you that rather than fill it.

intro.heading: Three sciences or one? The answer changes everything else
paragraphs: Families on Palm Jumeirah searching for science help usually describe the problem as a grade. The more useful description is a structure. A student entered for Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 is sitting three separate courses with three sets of papers, three practical routes and three final grades. A student entered for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 or Pearson Science Double Award 4SD0 is sitting one course that covers all three disciplines in a single set of papers. The content overlaps heavily. The weekly workload, the revision arithmetic and the sensible tutoring plan do not.

That matters more on this island than almost anywhere else in Dubai, because of a piece of geography. Palm Jumeirah has no secondary school. Every Year 10 and Year 11 student here leaves the island in the morning and returns across the Trunk in the afternoon, arriving home somewhere between 15:45 and 16:45 depending on whether you live on the Trunk, part-way down a frond or over on the Crescent. A triple scientist then has three subjects of homework, three sets of past papers and a practical paper to prepare for, in whatever is left of an evening that started in a car.

The second thing nobody explains is that the two exam boards assess practical work by different routes, and the route matters for how tutoring should work. Cambridge examines practical skills in a dedicated paper worth a fifth of the grade: either Paper 5, a practical test sat in a laboratory, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is a written paper about experiments. Pearson International GCSE has no separate practical paper at all and assesses practical skills inside the written papers. If your child is on Cambridge Paper 6, a very large share of the practical marks is available to a student who never touches apparatus, because the paper is about reading tables, spotting anomalies, controlling variables and suggesting improvements on paper.

IB Gram delivers these lessons one-to-one over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE and we run no centre in Dubai; home visits are a service we offer only in India. For science specifically, online delivery has a concrete advantage beyond scheduling: your child gets a chemist for chemistry and a physicist for physics instead of one general science tutor who is strong in one of the three and competent in the others, which is what a driving radius around a dead-end frond tends to produce.

This page is organised around the structure rather than around a sales pitch. It maps which science route the schools in the Palm commute belt actually run, shows how Cambridge and Pearson differ on practicals, sets out where marks go missing subject by subject, and works through the cost of three sciences from the cheapest end of the market upwards. Every AED figure is somebody else's published number with a source and a date, not our price list.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-palm-jumeir.programmesIntro: Science at 16 sits inside a longer sequence, and the choice made in Year 9 constrains what is available at 18. These are the programmes a science tutor working with Palm Jumeirah families is asked about, with what each one does to the science workload.

programmes.name: International GCSE science (Years 10-11)
programmes.description: Either three separate sciences, a double award covering all three in one course, or a single award. Most selective Dubai schools default to triple for the stronger sets and a double award for the rest, and the decision is usually taken at the end of Year 9. Both tiers exist at Cambridge: Core caps the grade range, Extended opens the top grades and examines additional content.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai the entry is made by the school as a Cambridge or Pearson centre, and Cambridge allocates each centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. For the practical sciences this matters twice over, because a Paper 5 practical test has to be scheduled in a laboratory with apparatus, and centres make the Paper 5 or Paper 6 decision for their candidates rather than leaving it to families.

programmes.name: IB MYP Sciences (Years 7-11)
programmes.description: The IB middle-school route run by several schools in the Palm commute belt. MYP Sciences is assessed against four criteria out of eight, including inquiring and designing and processing and evaluating, which are close cousins of the skills a Cambridge practical paper tests. Students coming from MYP often have strong investigation design and weak timed recall, which is the reverse of the usual IGCSE problem.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's IB continuum schools cluster in Al Barsha, Al Barsha South, Al Safa and Umm Al Sheif, so an island family in this route is on a twenty-five to forty-five minute afternoon run. MYP assessment is spread through units across the year rather than concentrated in a series, so science support here is steadier and less seasonal than for a Year 11 Cambridge candidate.

programmes.name: IB Diploma sciences (Years 12-13)
programmes.description: Biology, Chemistry, Physics, Computer Science, Design Technology, Environmental Systems and Societies and Sports Science, at Higher or Standard Level, with a scientific investigation as the internal assessment. A triple-science IGCSE background makes Higher Level a realistic choice in two of the three; a single or double award makes it a steep climb, and that is a decision taken at 14, not at 16.
programmes.countryNote: Medicine, dentistry and engineering applications from the UAE commonly expect Chemistry and one other science at Higher Level, so the Year 9 science decision quietly shapes the degree list five years later. No IB points figure for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency is published that this page can cite, so none appears here; confirm any such figure on the Ministry's own site.

programmes.name: A Level sciences (Years 12-13)
programmes.description: The other post-16 route in the belt. A Level Chemistry and Physics both assume fluency with the mathematical parts of IGCSE science: rearranging formulae, logarithms of concentration, moles and gradients. Students who arrive from a double award without that fluency spend the autumn term catching up on arithmetic rather than learning new chemistry, which is the most common first-term problem reported by Dubai sixth forms.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. A November science entry is usually a retake or an early entry, and it compresses revision into the first half of the autumn term, which is also when A Level content is heaviest.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-palm-jumeir.subjectsIntro: Science at IGCSE is not one subject and should not be bought as one. These are the courses a science tutor working with students on Palm Jumeirah is asked for, with what each one assesses and where it is hardest.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Multiple choice, theory and either a practical test or the alternative to practical. The marks cluster in precision of language: osmosis and water potential, enzyme graphs explained rather than described, transect and sampling method, genetic cross notation set out properly. Extended adds content and expects linked reasoning in the longer answers.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The syllabus where arithmetic decides grades. Reacting masses and moles, limiting reagents, ionic equations with state symbols, electrolysis products and half-equations, rates from a gradient, the organic homologous series and the tests for ions. A student who can do the chemistry but not the calculation sits two grades below their understanding.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Units, prefixes and formula rearrangement run through every paper. Moments, series and parallel circuit reasoning, ray diagrams with measured angles, graph gradients that are themselves quantities, specific heat capacity and radioactive decay. Physics rewards a student who writes the formula, substitutes and states the unit, and punishes one who calculates in their head.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: One course covering biology, chemistry and physics, examined together and awarded as a double award. It is the right choice for most students who are not heading into science at 18, and it is poorly served by tutors because it demands fluency across all three disciplines in one hour rather than depth in any one of them.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: A single-award course across the three sciences, lighter than 0654 and reported as one grade. Students on it sometimes want to move up to the double award or to triple science, and that decision is bounded by the centre's final entry deadline rather than by a conversation in a parents' evening.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers, with the longer paper carrying the larger share, and no separate practical paper. Practical skills are examined inside the written papers through core practicals, data tables and method evaluation. Extended six-mark answers reward structure and linked scientific reasoning rather than a list of recalled facts.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Two written papers on the 9 to 1 scale, with practical skills assessed within them. The calculation load is similar to Cambridge but the question framing is more structured, so method marks are more generously available to a student who writes out the working rather than only the answer.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Two written papers, with practical skills embedded rather than separately examined. The mathematical content is explicit and heavily weighted, which makes it the Pearson science where weak algebra shows up fastest. Students moving to A Level Physics from 4PH1 usually need the formula-handling habits built in Year 11, not Year 12.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel Science Double Award 4SD0
subjects.description: The Pearson equivalent of a co-ordinated course, covering all three sciences and awarding two grades. It suits students who need science qualifications without a science future, and it needs a tutor comfortable switching between disciplines inside one session, which is a different skill from subject depth.

subjects.name: Cambridge practical test and alternative to practical
subjects.description: Worth a fifth of the Cambridge grade in each separate science. Paper 6, the alternative to practical, is a written paper about experiments: variables, table headings with units, lines of best fit, anomalies, safety precautions and improvements. Almost all of it can be taught without apparatus, and almost nobody practises it deliberately.

sections.heading: Which science route is your child actually on?
paragraphs: The first thing to establish is not the grade, the school or the tutor. It is the entry. Three separate sciences means three syllabus codes, three sets of papers and three grades on the statement of results. A double award means one course across all three disciplines and two identical grades. A single award means one course and one grade. These three routes carry different content volumes, different practical arrangements and different consequences at 16, and they are decided by the school, usually at the end of Year 9.

Parents on Palm Jumeirah often discover the route by accident, halfway through Year 11, when a child mentions that they are not doing the same science papers as a friend at another school. By then the route is fixed in practice, because changing it means changing the centre's entry and often the teaching set. Finding out in Year 10 leaves a decision open; finding out in February of Year 11 leaves only revision.

The consequences run forward. Higher Level IB sciences and A Level sciences both assume the content depth of a separate-science entry, particularly in chemistry and physics. A student who sat a double award and wants A Level Chemistry can do it, and will spend the first term closing a gap in moles, bonding and organic chemistry while also meeting new material. That is a workable plan if it is chosen deliberately and a difficult autumn if it is discovered in September.

So the first email to your child's school asks four things: which science route is my child on, which board and syllabus codes, Core or Extended tier where that applies, and is the practical component Paper 5 or Paper 6. Those four answers take one reply to obtain, and they determine what any tutoring money should be spent on. A tutor who starts work without them is guessing, however good they are.
bullets: Three separate sciences: three codes, three papers sets, three grades

sections.heading: The science route by school belt, and what it does to your week
paragraphs: Schools in the Palm commute belt handle science differently, and the difference is visible in a student's week long before it is visible in a grade. A triple scientist has three teachers setting work, three past-paper banks and three practical routes to prepare for. A double-award student has one teacher, one paper set and one revision plan. The same child, in the same year, in two schools five kilometres apart, can be carrying very different loads.

The table below sets out the shape of science provision across the belt, with the practical route and what each route implies for tutoring. Treat the middle column as the pattern rather than a promise: schools change science offers between cohorts, and selective schools frequently run triple for upper sets and a double award for others inside the same year group. Confirm your child's own route from the exam entry rather than from the school's prospectus.

Read the last column against your own afternoon. A student returning to a frond at 16:45 with three sciences cannot usefully buy three weekly hours, because the hours would consume the independent practice time that makes the hours work. The sensible plan is one subject at a time in blocks, or two short specialist slots on the two calculation-heavy sciences, with the third subject held by school teaching and marked past papers.

Weekends are where the arithmetic eases. A Saturday morning from any Palm address costs nothing in travel and nothing in accumulated school day, which is why the heaviest science work belongs there: moles calculations, electrolysis half-equations, circuit reasoning, full timed papers. Families who keep one weekend slot and one short weekday slot get more from two hours than families who book three weekday hours and miss one of them every fortnight.

sections.heading: Cambridge and Pearson do not examine practical work the same way
paragraphs: This is the most consequential difference between the two boards and it is almost never explained to parents. Cambridge examines practical skills in a dedicated paper in each separate science, worth a fifth of the grade. The centre chooses between Paper 5, a practical test sat in a laboratory with apparatus, and Paper 6, the alternative to practical, which is a written paper about experiments. Pearson International GCSE has no separate practical paper. Practical skills appear inside the written papers, built around the core practicals in the specification.

What follows from that is a different revision plan for each board. If your child is a Cambridge candidate on Paper 6, a fifth of the grade is sitting in a written paper that tests whether they can identify independent, dependent and control variables, head a results table with units, plot and draw a line of best fit, spot an anomaly, read a scale correctly, state a safety precaution and suggest one genuine improvement to a method. None of that needs a laboratory, all of it is teachable online, and almost no student practises it deliberately because it is nobody's homework.

If your child is on Cambridge Paper 5, the practical test itself has to be sat with apparatus at the centre, and preparation is partly school work. A tutor can still do the larger half of the job, which is the written reasoning around the experiment: predicting, recording to consistent significant figures, processing data, evaluating method. The manipulation of glassware is a small part of the mark scheme compared with the thinking recorded on the page.

Pearson candidates need the same skills in a different wrapper. The specification names core practicals, and questions ask students to describe a method, interpret somebody else's data or evaluate a procedure. The marks behave like practical marks and sit inside a theory paper, which means they are often revised as theory and lost as practical. Naming them explicitly, and practising them from past papers with the mark scheme visible, is one of the cheapest grade gains available in IGCSE science.

sections.heading: How practical skills are taught when the lesson happens online
paragraphs: The reasonable worry about online science tuition is the laboratory. It deserves a straight answer rather than reassurance. Nobody can hand your child a burette over a video call, and no online lesson replaces the experience of running a titration badly and then running it well. What an online lesson can do is teach everything that is written down about an experiment, and in the mark scheme that is most of it.

Work through a Cambridge Paper 6 question and the point becomes obvious. The marks are for identifying the independent variable, naming two variables that must be controlled, completing a results table with a unit in the heading, calculating a mean to a consistent number of significant figures, plotting points accurately, drawing a line of best fit through them, circling the anomaly, explaining why it might have occurred, stating a safety precaution relevant to this experiment rather than a generic one, and suggesting an improvement that would actually reduce the error identified. Every one of those is a written skill.

For the chemistry and biology observation questions, a tutor shares a photograph or a recorded demonstration on screen and the student describes what they see in mark-scheme language: a white precipitate rather than a cloudy liquid, effervescence rather than bubbles, a colour change from orange to green rather than it went green. Precision of observation language is worth real marks and is routinely taught loosely in a busy school laboratory where the teacher is supervising thirty students and twenty flames.

The honest limit is this: school remains responsible for the apparatus work, and a Paper 5 practical test needs laboratory time your child can only get at their centre. Ask the school how many practical sessions are timetabled before the series. If the answer is few, the written practical reasoning becomes more important rather than less, because it is the part of the component that can still be rescued from a Palm Jumeirah dining table on a Tuesday evening.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one evening: the timetable problem on the island
paragraphs: A triple scientist living on Palm Jumeirah has a genuine arithmetic problem. Three subjects set homework. Three subjects have past-paper banks running to dozens of papers each. The school day ends between 14:45 and 15:30, the car crosses the Trunk, and the front door opens between 15:45 and 16:45 depending on the frond. Somewhere in the remaining hours there has to be dinner, Arabic or Islamic Education homework, sport, sleep and the independent practice that makes any tutoring worth paying for.

The most common mistake is to buy three weekly hours, one per science. It feels proportionate and it fails, because three hours of tuition plus three subjects of school homework leaves no space for the student to work alone, and working alone is where fluency comes from. A tutored student who never practises unsupervised arrives at the paper able to follow a method and unable to start one.

The pattern that works is concentration. Pick the weakest science from a marked paper rather than from an impression, give it six to eight consecutive weeks, and let the other two be held by school teaching plus marked past papers. Then reassess and move. Over a year a student gets three repaired subjects rather than three subjects receiving twenty minutes of attention each.

The table sets out a workable week for a triple scientist on three different Palm addresses. It assumes real arrival times rather than optimistic ones, and it puts calculation-heavy work in the weekend slot where working memory is intact. During Ramadan, shift the whole pattern later by two to three hours and keep the frequency: the marking cycle is what matters, and most families lose it entirely for a month by cancelling rather than moving.
