sections.heading: Where science marks go missing, subject by subject
paragraphs: Science marks are lost in predictable places, and the places differ by discipline. A general science tutor tends to treat all three subjects as one body of knowledge to be revised; a subject specialist knows that chemistry grades move with calculation fluency, physics grades move with formula discipline and biology grades move with precision of language. The table below is what Dubai teachers report most often, written so that a parent can check it against their own child's marked paper tonight.

In chemistry the single biggest leak is the mole. Reacting masses, limiting reagents, concentration and gas volumes are all one skill wearing four hats, and a student who is shaky on it loses marks on every paper regardless of how well they understand bonding. Electrolysis half-equations and ionic equations with state symbols follow close behind, because both are marked strictly and both are routinely written loosely.

In physics the leak is procedural. Students who write the formula, substitute values and state the unit score; students who calculate mentally lose method marks and make unit errors they never notice. Beyond that, graph gradients that are themselves physical quantities, the principle of moments, and series and parallel circuit reasoning account for most of the rest. Ray diagrams fail when angles are estimated rather than measured.

In biology the leak is language. Describe and explain are different instructions and attract different marks. Osmosis answers that omit water potential, enzyme graph answers that describe the curve without explaining the mechanism, and genetic crosses written without proper notation all lose marks the student believes they earned. Extended six-mark answers reward structure and linked reasoning, and a list of true facts in any order rarely reaches the top band.

sections.heading: What three sciences cost, starting from the cheapest option
paragraphs: Begin at the bottom of the market, because that is where most families start and because the arithmetic there is instructive. Budget online platforms in Dubai advertise science tuition from AED 33 to 65 an hour, and the published budget band runs AED 45 to 150. One hour a week at that level is roughly AED 240 to 600 a month, which is Bestimate's own estimate for weekly one-hour sessions in its Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026. For a single subject that is a reasonable experiment. For three sciences it triples, and the tutor at that price is usually a general science graduate rather than a chemist.

One step up, a qualified subject tutor working online sits in a published band of AED 150 to 300 an hour. A Dubai agency's rate card listed IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 when it was read in October 2026. Bestimate's monthly estimate for this tier is AED 600 to 1,200 for one hour a week. At this level you are buying someone who teaches the syllabus code rather than the subject in general, and that is the step where triple scientists usually stop paying for three subjects and start paying for one at a time.

Above that, IGCSE and IB specialists are published at AED 200 to 450 and more, with a UK agency operating in the Gulf at AED 270 and a named-tutor service at AED 650. Exam-year specialist support is estimated at AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more a month for weekly sessions. In-home visits across Dubai are quoted at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel included, and monthly in-home packages of four two-hour sessions have been advertised at AED 1,599 to 1,799, against around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions.

None of those figures is an IB Gram price and this page publishes none. The useful conclusion is about sequencing rather than tier. Three sciences bought simultaneously at any price point is usually the wrong purchase, because it consumes the independent practice time the money is meant to improve. One science at a time, at the level where the tutor knows the paper, costs less in total and produces a repaired subject rather than three lightly attended ones. Dubai school fees were confirmed frozen for 2026-27 by KHDA on 22 May 2026, which at least makes the tutoring decision a clean one rather than a competing one.

sections.heading: Online science lessons versus an in-home tutor on the island
paragraphs: The phrase in this page's address is the one parents type, so the comparison deserves a straight treatment. In-home science tutoring on Palm Jumeirah exists, it has real advantages, and for a younger child in a familiar room with a parent nearby it can be the right choice. For an IGCSE science candidate it runs into a specific problem, and the problem is specialisation rather than geography.

Three sciences need three kinds of expertise. The pool of tutors willing to drive onto a dead-end frond on the Palm at 17:00 is small, and the pool within it that contains a genuine chemist, a genuine physicist and a genuine biologist is smaller again. What families usually get is one person who is good at one science, adequate at the second and reading ahead in the third. The travel premium visible in the published bands, roughly AED 30 to 200 an hour above the comparable online rate, is paying for the drive and not for that third subject.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE; home tutoring is a service we run only in India, and no page on this site will promise a tutor at a UAE address. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, past papers on screen, recorded demonstrations where an observation is being taught and written answers marked between sessions. The trade is a person in the room against a specialist in each subject.

There is one more practical difference worth naming. Cancellations on this island are frequent, because school fixtures, trips and traffic all intervene, and a missed in-home slot is either lost or charged for while a missed online slot can be moved to the next evening at no cost to anybody. Over a two-year IGCSE course that difference adds up to a meaningful number of taught hours, which is the sort of thing that never appears in a comparison written by a provider who sells visits.

sections.heading: Entries, tiers, permits and the honesty line in science
paragraphs: Entry deadlines bind decisions that families think are still open, and the first thing to establish is which series your child is sitting. Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series, and those two are what UAE centres sit; the February/March series is offered to India only, so a key-dates document found through a general search may belong to a series your child will never take. Final entry deadlines are agreed between Cambridge and the centre and fall months before the first paper, and the Core-to-Extended decision, or in some schools the double-award-to-triple decision, is part of that entry. Pearson runs International GCSE in May/June and November, with its November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, and publishes provisional timetables for later series that can be revised.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For science this has an extra edge, because a Paper 5 practical test needs a laboratory slot and apparatus, so the centre's scheduling is less flexible than for a written paper. Ask the exams officer for the zone, the codes, the tier and the practical route in one email.

Private tutoring in the UAE needs a permit, and the detail is checkable. The private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is issued through MoHRE, and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, with MoHRE's own service page listing a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure appears here. No individual is KHDA approved either: that permit is issued to training institutes with premises.

The honesty line in science is narrower than in essay subjects and still worth stating. A tutor may teach a technique, set practice questions, mark written answers, explain a mark scheme and coach the process of planning an investigation. A tutor may not produce a school investigation, a coursework task or any assessed work on a student's behalf, and nobody at IB Gram will. Official syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to Cambridge and Pearson, so this page points at their own sites rather than hosting their documents.

process.title: Find out which route and which codes
process.description: One email to the exams officer: triple, double award or single award, which board, which syllabus codes, Core or Extended where it applies, and whether the practical component is Paper 5 or Paper 6. Those five answers decide what tutoring should target, and no tutor can plan properly without them.

process.title: Rank the three sciences from a marked paper
process.description: Not from an impression. Take the most recent marked paper in each science and look at where the marks actually went: calculation, command words, practical reasoning or content gaps. The weakest subject chosen this way is frequently not the subject the student complains about most.

process.title: A free trial lesson in the weakest science
process.description: One trial lesson, one subject, before any paid block is booked. The tutor works through that marked paper, names the two highest-yield fixes and says what six weeks would target. You decide afterwards whether to continue, and with which subject.

process.title: Block one subject for six to eight weeks
process.description: Concentrate rather than rotate. One science gets consecutive weeks of attention while the other two are held by school teaching and marked past papers. At the end of the block, reassess from a new marked paper and decide whether to continue or move to the next subject.

process.title: Add a practical-paper block before the series
process.description: Four focused sessions on Cambridge Paper 6 or the Pearson core practicals: variables, table headings and units, lines of best fit, anomalies, safety and improvements. It is a fifth of the Cambridge grade in each separate science and it is the part almost nobody practises on purpose.

process.title: Move the slot during Ramadan rather than pausing
process.description: School days shorten and the productive window moves to the evening after Iftar. Shifting the science slot two to three hours later for the month keeps the marking cycle intact, which matters more than the hours themselves. Families who cancel for the month usually lose six weeks, not four.

whyPoints.description: Three sciences are three teaching jobs. Online delivery means your child can have a specialist in each rather than one tutor who is strong in one discipline and reading ahead in the other two, which is what a driving radius around a Palm frond usually produces.

whyPoints.description: Cambridge Paper 5 or Paper 6 is worth a fifth of the grade in each separate science, and Pearson embeds the same skills in its written papers. We teach that component explicitly from past papers and mark schemes rather than hoping school covers it.

faqs.question: Is my child doing three separate sciences or one combined science course?
faqs.answer: The exam entry answers it. Three separate sciences means three syllabus codes, three sets of papers and three grades: Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. A double award means one course across all three disciplines awarded as two identical grades, such as Cambridge 0654 or Pearson 4SD0. A single award is one course and one grade, such as Cambridge 0653. The route is set by the school, usually at the end of Year 9, and it changes the homework load, the revision arithmetic and the sensible tutoring plan completely.

faqs.question: Does a Palm Jumeirah student doing triple science need three tutors?
faqs.answer: Almost never, and buying three is the commonest expensive mistake. Three weekly tutoring hours plus three subjects of school homework leaves no room for the independent practice that makes any of it work, and a student who only ever works with a tutor can follow a method but not start one. The pattern that works is one science at a time for six to eight consecutive weeks, chosen from a marked paper, while school teaching and marked past papers hold the other two. In Year 11, two short specialist slots on the two calculation-heavy sciences is the usual settled arrangement.

faqs.question: How is the Cambridge practical component examined, and how much is it worth?
faqs.answer: In each separate Cambridge science it is worth a fifth of the grade, and the centre chooses the route: Paper 5 is a practical test sat with apparatus in a laboratory, and Paper 6 is the alternative to practical, a written paper about experiments. Paper 6 asks for variables, results tables with units in the headings, means to consistent significant figures, lines of best fit, anomaly identification, relevant safety precautions and genuine method improvements. All of that is written reasoning, which is why a dedicated block on it is one of the cheapest grade gains available in IGCSE science.

faqs.question: Does Pearson International GCSE science have a practical exam?
faqs.answer: No separate one. Pearson assesses practical skills inside the written papers, built around the core practicals named in the specification, so questions ask students to describe a method, interpret data from an experiment or evaluate a procedure. Those marks behave like practical marks but sit in a theory paper, which is why they are so often revised as theory and lost as practical. Naming the core practicals explicitly and drilling them from past papers with the mark scheme visible is the fix, and it works the same way online as in person.

faqs.question: Can practical skills really be taught to my child over video?
faqs.answer: The written part, yes, and the written part is most of the marks. Variables, table design, units, significant figures, plotting, lines of best fit, anomalies, safety and improvement suggestions are all written skills taught from past papers. Observation language is taught from photographs and recorded demonstrations, where a student learns to write white precipitate rather than cloudy, and effervescence rather than bubbles. The honest limit is apparatus handling, which stays with the school, so it is worth asking how many laboratory sessions are timetabled before the series.

faqs.question: Which science syllabus codes should I be looking for on the exam entry?
faqs.answer: For Cambridge separate sciences, Biology is 0610, Chemistry is 0620 and Physics is 0625. Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences double award is 0654 and Combined Science single award is 0653. For Pearson, Biology is 4BI1, Chemistry is 4CH1, Physics is 4PH1, the Science Double Award is 4SD0 and the Single Award is 4SS0. The codes appear on the statement of entry and your school's exams officer can confirm them in one reply. Ask for the tier and the practical route in the same message, because a tutor needs all three to plan anything useful.

faqs.question: My child understands chemistry but keeps losing marks. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Usually the arithmetic rather than the chemistry. Moles, reacting masses, limiting reagents, concentration and gas volumes are one skill wearing several hats, and a student shaky on it loses marks on every paper regardless of how well they understand bonding or periodicity. Ionic equations missing state symbols and electrolysis half-equations with unbalanced charges come next, because both are marked strictly and both are routinely written loosely. Short, frequent calculation drills with the working written out move this faster than more content teaching does.

faqs.question: What time can a science session start if we live on a frond?
faqs.answer: Later than most families assume. There is no secondary school on Palm Jumeirah, so the school day ends between 14:45 and 15:30 somewhere off the island, the car crosses the Trunk, and a mid-frond front door opens between 16:15 and 16:45. That makes 17:00 or 17:15 the earliest honest weekday start for a frond address, and 17:30 or later for the Crescent, where the tunnel adds time twice. Calculation-heavy science belongs in a weekend morning instead, where there is no commute and no school day behind it.

faqs.question: What does IGCSE science tuition cost for a family on Palm Jumeirah?
faqs.answer: Published Dubai bands, read in October 2026, start at AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, with platforms advertising from AED 33 to 65. A qualified subject tutor online sits at AED 150 to 300, and an IGCSE or IB specialist at AED 200 to 450 or more. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel included. As monthly figures for one hour a week, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table estimates AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. None of these is our price list.

faqs.question: Can my child move from Core to Extended, or from a double award to triple science?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and the deadline rather than the conversation decides it. The binding moment is the centre's final entry, which Cambridge agrees with the school months before the first paper, so ask the exams officer for that date and for which of the two UAE series, June or November, your child is entered for. Moving up a tier means covering additional content and meeting harder questions, so the decision should be taken against a marked paper rather than against ambition. Moving from a double award to triple science usually also means changing teaching sets, which is a school decision rather than a family one.

faqs.question: Does a Paper 5 practical test affect how the school schedules exams?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is worth knowing about. A practical test needs a laboratory, apparatus and supervision, so it is less flexible to schedule than a written paper. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask your child's exams officer which zone the centre sits in and whether the entry is Paper 5 or Paper 6, then plan revision against that rather than a general timetable.

faqs.question: Is a general science tutor good enough for IGCSE, or do we need subject specialists?
faqs.answer: For a single award or a double award, a strong generalist who is genuinely comfortable across all three disciplines can work well, because the course is examined as one. For triple science in Year 11, specialists are usually better value, because chemistry grades move with calculation fluency, physics grades move with formula discipline and biology grades move with precision of language, and those are three different teaching skills. Online delivery is what makes two specialists practical, since neither has to reach a dead-end frond on the Palm at 17:00.

faqs.question: How many science sessions a week make sense in the eight weeks before the exams?
faqs.answer: Two is the usual answer, and the reason is marking cycles rather than teaching hours. Two sessions means two rounds of written answers marked, corrected and re-tested, and that cycle is what moves marks in a short run-up. A sensible eight-week block runs diagnostics and the weakest topics in weeks one to three, timed questions by topic in weeks four to six, and whole papers under exam conditions with marking in between for weeks seven and eight. Beyond two sessions a week, independent practice time becomes the limiting factor.

faqs.question: Do science tutors working with Dubai families need a government permit?
faqs.answer: Yes. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18, and MoHRE's own service page lists a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without the permit carries fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so be sceptical of any website quoting a specific amount, and remember that no individual is KHDA approved.

faqs.question: Is a tutor allowed to help with a school investigation or a coursework task?
faqs.answer: Within limits that are worth being precise about. A tutor may teach experimental design, explain what a mark scheme rewards, discuss how to structure a method or an evaluation, and give feedback on work the student has already written. A tutor may not plan the investigation for them, write any part of it, or produce assessed work on their behalf, and nobody at IB Gram will. The consequences of crossing that line fall on the student, which is why we state the boundary in writing rather than leaving it implied.

faqs.question: Will three IGCSE sciences count towards UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Sciences count as subjects within the British-track rule, which is specific and verifiable: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count of five, plus one accredited A Level at grade E or two AS Levels at the same grade. A double award producing two grades may count differently from three separate sciences, so confirm your child's own case with the Ministry. Equivalency is handled by the Ministry rather than by any tutoring provider, and tutoring is not a requirement for it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-palm-jumeir.closingHeading: Start with the entry, then pick one science
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-palm-jumeir.closingBody: Two emails do most of the work on this page. The first asks your child's exams officer for the science route, the board and codes, the tier and whether the practical component is Paper 5 or Paper 6. The second asks for the Cambridge administrative zone. With those answers, take the most recent marked paper in each science, find the weakest one, and give that subject six to eight consecutive weeks rather than giving all three twenty minutes. Lessons from IB Gram are one-to-one and online, with a free trial lesson in one subject before any paid block, written answers marked between sessions, and the practical paper taught deliberately rather than left to chance.

intro.heading: Three sciences, and the arithmetic nobody does before booking
paragraphs: Science is the only part of an IGCSE timetable that can triple a tutoring bill without anybody deciding to spend three times as much. It happens by accretion. Physics looks shaky in October, so a tutor is engaged. Chemistry comes back badly in the December assessment, so a second is added. By February biology has been neglected because the week is full, so a third appears. Nobody chose a three-tutor arrangement; it assembled itself, and the monthly figure at the end of it is two or three times what a deliberate plan would have cost.

The figures are worth having in front of you before that happens. Published online rates for a qualified subject tutor in Dubai are AED 150 to AED 300 an hour, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150 and TutorChase AED 270 for specialist work. In-home visits including travel are quoted at AED 180 to AED 500, with Bestimate's 2026 rate table putting the common range at AED 180 to AED 350. Budget online options start at AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik. Monthly packages appear at roughly AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four in-home visits of two hours. Each figure belongs to the provider named and was read in October 2026; none is an IB Gram price list.

Multiply the middle of that range by three subjects across two academic years and the number stops being incidental. One weekly hour per science at AED 200 is roughly AED 2,600 a month during term time, and something close to AED 50,000 across Years 10 and 11. The same commitment in two sciences is two thirds of that, and in one science with a diagnosed block in a second it is under half. Those are materially different decisions and most families make them without seeing the comparison.

Two specific facts change the arithmetic more than any negotiation on rate. The first is which specification the school uses: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a double award covering all three disciplines in one set of papers, which means one tutor rather than three. Families who hire three specialists for a 0654 candidate are spending triple for no additional coverage, and this is among the most common and most expensive misunderstandings in this market. The second is the practical component, worth 20 per cent on Cambridge separate and Co-ordinated Sciences, which is the same small skill set in all three subjects and therefore the only part of the syllabus where one paid hour genuinely counts three times.

IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE, since in-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. On a cost page the relevant consequence is that nothing in the rate covers the causeway onto the island, and that a session can switch from physics to chemistry between one week and the next without a second person having to be found and paid to make the same journey.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The most requested single science topic in this cluster. Students recite the rules and fail unfamiliar circuit diagrams, which is a practice problem. Resolvable in a block of four to six sessions rather than a standing weekly booking.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, motion and energy calculations
subjects.description: Rearranging before substituting is the real skill, and it is mathematics rather than physics. Worth diagnosing before funding, because a maths intervention may serve two sciences at once.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: The clearest dividing line between a middling and a strong Extended grade, and purely procedural. A funded term aimed specifically at limiting reagent and percentage yield beats a year of general chemistry support.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic chemistry and reaction types
subjects.description: Recall volume rather than conceptual difficulty, which means it responds to frequent short testing. One of the subjects where the published budget band is genuinely adequate for the task.

subjects.name: Chemistry: salt preparation and separation methods
subjects.description: Practical detail that the practical and alternative-to-practical papers probe directly: which method, which observation, how a product is separated. Cheap marks for anybody who rehearses the methods.

subjects.name: Biology: transport, respiration and photosynthesis
subjects.description: High mark density and precise language. Students who know the biology lose marks by giving correct ideas in the wrong order, which a marked script reveals in minutes and a block of sessions fixes.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares, ratios and vocabulary, procedural once the convention is learned. Among the most reliably recoverable marks in the whole science timetable and rarely worth premium rates.

subjects.name: Biology: human physiology and homeostasis
subjects.description: Negative feedback and hormonal control, where the loss is describing what happens without naming the controlling mechanism. A short, well-defined problem rather than a general weakness.

subjects.name: Practical skills and experimental design
subjects.levels: Cambridge Paper 5 or Paper 6; within written papers for Pearson
subjects.description: Twenty per cent of the grade on Cambridge separate and Co-ordinated Sciences, and the same skills in all three subjects. The single best value target in any science tutoring budget.

subjects.name: Graph and data handling across all three sciences

sections.heading: What one, two and three sciences actually cost
paragraphs: The table puts the arithmetic in one place, using the published market bands rather than any price of ours. It is a planning tool: the figures show the shape of a commitment rather than a quotation, and the point is the comparison between rows rather than any individual number.

Two things stand out. The first is how quickly parallel bookings scale. Three standing weekly hours at the middle of the published range is roughly AED 2,600 a month in term time and approaches AED 50,000 across the two IGCSE years. That is not a small line in a household budget, and almost nobody arrives at it deliberately. It arrives one subject at a time, each addition looking reasonable on its own.

The second is how much cheaper sequential blocks are than parallel bookings. Running one diagnosed block at a time, six to eight sessions each, with a shared skills hour running underneath, covers the same three sciences for well under half the parallel figure. It also fits the week, which parallel bookings do not: a Year 11 student in this cluster has two or at most three tutored hours available before unsupervised study time starts disappearing, and unsupervised practice is where science is consolidated.

The third row worth reading twice is the 0654 row. If the school enters for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences, one tutor covers all three disciplines, and the whole three-subject arithmetic collapses into a single-subject arithmetic. Families who have engaged three specialists for a 0654 candidate have spent triple for no additional coverage, and the fix costs nothing beyond asking the school which code appears on the entry statement.

sections.heading: Why the syllabus code is a budget document
paragraphs: The most consequential cost question in science tutoring is not what a tutor charges. It is which specification the school entered your child for, because the answer determines how many tutors are needed and whether a practical paper exists at all. It takes one email to the department and it is printed on the exam entry statement.

Cambridge separate sciences, Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625, each produce their own grade and go deepest in each discipline. All three include a practical component worth 20 per cent, entered either as Paper 5, a practical test with apparatus, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical answered in writing. A student taking all three separately may genuinely need subject-specific help in more than one of them, which is the expensive case.

Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 is a different proposition. It is a double award: one set of papers covering biology, chemistry and physics produces two grades, with a longer combined theory paper and the same practical component at 20 per cent. Depth in each discipline is shallower than in the separate sciences. What a 0654 student needs is one tutor comfortable moving across all three at the level the combined paper demands, which costs a third of three specialists. Combined Science 0653 is the single-award version and works the same way for budgeting purposes.

Pearson Edexcel sciences change the picture again. Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 each have two written papers at Foundation or Higher tier, with practical skills assessed inside those papers rather than in a separate component. For a family budgeting against the practical paper that matters: there is no Paper 5 or Paper 6 to prepare for, so the cheapest high-value target described later on this page does not exist in the same form, and the hours are better spent on long written questions instead.

sections.heading: The cheapest 20 per cent in the whole science timetable
paragraphs: On Cambridge separate sciences and Co-ordinated Sciences, the practical component carries 20 per cent of the grade. In a crowded Year 11 timetable it is also the component schools have least room to rehearse. That combination makes it the best value target available in a science budget, for a reason that is arithmetic rather than rhetorical.

What the practical and alternative-to-practical papers assess is a small and learnable set of skills. Reading a scale to the correct precision. Identifying independent, dependent and controlled variables in an unfamiliar method. Spotting the flaw in a described procedure. Proposing a specific improvement rather than suggesting greater care. Plotting a graph with sensible axes, drawing a line of best fit through scattered points, and reading a value off it. Describing a trend in the language the mark scheme rewards. That is most of it.

None of it needs apparatus. The alternative to practical paper is written, and the practical test rewards a student who knows what the examiner is looking for considerably more than one who has handled the equipment a few extra times. An hour spent marking past practical questions against the published scheme routinely moves a student further than an hour revising content they already half know.

The budget point is the multiplier. These are the same skills in biology, chemistry and physics, so one weekly hour on them serves three subjects. For a family with three sciences and a realistic ceiling of two tutored hours a week, this is the only part of the syllabus where a single hourly rate buys three subjects' worth of improvement. It is also the clearest case in this market where the efficient purchase and the cheap purchase are the same thing.

sections.heading: The four ways science tutoring money disappears
paragraphs: Overspending on science support in this community is rarely about the hourly rate. It is about buying the wrong arrangement, and the same four patterns recur.

The first is three parallel bookings. It happens by accretion rather than decision, it triples the monthly figure, and it displaces the unsupervised practice where science is actually consolidated. A Year 11 student here has two or at most three tutored hours available in a week that ends with school at 3:30pm, a causeway crossing, and activities until six. Three bookings do not fit; one of them quietly stops happening, usually the one scheduled latest, and the family keeps paying attention to a plan that has already collapsed.

The second is paying specialist rates for recall testing. A great deal of biology support is somebody testing definitions and keeping a student working, which is valuable and is not worth AED 300 an hour. The published budget band at AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik exists for exactly this task and is honest about what it provides. Save the specialist rate for reading a marked script against a mark scheme, which the budget band cannot do.

The third is funding the subject rather than the failure. Marks lost in calculation questions across physics and chemistry are one problem about quantitative technique, not two subject problems, and frequently the underlying issue is mathematics rather than science at all. One diagnostic hour across the marked scripts will say so, and when it does the budget halves.

The fourth is the two-hour in-home block. It exists because a tutor who has crossed the city and the causeway needs the trip to be worth making, not because a fifteen-year-old does productive science for 120 consecutive minutes. Market monthly packages reflect that: roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits against about AED 799 for eight shorter online sessions. The pricing follows travel economics rather than how science is learned.

sections.heading: Costs that sit outside the tutoring bill
paragraphs: A science budget that stops at the hourly rate will be wrong by the amount of an entry fee or a resit, and families discover this in August. Entries are made by the school, months before the papers, and the fees appear on a school bill rather than a tutoring one, but they belong in the same plan.

The calendar sets the timing, and it is worth being exact. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in the June series and the November series. The February/March series is offered to India only, so any February or March dates quoted at a Dubai family should be disregarded entirely. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November.

Checkable reference points help with planning a reserve. For Pearson, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Those are backward-looking citations and that is what makes them verifiable, though the live official timetable is what should be checked before acting, because provisional timetables are revised.

The practical consequence for a budget is a reserve rather than a precise figure. A resit decision taken in August needs funding in September, and the resulting grade arrives in the following January rather than in the summer, which matters for any sixth-form or university application that depends on it. There is also an avoidable waste worth naming: every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the timetable differs by zone, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Revision bought against the wrong dates is money spent twice.

sections.heading: Science tutoring against the rest of a Dubai school bill
paragraphs: Context matters for a figure approaching five digits across two years, and in Dubai the rest of the education budget has recently been unusually stable. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total.

The market around that continues to grow. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment, Indian at 26 per cent, US at 14 per cent and the International Baccalaureate at 7 per cent. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six openings in 2025-26 and a 6 per cent rise in enrolment.

Two consequences follow for a science budget on this island. A stable fee position means the tutoring figure can be set across the two IGCSE years in advance rather than revised each time a report arrives, which is what prevents the three-booking accretion this page opened with. And deep UK curriculum supply means no shortage of available science tutors and no reliable price signal distinguishing those who have taught your child's specification from those who have taught the subject, which is why asking about the code does more for a budget than negotiating a rate.

The proportion point is worth stating plainly. Against school fees, one well-chosen weekly hour plus a shared skills hour across two IGCSE years is a modest addition. Three parallel bookings at specialist rates is not, and it does not produce proportionally better results, because it takes away the practice time that converts teaching into marks. The expensive mistake in this market is the number of hours bought rather than the rate paid for them.

sections.heading: Verifying who you are paying, at no cost
paragraphs: Before a recurring payment starts there is a free set of checks, and it reduces to two questions. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 Regarding the Introduction of Private Tuition Work Permits, and it is granted free of charge for two years.

Because there is no fee, lacking one is a choice rather than an obstacle, and eligibility is broad: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE lists the service as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fees stated and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and since no fine schedule has been published, a specific amount quoted at you cannot be substantiated.

The second question concerns who may teach whom. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules prohibit private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. If a family is considering a teacher from their child's own school, that is the question to ask first. Separately, a tuition centre with premises and staff in Dubai requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, obtained with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry.

There are also claims that should affect how a rate is read. No grade, improvement or outcome can honestly be guaranteed, and no refund should be tied to a result. A satisfaction percentage, a pass rate or a star rating published without a sample size, a date and a method is a number nobody can check. And nobody should be offering copied syllabus documents, past papers or mark schemes as a package, because those belong to Cambridge International and to Pearson and are referenced rather than redistributed. Each of those checks is free, and together they tell a family more than a price comparison does.

faqs.question: What does funding all three IGCSE sciences cost per month in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At the published middle of the market, three standing weekly hours is roughly AED 1,800 to AED 3,600 a month, since qualified online subject tutors are listed at AED 150 to AED 300 an hour with Unitors from AED 150 and TutorChase at AED 270. Across the two IGCSE years that approaches AED 35,000 to AED 69,000. Almost no family decides on that figure; it accumulates one subject at a time, each addition looking reasonable on its own.

faqs.question: Can we cover three sciences without paying for three tutors?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, in two ways. If the school enters for Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654, one tutor covers all three disciplines because it is a double award from one set of papers. Otherwise, a shared weekly hour on the skills common to all three, graph work, variables, method evaluation and practical paper technique, plus one diagnosed block at a time in whichever subject the marked scripts implicate, covers the same ground for well under half the parallel cost.

faqs.question: Is hiring three separate tutors for Co-ordinated Sciences a mistake?
faqs.answer: It is one of the most expensive misunderstandings in this market. Cambridge 0654 is a double award: one set of papers covers biology, chemistry and physics and produces two grades, with a longer combined theory paper and a practical component at 20 per cent. The depth in each discipline is shallower than in the separate sciences. What the student needs is one tutor comfortable across all three at the level the combined paper demands, and asking the school which code appears on the entry statement costs nothing.

faqs.question: Which part of the science grade is cheapest to recover?
faqs.answer: The practical component, on Cambridge separate sciences and Co-ordinated Sciences, where it carries 20 per cent. It assesses a small learnable set of skills: reading a scale to the right precision, identifying variables, spotting a flaw in a method, proposing a specific improvement, plotting and reading a graph, and describing a trend in mark-scheme language. None of it needs apparatus, and all of it is the same in all three sciences, so one hour serves three subjects.

faqs.question: Do Pearson Edexcel science candidates have the same practical opportunity?
faqs.answer: Not in the same form, and it changes where the hours should go. Pearson Edexcel Biology 4BI1, Chemistry 4CH1 and Physics 4PH1 have no separate practical paper and assess those skills inside the two written papers. So there is no Paper 5 or Paper 6 to prepare for, and the equivalent best-value target becomes long written question technique and data handling inside the main papers. Confirm which board applies before any hours are bought against the wrong structure.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper tutor adequate for IGCSE biology?
faqs.answer: Often, and this is one of the few places where that is honestly true. A great deal of biology support is testing definitions, checking sequences and keeping a student working, which the published budget band at AED 33 to AED 52 at Tutopiya and AED 45 to AED 65 at EdFlik provides perfectly well. Save the specialist rate for reading a marked script against the mark scheme and identifying why a six-mark explanation earned three, which the budget band cannot reliably do.

faqs.question: Our mock results were poor in two sciences. Do we need two tutors?
faqs.answer: Probably not. Marks lost in calculation questions across physics and chemistry are one problem about quantitative technique rather than two subject problems, and the underlying cause is frequently mathematics rather than science. Marks lost in long explanation questions across biology and chemistry are one problem about writing to the mark allocation. A single diagnostic hour across the marked scripts will say which, and when it does the budget usually halves rather than doubling.

faqs.question: Why do in-home science packages use two-hour sessions?
faqs.answer: Travel economics rather than teaching. A tutor who has crossed the city and the causeway needs the trip to be worth making, which is why monthly in-home packages are commonly built around four two-hour visits at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799, against roughly AED 799 for eight shorter online sessions. A fifteen-year-old does not do productive science for 120 consecutive minutes, so the second half of a long visit tends to become supervised homework at a teaching rate.

faqs.question: How many tutored hours fit into a Year 11 week on this island?
faqs.answer: Two, or at most three. School in this cluster ends between 2:45pm and 3:30pm, the Al Wasl Road crossing plus the causeway queue takes thirty to forty-five minutes, activity programmes run to about 6pm, and useful work stops around 8:30pm. Beyond two or three tutored hours, the sessions start displacing unsupervised practice, which is where science is actually consolidated. Three parallel science bookings do not fit, and one of them quietly stops happening.

faqs.question: Should a science budget include money for a resit?
faqs.answer: A reserve rather than a precise figure. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June and November and Pearson Edexcel runs May/June and November, so a resit route exists. The timing is the planning issue: a decision taken in August needs funding in September, and the grade then arrives months later. Pearson's November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which gives the shape. Confirm current deadlines with the school's exams officer rather than any website.

faqs.question: Could we waste money revising against the wrong exam dates?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is entirely avoidable. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, the exam timetable differs by zone, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. Ask the school which zone it sits in, and make sure any tutor planning a revision schedule works from that version rather than one found through a search.

faqs.question: Do both Co-ordinated Sciences grades count towards MoE equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track rule is that a student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five. A double award produces two grades from one set of papers, which in practice contributes two of the five. One provider ranking for these searches publishes a different subject count. Verify the current requirement through the Ministry of Education's own channel rather than any tutoring website.

faqs.question: Are Dubai school fees rising, and should that change a science budget?
faqs.answer: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within an AED 2.5 billion total. For a science budget that stability is useful in a specific way: it means the two-year tutoring figure can be set in advance, which is the single best protection against the three-booking accretion that happens when each report prompts a new decision.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram charge extra for coming onto Pearl Jumeira?
faqs.answer: The question does not arise, because IB Gram does not offer home visits in Dubai or anywhere else in the UAE. In-home tutoring is a service offered only in India. Pearl Jumeira families are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the rate is identical whether a family lives on the island or inland, and three visiting tutors becoming six causeway crossings a week is not a cost anybody pays. A session can also switch subject week to week without finding a second person.

intro.heading: Three sciences, and each loses marks in its own way
paragraphs: A student described as weak at science is usually losing marks in three quite different ways at once, one per subject, and the three need different work. Physics loses marks to missing causal links and to mathematical execution. Chemistry loses them to notation: unbalanced equations, absent state symbols, unclaimed analysis marks. Biology loses them to imprecise terminology and to answers given out of sequence. None of those is a general science problem and none responds to general science revision.

Across all three sits a fourth category that behaves unlike the rest: practical and method questions. These follow rules rather than requiring laboratory instinct, and the rules are specific. A method has to be repeatable by a stranger, with quantities and controls stated. Units belong in table headings rather than beside values. Graphs need the dependent variable on the right axis and a line of best fit. A controlled variable needs a stated means of control, not just a name.

That fourth category is the best-value work available in science tutoring, because it appears in every paper in all three subjects and almost nobody is taught it directly. A fortnight of practical-question drilling lifts physics, chemistry and biology at the same time, which makes it the one intervention worth doing before any topic is revisited.

Remraam sets the practical conditions. It is a low-rise apartment community in Dubailand, built as the Al Thamam and Al Ramth clusters with its own park and retail, reached from Al Qudra Road and Emirates Road. South View School sits close by and takes students through Year 11, so the run home is short by the standards of this belt and an early-evening session with a student who is not yet tired is genuinely available.

Underneath all four categories sits a fifth that belongs to mathematics rather than to science. Rearrangement, standard form, proportional reasoning and gradients appear constantly in physics and chemistry, and a student who is competent but slow at them loses marks to time in both subjects while appearing to lack the science. Separating that out is often the single most efficient thing a first session can do, because repairing it moves marks in two subjects at once and sometimes in the mathematics paper as well.

The one thing this page will not claim is that online lessons replace a laboratory. The experiment belongs to the school, its equipment and its safety procedures. What a session does is teach everything the paper asks about practical work, which is where those marks actually sit. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only, and nothing here should be read as an offer to arrive at a Remraam address. The sections below take each subject in turn, then the rules that apply across all of them.

sections.heading: What each science paper actually tests
paragraphs: The three sciences look similar on a timetable and examine different things. Physics is the most mathematical: rearrangement, standard form, proportional reasoning and graph gradients appear throughout, and a student who is slow at any of them loses physics marks that resemble physics gaps. Chemistry is the most notational: equations, state symbols, units and significant figures are assessed constantly, and loose presentation costs marks that understanding earned. Biology is the most linguistic: terminology precision and the order of a long answer carry real credit.

Both boards examine across more than one paper per subject, and the papers within a subject are not interchangeable either. Shorter structured questions reward speed and precision; extended questions reward sequence and explicit reasoning. A student who allocates the same time per mark across a whole paper runs short, and one who never decides a question order abandons marks at the end that they could have collected.

Practical skills are examined in every one of these papers, in one form or another, and the form depends on which paper the school enters students for. Some centres use a practical-style written paper focused entirely on experimental skills. Confirming which paper a student sits changes what the final weeks should contain, and it is a question for the department rather than a guess.

The practical consequence of all this is that a plan should name the paper, not just the subject. Preparation for a structured paper and preparation for an extended-response paper look different, and preparation for a practical-skills paper looks different again.

sections.heading: Physics: the causal link and the arithmetic
paragraphs: Physics losses in this corridor concentrate in two places and both are diagnosable from a single marked paper. The first is explanation. A question asking why a current increases receives a description of what happens, and the explanation marks go uncollected while the recall marks arrive. The repair is a rule the student applies themselves: in an explanation, every sentence contains a because, and the answer contains as many creditable statements as the question has marks.

Electricity and electromagnetism carry the heaviest share of those losses. Students learn a result rather than the reasoning that produces it, so a question phrased unfamiliarly or with changed geometry defeats somebody who can answer the standard version. Working several physically different situations until the method rather than the answer is what gets remembered is the only reliable fix, and it takes weeks rather than days.

The second place is arithmetic. Rearranging a formula when the unknown sits in a denominator or under a root, converting between prefixes at speed, and handling standard form reliably are all tested implicitly in nearly every calculation question. A student who is competent but slow loses marks to time rather than to error, which looks like not knowing the physics and is not.

Gradients deserve a line of their own because they recur in papers and in practical questions. Physics constantly asks for a gradient to be converted into a physical quantity, and a student who treats a gradient as a bare number rather than as a quantity with units loses marks in several places at once. Always stating what the gradient physically represents is a habit worth installing early.

sections.heading: Chemistry: notation is the grade
paragraphs: Chemistry at IGCSE is unusually responsive to tutoring, because so many of its losses are mechanical rather than conceptual. An unbalanced equation is wrong whatever the student understands. State symbols omitted where the mark scheme required them cost a mark each time. A concentration quoted without units, or significant figures carried inconsistently, costs marks that the chemistry had already earned.

Moles work runs through everything and speed matters as much as accuracy. A student who is slow at mole calculations loses marks in stoichiometry, titrations, yields and rates, and loses time that the rest of the paper needed. Short daily sets, timed, are the repair, and they work faster than any amount of re-explanation because the problem is fluency rather than comprehension.

Electrolysis and qualitative analysis are the two topics where available marks go unclaimed most often. Electrolysis questions follow patterns that can be learned: identify the ions present, decide what is discharged at each electrode and why, then write the half-equations. Qualitative analysis tests are close to a memorisation task with a predictable mark allocation, and students who treat them as such collect marks others leave behind.

Organic chemistry at IGCSE is narrower than at Diploma level but the same error appears: reactions memorised as pairs of starting material and product rather than understood as types. Grouping by reaction type and practising under time is the approach that survives an unfamiliar question, and it is worth doing before the final term rather than during it.

sections.heading: Biology: terminology, sequence and the data question
paragraphs: Biology is often described as the easiest of the three and is the one where the most marks are lost to writing. Its long-answer questions reward sequence and precision: an answer about transport that never mentions water potential, or about respiration that never names the products, loses marks regardless of how well the student understands the process.

The repair is to treat key processes as sequences with required terms rather than as stories. Each process has a small set of words the mark scheme expects, in an order that makes the biology follow. Students who write out those sequences until they are automatic stop producing vague answers, and this is one of the few places where learning a form of words is legitimate and effective rather than a shortcut.

Command-term reading costs more in biology than in the other two sciences, because its questions are more often verbal. Describe, explain, suggest, compare and evaluate each oblige something different, and a strong answer written against the wrong command term earns a fraction of what it should. Covering the question stems and asking the student to state only what each term obliges is a fortnight's work that lifts every biology paper.

Data questions are the third area and they reward a mechanical discipline. Read the axes, the units and the scale before applying any biology. Students who apply the content to a misread figure produce confident wrong answers, and this is the single most common way a capable biology student loses easy marks.

sections.heading: Practical and method questions, rule by rule
paragraphs: This is the highest-value section on the page, because practical questions appear in every science paper in all three subjects and almost nobody is taught them directly. They are not a test of laboratory instinct. They are a test of whether a student knows a short set of rules, and the rules can be learned on a screen in a fortnight.

A method must be repeatable by a stranger. That means quantities stated, the independent variable and its range given, the dependent variable and how it is measured named, and the controls specified with a means of control rather than just a label. Students routinely list apparatus instead of describing a procedure, which earns almost nothing.

Tables and graphs carry their own conventions. Units belong in the table heading rather than beside each value. The independent variable goes in the first column. A graph needs a sensible scale using most of the grid, the dependent variable on the vertical axis, plotted points marked clearly and a line of best fit rather than dot-to-dot. Each of those is worth marks and each is a rule.

Finally, the vocabulary. Accuracy, precision, reliability, resolution, anomaly and systematic error are distinct terms with distinct meanings, and questions ask about them specifically. A student who uses accurate to mean all of them loses marks in every one of the three sciences. Learning the five or six definitions properly is an evening's work with a return across the whole set of papers.

sections.heading: The mathematics inside all three sciences
paragraphs: A significant share of science failure is mathematical, and treating it as science wastes a term. The pattern is consistent: a student understands the concept, cannot execute the manipulation under time, and concludes they are bad at the subject. In a marked script the errors cluster around the algebra rather than around the ideas, which makes the diagnosis straightforward once somebody looks.

The diagnostic test is simple enough for a parent to run. Take a question the student lost marks on, remove the science, and ask them to do the algebra alone. If it fails in isolation, the problem is mathematical and the hour belongs to manipulation practice rather than to another pass through the topic. If it succeeds, the problem is in the reasoning or the writing, and the hour belongs elsewhere.

The specific skills are few and recur constantly. Rearrangement, especially with the unknown in a denominator or under a root. Standard form and prefix conversion at speed. Proportional reasoning, which carries most of chemistry's calculation work. Gradients converted into quantities with units. Significant figures and units carried consistently to a final answer.

Because these are shared across physics and chemistry, repairing them is the most efficient single intervention in a three-science timetable. Twenty minutes a week of pure manipulation using science formulas, kept deliberately separate from any science reasoning so only one skill is tested at a time, moves marks in two subjects at once and sometimes in the mathematics paper as well.

sections.heading: Core and Extended: what the content difference actually is
paragraphs: Where a science subject is tiered, the difference between the tiers is content coverage rather than question style, and the entry caps the available grade. Core covers a narrower syllabus and reaches the middle of the grade scale; Extended covers the fuller syllabus and reaches the top. A student entered for Core cannot earn a top grade however well they perform, because the paper does not contain the questions that earn more.

The content that Extended adds is not evenly difficult. In chemistry it includes the harder mole and electrolysis work and more organic detail. In physics it extends electromagnetism and the quantitative treatment of several topics. In biology it adds biochemical and physiological detail that Core treats descriptively. Knowing which of those a student is actually struggling with changes the plan, because the Extended additions need teaching while the shared core often needs only repair.

The decision is usually made by the school late in Year 10 on the evidence available then, and it is contestable with work and with timing. A student aiming at an A Level or Higher Level Diploma science needs the higher tier, and the work that secures the placement is harder topics met early rather than revision done late. Asking the department which tier, what evidence would change it and the last amendment date turns the worry into a plan.

For a combined or coordinated award the equivalent question is which route the school runs, because the paper pattern and the depth expected are specific to it, and practising separate-science papers for a combined award is practising the wrong material.

sections.heading: Remraam, South View School and the board question
paragraphs: Remraam is unusually well placed in this belt for secondary access. South View School sits close to the community and takes students through Year 11, so the run home is short and an early-evening session with an alert student is a realistic option rather than a theoretical one. For science, where a timed section needs concentration, that matters more than it does for most subjects.

The board question is the one to settle before anything else. Schools in this corridor do not all use one board across a timetable, and some run Cambridge for one science and Pearson Edexcel for another, which means a single answer for the whole student is often wrong. Ask for a written list: subject, board, code, tier. Then check the code printed on any past paper the student has been given against that list.

This matters because the papers are not interchangeable. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 cover overlapping physics with different question styles, different scaffolding and different conventions about how much working must be shown. Eight weeks spent on the other board's papers teaches a student to expect questions that will not appear, and it is the most common avoidable error in self-directed science revision in this city.

The local tutor pool is broad rather than deep. The people advertising along this corridor, based around Dubai Investment Park, Dubai Sports City and Motor City, generally cover all three sciences at IGCSE level, which is a sensible model and a reason to select on which papers somebody has marked rather than on how close they live.

sections.heading: Costs, permits and what a tutor may not do
paragraphs: Three sciences do not have to cost three times one subject. Buying the practical-question fortnight first, then one science weekly where the marked work shows the largest recoverable loss, keeps the monthly figure in the same band as a single-subject arrangement for most of the year.

The published bands are checkable. Budget online and university-student tutors advertise from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour in Dubai, with EdFlik publishing AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Subject specialists run AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-led provision reaches AED 650 at BartyED. In-home visits are quoted at AED 180 to 500 with travel inside the price.

Monthly, Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, with packages seen including AED 799 for eight online sessions. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that Dubai private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. These are market figures with their sources named, not IB Gram prices.

On the legal and academic boundaries: an individual giving private lessons needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years, with MoHRE's service listing showing no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Tutoring without it attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, with no published fine schedule. Where a centre runs assessed work it must be the student's own, so a tutor explains criteria, critiques an approach and marks the student's own draft and never writes or completes it. Board material is linked rather than circulated.

faqs.question: Which science should a Remraam family fix first?
faqs.answer: Neither a subject nor a topic, but the practical and method questions, because their rules are shared across physics, chemistry and biology and appear in every paper. A fortnight on repeatable methods, table and graph conventions, stated means of control and the correct use of accuracy and precision lifts all three subjects at once. After that, take the single science where the marked scripts show the largest recoverable loss. Splitting one hour across three sciences produces three sets of homework and no practice time.

faqs.question: Why does our son lose marks in physics when he understands it?
faqs.answer: Two reasons usually, and a marked paper separates them. The first is explanation: a question asking why something happens receives a description of what happens, so the recall marks arrive and the explanation marks do not. The rule that fixes it is that every sentence in an explanation contains a because, and the answer carries as many creditable statements as the question has marks. The second is arithmetic under time: rearrangement with the unknown in a denominator, slow prefix conversion, standard form handled hesitantly.

faqs.question: What are the cheapest marks to recover in IGCSE chemistry?
faqs.answer: Notation, by a wide margin. Equations balanced, state symbols included where the scheme requires them, concentrations given with units and significant figures carried consistently are each worth a mark and each is mechanical. After those, qualitative analysis questions are close to a predictable memorisation task and are routinely left unclaimed, and electrolysis follows a learnable pattern: identify the ions, decide what is discharged at each electrode and why, write the half-equations. None of that requires new understanding.

faqs.question: Our daughter writes long biology answers and still scores poorly. Why?
faqs.answer: Almost always imprecision and order rather than length. Long-answer biology rewards a sequence containing the terms the mark scheme expects: transport explained without mentioning water potential, or respiration without naming the products, loses marks whatever she understands. Treating each key process as a sequence with required terms, written out until automatic, fixes it. The second cause is command-term misreading, which costs more in biology than elsewhere because its questions are more verbal, and that responds to a fortnight of drilling.

faqs.question: How are practical skills examined if lessons happen online?
faqs.answer: The experiment belongs to the school; the paper tests rules that can be drilled anywhere. A method must be repeatable by a stranger, with quantities, range, measurement and controls stated rather than apparatus listed. Units belong in table headings. Graphs need a sensible scale using most of the grid, the dependent variable on the vertical axis and a line of best fit. Anomalies are marked and explained rather than deleted. Confirm with the school which practical-style paper the student sits, since it changes the final weeks.

faqs.question: Do accuracy and precision actually get examined separately?
faqs.answer: Yes, and conflating them loses marks in all three sciences. Accuracy is closeness to the true value; precision is the spread of repeated measurements; resolution is the smallest change an instrument can detect; reliability concerns repeatability; a systematic error shifts every reading in the same direction. Questions ask about these specifically, and a student who uses accurate for all of them cannot answer correctly. Learning five or six definitions properly is an evening's work with a return across every science paper the student sits.

faqs.question: Is weak maths really behind science underperformance?
faqs.answer: Very often, and the test is quick. Take a question the student lost marks on, remove the science and ask for the algebra alone. If it fails in isolation, the hour belongs to manipulation practice rather than to another pass through the topic. The specific skills are few: rearrangement, standard form and prefixes at speed, proportional reasoning, gradients converted to quantities with units, and consistent significant figures. Because they are shared, repairing them moves marks in physics and chemistry simultaneously.

faqs.question: Do the sciences at South View School use the same exam board?
faqs.answer: Ask the school, per subject, because a single answer for the whole student is often wrong in this corridor. Schools here sometimes run Cambridge for one science and Pearson Edexcel for another. Request a written list of subject, board, code and tier, then check the code printed on any past paper against it. Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 cover overlapping physics with different question styles and conventions about shown working, so practice from the wrong board teaches the wrong habits.

faqs.question: What does Extended actually add over Core in the sciences?
faqs.answer: Content coverage rather than a harder style of question, plus access to the top of the grade scale. In chemistry the additions include harder mole and electrolysis work and more organic detail; in physics, extended electromagnetism and more quantitative treatment; in biology, biochemical and physiological detail that Core treats descriptively. The distinction matters for planning, because the Extended additions need teaching while the shared core often needs only repair. A Core entry caps the grade however well the student performs.

faqs.question: Should the same tutor cover physics, chemistry and biology here?
faqs.answer: At IGCSE level, often yes, and there are real advantages: shared calculation technique, shared graph and data skills, the practical-question rules taught once, and one review conversation instead of three. The question to ask is which papers they have marked in each subject rather than whether they can cover all three. Where the sciences sit with different boards, confirm they are comfortable with both sets of conventions. If one subject is a stretch, two tutors is better and costs the same per hour.

faqs.question: Which practice papers should a combined-award student use?
faqs.answer: The ones from the combined or coordinated route specifically, not separate-science papers. The paper pattern and the depth expected are its own, and a combined award spreads content from all three sciences across fewer questions, so each question carries proportionally more of the grade. Using separate-science papers trains for a depth the student will not face and a structure that does not match. Ask the school which award route it runs and get the exact code, then take past papers from that code only.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week do three sciences need?
faqs.answer: One or two, not three. The limiting factor is the student's own practice time between sessions, and three weekly hours leave none of it, which is how families end up paying more and seeing less. The efficient sequence is the practical-question fortnight first, then a single science weekly where the marked work shows the largest recoverable loss, picking up the others later. School holidays are the exception, where three or four sessions in a week is realistic because nothing competes.

faqs.question: Is an early-evening session better than a later one?
faqs.answer: For science, usually yes, and Remraam is one of the few communities in this belt where it is practical. With South View School close by, a student can be home soon after four and work a timed section while still alert, which matters because science questions reward concentration and reading carefully. A session at half past eight after a long journey produces less from the same hour. Because nobody is travelling to Al Thamam or Al Ramth, the slot can also move within the evening at no cost.

faqs.question: What does three-science support cost at market rates?
faqs.answer: Less than three times one subject, if sequenced. A qualified subject tutor working online sits at roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly hour run AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle band and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Buying the practical fortnight and then one science at a time keeps the monthly figure in a single-subject band for most of the year. These are published market figures, not IB Gram prices.

A free trial lesson over live video is arranged before any payment is taken, and the plan that comes back will name one science to take next rather than proposing three weekly hours. Lessons are online on Gulf Standard Time; the laboratory stays with the school, and home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India only.
