intro.heading: Three sciences, one evening, and a long drive in between
paragraphs: Serena sits off Al Qudra Road at the outer edge of the Dubailand belt, among clusters including Bella Casa and Casa Viva, with Mudon, Villanova and Remraam alongside. Its Year 10 and Year 11 students attend schools from the Dubailand and Sustainable City cluster ten minutes away to the larger British-curriculum schools in Al Barsha and Jumeirah Park, forty to fifty-five minutes away in the afternoon. The arrival time at home varies by nearly an hour, and science is the subject group most affected.

The reason is arithmetic rather than difficulty. Most IGCSE students carry three sciences, whether as separate subjects or as a coordinated course examined across all three disciplines. Three sets of homework, three sets of practical write-ups, and three bodies of content are competing for the same evening — and in this community that evening frequently starts after 16:40 and has dinner, Arabic homework and a tired fourteen-year-old in it as well.

That is why a generic weekly science hour so often fails here. It is not the teaching; it is that the hour was placed without reference to what else is in the evening or to what kind of science work the student can actually do at that point. Biology recall at 19:30 is fine. A physics problem-solving session at 19:30, after fifty minutes on Al Khail Road, measures fatigue.

IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE addresses — home visits are a service we run only in India — and there is no UAE office or centre. Serena students are taught one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, which means the slot is a scheduling choice rather than a constraint imposed by somebody's route. That is the practical advantage in a community where arrival times differ by forty minutes between neighbours.

This page therefore builds the week rather than selling the hour. What each discipline needs and when it can be taught. How practical catch-up collides with the commute. How to put together a revision week across three disciplines without doing everything badly. Which discipline deserves the best slot, which is a diagnosis rather than a preference. And the administrative facts — route, board, practical arrangements, series — that shape the whole year.

Every figure names its source. Where a decision depends on your child's specific entry, the answer sits in the school's entry statement rather than on any page, this one included. For scale, Dubai's private sector runs 227 schools teaching 17 curricula to 387,441 students, with UK curricula accounting for 37 per cent of enrolment, per Dubai Media Office figures for 2024-25. That variety is why two Serena neighbours on the same street can be sitting different science routes with different practical arrangements, and why a recommendation that suited one household may not transfer to the next.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-serena.subjectsIntro: These are the disciplines and components, each with a note on when in the evening the work can realistically be done and where the marks go.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: The largest reliable loss in UAE cohorts and the discipline most often dragging a coordinated grade. It needs reasoning about change in a connected system, which requires a fresh student — so it belongs in the earliest slot available or at the weekend.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, moments and density
subjects.description: Errors cluster around unit conversion and taking moments about the wrong point, both of which are procedural and can be drilled in a later slot once the method is understood. Question structures repeat year to year, so practice transfers well.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: A fluency problem under time pressure rather than a comprehension problem, which means it needs a student who is alert. Timed calculation practice in a good slot beats re-explanation in a bad one.

subjects.name: Chemistry: qualitative analysis
subjects.description: Ion and gas tests with expected observation wording. Recall-based and directly examined, which makes it ideal for a late evening slot and one of the most predictable mark sets available in the whole science component.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic chemistry
subjects.description: Narrow at IGCSE and rule-governed, so it is the fastest available gain in the chemistry component. Homologous series and the handful of reaction types can be secured in a fortnight of short sessions, including late ones.

subjects.name: Biology: enzymes and transport
subjects.description: The widest mark spread in the biology component. Marks go to explanation of mechanism rather than description of the observation, which is a command-term habit — correctable with a marked paper at almost any hour of the evening.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett square layout and ratio reasoning, which are reliably available marks for a student who practises the layout until it is automatic. Low-cost, high-certainty, and perfectly workable in a tired slot.

subjects.name: Required practical skills
subjects.description: Assessed through a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper depending on board and entry. Method description, variable control, graph plotting and improvement suggestions are written skills — teachable online and rarely practised deliberately.

subjects.name: Graph and data skills
subjects.description: Shared across all three disciplines, which makes this the one place where cross-discipline work genuinely pays: one session improves answers in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously. Needs concentration, so put it early.

subjects.name: Command terms in science
subjects.description: State, describe, explain, suggest and compare each carry a different expectation. Answering 'explain' with a description is the most common silent loss in the science component, and one session with a marked paper usually ends it.

sections.heading: What a Serena science week actually has to carry
paragraphs: Before scheduling anything, count what is already in the evening. A typical Year 10 or 11 student on a coordinated or separate-science route has homework from three disciplines, a practical write-up in whichever discipline had a laboratory lesson that week, Arabic and Islamic Education work required under KHDA rules, and whatever else the timetable produced. That is the context a tutoring hour has to fit into.

Then subtract the commute. Students at the Dubailand and Sustainable City schools arrive home around 15:45 to 16:05 and have a long usable evening. Students travelling back from the Al Barsha and Jumeirah Park cluster arrive between 16:20 and 16:50, having spent forty to fifty-five minutes in a car after a full school day. The second group has perhaps two usable hours before fatigue makes new technical work unproductive, and three sciences want all of it.

The consequence most families reach by trial and error is that something has to be deprioritised deliberately rather than by accident. The deliberate version is to identify the discipline that matters most — in a coordinated course the weakest one, since it sets the shared grade, and on separate sciences the one the post-16 plan needs — and give it the best slot. The accidental version is to spread a weekly hour evenly and watch all three stay where they were.

That is the whole argument of this page. Not that science needs more hours, but that the hours need placing. A tutor who asks what time your child gets home and what else is in the evening before proposing a slot is doing the part of the job that decides whether the rest of it works.
bullets: Count what is in the evening already: three disciplines, a write-up, Arabic homework
Late arrivals have about two usable hours before new technical work stops paying

sections.heading: Which science fits which slot
paragraphs: The three disciplines are not equally demanding at the same hour, and that is the most useful scheduling fact available to a family in this community. Matching the work to the slot can double what an hour achieves without changing the tutor or the rate.

Physics is the least forgiving. Problem-solving requires holding several steps in mind, and circuit reasoning in particular — what happens elsewhere when one component changes — collapses in a tired student. Chemistry splits: mole calculations need alertness, while qualitative analysis wording and organic reaction types are recall and pattern, perfectly learnable late. Biology is the most tolerant of all: command-term marking, diagram labelling, genetics layout and data interpretation all work at 19:30.

That produces a clear priority for the best slot in the week. If physics is the weak discipline, it takes the earliest hour, every time. If physics is fine and chemistry calculations are the problem, chemistry takes it. Biology almost never needs the best slot, which is counter-intuitive for families whose child finds biology hardest — the volume of content makes it feel hard while the losses are usually command-term habits.

The table below sets this out alongside the arrival bands. Treat the last column as the useful part: it names the specific work rather than the subject, because 'revise chemistry' is not a plan and 'learn the expected wording for the standard ion tests' is. The same logic applies to the length of each slot: a thirty-minute recall session that happens five evenings a week beats a ninety-minute session that collapses after a fortnight, and for three disciplines the short repeated version is almost always the sustainable one.

sections.heading: Practical catch-up, and why it collides with the commute
paragraphs: Science is the subject group most likely to generate after-school obligations, and in this belt those obligations collide directly with the drive. It is worth planning for rather than discovering.

Missed laboratory work has to be made up at school, because that is where the apparatus and supervision are. For a student at a near Dubailand school a catch-up session after lessons costs a slightly later pick-up. For a student at an Al Barsha school it can mean a second journey or a very late return, which removes the evening entirely. Families on the long commute should ask the department early what the catch-up policy is and whether written alternatives exist for a missed session.

The write-ups are the other half, and they are the homework nobody schedules. A practical report is slower than a problem sheet, it tends to be due within a few days, and it arrives in whichever week the laboratory lesson fell. In a three-discipline week that is unpredictable load, and it is the commonest reason a tutoring slot gets cancelled at short notice in this community.

What helps is making the written practical skills a deliberate part of the plan rather than an incidental. Method description, variable control, tabulation, graph plotting, uncertainty and specific improvements are examined — through a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper depending on board and entry — and teaching them properly makes every subsequent write-up faster. Three to five sessions there reduce the ongoing load as well as earning marks.

sections.heading: Building a revision week across three disciplines
paragraphs: Revision across three sciences is where most Serena families lose time, because the natural instinct is to rotate evenly and the result is shallow coverage of everything. A better week is uneven on purpose.

The principle is that revision should be organised by question form rather than by chapter, and that the forms differ in how much energy they need. Working timed questions and plotting unfamiliar data require concentration. Learning expected observation wording, practising Punnett squares, and labelling diagrams do not. Marking a paper with the mark scheme sits in between, and is more valuable than almost anything else per minute spent.

A week that works in this community looks roughly like the table below: the demanding forms placed where the student is fresh, the recall forms placed late, and one slot reserved for marking. It is deliberately not three equal science evenings, because three equal evenings produce three partial efforts, and in a coordinated course the shared grade will still be set by the weakest discipline.

One addition that costs nothing: ask the student to keep a single list of lost marks from every piece of marked work, categorised as content, method or command term. By the end of a term that list is a better revision plan than any schedule a tutor can write, because it is specific to them and it is evidence rather than assumption. It also tells you when to stop paying: when the method and command-term entries dry up and only a short content list remains, the expensive part of the work has been done and the rest is the student's own revision.

sections.heading: Which discipline deserves the best slot
paragraphs: This is a diagnosis rather than a preference, and it is answerable in ten minutes from a marked paper rather than from a conversation about which subject a student dislikes.

Take the most recent marked paper or mock. On a coordinated route the papers mix the three disciplines, so go through and separate the lost marks by discipline. In our experience of Dubai cohorts, the loss concentrates in physics more often than anywhere else, with chemistry calculations second. Biology losses tend to be distributed and command-term driven rather than concentrated, which is why biology is usually the wrong place to put the best hour even when it feels hardest to the student.

Then check the cause rather than the discipline. Whole questions blank means a content problem, which needs sustained teaching in a good slot. Answers started, partially right, and marked down means a technique problem — and technique work is both cheaper and more portable, since command-term and graph discipline improves all three disciplines at once.

The resulting plan for a typical Serena family on a coordinated route is specific: the weak discipline in the weekend or earliest slot, three sessions of cross-discipline skills work, and nothing scheduled for the two disciplines that were already functioning. That is a lighter week than three science evenings and it aims at the thing that was actually setting the ceiling. It is also easier to sustain through a Dubai year, which matters more than it sounds: the plan that survives mock weeks, practical write-ups and Ramadan is the plan that delivers, and an ambitious three-evening schedule rarely survives any of them.

sections.heading: Route and board, confirmed before the timetable
paragraphs: Scheduling well is wasted if the hour is spent on the wrong specification. The school's entry statement names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject, and departments inside one Dubai school sometimes differ, so check discipline by discipline.

Three things follow from the entry statement, and all three change the week. Whether the route is separate, coordinated or single award, which determines how many grades are at stake and therefore whether the week should favour one discipline. Which board, which determines whose past papers are worth the hour. And how practical skills are assessed — a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical written paper — which determines whether the plan should include procedural rehearsal at school or written method drilling at home.

The codes to confirm are Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 for separate biology, chemistry and physics, 0654 for Coordinated Sciences double award and 0653 for Combined Science; and Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 for the separate sciences, 4SD0 for the double award and 4SC0 for the single. Paper structures are revised between specification versions, so confirm against the board's current documents for your child's entry year.

None of those documents should cost anything. Boards publish their specifications and provisional timetables, and any tutor worth paying works from them directly. A provider selling them as a resource pack is charging for free material, which is a useful signal about the rest of the arrangement. The one document to pay attention to instead is your child's own entry statement, which is free, specific, and the only thing that settles what the year actually contains.

sections.heading: Mock season, Ramadan and the science calendar
paragraphs: Three predictable events move a science plan every year in this community, and anticipating them is the difference between adjusting and abandoning.

Mock season fills the evenings, and during it a tutoring slot is better spent on targeted review than on new content across three disciplines. The valuable work comes afterwards: mark the returned scripts properly, separate the lost marks by discipline and by cause, and rebuild the week from what the totals show. Mocks are the most accurate free diagnostic a family gets, and in science they are especially useful because they show which discipline is actually dragging a shared grade.

Ramadan shortens the school day, which changes arrival times and the hours when concentration is available. Slots commonly move later, often post-Iftar, and hold at the new time for the month before returning. Because no commute is involved, it is a diary change rather than a renegotiation. It is also the right period to shift the science week towards recall and marking, since those survive a disrupted routine where calculation practice and new circuit work do not.

The third is the unpredictable practical write-up and the school event that moves at a day's notice. An online session can usually be rescheduled within the same week; a missed in-home visit is a wasted journey and is normally charged in full. Across Year 10 and Year 11 that difference compounds into several hours of teaching either kept or lost, which matters more than a small difference in the hourly rate.

sections.heading: Entries, practical arrangements and the second series
paragraphs: The administrative calendar sets the outer limits on any science plan, and for science specifically it includes one item other subjects do not: the practical arrangements.

Cambridge runs IGCSE in a June series and a November series for UAE candidates. The February/March series is offered to India only and does not apply to a candidate sitting here, so advice built on a February window belongs to another country. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. Ask the exam officer which zone applies.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. Checkable reference points: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables for later series which may be revised, so work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

For science, ask two extra questions. What practical arrangements apply to your child's entry — practical examination or alternative-to-practical paper — because it changes what the final weeks should contain. And what a resit involves on a coordinated route, since the shared grade means the award rather than a single discipline is re-sat, which is a bigger decision than for a separate science. Both answers come from the exam office, and both are better known before results day than after it.

process.description: The plan names the slot, what goes in it, and what the student does alone in the lighter slots — recall, labelling, the lost-marks list. For late arrivals it includes a weekend session for problem work, because a 19:30 physics hour in this community is not a plan.

process.title: Adjusted for mocks, practicals and Ramadan
process.description: Mock scripts rebuild the plan, practical write-ups are expected rather than treated as surprises, and slots move later during Ramadan and back afterwards. Each session produces notes naming what was covered and what was set.

whyPoints.title: The slot matched to the discipline
whyPoints.description: Physics problem-solving needs a fresh student; chemistry observation wording and biology recall do not. Placing the work by energy rather than by syllabus order roughly doubles what the same hour achieves, and it costs nothing to do.

whyPoints.title: One discipline, not three
whyPoints.description: On coordinated and single-award routes the weakest discipline sets the shared grade, so the best slot and the paid hour should both go there. Spreading a weekly hour evenly across three sciences produces three partial efforts and leaves the ceiling untouched.

whyPoints.title: Practical load planned, not ignored
whyPoints.description: Write-ups arrive unpredictably and laboratory catch-up can cost a whole evening on the Al Barsha run. We expect both, and we teach the written practical skills deliberately, which earns marks and makes every subsequent write-up faster.

whyPoints.title: Route and board confirmed first
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0654 and Pearson 4SD0 are not interchangeable, and separate-science codes differ again. Confirming the specification and the practical assessment route from the entry statement prevents weeks of practice on the wrong papers.

whyPoints.title: Claims and figures you can check
whyPoints.description: Board documents are free and should be linked rather than resold, every AED figure here names its publisher, and there is no UAE office, no regulator approval, no named school as a client, and no home visits anywhere in the country.

faqs.question: How do I fit three sciences into a Serena evening?
faqs.answer: Unevenly, and on purpose. Count what is already there: homework from three disciplines, a practical write-up in whichever one had a laboratory lesson, and Arabic and Islamic Education work. Then place the demanding work where the student is fresh — physics problem-solving and chemistry calculations — and the recall work late: observation wording, definitions, Punnett squares, diagram labelling. For a student arriving home after 16:25, the demanding work realistically belongs at the weekend rather than in a weekday evening.

faqs.question: Which science should get the best slot in the week?
faqs.answer: The one the marked papers show as the concentration of lost marks, which in Dubai cohorts is most often physics and second most often chemistry calculations. On a coordinated or single-award route that discipline sets the shared grade, so it earns the best hour. Biology usually does not, even when the student finds it hardest: its content volume makes it feel heavy while its losses are typically command-term habits, which can be fixed at almost any hour with a marked paper.

faqs.question: Can physics really not be taught at 19:30?
faqs.answer: It can be taught; it is poorly learned. Physics problem-solving requires holding several steps in mind at once, and circuit reasoning — what happens elsewhere in the circuit when one component changes — is exactly the kind of work that collapses in a tired student. Worse, a timed physics attempt at that hour produces a misleading diagnosis as well as a bad score, and the next few sessions then get aimed at a problem the student does not have. Move the problem work; keep the recall work.

faqs.question: What happens when my child misses a science practical?
faqs.answer: It has to be made up at school, because that is where the apparatus and supervision are, and the cost to your week depends entirely on the commute. For a near Dubailand school it is a later pick-up. For a child at an Al Barsha school it can mean a second journey or a very late return, which removes the evening. Ask the science department early what the catch-up policy is and whether a written alternative exists for a missed session — the answer varies by school.

faqs.question: If the tutoring is online, who supervises the laboratory work?
faqs.answer: The school does, in its own laboratory, with its own equipment and technician. That does not change with online tutoring and nobody should imply otherwise. What online teaching covers is the written element of practical assessment, which is where most practical marks sit: describing a method precisely, identifying and controlling variables, tabulating, plotting and interpreting graphs, discussing uncertainty and suggesting specific improvements. Depending on board and entry that is examined through a practical examination or an alternative-to-practical paper.

faqs.question: How should the science week change during mock season?
faqs.answer: Stop teaching new content across three disciplines and use the slot for targeted review, because mock weeks have already filled the evenings. The valuable work comes after: mark the returned scripts, separate every lost mark by discipline and by cause — content, method or command term — and rebuild the week from the totals. In science this is especially useful, because it finally shows which discipline is dragging a shared grade rather than leaving the family to guess.

faqs.question: Is a practical write-up the reason sessions keep getting cancelled?
faqs.answer: Frequently, yes. A report is slower than a problem sheet, it tends to be due within a few days, and it lands in whichever week the laboratory lesson fell, so the load is unpredictable. Two things help. Expect it in the plan rather than treating it as a surprise, and teach the written practical skills properly early — three to five sessions on method, variables, tabulation, graphs and improvements both earns marks and makes every later write-up faster.

faqs.question: Should we support all three sciences or just one?
faqs.answer: On a coordinated or single-award route, one: the discipline the marked papers identify, because all three feed one or two shared grades and the weakest sets the ceiling. On separate sciences each grade stands alone, so choose by which subject the post-16 plan needs. In both cases, a short cross-discipline block on graphs and command terms is worth adding, because that work improves answers in biology, chemistry and physics simultaneously for a handful of sessions.

faqs.question: Do session times change during Ramadan for science students?
faqs.answer: Usually. Dubai schools shorten the day, which moves arrival times and shifts the hours when concentration is available, so slots commonly move later and often to post-Iftar before returning afterwards. Because no commute is involved it is a diary adjustment rather than a renegotiation. It is also the right month to move the science week towards recall and marking, since observation wording and definitions survive a disrupted routine where new circuit work and calculation practice do not.

faqs.question: How do I know which science route and board my child is on?
faqs.answer: Ask the exam office for the entry statement, which names the board, the syllabus code and the tier for every subject. The codes to look for are Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 for separate sciences, 0654 for Coordinated Sciences and 0653 for Combined, or Pearson 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, 4SD0 and 4SC0. Departments inside one Dubai school sometimes use different boards, so check discipline by discipline rather than assuming the school uses one throughout.

faqs.question: Will a science tutor come to our house in Serena?
faqs.answer: Not one of ours. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one over live video, there is no IB Gram office or centre in the country, and home visits are a service we run only in India. Independent in-home science tutors do work in this belt at roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour including travel, with Serena at the upper end because the round trip is eighty to a hundred and twenty minutes. The advantage of online here is scheduling: the slot can follow your child's arrival rather than a tutor's route.

faqs.question: What does science tutoring cost for a Serena family?
faqs.answer: A qualified subject tutor teaching online runs roughly AED 150 to 300 an hour, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. Budget online tuition is AED 33 to 65, per Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 and EdFlik from AED 45 to 65. In-home visits run AED 180 to 500 including travel, at the upper end for this address. Group classes are advertised in monthly packages from around AED 799 for eight sessions, which also costs about two hours of household time per visit from Serena.

faqs.question: Can my two children share a science tutor to save time?
faqs.answer: They can share a tutor; they rarely share a slot. Siblings in this belt are often on different routes or boards and on different bus routes with arrival times forty minutes apart, so staggered sessions work better — commonly the exam-year student in the better slot and the younger child later. A genuine pair session needs the same route, board and a similar starting point, which is more often found between neighbouring households in Serena, Villanova and Mudon than between siblings.

faqs.question: Is a permit needed to tutor science privately in Serena?
faqs.answer: Yes, as for any private tutoring in the UAE. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and u.ae states it is granted free of charge for two years, applied for through MoHRE's Private Tutor Licensing service with a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Because it is free, no tutor should pass on a licensing cost, and no fine schedule is published.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-serena.closingHeading: Place the hours before you buy them
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-serena.closingBody: For science in this community the scheduling decision matters as much as the tutor. Tell us the route and syllabus codes from the entry statement, the time your child actually gets home, and which discipline the last marked paper shows as the problem. You will get a proposed week — which science goes in the best slot, what the student does alone in the lighter ones, and whether the problem work belongs at the weekend — plus a free first lesson with the tutor who would continue. Teaching is live, one-to-one and online; the laboratory stays at school.

intro.heading: Science tuition fails on the clock before it fails on the teaching
paragraphs: Most families in Sobha Hartland who stop paying for a science tutor do not stop because the teaching was poor. They stop because the arrangement did not survive a normal week. The session was set for 4pm and pickup from a school off Al Khail Road lands at 3.45pm on a good day. The tutor had a slot after their previous booking and the previous booking was in Al Barsha. The child arrived at the session having already done an hour of homework and spent forty minutes of a paid hour being tired. None of that is a teaching problem and all of it is a money problem.

So this page starts with the timetable. Sobha Hartland is a compact masterplan on the Ras Al Khor side of the creek, with two substantial international schools inside it and a short drive to several more through Meydan, Nad Al Sheba, Al Jaddaf and Al Quoz. That geography is unusually favourable: a family whose child attends a school inside the masterplan has one of the shortest school runs in Dubai, which makes an early evening slot genuinely available. A family driving to Al Garhoud or Al Quoz does not, and should not book as though they do.

The second thing shaping the week is one most tuition providers ignore entirely. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. KHDA calculates the instructional time for those subjects on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory subject lesson run shorter than 25 minutes. For a Year 10 or Year 11 student sitting three separate sciences, those lessons occupy real timetable space and real homework time. A science revision plan that assumes a British school week is planning for a week this child does not have.

Third is the shape of IGCSE science itself. Most Sobha Hartland students sit Biology, Chemistry and Physics as three separate qualifications, which means three specifications, three sets of papers and three practical components landing in the same series. Revision cannot be spread evenly because the content volume differs and because the papers themselves are not evenly spaced in the timetable. Knowing which science is closest to its paper is worth more than knowing which science the student finds hardest.

The practical answer we have landed on is online delivery in a slot the family actually controls. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; nobody travels to an address in Sobha Hartland or elsewhere in the Emirates, and home visiting is a service we run in India only. The reason this matters for the school run is specific: a tutor driving between bookings offers the slot their route allows, while an online tutor offers the slot the student can use. Over a two-year IGCSE course that difference is a large number of recovered sessions.

programmes.name: IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics
programmes.description: Usually three separate qualifications sat at 16, on Cambridge 0610, 0620 and 0625 or Pearson Edexcel 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. Cambridge tiers at Core and Extended; the Extended tier carries the algebraic and quantitative treatment that A Level and the IB Diploma assume. Each science has written papers plus a practical component, which on most routes is an alternative-to-practical written paper rather than a timed laboratory examination.
programmes.countryNote: Across the schools serving Sobha Hartland the senior day ends between roughly 2.45pm and 3.30pm, and the drive adds anything from five minutes to forty. That spread decides whether a 4pm session is realistic or whether 5.30pm is the first honest option, and it is the question we ask before proposing a slot.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: Integrated science before the IGCSE split, usually taught as one subject with three strands. The decision that matters here is the one made in Year 9: three separate sciences, a double award, or a single combined qualification. That choice narrows what a student can take at 16 to 19, and it is made at an age when most students have no view about it.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai students in this band also carry the KHDA mandatory subjects, and in Years 7 to 9 the homework load from those sits alongside a wide option set. A weekly science session at this stage is as much about building a working week as about content, and an early slot is easier to protect than it will be in Year 11.

programmes.name: What IGCSE science leads into
programmes.description: IB Diploma sciences or A Level. Both assume the quantitative treatment carried by the Extended tier, and both assume a student can handle multi-step calculation without prompting. The Diploma adds a scientific investigation worth 20% of the subject grade at both Standard and Higher Level, which draws directly on the experimental reasoning IGCSE practical papers assess.
programmes.countryNote: Several schools within a Sobha Hartland school run offer the Diploma, and others run A Level, so the decision at 16 is a live one here rather than automatic. For MoE equivalency on the British track, five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3 are required, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that five.

programmes.name: The November resit route
programmes.ageRange: Ages 16-17 · The autumn after the papers
programmes.description: Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, so a grade that misses a requirement can be retaken in the autumn. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November. This matters to planning because a November entry means a defined eight to twelve week block of work rather than an indefinite commitment.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's academic year makes November resit preparation awkward, because the student is simultaneously starting a new course. Scheduling becomes the whole problem rather than part of it, and an online slot that can move inside the week is the difference between finishing the block and abandoning it.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-sobha-hartl.subjectsIntro: Science is three subjects at this level, and most Sobha Hartland enquiries involve two of them. These are the subjects we support alongside, with the specification detail a parent needs rather than a course summary.

subjects.name: IGCSE Physics
subjects.description: The science Sobha Hartland parents enquire about most. Marks concentrate in electricity and circuit analysis, equation rearrangement, and graph work with units. Extended-tier questions assume algebra the Core tier never requires, which is why a tier change mid-course needs a planned bridge rather than optimism.

subjects.name: IGCSE Chemistry
subjects.description: Mole calculations carried through several steps are the dividing line between a grade 6 and a grade 8 here. Organic chemistry is usually learned as a list and then collapses when a paper asks for reasoning. Both are technique problems with a fixed number of sessions behind them.

subjects.name: IGCSE Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the challenge rather than difficulty. Students lose marks to imprecise terminology and to describing a process when the question asked them to explain it. A revision plan that sequences topics against the paper order beats one that starts at the front of the book.

subjects.name: IGCSE Combined and Co-ordinated Science
subjects.description: Taken where a school offers a double award rather than three separate sciences. The content is a selection from all three sciences, so a tutor needs to know which topics are in and which are not, and parents should check before buying a full triple-science revision plan.

subjects.name: IGCSE Mathematics
subjects.description: Bought alongside science more often than any other subject, and frequently the real cause of a physics or chemistry grade. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and graph gradients appear in science papers, and weakness there reads as a science problem on a report card.

subjects.name: IGCSE English Language
subjects.description: Relevant to science because extended-response marks depend on precise written explanation. A student who writes vaguely under time pressure loses biology marks for reasons that have nothing to do with biology, and it is often the cheapest grade in the set to move.

subjects.name: IB MYP Sciences
subjects.description: Supported for students at continuum schools within a Sobha Hartland school run. Marks are criterion levels out of 8, not percentages, and the processing and evaluating criterion is the one that predicts later success in Diploma sciences.

subjects.name: IB Diploma Biology
subjects.description: Where a Sobha Hartland IGCSE biologist often goes next. The investigation is 20% of the grade at both levels, and the experimental reasoning assessed in IGCSE practical papers is its direct foundation, which is a reason to take those papers seriously rather than as a formality.

subjects.name: IB Diploma Chemistry
subjects.description: Restructured for first teaching in 2023 into structure and reactivity themes. The quantitative gap between IGCSE Core and this course is the single most common reason a strong IGCSE student struggles in DP1, and it is closed in the summer rather than in October.

subjects.name: IB Diploma Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level runs roughly 240 teaching hours against about 150 at Standard Level, with depth added inside each theme. An IGCSE Extended physicist arrives prepared; an IGCSE Core physicist arrives with a specific algebra gap in kinematics and circuits.

sections.heading: When the school day actually ends, and when a session fits
paragraphs: The first question we ask a Sobha Hartland family is not about grades. It is which school, and how long the drive takes at pickup. Across the schools in and around this neighbourhood the senior day ends somewhere between roughly 2.45pm and 3.30pm, and the journey home ranges from a five-minute hop inside the masterplan to forty minutes crossing Al Khail Road at the wrong moment. That spread decides whether 4pm is a real option or a fiction, and it is the single most useful piece of information in booking tuition.

The arithmetic parents rarely run is what happens after arrival. A student who gets home at 3.20pm can eat, change and start a session at 4.15pm with their attention intact. A student arriving at 4.10pm cannot start at 4.30pm in any useful sense, and a session booked there will quietly become forty minutes of teaching inside a paid hour. Booking later is not a compromise; it is how the hour gets used.

The second thing to place in the week is school homework. Three separate sciences plus mathematics plus English generates a predictable load, and most Sobha Hartland schools set it on a fixed cycle. A tuition session that lands on the heaviest homework evening competes with work the student must do, and the student will either skip the homework or arrive at the session having done it badly. Ask the school which evenings are heaviest, then book around them.

sections.heading: Three sciences, three specifications, one week
paragraphs: Most Sobha Hartland students sit Biology, Chemistry and Physics as three separate IGCSEs, which is three specifications running in parallel with three sets of papers in the same series. Parents sometimes treat science as one subject with a single grade problem, and that framing produces a revision plan that spends equal time on all three regardless of which is closest to an examination or which has the largest remaining content.

Content volume differs substantially. Biology is the widest and the most memory-dependent, so it rewards early, spaced coverage and punishes a late sprint. Chemistry has the heaviest quantitative spine, concentrated in mole calculations carried through several steps, so it rewards targeted technique work. Physics is the most algebra-dependent, which means weakness there often turns out to be a mathematics problem wearing a physics label. Those three profiles call for different session shapes, not equal time.

Tiering is the other structural fact. Cambridge offers Core and Extended tiers, and the Extended tier carries the algebraic and quantitative treatment that A Level and the IB Diploma assume. A student entered for Core has a ceiling on the available grade, and a student moved from Core to Extended mid-course has a specific, closable gap rather than a general weakness. Confirm with the school which tier each science is entered for before buying any revision plan, because it changes what the plan should contain.

The practical component is the piece most often misunderstood. On most routes the practical skills are assessed through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a timed laboratory examination, which means the examinable skill is reading and interpreting an experiment on paper: identifying variables, spotting a flaw in a method, reading a scale correctly, and explaining why a result is anomalous. Those are teachable in a handful of sessions and are routinely left untouched until the fortnight before the series.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Edexcel: find out which, because it changes the work
paragraphs: A surprising number of parents paying for IGCSE science tuition cannot say which board their child sits, and it is the first thing a tutor should ask. The two main routes for Sobha Hartland students are Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and they differ in ways that affect how a revision block should be built, not just in paper numbering.

Cambridge tiers at Core and Extended, which determines the grade ceiling and the depth of quantitative work expected. Cambridge also runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE and O Level, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. That is a real administrative risk and it sits with the centre, so ask your school which zone it is in.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is available in May/June and November each year. The November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why any plan should link the live official timetable rather than rely on dates restated elsewhere.

One thing to rule out immediately. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. A student in Dubai does not sit it, and any revision plan built around a February-March window is built for the wrong country. UAE candidates sit June and November, and November is the resit route.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects nobody factors into a revision plan
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. For a Sobha Hartland Year 11 sitting three sciences and mathematics, that is not a footnote. It is several lessons a week plus the homework attached to them, inside the same week the science revision has to happen.

The mechanics are specific. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, permits schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that the length of any mandatory subject lesson be at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Language of instruction follows the same logic. KHDA requires Standard Arabic as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic as the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Schools must also ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential point if your child needs support in them.

For a science revision plan the practical consequence is simple and usually ignored. The usable week is smaller than a British-curriculum planning template assumes, so a plan built on five free evenings is a plan for a week this student does not have. We build around three, and we ask which evenings carry the mandatory-subject homework. For these subjects themselves, note that KHDA states the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which constrains how any tutoring material for them can be described.

sections.heading: The series counted backwards from a Year 11 desk
paragraphs: No competitor page found in the research for this project publishes a calendar, which is odd, because the calendar is what decides when a family should spend. The useful version runs backwards from the papers. UAE candidates sit Cambridge in June with November as the resit route, and Pearson Edexcel in May/June with a November series. Before the papers sit the school's mock examinations, and before those sits the point at which an entry decision including tier is effectively locked.

Entry deadlines sit months before the exam, which is the part parents find counterintuitive. The published Pearson pattern gives a sense of the real distances: the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. So a November resit decision is effectively made in the weeks after August results, while the student is beginning a new academic year.

Counted backwards, the spending order is clear. Diagnosis belongs early in Year 10, when a tier decision is still open. Content support belongs across Year 10 and the autumn of Year 11. Paper technique and the alternative-to-practical paper belong in the spring term before the series. A resit block belongs in the eight to twelve weeks after results, with an end date attached. Anything bought outside that order is bought at the wrong time regardless of the rate.

One administrative item to settle this term rather than later: ask your school which Cambridge zone it sits in and which timetable version it uses. Cambridge states that using the wrong zone timetable can cause a missed exam and that it cannot accept responsibility in that case. It is a five-minute question with a serious tail risk.

sections.heading: Ramadan, holidays and the rest of the Dubai calendar
paragraphs: A revision plan that ignores the UAE academic calendar collapses twice a year. During Ramadan school hours shorten and the whole family's day reorganises around Iftar, which makes a late-afternoon session impractical and a post-Iftar session straightforward. Families regularly ask whether lessons can move to a later evening slot for that period, and the answer is yes. This is one of the clearest practical advantages of online delivery, because a shifted slot requires no change to anybody's travel.

The summer break is long and families in Sobha Hartland frequently spend part of it outside the UAE. That creates two options and one trap. The options are to pause and restart, or to continue from wherever the family is, which online delivery allows without renegotiating anything. The trap is a plan that assumes an uninterrupted summer of catch-up and then loses six weeks of it to travel, arriving in September with the gap untouched and the budget spent.

Winter and spring breaks are shorter and more useful than families expect, because they fall at the right distance from the papers. A short, defined block of work across a break can close a specific content gap without competing with school homework, which is the scarce resource during term. The condition is that the block has a named objective: this student finishes the break able to do multi-step mole calculations, not having generally revised chemistry.

Public examinations do not move for any of this, which is the whole point of counting backwards. The papers sit where Cambridge and Pearson place them. Everything else in the year is negotiable, and a plan that treats the negotiable parts as fixed and the fixed parts as negotiable is the most common planning error we see in this neighbourhood.

sections.heading: What the market charges, cheapest band first
paragraphs: Start at the bottom of the market, because for IGCSE science the bottom of the market is sometimes the right answer and nobody says so. Budget online tuition runs from roughly AED 45 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. For a Year 9 student who needs homework structure and someone to keep them honest, that band does the job. It is not the right band for Extended-tier quantitative chemistry, and the honest line between those two cases is drawn by a diagnosis rather than by a price list.

Above it, qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. That is the band where a tutor who knows the specification, the tier and the alternative-to-practical paper becomes plausible, and for most Year 10 and Year 11 science enquiries from Sobha Hartland it is the right one. Specialist IB and IGCSE tutors run AED 200 to AED 450 or more, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 Dubai table putting specialists at AED 200 to AED 450 or above.

In-home delivery sits at AED 180 to AED 350 per Bestimate, with independent home tutors advertising AED 200 to AED 500, and the premium is travel. For a Sobha Hartland family that premium buys a car crossing Al Khail Road, and it buys it at the most congested hour of the day, which is also the reason the slot on offer is the slot the route allows. Monthly comparisons make it starker: published packages include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions against AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions.

None of these are IB Gram's prices. They are the market's, cited with the publisher and read in October 2026, and they are on this page because three of the six strongest competitor pages for this query publish no price at all. What we cost follows a consultation after a free trial lesson, because it depends on the tier, the number of sciences and the weeks left before the series.

sections.heading: KHDA, the schools this neighbourhood feeds, and what an inspection says
paragraphs: Dubai private schools are regulated by KHDA, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described by u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi has ADEK, Sharjah the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the emirate regulator's role goes beyond inspection.

KHDA inspects annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes the report. For a science parent the limitation is that judgements aggregate across phases and subject groups, so the headline band says little about whether the IGCSE science team is strong or whether it is one teacher covering three specifications. Read the secondary science commentary specifically, and ask the school how many teachers cover each science at IGCSE.

The market around Sobha Hartland is growing rather than static. Dubai had 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25 offering 17 different curricula, with UK curriculum schools at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and International Baccalaureate at 7%, per Dubai Media Office figures. The 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%.

On cost context, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not increase for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family weighing science tuition against the rest of the education budget, a flat fee year is the first time in a while that decision can be made without a simultaneous fee rise to absorb. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, MoE, IB, Cambridge or Pearson approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership of any kind.

sections.heading: Starting, and what we tell you about the slot before you pay
paragraphs: The sequence is short and starts with the clock. Tell us which school, how long the pickup run takes, which evenings carry the heaviest homework, and which of the three sciences is furthest behind. We propose a tutor and a slot that fits that picture rather than one that fits our diary. You take a free trial lesson with no payment and no card, at the time you would actually use.

That last point matters more than it sounds. A trial run at a convenient Saturday morning tells you whether the teaching is good and nothing about whether a Tuesday at 4.30pm works for your child after a drive from Al Quoz. We would rather you trialled the real slot and discovered it is too early, because then we move it before anybody has paid for a term of half-attention.

Where tutors are based is a fair question with a public answer. Our science specialists work across the UAE and India and sessions run in your time zone. Nobody travels to a UAE address. There is no IB Gram office, centre or branch in the Emirates, and the conversion path here is a UAE-appropriate enquiry form and a free trial rather than an overseas phone number, which two ranking competitors use on UAE pages. If no specialist covers a particular science in your slot, we tell you the date it changes rather than substituting a generalist.

On data: the form collects your child's name, year group, school and the subject needing help, because a match and a realistic slot cannot be proposed without them. It is used for that and nothing else, and it can be deleted on request. The privacy notice is linked from every page, consistent with UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection.

faqs.question: What time can a science session realistically start after the Sobha Hartland school run?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which school. For a family attending one of the schools inside the Sobha Hartland masterplan, pickup is a five to ten minute hop and a 4pm or 4.15pm start works. For a run to Mohammed Bin Rashid City or Meydan, 4.45pm is the honest first option. Crossing Al Khail Road to Al Quoz pushes it to 5.30pm, and Al Garhoud to around 6pm. Booking earlier than those windows does not gain a family teaching time; it converts a paid hour into forty minutes of tired attention.

faqs.question: My child does three separate sciences. How should we split tuition time between them?
faqs.answer: Not evenly. Drive the rotation by what is closest to an assessment and by where the remaining content sits, not by which science feels hardest. Biology is the widest and most memory-dependent, so it rewards early spaced coverage. Chemistry concentrates its difficulty in multi-step mole calculation, which is a technique block rather than a long slog. Physics difficulty is frequently an algebra problem wearing a physics label, which a diagnosis catches in one session. One protected weekly slot that rotates by need beats three fragmented ones.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor come to our home in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: No. IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; nobody travels to an address in Sobha Hartland, Mohammed Bin Rashid City or elsewhere in the Emirates. Home visiting is a service we run in India only. UAE lessons are one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. For the school run specifically that is the point: a tutor driving between bookings offers the slot their route allows, while an online tutor offers the slot your child can actually use, and a missed lesson moves to the next evening rather than the next week.

faqs.question: How do I find out whether my child sits Cambridge or Edexcel science?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly, and ask for the specification code rather than the board name. Cambridge sciences are 0610 Biology, 0620 Chemistry and 0625 Physics, each tiered Core and Extended. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences are 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1. The code matters because past-paper practice from the wrong specification wastes the student's time and can teach content that is not examinable. While you are asking, also ask which tier each science is entered for, since Core caps the available grade.

faqs.question: Does the February-March exam series apply to a student in Dubai?
faqs.answer: No. The Cambridge February and March series is offered to India only. UAE candidates sit the June series, with November as the resit route, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November. Any revision plan built around a February-March window is built for the wrong country, which is worth checking if a provider has given you one. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the wrong zone timetable risks a missed exam, so ask your school which zone it is in.

faqs.question: How does the practical component work if lessons are online?
faqs.answer: On most IGCSE science routes the practical skills are assessed through a written alternative-to-practical paper rather than a timed laboratory examination, so the examinable skill is interpreting an experiment on paper. That means identifying independent and dependent variables, spotting a flaw in a stated method, reading a scale or instrument correctly, explaining an anomalous result and suggesting an improvement. All of that is taught perfectly well online. The hands-on laboratory work continues at your child's school, where the apparatus and the supervising teacher are.

faqs.question: Do mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons affect how we plan science revision?
faqs.answer: Yes, more than most plans allow for. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in every Dubai private school regardless of the licensed curriculum. KHDA calculates the instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises no mandatory lesson run shorter than 25 minutes. Those lessons and their homework occupy real space in a Year 11 week. A revision plan assuming five free evenings is planning for a week your child does not have, so we build around three and ask which carry the heaviest load.

faqs.question: How does the Ramadan timetable change a weekly science session in Sobha Hartland?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most families ask for it. School hours shorten during Ramadan and the household day reorganises around Iftar, which makes a late-afternoon session impractical and a post-Iftar session straightforward. Because nobody is travelling to your address, shifting the slot requires no change to anyone's route and can be arranged for the period and then reversed. The same flexibility covers family travel: sessions continue from wherever you are, in your time zone, rather than pausing for six weeks and arriving in September with the gap untouched.

faqs.question: What should we pay for IGCSE science tuition in Dubai?
faqs.answer: It depends which band the diagnosis points to, and sometimes the cheapest band is correct. Budget online tuition runs from about AED 45 an hour, with EdFlik from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52, which is adequate for Years 7 to 9 homework structure. Qualified subject tutors online sit at AED 150 to AED 300, Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150, and that is the right band for most Year 10 and 11 work. Specialists run AED 200 to AED 450 or more. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices.

faqs.question: For a Year 11 science student, is a single 90-minute slot or two shorter ones the better buy?
faqs.answer: For a Year 11 in the spring term, two short sessions usually beat one long one, and the cost for the same hours is identical. Attention for a student who has done a full school day plus a drive is typically good for 45 to 60 minutes and poor after 90. Two 45 or 60-minute sessions placed on the two evenings the child arrives home earliest lose far less of the paid time. One longer session is the better shape when the school run is long and defending a single evening is already hard.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science causes the most trouble for students in this part of Dubai?
faqs.answer: Physics generates the most enquiries from Sobha Hartland families, and in a large share of cases the underlying problem is mathematics rather than physics. Rearranging formulae, standard form, ratio and reading a graph gradient all appear in physics papers, and weakness there reads as a physics problem on a report card. Chemistry comes second, concentrated in multi-step mole calculation. Biology generates fewer enquiries but more surprise grades, because content breadth punishes a late sprint and students mistake familiarity with the material for recall under timed conditions.

faqs.question: When should we start if the papers are in the June series?
faqs.answer: Counted backwards, diagnosis belongs early in Year 10 while a tier decision is still open, content support across Year 10 and the autumn of Year 11, and paper technique plus the alternative-to-practical paper in the spring term before the series. School mocks sit in the Year 11 winter and are the best available diagnostic you will get for free. Starting in the final fortnight is still worth doing, but it is triage rather than teaching, and any provider implying otherwise is selling urgency rather than a plan.

faqs.question: My child missed a grade in June. How does a November resit block work?
faqs.answer: As a defined eight to twelve week block with an end date rather than an open commitment. The awkward part is the calendar: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to students on 20 August 2026. So the decision is made within weeks of August results, and the work happens while the student is also starting a new course. That is a scheduling problem first, which is why a slot that can move inside the week matters.

faqs.question: Do we need a tutor at all, or is the school's own support enough?
faqs.answer: Try the school first, and most families do not. School support sessions are usually free to enrolled students and run by the department that sets the internal assessments and knows the paper timetable. Ask what exists for senior science. The second free option is structured independent practice using the school's own past-paper access with a weekly plan attached. If a diagnosis concludes that the problem is workload or scheduling rather than science, those two work better than paid hours, and we will say so when that is what we see.

faqs.question: What does a school's KHDA inspection band tell us about its science teaching?
faqs.answer: Less than parents expect. KHDA inspects Dubai private schools annually on a six-band scale from Outstanding to Very Weak and publishes a report, but the judgements aggregate across phases and subject groups. A school rated Outstanding may have one teacher covering three IGCSE science specifications; a school rated Good may have a deep science department. Read the secondary science commentary specifically rather than the headline band, then ask the school how many teachers cover each science and which tier each is entered for.

faqs.question: Can one tutor cover all three sciences for the same student?
faqs.answer: Often yes at IGCSE, and it is usually efficient because one tutor can see which science is drifting and rotate towards it without anybody coordinating. The question to ask is which of the three they have taught to the end of a specification and which they are covering competently. Where a single tutor stops being the right answer is Extended-tier chemistry calculation or physics algebra sitting alongside a weak mathematics grade, because that needs the mathematics addressed directly rather than worked around inside a science hour.

intro.heading: Three sciences, three invoices: what TECOM families are actually buying
paragraphs: A parent in Barsha Heights types "IGCSE science tutor in TECOM" into Google because a Year 10 report card came back with three separate science grades and two of them were disappointing. What the search does not reveal is that science at IGCSE is not one subject. A child on the triple-award route sits Cambridge Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620 and Physics 0625 as three independent qualifications, with three sets of papers, three practical components and three mark schemes. The market charges by the hour and by the subject. One hour a week on each science at the qualified-tutor band is three hours, and at Dubai's published rates that is a meaningful monthly line in a household budget that already carries school fees.

The honest starting position is that most families do not need all three at the same intensity. Chemistry and physics share a mathematical spine; a child who cannot rearrange a formula reliably is losing marks in both, and that single weakness is cheaper to fix once than to pay for twice. Biology fails for a different reason, almost always vocabulary precision and the command terms, which responds to short, frequent, low-cost sessions rather than long ones. Treating the three sciences as one undifferentiated spend is the most common way money leaves a TECOM household without a grade moving.

The second thing worth knowing before you pay anybody is where the marks sit. On Cambridge Extended science papers, the theory paper carries half the grade, the multiple-choice paper carries three tenths, and the practical-skills paper carries the remaining fifth. That last component is the one almost nobody tutors, because it requires a tutor who can read a results table and spot that the student recorded four significant figures from a thermometer that reads to half a degree. It is also the component where improvement is fastest, because it is a set of habits rather than a body of knowledge. A parent paying AED 250 an hour for a tutor who only re-teaches the syllabus is buying the expensive half of the problem and leaving the cheap half untouched.

TECOM, which the KHDA school listings and most residents still also call Barsha Heights, sits between the Al Barsha school cluster and the Marina towers. The practical effect on tutoring is that children living in the same tower attend American School of Dubai, GEMS Dubai American Academy, Dubai College, GEMS Wellington International School and Nord Anglia International School Dubai, which means four different science departments, two exam boards and at least two different tiering decisions on the same corridor. A tutor matched by proximity is matched to a postcode. A tutor matched by syllabus code is matched to the paper.

Everything that follows is priced, sourced and counted. The AED figures belong to the providers who published them and are named as such; they are market context, not an IB Gram price list. Our own model is a free trial lesson first, then a quoted plan built around how many of the three sciences actually need weekly contact. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visiting is a service we run only in India, and the comparison table further down sets out what that decision saves a Barsha Heights family in both money and evening hours.
