dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-tecom.programmesIntro: Science at 16 arrives through one of two specifications, and the choice was made by the school, not the family. Knowing which one your child sits changes the papers, the practical arrangement and the number of tutoring hours a grade move actually needs.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology, Chemistry and Physics
programmes.description: Three separate qualifications, each tiered Core or Extended. Extended candidates sit a multiple-choice paper worth 30% of the grade, a structured theory paper worth 50%, and a practical-skills component worth 20%, taken either as a laboratory Practical Test or as the written Alternative to Practical. The Core tier caps the available grade, so the tiering decision made in Year 10 sets a ceiling before any revision begins.
programmes.countryNote: The dominant route in the British-curriculum schools around Al Barsha and Al Sufouh that TECOM children attend. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone timetable, so the timetable your child works from must be the one their own school issued, not a version downloaded from a search result.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Sciences
programmes.description: Two written papers per science, with practical skills assessed inside the written papers rather than in a separate component. The longer first paper carries the larger share of the marks. There is no tiering, so every candidate sits the same paper and the full grade range stays open throughout the course. Question style leans more heavily on extended written answers than the Cambridge equivalent.
programmes.countryNote: Used by several Dubai schools within reach of Barsha Heights, and the reason two neighbours can sit "IGCSE chemistry" and face genuinely different papers. Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Combined, Co-ordinated and Double Award Science
programmes.description: Routes that compress the three sciences into one or two qualifications rather than three. Cambridge Combined Science 0653 yields a single grade; Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 yields a double award. Pearson's Science Double Award 4SD0 does the same across six shorter papers. Content is reduced rather than simplified, which changes what a tutor should cut from a revision plan.
programmes.countryNote: The route that most changes the tutoring bill for a TECOM family, because a double award needs roughly two thirds of the contact hours of three separate sciences while still keeping most post-16 doors open. Schools in the Al Barsha cluster use it for students whose strengths lie outside science but who still need a recognised science qualification.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme Sciences
programmes.description: The feeder route in the IB schools near TECOM, assessed against four criteria rather than against papers. Students arriving into an IGCSE science class from MYP 4 or 5 are usually strong at investigation design and weak at the terse, mark-scheme-driven recall that a Cambridge theory paper rewards. That gap is a six-session problem, not a year-long one.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai International Academy and Nord Anglia International School Dubai both sit within the school run that TECOM households make, so mid-course transfers between MYP and IGCSE science happen on this corridor more often than the national pattern would suggest. The transfer costs money only if nobody maps the content gap first.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-tecom.subjectsIntro: Science tutoring is bought by subject and wasted by subject. What follows is what each one assesses and the specific place marks go missing, so you can decide which of them needs weekly contact and which needs a short, targeted block.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Biology 0610
subjects.description: Loses marks on command-term precision far more than on content. "Describe" and "explain" carry different mark allocations, and a correct idea phrased as a description earns nothing on an explain question. Transport in plants, homeostasis and inheritance are the recurring weak points. Cheap to improve with short frequent sessions.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620
subjects.description: The mole calculation sequence is where Extended candidates separate. Moles, concentration, reacting masses and percentage yield form one chain; a break anywhere in it costs marks across the whole paper. Electrolysis and organic reaction pathways follow. Needs sustained weekly contact for most students.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Physics 0625
subjects.description: Almost entirely an algebra problem dressed as a science one. Rearranging equations, unit conversion and reading a gradient off a graph account for a large share of lost marks. Electricity circuits and moments are the topics students name, but the underlying failure is usually mathematical.

subjects.name: Cambridge Co-ordinated Sciences 0654
subjects.description: Covers all three disciplines at reduced depth for two grades. The risk is a student revising from a triple-award resource and spending weeks on content their paper will never ask about. A tutor's first job here is deletion, which is why this route costs fewer hours.

subjects.name: Cambridge Combined Science 0653
subjects.description: One grade across the three sciences. Suits students loading their options elsewhere. Post-16 science routes usually want a double award or separate sciences, so the honest tutoring conversation here is about what the qualification keeps open and what it closes.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Biology 4BI1
subjects.description: Two written papers, more extended prose than its Cambridge counterpart, and practical skills folded into the written assessment. Students moving from a Cambridge scheme underestimate how much writing stamina the longer paper demands in the final forty minutes.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Chemistry 4CH1
subjects.description: Calculation-heavy with a distinctive emphasis on practical method description. Candidates are asked to write a method that would work, which is a different skill from recalling one. Marks are lost on control variables and on quantities that are not specified.

subjects.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE Physics 4PH1
subjects.description: Formulae are supplied in part, which shifts the difficulty from recall to selection. Students pick a plausible equation rather than the correct one. Radioactivity, waves and electrical energy calculations are the reliable mark-losers in this specification.

subjects.name: Practical skills: Paper 5 and Paper 6
subjects.description: Worth a fifth of each Cambridge science grade and tutored by almost nobody. Content is table design, significant figures appropriate to the instrument, anomalous-point identification, graph scaling and error discussion. A set of habits, learnable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Maths inside science
subjects.description: Standard form, significant figures, rearrangement, percentage change, gradient and ratio. The single highest-return tutoring target for a family paying for both chemistry and physics, because one block of work moves two grades and reduces the number of hours either subject needs afterwards.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580
subjects.description: Listed here because science grades frequently depend on it. A student weak on 0580 algebra will present as weak on 0625 physics, and tutoring the physics alone treats the symptom. Worth diagnosing before a physics plan is priced.

subjects.name: Cambridge IGCSE Additional Mathematics and post-16 bridging
subjects.description: Relevant to TECOM families whose children intend to carry a science into A Level or IB Diploma. A short bridging block in the summer after Year 11 costs less than remediation in Year 12, and it is the one piece of science-adjacent tutoring with a clear end date.

sections.heading: The three-science arithmetic, before anybody quotes you a rate
paragraphs: Start with the number of qualifications rather than the number of hours. A triple-award candidate holds three science grades, each with its own papers and its own mark scheme. A double-award candidate holds two grades drawn from one set of papers. A combined-science candidate holds one. Those three positions carry genuinely different tutoring costs, and the difference is larger than most families expect because it compounds: three subjects means three sets of past papers, three tiering decisions and three separate conversations with three different teachers.

The published rates in the Dubai market give the per-hour side of the sum. At the budget end, EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52 for online sessions, both typically with university-student tutors. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE and A Level tutors run from AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270 and Bestimate's 2026 rate table reaching AED 450 or more. At the top, BartyED publishes AED 650 for a named examiner. Every one of those figures belongs to the provider named beside it.

Multiply the hourly figure by the number of sciences and the monthly reality appears quickly. Bestimate's own monthly estimates for a single weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 at the mid tier, and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Those are per subject. Three sciences at the mid tier therefore lands somewhere between AED 1,800 and 3,600 a month if each one is booked independently, which is the number most families arrive at by accident rather than by decision. The table sets the three routes side by side so the decision can be made deliberately.

IB Gram does not publish a price list on these pages, and the figures above are not ours. Our position is a free trial lesson first, then a quoted plan that says plainly how many of the three sciences need weekly contact. Often the answer is one weekly subject plus a short finite block on practical skills, which is a materially smaller commitment than three standing appointments.

sections.heading: Which papers your child actually sits, by syllabus code
paragraphs: Ask a Dubai tutor which code they teach before anything else. "IGCSE science" is not a specification; 0620 and 4CH1 are, and they do not reward the same answers. A chemistry tutor working from Cambridge material with a Pearson candidate will spend weeks on a paper structure the student will never see. This is the most expensive mismatch in the market and it is entirely avoidable with one question.

On Cambridge separate sciences at Extended tier, the structure is consistent across 0610, 0620 and 0625. Paper 2 is multiple choice and carries 30% of the grade. Paper 4 is the structured theory paper and carries 50%. The practical-skills component carries the remaining 20%, taken either as Paper 5, a laboratory Practical Test, or Paper 6, the written Alternative to Practical. Which of those two a candidate sits is a school decision driven by laboratory capacity, so a TECOM parent should confirm it rather than assume. Core-tier candidates sit Paper 1 and Paper 3 in place of Papers 2 and 4, with a capped grade ceiling.

Pearson's International GCSE sciences work differently. Each of 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 runs two written papers, the first longer and carrying the larger share of the marks, with practical skills assessed inside those papers rather than separately. There is no tiering, so the full grade range stays available to every candidate from the first day of the course. Students crossing from a Cambridge scheme into a Pearson one, which happens on a school move, frequently underprepare for the extended written answers in the longer paper.

Confirm every weighting against the board's own current specification document before you build a revision plan on it. Boards revise specifications, and a weighting copied from a tutoring website two years old is a plausible-looking way to mis-allocate forty hours of a Year 11's time.

sections.heading: Paper 6 is the cheapest fifth of a Cambridge science grade
paragraphs: A fifth of every Cambridge separate-science grade sits on the practical-skills component, and it is the part of the course almost no tutoring money reaches. The reason is that it does not look like science teaching. There is no topic to re-explain. What a candidate needs is a set of specific, repeatable habits: a results table drawn with the independent variable in the first column and units in the headings rather than in the cells; readings recorded to the precision the instrument actually offers; a graph with a scale chosen so the plotted points occupy most of the grid; an anomalous result circled and named rather than quietly averaged away.

Those habits are learnable in a small number of sessions because each one is a rule, not an understanding. A student who loses four marks a paper on table conventions is losing them in exactly the same way every time, which makes the fix diagnosable from one piece of past-paper work. Compare that with organic chemistry, where a four-mark deficit can have five different causes and each needs separate teaching. The cost per mark recovered is not remotely similar, and a parent deciding where to spend first should know that.

The error-and-improvement questions at the end of an Alternative to Practical paper are the other reliable source of free marks. They ask what went wrong and how a method could be bettered, and most candidates answer with a generic sentence about being more careful. The marks go to candidates who name a specific source of error in that specific method and a specific change that addresses it. That is a scripted skill with a limited number of patterns, and drilling the patterns is fast work.

If your child sits Paper 5 rather than Paper 6, the content is the same thinking applied in a laboratory under time pressure, with the additional variable of apparatus handling. Confirm with the school which of the two is entered, because the preparation differs enough that getting it wrong wastes the whole block.
bullets: Independent variable in the first column, units in the heading, not in the cells

sections.heading: Where TECOM families waste science tutoring money
paragraphs: The first waste is intensity without diagnosis. A report card showing three weak science grades produces three bookings, and three bookings produce three tutors each re-teaching a term of content from the start. Six weeks later the household has spent a significant sum and the papers still come back with the same marks missing, because nobody established which marks were missing. A single diagnostic session against a past paper, with the script marked rather than the topics discussed, changes what the following twenty sessions do.

The second waste is the wrong tier of tutor for the job. A named examiner at AED 650 an hour, as BartyED publishes, is a defensible purchase for a candidate two marks off an A* on a specific paper with six weeks left. It is an indefensible purchase for a Year 9 who has not yet been tiered. Equally, a university-student tutor at AED 45 to 65, as EdFlik advertises, is reasonable value for homework supervision and poor value for a mole-calculation chain that needs a chemist. Matching the tier of tutor to the tier of problem is where most of the available saving sits.

The third waste is duplicated mathematics. A family paying separately for chemistry and physics is frequently paying two people to teach rearrangement, standard form and significant figures to the same child in the same month. Consolidating those two sciences with one tutor who can teach the shared mathematical spine once reduces both the hours and the confusion of two different notations.

The fourth is paying through exam weeks and school holidays out of habit. Sessions during a school's internal examination fortnight generally return very little, because the student has no capacity left. Pausing them and moving the hours to the fortnight afterwards costs nothing and returns more. Any arrangement that cannot be paused is an arrangement built for the provider.

sections.heading: The maths hiding inside chemistry and physics
paragraphs: Most physics difficulty reported to us from the Marina and New Dubai belt is not physics difficulty. A student who cannot confidently rearrange an equation with the unknown in the denominator will fail at pressure, density, resistance, wave speed and efficiency, and will appear to have five separate topic weaknesses. Teaching those five topics costs five times what teaching the rearrangement costs, and the rearrangement has to be taught anyway before any of the five will stick.

Chemistry has its own version. The mole sits at the centre of a chain that runs from relative formula mass through moles, concentration, reacting masses and percentage yield to limiting reagents. Each link depends on the one before. A student who is shaky on the first link produces wrong answers at the fifth and is told, accurately but unhelpfully, that they struggle with yield calculations. Repairing the chain in order is a handful of sessions. Repairing the symptoms is a term.

The arithmetic that underpins both sits in a short list: standard form, significant figures, unit prefixes from nano to mega, percentage change, ratio, and reading a gradient from a straight-line graph. None of it is beyond a competent Year 10. All of it is assumed rather than taught by science schemes of work that must get through a crowded specification, and it is the gap a tutor can close quickly because there is no conceptual depth to it, only fluency.

For a TECOM family paying for two sciences, this is where the clearest saving sits. One finite block of mathematical fluency work reduces the hours both chemistry and physics subsequently need, and it has the additional effect of lifting the Cambridge Mathematics 0580 grade that the same child is also sitting. One purchase, three grades touched.
bullets: Rearrangement with the unknown in the denominator, until it is automatic
Standard form and unit prefixes without a calculator prompt
Significant figures matched to the instrument or the data given
The mole chain taught in order: mass, moles, concentration, yield
Gradient and intercept read from a graph as a routine, not a puzzle

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with science coursework and investigations
paragraphs: IGCSE sciences no longer carry a large coursework component in the specifications TECOM schools generally use, but students still produce assessed investigation work, school-marked practical reports and, in IB MYP classes next door, criterion-marked investigations. The boundary matters, and it matters more in science than families expect, because a results table is easy for an adult to improve and impossible for a student to defend afterwards.

A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain what a criterion or a mark scheme rewards, model the technique on a different dataset, ask questions about a draft, and point out that a conclusion does not follow from the evidence presented. A tutor may not supply data, rewrite a method, produce the analysis, or edit a report to completion. The student's own work must remain the student's own work, and any tutor who offers otherwise is selling a malpractice risk that lands on the child, not on the provider.

The practical test of whether a line has been crossed is simple: could the student sit down tomorrow and explain every choice in the document without help? If the answer is no, the document is not theirs. We say this plainly on every page because the UAE tutoring market contains providers who sell completed assessed work outright, and a parent comparing options deserves to know which side of that line a provider stands on.

The same principle applies to past papers and mark schemes. We reference official specification documents and link to the board's own pages rather than redistributing them. Boards hold copyright in that material, and unreleased material carries an additional malpractice exposure for the candidate.
bullets: A tutor teaches the skill and questions the draft; the student produces the work
No supplied data, no rewritten methods, no analysis produced on the student's behalf
The test: can the student defend every choice unaided tomorrow?
Official specifications referenced and linked, never redistributed

sections.heading: Online against the in-home alternative, costed for a Barsha Heights tower
paragraphs: In-home tutoring is a real product in Dubai and it is reasonable to want it. The honest comparison is about what the premium buys. Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts in-home one-to-one visits at AED 180 to 350 an hour, and independent home tutors advertise between AED 200 and 500, against AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online. Monthly packages in the market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and between AED 1,599 and 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. The gap is the travel, and the travel is not a service the student receives.

For a Barsha Heights tower the travel cost is higher than the raw distance suggests. Visitor parking in TECOM towers is limited, building access needs a security desk, and a tutor arriving between 17:00 and 19:00 is crossing Sheikh Zayed Road at the worst hour of the day. A tutor who covers that journey twice in an evening cannot take many students, which is precisely why the hourly rate carries a premium. The family pays for a car on Sheikh Zayed Road.

The second cost is selection. Matching by travel radius means choosing from the tutors willing to drive to your tower at that hour. Matching by syllabus means choosing a 0620 chemist who has taught the Extended mole sequence to Cambridge candidates for years, wherever that person happens to live. For a specific code at a specific tier, those two pools are not the same size, and the narrower pool is the one that costs more per useful hour.

IB Gram does not offer home visits anywhere in the UAE; our home-visit service runs only in India. UAE lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared whiteboard, so a chemistry calculation is written out and worked through in the same way it would be on a kitchen table, and the recording or notes remain available afterwards. sections.heading: Cost in context: fees, exam entries and where tutoring sits
paragraphs: A tutoring figure means little without the numbers around it. Dubai's private school sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 different curricula, with UK-curriculum provision accounting for the largest share of enrolment. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. For a family budgeting science support, that fee freeze is the most useful piece of context available this year: the largest education line in the household is flat, which makes a deliberate tutoring decision easier to size.

Exam entry is the line families forget. Where a student sits papers through their own school, entries are handled by the school and appear on a fees statement. Where a student sits as a private candidate, which happens after a mid-year arrival or a subject dropped and resumed, entry is arranged with a registered exam centre and the costs sit with the family. Confirm the figure with the centre directly; it varies by centre and by subject count, and no number quoted on a tutoring website should be treated as authoritative.

Against that backdrop, the sensible way to size science tutoring is per paper rather than per month. A fifth of a Cambridge science grade sits on practical skills, and a short block there is a small, defined cost. Half sits on the theory paper, which is where sustained weekly work earns its money. Three tenths sits on multiple choice, which responds to timed practice more than to teaching. Allocating spend in those proportions is a different exercise from booking three tutors and hoping.

Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK-curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. More capacity means more mid-year moves, and mid-year moves are the single most common trigger for a sudden, poorly-planned science tutoring spend.

sections.heading: Starting from TECOM, with the limits stated up front
paragraphs: The sequence is short. You tell us the syllabus codes, the tier, the school and which of the three sciences is genuinely in trouble. We run a free trial lesson against a past paper rather than a conversation, so what comes back is a marked script and a short list of where the marks went. Then we quote a plan that says how many weekly hours, on which subject, for how long, and what it leaves out.

Two limits are worth stating before you spend time on the enquiry. First, there are narrow combinations where no UAE-resident tutor is free at the hour a TECOM family wants, and the honest answer in that case is a tutor elsewhere in our network working to Gulf Standard Time, disclosed in advance rather than discovered later. Second, nobody can promise a grade. A tutor can tell you which marks are reachable from where your child is now, and that is a more useful thing to be told than a number.

On regulation, the position is straightforward and worth knowing whoever you hire. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you. Dubai's private schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. IB Gram claims no regulator approval, accreditation or partnership, because it holds none.

What we will claim is specific. Tutors matched to the syllabus code rather than to a postcode, one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, a free trial before any payment, session notes for a parent who was at a desk, and a plan that can be paused during an internal exam fortnight. For an IGCSE science tutor in TECOM, that combination is what the money buys.

process.title: Tell us the codes, not just the subjects
process.description: 0620 Extended with Paper 6, or 4CH1 untiered, are different requests. Send the syllabus codes, the tier, the school and the term the trouble started. That one message removes the most expensive mismatch in the Dubai tutoring market before any money changes hands.

process.title: Free trial against a past paper
process.description: The trial lesson is a diagnostic, not a sales call. The tutor works through recent past-paper questions with your child and marks the script. What comes back to you is a short list of where marks were lost, by paper and by question type, rather than a general impression.

process.title: A quoted plan that names what it drops
process.description: We put the hours in writing: which science gets weekly contact, which gets a finite block, what the mathematical underpinning needs, and what the plan deliberately leaves out. A plan that covers everything is a plan nobody has thought about.

process.title: Weekly sessions on Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Slots are set after the school run, usually between 17:30 and 19:30 for Barsha Heights families, and held each week. Sessions run one-to-one over live video with a shared whiteboard, and notes follow afterwards for a parent who was still at work.

process.title: Review at six sessions against the same paper
process.description: After roughly six sessions we re-run a comparable past paper and compare the two marked scripts. If the marks have not moved in the places the plan targeted, we change the plan or the tutor. That review is the point at which continuing or stopping should be decided.

process.title: Pause, stop or shift as the term demands
process.description: Internal exam fortnights, business travel, Ramadan timings and the run-up to a June or November series all change what a week can carry. Sessions pause and resume without losing the slot, and the arrangement ends when the family says it ends.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus code, not by driving distance
whyPoints.description: A 0620 Extended chemist who has taught the mole sequence to Cambridge candidates for years is a different person from the nearest available science graduate. Online delivery means the first pool is the one you choose from, which is the whole argument for the format.

whyPoints.title: The practical-skills paper is treated as a subject
whyPoints.description: A fifth of each Cambridge separate-science grade sits on Paper 5 or Paper 6, and most providers never mention it. We treat table conventions, significant figures, graph scaling and error discussion as teachable content with a defined end point.

whyPoints.title: AED figures attributed to whoever published them
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page names its source and its tier. Three of six competitor pages reviewed in our market research publish no price at all, and two quote US dollars to families who transact in dirhams. Market context is only useful if it is checkable.

whyPoints.title: Academic honesty stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. We do not produce assessed work, supply data or edit a report to completion, and we say so on the page because parts of this market do the opposite.

whyPoints.title: One tutor can hold two sciences
whyPoints.description: Chemistry and physics share a mathematical spine. Consolidating them with a tutor who teaches both means that spine is taught once, which usually reduces total hours rather than adding a second standing appointment.

whyPoints.title: Delivery and its limits disclosed before payment
whyPoints.description: Lessons are online, one-to-one, over live video. Home visits are an India-only service and are not offered anywhere in the UAE. Where no UAE-resident specialist is free at your hour, we say so in advance and name the alternative.

faqs.question: How much should I expect to pay for an IGCSE science tutor in TECOM?
faqs.answer: The Dubai market splits by tier rather than by area. Online sessions with university-student tutors advertise from AED 45 to 65 at EdFlik and AED 33 to 52 at Tutopiya. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE tuition from AED 150. Specialist IGCSE support runs AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270. Those figures belong to the providers named. The number that matters more is how many of the three sciences need weekly contact, because that multiplier moves the monthly total further than the hourly rate does.

faqs.question: Does my child need separate tutors for biology, chemistry and physics?
faqs.answer: Usually not three. Chemistry and physics share rearrangement, standard form, significant figures and graph work, so one tutor who holds both can teach that spine once instead of twice, which generally reduces total hours. Biology fails differently, almost always on command-term precision and vocabulary, and responds to shorter, more frequent sessions. A practical first step is a marked past-paper script for each science. That usually shows one subject needing sustained weekly work and the other two needing short, defined blocks, which is a smaller commitment than three standing appointments.

faqs.question: What is Paper 6 and why does it matter so much?
faqs.answer: Paper 6 is the written Alternative to Practical on Cambridge separate sciences, and together with the laboratory Paper 5 it carries 20% of the Extended grade. It assesses table design, precision appropriate to the instrument, graph scaling, anomalous-result identification and improvement suggestions. Almost no tutoring in this market touches it, which makes it the cheapest fifth of a grade available. The reason it is cheap is that the content is a set of rules rather than a body of understanding, so a student losing the same four marks every paper can be taught the rule in a handful of sessions. Confirm with the school whether Paper 5 or Paper 6 is entered.

faqs.question: Which syllabus codes do Barsha Heights children usually sit for science?
faqs.answer: Both of the major international routes appear on this corridor. Cambridge separate sciences are 0610 biology, 0620 chemistry and 0625 physics, with Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 as the double award and Combined Science 0653 as the single. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1, with Science Double Award 4SD0. Schools within the TECOM school run use different combinations, so two children in the same tower can sit genuinely different chemistry papers. Ask the school for the code and the tier in writing before booking any tutoring, because the papers reward different things.

faqs.question: Is Co-ordinated Sciences cheaper to support than three separate sciences?
faqs.answer: Materially, yes. Co-ordinated Sciences 0654 produces two grades from one set of papers covering reduced content across the three disciplines, so the weekly hours needed sit closer to one or one and a half than to two or three. The saving disappears if the tutor does not know what to delete. The common failure is a double-award candidate revising from triple-award material and spending weeks on content their paper will never ask about. The first job on this route is mapping the specification against the resources the student already owns, and cutting.

faqs.question: My child is weak in physics. Is the problem actually maths?
faqs.answer: Often it is. A student who cannot reliably rearrange an equation with the unknown in the denominator will struggle with pressure, density, resistance, wave speed and efficiency, and will look as if they have five topic weaknesses rather than one skill gap. Teaching five topics costs roughly five times what teaching the rearrangement costs, and the rearrangement has to be taught first anyway. A diagnostic that separates mathematical fluency from physics understanding is worth running before any physics plan is priced, because it changes both the hours and the order of work.

faqs.question: Do Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE science papers need different preparation?
faqs.answer: Yes, enough that using the wrong past papers wastes weeks. Cambridge Extended separate sciences use a multiple-choice paper at 30%, a structured theory paper at 50% and a practical-skills component at 20%, and candidates are tiered Core or Extended. Pearson's 4BI1, 4CH1 and 4PH1 run two written papers with practical skills folded into them and no tiering at all, with more extended written answers and more method-writing. A student crossing from one to the other on a school move typically underprepares for the writing stamina the longer Pearson paper demands.

faqs.question: When do TECOM students actually sit their IGCSE science exams?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs International GCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and UAE candidates sit those two. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and November; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who use the wrong zone timetable, so work only from the timetable your child's school issued.

faqs.question: What time of day do science sessions realistically work for a TECOM household?
faqs.answer: The Al Barsha and Al Sufouh bus runs put most secondary students back into a Barsha Heights tower between 15:45 and 16:45, depending on the campus and the direction of travel. A session starting before 17:00 competes with the journey and with food. The reliable window is 17:30 to 19:30 on Gulf Standard Time, which also suits households where both parents work until 18:00, because the lesson is already running when they get in and the notes arrive afterwards. During Ramadan, families commonly move sessions to a post-Iftar slot instead.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with a school science investigation report?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain what the mark scheme or criterion rewards, model the technique on a different dataset, and ask questions about a draft that expose a conclusion the evidence does not support. A tutor may not supply data, rewrite a method or produce the analysis. The practical test is whether your child could sit down tomorrow and defend every choice in the document unaided. If not, it is not their work, and the consequence of that falls on the student rather than on the provider.

faqs.question: Does a science tutor in Dubai need a permit, and does it cost anything?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you see quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Is a group science class at a tuition centre better value?
faqs.answer: It can be, for the right problem. A group class is reasonable value for timed multiple-choice practice and for general content coverage, where one explanation genuinely serves several students. It is poor value for a broken mole-calculation chain or for practical-skills habits, because those need a marked script and an individual correction. A sensible hybrid is a group class for breadth plus a short one-to-one block on the specific component losing marks, which usually costs less in total than open-ended individual tutoring across all three sciences.

faqs.question: Will my child's IGCSE science grades satisfy UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: For the British track, the Ministry requires a pass in five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. Sciences normally count towards the five. Equivalency is a Ministry process, not something a tutoring provider performs or can guarantee, so verify the current requirements on the Ministry's own channel before planning around them.

faqs.question: My child has eight weeks before the papers. Is it too late to start science tutoring?
faqs.answer: Eight weeks changes what is worth attempting rather than whether anything is. In that window the highest-return targets are the practical-skills component, because it is habit-based and fast to fix, timed multiple-choice technique, and the two or three theory topics carrying the most marks on that specific paper. Re-teaching a year of content is not available and should not be sold to you. A marked past-paper script in the first session is what tells you which of those targets applies, and any plan offered before that script exists is guesswork.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based tutor covers my child's exact specification?
faqs.answer: It happens on narrow combinations, usually a less common specification at an awkward hour. The honest answer is that we match a tutor elsewhere in our network who teaches that specification and schedules to Gulf Standard Time, and we tell you that before you pay rather than after. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video in either case, so the format does not change. Home visits are not part of the arrangement anywhere in the UAE; that is a service we run only in India.

faqs.question: What should improvement look like after a term of TECOM science lessons?
faqs.answer: Set the measure before the first session. The measure should be marks on comparable past papers, broken down by paper and question type, not a general report that confidence has improved. We mark a script in the trial lesson, keep it, and re-run a comparable paper after roughly six sessions. If the marks have not moved in the places the plan targeted, the plan or the tutor changes. That review point is also the natural moment to decide whether to continue paying, which is a decision every provider should make easy.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-tecom.closingHeading: Price the papers, not the panic
dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-tecom.closingBody: An IGCSE science tutor in TECOM is a decision with three variables: which specification your child sits, how many of the three sciences genuinely need weekly contact, and which component is actually losing the marks. Get those three right and the monthly figure is usually smaller than the one a family arrives at by booking three tutors in a week. Send us the syllabus codes, the tier and the school. The free trial lesson is a marked past paper, the plan that follows names what it leaves out, and every session runs one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-greens.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are listed by individual science rather than as general science teachers, because the three subjects fail in different places and a Year 11 rarely needs all three equally. Each names the syllabus codes they cover so you can check them against the examination entry.

intro.heading: Three sciences and four evenings
paragraphs: A Greens family with a Year 11 sitting the three separate sciences is managing a bigger timetable than they usually realise. On the Cambridge route each subject carries three papers, which is nine papers in a single series. On the Pearson route each carries two, which is six. Either way, the preparation has to fit into the evenings left after a school day that ends between about three and half past three, a bus that arrives later than that, and clubs that run to half past four two or three times a week.

Count the week honestly and it is short. Monday through Thursday each offer something between ninety minutes and two and a half hours of usable time once the journey, a meal and school homework are accounted for. Friday is a half day at most Dubai schools, which makes the early afternoon the best fresh slot of the week and the one nobody books. Saturday and Sunday are the UAE weekend and the only place a full timed paper fits without compressing everything else.

That arithmetic is the whole reason this page exists. A tutoring plan that assumes three weekly hours for three sciences will collide with homework by the second week of term and be abandoned by half-term. A plan built around one rotating science, one protected long evening and a weekend paper slot survives to May. The difference is scheduling rather than effort, and it is decided before the first session rather than during it.

The second thing families misjudge is the practical paper. Cambridge candidates sit either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and Pearson assesses the same skills inside the written papers. In both cases what is being tested is reading an unfamiliar method, identifying the variable that was controlled, tabulating results, plotting them and criticising the procedure. All of that is written work. None of it requires a tutor at a bench, which is why online support covers it completely.

The third is route. Not every Greens student sits three sciences. Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654 awards two IGCSEs across three papers and Combined Science 0653 awards one, and Pearson's Science Double Award 4SD0 does the same job as Coordinated Sciences. A child at one of the IB continuum schools near The Greens may be in the Middle Years Programme and not sitting IGCSE sciences at all. Confirming which of these applies takes one look at the examination entry and changes the plan entirely.

Everything below is built from the week outwards: the routes, the evenings, the practical papers, where each science actually loses marks, when support has to start, and what three-subject help costs in this part of Dubai. All IB Gram lessons in the UAE are delivered one-to-one over live video; home visits are a service offered only in India.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-greens.programmesIntro: Four science routes are sat at sixteen in the schools around The Greens, and they differ in the number of qualifications awarded and the number of papers written. The entry form settles which one your child is on.

programmes.name: Cambridge separate sciences: Biology 0610, Chemistry 0620, Physics 0625
programmes.description: Three IGCSEs and nine papers. Each subject carries a multiple-choice paper, a theory paper and either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical paper, and each is tiered Core and Extended. It is the route expected by most schools before A Level sciences or Higher Level Diploma sciences, and it is the heaviest option block a Year 11 can carry.
programmes.countryNote: In the Emirates Living and Al Barsha clusters this is the default for students aiming at medicine or engineering, and it is where the timetable pressure on a Greens family is greatest. Nine papers in one series means revision has to be rotated rather than parallel, which is a scheduling decision made in September rather than in March.

programmes.name: Cambridge Coordinated Sciences 0654, double award
programmes.description: Two IGCSEs from three papers, covering biology, chemistry and physics in a single coordinated course. The content is compressed rather than simplified, so the common difficulty is thin coverage across a wide syllabus rather than depth in any one discipline. Core and Extended tiers both exist, and the practical component works exactly as it does on the separate sciences.
programmes.countryNote: Coordinated Sciences suits a Greens student who needs science breadth without surrendering three option blocks, and it is frequently a better outcome than three separate sciences taken thinly. For tutoring it changes the diagnosis: the gaps are usually spread evenly across all three disciplines rather than concentrated in one.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sciences: 4BI1, 4CH1, 4PH1 and 4SD0
programmes.description: Separate sciences carry two papers each rather than three, and practical skills are assessed inside those written papers rather than through a separate practical test. The Science Double Award 4SD0 awards two IGCSEs across three papers and plays the same role as Cambridge Coordinated Sciences on the Edexcel route.
programmes.countryNote: The November series is the practical advantage here for a Greens family. Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May and June and again in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026, so a missed science grade does not cost a full academic year.

programmes.name: Lower secondary science into IGCSE
programmes.description: The three years before the option blocks are chosen, ending for many Cambridge schools in Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests. The set a student lands in at the end of Year 9 often determines whether triple science is offered at all, and whether a Core or Extended entry follows two years later.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, so the decision window falls inside a Dubai school year rather than at its end. For Greens families the cheapest intervention of the whole five-year run is a short block in Year 9 on the two topics that decide the set.

dubai/igcse-science-tutor-in-the-greens.subjectsIntro: Twelve separable pieces of work sit behind the phrase "science tutoring". These are the ones that cost marks in the schools around The Greens, grouped by subject, with the practical paper treated as its own skill because it is.

subjects.name: Physics: electricity and circuits
subjects.description: Series and parallel reasoning, potential dividers, resistance and power. It is the single largest source of lost physics marks because it is applied rather than recalled: the student knows the formulae and cannot decide which part of the circuit the question is asking about.

subjects.name: Physics: forces, moments and motion
subjects.description: Equilibrium, moments about a pivot, momentum and motion graphs. Marks disappear when the diagram is not drawn, because the pivot and the distances then get guessed. Drawing is a habit and it is cheap to install.

subjects.name: Physics: waves, light and sound
subjects.description: Reflection, refraction, total internal reflection and the wave equation. Ray-diagram questions reward precision with a ruler and a protractor, and students lose marks for sketches that would be correct if they were drawn accurately.

subjects.name: Physics: thermal physics and energy
subjects.description: Specific heat capacity, latent heat, energy transfers and efficiency. The calculations are routine and the losses are almost entirely units and the conversion between kilojoules and joules, which is a checking habit rather than a concept.

subjects.name: Chemistry: moles and stoichiometry
subjects.description: Reacting masses, concentrations, gas volumes and percentage yield. Arithmetic-dense and time-pressured, and the dividing line between the middle and the top grades in Extended chemistry. It responds to volume of practice rather than to further explanation.

subjects.name: Chemistry: acids, bases, salts and tests
subjects.description: Preparation of salts, neutralisation, and the ion and gas tests that recur in every series. These are recall marks and they are reliably available, which makes them the first thing to secure when a student is short of time.

subjects.name: Chemistry: organic chemistry
subjects.description: Homologous series, addition and substitution, polymers and fuels. It arrives late in Year 11 in most schemes of work and is therefore under-practised rather than genuinely difficult, which makes a short block unusually productive.

subjects.name: Chemistry: rates and reversible reactions
subjects.description: Collision theory, catalysts and Le Chatelier reasoning on industrial processes. Explanation questions require the mechanism of the change rather than the direction of it, and a student who says the equilibrium shifts without saying why earns part marks.

subjects.name: Biology: cells, transport and enzymes
subjects.description: Diffusion, osmosis, active transport and enzyme behaviour. Osmosis questions are where precise wording earns marks, since describing water movement without naming the water potential gradient scores less than it appears to deserve.

subjects.name: Biology: genetics and inheritance
subjects.description: Punnett squares, ratios, sex linkage and variation. The obstacle is notation and ratio reasoning rather than recall, so it behaves more like a mathematics topic and improves quickly with a couple of focused sessions.

subjects.name: Biology: human physiology and homeostasis
subjects.description: Circulation, gas exchange, excretion and temperature control. The volume of precise terminology is what catches students out, and active recall in short frequent bursts beats long rereading sessions by a wide margin.

subjects.name: Practical skills and the alternative-to-practical paper
subjects.description: Reading an unfamiliar method, identifying variables, tabulating, plotting with a sensible scale and criticising a procedure. Taught thinly in most schools because laboratory time is short, worth marks in every series, and entirely written work rather than bench work.

sections.heading: What an IGCSE science tutor is actually being hired for
paragraphs: Three distinct things get called science tutoring, and they need different plans. Three separate sciences means three IGCSEs and, on the Cambridge route, nine papers in one series. Coordinated Sciences 0654 means two IGCSEs from three papers covering all three disciplines. Combined Science 0653 means one IGCSE from three papers. Pearson offers the separate sciences with two papers each and the Science Double Award 4SD0 with three papers for two qualifications.

The route changes the diagnosis before it changes anything else. A triple-science student usually has one weak subject and two reasonable ones, so the money belongs on that subject and the plan is narrow. A Coordinated Sciences student usually has thin coverage spread across all three disciplines, because the course compresses a very wide syllabus, and the plan is a rotation rather than a focus. Treating the second case like the first wastes a term.

The table below sets the routes side by side. Read the papers column carefully if you are planning a revision timetable, because nine papers and three papers are completely different logistical problems even when the content overlaps. It is also worth checking against the examination entry rather than against what you remember being chosen in Year 9, since option blocks change and schools occasionally move a student between routes.

Verify every code with the board rather than with a tutoring page, this one included. Cambridge publishes syllabuses at cambridgeinternational.org and Pearson at qualifications.pearson.com, and both revise specifications on published cycles. Cambridge also allocates each examination centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong version.

sections.heading: Three sciences, one Greens week
paragraphs: This is the section every other page for this query leaves out. Secondary school days around The Greens finish between roughly three and half past three, buses load after form groups, and clubs run to half past four two or three times a week. What remains, once a meal and the school's own homework are accounted for, is four weekday evenings of between ninety minutes and two and a half hours, a short Friday, and a weekend.

The table below maps that week. Two rows matter more than the others. The long midweek evening is the only weekday slot with room for ninety minutes or for two shorter sessions back to back, and it should be protected rather than filled opportunistically. And the Friday half day, which most Dubai schools run, offers an early-afternoon hour with a student who has not just finished a full day. It is the freshest window of the week and the least booked in this community.

What does not work is three separate weekly science hours on three separate evenings. It looks reasonable on a calendar and it collides with homework in the second week of term, because Year 11 homework is not evenly distributed and a mock or a coursework deadline takes a whole evening without warning. Plans built that way are abandoned by half-term, and the sessions already paid for are the cheapest part of what was lost.

The pattern that survives is narrower: one rotating science on a fixed weekday, one protected long evening for two subjects if all three genuinely need work, and the weekend for complete timed papers. Timings in the table are indicative rather than measured, so set yours against your own school's published day and your own bus route before committing to a slot.

sections.heading: How practical skills are assessed when nobody is at a bench
paragraphs: Parents reasonably assume that a practical paper needs practical tutoring. It does not, and understanding why removes the main objection to online science support. Cambridge candidates sit either Paper 5, a practical test taken at the centre, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical. Pearson assesses the same skills inside its written papers rather than through a separate component. In every one of those cases the student is writing, reading and plotting rather than handling apparatus.

What the papers actually test is a short list. Reading an unfamiliar method and working out what it is measuring. Identifying the independent, dependent and controlled variables. Recording results in a table with consistent significant figures and correct units. Choosing a sensible scale, plotting accurately and drawing a line of best fit. Reading a value from a graph or finding a gradient. And criticising the procedure in a way that names a specific weakness rather than apologising for the experiment.

Every item on that list is taught better with a shared screen and a past paper than with equipment, because each one is a marking convention as much as a scientific skill. A student who plots accurately but chooses a scale that wastes half the grid loses marks a demonstration would never reveal. The school's laboratory work covers manipulation and safety, which are the school's job and not a tutoring product.

The table below sets out the component by board and route, and the right-hand column is the one to read if somebody has told you science cannot be tutored online. It can, and the practical papers are among the clearest examples, because they are the part of the course most schools teach thinnest and most families never practise.

sections.heading: Where each science actually loses marks
paragraphs: Marks in IGCSE science are lost in predictable places, and the useful consequence is that a diagnosis can be specific. Physics loses most of its marks in electricity, because series and parallel reasoning is applied rather than recalled, and in moments, because students do not draw the diagram and then guess the pivot. Both are fixable in a small number of sessions once named.

Chemistry loses marks in two very different places. Moles and reacting masses are arithmetic-dense under time pressure and separate the middle grades from the top ones in Extended papers; they respond to volume of practice rather than to more explanation. Organic chemistry, by contrast, arrives late in most Year 11 schemes of work and is simply under-practised, which is why a short block on it so often produces a disproportionate gain.

Biology loses marks to precision and volume. Osmosis answers that describe water moving without naming a water potential gradient score less than they look like they should. Genetics behaves like a mathematics topic, where notation and ratio reasoning rather than recall are the obstacle. Human physiology is a terminology load, and short frequent active recall beats long rereading by a wide margin.

The table puts those alongside an honest estimate of the session time each takes. The last row is the one worth acting on first: graph and table work on the practical paper is taught thinly everywhere, counts in every series, and is the highest-yield two sessions available in the whole subject group.

sections.heading: Cambridge or Pearson: what changes between the boards
paragraphs: Dubai's private schools run seventeen different curricula, with the UK curriculum carrying thirty-seven per cent of enrolment, and inside that share both Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE are sat. Some schools split boards by department, so a child can face Cambridge sciences and a Pearson mathematics paper in the same summer. The examination entry is the only reliable source for which applies.

Paper counts differ. A Cambridge separate science carries three papers and a Pearson separate science carries two, which changes the shape of a revision timetable even when the content largely overlaps. Tiering differs too: Cambridge sciences are entered Core or Extended, which caps the grade available, while the Pearson separate sciences are untiered.

The practical assessment is the most consequential difference. A Cambridge student has a dedicated component, either the practical test or the alternative to practical, and so has a specific paper to practise. A Pearson student meets the same skills embedded inside the written papers, which makes them easy to overlook entirely until a mock reveals them. Neither arrangement is harder; they simply need different preparation, and a tutor who assumes the wrong one will miss a component.

There is a scheduling difference as well. Pearson runs International GCSE examinations in May and June and again in November each year, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reaching students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, and for a centre in The Greens that is the whole list -- the February and March series is offered to India only, so any March date you find belongs to another country. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official timetable rather than from any restated date.

sections.heading: When science support has to start, counted from the entry deadline
paragraphs: The decision with a hard deadline is the tier, and on the Cambridge sciences that deadline falls months before the paper. A student in The Greens is choosing between two series, June and November, and each one closes its entries long before anyone sits anything: the June entry is made in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first script, with forecast grades due a few weeks before the exam period and results in August. November works the same way and reports in January, which is what makes it the resit route rather than a first choice. The precise days come from the school's statement of entry, and the practical consequence does not change with them: the Core or Extended decision is locked well before the first paper, so it has to be argued in the autumn term while there is still evidence to argue with.

That matters for a Greens family because the tier caps the grade. A parent discovering a Core entry in April cannot change it for that series, however good the revision. A parent reviewing it in September has a specific conversation available with the school, based on the marks the student produces on an Extended paper under timed conditions rather than on a general sense of ability.

Working backwards from there gives a sensible calendar. Year 10 is for foundational topics and for the tier conversation. The first half of Year 11 is for the heavy content, electricity, moles and genetics, while there is still time for practice to take effect. The second half is for complete timed papers, including the practical paper, which is the component nobody has practised enough. New content introduced after the mocks rarely converts into marks.

No International Baccalaureate session or results date appears on this page. The IB's own site is not reliably readable by automated checks, so those dates should come from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly rather than from any tutoring page.

sections.heading: One tutor or three?
paragraphs: A single tutor across all three sciences is cheaper to arrange and usually worse value. The three subjects fail in different ways: physics on applied reasoning, chemistry on arithmetic density and late-arriving content, biology on precision and terminology volume. A generalist will teach each one adequately and none of them well, and the first place that shows is the Extended papers where the top two grades are decided.

The honest exception is a Coordinated Sciences or Double Award student whose gaps are spread evenly across the three disciplines. There the course itself is coordinated, the content is compressed, and a single tutor who knows that syllabus can work across it coherently. That is a route-specific answer rather than a general one, which is why the route question comes first on this page.

For a triple-science student the efficient arrangement is usually one specialist for the weak subject and nothing for the other two, reviewed each term. Families who buy three weekly hours because there are three subjects are buying symmetry rather than need, and symmetry is expensive. A diagnostic on each subject costs three sessions and frequently reveals that only one of them requires a standing arrangement.

Where two subjects genuinely need work, two shorter back-to-back sessions with two different specialists on the long midweek evening beats one longer session with a generalist. It keeps the weekly footprint to a single evening, which is what makes a plan survive a Dubai term, and each hour is taught by someone who knows where that specific paper loses marks.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects competing for the same evenings
paragraphs: An international curriculum does not replace the UAE's own requirements, and families new to Dubai are regularly surprised by this. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They sit on the timetable alongside the three sciences and they generate their own homework.

KHDA is specific about how they run. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least twenty-five minutes.

For a Year 11 carrying nine science papers, those lessons and their homework are part of the arithmetic of the week. A tutoring plan that assumes the only competing work is science homework will overcommit the evenings. This is the practical reason the rotation model beats three weekly hours: it leaves room for the subjects that are compulsory whatever the family's plans for science.

If support for those subjects is what you actually need, one constraint is worth knowing. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, so help has to work with the school's own material rather than import a parallel syllabus. KHDA also requires that school teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA permission to teach those subjects, which is a credential a parent can ask about directly.

sections.heading: What three-subject science support costs in this part of Dubai
paragraphs: Published 2026 rates across the emirate put budget and university-student online tutoring at roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, qualified subject tutors online at about AED 150 to 300, and IGCSE specialists from around AED 200 to 450 and upwards. Bestimate's Dubai cost table estimates a single weekly hour at AED 240 to 600 a month at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to beyond AED 2,000 for exam-year specialist support. None of these figures is an IB Gram price.

Multiply that by three subjects and the reason this page argues for a narrow plan becomes financial as well as practical. Three weekly specialist hours across a Year 11 is a five-figure commitment in dirhams, for a student who in most cases has one genuinely weak science. One specialist hour plus a weekend practical block costs a fraction of it and targets the marks that are actually missing.

In-home visits are quoted in Dubai from roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel inside the price, and advertised monthly packages of four two-hour visits run at AED 1,599 to 1,799. For a Greens household the premium costs evening minutes as well as dirhams, and the week described earlier has very few to spare. IB Gram does not make home visits in Dubai; home visits are a service offered only in India.

One piece of context on the wider cost of schooling here. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. For a family budgeting science support across two years, a flat school fee is the one fixed point in the calculation.

faqs.question: Should my child take three separate IGCSE sciences or Coordinated Sciences?
faqs.answer: It depends on where they are going rather than on how able they are. Three separate sciences is the route most schools expect before A Level or Higher Level Diploma sciences, and on the Cambridge syllabuses it means nine papers in one series. Coordinated Sciences 0654 awards two IGCSEs from three papers and preserves two option blocks for other subjects. A student taking three sciences thinly often ends up with worse grades than one taking Coordinated Sciences properly, so discuss it with the school before Year 10.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science route do schools near The Greens teach?
faqs.answer: All of them appear within reach of the community. British-curriculum campuses in Emirates Living, Al Sufouh and Al Barsha run Cambridge or Pearson separate sciences and the coordinated or double-award routes, and the IB continuum campuses near The Greens run the Middle Years Programme at this age instead, so a fourteen to sixteen-year-old there may not be sitting IGCSE science at all. The examination entry settles it. Schools are named on this page as neighbourhood context only, with no affiliation implied.

faqs.question: How do we fit three sciences into one week of after-school time?
faqs.answer: By not giving each one a separate weekly hour. Secondary days here end between about 15:00 and 15:30, buses load after form groups and clubs run to half past four, which leaves four weekday evenings of roughly ninety minutes to two and a half hours each. The pattern that survives is one rotating science on a fixed weekday, the longest midweek evening protected for two subjects if all three need work, and the weekend or the Friday half-day for complete timed papers.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals assessed if the tutoring is online?
faqs.answer: The assessed practical component is written in every case. Cambridge candidates sit a practical test or the alternative-to-practical paper; Pearson embeds the same skills inside its written papers. What is tested is reading an unfamiliar method, identifying variables, tabulating with correct units, choosing a sensible scale, plotting accurately and criticising a procedure. All of that is taught better with a shared screen and a past paper than with apparatus. Manipulation and safety belong to the school's laboratory lessons.

faqs.question: What time can an IGCSE science session start after the school bus reaches The Greens?
faqs.answer: Around 16:00 for schools inside Emirates Living and closer to 16:30 for the Al Sufouh, Al Barsha and southern campuses, once the bus and any club are accounted for. Published finish times are not departure times, since secondary buses load after form groups. Treat those figures as indicative and set your slot against your own school day and bus route. Families who book 16:30 generally keep the slot until May; families who try 15:30 usually abandon it by October.

faqs.question: Is one science tutor enough, or do we need three?
faqs.answer: For a triple-science student, usually one, and rarely three. The three subjects fail differently, so a generalist teaches each adequately and none well, but most students have one genuinely weak science rather than three. Three diagnostic sessions typically show which. For a Coordinated Sciences or Double Award student the answer flips: the course is coordinated and compressed, the gaps are spread across all three disciplines, and a single tutor who knows that syllabus can work across it coherently.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE science paper covers the practical component?
faqs.answer: On the Cambridge separate sciences and on Coordinated and Combined Science, candidates sit either Paper 5, a practical test taken at the centre, or Paper 6, the alternative to practical, depending on what the school enters. On Pearson's separate sciences and Science Double Award there is no separate practical paper; those skills are assessed inside the written papers. Check which applies on the examination entry, because a student who has only practised one format finds the other unfamiliar in the hall.

faqs.question: Does Edexcel International GCSE science differ from Cambridge for a Greens student?
faqs.answer: Yes, in three ways that change preparation. Paper counts differ, with three papers per Cambridge separate science against two per Pearson subject. Cambridge sciences are tiered Core and Extended, which caps the grade the entry allows, while the Pearson separate sciences are untiered. And the practical skills sit in a dedicated Cambridge paper but inside the Pearson written papers, which makes them easy to overlook entirely until a mock reveals them. Neither is harder; they need different practice.

faqs.question: When should a Year 10 in The Greens start IGCSE science support?
faqs.answer: Early in Year 10 if the tier decision is still open, because that is when evidence can still influence it. Cambridge entries close months ahead of the papers on both of the series a Dubai candidate can sit: the June entry is made in the spring and the November entry earlier still, and the exact day is on your school's statement of entry. Either way Core or Extended is locked long before the exam period and cannot be revised by revision. If the entry is fixed, the useful starting point is a diagnostic on the subject the last report flagged, aimed at naming two topics rather than describing a weakness.

faqs.question: Where do Greens science students lose the most marks across the three papers?
faqs.answer: In physics, electricity and moments, because both are applied rather than recalled and the diagram often is not drawn. In chemistry, moles and reacting masses under time pressure, and organic chemistry, which arrives late in Year 11 and is simply under-practised. In biology, osmosis wording, genetics notation and the sheer volume of physiology terminology. Across all routes, the graph, table and procedure-criticism questions on the practical paper, which are taught thinly everywhere because laboratory time is short.

faqs.question: Can science sessions run during the Dubai school holidays?
faqs.answer: Yes, and holidays do more work per hour than term time. The Dubai academic year breaks for around a fortnight in December, again in spring and for nine or ten weeks in summer, and those breaks sit awkwardly close to the examination series. A block of alternate-day sessions through a break closes a topic gap at a quieter point in the calendar, with a student who is not already tired from a school day and with nothing else competing for the evening.

faqs.question: What does supporting all three IGCSE sciences at once cost in The Greens?
faqs.answer: At the published Dubai specialist band of roughly AED 200 to 450 an hour, three weekly hours across a Year 11 is a five-figure commitment in dirhams. Qualified subject tutors online sit at about AED 150 to 300, and Bestimate's Dubai cost table puts a single weekly hour at AED 600 to 1,200 a month in the middle of the market. Since most triple-science students have one genuinely weak subject, one specialist hour plus a weekend practical block usually costs a fraction and targets the missing marks.

faqs.question: Do the mandatory UAE subjects leave room for science tutoring midweek?
faqs.answer: They take real space, which is why the rotation model exists. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit and they generate their own homework. A plan that assumes science homework is the only competing work will overcommit the four usable weekday evenings.

faqs.question: Can my child sit IGCSE science papers as a private candidate in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, through an examination centre rather than through a tutor, and the administration is more demanding than the examination. The centre handles the entry, fees are set by the centre and the board, and deadlines fall earlier than families expect. Practical components need particular attention, since a Cambridge practical test has to be taken at a centre equipped for it. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so work from the live official timetable rather than from a restated date.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE science tutor do in the first session?
faqs.answer: Works a real past paper with the student and reports back on named topics rather than impressions. For a Cambridge candidate that usually includes a few questions from the alternative-to-practical paper, because it is the component least practised and the quickest to diagnose. The session should also confirm the route and tier on the examination entry and establish whether the weakness is content, technique or practice, since those three point to very different plans and very different costs.
